### threat

- precondition app-status-check: an app outside GitHub Actions, such as an outside CI, makes a commit status or a check run for a commit whose message an attacker writes (a commit of a pull request from a fork, or a commit that merges a pull request; the message of a commit that merges a pull request can have the title of the pull request), and the commit status or the check run starts a run of status, check_suite or check_run, which runs the workflow of the default branch, whatever branch the commit is on. The payload of a run of any of the three events has the SHA of the commit, and the payload of a run of status or check_suite also has the message, the author name and the committer name of the commit. A finding of a workflow whose on has only events among status, check_suite and check_run (one, two or all three) holds only when the fact of the commit is true: repo.fork-pr-app-checks for a commit of a pull request from a fork, and repo.merge-commit-app-checks for a commit that the merge of a pull request puts in a branch of the repository or that a merge queue of the repository makes. A finding kind asks the fact of each kind of commit that its attackers write; the finding of a finding kind that asks both facts holds when at least one of the two facts is true. The rule does not ask these facts of a workflow whose on has another event too, and reports the finding of such a workflow whatever the values of the facts are. The finding is conditional when no file of facts and no --fact answers the facts
  - observed: 2026-11-05, runner 2.338.2: a GitHub App made a commit status and a check run for a commit of a pull request from a fork: runs of status, check_suite and check_run started on the default branch, and the message of the commit, with \$( ) in it, was in commit.commit.message of status and in check_suite.head_commit.message of check_suite
  - observed: 2026-11-06, runner 2.338.2: the same again: the SHA of the commit of the pull request was in sha and commit.sha of status, check_suite.head_sha and check_suite.head_commit.id of check_suite, and check_run.head_sha and check_run.check_suite.head_sha of check_run; check_suite.after and check_suite.before were null; the author name and the committer name of the commit, with \$( ) in each, were in the payloads of status and check_suite
  - cites:
    - <https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows#status>
    - <https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows#check_suite>
    - <https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows#check_run>
- precondition callers-events: a reusable workflow or a composite action that is among the inputs runs on the events of the callers of the workflow or the action, whoever the callers are; when the inputs are the whole repository and hold every caller of the workflow or the action, the rule reads the workflow or the action on the events of the callers, with the values that the callers give under with
  - cites:
    - <https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows#workflow_call>
    - <https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7x29-qqmq-v6qc>
- precondition text-reaches: what the attacker wrote reaches the agent, in its prompt or what its tools read, and steers it; the actions warn of it
  - cites:
    - <https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action/blob/6fed3ca145920b639991cb756090506e1bcaf515/docs/security.md>
    - <https://github.com/openai/codex-action/blob/bdf19a4a223ec2549a3e2274a0cf61556bc07675/docs/security.md>
- actor: fork-pr-author
  - via: opens or updates a pull request from a fork, which runs pull_request_target, and workflow_run after its pull_request; or pushes a commit to the pull request, and an app outside GitHub Actions makes a commit status or a check run for the commit, and the commit status or the check run starts a run of status, check_suite or check_run whose actor is the app
  - events: pull_request_target, workflow_run, status, check_suite, check_run
  - run starters: pull_request_target: attacker, workflow_run: attacker, status: attacker, check_suite: attacker, check_run: attacker
  - gains: run-code, read-secrets, write-with-token, write-cache
- actor: issue-author
  - via: opens an issue or a discussion
  - events: issues, discussion
  - run starters: issues: attacker, discussion: attacker
  - gains: run-code, read-secrets, write-with-token, write-cache
- actor: commenter
  - via: comments on an issue, a pull request or a discussion, or reviews a pull request from a branch of the repository or comments on the diff of the pull request
  - events: issue_comment, discussion_comment, pull_request_review, pull_request_review_comment
  - run starters: issue_comment: attacker, discussion_comment: attacker, pull_request_review: attacker, pull_request_review_comment: attacker
  - gains: run-code, read-secrets, write-with-token, write-cache
- actor: anyone-who-forks
  - via: forks the repository
  - events: fork
  - run starters: fork: attacker
  - gains: run-code, read-secrets, write-with-token, write-cache
- actor: merged-commit-author
  - via: writes the message of a commit that is merged, or put in a merge queue, and an app outside GitHub Actions makes a commit status or a check run for the commit, and the commit status or the check run starts a run of status, check_suite or check_run
  - events: status, check_suite, check_run
  - run starters: status: other, check_suite: other, check_run: other
  - gains: run-code, read-secrets, write-with-token, write-cache

## allowed-actions

- problem: a uses names an action, a reusable workflow or a Docker image that the setting of allowed actions of GitHub (the fact repo.allowed-actions) does not allow, or names an action by a tag or a branch where the setting requires a full commit SHA: GitHub does not start the run of a workflow that has a uses that the setting does not allow, and fails the job when a step of a composite action that the job runs has a uses that the setting does not allow, or when any step of the job names an action by a tag or a branch where the setting requires a full commit SHA
- expected: every uses of another repository and every uses of a Docker image is one that the setting of allowed actions of GitHub allows, and, when the setting requires a full commit SHA, every uses of an action names a full commit SHA
- targets: workflow, action-metadata
- quality rule: a finding of the quality rule alone gives no attacker a gain, and the findings of the quality rule set no bit of the exit code
- default run: given-facts: the rule runs, with all its kinds of findings, when --rule names the rule; in a run without --rule, the rule runs only when --facts or --fact (also the key facts or fact of a configuration file) answers the fact repo.allowed-actions with found (a value) or with absent (an answer, written in a file of facts or in --fact, that the fact does not exist); a fact that the file of facts and --fact leave out has no answer, and then the rule does not run, and --online alone does not make the rule run either

### finding kinds

- allowed-actions.unstarted-run
  - detected: the setting of allowed actions of GitHub (repo.allowed-actions) does not allow {uses}, when {uses} is read as GitHub reads a uses (with empty parts and the path parts "." dropped, and the path parts ".." resolved, so that owner//repo/./path@v1 is read as owner/repo/path@v1; a Docker image is compared as written)
  - arguments:
    - {uses}: The uses, as written.
  - consequence: GitHub does not start the run of the workflow: no job of the run runs, even the jobs that do not use the action, the reusable workflow or the image, and only the page of the run shows the error. GitHub checks the uses before the run starts, so a step whose if is false does not avoid the error
  - remedy: ask an administrator of the repository, or of the organization that owns the repository, to allow the uses in the setting of allowed actions, or replace the uses with a uses that the setting allows
  - fact kinds: repo.allowed-actions
  - true positives:
    - unstarted-run.remote-callee.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
      #   the repository example-org/allowed-actions-remote, which the fact
      #   workflow.definition answers with the workflow of the true positive
      #   unstarted-run (unstarted-run.yml) of the rule, with on: workflow_call in
      #   place of the on of unstarted-run.yml. The job passes its secrets with
      #   secrets: inherit. In the true positive, the setting of allowed actions
      #   of GitHub allows gradle/* and docker://alpine:*, and blocks
      #   gradle/actions/setup-gradle@*. One step, whose if is false, uses
      #   gradle/actions/setup-gradle. Another step uses the Docker image busybox,
      #   which no pattern allows. Another step uses actions/cache, which no
      #   pattern allows.
      # reason: the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event that started the
      #   run of the calling job, so the reason of the true positive holds: GitHub
      #   checks each uses before the run starts, also the uses of a step whose if
      #   is false, and does not start the run: no job of the run runs (in runs
      #   that the authors of the rule made on GitHub, such runs ended as
      #   startup_failure).
      on: push
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        c:
          uses: example-org/allowed-actions-remote/.github/workflows/w.yml@v1
          secrets: inherit
      ```
    - unstarted-run.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: the setting of allowed actions of GitHub allows gradle/* and
      #   docker://alpine:*, and blocks gradle/actions/setup-gradle@*. One step,
      #   whose if is false, uses gradle/actions/setup-gradle. Another step uses
      #   the Docker image busybox, which no pattern allows. Another step uses
      #   actions/cache, which no pattern allows.
      # reason: GitHub checks each uses before the run starts, also the uses of a
      #   step whose if is false, and does not start the run: no job of the run
      #   runs (in runs that the authors of the rule made on GitHub, such runs
      #   ended as startup_failure).
      on: push
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          timeout-minutes: 10
          steps:
            - uses: gradle/actions/wrapper-validation@ed408507eac070d1f99cc633dbcf757c94c7933a # v4
            - if: false
              uses: gradle/actions/setup-gradle@ed408507eac070d1f99cc633dbcf757c94c7933a # v4
            - uses: docker://busybox:1.36
            - uses: actions/cache@v4
              with:
                path: ~/.cache
                key: cache-${{ github.sha }}
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - unstarted-run.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: the setting of allowed actions of GitHub allows gradle/* and
      #   docker://alpine:*, and blocks gradle/actions/setup-gradle@*; the
      #   workflow uses gradle/actions/wrapper-validation and the image alpine.
      # reason: the setting allows each uses, so GitHub starts the run.
      on: push
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          timeout-minutes: 10
          steps:
            - uses: gradle/actions/wrapper-validation@ed408507eac070d1f99cc633dbcf757c94c7933a # v4
            - uses: docker://alpine:3.20
      ```
- allowed-actions.failed-job
  - detected: the setting of allowed actions of GitHub (repo.allowed-actions) does not allow {uses}, a uses of a step of a composite action, when {uses} is read as GitHub reads a uses (with empty parts and the path parts "." dropped, and the path parts ".." resolved, so that owner//repo/./path@v1 is read as owner/repo/path@v1)
  - arguments:
    - {uses}: The uses, as written.
  - consequence: GitHub fails the job that runs the composite action in the step "Set up job", before any step of the job runs, and the job shows the error in its log; the jobs whose needs does not name the failed job still run
  - remedy: ask an administrator of the repository, or of the organization that owns the repository, to allow the uses in the setting of allowed actions, or replace the uses with a uses that the setting allows
  - fact kinds: repo.allowed-actions
  - true positives:
    - failed-job.action.yml (action-metadata, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a composite action of the repository uses
      #   gradle/actions/setup-gradle, which the setting of allowed actions of
      #   GitHub blocks with !gradle/actions/setup-gradle@*.
      # reason: GitHub fails each job that runs the composite action in the step
      #   Set up job, before any step of the job runs (in runs that the authors of
      #   the rule made on GitHub, the job failed with the error "The action ... is
      #   not allowed").
      name: build
      description: build with Gradle
      runs:
        using: composite
        steps:
          - uses: gradle/actions/setup-gradle@ed408507eac070d1f99cc633dbcf757c94c7933a # v4
          - run: ./gradlew build
            shell: bash
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - failed-job.action.yml (action-metadata, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a composite action of the repository uses
      #   gradle/actions/wrapper-validation, which the setting of allowed actions
      #   of GitHub allows with gradle/*.
      # reason: the setting allows the uses, so the job runs the steps.
      name: validate
      description: validate the Gradle wrapper
      runs:
        using: composite
        steps:
          - uses: gradle/actions/wrapper-validation@ed408507eac070d1f99cc633dbcf757c94c7933a # v4
      ```
- allowed-actions.unpinned-action
  - detected: {uses} names an action by a tag or a branch, not by a full commit SHA, and the setting of allowed actions of GitHub (repo.allowed-actions) requires a full commit SHA for each action (sha_pinning_required). This kind does not apply to a uses of a reusable workflow or of a Docker image, which may name a tag under the setting
  - arguments:
    - {uses}: The uses, as written.
  - consequence: GitHub fails the job of the uses in the step "Set up job", before any step of the job runs, and the job shows the error in its log; the jobs whose needs does not name the failed job still run
  - remedy: name the action by the full commit SHA of the commit that the tag or the branch names, such as owner/repo@ followed by the 40 hexadecimal digits of the SHA
  - fact kinds: repo.allowed-actions
  - true positives:
    - unpinned-action.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: the setting of allowed actions of GitHub allows all actions and
      #   requires a full commit SHA for each action; a step uses actions/cache by
      #   the tag v4.
      # reason: GitHub fails the job in the step Set up job (in runs that the
      #   authors of the rule made on GitHub, the job failed with the error "all
      #   actions must be pinned to a full-length commit SHA").
      on: push
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          timeout-minutes: 10
          steps:
            - uses: actions/cache@v4
              with:
                path: ~/.cache
                key: cache-${{ github.sha }}
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - unpinned-action.never-runs.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: the setting of allowed actions of GitHub allows all actions and
      #   requires a full commit SHA for each action; on push, the job whose id is
      #   disabled has if: false, and the job whose id is on-failure needs the job
      #   build and has if: needs.build.result == 'failure'; each of the two jobs
      #   uses actions/cache by the tag v4.
      # reason: GitHub skips the job disabled because the if of the job disabled is
      #   false. The if of the job on-failure calls no status function, so GitHub
      #   evaluates the if of the job on-failure only when the job build succeeded;
      #   needs.build.result is then success, and the if is false. When the job
      #   build fails or is skipped, GitHub skips the job on-failure without
      #   evaluating the if. So neither job runs
      #   (https://github.com/github/docs/blob/404a5f4de6cd5311e3ce2d5c076571291e0107d6/data/reusables/actions/jobs/section-using-conditions-to-control-job-execution.md);
      #   GitHub does not run the step Set up job of a job that GitHub skips, so
      #   neither job fails.
      on: push
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          timeout-minutes: 10
          steps:
            - run: echo built
        disabled:
          if: false
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          timeout-minutes: 10
          steps:
            - uses: actions/cache@v4
              with:
                path: ~/.cache
                key: cache-${{ github.sha }}
        on-failure:
          needs: build
          if: needs.build.result == 'failure'
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          timeout-minutes: 10
          steps:
            - uses: actions/cache@v4
              with:
                path: ~/.cache
                key: cache-${{ github.sha }}
      ```
    - unpinned-action.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: the setting of allowed actions of GitHub requires a full commit
      #   SHA for each action; the workflow uses actions/cache by a full commit
      #   SHA, and the Docker image alpine by a tag.
      # reason: GitHub requires the full commit SHA of an action only, and a
      #   Docker image may still name a tag (in a run that the authors of the rule
      #   made on GitHub, a docker:// step by a tag ran).
      on: push
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          timeout-minutes: 10
          steps:
            - uses: actions/cache@0057852bfaa89a56745cba8c7296529d2fc39830 # v4
              with:
                path: ~/.cache
                key: cache-${{ github.sha }}
            - uses: docker://alpine:3.20
      ```

### undetected forms

- list-unknown: a run that names the rule with --rule but has no answer of repo.allowed-actions: the rule has no setting to compare the uses with, and reports nothing
  - finding kinds: allowed-actions.unstarted-run, allowed-actions.failed-job, allowed-actions.unpinned-action
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: list-unknown.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the run names allowed-actions with --rule but has no answer of
    #   repo.allowed-actions.
    # reason: the setting of allowed actions of GitHub may not allow
    #   gradle/actions/setup-gradle, and then GitHub does not start the run.
    # cause: without an answer of repo.allowed-actions the rule has no setting
    #   to compare the uses with.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 10
        steps:
          - uses: gradle/actions/setup-gradle@ed408507eac070d1f99cc633dbcf757c94c7933a # v4
    ```
- verified-creator: a uses of an action that only the option of the setting for the verified creators of GitHub Marketplace (verified_allowed) could allow: the workflow does not say whether GitHub verified the creator of the action, so the rule does not report the uses
  - finding kinds: allowed-actions.unstarted-run, allowed-actions.failed-job
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: verified-creator.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the setting of allowed actions of GitHub allows the actions of
    #   the verified creators of GitHub Marketplace, and no pattern; a step uses
    #   example-creator/deploy-action.
    # reason: when GitHub has not verified example-creator, the setting does not
    #   allow the uses, and GitHub does not start the run.
    # cause: whether GitHub verified the creator of an action is not in the
    #   workflow, and no fact answers it.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 10
        steps:
          - uses: example-creator/deploy-action@ed408507eac070d1f99cc633dbcf757c94c7933a
    ```
- lockfile-tag: a workflow that a dependency lockfile of the repository covers, and a uses by a tag that a pattern of the setting names by the same tag: GitHub compares a locked uses by the commit SHA of the lockfile, not by the tag, so the pattern does not allow the uses, and the rule, which does not read the lockfile, reads the uses as allowed
  - finding kinds: allowed-actions.unstarted-run, allowed-actions.failed-job
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - example: lockfile-tag.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a dependency lockfile of the repository covers the workflow,
    #   and the setting of allowed actions of GitHub allows actions/cache@v4; a
    #   step uses actions/cache@v4.
    # reason: GitHub compares a locked uses by the commit SHA of the lockfile,
    #   not by the tag, so the pattern actions/cache@v4 does not allow the uses,
    #   and GitHub does not start the run.
    # cause: the rule does not read the lockfile, and compares the uses as
    #   written.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 10
        steps:
          - uses: actions/cache@v4
            with:
              path: ~/.cache
              key: cache-${{ github.sha }}
    ```
- remote-composite: a uses inside the action.yml of a composite action of another repository when action.definition has no answer for the composite action: the rule reads the steps of a composite action of another repository only from the answer of the fact action.definition
  - finding kinds: allowed-actions.unstarted-run, allowed-actions.failed-job, allowed-actions.unpinned-action
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-composite.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a step uses example-org/unasked-composite@v1, a composite
    #   action of another repository that the pattern * of the setting of
    #   allowed actions of GitHub allows (the setting also blocks
    #   gradle/actions/setup-gradle@*), and the run has no answer of
    #   action.definition for the composite action.
    # reason: a step of the composite action may use an action that the setting
    #   does not allow, and then GitHub fails the job.
    # cause: the rule reads the steps of a composite action of another
    #   repository only from the answer of action.definition.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 10
        steps:
          - uses: example-org/unasked-composite@v1
    ```
- outside-actions-directory: a uses whose path uses .. to name a directory above the directory where the runner puts the actions of the job (\_actions): the directory that the path points to is decided when the job runs
  - finding kinds: allowed-actions.unstarted-run, allowed-actions.failed-job
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: outside-actions-directory.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a step uses example-org/unlisted-tools with a path that goes
    #   with .. above the directory where the runner puts the actions of the
    #   job; the setting of allowed actions of GitHub is * and !example-org/*.
    # reason: GitHub may not allow the action that the path names.
    # cause: what the path names is decided when the job runs, and a path above
    #   the directory of actions names no action that the rule can compare.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 10
        steps:
          - uses: example-org/unlisted-tools/../../../../setup@v1
    ```
- self-outside: a \$/ uses whose path goes with .. above the root of the repository into the directory of another action, which runs the code of another repository: the rule does not compare such a uses with the setting
  - finding kinds: allowed-actions.unstarted-run, allowed-actions.failed-job
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: self-outside.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the first step uses example-org/partly-listed/setup@v1, which
    #   the pattern * of the setting of allowed actions of GitHub allows; the
    #   second step is a $/ uses whose path goes with .. above the root of the
    #   repository into the directory where the runner put
    #   example-org/partly-listed, and the setting blocks
    #   example-org/partly-listed/hidden@*.
    # reason: the second step runs the action hidden of
    #   example-org/partly-listed, which the setting does not allow.
    # cause: the rule does not compare a $/ uses with the setting.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 10
        steps:
          - uses: example-org/partly-listed/setup@v1
          - uses: $/../../../example-org/partly-listed/v1/hidden
    ```
- composite-image: a docker:// step of a composite action, of the repository or of another repository: the authors of the rule did not try whether the setting of allowed actions of GitHub checks the image of such a step, so the rule does not compare such an image with the setting. The authors of the rule saw that a docker:// step of a workflow by a tag runs when the setting requires a full commit SHA, but did not try a docker:// step of a composite action
  - finding kinds: allowed-actions.unstarted-run, allowed-actions.failed-job, allowed-actions.unpinned-action
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: composite-image.action.yml (action-metadata, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a composite action of the repository has a docker:// step of
    #   the image busybox, which no pattern of the setting of allowed actions of
    #   GitHub names.
    # reason: if GitHub checks the image of a docker:// step of a composite
    #   action with the setting, GitHub fails each job that runs the composite
    #   action.
    # cause: the authors of the rule did not try whether the setting checks the
    #   image of a docker:// step of a composite action.
    name: scan
    description: scan the workspace
    runs:
      using: composite
      steps:
        - uses: docker://busybox:1.36
    ```
- remote-called-pinning: a step, in a reusable workflow of another repository that a job calls, that names an action by a tag or a branch where the setting of allowed actions of GitHub requires a full commit SHA: the authors of the rule did not try whether GitHub requires the pin of such a step by the setting of the repository of the caller, so the rule does not report such a step as unpinned
  - finding kinds: allowed-actions.unpinned-action
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-called-pinning.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the setting of allowed actions of GitHub allows all actions and
    #   requires a full commit SHA; a job calls the reusable workflow
    #   .github/workflows/w.yml of example-org/allowed-actions-remote, whose step
    #   uses actions/cache by the tag v4.
    # reason: if GitHub requires the pin of a step of a called workflow by the
    #   setting of the repository of the caller, GitHub fails the job of the
    #   called workflow.
    # cause: the authors of the rule did not try which repository's setting
    #   GitHub applies to the pin of a step of a called workflow of another
    #   repository, so the rule does not report the step as unpinned.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/allowed-actions-remote/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```
- metadata-image: the runs.image (docker://) of the action metadata file of a Docker container action: the authors of the rule did not try whether the setting of allowed actions of GitHub checks the image that a Docker container action runs, so the rule does not compare the runs.image with the setting
  - finding kinds: allowed-actions.unstarted-run, allowed-actions.failed-job, allowed-actions.unpinned-action
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: metadata-image.action.yml (action-metadata, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the action.yml of a Docker container action of the repository
    #   names the image busybox, which no pattern of the setting of allowed
    #   actions of GitHub names.
    # reason: if GitHub checks the image of a Docker container action with the
    #   setting, GitHub fails the job that uses the action.
    # cause: whether GitHub checks the runs.image of an action was not tried, so
    #   the rule does not compare the runs.image with the setting.
    name: scan
    description: scan the workspace
    runs:
      using: docker
      image: docker://busybox:1.36
    ```
- remote-callee: a job or a step inside a reusable workflow of another repository (uses: owner/repo/.github/workflows/&lt;file>@&lt;ref>) whose content the fact workflow.definition does not give. For every rule: a run that does not ask the fact (a run without --online and without the answer in --facts). For a quality rule, also: a run where the linter asked the fact and got no answer (an answer of unknown: the GitHub API did not give the file), and a call deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact. The rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition. For a rule that is not a quality rule (a rule with a threat), the last two forms are the inconclusive kind remote-callee-unknown, not this form
  - finding kinds: allowed-actions.unstarted-run, allowed-actions.failed-job, allowed-actions.unpinned-action
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-callee.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
    #   the repository example-org/allowed-actions-unanswered, whose content is
    #   the workflow of the true positive unstarted-run (unstarted-run.yml) of
    #   the rule, with on: workflow_call in place of the on of
    #   unstarted-run.yml. The linter has no answer of the fact
    #   workflow.definition for the reusable workflow.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event
    #   that started the run of the calling job, and the linter does not read
    #   the reusable workflow.
    # cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from
    #   the answer of workflow.definition.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/allowed-actions-unanswered/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

### false positive forms

- owner-unknown: a run without --repo, and a uses of an action or a reusable workflow of another repository of the same owner: the setting allows each action and each reusable workflow of the same owner, and without the name of the repository the rule does not know the owner, so the rule reports the uses; pass --repo to the linter
  - finding kinds: allowed-actions.unstarted-run, allowed-actions.failed-job
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: owner-unknown.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the workflow of the repository example-org/app uses
    #   example-org/shared-actions/setup, an action of the same owner; the
    #   setting of allowed actions of GitHub has no pattern, and the run has no
    #   --repo.
    # reason: the setting allows each action of the owner of the repository, so
    #   GitHub starts the run.
    # cause: without --repo the rule does not know the owner of the repository.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 10
        steps:
          - uses: example-org/shared-actions/setup@ed408507eac070d1f99cc633dbcf757c94c7933a
    ```
- same-enterprise: a repository of an organization of an enterprise of GitHub Enterprise Cloud, and a uses of a repository of another organization of the same enterprise: the setting allows each action of the enterprise, and the rule, which knows only the owner of the repository, reports the uses
  - finding kinds: allowed-actions.unstarted-run, allowed-actions.failed-job
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: same-enterprise.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the repository belongs to an organization of an enterprise of
    #   GitHub Enterprise Cloud, and the workflow uses example-sister-org/tools,
    #   an action of another organization of the same enterprise; the setting of
    #   allowed actions of GitHub has no pattern.
    # reason: the setting allows each action of the enterprise, so GitHub starts
    #   the run.
    # cause: the rule does not know which organizations are of the same
    #   enterprise.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 10
        steps:
          - uses: example-sister-org/tools@ed408507eac070d1f99cc633dbcf757c94c7933a
    ```
- lockfile-sha: a workflow that a dependency lockfile of the repository covers, and a uses by a tag, where a pattern of the setting names the commit SHA to which the lockfile locks the tag: GitHub compares a locked uses by the commit SHA of the lockfile, so the pattern allows the uses, and the rule, which does not read the lockfile, reports the uses
  - finding kinds: allowed-actions.unstarted-run, allowed-actions.failed-job
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - example: lockfile-sha.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a dependency lockfile of the repository covers the workflow
    #   and locks actions/cache@v4 to the commit 0057852bfaa89a56745cba8c7296529d2fc39830, and the setting of
    #   allowed actions of GitHub allows actions/cache@0057852bfaa89a56745cba8c7296529d2fc39830; a step uses
    #   actions/cache@v4.
    # reason: GitHub compares a locked uses by the commit SHA of the lockfile,
    #   so the pattern allows the uses, and GitHub starts the run.
    # cause: the rule does not read the lockfile, and compares the uses as
    #   written.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 10
        steps:
          - uses: actions/cache@v4
            with:
              path: ~/.cache
              key: cache-${{ github.sha }}
    ```
- lockfile-pinned: a workflow that a dependency lockfile of the repository covers, and a uses of an action by a tag or a branch that the lockfile locks, where the setting requires a full commit SHA: a locked uses satisfies the requirement of a full commit SHA, so GitHub runs the job, and the rule, which does not read the lockfile, reports the uses
  - finding kinds: allowed-actions.unpinned-action
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - example: lockfile-pinned.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a dependency lockfile of the repository covers the workflow
    #   and locks actions/cache@v4 to a commit, and the setting of allowed
    #   actions of GitHub allows all actions and requires a full commit SHA; a
    #   step uses actions/cache@v4.
    # reason: a locked uses satisfies the requirement of a full commit SHA (the
    #   documents of GitHub say so for the workflows that a lockfile covers), so
    #   GitHub runs the job.
    # cause: the rule does not read the lockfile.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 10
        steps:
          - uses: actions/cache@v4
            with:
              path: ~/.cache
              key: cache-${{ github.sha }}
    ```
- job-never-runs: a uses in a job that GitHub never runs because the if of the job is false in every run, and the if is false because of a value other than github.event_name and github.event.action (for example, if: github.event.pull_request.merged == true in a workflow that runs only on pull_request with types: &#91;opened]): GitHub skips the job, so the step "Set up job" of the job does not run and the job does not fail. In the if of a job, and in the if of each job that the job needs, the rule reads only github.event_name, github.event.action and needs.&lt;job_id>.result. A uses in the workflow file that the setting does not allow still stops the run, because GitHub checks every uses in the workflow file before the run starts.
  - finding kinds: allowed-actions.failed-job, allowed-actions.unpinned-action
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: job-never-runs.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the setting of allowed actions of GitHub allows all actions and
    #   requires a full commit SHA; the workflow runs only on pull_request with
    #   types: [opened]; the job deploy has if:
    #   github.event.pull_request.merged == true and uses actions/cache by the tag
    #   v4.
    # reason: a pull request is not merged when the pull request is opened, so
    #   github.event.pull_request.merged is false in every run of the workflow,
    #   the if of the job deploy is false in every run, and GitHub never runs the
    #   job deploy
    #   (https://github.com/github/docs/blob/404a5f4de6cd5311e3ce2d5c076571291e0107d6/data/reusables/actions/jobs/section-using-conditions-to-control-job-execution.md);
    #   GitHub does not run the step Set up job of a job that GitHub skips, so the
    #   job does not fail.
    # cause: the rule reads only github.event_name and github.event.action in the
    #   if of a job, and reads the if of the job deploy as an if that may be true.
    on:
      pull_request:
        types: [opened]
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      deploy:
        if: github.event.pull_request.merged == true
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 10
        steps:
          - uses: actions/cache@v4
            with:
              path: ~/.cache
              key: cache-${{ github.sha }}
    ```
- other-repository-caller: an action metadata file of the repository that only the workflows of other repositories use: GitHub compares the uses of the steps of the action with the setting of the repository of the workflow that runs the action, not with the setting of the repository of the action
  - finding kinds: allowed-actions.failed-job, allowed-actions.unpinned-action
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: other-repository-caller.action.yml (action-metadata, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a composite action of the repository uses
    #   gradle/actions/setup-gradle, which the setting of allowed actions of
    #   GitHub of the repository blocks; only the workflows of other
    #   repositories, whose settings allow gradle/actions/setup-gradle, use the
    #   composite action.
    # reason: GitHub compares the steps of the composite action with the setting
    #   of the repository of the workflow that runs the action, so the jobs run.
    # cause: the rule compares an action metadata file of the repository with
    #   the setting of the repository.
    name: setup
    description: set up Gradle
    runs:
      using: composite
      steps:
        - uses: gradle/actions/setup-gradle@ed408507eac070d1f99cc633dbcf757c94c7933a # v4
    ```

## archived-uses

- problem: a uses names an action or a reusable workflow of a repository that is archived
- expected: every uses that names an action or a reusable workflow of another repository names one of a repository that is not archived
- targets: workflow, action-metadata
- quality rule: a finding of the quality rule alone gives no attacker a gain, and the findings of the quality rule set no bit of the exit code
- default run: facts: the rule runs, with all its kinds of findings (also those that need no fact), when --rule names the rule; in a run without --rule, the rule runs when --online is given, or when --facts or --fact gives a found or absent answer to any fact of repo.archived

### finding kinds

- archived-uses.archived-repository
  - detected: {uses} names {repo}, a repository that is archived
  - arguments:
    - {uses}: The uses, as written.
    - {repo}: A repository, owner/name. GitHub compares the owner and the name without case, so two facts are the same when the two facts differ only in the case of ASCII letters; sisakulint writes the owner and the name in lower case.
  - consequence: an archived repository is read-only and is no longer maintained: when an error or a vulnerability is found in the action or the reusable workflow, the repository gets no fixed version, and the runner still runs the version that the uses names (the rule known-vulnerable-actions of this linter reports an advisory of the GitHub Advisory Database about the action)
  - remedy: replace the action or the reusable workflow with one that is maintained, or fork the repository, maintain the fork, and point the uses to the fork
  - fact kinds: repo.archived
  - true positives:
    - archived-repository.composite.action.yml (action-metadata, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a composite action of the repository makes a GitHub release
      #   with actions/create-release@v1, whose repository GitHub archived.
      # reason: an archived repository is read-only: an error or a vulnerability
      #   found in the action is never fixed in that repository, and the runner
      #   still runs v1 in every job that uses the composite action.
      name: release
      description: makes a release of the build
      runs:
        using: composite
        steps:
          - uses: actions/create-release@v1
            with:
              tag_name: v1.0.0
      ```
    - archived-repository.remote-called-call.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a job calls example-org/nested-workflow/.github/workflows/build.yml@v1,
      #   a reusable workflow of another repository whose job calls a reusable
      #   workflow of actions/create-release, an archived repository.
      # reason: the called workflow calls a workflow that no one maintains, whose
      #   flaws no one fixes; workflow.definition answers the file of the called
      #   workflow.
      on: push
      jobs:
        build:
          uses: example-org/nested-workflow/.github/workflows/build.yml@v1
      ```
    - archived-repository.remote-called.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a job calls example-org/release-workflow/.github/workflows/release.yml@v1,
      #   a reusable workflow of another repository whose step uses
      #   actions/create-release@v1, of an archived repository.
      # reason: the step of the called workflow runs an action that no one
      #   maintains, whose flaws no one fixes; workflow.definition answers the
      #   file of the called workflow.
      on: push
      jobs:
        release:
          uses: example-org/release-workflow/.github/workflows/release.yml@v1
      ```
    - archived-repository.remote-callee.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
      #   the repository example-org/archived-uses-remote, which the fact
      #   workflow.definition answers with the workflow of the true positive
      #   archived-repository (archived-repository.remote-called-call.yml) of the
      #   rule, with on: workflow_call in place of the on of
      #   archived-repository.remote-called-call.yml. The job passes its secrets
      #   with secrets: inherit. In the true positive, a job calls
      #   example-org/nested-workflow/.github/workflows/build.yml@v1, a reusable
      #   workflow of another repository whose job calls a reusable workflow of
      #   actions/create-release, an archived repository.
      # reason: the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event that started the
      #   run of the calling job, so the reason of the true positive holds: the
      #   called workflow calls a workflow that no one maintains, whose flaws no
      #   one fixes; workflow.definition answers the file of the called workflow.
      on: push
      jobs:
        c:
          uses: example-org/archived-uses-remote/.github/workflows/w.yml@v1
          secrets: inherit
      ```
    - archived-repository.remote-composite.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a workflow runs example-org/node-composite@v1, a composite
      #   action of another repository, whose step uses actions/create-release@v1;
      #   actions/create-release is archived.
      # reason: an archived repository is read-only: its maintainers fix nothing
      #   in it; action.definition answers the file of the composite action, as
      #   the archive the runner downloads has it.
      on: push
      permissions: {contents: write}
      jobs:
        release:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: example-org/node-composite@v1
      ```
    - archived-repository.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a workflow makes a GitHub release with
      #   actions/create-release@v1, whose repository GitHub archived.
      # reason: an archived repository is read-only: an error or a vulnerability
      #   found in the action is never fixed in that repository, and the runner
      #   still downloads and runs v1.
      on: push
      permissions: {contents: write}
      jobs:
        release:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/create-release@v1
              with:
                tag_name: v1.0.0
              env:
                GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - archived-repository.remote-composite.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a workflow runs example-org/current-composite@v1, a composite
      #   action of another repository, whose step uses actions/checkout@v4, a
      #   repository that is not archived.
      # reason: neither the composite action nor the action its step uses is of
      #   an archived repository.
      on: push
      permissions: {contents: read}
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: example-org/current-composite@v1
      ```
    - archived-repository.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a workflow checks out its repository with actions/checkout@v5,
      #   whose repository is not archived.
      # reason: the repository of the action is maintained, so an error found in
      #   the action can be fixed in a later version.
      on: push
      permissions: {contents: read}
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v5
              with:
                persist-credentials: false
      ```

### undetected forms

- remote-composite: a uses inside the action.yml of a composite action of another repository (a step of that composite action, not the uses that names the composite action) when action.definition has no answer for the composite action (a run without --online and without the answer in --facts, an answer of unknown, or an action deeper than the 4 levels of actions the linter reads): the rule reads the steps of a composite action of another repository only from the answer
  - finding kinds: archived-uses.archived-repository
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-composite.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a workflow runs example-org/release-action@v1, a composite
    #   action of another repository, and the steps of that composite action
    #   use an action of an archived repository.
    # reason: the archived action runs in the job, and nobody fixes an error
    #   found in the archived action.
    # cause: the rule reads the uses of the inputs only, and does not fetch the
    #   action.yml of a composite action of another repository.
    on: push
    permissions: {contents: write}
    jobs:
      release:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: example-org/release-action@v1
    ```
- remote-callee: a job or a step inside a reusable workflow of another repository (uses: owner/repo/.github/workflows/&lt;file>@&lt;ref>) whose content the fact workflow.definition does not give. For every rule: a run that does not ask the fact (a run without --online and without the answer in --facts). For a quality rule, also: a run where the linter asked the fact and got no answer (an answer of unknown: the GitHub API did not give the file), and a call deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact. The rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition. For a rule that is not a quality rule (a rule with a threat), the last two forms are the inconclusive kind remote-callee-unknown, not this form
  - finding kinds: archived-uses.archived-repository
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-callee.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
    #   the repository example-org/archived-uses-unanswered, whose content is
    #   the workflow of the true positive archived-repository
    #   (archived-repository.remote-called-call.yml) of the rule, with on:
    #   workflow_call in place of the on of
    #   archived-repository.remote-called-call.yml. The linter has no answer of
    #   the fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event
    #   that started the run of the calling job, and the linter does not read
    #   the reusable workflow.
    # cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from
    #   the answer of workflow.definition.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/archived-uses-unanswered/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

## argument-injection

- problem: an attacker's value is passed to a command so that a word the command gets starts with the attacker's value; the command reads a word that starts with - as an option, and some options make the command run a program or code that is written after the name of the option
- expected: the command never reads the attacker's value as an option: the value is inside double quotes, and either the value comes after the word that ends the command's options (-- for most commands, --end-of-options for git), or, when the value starts with -, the step exits with an error before the step runs the command
- severity: critical (the worst of its kinds)
- targets: workflow, action-metadata
- facets:
  - weakness: argument-injection
  - attack-means: string
- default run: always: in a run without --rule, the rule runs unless --skip-rule names the rule

### finding kinds

- argument-injection.option
  - detected: {command} gets a word that starts with the value of {expr_ref}, or, when the value is outside quotes or is a \${{ }} that the runner writes into the script before the shell reads the script, a word that starts after a blank in the value; an attacker controls the value of {expr_ref} on {controlled_on}; the word is at a place in the order of the words of {command} where {command} reads a word that starts with - as an option (a place before a word such as -- that ends the options), and the attacker can write at that place an option in the list {options}, which makes {command} run a program or code that is written after the name of the option
  - arguments:
    - {command}: The command and the subcommands of the command, such as tar or git fetch.
    - {expr_ref}: The reference whose value begins the word, such as github.event.pull_request.title.
    - {controlled_on}: The events on which an attacker controls the value of the expression, each event named once.
    - {options}: The options of the command that run a program, as the attacker writes the options: for one word that holds both the option and the program, a long option with = (--to-command=) or a short option followed by the program in the same word (-e&lt;script>); for two words, the option and then the program, a short option as a word by itself (-c).
  - consequence: the attacker makes the attacker's value start with the name of one of the options that the finding names, followed by a program; the command reads the word as the option whose name starts the word, and runs the program in the step, with whatever the step can reach, such as the secrets and the token in its env, the credentials actions/checkout leaves in .git/config, the network, and sudo on a GitHub-hosted runner
  - remedy: A variable of env and double quotes ("\$X") stop the shell from running the value as code, but the variable and the quotes do not stop the command from reading the value as an option. In either fix below, keep the value in the variable of env, and pass the variable to the command inside double quotes. Then either put the word that ends the command's options (--; --end-of-options for git) after the last option the command needs and before the value, for example right before the value (tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt -- "\$X"), so that the command reads every word after that word as a plain argument; or, before the command, end the step with an error when the value starts with -, such as &#91;&#91; \$X != -\* ]] || exit 1 for the variable X that holds the value. The shell check &#91;&#91; \$X != -\* ]] works only when the command gets the value inside double quotes: when the command gets the value outside quotes, a blank in the value starts a new word, and the new word can start with -. For make, -- is not enough: make reads a word of the form NAME=value as the assignment of a variable even after --, so for make end the step with an error when the value starts with - or contains =, such as &#91;&#91; \$X != -\* && \$X != \*=\* ]] || exit 1
  - severity: critical (found from the CVSS metrics below by the table)
  - fact kinds: repo.pull-request-target-allowed (provider: repo-setting), repo.fork-pr-app-checks (provider: repo-setting), repo.merge-commit-app-checks (provider: repo-setting)
  - attackers: fork-pr-author, issue-author, commenter, merged-commit-author, anyone-who-forks
  - preconditions: option-anywhere, option-runs-program, attacker-dash, attacker-event, callers-events, app-status-check
  - true positives:
    - option.arithmetic.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on pull_request_target, a step extracts an archive in a $( ) inside
      #   $(( )) and passes the name of the pull request's head branch to tar after
      #   the file names.
      # reason: bash expands the $( ) inside $(( )) before it evaluates the
      #   expression, and tar reads a word that begins with - as an option even
      #   after its file names.
      # attack-value: github.head_ref = "--to-command=sh${IFS}-c${IFS}id"
      # attack-run-behavior: tar reads the word as --to-command and runs sh -c id
      #   in the step, with what the step can reach.
      on: pull_request_target
      permissions:
        contents: write
      jobs:
        unpack:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                HEAD_REF: ${{ github.head_ref }}
              run: |
                echo $(( $(tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt "$HEAD_REF"; echo 0) ))
      ```
    - option.array-element.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on pull_request_target, a step extracts an archive and passes
      #   the name of the pull request's head branch to tar after the file names,
      #   as the element 0 of the variable of env (${HEAD_REF[0]}), inside quotes.
      # reason: the element 0 of a variable that is not an array is the value of
      #   the variable, and tar reads a word that begins with - as an option even
      #   after its file names: the attacker names the branch --to-command=<a
      #   program>, and tar runs that program for each file it extracts.
      # attack-value: github.head_ref = "--to-command=sh${IFS}-c${IFS}id"
      # attack-run-behavior: tar reads the word as --to-command and runs sh -c id
      #   in the step, with what the step can reach.
      on: pull_request_target
      permissions:
        contents: write
      jobs:
        unpack:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                HEAD_REF: ${{ github.head_ref }}
              run: tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt "${HEAD_REF[0]}"
      ```
    - option.backquote.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on pull_request_target, a step extracts an archive in ` ` and
      #   passes the name of the pull request's head branch to tar after the file
      #   names.
      # reason: bash runs the tar in ` `, which reads a word that begins with - as
      #   an option even after its file names.
      # attack-value: github.head_ref = "--to-command=sh${IFS}-c${IFS}id"
      # attack-run-behavior: tar reads the word as --to-command and runs sh -c id
      #   in the step, with what the step can reach.
      on: pull_request_target
      permissions:
        contents: write
      jobs:
        unpack:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                HEAD_REF: ${{ github.head_ref }}
              run: |
                echo `tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt "$HEAD_REF"`
      ```
    - option.element-before-command.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on pull_request_target, a step extracts an archive and passes
      #   the name of the pull request's head branch to tar after the file names,
      #   after an assignment of an element of an array before the command word.
      # reason: bash refuses the assignment of the element before the command word
      #   and runs tar, which reads a word that begins with - as an option even
      #   after its file names.
      # attack-value: github.head_ref = "--to-command=sh${IFS}-c${IFS}id"
      # attack-run-behavior: tar reads the word as --to-command and runs sh -c id
      #   in the step, with what the step can reach.
      on: pull_request_target
      permissions:
        contents: write
      jobs:
        unpack:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                HEAD_REF: ${{ github.head_ref }}
              run: |
                a[0]=x tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt "$HEAD_REF"
      ```
    - option.for-words.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on pull_request_target, a step extracts from an archive the
      #   members that match the pull request's title with tar -xv inside $( ) in
      #   the words of for, passing the title through env and inside quotes, and
      #   prints the names tar lists.
      # reason: bash expands the words of for before the loop and runs the tar in $(
      #   ) as any other command, and tar reads a word that begins with - as an
      #   option even after its file names.
      # attack-value: github.event.pull_request.title = "--to-command=echo PWNED"
      # attack-run-behavior: tar in $( ) reads the title as --to-command and runs
      #   echo PWNED for each member it extracts; PWNED goes into the words of for,
      #   and echo prints PWNED.
      on: pull_request_target
      jobs:
        unpack:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
              run: |
                for name in $(tar -xvf archive.tar "$TITLE"); do
                  echo "$name"
                done
      ```
    - option.format.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on pull_request_target, a step extracts an archive and passes
      #   format('{0}', github.head_ref), the name of the pull request's head
      #   branch, to tar after the file names, through env and inside quotes.
      # reason: format writes the argument that the placeholder {0} names at the
      #   start of the text of format, so the value begins as the branch name
      #   does; tar
      #   reads a word that begins with - as an option even after its file names,
      #   and GitHub takes a branch whose name begins with -: the attacker names
      #   the branch --to-command=<a program>, and tar runs that program for each
      #   file it extracts, in a job with the repository's token.
      # attack-value: github.head_ref = "--to-command=sh${IFS}-c${IFS}id"
      # attack-run-behavior: tar reads the word as --to-command and runs sh -c id
      #   in the step, with what the step can reach.
      on: pull_request_target
      permissions:
        contents: write
      jobs:
        unpack:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                HEAD_REF: ${{ format('{0}', github.head_ref) }}
              run: tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt "$HEAD_REF"
      ```
    - option.local-remote.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on pull_request_target, a step fetches from the repository at
      #   the local path /tmp/r and passes the name of the pull request's head
      #   branch to git fetch after the repository, through env and inside quotes.
      # reason: git fetch reads a word that begins with - as an option even after
      #   the repository, and git runs the program given as the value of
      #   --upload-pack in place of git-upload-pack. For a repository on a local path, git runs
      #   that program on the runner, and git runs the program even when /tmp/r
      #   does not exist.
      # attack-value: github.head_ref = "--upload-pack=echo${IFS}PWNED>&2;false"
      # attack-run-behavior: git fetch reads the word as --upload-pack and runs
      #   echo${IFS}PWNED>&2;false through the shell on the runner: the shell
      #   expands ${IFS} to a blank and prints PWNED, and the fetch then fails.
      on: pull_request_target
      permissions:
        contents: write
      jobs:
        fetch:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                HEAD_REF: ${{ github.head_ref }}
              run: git fetch /tmp/r "$HEAD_REF"
      ```
    - option.no-caller.action.yml (action-metadata, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a composite action with no caller among the files that the
      #   linter reads; a step extracts an archive and passes the name of the head
      #   branch of a pull request to tar after the file names, through env and
      #   inside quotes.
      # reason: with no caller among the files that the linter reads, the rule
      #   reads the action on every event an attacker triggers, pull_request_target
      #   among the events. tar reads a word that begins with - as an option even
      #   after the file names, and GitHub takes a branch whose name begins with -:
      #   the attacker names the branch --to-command=<a program>, and tar runs the
      #   program for each file tar extracts, in a job with the token of the
      #   repository.
      # attack-value: github.head_ref = "--to-command=sh${IFS}-c${IFS}id"
      # attack-run-behavior: tar reads the word as --to-command and runs sh -c id
      #   in the step, with what the step can reach.
      name: unpack
      description: unpack the archive
      runs:
        using: composite
        steps:
          - env:
              HEAD_REF: ${{ github.head_ref }}
            run: tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt "$HEAD_REF"
            shell: bash
      ```
    - option.redirect-substitution.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on pull_request_target, a step extracts from an archive the
      #   members that match the pull request's title with tar -xv inside $( ) in
      #   the target of a redirect, passing the title through env and inside
      #   quotes.
      # reason: bash runs the $( ) in the target of the redirect, and tar reads a
      #   title that starts with - as an option.
      # attack-value: github.event.pull_request.title = "--to-command=echo PWNED"
      # attack-run-behavior: tar in $( ) reads the title as --to-command and runs
      #   echo PWNED for each member it extracts; the value of the $( ), which is
      #   the name of the file of the redirect, holds the names of the members
      #   that tar lists and the line PWNED that echo PWNED writes, and echo done
      #   writes to the file of that name.
      on: pull_request_target
      jobs:
        unpack:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
              run: echo done > "$(tar -xvf archive.tar "$TITLE")"
      ```
    - option.remote-callee.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
      #   the repository example-org/argument-injection-remote, which the fact
      #   workflow.definition answers with the workflow of the true positive
      #   option (option.arithmetic.yml) of the rule, with on: workflow_call in
      #   place of the on of option.arithmetic.yml. The job passes its secrets
      #   with secrets: inherit. In the true positive, on pull_request_target, a
      #   step extracts an archive in a $( ) inside $(( )) and passes the name of
      #   the pull request's head branch to tar after the file names.
      # reason: the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event that started the
      #   run of the calling job, so the reason of the true positive holds: bash
      #   expands the $( ) inside $(( )) before it evaluates the expression, and
      #   tar reads a word that begins with - as an option even after its file
      #   names.
      # attack-value: github.head_ref = "--to-command=sh${IFS}-c${IFS}id"
      # attack-run-behavior: tar reads the word as --to-command and runs sh -c id
      #   in the step, with what the step can reach.
      on: pull_request_target
      permissions:
        contents: write
      jobs:
        c:
          uses: example-org/argument-injection-remote/.github/workflows/w.yml@v1
          secrets: inherit
      ```
    - option.repository-name.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on pull_request_target, a step prints a file with sed and
      #   passes the name of the repository of the pull request's head to sed
      #   after the file, through env and inside quotes.
      # reason: GNU sed reads a word that begins with - as an option even after
      #   its operands, and GitHub accepts the name of a repository that begins
      #   with - (a rename of a fork to -dash-probe was observed).
      #   The name of a repository holds only ASCII letters, digits, ., - and _,
      #   and those characters are enough for the short option -e of sed with
      #   its script in the same word: in the script 1eid, the sed command 1e
      #   runs the command id at line 1.
      # attack-value: github.event.pull_request.head.repo.name = "-e1eid"
      # attack-run-behavior: sed reads the word as -e with the script 1eid, runs
      #   the command id at line 1 of notes.txt, and prints the output of id in
      #   the step (on the runner, uid=1001(runner) ...).
      on: pull_request_target
      permissions:
        contents: write
      jobs:
        show:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                NAME: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.repo.name }}
              run: sed -n p notes.txt "$NAME"
      ```
    - option.runner-variable.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on pull_request_target, a step passes $GITHUB_HEAD_REF, which
      #   the runner sets, to tar after the file names, inside quotes.
      # reason: GITHUB_HEAD_REF has the name of the pull request's head branch,
      #   which the author of the pull request chooses and which may begin with -;
      #   tar reads the value as an option.
      # attack-value: github.head_ref = "--to-command=echo${IFS}PWNED"
      # attack-run-behavior: GITHUB_HEAD_REF is the branch's name, and tar reads
      #   "$GITHUB_HEAD_REF" as --to-command and runs echo${IFS}PWNED through the
      #   shell for notes.txt as it extracts it, which prints PWNED.
      on: pull_request_target
      jobs:
        unpack:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt "$GITHUB_HEAD_REF"
      ```
    - option.status-commit.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on status, which an app outside GitHub Actions starts when the
      #   app writes a status for a commit, the job writes the message of the
      #   commit of the status (github.event.commit.commit.message) as an argument
      #   of tar.
      # reason: an outside CI that writes a status for a commit of a pull request
      #   from a fork starts a run of status on the default branch, with the
      #   message of that commit, which the author of the pull request writes, in
      #   the payload (seen on GitHub).
      # attack-value: github.event.commit.commit.message = "--to-command=echo PWNED"
      # attack-run-behavior: an outside CI writes a status for the commit of the
      #   pull request from a fork whose message is the value; the run of status
      #   starts on the default branch, and tar reads the message as its option
      #   --to-command, which runs echo PWNED for each file it extracts.
      on: status
      jobs:
        j:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt "${{ github.event.commit.commit.message }}"
      ```
    - option.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on pull_request_target, a step extracts an archive and passes
      #   the name of the pull request's head branch to tar after the file names,
      #   through env and inside quotes.
      # reason: tar reads a word that begins with - as an option even after its
      #   file names, and GitHub takes a branch whose name begins with -: the
      #   attacker names the branch --to-command=<a program>, and tar runs that
      #   program for each file it extracts, in a job with the repository's token.
      # attack-value: github.head_ref = "--to-command=sh${IFS}-c${IFS}id"
      # attack-run-behavior: tar reads the word as --to-command and runs sh -c id
      #   in the step, with what the step can reach.
      on: pull_request_target
      permissions:
        contents: write
      jobs:
        unpack:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                HEAD_REF: ${{ github.head_ref }}
              run: tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt "$HEAD_REF"
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - option.full-name.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on pull_request_target, a step extracts an archive and passes
      #   the full name of the repository of the pull request's head
      #   (owner/name) to tar after the file names, through env and inside
      #   quotes.
      # reason: the full name begins with the login of the owner of the
      #   repository; when the authors of the linter tried on 2026-11-01, GitHub
      #   refused a login that begins with -, so tar reads the word as the name of
      #   a member of the archive to extract, not as an option. An account made before GitHub refused such a login can have a
      #   login that begins with -, and a repository of such an account is the
      #   undetected form dash-login.
      # attack-value: github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name = "attacker/-Ipython3"
      # attack-run-behavior: tar looks for a file named attacker/-Ipython3 in the
      #   archive, does not find the file, and runs nothing.
      on: pull_request_target
      jobs:
        unpack:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                FULL_NAME: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name }}
              run: tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt "$FULL_NAME"
      ```
    - option.head-label.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on pull_request_target, a step extracts an archive and passes
      #   the label of the pull request's head (owner:branch) to tar after the
      #   file names, through env and inside quotes.
      # reason: the label begins with the login of the owner of the head; when
      #   the authors of the linter tried on 2026-11-01, GitHub refused a login
      #   that begins with -, so tar reads the word as the name of a member of
      #   the archive to extract, not as an option. An
      #   account made before GitHub refused such a login can have a login that
      #   begins with -, and a pull request from such an account is the undetected
      #   form dash-login.
      # attack-value: github.event.pull_request.head.label = "attacker:--to-command=echo${IFS}PWNED"
      # attack-run-behavior: tar looks for a file named
      #   attacker:--to-command=echo${IFS}PWNED in the archive, does not find the
      #   file, and runs nothing.
      on: pull_request_target
      jobs:
        unpack:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                LABEL: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.label }}
              run: tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt "$LABEL"
      ```
    - option.if-compared.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issue_comment, a job runs only when the comment's body is
      #   notes.txt, and a step passes env.NAME, which holds the body, to tar as
      #   the name of a file to extract.
      # reason: == of a GitHub Actions expression ignores the case of letters, so the if of
      #   the job lets the body be only notes.txt, with the case of each letter
      #   chosen by the attacker; the word that
      #   tar gets never starts with -, and tar reads the word as a name of a
      #   file, not as an option.
      # attack-value: github.event.comment.body = "--to-command=echo PWNED"
      # attack-run-behavior: the if of the job is false for this body, so the
      #   job does not run, and nothing is printed.
      on:
        issue_comment:
          types: [created]
      jobs:
        j:
          if: github.event.comment.body == 'notes.txt'
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                NAME: ${{ github.event.comment.body }}
              run: tar -xf archive.tar "$NAME"
      ```
    - option.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on pull_request_target, a step extracts an archive and passes
      #   the name of the pull request's head branch to tar after --.
      # reason: tar reads every word after -- as a file name, not an option, so
      #   a branch named --to-command=... is only a name of a file to extract.
      # attack-value: github.head_ref = "--to-command=sh${IFS}-c${IFS}id"
      # attack-run-behavior: tar looks for a member named
      #   --to-command=sh${IFS}-c${IFS}id in the archive and runs nothing.
      on: pull_request_target
      permissions:
        contents: write
      jobs:
        unpack:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                HEAD_REF: ${{ github.head_ref }}
              run: tar -xf archive.tar -- notes.txt "$HEAD_REF"
      ```
- argument-injection.wiki
  - detected: {command} gets a word that starts with the value of {expr_ref}, and an attacker controls the value on gollum alone; for the name of a wiki page (page_name), GitHub makes the name from the title that the attacker writes and turns each +, < and > of the title into a -, and each blank of the title into a - after trimming the blanks at the head and the end of the title, so that a + at the head of the title makes a - at the head of the name; the word is at a place in the order of the words of {command} where {command} reads a word that starts with - as an option, and the attacker can write at that place an option in the list {options}, which makes {command} run a program or code that is written after the name of the option
  - arguments:
    - {command}: The command and the subcommands of the command, such as tar or git fetch.
    - {expr_ref}: The reference whose value begins the word, such as github.event.pull_request.title.
    - {options}: The options of the command that run a program, as the attacker writes the options: for one word that holds both the option and the program, a long option with = (--to-command=) or a short option followed by the program in the same word (-e&lt;script>); for two words, the option and then the program, a short option as a word by itself (-c).
  - consequence: the attacker makes the attacker's value start with the name of one of the options that the finding names, followed by a program; the command reads the word as the option whose name starts the word, and runs the program in the step, with whatever the step can reach, such as the secrets and the token in its env, the credentials actions/checkout leaves in .git/config, the network, and sudo on a GitHub-hosted runner
  - remedy: A variable of env and double quotes ("\$X") stop the shell from running the value as code, but the variable and the quotes do not stop the command from reading the value as an option. In either fix below, keep the value in the variable of env, and pass the variable to the command inside double quotes. Then either put the word that ends the command's options (--; --end-of-options for git) after the last option the command needs and before the value, for example right before the value (tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt -- "\$X"), so that the command reads every word after that word as a plain argument; or, before the command, end the step with an error when the value starts with -, such as &#91;&#91; \$X != -\* ]] || exit 1 for the variable X that holds the value. The shell check &#91;&#91; \$X != -\* ]] works only when the command gets the value inside double quotes: when the command gets the value outside quotes, a blank in the value starts a new word, and the new word can start with -. For make, -- is not enough: make reads a word of the form NAME=value as the assignment of a variable even after --, so for make end the step with an error when the value starts with - or contains =, such as &#91;&#91; \$X != -\* && \$X != \*=\* ]] || exit 1
  - severity: critical (found from the CVSS metrics below by the table)
  - fact kinds: repo.wiki-open (provider: repo-setting)
  - attackers: wiki-editor
  - preconditions: option-anywhere, option-runs-program, attacker-dash, attacker-event, callers-events, wiki-open
  - true positives:
    - wiki.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on gollum, a step extracts an archive and passes the name of
      #   the wiki page (page_name) to tar after the file names, through env and
      #   inside quotes.
      # reason: anyone may edit the wiki when the wiki is open to all
      #   (repo.wiki-open true). For a page made on the web interface, GitHub makes
      #   the name of the page from the title, turns each +, < and > of the title
      #   into a -, and turns each blank of the title into a - after trimming the
      ```
