      ```yaml
      #   blanks at the head and the end of the title, so the editor of the wiki
      #   makes the name begin with -, and tar reads a word that begins with - as an
      #   option even after the file names of tar. Double quotes keep the name as
      #   one word but do not stop tar from reading the word as an option. The title
      #   ++to+command=id makes the name --to-command=id.
      # attack-value: github.event.pages[0].page_name = "--to-command=id"
      # attack-run-behavior: tar reads the word as --to-command and runs id for
      #   each file that tar extracts, in the step, with what the step can reach.
      on: gollum
      jobs:
        unpack:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                PAGE: ${{ github.event.pages[0].page_name }}
              run: tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt "$PAGE"
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - wiki.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on gollum, a step extracts an archive and passes the name of
      #   the wiki page (page_name) to tar after --, through env and inside
      #   quotes.
      # reason: tar reads every word after -- as the name of a file, so a name of
      #   the page that begins with - is not an option of tar. The title
      #   ++to+command=id makes the name --to-command=id.
      # attack-value: github.event.pages[0].page_name = "--to-command=id"
      # attack-run-behavior: tar looks for a file named --to-command=id in the
      #   archive and runs no program.
      on: gollum
      jobs:
        unpack:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                PAGE: ${{ github.event.pages[0].page_name }}
              run: tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt -- "$PAGE"
      ```

### undetected forms

- wiki-summary: the summary of a wiki page (github.event.pages&#91;\*].summary) in a job that runs on gollum: the rule reads the summary as a value that nobody writes. The gollum payloads that the authors of the linter saw had a null summary each time: for pages made and edited on the web interface of GitHub and pushed by git, an edit message on the web interface and a commit message of git did not go into the summary. The authors saw only pages that the owner of a public repository made and edited, and did not try an edit by an account with no role in the repository
  - finding kinds: argument-injection.option, argument-injection.wiki
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: wiki-summary.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on gollum, a step extracts an archive and passes the summary of
    #   the wiki page to tar after the file names, through env and inside
    #   quotes.
    # reason: a limitation (run time): GitHub decides the summary of a wiki page
    #   when the event happens. The gollum payloads that the authors of the
    #   linter saw had a null summary each time, for pages made and edited on
    #   the web interface and pushed by git; an edit by an account with no role
    #   in the repository was not tried.
    # cause: the rule reads the summary of a wiki page as a value that nobody
    #   writes.
    # attack-value: github.event.pages[0].summary = "--to-command=id"
    # attack-run-behavior: if GitHub ever put a summary that the editor of the
    #   wiki writes in the payload, a summary that begins with --to-command=
    #   would make tar run a program.
    on: gollum
    jobs:
      unpack:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              SUMMARY: ${{ github.event.pages[0].summary }}
            run: tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt "$SUMMARY"
    ```
- fork-review: a job on pull_request_review or pull_request_review_comment that runs only for a pull request from a fork, such as a job whose if: condition is github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name != github.repository: the run of a review that the attacker writes on the pull request of another person from a fork has the secrets of the repository or a token that writes only where a private repository gives secrets or a token that writes to the runs of pull requests from forks (repo.fork-pr-secrets, repo.fork-pr-write-tokens). The rule does not read the facts repo.fork-pr-secrets and repo.fork-pr-write-tokens for the runs of a review, and does not count the run of a review of a pull request from a fork as a run of the attacker. When the attacker opened the pull request from a fork, a review of that pull request gives the attacker nothing more than the pull request itself gives: the run takes the workflow of the merge commit of the pull request (GitHub's documentation gives refs/pull/&lt;n>/merge as the ref of the run of a review), and the attacker can change that workflow in the pull request
  - finding kinds: argument-injection.option, argument-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: fork-review.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on comments on the diff, a step passes the comment's body to
    #   tar as the last argument, in a job that runs only for a pull request
    #   from a fork.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the job runs only for a pull request from a
    #   fork. Where a private repository gives secrets or a token that writes
    #   to the runs of pull requests from forks, the run of a review that the
    #   attacker writes on the pull request of another person from a fork has
    #   those secrets or that token, and the job runs for the attacker.
    # cause: the rule does not read the settings of a private repository for
    #   the runs of pull requests from forks, and does not count the run of a
    #   review of a pull request from a fork as a run of the attacker.
    # attack-value: github.event.comment.body = "--to-command=echo PWNED"
    # attack-run-behavior: the comment of the attacker on the diff of the pull
    #   request of another person from a fork starts the job a; tar reads the
    #   value as the option --to-command, and runs echo PWNED for each file
    #   that tar extracts.
    on: pull_request_review_comment
    jobs:
      a:
        if: github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name != github.repository
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              B: ${{ github.event.comment.body }}
            run: tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt "$B"
    ```
- program-argument: a value in an argument the command reads as a program of its own: the script of sed (with its e command), the program of awk; what CodeQL's argument injection reports
  - finding kinds: argument-injection.option, argument-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: program-argument.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issue_comment, a step puts the comment's body into the
    #   script of sed, through env and inside quotes. This is the example of the
    #   help of CodeQL's query of argument injection
    #   (https://github.com/github/codeql/blob/35510a53689cb54aa6fc664b169b1e44920fb88e/actions/ql/src/experimental/Security/CWE-088/ArgumentInjectionCritical.md).
    # reason: a todo (the same file): sed reads its first word that is not an
    #   option as its script, and the e command of GNU sed's script runs a
    #   command; reading the value inside the script of sed (or the program of
    #   awk) would find it.
    # cause: the rule reads a value only where the command can read it as an
    #   option: at the head of a word, or outside quotes, where a blank in it
    #   starts a new word. Here the value is inside quotes, after
    #   s/BODY_PLACEHOLDER/ in the word of the script.
    # attack-value: github.event.comment.body = "BAR/g;1e echo PWNED;#"
    # attack-run-behavior: the script becomes s/BODY_PLACEHOLDER/BAR/g;1e echo
    #   PWNED;#/g, and sed runs echo PWNED as the e command at the first line,
    #   which writes PWNED into replaced.txt.
    on: issue_comment

    jobs:
      echo-body:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              BODY: ${{ github.event.comment.body }}
            run: |
              cat file.txt | sed  "s/BODY_PLACEHOLDER/$BODY/g" > replaced.txt
    ```
  - example: program-argument.ghsl-2026-229.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, the step prev puts the output prefix of
    #   the step version, through env and inside quotes, into the pattern of grep
    #   and into the program of sed (s#^${PREFIX}#v#). The step version writes the
    #   output from the version in the file version.json of the head commit of the
    #   pull request. These are the steps of the reusable workflow
    #   release-check.yml of ipdxco/unified-github-workflows (commit
    #   e08e90c46d931f457e5d8e292ffa988c0c0b5b70, lines 68-103 and 154-184),
    #   written in the calling workflow.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the e flag of the s command of GNU sed runs
    #   a command; reading the value inside the program of sed would find it.
    # cause: the rule reads a value only where the command can read the value as
    #   an option: at the head of a word, or outside quotes, where a blank in the
    #   value starts a new word. In this example, the value is inside quotes,
    #   after s#^ in the word of the program of sed.
    # attack-value: the output prefix of the step version = "v\\|.*#id>/dev/stderr#e;#"
    # attack-run-behavior: grep keeps each tag that starts with v, and sed runs
    #   the program s#^v\|.*#id>/dev/stderr#e;##v#, whose e flag runs id for each
    #   of those tags.
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2026-229_ipdxco_unified-github-workflows/
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        paths: [ "version.json" ]
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
    jobs:
      release-check:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v5
          - id: version
            env:
              HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
            run: |
              prefix="v"
              echo "prefix=$prefix" | tee -a $GITHUB_OUTPUT
              git fetch origin "$HEAD_SHA"
              git checkout "$HEAD_SHA" -- version.json
              version="$(yq -r '.version | select(type == "!!str")' version.json)"
              git checkout HEAD -- version.json
              version="${version#v}"
              echo "version=$version" | tee -a $GITHUB_OUTPUT
              echo "tag=${prefix}${version}" | tee -a $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          - id: prev
            env:
              PREFIX: ${{ steps.version.outputs.prefix }}
            run: |
              git fetch origin --tags
              vs=$(git tag | grep "^${PREFIX}" | sed "s#^${PREFIX}#v#" | paste -sd , -)
              echo "vs=$vs"
    ```
- other-option: an option not seen to run a program that does other harm: a file it writes (curl -o, git diff --output), files it deletes (find -delete), refs it overwrites (git push --mirror), and --receive-pack of git push and --exec of git archive, which were not seen to run
  - finding kinds: argument-injection.option, argument-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: other-option.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a step diffs the work tree and passes
    #   the name of the pull request's head branch to git diff, through env and
    #   inside quotes.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): git diff reads a word that begins with -
    #   as an option, and its option --output writes the diff to the file named
    #   in it, over what is there; declaring options that do harm other than
    #   running a program would find it.
    # cause: the rule reports only an option seen to run a program, and the
    #   table of commands declares none for git diff.
    # attack-value: github.head_ref = "--output=scripts/build.sh"
    # attack-run-behavior: git diff reads the word as --output and writes the
    #   diff into scripts/build.sh in place of the script, which a later step
    #   that runs it then runs as it is.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      diff:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              HEAD_REF: ${{ github.head_ref }}
            run: git diff "$HEAD_REF"
    ```
- other-command: a command the table of commands does not have, or one with no option that runs a program
  - finding kinds: argument-injection.option, argument-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: other-command.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a step runs awk with the program in
    #   count.awk and passes the pull request's title to it as the file to read,
    #   through env and inside quotes.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): gawk reads options up to its first word
    #   that is not one, so a title that begins with - is an option, and its
    #   option --source adds program text, where system() runs a command; an
    #   entry of awk in the table of commands would find it.
    # cause: awk is not in the table of commands, so the rule does not know
    #   which of its words it reads as options, nor that one runs a program.
    # attack-value: github.event.pull_request.title = "--source=BEGIN { system(\"echo PWNED\") }"
    # attack-run-behavior: gawk reads the word as --source, adds its text to
    #   the program of count.awk, and runs system("echo PWNED") before it reads
    #   any input, which prints PWNED.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      count:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
            run: awk -f count.awk "$TITLE"
    ```
- shell-derived: a value the script makes: an assignment, \$( ), a function's argument (\$1), standard input, xargs
  - finding kinds: argument-injection.option, argument-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: shell-derived.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a step takes the parts in brackets of
    #   the pull request's title into message with $( ), as the step "get
    #   message" of Azure/azure-cli's .github/workflows/AddPRComment.yml does
    #   (https://github.com/Azure/azure-cli/blob/ea42584eda8f5b658d4d7daf42656c1292eeba24/.github/workflows/AddPRComment.yml,
    #   GHSL-2024-294,
    #   https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-294_Azure-cli/),
    #   and then passes message to tar after the file names. The line of tar
    #   is added here: the advisory put -a into [ -z $message ], an operator of
    #   test that runs no program, to pass the check on its way to a line
    #   break in $GITHUB_ENV.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): message holds the attacker's text, and
    #   following a value through what the script makes of it would find it.
    # cause: the rule reads a value through ${{ }} and through the variables of
    #   the workflow's env; message is one the script sets from $( ).
    # attack-value: github.event.pull_request.title = "[--to-command=echo PWNED]"
    # attack-run-behavior: grep -oP takes [--to-command=echo PWNED] out of the
    #   title and sed takes away the brackets, so message is --to-command=echo
    #   PWNED; [ -z $message ] fails with an error and the step goes on, and tar
    #   reads "$message" as --to-command and runs echo PWNED for notes.txt as it
    #   extracts it, which prints PWNED.
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-294_Azure-cli/
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [opened]
        branches:
          - dev
          - release

    permissions:
      pull-requests: write

    jobs:
      thank-user:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        name: Say thanks for the PR
        steps:
          - name: get message
            env:
              TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
            run: |
              message=$(echo "$TITLE" | grep -oP '[{\[][^}\]]+[}\]]' | sed 's/{\|}\|\[\|\]//g')
              echo "message=$message" >> $GITHUB_ENV
              if [ -z $message ]; then
                  echo "message=$(echo 'Thank you for your contribution! We will review the pull request and get back to you soon.')" >> $GITHUB_ENV
              fi
              tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt "$message"
    ```
- env-file-variable: a variable a step before sets through \$GITHUB_ENV: the rule reads the variables of the workflow's env
  - finding kinds: argument-injection.option, argument-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: env-file-variable.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a step writes the name of the pull
    #   request's head branch to $GITHUB_ENV as BRANCH, and the next step passes
    #   $BRANCH to tar after the file names, inside quotes.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): BRANCH holds the branch's name in the
    #   steps after the first, and reading what a step writes to $GITHUB_ENV
    #   would find it.
    # cause: the rule reads the variables of the workflow's env (workflow, job
    #   and step); BRANCH is set by a step at run time.
    # attack-value: github.head_ref = "--to-command=echo${IFS}PWNED"
    # attack-run-behavior: the runner sets BRANCH to the value in the second
    #   step, and tar reads "$BRANCH" as --to-command and runs echo${IFS}PWNED
    #   through the shell for notes.txt as it extracts it, which prints PWNED.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      unpack:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              HEAD_REF: ${{ github.head_ref }}
            run: echo "BRANCH=$HEAD_REF" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          - run: tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt "$BRANCH"
    ```
- empty-prefix: a value after another expansion in the same word that may be empty ("\${P}\$X"), or after a word whose text is not known that may be empty or an option (\$OPTS "\$X")
  - finding kinds: argument-injection.option, argument-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: empty-prefix.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a step passes to tar, after the file
    #   names, a word of the variable ARCHIVE_PREFIX followed by the pull
    #   request's title, through env and inside quotes.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the variable ARCHIVE_PREFIX may be unset,
    #   and then the word begins with the title; reading whether what is before
    #   the value may be empty would find it.
    # cause: the rule reads a value inside quotes only at the head of its word,
    #   and here ${PREFIX} is before it.
    # attack-value: github.event.pull_request.title = "--to-command=echo PWNED"
    # attack-run-behavior: with the variable ARCHIVE_PREFIX unset, PREFIX is
    #   empty, so tar gets the word --to-command=echo PWNED, reads it as
    #   --to-command, and runs echo PWNED for notes.txt as it extracts it, which
    #   prints PWNED.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      unpack:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              PREFIX: ${{ vars.ARCHIVE_PREFIX }}
              TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
            run: tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt "${PREFIX}$TITLE"
    ```
- param-operator: a variable with an operator that changes its value (\${X#prefix}, \${X/a/b})
  - finding kinds: argument-injection.option, argument-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: param-operator.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a step passes the pull request's title
    #   with a leading v taken away, "${TITLE#v}", to tar after the file names,
    #   through env and inside quotes.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): ${TITLE#v} is the title itself when it
    #   does not begin with v, and reading what the operator leaves would find
    #   it.
    # cause: the rule reads a variable only bare or with an operator that keeps
    #   its value (${TITLE:-x}); # changes the value, so it does not read it.
    # attack-value: github.event.pull_request.title = "--to-command=echo PWNED"
    # attack-run-behavior: the title does not begin with v, so the word is the
    #   title as it is; tar reads it as --to-command and runs echo PWNED for
    #   notes.txt as it extracts it, which prints PWNED.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      unpack:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
            run: tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt "${TITLE#v}"
    ```
- command-word: a value that is the command's name (\$CMD args), or an argument of a wrapper whose words are not known (env A="\$X" tar)
  - finding kinds: argument-injection.option, argument-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: command-word.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issue_comment, a step runs the comment's body, through env
    #   and outside quotes, as the command to which it passes -xf archive.tar
    #   notes.txt.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the attacker names the command and puts
    #   its options before the script's words; reading the value at the place
    #   of the command's name would find it.
    # cause: the rule reads the words of a command it knows by its name, and
    #   the name here is a value not known until run time.
    # attack-value: github.event.comment.body = "tar --to-command=echo${IFS}PWNED"
    # attack-run-behavior: bash splits the value at the blank, so the command
    #   is tar --to-command=echo${IFS}PWNED -xf archive.tar notes.txt; tar runs
    #   echo${IFS}PWNED through the shell for notes.txt as it extracts it, which
    #   prints PWNED.
    on: issue_comment
    jobs:
      run:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              TOOL: ${{ github.event.comment.body }}
            run: $TOOL -xf archive.tar notes.txt
    ```
- unwalked-place: a command in a place the rule does not walk: \$( ) in the words of case
  - finding kinds: argument-injection.option, argument-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: unwalked-place.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a step extracts from an archive the
    #   members that match the pull request's title with tar -xv inside $( ) in
    #   the word of case, passing the title through env and inside quotes, and
    #   prints a line when tar lists a member.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the tar in $( ) runs as a command, and
    #   walking the word of case would find the tar.
    # cause: the rule walks the commands of the script and their $( ), but not $(
    #   ) in the words of case.
    # attack-value: github.event.pull_request.title = "--to-command=echo PWNED"
    # attack-run-behavior: tar in $( ) reads the title as --to-command and runs
    #   echo PWNED for each member it extracts.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      unpack:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
            run: |
              case "$(tar -xvf archive.tar "$TITLE")" in
                ?*) echo "extracted" ;;
              esac
    ```
- unread-command: a command in a part of the script that the parser of the script does not read: the commands of each clause of case, \$( ) inside the ( ) of the assignment of an array, and the code that another shell reads from the argument of -c (bash -c '...')
  - finding kinds: argument-injection.option, argument-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: unread-command.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a step extracts an archive inside a
    #   clause of case and passes the pull request's title to tar after the
    #   file names, through env and inside quotes.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the tar in the clause runs as any other
    #   command does, and walking the commands of each clause of case would
    #   find the tar.
    # cause: the parser of the script finds the case statement but does not
    #   read the commands in the clauses of the case statement.
    # attack-value: github.event.pull_request.title = "--to-command=echo PWNED"
    # attack-run-behavior: the clause a) runs, and tar reads the title as
    #   --to-command and runs echo PWNED for notes.txt as tar extracts it,
    #   which prints PWNED.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      unpack:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
            run: |
              case a in
                a) tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt "$TITLE" ;;
              esac
    ```
- rewritten-url: an HTTPS URL that git rewrites to a local path or to an SSH remote by the setting url.&lt;base>.insteadOf (git config): the rule takes the URL as written in the script, without the git config commands that run earlier in the script, and reports nothing for an HTTPS remote
  - finding kinds: argument-injection.option, argument-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: rewritten-url.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a step sets git to rewrite an HTTPS
    #   URL to the local path /tmp/r, and fetches from that URL with the name of
    #   the pull request's head branch after the URL, through env and inside
    #   quotes.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): git fetch reads the word as --upload-pack,
    #   and git rewrites the URL to /tmp/r by url./tmp/r.insteadOf (the key
    #   url.<base>.insteadOf with /tmp/r as the base), so git runs the program
    #   given as the value of --upload-pack on the runner; reading the git config of
    #   the script would find it.
    # cause: the rule takes the URL as written in the script, without the git
    #   config commands that run earlier in the script, and reports nothing for
    #   an HTTPS remote, where git does not use the program.
    # attack-value: github.head_ref = "--upload-pack=echo${IFS}PWNED>&2;false"
    # attack-run-behavior: git fetches from /tmp/r in place of the URL and runs
    #   echo${IFS}PWNED>&2;false through the shell: the shell expands ${IFS}
    #   to a blank and prints PWNED, and the fetch then fails.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      fetch:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              HEAD_REF: ${{ github.head_ref }}
            run: |
              git config --global url./tmp/r.insteadOf https://example.com/r
              git fetch https://example.com/r "$HEAD_REF"
    ```
- make-variable: a value passed to make in a word of the form NAME=value, where the word need not start with -: make reads such a word as the assignment of a variable even after --, and the value of the variable can change a command that a rule of the makefile runs (CC=...)
  - finding kinds: argument-injection.option, argument-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: make-variable.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a step runs make all and passes the
    #   pull request's title to make after --, through env and inside quotes.
    #   The makefile runs $(CC) --version in the rule all.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): -- stops make from reading the title as
    #   an option, but make reads a word of the form NAME=value as the
    #   assignment of a variable even after --. The title CC=<a command> makes
    #   the recipe of the rule all run that command.
    # cause: the rule reads a value only where the command can read the value
    #   as an option, and after -- no word is an option.
    # attack-value: github.event.pull_request.title = "CC=sh -c \"echo PWNED\" #"
    # attack-run-behavior: make assigns sh -c "echo PWNED" # to CC, and the
    #   recipe of the rule all runs sh -c "echo PWNED", which prints PWNED; the
    #   # makes the rest of the line a comment of the shell.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
            run: make all -- "$TITLE"
    ```
- dash-login: the label (owner:branch) of the head of a pull request, or the full name (owner/name) of a repository, where the login of the owner begins with -: when the authors of the linter tried on 2026-11-01, GitHub refused a login that begins with - at sign-up and at a rename, but accounts with such a login remain from earlier, and the rule assumes that the label and the full name do not begin with -. On 2026-11-01 the user search of GitHub found 9 accounts whose login begins with -, all made in 2009: the 36 searches for - followed by a letter or a digit (gh api 'search/users?q=%22-a%22+in:login' for -a, and the same search for -b to -z and for -0 to -9) found 8 accounts in all, and the search gh api 'search/users?q=%22-%22+in:login' for - alone found 1 more account, the account whose login is - (a search word of two or more characters matches the start of a login, and a search word of one character matches the whole login). The 9 accounts are users. When the authors of the linter tried on 2026-11-01 to create an organization whose name begins with - on the web, GitHub removed the leading - from the login of the organization; the creation of an organization through the API was not tried
  - finding kinds: argument-injection.option, argument-injection.wiki
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: dash-login.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a step extracts an archive and passes
    #   the label of the pull request's head (owner:branch) to tar after the
    #   file names, through env and inside quotes.
    # reason: a limitation (run time): the account that opens the pull request
    #   decides the label when the event happens. A few accounts made in 2009
    #   have a login that begins with -, and the label of a pull request from
    #   one of the accounts begins with -.
    # cause: the rule assumes that the label does not begin with -, because
    #   the label begins with a login.
    # attack-value: github.event.pull_request.head.label = "-x:main"
    # attack-run-behavior: tar reads the letters after - as short options one
    #   by one, so the letters of the login decide which options tar reads, and
    #   the harm depends on those letters. With -x:main, tar takes -x and stops
    #   at : with "invalid option -- ':'". None of the 9 logins found begins
    #   with -I or -F, the short options of tar that run a program; with another
    #   command, the same letters can be an option that runs code, such as -c of
    #   python3.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      unpack:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              LABEL: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.label }}
            run: tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt "$LABEL"
    ```
- written-label: the label (owner:branch) of the head of a pull request written into the script with \${{ }} (tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt \${{ github.event.pull_request.head.label }}): the runner writes the label into the script before the shell reads the script, and the attacker can write \${IFS} in the name of the branch, so, when the label is outside quotes, a word after the first word of the label can begin with -. The rule code-injection of this linter reports the same \${{ }}, and the fix of code-injection, which moves the label to a variable of env inside double quotes, passes the label as one word, owner:branch, which begins with the login. The attacker can also write \$( ) in the name of the branch; in the script written with \${{ }}, the shell runs that \$( ) even inside double quotes ("\${{ ... }}"), so the attacker already writes code that the shell runs, and a word that the command reads as an option gives the attacker nothing more. Through a variable of env inside double quotes, the shell does not split the label, so the label stays one word that begins with the login. Through a variable of env outside quotes, the shell splits the label at the characters of IFS, which are blanks by default, and the name of a branch holds no blank, so the label also stays one word (a script that changes IFS is the undetected form changed-ifs). The full name holds no \$, no quote and no blank, so the full name written with \${{ }} is also one word that begins with the login
  - finding kinds: argument-injection.option, argument-injection.wiki
  - disposition: other-rule (rule: code-injection)
  - example: written-label.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a step extracts an archive and passes
    #   the label of the pull request's head (owner:branch) to tar after the
    #   file names, written into the script with ${{ }} and outside quotes.
    # reason: another rule's: code-injection reports the same ${{ }}. The
    #   attacker writes ${IFS} in the name of the branch, so the shell splits
    #   the label into words, and a word after the first word begins with -.
    #   The attacker can also write $( ) in the name of the branch and run code
    #   without an option.
    # cause: the rule reads the label as one word that begins with the login,
    #   and does not read the words after the shell splits the label.
    # attack-value: github.event.pull_request.head.label = "attacker:x${IFS}--to-command=id"
    # attack-run-behavior: the shell splits the label into attacker:x and
    #   --to-command=id; tar reads --to-command=id as an option and, while tar
    #   extracts notes.txt, runs id with the content of notes.txt as the input
    #   of id, and id prints the user and the groups of the runner.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      unpack:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.label }}
    ```
- changed-ifs: a value outside quotes in a script that sets IFS (IFS=:): the shell splits a value outside quotes at the characters of IFS, so a part of the value after the first part can begin with -, such as the name of the branch in the label (owner:branch) of the head of a pull request with IFS=:, or the name of the repository in a full name (owner/name) with IFS=/. The rule assumes that the shell splits a value outside quotes at blanks only, and the rule does not read an assignment to IFS in the script
  - finding kinds: argument-injection.option, argument-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: changed-ifs.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a step sets IFS to : and passes the
    #   label of the pull request's head (owner:branch) to tar after the file
    #   names, through env and outside quotes.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the shell splits a value outside quotes
    #   at the characters of IFS, so with IFS=: the shell splits the label into
    #   the login and the name of the branch, and the name of the branch can
    #   begin with -.
    # cause: the rule assumes that the shell splits a value outside quotes at
    #   blanks only, and does not read an assignment to IFS in the script.
    # attack-value: github.event.pull_request.head.label = "attacker:--to-command=id"
    # attack-run-behavior: the shell splits the label into attacker and
    #   --to-command=id; tar reads --to-command=id as an option and, while tar
    #   extracts notes.txt, runs id with the content of notes.txt as the input
    #   of id, and id prints the user and the groups of the runner.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      unpack:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              LABEL: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.label }}
            run: |
              IFS=:
              tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt $LABEL
    ```
- other-shell: a run of pwsh, cmd or python, and a run whose shell the rule cannot determine to be bash or sh: a shell: value whose command is not bash or sh, such as pwsh -File {0}; a shell: value of bash or sh with an option that the rule does not read, such as bash -c 'make' {0}, bash -v {0} or bash -O extglob {0}; a shell: value that names bash or sh by a path, such as /usr/bin/bash -e {0}, on a runner where the rule does not know that the path exists (any runner other than one whose runs-on is a single label that starts with ubuntu-, or with macos- for /bin/bash and /bin/sh) or in a step of a composite action; a shell: that is an expression; or a step without shell: whose job and workflow have no defaults.run.shell and whose job has a runs-on that is not a single label that starts with ubuntu-, macos- or windows-, such as self-hosted or an expression: the rule reads the runs of bash and sh only
  - finding kinds: argument-injection.option, argument-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: other-shell.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, a run of pwsh passes the issue's title to tar after
    #   the file names, through env.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): reading pwsh would find it.
    # cause: the rule reads runs of bash and sh only.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "--to-command=echo PWNED"
    # attack-run-behavior: pwsh passes "$env:TITLE" to tar as one word, and tar
    #   reads it as --to-command and runs echo PWNED for notes.txt as it
    #   extracts it, which prints PWNED.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - shell: pwsh
            env:
              TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
            run: tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt "$env:TITLE"
    ```
- pull-request: a job that runs only on pull_request, in one of two cases. In the first case, only the pull requests of the repository run the workflow: the author of a pull request can change the workflow itself, so the run of the job gives the author what the run has (read-only from a fork, or what a private repository sends to the runs of pull requests from forks: secrets, a token that writes) without the flaw of the rule, and the flaw of the rule adds nothing to what the author gets. In the second case, a ruleset of the organization or the enterprise runs the workflow on the pull requests of its other repositories (Require workflows to pass before merging, of GitHub Enterprise): the author of such a pull request cannot change the workflow, and whether the run has more than the pull_request workflow of the author would get (the token, secrets) is known from GitHub's documentation only, as no such run was observed; making a required check pass is outside the threat model of the rule. The workflow does not say which case holds, and the rule does not read which case holds
  - finding kinds: argument-injection.option, argument-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: pull-request.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request, a step passes the pull request's title and
    #   github.head_ref to tar after the file names, through env and inside
    #   quotes.
    # reason: when only the pull requests of the repository run the workflow, the
    #   author of the pull request can change the workflow itself and gets what the
    #   run has without the flaw, so the flaw adds nothing to what the author gets;
    #   when a ruleset of the organization or the enterprise runs the workflow on
    #   the pull requests of its other repositories, the author cannot change the
    #   workflow, and what the run of the ruleset has beyond the author's own
    #   pull_request workflow is not known. The workflow does not say which case
    #   holds.
    # cause: pull_request is none of the attacker's events the rule reads. The
    #   rule does not read whether a ruleset runs the workflow.
    # attack-value: github.head_ref = "--to-command=echo${IFS}PWNED"
    # attack-run-behavior: the branch name of the pull request is the value, so
    #   tar reads "$HEAD_REF" as --to-command and runs echo${IFS}PWNED through the
    #   shell for notes.txt as it extracts it, which prints PWNED. When a ruleset of
    #   the organization runs the workflow on a pull request of another repository,
    #   the same steps run in the run of the ruleset; what the run of the ruleset
    #   has was not observed, so whether the steps do harm in the run of the ruleset
    #   is not known.
    on: pull_request
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
              HEAD_REF: ${{ github.head_ref }}
            run: tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt "$TITLE" "$HEAD_REF"
    ```
- dispatch: a value of the event of workflow_dispatch other than its inputs, in a job that runs only on workflow_dispatch: the event has the ref, which is a branch or a tag that the repository already has, and values that GitHub fills, such as the login of the account that dispatches the workflow; the event has no text of an issue, a comment or a pull request. Whoever dispatches the workflow chooses the ref and the inputs of the dispatch, and nothing else of the event. A token that cannot change the files of the repository can dispatch the workflow, such as a fine-grained token that has the permission Actions with write access and no permission Contents. The rule reports an input of the dispatch with the inconclusive kind input-dispatch
  - finding kinds: argument-injection.option, argument-injection.wiki
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: dispatch.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on workflow_dispatch, a step passes the title of the issue to
    #   tar after the file names, by ${{ }} inside quotes. If the workflow also
    #   ran on issues, the rule would report the same step.
    # reason: no added gain: on workflow_dispatch the event has no issue object,
    #   so the expression of the title gives an empty string; whoever dispatches
    #   the workflow chooses the ref and the inputs of the dispatch, and the step
    #   reads no input of the dispatch.
    # cause: the table of the attacker's events that the rule reads does not
    #   have workflow_dispatch; the rule reports an input of a dispatch with the
    #   inconclusive kind input-dispatch.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "--to-command=echo PWNED"
    # attack-run-behavior: with the value put in, tar reads the word as
    #   --to-command and runs echo PWNED for notes.txt as it extracts it, which
    #   prints PWNED. On workflow_dispatch the event has no issue object,
    #   though: the expression gives an empty string, and tar gets an empty file
    #   name.
    on: workflow_dispatch
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt "${{ github.event.issue.title }}"
    ```
- repository-dispatch: a value of the client_payload of repository_dispatch (github.event.client_payload): only a credential with write access to the permission Contents of the repository can send repository_dispatch, and the credential premise assumes that no attacker holds such a credential; the sender chooses the whole client_payload
  - finding kinds: argument-injection.option, argument-injection.wiki
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: repository-dispatch.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on repository_dispatch, a step passes the value title of the
    #   client_payload to tar after the file names, by ${{ }} inside quotes.
    # reason: the form adds nothing to what the attacker gets (the disposition
    #   no-added-gain): only a credential with write access to the permission
    #   Contents of the repository can send repository_dispatch, and the
    #   credential premise assumes that no attacker holds such a credential; the
    #   sender chooses the whole client_payload.
    # cause: the table of the attacker's events that the rule reads leaves out
    #   repository_dispatch on purpose: the credential premise leaves the sender
    #   of repository_dispatch out of the threat model.
    # attack-value: github.event.client_payload.title = "--to-command=echo PWNED"
    # attack-run-behavior: when a repository_dispatch with the value in its
    #   client_payload runs the workflow, tar reads the word as --to-command and
    #   runs echo PWNED for notes.txt as it extracts the file, which prints PWNED.
    on: repository_dispatch
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt "${{ github.event.client_payload.title }}"
    ```
- app-written: a value that an app outside GitHub Actions writes into a field of a commit status or a check run (the fields context, description and target_url of status; the fields name, output, details_url and external_id of check_run): the app may copy a value of a pull request from a fork into the field, such as the name of a job that a configuration file of the pull request gives to an outside CI; the rule reads the field as a field whose value the app chooses
  - finding kinds: argument-injection.option, argument-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: app-written.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on check_run, which an app outside GitHub Actions starts when
    #   the app makes a check run for a commit, the job writes the name of the
    #   check run (github.event.check_run.name) where the rule reads it.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the app writes the name of the check run, and an
    #   app may copy a value of a pull request from a fork into the name, such
    #   as the name of a job that a configuration file of the pull request gives
    #   to an outside CI.
    # cause: the table of what an attacker controls reads the values that the
    #   app writes into a commit status or a check run as the values that the
    #   app chooses.
    # attack-value: github.event.check_run.name = "--to-command=echo PWNED"
    # attack-run-behavior: an outside CI copies the name of a job from the
    #   configuration file of the pull request from a fork into the name of the
    #   check run; the run of check_run starts on the default branch, and the
    #   value does there what the attack value of the message of the commit does
    #   on status.
    on: check_run
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt "${{ github.event.check_run.name }}"
    ```
- deployment-status: a value of the payload of deployment_status, such as the SHA of the deployment (deployment.sha), when an app outside GitHub Actions makes a deployment and a status of the deployment for a commit of a pull request from a fork: no run of deployment_status started when the authors of the linter tried this, and why the run did not start was not found; the rule does not read deployment_status as an event that an attacker starts
  - finding kinds: argument-injection.option, argument-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: deployment-status.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on deployment_status, which an app outside GitHub Actions
    #   starts when the app makes a status of a deployment, the job writes the
    #   description of the deployment (github.event.deployment.description)
    #   where the rule reads it.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): no run of deployment_status started when a GitHub
    #   App made a deployment and a status of the deployment for a commit of a
    #   pull request from a fork (seen on GitHub), and why the run did not start
    #   was not found.
    # cause: the table of the attacker's events that the rule reads does not
    #   have deployment_status.
    # attack-value: github.event.deployment.description = "--to-command=echo PWNED"
    # attack-run-behavior: an outside app makes a deployment for the commit of
    #   the pull request from a fork with a description that the pull request
    #   gives, and a status of the deployment; if a run of deployment_status
    #   starts on the default branch, the value does there what the attack value
    #   of the message of the commit does on status.
    on: deployment_status
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt "${{ github.event.deployment.description }}"
    ```
- dispatch-relay: a workflow on an event of an attacker that puts a value the attacker writes into the client_payload of a repository_dispatch that the workflow sends (gh api with client_payload to the endpoint dispatches, peter-evans/repository-dispatch), and a workflow on repository_dispatch that uses the value: the flaw is in the workflow that sends the repository_dispatch, and the rule does not read what a workflow sends to another workflow
  - finding kinds: argument-injection.option, argument-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - example: .github/workflows/receiver.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: sender.yml runs on issues opened, and with the GITHUB_TOKEN
    #   sends a repository_dispatch of the type relay whose client_payload has the
    #   title of the issue as the value title; receiver.yml runs on that
    #   repository_dispatch, and a step passes the value title of the
    #   client_payload to tar after the file names, by ${{ }} inside quotes.
    # reason: the author of the issue writes the value, and sender.yml relays
    #   the value to receiver.yml in a repository_dispatch that a run of the
    #   repository sends with a token of the repository; GitHub creates a workflow
    #   run for a repository_dispatch sent with the GITHUB_TOKEN, as an exception
    #   to the rule that an event that the GITHUB_TOKEN triggers creates no
    #   workflow run.
    # cause: the rule reads the events of each workflow alone, and does not read
    #   what a workflow sends to another workflow as the client_payload of a
    #   repository_dispatch.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "--to-command=echo PWNED"
    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens an issue whose title is the value;
    #   sender.yml sends the value, and in the run of receiver.yml tar reads the
    #   word as --to-command and runs echo PWNED for notes.txt as it extracts the
    #   file, which prints PWNED.
    on:
      repository_dispatch:
        types: [relay]
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt "${{ github.event.client_payload.title }}"
    ```
    - .github/workflows/sender.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on:
        issues:
          types: [opened]
      permissions:
        contents: write
      jobs:
        relay:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
                VALUE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
              run: gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/dispatches" -f event_type=relay -f "client_payload[title]=$VALUE"
      ```
- dispatch-input-call: an input of workflow_dispatch that a caller of the same repository passes, as an input of the call (under the key with: of the calling job or step), to a reusable workflow or a composite action, which uses the input as a value: the one who dispatches the caller chooses the value, and the rule reads the events of a called workflow or action from the table of the callers, and does not follow the value of an input of workflow_dispatch that the caller gives
  - finding kinds: argument-injection.option, argument-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - example: .github/workflows/called.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: caller.yml runs on workflow_dispatch with the input x, and
    #   calls called.yml with the input x of the dispatch as the input x of
    #   called.yml; called.yml passes the input x to tar after the file names, by
    #   ${{ }} inside quotes.
    # reason: the one who dispatches caller.yml chooses the value:
    #   input-dispatch reports such a value where a workflow on workflow_dispatch
    #   refers to its input directly, but through the call the value is the input
    #   x of called.yml.
    # cause: the rule reads the events of a called workflow from the table of
    #   the callers, and does not follow the value of an input of
    #   workflow_dispatch that a caller gives in with.
    # attack-value: inputs.x = "--to-command=echo PWNED"
    # attack-run-behavior: when the one who dispatches caller.yml gives the
    #   value as x, tar reads the word as --to-command and runs echo PWNED for
    #   notes.txt as it extracts the file, which prints PWNED.
    on:
      workflow_call:
        inputs:
          x: {type: string}
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt "${{ inputs.x }}"
    ```
    - .github/workflows/caller.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on:
        workflow_dispatch:
          inputs:
            x: {type: string}
      jobs:
        call:
          uses: ./.github/workflows/called.yml
          with:
            x: ${{ inputs.x }}
          secrets: inherit
      ```
- outside-caller: a reusable workflow or composite action that callers in the repository decide, called from another repository on an event, or with a value, an attacker controls: the caller's run has the caller's token and secrets, not the repository's
  - finding kinds: argument-injection.option, argument-injection.wiki
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: .github/workflows/called.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the workflow is called; a step passes github.event.issue.title
    #   to tar after the file names, through env and inside quotes. Its one
    #   caller in the repository, ci.yml, runs on push.
    # reason: no added gain for this repository: ci.yml calls the workflow on
    #   push alone, and github.event of a push has no issue, so the value that the
    #   run reads is not a value that an attacker wrote. Another repository may
    #   call the workflow on an event whose payload has what an attacker wrote,
    #   but that run has the token and the secrets of the other repository.
    # cause: the rule reads a called workflow on the events of its callers in
    #   the repository, and ci.yml runs on push alone.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "--to-command=echo PWNED"
    # attack-run-behavior: ci.yml calls it on push, whose payload has no issue,
    #   so there TITLE is empty; when a workflow of another repository calls it
    #   on issues, tar reads "$TITLE" as --to-command in that run and runs echo
    #   PWNED for notes.txt as it extracts it, which prints PWNED.
    on:
      workflow_call:
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
            run: tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt "$TITLE"
    ```
    - .github/workflows/ci.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: push
      jobs:
        call:
          uses: ./.github/workflows/called.yml
      ```
- not-attacker: secrets, vars, runner, the outcome of a step, the result of a job. A run of the linter that adds the attacker variables-writer reports a reference of vars where the rule reads the value as written by the attacker, and a run of the linter that adds the attacker secrets-writer reports such a reference of secrets except secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN (--add-attacker); no run reports runner, the outcome of a step or the result of a job
  - finding kinds: argument-injection.option, argument-injection.wiki
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - added attackers: variables-writer, secrets-writer
  - example: not-attacker.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, a step passes secrets, variables, the runner, the
    #   outcome of a step and the result of a job to tar after the file names,
    #   by ${{ }} inside quotes.
    # reason: no added gain: no attacker writes them.
    # cause: the rule reads as what an attacker may write only references to
    #   github (through its table of contexts), env, the outputs of steps and of
    #   jobs needed, inputs and matrix; secrets, vars, runner, steps.<id>.outcome
    #   and needs.<id>.result are none of these, so it reads them as values no
    #   attacker writes.
    # attack-value: vars.NAME = "--to-command=echo PWNED"
    # attack-run-behavior: the variable NAME is set by one who may change the
    #   repository's settings; were it the value, tar would read the word as
    #   --to-command and run echo PWNED for notes.txt as it extracts it.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt "${{ secrets.TOKEN }}" "${{ vars.NAME }}" "${{ runner.os }}" "${{ steps.s.outcome }}" "${{ needs.a.result }}"
    ```
- merged-pusher: a value that the author of a pull request writes in the profile of the account of the author (the profile name, the public email of the profile), in github.event.pull_request.merged_by of a merged pull request, or in github.event.pusher of the push that GitHub makes when GitHub merges a pull request by a rebase, by auto-merge or from a merge queue: the rule reads merged_by and the pusher as the account that merged or pushed, and the account that merged or pushed holds a credential that can merge or push; whether GitHub sets merged_by of a merged pull request, or the pusher of the push that GitHub makes when GitHub merges a pull request by a rebase, by auto-merge or from a merge queue, to the account of the author of the merged pull request was not checked
  - finding kinds: argument-injection.option, argument-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: merged-pusher.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on a pull request that is closed, a step passes the name of the
    #   account that merged the pull request to tar after the file names.
    # reason: whether GitHub sets merged_by of a merged pull request to the
    #   account of the author of the pull request was not checked: no payload with
    #   merged_by was seen on GitHub. Were merged_by the author, the author would
    #   write the name of merged_by, which is the profile name of the account of
    #   the author.
    # cause: the table of what an attacker controls reads merged_by as the
    #   account that merged the pull request, and the account that merged the pull
    #   request holds a credential that can merge.
    # attack-value: github.event.pull_request.merged_by.name = "--to-command=echo PWNED"
    # attack-run-behavior: were merged_by the author of the pull request and the
    #   profile name of the account of the author this value, tar would read the
    #   word as --to-command and run echo PWNED for notes.txt as tar extracts
    #   notes.txt.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [closed]
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              MERGER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.merged_by.name }}
            run: tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt "$MERGER"
    ```
- compared: a context compared, negated, or given to contains, startsWith, endsWith or hashFiles: what is written out is a bool or a hash
  - finding kinds: argument-injection.option, argument-injection.wiki
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: compared.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, a step passes to tar after the file names the
    #   issue's title and body compared, negated, or given to contains,
    #   startsWith, endsWith or hashFiles, by ${{ }} inside quotes.
    # reason: no added gain: what is written out is a bool or a hash.
    # cause: the rule reads the value of such an expression as not the
    #   attacker's text.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "--to-command=echo PWNED"
    # attack-run-behavior: each expression gives true or false, and hashFiles
    #   gives a hash or an empty string, so no word begins with -, and tar takes
    #   them as names of files to extract.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: >-
              tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt "${{ github.event.issue.title == 'x' }}" "${{ !github.event.issue.body }}"
              "${{ contains(github.event.issue.title, 'x') }}" "${{ startsWith(github.event.issue.title, 'x') }}"
              "${{ endsWith(github.event.issue.title, 'x') }}" "${{ hashFiles(github.event.issue.title) }}"
    ```
- new-activity-type: an activity type GitHub added after the schemas the tables are made from, written in types: a value of types the tables do not have is dropped, as GitHub drops one it has no such activity type for
  - finding kinds: argument-injection.option, argument-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: pin-update)
  - example: new-activity-type.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues of an activity type added_later, a step passes the
    #   issue's title to tar after the file names, through env and inside
    #   quotes.
    # reason: a todo (a pin update): an activity type GitHub added after the
    #   pinned schemas is missed until the pins are updated.
    # cause: the analysis drops a value of types it does not know, as GitHub
    #   does for a value it has no such activity type for, so the job has no
    #   attacker's event.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "--to-command=echo PWNED"
    # attack-run-behavior: when GitHub sends issues with the activity type
    #   added_later, tar reads "$TITLE" as --to-command and runs echo PWNED for
    #   notes.txt as it extracts it, which prints PWNED.
    on:
      issues:
        types: [added_later]
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
            run: tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt "$TITLE"
    ```
- insider-association: an if that lets in MEMBER or COLLABORATOR by the author_association of the issue, the pull request or the discussion the run is of, which the following pass: a member or a collaborator whose repository role is Read only, who gets, in the run, a token that writes and the secrets, more than what the Read role gives; the account of such a member or collaborator, taken over; and an outsider who becomes a MEMBER with the Read role, in an organization that lets anyone become a member (a bot that invites whoever asks). A member or a collaborator whose role is Triage or above holds a credential that can add a label or write to the repository, which the credential premise assumes no attacker holds. Who is a member, and with what role, is not in the workflow
  - finding kinds: argument-injection.option, argument-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - added attackers: read-member, triage-account, writer-issues-token, required-reviewer
  - example: insider-association.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues opened, a job whose if lets in an issue whose
    #   author_association is MEMBER passes the issue's title to tar after the
    #   file names, through env and inside quotes.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): a member of the organization, who may have read
    #   access only, passes this if (in an organization that lets anyone become a
    #   member, such as by a bot that invites whoever asks, an outsider becomes such
    #   a member), and gets the job's token and secrets past what the Read role
    #   gives; who is a member, and with what role, is not in the workflow.
    # cause: the rule evaluates the if with the attacker's author_association
    #   (NONE, FIRST_TIMER, FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR or CONTRIBUTOR), for which it
    #   is false, so no attacker's event runs the job.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "--to-command=echo PWNED"
    # attack-run-behavior: the job's if is false for an issue whose
    #   author_association is not MEMBER, and the runner skips the job; for an
    #   issue a member opens, tar reads "$TITLE" as --to-command and runs echo
    #   PWNED for notes.txt as it extracts it, which prints PWNED.
    on:
      issues:
        types: [opened]
    jobs:
      a:
        if: github.event.issue.author_association == 'MEMBER'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
            run: tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt "$TITLE"
    ```
- remote-callee: a job or a step inside a reusable workflow of another repository (uses: owner/repo/.github/workflows/&lt;file>@&lt;ref>) whose content the fact workflow.definition does not give. For every rule: a run that does not ask the fact (a run without --online and without the answer in --facts). For a quality rule, also: a run where the linter asked the fact and got no answer (an answer of unknown: the GitHub API did not give the file), and a call deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact. The rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition. For a rule that is not a quality rule (a rule with a threat), the last two forms are the inconclusive kind remote-callee-unknown, not this form
  - finding kinds: argument-injection.option, argument-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-callee.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
    #   the repository example-org/argument-injection-unanswered, whose content
    #   is the workflow of the true positive option (option.arithmetic.yml) of
    #   the rule, with on: workflow_call in place of the on of
    #   option.arithmetic.yml. The linter has no answer of the fact
    #   workflow.definition for the reusable workflow.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event
    #   that started the run of the calling job, and the linter does not read
    #   the reusable workflow.
    # cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from
    #   the answer of workflow.definition.
    # attack-value: github.head_ref = "--to-command=sh${IFS}-c${IFS}id"
    # attack-run-behavior: tar reads the word as --to-command and runs sh -c id
    #   in the step, with what the step can reach.
    on: pull_request_target
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/argument-injection-unanswered/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

### inconclusive

- remote-program: an option whose program runs on the machine that holds the repository that git reads (--upload-pack of git fetch, clone, pull and ls-remote), where the command names an SSH remote, or no word written in the script (not a variable) before the attacker's value names the repository: for a repository on a local path the program runs on the runner, for an SSH remote the program runs on the remote host, and for an HTTPS remote no program runs. The rule reports a repository on a local path as a finding and reports nothing for an HTTPS remote. When the command names no repository, the repository comes from the settings of the repository at run time (when git fetch reads "\$X" as an option, git fetch names no repository and reads the remote origin). When the attacker's value can hold blanks and is outside quotes, the attacker can write the repository too, and the rule reports a finding. The rule does not decide what a program on the remote host can reach
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: remote-program.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a step fetches and passes the name of
    #   the pull request's head branch to git fetch, through env and inside
    #   quotes, without naming a repository.
    # reason: git fetch reads the word as an option, and the option
    #   --upload-pack names the program that runs on the side of the repository
    #   that git fetches from: on the runner for a repository on a local path,
    #   on the remote host for an SSH remote, and nowhere for an HTTPS remote.
    #   The command names no repository, so git fetch reads the remote origin
    #   from the settings of the repository at run time, and whether the
    #   program runs on the runner is decided at run time.
    # attack-value: github.head_ref = "--upload-pack=echo${IFS}PWNED>&2;false"
    # attack-run-behavior: git fetch reads the word as --upload-pack and fetches
    #   from origin. When origin is the HTTPS URL that actions/checkout sets,
    #   git does not use the program, and nothing is printed; when origin is a
    #   local path, git runs the program on the runner and the shell prints
    #   PWNED.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      fetch:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              HEAD_REF: ${{ github.head_ref }}
            run: git fetch "$HEAD_REF"
    ```
- unverified-option: a command with an option that the linter's table of commands declares to run code or a program, where no test by the authors of the linter has seen whether the option runs the program when the value has a form that an attacker can write. A value such as github.event.pull_request.head.repo.name, the name of a repository, is of this kind for tar: the name holds only ASCII letters, digits, ., - and \_, and can be -I followed by the name of a program (-Ipython3); tar then starts that program with the single argument -d and the archive on the standard input of the program, and the attacker writes only the name of the program, not the arguments of the program. Whether a program started in that way does harm depends on the content of the archive, and no test by the authors of the linter has checked that
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: unverified-option.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a step runs make all and passes the
    #   name of the pull request's head branch to make after the target, through
    #   env and inside quotes.
    # reason: make reads a word that begins with - as an option even after its
    #   targets, and its option --eval reads its value as a makefile, where
    #   $(shell ...) runs a program. A branch's name has no blanks, and --eval
    #   was seen to run a program only from a word with blanks: the value
    #   without blanks that a test tried ran nothing, and whether another value
    #   without blanks runs a program is not known.
    # attack-value: github.head_ref = "--eval=$(shell${IFS}echo${IFS}PWNED>&2)"
    # attack-run-behavior: make reads the word as --eval and reads its value as
    #   a makefile. The value comes from env inside double quotes, so the shell
    #   passes ${IFS} to make as text, and make expands ${IFS} as a variable of
    #   make, which is empty; no blank follows the name of the function shell,
    #   and nothing runs.
    #   Whether another value without blanks reaches $(shell ...) is not known;
    #   if a value did, make would run the command of $(shell ...) in the step.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              HEAD_REF: ${{ github.head_ref }}
            run: make all "$HEAD_REF"
    ```
- undeclared-option: the value after an option the table of commands does not declare, which may take the value as its own
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: undeclared-option.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a step extracts from an archive the
    #   members that match the pull request's title as a pattern, passing the
    #   title to tar after --wildcards, through env and inside quotes.
    # reason: the table of commands does not declare --wildcards, so whether it
    #   takes the next word as its value (and tar then does not read the title
    #   as an option) or takes none (and tar reads the title as an option) is
    #   not known.
    # attack-value: github.event.pull_request.title = "--to-command=echo PWNED"
    # attack-run-behavior: --wildcards of GNU tar takes no value, so tar reads
    #   the title as --to-command and runs echo PWNED for each member it
    #   extracts, which prints PWNED.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      unpack:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
            run: tar -xf archive.tar --wildcards "$TITLE"
    ```
- value-head: a value an attacker shapes, for which the linter does not know whether the value can begin with -: a URL, an email, the name of a default branch, the head branch of a workflow_run. The title of a wiki page is not of this kind: the title holds no -, so the title cannot begin with -, and the rule reports nothing on the title. The label (owner:branch) of the head of a pull request and the full name (owner/name) of a repository are not of this kind: the label and the full name begin with the login of an account; when the authors of the linter tried on 2026-11-01, GitHub refused a login that begins with - at sign-up and at a rename, so the rule assumes that the label and the full name do not begin with -, and the rule reports nothing on the label or the full name (a label or a full name of an older account whose login begins with - is the undetected form dash-login)
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: value-head.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a step extracts an archive and passes
    #   the default branch of the repository of the pull request's head to tar
    #   after the file names, through env and inside quotes.
    # reason: GNU tar, the tar of ubuntu-latest, reads a word that begins with
    #   - as an option even after its file names, and the linter's table of
    #   values has no entry that says whether the default branch of the
    #   repository of the head can begin with -: the owner of a fork names the
    #   branches of the fork, and GitHub accepted
    #   git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<name> for a name that begins with -,
    #   though git check-ref-format --branch refuses such a name.
    # attack-value: github.event.pull_request.head.repo.default_branch = "--to-command=echo${IFS}PWNED"
    # attack-run-behavior: if the default branch had this value, tar would read
    #   the word as --to-command and, while tar extracts notes.txt, run echo
    #   PWNED with the content of notes.txt as the input of echo.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      unpack:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              BRANCH: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.repo.default_branch }}
            run: tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt "$BRANCH"
    ```
- step-output-run: the output of a step that runs a script (steps.&lt;id>.outputs), which the script writes to \$GITHUB_OUTPUT
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: step-output-run.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the step s runs a script that writes the output o to
    #   $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the next step passes steps.s.outputs.o to tar after
    #   the file names, by ${{ }} inside quotes.
    # reason: the output is what the script writes at run time, so whether an
    #   attacker controls it is not known.
    # cause: the rule does not yet follow what a script writes to
    #   $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
    # attack-value: steps.s.outputs.o = "--to-command=echo PWNED"
    # attack-run-behavior: when the script of the step s writes o with the value
    #   to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, tar reads the word as --to-command and runs echo
    #   PWNED for notes.txt as it extracts it, which prints PWNED.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: s
            run: echo "o=x" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          - run: tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt "${{ steps.s.outputs.o }}"
    ```
- step-output-local-action: the output of a step that uses a local action (./, in the workspace of the job, which is the repository that the job checks out; \$/, the repository of the action)
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - example: step-output-local-action.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the step s uses the local action ./.github/actions/a, and the
    #   next step passes steps.s.outputs.o to tar after the file names, by
    #   ${{ }} inside quotes.
    # reason: the output is what the local action sets; that action is in the
    #   workspace of the job (the repository the job checks out), not in this
    #   workflow, so whether an attacker controls the output is not known.
    # cause: the rule does not read the outputs a local action sets: it gives
    #   this kind to steps.<id>.outputs of any step that uses a local action,
    #   whether its action.yml is among the files read or not.
    # attack-value: steps.s.outputs.o = "--to-command=echo PWNED"
    # attack-run-behavior: when ./.github/actions/a sets the output o to the
    #   value, tar reads the word as --to-command and runs echo PWNED for
    #   notes.txt as it extracts it, which prints PWNED.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: s
            uses: ./.github/actions/a
          - run: tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt "${{ steps.s.outputs.o }}"
    ```
- step-output-remote-action: the output of a step that uses an action of another repository
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: step-output-remote-action.yml (workflow, inconclusive)

    ```yaml
    #   repository, and the next step passes steps.s.outputs.o to tar after the

    # reason: the output is what that action sets, and its action.yml is not in
    #   the input, so whether an attacker controls the output is not known.
    # cause: the rule does not yet ask for the action.yml of another repository

    # attack-value: steps.s.outputs.o = "--to-command=echo PWNED"
    # attack-run-behavior: when some/action@v1 sets the output o to the value,
    ```

- step-output-docker: the output of a step that runs a Docker image (docker://), which the image writes at run time
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: step-output-docker.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the step s runs the Docker image docker://alpine:3, and the
    #   next step passes steps.s.outputs.o to tar after the file names, by
    #   ${{ }} inside quotes.
    # reason: the image writes the output at run time; nothing the rule could
    #   read is expected to tell what it writes, so whether an attacker controls
    #   it is not known.
    # attack-value: steps.s.outputs.o = "--to-command=echo PWNED"
    # attack-run-behavior: when the image sets the output o to the value, tar
    #   reads the word as --to-command and runs echo PWNED for notes.txt as it
    #   extracts it, which prints PWNED.
    on: issues

      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: s
            uses: docker://alpine:3
    ```
