- artifact-poisoning.download
  - detected: {uses} takes the artifact of {pr_run_ref} into the workspace on {pr_code_on}
  - arguments:
    - {uses}: The uses of the download, as written.
    - {pr_run_ref}: What makes the download take the artifact of the attacker's run, as written: an expression such as github.event.workflow_run.id, the input allow_forks with the value true, or, when the step has no input run_id (or an input run_id whose \${{ }} is empty on the event of the job) and no input allow_forks with the value true, the value of the key uses of the step (dawidd6/action-download-artifact@&lt;ref>), whose search of the runs of a workflow takes the attacker's run; or, for an artifact of the current run, jobs.&lt;id> of the job that checks out the code of the pull request and uploads the artifact.
    - {pr_code_on}: The events on which the finding holds, each event named once.
  - consequence: its files replace those of the workspace; a step that runs any of them (a build, a test, a script) runs the pull request's author's code with the job's secrets and its token
  - remedy: download to \${{ runner.temp }}/artifacts, or say in a file of facts that the files are only read as data
  - severity: critical (found from the CVSS metrics below by the table)
  - fix kinds: runner-temp-path
  - fact kinds: repo.environment-protected (provider: repo-setting), repo.default-token-write (provider: repo-setting), git.commit-contains (provider: github), download.executed (provider: user-supplied), repo.pull-request-target-allowed (provider: repo-setting)
  - attackers: fork-pr-author
  - preconditions: attacker-run, download-event, no-approval, token-reads, into-workspace, callers-events
  - true positives:
    - download.ghsl-2026-204.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on workflow_run, the job checks out the directory
      #   .github/workflows/scripts, downloads the artifact assign-reviewer-review
      #   of the run that triggered the job into the workspace, and a step of
      #   actions/github-script loads
      #   .github/workflows/scripts/assign_reviewer_lib.js with require and calls
      #   it. These are the steps of assign_reviewer_review_apply.yaml of
      #   spiffe/spire (commit ef8527ec91013c6c1b4741e0f6ac0786576e620e, lines
      #   34-77).
      # reason: the files of the artifact replace the script that the job checked
      #   out, and the step of actions/github-script runs the script. The rule does
      #   not read a require of actions/github-script as a step that runs the files
      #   of the artifact. The rule reports the kind download, a finding on the
      #   download itself: the download puts files of the attacker into the
      #   workspace, and the rule reports download when the rule cannot read whether
      #   a later step runs the files. The rule reports the kind executed instead
      #   when the rule reads that a later step runs the files.
      # attack-value: the file .github/workflows/scripts/assign_reviewer_lib.js of the artifact assign-reviewer-review = "module.exports = async () => { console.log('PWNED') }"
      # attack-run-behavior: the download writes the file over the script of the
      #   checkout, and the step of actions/github-script loads the file and calls
      #   it, which prints PWNED.
      # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2026-204_spiffe_spire_repository/
      on:
        workflow_run:
          workflows: [assign-reviewer-review-capture]
          types: [completed]
      permissions:
        contents: read
      jobs:
        apply:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          if: github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'
          permissions:
            contents: read
            issues: write
            pull-requests: write
            actions: read
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
              with:
                persist-credentials: false
                sparse-checkout: .github/workflows/scripts
            - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
              with:
                name: assign-reviewer-review
                run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
                github-token: ${{ github.token }}
            - uses: actions/github-script@3a2844b7e9c422d3c10d287c895573f7108da1b3 # v9.0.0
              with:
                script: |
                  const courtLib = require('./.github/workflows/scripts/assign_reviewer_lib.js');
                  const court = await courtLib({ github, context, core });
      ```
    - download.no-row-event.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on member, an event that the GitHub document of the events that
      #   trigger workflows does not name, the job downloads with
      #   dawidd6/action-download-artifact v3 the artifact named out, from the
      #   newest run of its own workflow into the workspace, and no step after the
      #   download is seen to run the files of the artifact.
      # reason: the search takes the run of a pull request from a fork on any event
      #   of the job; what a run of member has is not documented, and the rule
      #   reports the job as on any other event (the fact download.executed true).
      # attack-value: the file build.sh in the artifact named out, from the fork's pull_request run of the workflow = "echo PWNED\n"
      # attack-run-behavior: the pull request from a fork changes the workflow to
      #   run on pull_request too, and the pull_request run uploads build.sh in
      #   the artifact named out; the next member run takes that run, the newest
      #   successful one, and a step that runs build.sh prints PWNED.
      on: member
      permissions:
        actions: read
        contents: read
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: dawidd6/action-download-artifact@v3
              with:
                name: out
      ```
    - download.snap-install.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on workflow_run of the workflow Release Dev, the job downloads
      #   the artifact snap-linux-amd64 of the run that triggered the job into the
      #   directory release/, installs the snap file of the artifact with
      #   snap install --dangerous, and runs the command openshell of the snap.
      #   These are the steps of the job ubuntu-snap of release-canary.yml of
      #   NVIDIA/OpenShell (commit a408f5dd083a9a4be259bb44478598002f9387a6, lines
      #   189-235), without the steps that install snapd, install the snap docker
      #   and connect the interfaces, and without the input release-dev-run-id of
      #   workflow_dispatch.
      # reason: a pull request from a fork can change the workflow Release Dev to
      #   run on pull_request under the same name, and the run of the pull request
      #   then triggers this workflow_run; the download takes the artifact of the
      #   run of the pull request by workflow_run.id and the token of this run. The
      #   rule does not read snap install and the later command openshell as steps
      #   that run the files of the artifact. The rule reports the kind download, a
      #   finding on the download itself, and not the kind executed.
      # attack-value: the program of the app openshell in the snap file of the artifact snap-linux-amd64 = "#!/bin/sh\necho PWNED\n"
      # attack-run-behavior: snap install --dangerous installs the snap file of
      #   the artifact without a signature (snapd 2.78: "Install the given snap
      #   file even if there are no pre-acknowledged signatures for it",
      #   https://github.com/canonical/snapd/blob/00b63144e44cdb7bd059e40e947e720b942c55ec/cmd/snapd/cli/cmd_snap_op.go#L1632).
      #   The command openshell of the later step runs the app openshell of the
      #   installed snap, as the command of an app whose name is the name of the
      #   snap is /snap/bin/<the snap name>
      #   (https://github.com/canonical/snapd/blob/00b63144e44cdb7bd059e40e947e720b942c55ec/snap/info.go#L1519-L1521
      #   and #L1872-L1878). The program of the app prints PWNED, with the
      #   GITHUB_TOKEN of this run.
      # source: https://github.com/NVIDIA/OpenShell/blob/a408f5dd083a9a4be259bb44478598002f9387a6/.github/workflows/release-canary.yml#L189-L235
      on:
        workflow_run:
          workflows: ["Release Dev"]
          types: [completed]
      permissions:
        actions: read
        contents: read
      jobs:
        ubuntu-snap:
          if: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' }}
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
              with:
                github-token: ${{ github.token }}
                run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
                pattern: snap-linux-amd64
                path: release/
                merge-multiple: true
            - run: sudo snap install ./release/*.snap --dangerous
            - run: openshell --version
      ```
    - download.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: workflow_run downloads the artifact of the run that started it
      #   into the workspace with dawidd6/action-download-artifact, and then reads
      #   ./build.sh into its shell by source.
      # reason: the run of ci that starts this one may be a pull request's from a
      #   fork, whose author then decides the artifact's files; the job checks out
      #   nothing, so the build.sh that source reads can only come from the artifact
      #   (download.executed true), and it runs in this workflow_run, with the base
      #   repository's token, not in the pull request's run.
      # attack-value: the file build.sh in the artifact of the pull request's ci run = "echo PWNED\n"
      # attack-run-behavior: the fork's pull request changes ci so its run uploads
      #   build.sh; when that run completes, the download takes its artifact by
      #   workflow_run.id into the workspace, and source ./build.sh runs it, which
      #   prints PWNED, with this run's GITHUB_TOKEN and the base repository's
      #   secrets.
      on:
        workflow_run:
          workflows: [ci]
          types: [completed]
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: dawidd6/action-download-artifact@v6
              with:
                run_id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
            - run: source ./build.sh
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - download.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on workflow_run, the job downloads the artifact of the run that
      #   started it to ${{ runner.temp }}/artifacts, outside the workspace, and
      #   then only runs echo done.
      # reason: unlike a download into the workspace, the artifact's files replace
      #   none of the workspace's, and no step of this job runs anything under
      #   runner.temp, so none of the artifact's files run.
      # attack-value: the file build.sh in the artifact of the pull request's ci run = "echo PWNED\n"
      # attack-run-behavior: the download puts the artifact's build.sh under
      #   runner.temp/artifacts, and the job then only runs echo done; nothing
      #   runs build.sh.
      on:
        workflow_run:
          workflows: [ci]
          types: [completed]
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: dawidd6/action-download-artifact@v6
              with:
                run_id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
                path: ${{ runner.temp }}/artifacts
            - run: echo done
      ```

### fix kinds

- runner-temp-path: put the artifact's files out of the workspace: path: \${{ runner.temp }}/artifacts
  - safety: review
  - possible side effects:
    - artifact-path-moved: Steps that read the files of the artifact where they were no longer find them.

### undetected forms

- outside-caller: a reusable workflow or composite action that callers in the repository decide, called from another repository on an event, or with a value, an attacker controls: the caller's run has the caller's token and secrets, not the repository's
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed, artifact-poisoning.download
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: .github/workflows/called.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the workflow is called; it downloads the artifact of
    #   github.event.workflow_run.id into the workspace, and npm ci runs. Its
    #   one caller in the repository, ci.yml, runs on push.
    # reason: no added gain for this repository: ci.yml calls the workflow on
    #   push alone, and github.event of a push has no workflow_run, so the value
    #   that the run reads is not a value that an attacker wrote. Another
    #   repository may call the workflow on an event whose payload has what an
    #   attacker wrote, but that run has the token and the secrets of the other
    #   repository.
    # cause: the rule reads a called workflow on the events of its callers in
    #   the repository, and ci.yml runs on push alone.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the artifact of the pull request's ci run = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: ci.yml calls it on push, whose event has no
    #   workflow_run, so run-id is empty, the download does not name the fork's
    #   ci run, and npm ci reads no package.json of the pull request. A workflow
    #   of another repository that calls it on workflow_run would download the
    #   fork's artifact, with that repository's token.
    on:
      workflow_call:
    permissions:
      actions: read
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
            with:
              run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
              github-token: ${{ github.token }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
    - .github/workflows/ci.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: push
      jobs:
        call:
          uses: ./.github/workflows/called.yml
      ```
- labeler-same-run: a job on pull_request_target with the activity type labeled that downloads and runs an artifact that another job of the same run uploads after the other job checks out the code of the pull request, where the if of each job requires a label that actions/labeler adds to the pull request of the attacker. The rule reads an upload of the same run only from a job that no label and no environment approves, and does not read whether actions/labeler adds the label that the job that uploads requires. untrusted-checkout reports the checkout of the job that uploads.
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed, artifact-poisoning.download
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: .github/workflows/labeled.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: labeler.yml runs actions/labeler on pull_request_target with a
    #   personal access token; the configuration .github/labeler.yml adds the
    #   label safe-to-test to a pull request that changes a file under site/;
    #   labeled.yml runs on pull_request_target on labeled, and when the label is
    #   safe-to-test, the job build checks out the head of the pull request, runs
    #   npm ci and npm run build, and uploads dist, and the job deploy, which
    #   needs build, downloads dist and runs ./dist/deploy.sh.
    # reason: actions/labeler adds the label safe-to-test to the pull request of
    #   the attacker, so no person approves the labeled run, and the job deploy
    #   runs the deploy.sh that the code of the pull request wrote in the run of
    #   the job build.
    # cause: the rule reads an upload of the same run only from a job that no
    #   label and no environment approves, and does not read whether
    #   actions/labeler adds the label that the job build requires.
    # attack-value: the file dist/deploy.sh in the artifact dist of the job build = "#!/bin/sh\necho PWNED\n"
    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork that
    #   changes a file under site/ and whose build writes dist/deploy.sh;
    #   actions/labeler adds the label safe-to-test, which starts labeled.yml;
    #   the job build uploads dist, and the job deploy downloads dist and runs
    #   ./dist/deploy.sh, which prints PWNED.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    jobs:
      build:
        if: github.event.label.name == 'safe-to-test'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: npm ci && npm run build
          - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
            with: {name: dist, path: dist}
      deploy:
        needs: build
        if: github.event.label.name == 'safe-to-test'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
            with: {name: dist}
          - run: ./dist/deploy.sh
    ```
    - .github/labeler.yml (repo-file)
      ```yaml
      safe-to-test:
        - changed-files:
            - any-glob-to-any-file: 'site/**'
      ```
    - .github/workflows/labeler.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: pull_request_target
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        label:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/labeler@v5
              with:
                repo-token: ${{ secrets.LABELER_PAT }}
      ```
- run-command: an artifact downloaded by a command of a run: gh run download, gh api …/zip, curl
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed, artifact-poisoning.download
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: run-command.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on workflow_run, gh downloads the artifact of the run
    #   workflow_run follows, and ./out/run.sh runs.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): reading the command would find the
    #   download.
    # cause: the commands of a run are not read for a download.
    # attack-value: the file out/run.sh in the artifact out of the pull request's ci run = "#!/bin/sh\necho PWNED\n"
    # attack-run-behavior: gh run download, with the job's token, takes the
    #   artifact out of the fork's ci run into the workspace, and ./out/run.sh
    #   runs it, which prints PWNED, with the base repository's secrets.
    on:
      workflow_run:
        workflows: [ci]
        types: [completed]
    permissions: {actions: read}
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: gh run download ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }} -n out
            env:
              GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          - run: ./out/run.sh
    ```
- github-script: an artifact downloaded by github-script (downloadArtifact)
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed, artifact-poisoning.download
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: github-script.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on workflow_run, actions/github-script lists the artifacts of
    #   the run workflow_run follows, downloads the first as out.zip, and a run
    #   unzips it and runs ./run.sh. GHSL-2025-087 has the same download:
    #   docs_pr_comment.yml of PX4/PX4-Autopilot (commit
    #   8c6337e94eccfdd4dc8bce3df10b644ed16d72ba, lines 14-36) downloads the
    #   artifact pr_number of the run of docs_flaw_checker.yml on
    #   pull_request_target with github-script and unzips it; there the files
    #   are read with juliangruber/read-file-action and written into a run by
    #   ${{ }} (line 59), not run as a script.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the script downloads the artifact; reading
    #   the script would find it.
    # cause: scripts are not read for a download: the rule reads
    #   actions/download-artifact and dawidd6/action-download-artifact.
    # attack-value: the file run.sh in the first artifact of the pull request's ci run = "#!/bin/sh\necho PWNED\n"
    # attack-run-behavior: the script downloads the first artifact of the run
    #   workflow_run follows, the fork's ci run, as out.zip with the job's
    #   token; unzip puts run.sh in the workspace, and ./run.sh runs it, which
    #   prints PWNED, with the base repository's secrets.
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2025-087_PX4_PX4-Autopilot/
    on:
      workflow_run:
        workflows: [ci]
        types: [completed]
    permissions: {actions: read}
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/github-script@v7
            with:
              script: |
                const all = await github.rest.actions.listWorkflowRunArtifacts({owner: context.repo.owner, repo: context.repo.repo, run_id: context.payload.workflow_run.id});
                const d = await github.rest.actions.downloadArtifact({owner: context.repo.owner, repo: context.repo.repo, artifact_id: all.data.artifacts[0].id, archive_format: 'zip'});
                require('fs').writeFileSync('out.zip', Buffer.from(d.data));
          - run: unzip out.zip && ./run.sh
    ```
- other-action: an artifact downloaded by an action other than actions/download-artifact and dawidd6/action-download-artifact
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed, artifact-poisoning.download
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: other-action.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on workflow_run, aochmann/actions-download-artifact downloads
    #   the artifact of ci.yml, and ./run.sh runs.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): an action of neither table downloads the
    #   artifact; what its inputs mean is in its action.yml, another
    #   repository's.
    # cause: the rule reads the downloads of actions/download-artifact and
    #   dawidd6/action-download-artifact only.
    # attack-value: the file run.sh in the artifact of the latest ci.yml run = "#!/bin/sh\necho PWNED\n"
    # attack-run-behavior: aochmann/actions-download-artifact takes the artifact
    #   of a ci.yml run, which may be a fork's, into the workspace, and ./run.sh
    #   runs it, which prints PWNED, with the base repository's secrets.
    on:
      workflow_run:
        workflows: [ci]
        types: [completed]
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: aochmann/actions-download-artifact@1.0.4
            with:
              workflow: ci.yml
          - run: ./run.sh
    ```
- local-action: a download inside a local action the job uses, whose action.yml is another file of the repository
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed, artifact-poisoning.download
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - example: local-action.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on workflow_run, a step uses a local action that downloads the
    #   artifact (GHSL-2024-314, aws/karpenter-provider-aws: uses:
    #   ./.github/actions/download-artifact), and make snapshot runs.
    # reason: a todo (a file of the repository): the download is in the local
    #   action's action.yml; reading it would find it.
    # cause: its action.yml is another file, which the rule does not read with
    #   the workflow.
    # attack-value: the file Makefile in the artifact of the ApprovalComment run = "snapshot:\n	echo PWNED\n"
    # attack-run-behavior: when the local action downloads the artifact of the
    #   run workflow_run follows into the workspace, make snapshot reads its
    #   Makefile and runs the snapshot recipe, which prints PWNED, with the base
    #   repository's secrets; the action.yml is not part of this example.
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-314_AWS_Karpenter_Provider/
    on:
      workflow_run:
        workflows: [ApprovalComment]
        types: [completed]
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: ./.github/actions/download-artifact
          - run: make snapshot
    ```
- read-as-data: a file of the artifact read as a value: written to \$GITHUB_ENV or \$GITHUB_OUTPUT, or put in a run, which may run as code
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed, artifact-poisoning.download
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: read-as-data.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on workflow_run, the artifact is downloaded under runner.temp,
    #   and a run writes its file pr-id.txt to $GITHUB_OUTPUT (GHSL-2024-124,
    #   quarkusio/quarkus preview.yml: echo
    #   "id=$(<documentation-temp/pr-id.txt)" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT, then ${{
    #   steps.pr.outputs.id }} in a run). GHSL-2024-276 and GHSL-2024-281 have
    #   the same form: preview-deploy.yml of ant-design-blazor/ant-design-blazor
    #   (commit d3668d9cecc65f2ee0dac920aa55e8f393c6773d) and of
    #   ant-design/ant-design-web3 (commit
    #   cbbf0cefce42cabb9ef0348db507ddd3ce00dcf4) download the artifact pr with
    #   dawidd6/action-download-artifact into the workspace, write pr-id.txt to
    #   the output id, and write ${{ steps.pr.outputs.id }} into the run of
    #   npx surge. In those files, artifact-poisoning reports executed for
    #   another reason: npx surge --project ./ runs in the workspace where the
    #   artifact is.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the artifact's file is read as a value,
    #   which may run as code; following the value would find it.
    # cause: the value's way through the shell is not followed.
    # attack-value: the file pr-id.txt in the artifact of the pull request's ci run = "1$(echo PWNED)"
    # attack-run-behavior: the download puts pr-id.txt under runner.temp/pr, and
    #   the step writes id=1$(echo PWNED) to GITHUB_OUTPUT; the shell does not
    #   expand the output of the command substitution again, so nothing runs
    #   here, and a later run step that writes steps.pr.outputs.id with ${{ }},
    #   as quarkus preview.yml does, would run echo PWNED. This example has no
    #   such step.
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-124_GHSL-2024-125_quarkus/
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-276_Ant-design-blazor/
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-281_Ant-design-web3/
    on:
      workflow_run:
        workflows: [ci]
        types: [completed]
    permissions: {actions: read}
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
            with:
              run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
              github-token: ${{ github.token }}
              path: ${{ runner.temp }}/pr
          - id: pr
            run: echo "id=$(cat $RUNNER_TEMP/pr/pr-id.txt)" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
    ```
  - example: read-as-data.ghsl-2026-225.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on workflow_run, the job downloads the artifact rebuilt-dist of
    #   the run of a pull request that triggered the job under runner.temp, a
    #   step writes the first line of the file dist-meta/head-ref of the artifact
    #   to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the job checks out that branch and pushes to it.
    #   These are the steps of commit-dist.yml of actions/attest (commit
    #   60c80190bb1a4fb35e5724ede753db5656412b68, lines 13-79 and 92-110); the
    #   validation of the values and the copy of dist/ are cut.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): following the value from the file of the
    #   artifact to the ref of the checkout and of the push would find it.
    # cause: the rule reports the files of an artifact that a step runs, and
    #   does not follow a file that a step reads as a value.
    # attack-value: the file dist-meta/head-ref of the artifact rebuilt-dist = "main"
    # attack-run-behavior: the step check writes head-ref=main to
    #   $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the job checks out main and pushes to main, a branch
    #   that the author of the pull request chose (in the advisory, with dist/
    #   of the artifact copied into the checkout).
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2026-225_actions_attest/
    on:
      workflow_run:
        workflows: ["Rebuild dist"]
        types:
          - completed
    permissions:
      contents: read
    jobs:
      commit:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions:
          contents: write
        if: >
          github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' &&
          github.event.workflow_run.event == 'pull_request'
        steps:
          - name: Download rebuilt dist/
            uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
            continue-on-error: true
            with:
              name: rebuilt-dist
              run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
              github-token: ${{ github.token }}
              path: ${{ runner.temp }}/incoming
          - name: Check for artifact
            id: check
            run: |
              incoming="${{ runner.temp }}/incoming"
              head_ref="$(head -n1 "$incoming/dist-meta/head-ref" | tr -d '\r\n')"
              echo "head-ref=$head_ref" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          - name: Checkout PR branch
            uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
            with:
              ref: ${{ steps.check.outputs.head-ref }}
              token: ${{ github.token }}
          - run: git push origin HEAD:${{ steps.check.outputs.head-ref }}
    ```
- same-run-pr-code: an artifact of the current run that another job made from a pull request's code that the other job checked out, where the job that downloads does not list the job that uploads in its needs, directly or through other jobs, or where an approval admits the job that uploads; also an upload that the rule does not read as such: an upload in a reusable workflow that a job of the workflow calls, an upload inside a composite action that a step uses, and actions/upload-artifact/merge, which uploads again the artifacts of other jobs under a new name. The rule reads such an upload only when the job of the download lists the job of the upload in needs, directly or through other jobs, no approval admits the job of the upload, and a step of that job uses actions/upload-artifact itself
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed, artifact-poisoning.download
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: same-run-pr-code.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, the job build checks out and builds the
    #   pull request's head and uploads dist; the job deploy, which does not
    #   need build, downloads dist from the current run and runs ./dist/deploy.sh.
    # reason: deploy may download dist after build uploads dist, and then runs
    #   what the pull request's code made, with the base repository's token and
    #   secrets.
    # cause: the rule reads an upload of the current run only in a job that the
    #   job of the download needs, directly or through other jobs; without
    #   needs, the two jobs run at the same time, and whether the upload comes
    #   first depends on the run.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"build\":\"mkdir -p dist && echo 'echo PWNED' > dist/deploy.sh\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: when the job build uploads dist before the job deploy
    #   downloads, ./dist/deploy.sh runs the file that the build of the pull
    #   request wrote, which prints PWNED, with the base repository's token and
    #   secrets; when the download comes first, the download fails because the
    #   artifact dist is not there yet.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: npm ci && npm run build
          - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
            with: {name: dist, path: dist}
      deploy:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
            with: {name: dist}
          - run: ./dist/deploy.sh
    ```
- dispatch-ref: an artifact of the current run that a job built from a ref that an input of workflow_dispatch names
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed, artifact-poisoning.download
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: dispatcher)
  - example: dispatch-ref.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on workflow_dispatch, the job build checks out the ref of an
    #   input, builds and uploads an artifact; the job publish downloads it in
    #   the current run and runs ./out/publish.sh.
    # reason: a limitation (decided by dispatcher): whoever dispatches the workflow
    #   chooses the ref the job builds, and so what the artifact has.
    # cause: the download has no run-id, so the rule reads it as of the current
    #   run, which no pull request from a fork drives.
    # attack-value: inputs.ref = "refs/pull/1/head"
    # attack-run-behavior: when the pull request 1 is from a fork, the job build
    #   checks out the head of the fork's pull request, whose build.sh writes
    #   out/publish.sh that prints PWNED; the upload takes out,
    #   the job publish downloads it in the environment release, and
    #   ./out/publish.sh runs it with that environment's secrets.
    on:
      workflow_dispatch:
        inputs:
          ref: {type: string}
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with: {ref: '${{ inputs.ref }}'}
          - run: ./build.sh
          - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
            with: {name: out, path: out}
      publish:
        needs: build
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        environment: release
        steps:
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
            with: {name: out}
          - run: ./out/publish.sh
    ```
- producer-dependency: an artifact whose producer took what is bad from a dependency it built with
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed, artifact-poisoning.download
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: producer-dependency.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, the job build runs npm ci and npm run build and
    #   uploads dist; the job deploy downloads it and runs ./dist/deploy.sh.
    # reason: a limitation (run time): what the producer built with may put what
    #   is bad in the artifact; the bytes of an artifact are not known from the
    #   workflow.
    # cause: the rule reads which run an artifact is of, not what is in it; this
    #   one is of the current run on push.
    # attack-value: the file dist/deploy.sh that a dependency of package-lock.json writes in the build = "#!/bin/sh\necho PWNED\n"
    # attack-run-behavior: npm ci and npm run build run the code of the
    #   dependencies, one of which writes dist/deploy.sh; the upload takes dist,
    #   the job deploy downloads it, and ./dist/deploy.sh runs it, which prints
    #   PWNED, with the push run's token and secrets.
    on: push
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - run: npm ci && npm run build
          - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
            with: {name: dist, path: dist}
      deploy:
        needs: build
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
            with: {name: dist}
          - run: ./dist/deploy.sh
    ```
- runner-temp-indirect: a download under runner.temp whose files a step runs without writing the path of the file as a command or as an argument of a command in the run: script of the step, for example by: the source command or its short form, the . (dot) command, a shell that gets the path inside the code of its -c option (bash -c '\$RUNNER_TEMP/x.sh'), a path that format() makes (\${{ format('{0}/x.sh', runner.temp) }}), a shell variable that holds the path (bash \$S, where an earlier line or the env of the step sets S to \$RUNNER_TEMP/x.sh), or a \${{ }} in the path whose value goes to a parent directory with .. and so points outside the directory written before the \${{ }} (\$RUNNER_TEMP/pr/\${{ matrix.f }}, where matrix.f is ../a/x.sh and the download is in runner.temp/a)
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed, artifact-poisoning.download
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: runner-temp-indirect.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on workflow_run, the artifact is downloaded under runner.temp,
    #   and a step reads a file of it into its shell by the source command.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): reading the source command would find
    #   that the file runs.
    # cause: a command that names $RUNNER_TEMP/... or ${{ runner.temp }}/... is
    #   read as running the file only as a program or as the file of an
    #   interpreter, and the source command is neither.
    # attack-value: the file x.sh in the artifact of the pull request's ci run = "#!/bin/sh\necho PWNED\n"
    # attack-run-behavior: the download puts x.sh under runner.temp/a, and
    #   source $RUNNER_TEMP/a/x.sh runs it in the shell of the step, printing
    #   PWNED, with the base repository's secrets.
    on:
      workflow_run:
        workflows: [ci]
        types: [completed]
    permissions: {actions: read}
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
            with:
              run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
              github-token: ${{ github.token }}
              path: ${{ runner.temp }}/a
          - run: source $RUNNER_TEMP/a/x.sh
    ```
  - example: runner-temp-indirect.expression-climbs.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on workflow_run, the artifact is downloaded under runner.temp/a,
    #   and a step runs bash $RUNNER_TEMP/pr/${{ matrix.f }}, where the matrix
    #   gives f the value ../a/x.sh.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): reading the value of the ${{ }} would
    #   find that the path goes up out of runner.temp/pr into runner.temp/a.
    # cause: the rule reads the ${{ }} of a path as a part that stays under the
    #   directory written before the ${{ }}, runner.temp/pr, and the files are
    #   in runner.temp/a.
    # attack-value: the file x.sh in the artifact of the pull request's ci run = "#!/bin/sh\necho PWNED\n"
    # attack-run-behavior: the download puts x.sh in runner.temp/a, and
    #   bash $RUNNER_TEMP/pr/../a/x.sh runs it, which prints PWNED, with the
    #   base repository's secrets.
    on:
      workflow_run:
        workflows: [ci]
        types: [completed]
    permissions: {actions: read}
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        strategy:
          matrix:
            f: [../a/x.sh]
        steps:
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
            with:
              run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
              github-token: ${{ github.token }}
              path: ${{ runner.temp }}/a
          - run: bash $RUNNER_TEMP/pr/${{ matrix.f }}
    ```
  - example: runner-temp-indirect.shell-variable.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on workflow_run, the artifact is downloaded under runner.temp,
    #   and a step runs its file by a shell variable that holds the path.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): reading the value of the shell variable,
    #   which the env of the step sets, would find that the file runs.
    # cause: only a command that names $RUNNER_TEMP/... or ${{ runner.temp
    #   }}/... is read as running the files; the value of $S is not read.
    # attack-value: the file x.sh in the artifact of the pull request's ci run = "#!/bin/sh\necho PWNED\n"
    # attack-run-behavior: the download puts x.sh under runner.temp/a; the
    #   step runs bash $S with S set to $RUNNER_TEMP/a/x.sh, which prints PWNED,
    #   with the base repository's secrets.
    on:
      workflow_run:
        workflows: [ci]
        types: [completed]
    permissions: {actions: read}
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
            with:
              run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
              github-token: ${{ github.token }}
              path: ${{ runner.temp }}/a
          - run: bash $S
            env:
              S: ${{ runner.temp }}/a/x.sh
    ```
- caller-omitted-input: an input of a reusable workflow, which callers in the repository call, used as the input run_id of dawidd6/action-download-artifact, when a caller does not give the input (an input that is not required), or an input of a composite action that the step that uses the action does not give: the value is then empty, and the action searches the runs of the workflow; the rule reads an input that the callers give as a value that is not empty
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed, artifact-poisoning.download
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - example: .github/workflows/called.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: caller.yml runs on push and calls called.yml without the input
    #   run; called.yml downloads with dawidd6/action-download-artifact v6 the
    #   artifact named out, from the run that the input run names, and runs
    #   build.sh with bash.
    # reason: a todo (a file of the repository): the input run is not required,
    #   and the call gives no value, so the input run_id is empty, and the
    #   action searches the runs of the workflow, which takes the run of a
    #   review of a pull request from a fork.
    # cause: the rule reads an input of a workflow that callers in the
    #   repository call as a value that the callers give, which is not empty.
    # attack-value: the file build.sh in the artifact named out, from the pull_request_review run of the fork's pull request = "echo PWNED\n"
    # attack-run-behavior: the pull request from a fork adds pull_request_review
    #   to called.yml and uploads build.sh in the artifact named out; the author
    #   writes a comment-only review, and the next push run of caller.yml calls
    #   called.yml, whose download takes that run, and bash build.sh prints
    #   PWNED.
    on:
      workflow_call:
        inputs:
          run: {type: string, required: false}
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: dawidd6/action-download-artifact@v6
            with:
              run_id: ${{ inputs.run }}
              name: out
          - run: bash build.sh
    ```
    - .github/workflows/caller.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: push
      jobs:
        c:
          uses: ./.github/workflows/called.yml
      ```
- run-id-condition: an input run_id of dawidd6/action-download-artifact whose \${{ }} gives github.run_id on some events and an empty value on others (\${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.run_id || '' }}): the action searches the runs of the workflow when the value is empty; the rule reads a run_id that writes github.run_id as a value that is never empty
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed, artifact-poisoning.download
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: run-id-condition.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push and schedule, dawidd6/action-download-artifact v6
    #   downloads with the input run_id github.run_id on push and an empty value
    #   on schedule, the artifact named out into the workspace, and build.sh runs
    #   with bash.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): on schedule the input run_id is empty, so
    #   the action searches the runs of the workflow, which takes the run of a
    #   review of a pull request from a fork.
    # cause: the rule reads a run_id that writes github.run_id as a value that
    #   is never empty, and does not read the condition around github.run_id.
    # attack-value: the file build.sh in the artifact named out, from the pull_request_review run of the fork's pull request = "echo PWNED\n"
    # attack-run-behavior: the pull request from a fork adds pull_request_review
    #   to the workflow and uploads build.sh in the artifact named out; the
    #   author writes a comment-only review, and the next schedule run takes that
    #   run, and bash build.sh prints PWNED.
    on:
      push:
      schedule:
        - cron: "0 0 * * *"
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: dawidd6/action-download-artifact@v6
            with:
              run_id: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.run_id || '' }}
              name: out
          - run: bash build.sh
    ```
- runtime-token: an artifact of the current run replaced by code of the run that has ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed, artifact-poisoning.download
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: runtime-token.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request, the job test checks out the pull request and
    #   runs npm test; the job deploy downloads the artifact site and runs
    #   ./site/deploy.sh.
    # reason: a limitation (run time): a step of the run that has
    #   ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN replaces the artifact another job downloads; which
    #   code has it is decided at run time.
    # cause: the download has no run-id, so the rule reads it as of the current
    #   run, which it does not take as an attacker's.
    # attack: the pull request's test script takes the run's
    #   ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN and with it uploads an artifact named site whose
    #   deploy.sh prints PWNED.
    # attack-run-behavior: the job deploy downloads site of the current run,
    #   which holds the attacker's files, and ./site/deploy.sh runs it, in the
    #   pull_request run, whose token for a fork's pull request is read-only.
    on: pull_request
    jobs:
      test:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - run: npm test
      deploy:
        needs: test
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
            with: {name: site}
          - run: ./site/deploy.sh
    ```
- insider-association: an if that lets in MEMBER or COLLABORATOR by the author_association of the issue, the pull request or the discussion the run is of, which the following pass: a member or a collaborator whose repository role is Read only, who gets, in the run, a token that writes and the secrets, more than what the Read role gives; the account of such a member or collaborator, taken over; and an outsider who becomes a MEMBER with the Read role, in an organization that lets anyone become a member (a bot that invites whoever asks). A member or a collaborator whose role is Triage or above holds a credential that can add a label or write to the repository, which the credential premise assumes no attacker holds. Who is a member, and with what role, is not in the workflow
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed, artifact-poisoning.download
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - added attackers: read-member, triage-account, writer-issues-token, required-reviewer
  - example: insider-association.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues opened, a job whose if lets in an issue whose
    #   author_association is MEMBER downloads an artifact with
    #   dawidd6/action-download-artifact and runs ./run.sh.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): a member of the organization, who may have read
    #   access only, passes this if (in an organization that lets anyone become a
    #   member, such as by a bot that invites whoever asks, an outsider becomes such
    #   a member), and gets the job's token and secrets past what the Read role
    #   gives; who is a member, and with what role, is not in the workflow.
    # cause: the rule evaluates the if with the attacker's author_association
    #   (NONE, FIRST_TIMER, FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR or CONTRIBUTOR), for which it
    #   is false, so no attacker's event runs the job.
    # attack-value: the file run.sh in the artifact of the latest ci.yml run = "#!/bin/sh\necho PWNED\n"
    # attack-run-behavior: for an issue whose author is a MEMBER, the if is
    #   true; dawidd6/action-download-artifact@v3, with workflow ci.yml and no
    #   run_id, takes the artifact of the latest ci.yml run, which may be a
    #   fork's, and ./run.sh runs it; for an author with NONE, FIRST_TIMER,
    #   FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR or CONTRIBUTOR the job is skipped.
    on:
      issues:
        types: [opened]
    jobs:
      a:
        if: github.event.issue.author_association == 'MEMBER'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: dawidd6/action-download-artifact@v3
            with:
              workflow: ci.yml
          - run: ./run.sh
    ```
- repository-dispatch: a value of the client_payload of repository_dispatch (github.event.client_payload): only a credential with write access to the permission Contents of the repository can send repository_dispatch, and the credential premise assumes that no attacker holds such a credential; the sender chooses the whole client_payload
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed, artifact-poisoning.download
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: repository-dispatch.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on repository_dispatch, dawidd6/action-download-artifact takes
    #   the artifact of the run that the value run of the client_payload names,
    #   and ./out/publish.sh runs.
    # reason: the form adds nothing to what the attacker gets (the disposition
    #   no-added-gain): only a credential with write access to the permission
    #   Contents of the repository can send repository_dispatch, and the
    #   credential premise assumes that no attacker holds such a credential; the
    #   sender chooses the whole client_payload.
    # cause: the table of the attacker's events that the rule reads leaves out
    #   repository_dispatch on purpose: the credential premise leaves the sender
    #   of repository_dispatch out of the threat model.
    # attack-value: github.event.client_payload.run = "1234"
    # attack-run-behavior: when a repository_dispatch with the value in its
    #   client_payload runs the workflow, the download takes the artifact of the
    #   run 1234, a pull_request run of a pull request from a fork whose workflow
    #   uploads out/publish.sh that prints PWNED, and ./out/publish.sh runs the
    #   file, which prints PWNED, with the secrets of the repository.
    on: repository_dispatch
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: dawidd6/action-download-artifact@v6
            with:
              run_id: ${{ github.event.client_payload.run }}
              name: out
              path: out
          - run: ./out/publish.sh
    ```
- dispatch-relay: a workflow on an event of an attacker that puts a value the attacker writes into the client_payload of a repository_dispatch that the workflow sends (gh api with client_payload to the endpoint dispatches, peter-evans/repository-dispatch), and a workflow on repository_dispatch that uses the value: the flaw is in the workflow that sends the repository_dispatch, and the rule does not read what a workflow sends to another workflow
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed, artifact-poisoning.download
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - example: .github/workflows/receiver.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: sender.yml runs on issues opened, and with the GITHUB_TOKEN
    #   sends a repository_dispatch of the type relay whose client_payload has the
    #   title of the issue as the value run; receiver.yml runs on that
    #   repository_dispatch, and dawidd6/action-download-artifact takes the
    #   artifact of the run that the value run of the client_payload names, and
    #   ./out/publish.sh runs.
    # reason: the author of the issue writes the value, and sender.yml relays
    #   the value to receiver.yml in a repository_dispatch that a run of the
    #   repository sends with a token of the repository; GitHub creates a workflow
    #   run for a repository_dispatch sent with the GITHUB_TOKEN, as an exception
    #   to the rule that an event that the GITHUB_TOKEN triggers creates no
    #   workflow run.
    # cause: the rule reads the events of each workflow alone, and does not read
    #   what a workflow sends to another workflow as the client_payload of a
    #   repository_dispatch.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "1234"
    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens an issue whose title is the value;
    #   sender.yml sends the value, and in the run of receiver.yml the download
    #   takes the artifact of the run 1234, a pull_request run of a pull request
    #   from a fork whose workflow uploads out/publish.sh that prints PWNED, and
    #   ./out/publish.sh runs the file, which prints PWNED, with the secrets of
    #   the repository.
    on:
      repository_dispatch:
        types: [relay]
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: dawidd6/action-download-artifact@v6
            with:
              run_id: ${{ github.event.client_payload.run }}
              name: out
              path: out
          - run: ./out/publish.sh
    ```

- dispatch-derived: a value that an env or the output of a step makes from an input of workflow_dispatch, in a job that runs only on workflow_dispatch (env: REF: refs/pull/\${{ inputs.pr }}/head; the output of gh pr view with the input pr), used as the ref of a checkout, the run that a download takes (the input run-id of actions/download-artifact), the key or the path of the cache, or a prompt: the one who dispatches the workflow chooses the value too, and the rule reports only an input of workflow_dispatch that the value refers to directly (input-dispatch)

    ```yaml
    # situation: on workflow_dispatch with the input pr, the env RUN of the job
    #   is the input pr, actions/download-artifact takes the artifact named out,
    #   from the run env.RUN with the token, and ./out/publish.sh runs.

    # cause: the rule reports an input of workflow_dispatch that a value refers
    #   to directly (the inconclusive kind input-dispatch), and does not follow
    #   a value that an env or the output of a step makes from the input in a
    #   job that runs only on workflow_dispatch.
    # attack-value: inputs.pr = "1234"
    # attack-run-behavior: when the one who dispatches the workflow gives the
    #   value, the download takes the artifact of the run 1234, a pull_request
    #   run of a pull request from a fork whose workflow uploads out/publish.sh
    #   that prints PWNED, and ./out/publish.sh runs the file, which prints
    #   PWNED, with the secrets of the repository.
    on:
      workflow_dispatch:
        inputs:
          pr: {type: string}
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        env:
          RUN: ${{ inputs.pr }}
        steps:
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
            with:
              run-id: ${{ env.RUN }}
              github-token: ${{ github.token }}
              name: out
              path: out
          - run: ./out/publish.sh
    ```
- npm-abbreviation: a command that runs npm followed by an abbreviation of the name of an npm command that runs code of the checked out tree (for example, npm tes for npm test), in a run step or in a permission of an agent. npm runs a word as an npm command when the word is the beginning of exactly one command name or alias name of the npm release that the job uses. The rule does not read abbreviations of npm command names.
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: npm-abbreviation.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a job downloads the artifact out of the latest run of
    #   the workflow into the workspace and runs npm tes.
    # reason: a limitation (run time): npm reads tes as the npm command test,
    #   because tes is the beginning of no other command name or alias name of
    #   the npm release that the job uses, and npm test runs the script test of
    #   the package.json of the artifact; which names the npm release has is known when
    #   the job runs.
    # cause: the rule reads npm tes as a step that runs nothing of the
    #   artifact, so the rule reports artifact-poisoning.download, not
    #   artifact-poisoning.executed.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the artifact out = "{\"scripts\":{\"test\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: the download puts the package.json of the attacker
    #   in the workspace, and npm tes runs its script test, which prints PWNED.
    on: push
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: dawidd6/action-download-artifact@v3
            with:
              name: out
          - run: npm tes
    ```
- npm-option-value-command: a command that runs npm with an option placed before the npm command, when the value of the option is the name of an npm command and the npm command runs code of the checked out tree (for example, npm --cache view ci, in which view is the name of a directory), in a run step or in a permission of an agent. The rule reads the first word after npm, other than the value of the option --prefix or -C, that is the name or the alias name of an npm command as the npm command, and so reads the value view as the npm command.
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: npm-option-value-command.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a job downloads the artifact out of the latest run of
    #   the workflow into the workspace and runs npm --cache view ci.
    # reason: a limitation (run time): npm reads view as the value of the
    #   option --cache, which takes a value, and runs npm ci, which runs the
    #   script preinstall of the package.json of the artifact; which options take
    #   a value is in the definitions of the npm release that the job uses,
    #   which is known when the job runs.
    # cause: the rule reads the first word after npm that is the name of an
    #   npm command as the npm command, so the rule reads npm --cache view ci as
    #   npm view, a step that runs no code of the tree, and reports artifact-poisoning.download, not
    #   artifact-poisoning.executed.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the artifact = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: npm --cache view ci runs the script preinstall,
    #   which prints PWNED, in the job.
    on: push
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: dawidd6/action-download-artifact@v3
            with:
              name: out
          - run: npm --cache view ci
    ```
- script-label: a label that a workflow of the same repository adds from what an attacker wrote, with a token other than the GITHUB_TOKEN, by a script (gh pr edit --add-label, the labels endpoint of the REST API through gh api, addLabels of actions/github-script) or by an action other than actions/labeler: the label is on the pull request or the issue of the attacker, and the rule does not read the scripts and the actions that add labels
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed, artifact-poisoning.download
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - example: .github/workflows/labeled.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: labeler.yml runs on pull_request_target and adds the label
    #   safe-to-test with gh and a personal access token to a pull request whose
    #   title has [site]; labeled.yml runs on pull_request_target on labeled when
    #   the label is safe-to-test, and the job downloads the artifact out of the
    #   run that the output of a step names, and runs ./out/publish.sh.
    # reason: the attacker writes the title of the pull request, and a label that
    #   a personal access token adds starts the labeled run, so no person approves
    #   the run before the label starts the run.
    # cause: the rule reads the steps of actions/labeler, and does not read the
    #   scripts that add labels.
    # attack-value: the title of the pull request = "[site] fix"
    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork whose
    #   title has [site]; gh adds the label safe-to-test, which starts
    #   labeled.yml, and when the step names a run of the workflow build.yml of
    #   the pull request, the download puts the out/publish.sh of the attacker in
    #   out, and the step runs the file, which prints PWNED, with the secrets of
    #   the repository.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    jobs:
      build:
        if: github.event.label.name == 'safe-to-test'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: run
            run: echo "id=$(gh run list --workflow build.yml --json databaseId -q '.[0].databaseId')" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            env:
              GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
            with:
              name: out
              path: out
              run-id: ${{ steps.run.outputs.id }}
              github-token: ${{ github.token }}
          - run: ./out/publish.sh
    ```
    - .github/workflows/labeler.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: pull_request_target
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        label:
          if: contains(github.event.pull_request.title, '[site]')
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: gh pr edit "$PR" --repo "$REPO" --add-label safe-to-test
              env:
                GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.LABELER_PAT }}
                PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
                REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
      ```
- outside-bot-label: a label that a bot outside the repository adds, such as a bot that adds a label for a command in a comment: the settings of the bot are outside the repository, and the rule does not read whether the bot adds the label for a comment of any user
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed, artifact-poisoning.download
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: outside-bot-label.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a bot outside the repository adds the label safe-to-test when a
    #   comment /ok-to-test is posted on a pull request; labeled.yml runs on
    #   pull_request_target on labeled when the label is safe-to-test, and the job
    #   downloads the artifact out of the run that the output of a step names, and
    #   runs ./out/publish.sh.
    # reason: whether the bot adds the label for a comment of any user, or only
    #   for a comment of a member of the organization that owns the repository, is
    #   in the settings of the bot, which are outside the repository; when the bot
    #   adds the label for a comment of any user, no person approves the run
    #   before the label starts the run.
    # cause: the rule does not read the bots outside the repository that add
    #   labels.
    # attack-value: the file out/publish.sh in the artifact of a run of the pull request = "#!/bin/sh\necho PWNED\n"
    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork and
    #   comments /ok-to-test; when the bot adds the label for the comment, when
    #   the step names a run of the workflow build.yml of the pull request, the
    #   download puts the out/publish.sh of the attacker in out, and the step runs
    #   the file, which prints PWNED, with the secrets of the repository.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    jobs:
      build:
        if: github.event.label.name == 'safe-to-test'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: run
            run: echo "id=$(gh run list --workflow build.yml --json databaseId -q '.[0].databaseId')" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            env:
              GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
            with:
              name: out
              path: out
              run-id: ${{ steps.run.outputs.id }}
              github-token: ${{ github.token }}
          - run: ./out/publish.sh
    ```
- labeler-pull-request: actions/labeler in a workflow on pull_request with a token other than the GITHUB_TOKEN: a run on the event pull_request for a pull request from a fork gets the secret of the token only when a private repository sends secrets to the runs of pull requests from forks (repo.fork-pr-secrets), and the rule does not read the workflows on pull_request that add labels

    # attack-value: the file out/publish.sh in the artifact of a run of the pull request = "#!/bin/sh\necho PWNED\n"
    # attack-run-behavior: when the repository sends secrets to the runs of pull

            env:

          - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4

- remote-callee: a job or a step inside a reusable workflow of another repository (uses: owner/repo/.github/workflows/&lt;file>@&lt;ref>) whose content the fact workflow.definition does not give. For every rule: a run that does not ask the fact (a run without --online and without the answer in --facts). For a quality rule, also: a run where the linter asked the fact and got no answer (an answer of unknown: the GitHub API did not give the file), and a call deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact. The rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition. For a rule that is not a quality rule (a rule with a threat), the last two forms are the inconclusive kind remote-callee-unknown, not this form
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed, artifact-poisoning.download
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-callee.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
    #   the repository example-org/artifact-poisoning-unanswered, whose content
    #   is the workflow of the true positive executed (executed.push-search.yml)
    #   of the rule, with on: workflow_call in place of the on of
    #   executed.push-search.yml. The linter has no answer of the fact
    #   workflow.definition for the reusable workflow.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event
    #   that started the run of the calling job, and the linter does not read
    #   the reusable workflow.
    # cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from
    #   the answer of workflow.definition.
    # attack-value: the file build.sh in the artifact named out, from the fork's pull_request run of the workflow = "echo PWNED\n"
    # attack-run-behavior: the pull request from a fork changes the workflow to
    #   run on pull_request too, and the pull_request run uploads build.sh in
    #   the artifact named out; the next push run takes that run, the newest
    #   successful one, and bash build.sh prints PWNED in a job that has the
    #   base repository's secrets and a token of actions: read.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/artifact-poisoning-unanswered/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

### inconclusive

- download-input-unknown: a download whose token, run-id, repository, run_id or repo has what a step or a job computes, an input other than one of workflow_dispatch (or an input of workflow_dispatch in a workflow that also has workflow_call, when a workflow on an event of a pull request calls the workflow), an env, a matrix or a variable, or whose with is a whole \${{ }}: which run it takes is not analyzed
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: download-input-unknown.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on workflow_run, a step computes a run id and writes it to
    #   $GITHUB_OUTPUT; actions/download-artifact takes its run-id from that
    #   output, and ./run.sh runs after it.
    # reason: the run-id is what a step computes, so which run the download
    #   takes is not analyzed.
    # attack-value: the file run.sh in the artifact of the pull request's ci run = "#!/bin/sh\necho PWNED\n"
    # attack-run-behavior: when steps.find.outputs.id names the ci run of the
    #   fork's pull request (the example writes 1; a step that looks up
    #   workflow_run.id would give that run), the download takes its artifact
    #   into the workspace, and ./run.sh runs it, which prints PWNED, with the
    #   base repository's secrets.
    on:
      workflow_run:
        workflows: [ci]
        types: [completed]
    permissions: {actions: read}
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: find
            run: echo "id=1" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
            with:
              run-id: ${{ steps.find.outputs.id }}
              github-token: ${{ github.token }}
          - run: ./run.sh
    ```
  - example: .github/workflows/labeled.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: labeler.yml runs, on pull_request_target,
    #   actions/checkout@v4 of the head of the pull request, which the guard of
    #   actions/checkout stops, and then actions/labeler with if: always() and a
    #   personal access token; the configuration .github/labeler.yml adds the
    #   label safe-to-test to a pull request that changes a file under site/;
    #   labeled.yml runs on pull_request_target on labeled when the label is
    #   safe-to-test, and the job downloads the artifact out of the run that the
    #   output of a step names, and runs ./out/publish.sh.
    # reason: actions/labeler runs after the checkout fails, because of
    #   always(), on the pull request of the attacker, so no person approves the
    #   labeled run before the label starts the run; the run-id of the download
    #   is what a step computes, so which run the download takes is not
    #   analyzed.
    # attack-value: the file out/publish.sh in the artifact of a run of the pull request = "#!/bin/sh\necho PWNED\n"
    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork that
    #   changes a file under site/ and the files of the attack; actions/labeler
    #   adds the label safe-to-test, which starts labeled.yml, and when the step
    #   names a run of the workflow build.yml of the pull request, the download
    #   puts the out/publish.sh of the attacker in out, and the step runs the
    #   file, which prints PWNED, with the secrets of the repository.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    jobs:
      build:
        if: github.event.label.name == 'safe-to-test'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: run
            run: echo "id=$(gh run list --workflow build.yml --json databaseId -q '.[0].databaseId')" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            env:
              GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
            with:
              name: out
              path: out
              run-id: ${{ steps.run.outputs.id }}
              github-token: ${{ github.token }}
          - run: ./out/publish.sh
    ```
    - .github/labeler.yml (repo-file)
      ```yaml
      safe-to-test:
        - changed-files:
            - any-glob-to-any-file: 'site/**'
      ```
    - .github/workflows/labeler.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: pull_request_target
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        label:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
              with:
                ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
            - uses: actions/labeler@v5
              if: always()
              with:
                repo-token: ${{ secrets.LABELER_PAT }}
      ```
- input-dispatch: a download whose token, run-id, repository, run_id or repo has a \${{ }} that refers to an input of workflow_dispatch (inputs, github.event.inputs), alone or with other values: whoever dispatches the workflow chooses the value of the input. A credential whose only write access is to the permission Actions can dispatch the workflow, and the credential premise keeps the holder of such a credential as a possible attacker; the linter does not know whether such a credential exists or who holds it. The rule reports the value in a job with an environment that has required reviewers too, where a required reviewer of the environment can stop the run
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: dispatcher)
  - example: input-dispatch.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on workflow_dispatch, dawidd6/action-download-artifact takes
    #   the artifact of the run that the input run names, and ./out/publish.sh
    #   runs.
    # reason: whoever dispatches the workflow chooses the value of the input,
    #   and the workflow does not tell who that is, so whether an attacker
    #   chooses the run is not known; nothing the rule could read is expected
    #   to tell it.
    # attack-value: inputs.run = "1234"
    # attack-run-behavior: when the one who dispatches the workflow gives as
    #   the input run the ID 1234 of a pull_request run of a pull request from
    #   a fork, whose workflow uploads out/publish.sh that prints PWNED, the
    #   download puts the file in out, and ./out/publish.sh runs it, which
    #   prints PWNED, with the secrets of the repository.
    on:
      workflow_dispatch:
        inputs:
          run: {type: string}
    jobs:
      publish:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: dawidd6/action-download-artifact@v6
            with:
              run_id: ${{ inputs.run }}
              name: out
              path: out
          - run: ./out/publish.sh
    ```
- download-path-unknown: a download whose path is absolute, under \~, a \${{ }} other than runner.temp and github.workspace, a Windows path, or leaves by ..: whether it is in the workspace is not known from the workflow (on a self-hosted runner /tmp and /var can hold the workspace)
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: download-path-unknown.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml

    #   actions/download-artifact puts the artifact of the triggering run in
    #   /tmp/artifacts, and ./run.sh runs after it.
    # reason: the path is absolute; whether it is in the workspace is not known
    #   from the workflow, because on a self-hosted runner /tmp and /var can
    #   hold the workspace.
    # attack-value: the file run.sh in the artifact of the pull request's ci run = "#!/bin/sh\necho PWNED\n"
    # attack-run-behavior: when the self-hosted runner's workspace is
    #   /tmp/artifacts, the download puts run.sh in it, and ./run.sh runs it,
    #   which prints PWNED, with the base repository's secrets.
    on:
      workflow_run:
        workflows: [ci]
        types: [completed]
    permissions: {actions: read}
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: [self-hosted]
        steps:
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
            with:
              run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
              github-token: ${{ github.token }}
              path: /tmp/artifacts
          - run: ./run.sh
    ```

- labeler-unknown: a job on pull_request_target with the activity type labeled, where the run of the job starts when a workflow of the repository of the job adds a label to the pull request of an attacker by running actions/labeler with a token other than the GITHUB_TOKEN (a label that a step adds with a token other than the GITHUB_TOKEN starts a run with the activity type labeled), where the linter does not know at least one of the following: the release of actions/labeler;
