- remote-callee-unknown: a job that calls a reusable workflow of another repository, when the linter asked the fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow and got no answer (the token that the linter uses cannot read the file, the file is larger than the limit, or the linter has used up the requests it may send to the GitHub API), or when the call is deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact: the rule does not read the jobs and the steps of the reusable workflow
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-callee-unknown.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
    #   the repository example-org/artifact-poisoning-unknown, whose content is
    #   the workflow of the true positive executed (executed.push-search.yml) of
    #   the rule, with on: workflow_call in place of the on of
    #   executed.push-search.yml. The linter asked the fact workflow.definition
    #   for the reusable workflow and got no answer.
    # reason: what the jobs of the reusable workflow do is in the file that the
    #   linter could not read; whoever changes the uses, such as the author of a
    #   pull request, can name a reusable workflow that the token that the
    #   linter uses cannot read.
    # attack-value: the file build.sh in the artifact named out, from the fork's pull_request run of the workflow = "echo PWNED\n"
    # attack-run-behavior: the pull request from a fork changes the workflow to
    #   run on pull_request too, and the pull_request run uploads build.sh in
    #   the artifact named out; the next push run takes that run, the newest
    #   successful one, and bash build.sh prints PWNED in a job that has the
    #   base repository's secrets and a token of actions: read.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/artifact-poisoning-unknown/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

### false positive forms

- approval-if: an if of the job that keeps out the runs of forks (github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name == github.repository), when the run before it is of pull_request: a run of pull_request_target or issue_comment before it has the repository as its head too, and which it is is in that workflow
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed, artifact-poisoning.download
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - example: approval-if.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the job runs on workflow_run, downloads the artifact of the run
    #   before it and runs npm ci, but only when the head repository of that run
    #   is the repository itself, so not for a run of a fork's pull request,
    #   whose head repository is the fork.
    # reason: when the run before it is a pull_request run, no run of an
    #   attacker's passes the if.
    # cause: a run of pull_request_target or issue_comment that an attacker
    #   triggers has the repository as its head too, and which it is is in the
    #   workflow before it, which the rule does not read; so it does not take
    #   the if as keeping the attacker out.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the artifact of the pull request's ci run = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: for a ci run of the fork's pull request,
    #   workflow_run.head_repository is the fork, so the if is false and the job
    #   is skipped: nothing is downloaded, and npm ci does not run.
    on:
      workflow_run:
        workflows: [ci]
        types: [completed]
    permissions: {actions: read}
    jobs:
      a:
        if: github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name == github.repository
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
            with:
              run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
              github-token: ${{ github.token }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
- search-filter: a search of the runs of a workflow by dawidd6/action-download-artifact (no input run_id, or an input run_id that is empty on the event of the job) with the input event push, or, in a job on push, with the input commit \${{ github.sha }}: the search then lists only the push runs of the workflow, or only the runs of the commit pushed to the repository, and those runs run the workflow of a commit pushed to the repository. In contrast, with any other input event the finding holds: with pull_request, pull_request_target, pull_request_review or pull_request_review_comment, the list keeps the runs that a pull request from a fork starts, and with issue_comment or workflow_run, the list keeps runs whose artifacts can hold the files of a pull request from a fork (a run that builds the head of the pull request, or a run that uploads again the artifact of a run of a fork)
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed, artifact-poisoning.download
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: search-filter.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, the job downloads with
    #   dawidd6/action-download-artifact v20, with the input event push, the
    #   artifact named out, from the newest push run of its own workflow into
    #   the workspace, and then runs build.sh with bash.
    # reason: the input event push makes the search list only the push runs of
    #   the workflow, which run the workflow of a commit pushed to the
    #   repository; no run of a pull request from a fork, and no run of a review
    #   of such a pull request, is in the list.
    # cause: the rule does not read the inputs event and commit, by which the
    #   search lists the runs.
    # attack-value: the file build.sh in the artifact named out, from the fork's pull_request run of the workflow = "echo PWNED\n"
    # attack-run-behavior: the pull request from a fork changes the workflow to
    #   run on pull_request too, and the pull_request run uploads build.sh in
    #   the artifact named out; the next push run lists only the push runs,
    #   takes the artifact of the newest push run, which a push to the
    #   repository made, and bash build.sh runs that build.sh, not the
    #   attacker's.
    on: push
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: dawidd6/action-download-artifact@v20
            with:
              name: out
              event: push
          - run: bash build.sh
    ```
- no-exec-bit: a file of the artifact run by its path with no chmod (./x.sh, or after a wrapper such as sudo ./x.sh): the files of an artifact lose their mode, so the step fails and runs nothing
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: no-exec-bit.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the job runs on workflow_run, downloads the artifact of the run
    #   before it and runs ./build.sh with no chmod.
    # reason: the files of an artifact lose their mode ("File permissions are
    #   not maintained during zipped artifact upload. All directories will have
    #   755 and all files will have 644.", the README of
    #   actions/upload-artifact,
    #   https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact/blob/043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a/README.md#permission-loss),
    #   so ./build.sh fails and runs nothing.
    # cause: the rule reads a step that names ./build.sh as running what the
    #   download put, and does not ask whether the file can be executed.
    # attack-value: the file build.sh in the artifact of the pull request's ci run = "#!/bin/sh\necho PWNED\n"
    # attack-run-behavior: the download puts build.sh in the workspace with mode
    #   644, and ./build.sh fails with permission denied, so the echo PWNED in
    #   it does not run.
    on:
      workflow_run:
        workflows: [ci]
        types: [completed]
    permissions: {actions: read}
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
            with:
              run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
              github-token: ${{ github.token }}
          - run: ./build.sh
    ```
- written-after-checkout: a job that uploads an artifact in the same workflow run as the job that downloads the artifact, checks out the code of the pull request into the root of the workspace (with no input path of actions/checkout), runs no code of the checkout, and uploads only files that a later step of the same job creates or overwrites with > (not appends to with >>), such as a file into which echo writes the number of the pull request: the rule takes every file under the directory of the checkout as code of the pull request, and every file of the workspace is under the root of the workspace, so the rule reads the artifact as holding code of the pull request, though the artifact holds only the files that the job wrote
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed, artifact-poisoning.download
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: written-after-checkout.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, the job build checks out the head of
    #   the pull request into the root of the workspace, runs nothing of the
    #   checkout, writes the number of the pull request into number.txt and
    #   uploads number.txt; the job deploy, which lists build in its needs,
    #   downloads the artifact and runs ./run.sh, a file that the artifact does
    #   not hold, so the step ./run.sh fails.
    # reason: the artifact holds number.txt only, which a run step of build
    #   writes from the number that GitHub gives the pull request, and holds no
    #   file of the checkout, so ./run.sh does not run what the author of the
    #   pull request wrote.
    # cause: the checkout has no input path of actions/checkout, so the
    #   directory of the checkout is the root of the workspace, and the rule
    #   takes the upload of any file under the root as an upload of the code of
    #   the pull request.
    # attack-value: the file run.sh in the pull request's head = "#!/bin/sh\necho PWNED\n"
    # attack-run-behavior: the checkout puts the head of the pull request in the
    #   workspace of build, and no step runs a file of the checkout; the upload
    #   takes number.txt only, so the download in deploy puts no run.sh of the
    #   pull request in the workspace.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: echo ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }} > number.txt
          - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
            with: {name: out, path: number.txt}
      deploy:
        needs: build
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
            with: {name: out}
          - run: ./run.sh
    ```
- unknown-version: a ref of actions/download-artifact whose version is not known (a branch such as releases/v2, which moves), which the rule reads as v4 or later: the worst case, as v4 or later reads the inputs run-id and github-token and can take the artifact of another run
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed, artifact-poisoning.download
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: unknown-version.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on workflow_run, the job downloads with the branch releases/v2
    #   of actions/download-artifact, with the input run-id
    #   github.event.workflow_run.id (the run that started this workflow) and a
    #   token, into the workspace, and then runs npm ci.
    # reason: the branch releases/v2 is a version before v4, whose inputs are
    #   name and path only: the download takes the artifacts of the current run,
    #   which no pull request from a fork drives, whatever the input run-id is.
    # cause: the version of a branch is not known, and the rule reads it as v4
    #   or later, which reads the inputs run-id and github-token.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the artifact of the pull request's ci run = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: the branch releases/v2 reads no input run-id, so the
    #   download takes no artifact of the fork's ci run, and npm ci reads no
    #   package.json of the pull request.
    on:
      workflow_run:
        workflows: [ci]
        types: [completed]
    permissions:
      actions: read
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@releases/v2
            with:
              run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
              github-token: ${{ github.token }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
- not-executed: a job that runs nothing it downloaded, such as one that only publishes it
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.download
  - fact kinds:
    - download.executed (provider: user-supplied, answer that removes the finding: false)
  - example: not-executed.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the job runs on workflow_run, downloads the artifact of the run
    #   before it, and only counts the lines of what it downloaded.
    # reason: the job runs none of what it downloaded.
    # cause: unless a file of facts or --fact says that no step runs what the
    #   download puts in the workspace (download.executed false), the rule reports
    #   the finding, also when no step is seen to run it. When no file of facts
    #   and no --fact answers download.executed, the finding is conditional.
    # attack-value: the file build.sh in the artifact of the pull request's ci run = "#!/bin/sh\necho PWNED\n"
    # attack-run-behavior: the download puts the artifact's files in the
    #   workspace, and the job only runs wc -l report.txt, which counts lines;
    #   build.sh does not run.
    on:
      workflow_run:
        workflows: [ci]
        types: [completed]
    permissions: {actions: read}
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
            with:
              run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
              github-token: ${{ github.token }}
          - run: wc -l report.txt
    ```
- remote-not-executed: a job of a reusable workflow of another repository that runs nothing it downloaded, as in the form not-executed: the fact download.executed names a step of the input and cannot name a step of a reusable workflow of another repository, so no answer of the fact removes the finding
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.download
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-not-executed.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the job on workflow_run calls the reusable workflow w.yml of
    #   the repository example-org/remote-download-workflow, whose job downloads
    #   the artifact of the run before it and only counts the lines of what it
    #   downloaded.
    # reason: the job of the reusable workflow runs none of what it downloaded.
    # cause: when no step is seen to run the download, the rule takes it as run;
    #   the fact download.executed names a step of the input, and has no form for
    #   a step of a reusable workflow of another repository, so a file of facts
    #   cannot remove the finding.
    # attack-value: the file build.sh in the artifact of the pull request's ci run = "#!/bin/sh\necho PWNED\n"
    # attack-run-behavior: the download puts the artifact's files in the
    #   workspace, and the job of the reusable workflow only runs wc -l
    #   report.txt, which counts lines; build.sh does not run.
    on:
      workflow_run:
        workflows: [ci]
        types: [completed]
    permissions: {actions: read}
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/remote-download-workflow/.github/workflows/w.yml@v1
    ```
- environment-protected: a job whose environment has required reviewers, who approve it before it runs
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed, artifact-poisoning.download
  - fact kinds:
    - repo.environment-protected (provider: repo-setting, answer that removes the finding: true)
  - example: environment-protected.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the job runs on workflow_run in the environment production,
    #   downloads the artifact of the run before it and runs npm ci.
    # reason: the environment production has required reviewers, who approve the
    #   job before it runs.
    # cause: unless a file of facts or --fact says that the environment has
    #   required reviewers (repo.environment-protected true), the rule reports the
    #   finding. When no source answers repo.environment-protected, the finding is
    #   conditional.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the artifact of the pull request's ci run = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: the job waits until a required reviewer of production
    #   approves it; a reviewer who sees that the run before it is of a fork's
    #   pull request does not approve, and nothing is downloaded or run.
    on:
      workflow_run:
        workflows: [ci]
        types: [completed]
    permissions: {actions: read}
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        environment: production
        steps:
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
            with:
              run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
              github-token: ${{ github.token }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
- default-token-read: a job that writes no permissions, in a repository whose default token is read: the token reads no artifact of another run
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed, artifact-poisoning.download
  - fact kinds:
    - repo.default-token-write (provider: repo-setting, answer that removes the finding: false)
  - example: default-token-read.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the job runs on workflow_run, writes no permissions, downloads
    #   the artifact of the run before it with github.token and runs npm ci.
    # reason: the repository's default token is read, which reads no artifact of
    #   another run.
    # cause: unless a file of facts or --fact says that the default token is read
    #   (repo.default-token-write false), the rule treats the default token as a
    #   token that may write and reports the finding. When no source answers
    #   repo.default-token-write, the finding is conditional.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the artifact of the pull request's ci run = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: the job's github.token is the repository's default,
    #   read, which cannot read the artifacts of another run, so the download
    #   fails and the job stops before npm ci; the preinstall does not run.
    on:
      workflow_run:
        workflows: [ci]
        types: [completed]
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
            with:
              run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
              github-token: ${{ github.token }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
- npm-unknown-command: a command that runs npm with a word that is not an option and is not the name, an alias name, or the beginning of exactly one name of an npm command, before the name of an npm command that runs code of the checked out tree (for example, npm web ci), in a run step or in a permission of an agent. npm stops with an error at the first word that is not an option when the word is not the name of an npm command, and runs no code of the tree. The rule reads the first word after npm, other than the value of the option --prefix or -C, that is the name or the alias name of an npm command as the npm command.
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: npm-unknown-command.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a job downloads the artifact out of the latest run of
    #   the workflow into the workspace and runs npm web ci.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): npm stops with an error at web, the
    #   first word that is not an option, because web is not the name, an alias
    #   name or the beginning of exactly one name of an npm command, and npm
    #   runs no code of the artifact.
    # cause: the rule reads the first word after npm that is the name of an
    #   npm command, ci, as the npm command, so the rule reports artifact-poisoning.executed.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the artifact = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: npm web ci stops with the error Unknown command and
    #   does not run the script preinstall, so PWNED is not printed.
    on: push
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: dawidd6/action-download-artifact@v3
            with:
              name: out
          - run: npm web ci
    ```
- npm-option-value-operand: a command that runs npm version, npm uninstall, npm explore or npm edit with no operand, but with an option whose value the rule reads as an operand (for example, npm version --preid beta), in a run step or in a permission of an agent. In that case, npm runs no code of the checked out tree. The rule reads every word after the npm command that is not an option, other than the value of the option --prefix or -C, as an operand.
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: npm-option-value-operand.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a job downloads the artifact out of the latest run of
    #   the workflow into the workspace and runs npm version --preid beta.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): npm version with no operand prints the
    #   version of the package.json and runs no script of the artifact; beta is the
    #   value of the option --preid.
    # cause: the rule reads beta as an operand of npm version, so the rule
    #   reports artifact-poisoning.executed.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the artifact = "{\"scripts\":{\"preversion\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: npm version --preid beta prints the version and does
    #   not run the script preversion, so PWNED is not printed.
    on: push
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: dawidd6/action-download-artifact@v3
            with:
              name: out
          - run: npm version --preid beta
    ```
- cd-out-of-tree: a run step with a command that changes the directory of the shell or of a tool (cd, pushd, popd, env -C, sudo -D, and in pwsh a word that is Set-Location or one of its aliases), in which a tool runs in a directory out of the checked out tree (for example, cd \${{ runner.temp }} && npm ci, after a checkout of the tree into the directory pr). The rule does not read the directory that the command changes to, and reads every tool of the step as a tool that may run in any directory.
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: cd-out-of-tree.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a job downloads the artifact out of the latest run of
    #   the workflow into the directory pr and runs cd ${{ runner.temp }} && npm ci.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the step changes its directory to runner.temp,
    #   out of the artifact, which the job puts into the directory pr, and npm ci reads
    #   the package.json of runner.temp, so npm runs no code of the artifact.
    # cause: the rule does not read the directory that a cd command changes
    #   to, and reads npm ci of a step with a cd command as a tool that may run
    #   in any directory, so the rule reports artifact-poisoning.executed.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the artifact = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: npm ci in runner.temp finds no package.json of the
    #   attacker and does not run the script preinstall, so PWNED is not
    #   printed.
    on: push
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: dawidd6/action-download-artifact@v3
            with:
              name: out
              path: pr
          - run: cd ${{ runner.temp }} && npm ci
    ```
- ignored-pnpmfile: a command that runs a pnpm command that runs no code of the checked out tree, with the pnpm setting ignore-pnpmfile set to true (for example, pnpm --config.ignore-pnpmfile=true store prune), in a run step or in a permission of an agent. pnpm loads no .pnpmfile.cjs of the tree when the pnpm setting ignore-pnpmfile is true. The rule reads every run of pnpm as a run that runs code of the tree.
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: ignored-pnpmfile.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a job downloads the artifact out of the latest run of
    #   the workflow into the workspace and runs pnpm
    #   --config.ignore-pnpmfile=true store prune.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): pnpm loads no .pnpmfile.cjs of the tree
    #   when the pnpm setting ignore-pnpmfile is true, and the pnpm command
    #   store prune runs no script of the package.json, so pnpm runs no code of
    #   the artifact; the job still puts the files of the artifact in the
    #   workspace, which the finding artifact-poisoning.download says.
    # cause: the rule reads every run of pnpm as a run that runs code of the
    #   tree, so the rule reports artifact-poisoning.executed.
    # attack-value: the file .pnpmfile.cjs in the artifact out = "console.log('PWNED')"
    # attack-run-behavior: pnpm --config.ignore-pnpmfile=true store prune does
    #   not load the .pnpmfile.cjs of the artifact, so PWNED is not printed.
    on: push
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: dawidd6/action-download-artifact@v3
            with:
              name: out
          - run: pnpm --config.ignore-pnpmfile=true store prune
    ```
- absolute-path-out-of-tree: a command that runs a tool in a directory, or runs a file, that a path out of the checked out tree names, when the path is an absolute path that names the directory of a tool or a file given to an interpreter, or a path that leaves the workspace by .. (for example, pnpm --dir /opt/tool install, bash /opt/x.sh, or npm --prefix ../other ci after a checkout of the tree into the directory pr), in a run step or in a permission of an agent. The rule reads an absolute path, and a path that leaves the workspace by .., as a path that may name a directory of the tree, because the workspace that holds the tree also has an absolute path, and a path that leaves the workspace by .. may come back into the workspace.
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: absolute-path-out-of-tree.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a job downloads the artifact out of the latest run of
    #   the workflow under runner.temp and runs pnpm --dir /opt/tool install.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): pnpm runs in /opt/tool, out of the artifact, and loads the
    #   .pnpmfile.cjs and the package.json of /opt/tool, so pnpm runs no code
    #   of the artifact, which the download puts under runner.temp.
    # cause: the rule reads the absolute path /opt/tool as a path that may name
    #   a directory of the tree, so the rule reports artifact-poisoning.executed.
    # attack-value: the file .pnpmfile.cjs in the artifact = "console.log('PWNED')"
    # attack-run-behavior: pnpm --dir /opt/tool install does not load the .pnpmfile.cjs
    #   of the attacker, so PWNED is not printed.
    on: push
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: dawidd6/action-download-artifact@v3
            with:
              name: out
              path: ${{ runner.temp }}/out
          - run: pnpm --dir /opt/tool install
    ```
- pytest-path-out-of-tree: a command that runs pytest, in a directory of the checked out tree or in a directory that holds the tree, with only paths out of the tree as its arguments (for example, pytest /opt/tests run in the root of the tree, or pytest tests run in the root of the workspace when the tree is in the directory pr), in a run step or in a permission of an agent. In that case, pytest collects no test and loads no conftest.py of the tree. The rule reads the directory that pytest runs in, and every directory under it, as directories whose tests pytest collects.
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: pytest-path-out-of-tree.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a job downloads the artifact out of the latest run of
    #   the workflow under runner.temp and runs pytest /opt/tests.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): pytest collects the tests of /opt/tests only, and loads no
    #   conftest.py and no test of the directory it runs in, so pytest runs no
    #   code of the artifact, which the download puts under runner.temp.
    # cause: the rule reads the directory that pytest runs in as a directory
    #   whose tests pytest collects, so the rule reports artifact-poisoning.executed.
    # attack-value: the file conftest.py in the artifact = "import os; os.system('echo PWNED')"
    # attack-run-behavior: pytest /opt/tests does not import the conftest.py of the
    #   attacker, so PWNED is not printed.
    on: push
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: dawidd6/action-download-artifact@v3
            with:
              name: out
              path: ${{ runner.temp }}/out
          - run: pytest /opt/tests
    ```
- tool-directory-out-of-tree: a command that runs a tool, or runs a file by a relative path, in a directory out of the checked out tree that the working-directory of the step, the defaults of the job or of the workflow, or an option of the tool names (for example, npm ci with the working-directory \${{ runner.temp }}, or pnpm -C \${{ runner.temp }}/tool install), in a run step or in a permission of an agent. The rule also reads the tool as a tool that may run in the root of the workspace, because the tool may read the tree in a way that the rule does not read.
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: tool-directory-out-of-tree.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a job downloads the artifact out of the latest run of
    #   the workflow into the workspace, and a later step runs npm ci with the
    #   working-directory ${{ runner.temp }}.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): npm ci runs in runner.temp, out of
    #   the artifact, and reads the package.json of runner.temp, so npm runs no
    #   code of the artifact.
    # cause: the rule also reads a tool whose directory is out of the tree as
    #   a tool that may run in the root of the workspace, so the rule reports
    #   artifact-poisoning.executed.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the artifact = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: npm ci in runner.temp finds no package.json of the
    #   attacker and does not run the script preinstall, so PWNED is not
    #   printed.
    on: push
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: dawidd6/action-download-artifact@v3
            with:
              name: out
          - run: npm ci
            working-directory: ${{ runner.temp }}
    ```
- callee: a reusable workflow or a composite action when all of the following are true: the rule does not know all of the callers of the reusable workflow or the composite action; every workflow that runs the reusable workflow or the composite action (directly, or through another reusable workflow or composite action) is a workflow in the same repository; and the rule would report no finding of the finding kind if the rule read the reusable workflow or the composite action only on the events on which the workflows in the same repository run the reusable workflow or the composite action (for example, every workflow that runs the reusable workflow or the composite action runs only on push). When the rule does not know all of the callers, the rule can read the reusable workflow or the composite action on every event (the worst case). For example, the rule does not know all of the callers when no caller is among the inputs; when the inputs are not the whole repository; for a composite action, when an input is excluded or cannot be read; when a caller names the reusable workflow or the composite action by a name of the form owner/repo/path@ref instead of by a ./ path, in which owner/repo is the repository that the --repo flag names, or is any repository when no --repo flag is given; when a step names the composite action by a ./ path, and either no checkout step runs before that step or the last checkout step before that step is not a plain checkout step (a plain checkout step has no ref input, no repository input and no path input); when a step inside a composite action names another composite action by a ./ path; or when the rule does not know all of the callers of a caller
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed, artifact-poisoning.download
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - example: .github/workflows/called.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: ci.yml of the repository o/r calls this reusable workflow on
    #   push only, by the name o/r/.github/workflows/called.yml@main, not by the
    #   path ./.github/workflows/called.yml.
    # reason: when the run of the linter names the repository (--repo o/r), the
    #   call by the name is a call of this file, and the only caller runs on
    #   push, which no attacker of the finding kind triggers. A run without
    #   --repo reads the call by the name o/r/.github/workflows/called.yml@main
    #   as a call that may name a file of the repository, because the run does
    #   not know which repository the inputs are; the rule does not resolve the
    #   call to this file, so the rule reads this file on every event and reports
    #   the same finding.
    # cause: the rule does not resolve a call by the name of the repository to
    #   the file, so the rule reads this workflow on every event.
    # attack: the attacker opens an issue, a pull request or a comment with a
    #   value that would reach this workflow on an event of the attacker.
    # attack-run-behavior: only a push to the repository runs ci.yml, which
    #   calls this workflow on push; the run of the push reads no value of the
    #   attacker's issue, pull request or comment.

      workflow_call:
    permissions:
      actions: read
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
            with:
              run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
              github-token: ${{ github.token }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
    - finding on: .github/workflows/called.yml
    - .github/workflows/ci.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: push
      jobs:
        call:
          uses: o/r/.github/workflows/called.yml@main
          secrets: inherit
      ```
- unmatchable-pattern: a label of the configuration of actions/labeler whose globs or regular expressions match no path or no branch name, such as the glob pages/\*\* together with the negated glob !pages/\*\*: the rule reads each glob and each regular expression as one that a pull request can match
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed, artifact-poisoning.download
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: .github/workflows/labeled.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml

    #   personal access token; the configuration .github/labeler.yml adds the
    #   label safe-to-test to a pull request that changes a file that is under
    #   site/ and not under site/, which no file is; labeled.yml runs on
    #   pull_request_target on opened and labeled; the job build checks out the
    #   head of the pull request and uploads dist, and the job deploy, which
    #   needs build and runs on labeled when the if github.event.label.name ==
    #   'safe-to-test' is true, downloads dist and runs ./dist/deploy.sh.
    # reason: no file matches both globs, so actions/labeler never adds the
    #   label, and only a person adds it.
    # cause: the rule reads each glob as one that a pull request can match.
    # attack-value: the file dist/deploy.sh in the artifact dist of the job build = "#!/bin/sh\necho PWNED\n"
    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork that

    #   labeled.yml does not run until a person adds the label safe-to-test.

              persist-credentials: false
          - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
            with: {name: dist, path: dist}

        if: github.event.action == 'labeled' && (github.event.label.name == 'safe-to-test')

        steps:
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
            with: {name: dist}
          - run: ./dist/deploy.sh
    ```

- labeler-skipped-need: a job whose if calls no status function, that runs actions/labeler or waits for the label that actions/labeler adds (on the activity type labeled, in the job itself or in a job of a reusable workflow that the job calls), and that depends through the needs key on a job whose if calls a status function (for example, if: always()), where the job whose if calls a status function depends through the needs key, directly or through other jobs, on a job that GitHub skips, or that fails, in the run on the pull request of the attacker. GitHub applies a failure or a skip to every job after the skipped or failed job in the chain of the needs key, also after the job whose if calls a status function, so GitHub skips the job that runs actions/labeler or waits for the label, and the step of actions/labeler in a skipped job adds no label. The rule reads the ifs of the chain of the needs key only up to the job whose if calls a status function, and reads the job that runs actions/labeler or waits for the label as a job that runs.

    ```yaml
    #   and the observation in https://github.com/actions/runner/issues/2205).

            with: {name: dist, path: dist}
    ```

      ```yaml
        report:

        label:
      ```

- labeler-other-user: a step of actions/labeler whose if is true only when a step before the step of actions/labeler has failed (for example, if: failure()), after a step that has no timeout-minutes and that runs the code of the pull request of the attacker as a user that is neither root nor the user of the shell of the step (for example, sudo -u nobody, or su nobody -c), where a failure of the code does not end the step (for example, the left of || true, or the condition of an if statement of the shell script). The code of the attacker runs as a user that is not the user of the shell of the step, so the code of the attacker cannot stop the shell of the step by a signal, and the step does not fail. The rule reads the step that runs the code of the attacker as a step that the attacker can make fail, so the rule reads the step of actions/labeler as a step that runs after a failure.
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed, artifact-poisoning.download
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: .github/workflows/labeled.yml (workflow, false-positive)

    ```yaml
    #   the step does not fail, and the step of actions/labeler, whose if is

    #   attacker can make fail, so the rule reads the step of actions/labeler as

          - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
            with: {name: dist, path: dist}

        needs: build
        if: github.event.action == 'labeled' && (github.event.label.name == 'safe-to-test')
    ```

- pull-request-target-blocked: a workflow whose on has pull_request_target and no other event (no workflow_call event either), in a repository whose Actions policies block the runs of the workflow on pull_request_target (repo.pull-request-target-allowed false): an event policy that an administrator sets without pull_request_target among the allowed events, or the default policy that GitHub adds to a public repository without an applicable event policy, from the time when GitHub enforces the default policy on the repository. GitHub's documents say that GitHub evaluates the policies before a run, and that a run that a policy does not allow fails with an error. The documents do not say whether a job of such a run starts before the run fails; the rule assumes that no job of such a run starts
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed, artifact-poisoning.download
  - fact kinds:
    - repo.pull-request-target-allowed (provider: repo-setting, answer that removes the finding: false)
  - example: pull-request-target-blocked.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a job downloads the artifact of the ci
    #   run of the pull request, from forks too, into the workspace with
    #   dawidd6/action-download-artifact, and then reads ./build.sh into its shell
    #   by source.
    # reason: the Actions policies of the repository block the runs of the
    #   workflow on pull_request_target: the default policy that GitHub adds to a
    #   public repository without an applicable event policy, from the time when
    #   GitHub enforces the default policy on the repository, or an event policy
    #   whose list of allowed events does not have pull_request_target. GitHub's
    #   documents say that GitHub evaluates the policies before a run, and that a
    #   run that a policy does not allow fails with an error; the documents do not
    #   say whether a job of such a run starts before the run fails, and the rule
    #   assumes that no job starts.
    # cause: unless a file of facts or --fact says that the Actions policies block
    #   runs on pull_request_target (repo.pull-request-target-allowed false), the
    #   rule reports the finding. When no file of facts and no --fact answers
    #   repo.pull-request-target-allowed, the finding is conditional.
    # attack-value: the file build.sh in the artifact of the ci run of the pull request = "echo PWNED\n"
    # attack-run-behavior: the pull request of the attacker triggers
    #   pull_request_target, and the run fails with an error, and no job of the
    #   run starts (the assumption of the reason), so source never reads build.sh.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: dawidd6/action-download-artifact@v6
            with:
              workflow: ci.yml
              pr: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
              allow_forks: true
          - run: source ./build.sh
    ```
- actions-policy: a run that the Actions policies of the repository block, in four cases where the rule does not take the policies into account. First, an event policy that blocks an event of the attackers other than pull_request_target (such as issue_comment) in a workflow whose on has that event: the rules ask a fact only for pull_request_target. Second, an actor rule that does not allow the account of the attacker (for example, an actor rule that allows only the repository roles with write access): repo.pull-request-target-allowed is one value for all the runs of a workflow file on pull_request_target, and an actor rule blocks a run by the account that starts the run, so the fact cannot tell what an actor rule blocks. Third, a workflow whose on has pull_request_target and another event: the rule does not ask repo.pull-request-target-allowed for such a workflow, because a run on the other event can reach the job. When the if of the job is false on the other event, so that the job runs only on pull_request_target, and a policy blocks pull_request_target, the finding is a false positive. Fourth, a reusable workflow (on workflow_call) or an action that only workflows on pull_request_target call: the rule asks repo.pull-request-target-allowed only of a workflow whose on has pull_request_target, not of the reusable workflow or the action, so a finding in the reusable workflow or the action is still reported when the policies block the runs of every caller
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed, artifact-poisoning.download
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: actions-policy.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a job downloads the artifact of the ci
    #   run of the pull request, from forks too, into the workspace with
    #   dawidd6/action-download-artifact, and then reads ./build.sh into its shell
    #   by source.
    # reason: an actor rule of the Actions policies of the repository allows
    #   only the repository roles with write access to trigger the workflow, so a
    #   run that a pull request from an account without write access triggers
    #   fails. GitHub's documents say that GitHub evaluates the policies before a
    #   run, and that a run that a policy does not allow fails with an error; the
    #   documents do not say whether a job of such a run starts before the run
    #   fails, and the rule assumes that no job starts.
    # cause: the rule does not take the actor rules of the Actions policies into
    #   account: repo.pull-request-target-allowed is one value for all the runs of
    #   the workflow file on pull_request_target, and an actor rule blocks a run
    #   by the account that starts the run.
    # attack-value: the file build.sh in the artifact of the ci run of the pull request = "echo PWNED\n"
    # attack-run-behavior: the account of the attacker is not an allowed actor,
    #   so the run on pull_request_target fails with an error, and no job of the
    #   run starts (the assumption of the reason), so source never reads build.sh.
    name: policy
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: dawidd6/action-download-artifact@v6
            with:
              workflow: ci.yml
              pr: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
              allow_forks: true
          - run: source ./build.sh
    ```
- actions-not-allowed: a workflow whose run GitHub does not start, or a job that GitHub fails in the step "Set up job", because of the setting of allowed actions of GitHub (the fact repo.allowed-actions, which the quality rule allowed-actions reads): GitHub does not start a run of a workflow that has a uses, or that calls a reusable workflow that has a uses, that the setting does not allow, and fails a job before any step of the job runs when a step of a composite action that the job runs has a uses that the setting does not allow, or when the setting requires a full commit SHA and a step names an action by a tag or a branch. The harm that the finding reports happens only when GitHub runs the workflow or the job, and the rule does not read repo.allowed-actions
  - finding kinds: artifact-poisoning.executed, artifact-poisoning.download
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: actions-not-allowed.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the workflow of the true positive executed (executed.yml) of
    #   the rule, with a job added whose step uses
    #   example-org/not-allowed-action, which the setting of allowed actions of
    #   GitHub (repo.allowed-actions) blocks with
    #   !example-org/not-allowed-action@*. In the true positive, workflow_run
    #   downloads, with actions/download-artifact and the id of the run that
    #   started it, that run's artifact into the workspace, and then runs npm
    #   ci.
    # reason: GitHub checks each uses of the workflow before the run starts, and
    #   does not start the run because of the uses of
    #   example-org/not-allowed-action: no job of the run runs, so what the
    #   reason of the true positive says does not happen (in runs that the
    #   authors of the rule made on GitHub, such runs ended as startup_failure).
    # cause: the rule does not read repo.allowed-actions.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the artifact of the pull request's ci run = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: GitHub does not start the run, so no step of the run
    #   runs, and the attack does nothing.
    on:
      workflow_run:
        workflows: [ci]
        types: [completed]
    permissions:
      actions: read
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
            with:
              run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
              github-token: ${{ github.token }}
          - run: npm ci
      not-allowed:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: example-org/not-allowed-action@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

### threat

- precondition callers-events: a reusable workflow or a composite action that is among the inputs runs on the events of the callers of the workflow or the action, whoever the callers are; when the inputs are the whole repository and hold every caller of the workflow or the action, the rule reads the workflow or the action on the events of the callers, with the values that the callers give under with
  - cites:
    - <https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows#workflow_call>
    - <https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7x29-qqmq-v6qc>
- precondition attacker-run: the download takes the artifact of a run the attacker drives: actions/download-artifact v4 or later with a token and the input run-id github.event.workflow_run.id, or dawidd6/action-download-artifact in one of three forms: with the input run_id github.event.workflow_run.id; with the input repo of the fork; or with no input run_id, or with an input run_id whose \${{ }} is empty on the event of the job, with which dawidd6/action-download-artifact searches the runs of the workflow. The search takes the run of a pull request from a fork when the input allow_forks is true or the version of dawidd6/action-download-artifact is before v4. Whatever the input allow_forks is, the search also takes the run of a review of a pull request from a fork: the run of the review runs the workflow of the merge commit of the pull request, and the head repository of the run of the review is the base repository. Without a token, actions/download-artifact takes the current run's artifacts
  - observed: 2026-10-04, runner 2.337.0: a pull request from a fork changed the workflow workflow_run follows, on push alone, to run on pull_request under the same name; its run triggered the base's workflow_run, whose download with a token and run-id github.event.workflow_run.id took the fork's artifact; without the token it found none
  - observed: 2026-11-05, runner 2.338.2: a pull request from a fork added pull_request_review to the workflow, and a comment-only review of the pull request started a pull_request_review run of the workflow; the head repository of that run was the base repository, and a job of a later push run, with dawidd6/action-download-artifact v20 and no input allow_forks, did not skip that run and took the artifact of that run
  - cites:
    - <https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/blob/v8.0.1/src/download-artifact.ts>
    - <https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5xr6-xhww-33m4>
    - <https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows#workflow_run>
    - <https://www.legitsecurity.com/blog/artifact-poisoning-vulnerability-discovered-in-rust>
    - <https://github.com/dawidd6/action-download-artifact/blob/09f2f74827fd3a8607589e5ad7f9398816f540fe/main.js>
- precondition download-event: the job runs on an event on which the download takes the attacker's artifact, with the repository's secrets or a token that may write: workflow_run, for a run-id or run_id of github.event.workflow_run.id or a repo of github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name; pull_request_target, for a repo of github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name; and any event of the job, for a search of runs by dawidd6/action-download-artifact, as the search does not filter the runs by the event of the job: push, schedule and workflow_dispatch, which only those who can write to the repository start, count too. A job on pull_request counts only when the pull request is from a branch of the repository: the run of a pull request from a fork runs the workflow of the pull request, which the author of the pull request can change, with a read-only token and no secrets
  - observed: 2026-11-05, runner 2.338.2: a job of a push run, with dawidd6/action-download-artifact v3.1.4 and no input workflow, run_id or allow_forks, took the artifact of the newest run of its workflow, a pull_request run of a pull request from a fork; v20, whose input allow_forks is false by default, skipped that run, whose head repository was the fork
  - cites:
    - <https://github.com/dawidd6/action-download-artifact/blob/09f2f74827fd3a8607589e5ad7f9398816f540fe/main.js>
- precondition no-approval: no one approves the run: either the job runs on at least one event other than pull_request_target with the activity type labeled, and a run on the other event starts with no label added, or no person adds the label that starts the run, as the label is a label that a workflow of the repository of the job adds to the pull request of an attacker by running actions/labeler with a token other than the GITHUB_TOKEN; and the job has no environment that has required reviewers (repo.environment-protected false)
  - observed: 2026-09-28, runner 2.337.0: a push after the label ran no labeled run, and ran pull_request_target on synchronize
- precondition token-reads: the token may read the artifacts of another run: the scope actions, read-all or write-all for the GITHUB_TOKEN, or the repository's permissive default when no permissions are written (repo.default-token-write true); permissions written without actions set it to none
  - cites:
    - <https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/security/github_token>
- precondition into-workspace: the files go into the workspace, where they replace the files a build reads (no path, a relative one, a literal \$RUNNER_TEMP, or a release with the zip-slip of 4.0.0 to 4.1.2), or a step after it names them to run; when none is seen to run, the finding holds if one does (download.executed true)
  - observed: 2026-10-04, runner 2.337.0: actions/download-artifact@v4 with no path put the artifact's x.sh over the x.sh a step before had written in the workspace
  - cites:
    - <https://github.com/github/codeql/blob/f7617abe602d4763cd08c6a57b6a6bc347e7e325/actions/ql/src/Security/CWE-829/ArtifactPoisoningCritical.md>
- actor: fork-pr-author
  - via: opens a pull request from a fork whose run uploads an artifact of their making, which a run of the job downloads
  - events: branch_protection_rule, check_run, check_suite, create, delete, deployment, deployment_status, discussion, discussion_comment, fork, gollum, image_version, interactive_component, issue_comment, issues, label, member, merge_group, milestone, registry_package, page_build, project_card, project_column, project, public, pull_request_review_comment, pull_request_review, pull_request, pull_request_target, push, release, repository_dispatch, status, watch, workflow_run, workflow_dispatch, schedule, dynamic, workflow_call, pull_request_comment
  - run starters: branch_protection_rule: other, check_run: attacker, check_suite: attacker, create: other, delete: other, deployment: other, deployment_status: other, discussion: attacker, discussion_comment: attacker, fork: attacker, gollum: attacker, image_version: other, interactive_component: other, issue_comment: attacker, issues: attacker, label: other, member: other, merge_group: other, milestone: other, registry_package: other, page_build: other, project_card: other, project_column: other, project: other, public: other, pull_request_review_comment: attacker, pull_request_review: attacker, pull_request: attacker, pull_request_target: attacker, push: other, release: other, repository_dispatch: other, status: attacker, watch: attacker, workflow_run: attacker, workflow_dispatch: other, schedule: other, dynamic: other, workflow_call: other, pull_request_comment: other
  - gains: run-code, read-secrets, write-with-token, write-cache

## artipacked

- problem: a step leaves a git credential in .git/config, or, for actions/checkout v6 and later, in a file of RUNNER_TEMP, and actions/upload-artifact after the step puts the file in an artifact, which anyone who can read the repository downloads
- expected: a checkout whose credential is not left (persist-credentials: false), or an upload of only the files the artifact needs
- severity: critical (the worst of its kinds)
- targets: workflow, action-metadata
- facets:
  - weakness: credential-leak
  - attack-means: none
- default run: always: in a run without --rule, the rule runs unless --skip-rule names the rule

### finding kinds

- artipacked.github-token
  - detected: {uses} leaves the job's GITHUB_TOKEN in a file (.git/config, or, for actions/checkout v6 and later, a file of RUNNER_TEMP), and {upload} puts the file in an artifact while the job goes on
  - arguments:
    - {uses}: The uses of the step that leaves the token, as written.
    - {upload}: The uses, as written, of one upload that runs after the step and puts the file of the token in an artifact: the first of those uploads that puts the file in an artifact on no condition, else the first of those uploads.
  - consequence: anyone who can read the repository's artifacts takes the token and writes what the job may write until the job ends
  - remedy: set persist-credentials: false on the checkout, or upload only the files the artifact needs
  - severity: critical (found from the CVSS metrics below by the table)
  - fix kinds: persist-credentials-false
  - fact kinds: repo.default-token-write (provider: repo-setting), git.commit-contains (provider: github)
  - attackers: artifact-reader
  - preconditions: leaves-git-credential, artifact-taken, token-writes
  - incidents: artipacked-2024
  - true positives:
    - github-token.last-step.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: actions/checkout leaves the job's token in .git/config, and
      #   actions/upload-artifact, the last step, uploads the workspace with its
      #   hidden files.
      # reason: include-hidden-files: true puts .git/config, with the token, in
      #   the artifact; v4 artifacts can be downloaded while the run goes on, and
      #   the token, which may write contents, still works through the post steps;
      #   the fixed workflow of quay/clair, whose token was taken this way, had
      #   its upload as the last step.
      # attack: a reader of the repository's artifacts (anyone, in a public
      #   repository) downloads the artifact through the API while the job still
      #   runs, and takes the token from the line
      #   http.https://github.com/.extraheader (AUTHORIZATION: basic, the base64
      #   of x-access-token:<token>) of .git/config.
      # attack-run-behavior: the checkout writes the job's GITHUB_TOKEN, which may
      #   write contents, into .git/config; the upload, with include-hidden-files:
      #   true, puts .git/config in the artifact, which can be downloaded once the
      #   upload ends; the post steps still run after it, and until the job ends
      #   the token pushes to the repository.
      on: push
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          permissions:
            contents: write
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
              with:
                path: .
                include-hidden-files: true
      ```
    - github-token.no-caller.action.yml (action-metadata, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a composite action with no caller among the files that the
      #   linter reads; actions/checkout leaves the token of the job in .git/config,
      #   actions/upload-artifact uploads the workspace with the hidden files, and a
      #   step runs after the upload.
      # reason: include-hidden-files: true puts .git/config, with the token, in
      #   the artifact, which v4 lets anyone who can read the artifacts download as
      #   soon as the upload ends, while the step after the upload keeps the job,
      #   and the token, alive; the job of a workflow that calls the action decides
      #   whether the token may write contents.
      # attack: a reader of the artifacts of the repository (anyone, in a public
      #   repository) downloads the artifact through the API while the job still
      #   runs, and takes the token from the line
      #   http.https://github.com/.extraheader (AUTHORIZATION: basic, the base64 of
      #   x-access-token:<token>) of .git/config.
      # attack-run-behavior: the checkout writes the GITHUB_TOKEN of the job into
      #   .git/config; the upload, with include-hidden-files: true, puts .git/config
      #   in the artifact, which can be downloaded once the upload ends, and while
      #   echo after the upload and the post steps run, the token pushes to the
      #   repository when the token may write contents.
      name: package
      description: upload the workspace
      runs:
        using: composite
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
            with:
              path: .
              include-hidden-files: true
          - run: echo after the upload
            shell: bash
      ```
    - github-token.remote-callee.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
      #   the repository example-org/artipacked-remote, which the fact
      #   workflow.definition answers with the workflow of the true positive
      #   github-token (github-token.last-step.yml) of the rule, with on:
      #   workflow_call in place of the on of github-token.last-step.yml. The job
      #   passes its secrets with secrets: inherit. In the true positive,
      #   actions/checkout leaves the job's token in .git/config, and
      #   actions/upload-artifact, the last step, uploads the workspace with its
      #   hidden files.
      # reason: the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event that started the
      #   run of the calling job, so the reason of the true positive holds:
      #   include-hidden-files: true puts .git/config, with the token, in the
      #   artifact; v4 artifacts can be downloaded while the run goes on, and the
      #   token, which may write contents, still works through the post steps; the
      #   fixed workflow of quay/clair, whose token was taken this way, had its
      #   upload as the last step.
      # attack: a reader of the repository's artifacts (anyone, in a public
      #   repository) downloads the artifact through the API while the job still
      #   runs, and takes the token from the line
      #   http.https://github.com/.extraheader (AUTHORIZATION: basic, the base64
      #   of x-access-token:<token>) of .git/config.
      # attack-run-behavior: the checkout writes the job's GITHUB_TOKEN, which may
      #   write contents, into .git/config; the upload, with include-hidden-files:
      #   true, puts .git/config in the artifact, which can be downloaded once the
      #   upload ends; the post steps still run after it, and until the job ends
      #   the token pushes to the repository.
      on: push
      jobs:
        c:
          uses: example-org/artipacked-remote/.github/workflows/w.yml@v1
          secrets: inherit
      ```
    - github-token.runner-temp.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: actions/checkout v6 leaves the job's token in a file of
      #   RUNNER_TEMP, actions/upload-artifact uploads ${{ runner.temp }}, and a
      #   step runs after it.
      # reason: the path ${{ runner.temp }} puts git-credentials-<uuid>.config,
      #   with the token, in the artifact, before the post step of the checkout
      #   removes the file at the end of the job, and v4 lets anyone who can read
      #   the artifacts download the artifact as soon as the upload ends, while the
      #   step after the upload keeps the job, and the token, which may write
      #   contents, alive.
      # attack: a reader of the repository's artifacts (anyone, in a public
      #   repository) downloads the artifact through the API while the job still
      #   runs, and takes the token from the line of
      #   git-credentials-<uuid>.config that holds the header AUTHORIZATION: basic,
      #   the base64 of x-access-token:<token>.
      # attack-run-behavior: the checkout writes the job's GITHUB_TOKEN, which may
      #   write contents, into git-credentials-<uuid>.config of RUNNER_TEMP; the
      #   upload puts the file in the artifact, which can be downloaded once the
      #   upload ends, and while echo after the upload and the post steps run, the
      #   attacker pushes to the repository with the token.
      on: push
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          permissions:
            contents: write
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v6
            - run: make
            - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
              with:
                name: tmp
                path: ${{ runner.temp }}
            - run: echo after the upload
      ```
    - github-token.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml

      #   actions/upload-artifact uploads the workspace with its hidden files, and
      #   a step runs after it.
      # reason: include-hidden-files: true puts .git/config, with the token, in

      # attack-run-behavior: the checkout writes the job's GITHUB_TOKEN, which may

        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest

            contents: write
      ```
