## bot-conditions

- problem: an if lets only Dependabot in by comparing the actor of the run with dependabot&#91;bot], but the actor is whoever made the latest change: an attacker has Dependabot push to their own pull request, and the run of that push passes the if
- expected: the if compares the author of the pull request (github.event.pull_request.user.login), whom no push changes
- severity: critical
- targets: workflow, action-metadata
- facets:
  - weakness: gate-bypass
  - attack-means: operation
- default run: always: in a run without --rule, the rule runs unless --skip-rule names the rule

### finding kinds

- bot-conditions.dependabot
  - detected: {path} is compared with {literal} in an if on {attacker_on}, and a run of Dependabot's push to the attacker's pull request passes it
  - arguments:
    - {path}: The reference compared, as written, such as github.actor.
    - {literal}: The string or the number that the path is compared with.
    - {attacker_on}: The privileged events the if may run on, each event named once.
  - consequence: an attacker has the job run on their pull request: they comment @dependabot recreate on Dependabot's pull request in their fork, whose branch their pull request is from, and Dependabot's push makes the actor dependabot&#91;bot]
  - remedy: compare the author of the pull request, github.event.pull_request.user.login, which Dependabot's push does not change
  - severity: critical (found from the CVSS metrics below by the table)
  - fix kinds: author-context
  - fact kinds: repo.pull-request-target-allowed (provider: repo-setting)
  - attackers: fork-pr-author
  - preconditions: actor-compared, dependabot-push, callers-events
  - true positives:
    - dependabot.no-caller.action.yml (action-metadata, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a composite action with no caller among the files that the
      #   linter reads; a step runs only on pull_request_target when the actor is
      #   dependabot[bot], and then has gh pr merge --auto --rebase merge the pull
      #   request with the token of the job.
      # reason: with no caller among the files that the linter reads, the rule
      #   reads the action on every event an attacker triggers, pull_request_target
      #   among the events. github.actor names whoever caused the event, not who
      #   wrote the pull request, so the if also lets in a pull request whose last
      #   push Dependabot made, and gh pr merge then merges the code of that pull
      #   request with the token of the job.
      # attack: the attacker enables Dependabot in the attacker's fork, opens a
      #   pull request to this repository from the branch of a pull request
      #   Dependabot opened in the fork, then comments @dependabot recreate on the
      #   pull request of Dependabot in the fork, so that Dependabot pushes to the
      #   branch of the pull request (Synacktiv did so against a copy of
      #   spring-projects/spring-security in 2024, and the file evil.txt of
      #   Synacktiv was merged).
      # attack-run-behavior: the push of Dependabot runs pull_request_target on
      #   synchronize with github.actor dependabot[bot], so the if is true and gh pr
      #   merge --auto --rebase turns on auto-merge for the attacker's pull request
      #   with the token of the job, which GitHub merges once the requirements of
      #   the pull request are met.
      name: merge dependabot
      description: merge the pull requests of Dependabot
      runs:
        using: composite
        steps:
          - if: github.event_name == 'pull_request_target' && github.actor == 'dependabot[bot]'
            run: gh pr merge --auto --rebase "$PR"
            shell: bash
            env:
              PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.html_url }}
              GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      ```
    - dependabot.remote-callee.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
      #   the repository example-org/bot-conditions-remote, which the fact
      #   workflow.definition answers with the workflow of the true positive
      #   dependabot (dependabot.yml) of the rule, with on: workflow_call in place
      #   of the on of dependabot.yml. The job passes its secrets with secrets:
      #   inherit. In the true positive, on pull_request_target, the job runs only
      #   when the actor is dependabot[bot], and then has gh pr merge --auto merge
      #   the pull request with a token that may write contents and pull requests.
      # reason: the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event that started the
      #   run of the calling job, so the reason of the true positive holds:
      #   github.actor names whoever caused the event, not who wrote the pull
      #   request, so the if also lets in a pull request whose last push
      #   Dependabot made, and gh pr merge then merges that pull request's code
      #   with the job's token.
      # attack: the attacker enables Dependabot in their fork, opens a pull
      #   request to this repository from the branch of a pull request Dependabot
      #   opened in the fork, then comments @dependabot recreate on Dependabot's
      #   pull request there, so that Dependabot pushes to that branch (Synacktiv
      #   did so against a copy of spring-projects/spring-security in 2024, and
      #   their file evil.txt was merged).
      # attack-run-behavior: Dependabot's push runs pull_request_target on
      #   synchronize with github.actor dependabot[bot], so the if is true and the
      #   job merge starts with contents: write and pull-requests: write; gh pr
      #   merge --auto --rebase turns on auto-merge for the attacker's pull
      #   request, which GitHub merges once its requirements are met.
      on: pull_request_target
      jobs:
        c:
          uses: example-org/bot-conditions-remote/.github/workflows/w.yml@v1
          secrets: inherit
      ```
    - dependabot.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on pull_request_target, the job runs only when the actor is
      #   dependabot[bot], and then has gh pr merge --auto merge the pull request
      #   with a token that may write contents and pull requests.
      # reason: github.actor names whoever caused the event, not who wrote the
      #   pull request, so the if also lets in a pull request whose last push
      #   Dependabot made, and gh pr merge then merges that pull request's code
      #   with the job's token.
      # attack: the attacker enables Dependabot in their fork, opens a pull
      #   request to this repository from the branch of a pull request Dependabot
      #   opened in the fork, then comments @dependabot recreate on Dependabot's
      #   pull request there, so that Dependabot pushes to that branch (Synacktiv
      #   did so against a copy of spring-projects/spring-security in 2024, and
      #   their file evil.txt was merged).
      # attack-run-behavior: Dependabot's push runs pull_request_target on
      #   synchronize with github.actor dependabot[bot], so the if is true and the
      #   job merge starts with contents: write and pull-requests: write; gh pr
      #   merge --auto --rebase turns on auto-merge for the attacker's pull
      #   request, which GitHub merges once its requirements are met.
      on: pull_request_target
      jobs:
        merge:
          if: github.actor == 'dependabot[bot]'
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          permissions:
            contents: write
            pull-requests: write
          steps:
            - run: gh pr merge --auto --rebase "$PR"
              env:
                PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.html_url }}
                GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - called/action.yml (action-metadata, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: the composite action of the true positive dependabot.no-caller
      #   of this rule; the only caller, ci.yml, runs on push and calls the action
      #   after actions/checkout.
      # reason: the files that the linter reads are the whole repository and hold
      #   every caller of the action, so the rule reads the action on the events of
      #   the callers, here push alone, and a push comes from one who can write to
      #   the repository, not from the attacker. The if of the step of the action is
      #   false on push as well; the rule reports nothing because of the event of
      #   the caller, not because of the steps.
      # attack: the attacker enables Dependabot in the attacker's fork, opens a
      #   pull request to this repository from the branch of a pull request
      #   Dependabot opened in the fork, then comments @dependabot recreate on the
      #   pull request of Dependabot in the fork, so that Dependabot pushes to the
      #   branch of the pull request (Synacktiv did so against a copy of
      #   spring-projects/spring-security in 2024, and the file evil.txt of
      #   Synacktiv was merged).
      # attack-run-behavior: the attacker cannot push to the repository, so the
      #   attacker starts no run of ci.yml, and the steps of the action never run on
      #   an event of the attacker.
      name: merge dependabot
      description: merge the pull requests of Dependabot
      runs:
        using: composite
        steps:
          - if: github.event_name == 'pull_request_target' && github.actor == 'dependabot[bot]'
            run: gh pr merge --auto --rebase "$PR"
            shell: bash
            env:
              PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.html_url }}
              GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      ```
      - .github/workflows/ci.yml (workflow)
        ```yaml
        on: push
        jobs:
          j:
            runs-on: ubuntu-latest
            steps:
              - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2
              - uses: ./called
        ```
    - dependabot.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on pull_request_target, the job merges the pull request only if
      #   its author, github.event.pull_request.user.login, is dependabot[bot].
      # reason: the if reads the author of the pull request, not the actor of the
      #   run: Dependabot's push to an attacker's pull request makes Dependabot
      #   the actor, but the attacker stays the author, so the if does not pass.
      # attack: the attacker enables Dependabot in their fork, opens a pull
      #   request to this repository from the branch of a pull request Dependabot
      #   opened in the fork, then comments @dependabot recreate on Dependabot's
      #   pull request there, so that Dependabot pushes to that branch (Synacktiv
      #   did so against a copy of spring-projects/spring-security in 2024, and
      #   their file evil.txt was merged).
      # attack-run-behavior: Dependabot's push runs pull_request_target on
      #   synchronize with github.actor dependabot[bot], but
      #   github.event.pull_request.user.login is the attacker's login, as they
      #   opened the pull request, so the if is false and the job merge is
      #   skipped.
      on: pull_request_target
      jobs:
        merge:
          if: github.event.pull_request.user.login == 'dependabot[bot]'
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          permissions:
            contents: write
            pull-requests: write
          steps:
            - run: gh pr merge --auto --rebase "$PR"
              env:
                PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.html_url }}
                GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      ```

### fix kinds

- author-context: compare the author of the pull request in place of the actor: github.event.pull_request.user.login
  - safety: review
  - possible side effects:
    - actor-not-compared: A workflow meant to compare the actor (as for a run after a push of Dependabot) changes its meaning.

### undetected forms

- caller-by-repository-name: a comparison with a bot in a reusable workflow that a workflow of the same repository calls by the name owner/repo/.github/workflows/&lt;file>@&lt;ref> of the repository (the repository that --repo names) instead of the path ./.github/workflows/&lt;file>: the rule does not resolve the call by the name to the file, so the rule reads the if on the events of the reusable workflow alone (workflow_call), which no attacker triggers
  - finding kinds: bot-conditions.dependabot
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: .github/workflows/called.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: ci.yml of the repository o/r calls this reusable workflow on
    #   pull_request_target by the name o/r/.github/workflows/called.yml@main,
    #   not by the path ./.github/workflows/called.yml; the job merges the pull
    #   request with a token that can write contents if github.actor is
    #   dependabot[bot].
    # reason: a todo (the same file): when the run of the linter names the
    #   repository (--repo o/r), the call by the name is a call of this file, and
    #   a push of Dependabot to the attacker's pull request starts the run with
    #   github.actor dependabot[bot]. A run without --repo reads o/r as another
    #   repository, and reports nothing either.
    # cause: the rule does not resolve a call by the name of the repository to
    #   the file, so the rule reads the if on the events of this workflow alone
    #   (workflow_call), which no attacker triggers.
    # attack: the attacker enables Dependabot in their fork, opens a pull
    #   request to this repository from the branch of a pull request that
    #   Dependabot opened in the fork, then comments @dependabot recreate on the
    #   pull request of Dependabot there, so that Dependabot pushes to that
    #   branch.
    # attack-run-behavior: the push of Dependabot runs ci.yml on
    #   pull_request_target with github.actor dependabot[bot]; the if of this
    #   workflow is true, and gh pr merge --auto --rebase runs on the attacker's
    #   pull request with a token that can write contents.
    on: workflow_call
    jobs:
      merge:
        if: github.actor == 'dependabot[bot]'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions:
          contents: write
        steps:
          - run: gh pr merge --auto --rebase "$PR"
            env:
              PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.html_url }}
              GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    ```
    - .github/workflows/ci.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: pull_request_target
      jobs:
        call:
          uses: o/r/.github/workflows/called.yml@main
      ```
- app-commit-event: a value of the payload of status, check_suite or check_run, such as the message of the commit (commit.commit.message of status, check_suite.head_commit.message of check_suite), when an app outside GitHub Actions, such as an outside CI, makes a commit status or a check run for a commit whose message an attacker writes: the run of status, check_suite or check_run starts on the default branch with the commit in the payload, and the actor of the run is the app. This rule reads a run of a privileged event only in two cases, as the attacker run table says: the attacker is the actor of the run, or another person (such as a maintainer) acts on what the attacker wrote, and the act starts the run. The attacker run table has no rows of a run whose actor is an app. The rule also does not read a value of the payload of deployment_status, because the rule does not read deployment_status as an event that an attacker starts
  - finding kinds: bot-conditions.dependabot
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: app-commit-event.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on status, the job runs only when the actor is netlify[bot],
    #   checks out the commit of the status (github.event.sha) and runs a build
    #   with a token that writes.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): when an outside app, here Netlify, writes
    #   a status for a commit of a pull request from a fork, the run of status
    #   starts on the default branch, and the actor of the run is the bot of the
    #   app (seen on GitHub for a GitHub App), so the check of the actor lets in
    #   the run of a commit of the pull request.
    # cause: the rule reads a run of a privileged event only where the attacker
    #   is the actor of the run or the run is of the act of another person on
    #   what the attacker wrote, by the attacker run table, which has no rows of
    #   status, check_suite and check_run.
    # attack-value: the file package.json at the head of the pull request from a fork = "{\"scripts\":{\"build\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: Netlify writes a status for the commit of the pull
    #   request from a fork; the run of status, whose actor is netlify[bot],
    #   passes the if, checks out that commit, and npm run build prints PWNED.
    on: status
    jobs:
      j:
        if: github.actor == 'netlify[bot]'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions: {contents: write}
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.sha }}
          - run: npm run build
    ```
- fork-review: a job on pull_request_review or pull_request_review_comment that runs only for a pull request from a fork, such as a job whose if: condition is github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name != github.repository: the run of a review that the attacker writes on the pull request of another person from a fork has the secrets of the repository or a token that writes only where a private repository gives secrets or a token that writes to the runs of pull requests from forks (repo.fork-pr-secrets, repo.fork-pr-write-tokens). The rule does not read the facts repo.fork-pr-secrets and repo.fork-pr-write-tokens for the runs of a review, and does not count the run of a review of a pull request from a fork as a run of the attacker. When the attacker opened the pull request from a fork, a review of that pull request gives the attacker nothing more than the pull request itself gives: the run takes the workflow of the merge commit of the pull request (GitHub's documentation gives refs/pull/&lt;n>/merge as the ref of the run of a review), and the attacker can change that workflow in the pull request
  - finding kinds: bot-conditions.dependabot
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: fork-review.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on comments on the diff, a step merges the pull request only
    #   if the actor is dependabot[bot], in a job that runs only for a pull
    #   request from a fork.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the job runs only for a pull request from a
    #   fork. Where a private repository gives secrets or a token that writes
    #   to the runs of pull requests from forks, the run of a review that the
    #   attacker writes on the pull request of another person from a fork has
    #   those secrets or that token, and the job runs for the attacker.
    # cause: the rule does not read the settings of a private repository for
    #   the runs of pull requests from forks, and does not count the run of a
    #   review of a pull request from a fork as a run of the attacker.
    # attack: in the case where the attacker can have a bot that the if lets
    #   in act on the pull request of another person from a fork, as the
    #   inconclusive kind other-bot of this rule says of a run of a pull
    #   request from a branch of the repository, the attacker has that bot
    #   comment on the diff of that pull request.
    # attack-run-behavior: the comment of the bot starts the job a with the
    #   actor that the if compares, and gh pr merge --auto --rebase turns on
    #   auto-merge for the pull request with the token of the run.
    on: pull_request_review_comment
    jobs:
      a:
        if: github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name != github.repository
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - if: github.actor == 'dependabot[bot]'
            run: gh pr merge --auto --rebase "$PR"
            env:
              PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.html_url }}
              GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    ```
- caller-value: an actor compared in an action through inputs.&lt;name>, which a caller gives under with:, such as with: who: \${{ github.actor }}: the rule does not follow the value under with: into inputs.&lt;name>
  - finding kinds: bot-conditions.dependabot
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - example: called/action.yml (action-metadata, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the composite action has gh pr merge --auto merge the pull
    #   request with the token of the job only if inputs.who is dependabot[bot];
    #   ci.yml calls the action on pull_request_target and gives github.actor as
    #   who.
    # reason: a todo (a file of the repository): github.actor names whoever
    #   caused the event, not who wrote the pull request, so the if also lets in a
    #   pull request whose last push Dependabot made, and gh pr merge then merges
    #   the code of the pull request with the token of the job.
    # cause: the rule does not follow the value under with: of the caller into
    #   inputs.who of the action, so the rule does not see that inputs.who holds
    #   github.actor.
    # attack: the attacker enables Dependabot in the attacker's fork, opens a
    #   pull request to this repository from the branch of a pull request
    #   Dependabot opened in the fork, then comments @dependabot recreate on the
    #   pull request of Dependabot in the fork, so that Dependabot pushes to the
    #   branch of the pull request.
    # attack-run-behavior: the push of Dependabot runs ci.yml on
    #   pull_request_target on synchronize with github.actor dependabot[bot], so
    #   the if is true and gh pr merge --auto --rebase turns on auto-merge for the
    #   attacker's pull request with the token of the job.
    name: merge dependabot
    description: merge the pull requests of Dependabot
    inputs:
      who:
        description: the actor to compare
    runs:
      using: composite
      steps:
        - if: inputs.who == 'dependabot[bot]'
          run: gh pr merge --auto --rebase "$PR"
          shell: bash
          env:
            PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.html_url }}
            GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    ```
    - .github/workflows/ci.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: pull_request_target
      jobs:
        merge:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          permissions:
            contents: write
            pull-requests: write
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2
            - uses: ./called
              with:
                who: ${{ github.actor }}
      ```
- outside-caller: a reusable workflow or composite action that callers in the repository decide, called from another repository on an event, or with a value, an attacker controls: the caller's run has the caller's token and secrets, not the repository's
  - finding kinds: bot-conditions.dependabot
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: .github/workflows/called.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the workflow is called; a job merges when github.actor is
    #   dependabot[bot]. Its one caller in the repository, ci.yml, runs on push.
    # reason: no added gain for this repository: ci.yml calls the workflow on
    #   push alone, and a push needs write access to the repository, so no run of
    #   the workflow has a value that an attacker wrote: a rerun, which a
    #   credential whose only write access is to the permission Actions can start,
    #   keeps the actor and the payload of the run. Another repository may call
    #   the workflow on an event whose payload has what an attacker wrote, but
    #   that run has the token and the secrets of the other repository.
    # cause: the rule reads a called workflow on the events of its callers in
    #   the repository, and ci.yml runs on push alone.
    # attack: the attacker enables Dependabot in their fork, opens a pull
    #   request to this repository from the branch of a pull request Dependabot
    #   opened in the fork, then comments @dependabot recreate on Dependabot's
    #   pull request there, so that Dependabot pushes to that branch (Synacktiv
    #   did so against a copy of spring-projects/spring-security in 2024, and
    #   their file evil.txt was merged).
    # attack-run-behavior: ci.yml calls this workflow on push only, so
    #   Dependabot's push to the branch in the fork does not start it; a caller
    #   of another repository on pull_request_target would pass the if on that
    #   push (github.actor dependabot[bot]) and merge with that caller's
    #   token.
    on:
      workflow_call:
    jobs:
      merge:
        if: github.actor == 'dependabot[bot]'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions:
          contents: write
          pull-requests: write
        steps:
          - run: gh pr merge --auto --rebase "$PR"
            env:
              PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.html_url }}
              GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    ```
    - .github/workflows/ci.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: push
      jobs:
        call:
          uses: ./.github/workflows/called.yml
      ```
- not-attacker-event: a comparison with a bot in a workflow that runs on no privileged event (not privileged events: push, schedule): no run of Dependabot's push to the attacker's pull request reaches it
  - finding kinds: bot-conditions.dependabot
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: not-attacker-event.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a job merges when github.actor is dependabot[bot].
    # reason: no added gain: push runs it, which no attacker's pull request
    #   triggers; Dependabot's push to the attacker's branch does not reach it.
    # cause: push is none of the attacker's events the rule reads the if on.
    # attack: the attacker enables Dependabot in their fork, opens a pull
    #   request to this repository from the branch of a pull request Dependabot
    #   opened in the fork, then comments @dependabot recreate on Dependabot's
    #   pull request there, so that Dependabot pushes to that branch (Synacktiv
    #   did so against a copy of spring-projects/spring-security in 2024, and
    #   their file evil.txt was merged).
    # attack-run-behavior: Dependabot's push goes to the branch in the fork and
    #   runs this repository's workflows of pull_request and
    #   pull_request_target, not this one; push runs it only for pushes to this
    #   repository, where github.actor is dependabot[bot] only for Dependabot's
    #   own branches.
    on: push
    jobs:
      merge:
        if: github.actor == 'dependabot[bot]'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions:
          contents: write
          pull-requests: write
        steps:
          - run: gh pr merge --auto --rebase "$PR"
            env:
              PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.html_url }}
              GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    ```
- actor-in-step-output: the actor compared through the output of a step or an env
  - finding kinds: bot-conditions.dependabot
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: actor-in-step-output.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a step writes github.actor to its
    #   output, and the next step merges when the output is dependabot[bot].
    # reason: a todo (the same file): following the output would find the
    #   comparison.
    # cause: the actor reaches the if through the output of a step, which the
    #   rule does not follow.
    # attack: the attacker enables Dependabot in their fork, opens a pull
    #   request to this repository from the branch of a pull request Dependabot
    #   opened in the fork, then comments @dependabot recreate on Dependabot's
    #   pull request there, so that Dependabot pushes to that branch (Synacktiv
    #   did so against a copy of spring-projects/spring-security in 2024, and
    #   their file evil.txt was merged).
    # attack-run-behavior: Dependabot's push runs pull_request_target on
    #   synchronize with github.actor dependabot[bot]; the step who writes
    #   actor=dependabot[bot] to GITHUB_OUTPUT, so the next step's if is true,
    #   and gh pr merge --auto --rebase runs on the attacker's pull request with
    #   a token that has contents: write.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      merge:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions:
          contents: write
        steps:
          - id: who
            run: echo "actor=${{ github.actor }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          - if: steps.who.outputs.actor == 'dependabot[bot]'
            run: gh pr merge --auto --rebase "$PR"
            env:
              PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.html_url }}
              GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    ```
- path-first: the actor as the first argument of contains, startsWith or endsWith (endsWith(github.actor, '&#91;bot]')), which the rule does not read as a comparison
  - finding kinds: bot-conditions.dependabot
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: path-first.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a job with contents write runs when
    #   endsWith(github.actor, '[bot]').
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the run of Dependabot's push passes it.
    # cause: the actor is the first argument, compared with a suffix, which the
    #   rule does not read as a comparison.
    # attack: the attacker enables Dependabot in their fork, opens a pull
    #   request to this repository from the branch of a pull request Dependabot
    #   opened in the fork, then comments @dependabot recreate on Dependabot's
    #   pull request there, so that Dependabot pushes to that branch (Synacktiv
    #   did so against a copy of spring-projects/spring-security in 2024, and
    #   their file evil.txt was merged).
    # attack-run-behavior: Dependabot's push runs pull_request_target on
    #   synchronize with github.actor dependabot[bot], which ends with [bot], so
    #   the if is true and the job merge runs echo merge with contents:
    #   write.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      merge:
        if: endsWith(github.actor, '[bot]')
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions:
          contents: write
        steps:
          - run: echo merge
    ```
- workflow-run-actor: github.actor compared with a bot in a job on workflow_run: whether the run of Dependabot's push makes the actor of workflow_run dependabot&#91;bot] is not known
  - finding kinds: bot-conditions.dependabot
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: workflow-run-actor.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on workflow_run after a run of a pull request, a job with
    #   contents write runs when github.actor is dependabot[bot].
    # reason: a todo (a fact): whether Dependabot's push to the attacker's
    #   branch makes its actor dependabot[bot] is not known.
    # cause: the rule knows no run of Dependabot on workflow_run, so it does not
    #   read the comparison as one Dependabot passes. Nor does it report the
    #   comparison as one with another bot: it does not take the attacker as
    #   triggering workflow_run themselves.
    # attack: the attacker enables Dependabot in their fork, opens a pull
    #   request to this repository from the branch of a pull request Dependabot
    #   opened in the fork, then comments @dependabot recreate on Dependabot's
    #   pull request there, so that Dependabot pushes to that branch (Synacktiv
    #   did so against a copy of spring-projects/spring-security in 2024, and
    #   their file evil.txt was merged).
    # attack-run-behavior: the run of ci for Dependabot's push completes and
    #   starts this workflow on workflow_run; in the case where its github.actor
    #   is dependabot[bot], which is not known, the if is true and the job merge
    #   runs echo merge with contents: write.
    on:
      workflow_run:
        workflows: [ci]
        types: [completed]
    jobs:
      merge:
        if: github.actor == 'dependabot[bot]'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions:
          contents: write
        steps:
          - run: echo merge
    ```
- remote-callee: a job or a step inside a reusable workflow of another repository (uses: owner/repo/.github/workflows/&lt;file>@&lt;ref>) whose content the fact workflow.definition does not give. For every rule: a run that does not ask the fact (a run without --online and without the answer in --facts). For a quality rule, also: a run where the linter asked the fact and got no answer (an answer of unknown: the GitHub API did not give the file), and a call deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact. The rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition. For a rule that is not a quality rule (a rule with a threat), the last two forms are the inconclusive kind remote-callee-unknown, not this form
  - finding kinds: bot-conditions.dependabot
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-callee.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
    #   the repository example-org/bot-conditions-unanswered, whose content is
    #   the workflow of the true positive dependabot (dependabot.yml) of the
    #   rule, with on: workflow_call in place of the on of dependabot.yml. The
    #   linter has no answer of the fact workflow.definition for the reusable
    #   workflow.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event
    #   that started the run of the calling job, and the linter does not read
    #   the reusable workflow.
    # cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from
    #   the answer of workflow.definition.
    # attack: the attacker enables Dependabot in their fork, opens a pull
    #   request to this repository from the branch of a pull request Dependabot
    #   opened in the fork, then comments @dependabot recreate on Dependabot's
    #   pull request there, so that Dependabot pushes to that branch (Synacktiv
    #   did so against a copy of spring-projects/spring-security in 2024, and
    #   their file evil.txt was merged).
    # attack-run-behavior: Dependabot's push runs pull_request_target on
    #   synchronize with github.actor dependabot[bot], so the if is true and the
    #   job merge starts with contents: write and pull-requests: write; gh pr
    #   merge --auto --rebase turns on auto-merge for the attacker's pull
    #   request, which GitHub merges once its requirements are met.
    on: pull_request_target
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/bot-conditions-unanswered/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

### inconclusive

- other-bot: a comparison of the actor with a bot other than Dependabot (renovate&#91;bot], github-actions&#91;bot]): whether an attacker can have it act on their pull request is not known
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: other-bot.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a job with write permissions runs only
    #   when github.actor is renovate[bot], a bot other than Dependabot, and
    #   merges the pull request.
    # reason: whether an attacker can have Renovate push to their pull request
    #   is not known.
    # attack: in the case where the attacker can have Renovate push to their
    #   pull request, as Dependabot's recreate is used against the true positive
    #   of dependabot, they open the pull request and have Renovate push to it.
    # attack-run-behavior: Renovate's push runs pull_request_target on
    #   synchronize with github.actor renovate[bot], so the if is true and the
    #   job merge starts with contents: write and pull-requests: write; gh pr
    #   merge --auto --rebase turns on auto-merge for the attacker's pull
    #   request.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      merge:
        if: github.actor == 'renovate[bot]'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions:
          contents: write
          pull-requests: write
        steps:
          - run: gh pr merge --auto --rebase "$PR"
            env:
              PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.html_url }}
              GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    ```
- remote-callee-unknown: a job that calls a reusable workflow of another repository, when the linter asked the fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow and got no answer (the token that the linter uses cannot read the file, the file is larger than the limit, or the linter has used up the requests it may send to the GitHub API), or when the call is deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact: the rule does not read the jobs and the steps of the reusable workflow
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-callee-unknown.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
    #   the repository example-org/bot-conditions-unknown, whose content is the
    #   workflow of the true positive dependabot (dependabot.yml) of the rule,
    #   with on: workflow_call in place of the on of dependabot.yml. The linter
    #   asked the fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow and got no
    #   answer.
    # reason: what the jobs of the reusable workflow do is in the file that the
    #   linter could not read; whoever changes the uses, such as the author of a
    #   pull request, can name a reusable workflow that the token that the
    #   linter uses cannot read.
    # attack: the attacker enables Dependabot in their fork, opens a pull
    #   request to this repository from the branch of a pull request Dependabot
    #   opened in the fork, then comments @dependabot recreate on Dependabot's
    #   pull request there, so that Dependabot pushes to that branch (Synacktiv
    #   did so against a copy of spring-projects/spring-security in 2024, and
    #   their file evil.txt was merged).
    # attack-run-behavior: Dependabot's push runs pull_request_target on
    #   synchronize with github.actor dependabot[bot], so the if is true and the
    #   job merge starts with contents: write and pull-requests: write; gh pr
    #   merge --auto --rebase turns on auto-merge for the attacker's pull
    #   request, which GitHub merges once its requirements are met.
    on: pull_request_target
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/bot-conditions-unknown/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

### false positive forms

- callee: a reusable workflow or a composite action when all of the following are true: the rule does not know all of the callers of the reusable workflow or the composite action; every workflow that runs the reusable workflow or the composite action (directly, or through another reusable workflow or composite action) is a workflow in the same repository; and the rule would report no finding of the finding kind if the rule read the reusable workflow or the composite action only on the events on which the workflows in the same repository run the reusable workflow or the composite action (for example, every workflow that runs the reusable workflow or the composite action runs only on push). When the rule does not know all of the callers, the rule can read the reusable workflow or the composite action on every event (the worst case). For example, the rule does not know all of the callers when no caller is among the inputs; when the inputs are not the whole repository; for a composite action, when an input is excluded or cannot be read; when a caller names the reusable workflow or the composite action by a name of the form owner/repo/path@ref instead of by a ./ path, in which owner/repo is the repository that the --repo flag names, or is any repository when no --repo flag is given; when a step names the composite action by a ./ path, and either no checkout step runs before that step or the last checkout step before that step is not a plain checkout step (a plain checkout step has no ref input, no repository input and no path input); when a step inside a composite action names another composite action by a ./ path; or when the rule does not know all of the callers of a caller
  - finding kinds: bot-conditions.dependabot
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - example: .github/workflows/called.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a.yml of the repository o/r runs on push alone and calls b.yml by
    #   the name o/r/.github/workflows/b.yml@main, not by the path
    #   ./.github/workflows/b.yml; b.yml calls this reusable workflow by the path
    #   ./.github/workflows/called.yml. No other workflow calls b.yml or this
    #   reusable workflow.
    # reason: when the run of the linter names the repository (--repo o/r), the
    #   only workflow that runs this reusable workflow is a.yml, through b.yml,
    #   and a.yml runs on push alone. A push of Dependabot to the branch of a
    #   pull request from a fork goes to the fork, so the push of Dependabot
    #   starts no run of a.yml. A run without --repo reads the call by the name
    #   o/r/.github/workflows/b.yml@main as a call that may name a file of the
    #   repository, because the run does not know which repository the inputs
    #   are; the rule does not resolve the call to b.yml, so the rule reads
    #   b.yml, and this reusable workflow through b.yml, on every event and
    #   reports the same finding.
    # cause: the rule does not resolve the call by the name of the repository to
    #   b.yml, so the rule does not know all of the callers of b.yml, and reads
    #   b.yml, and this reusable workflow through b.yml, on every event.
    # attack: the attacker opens a pull request to this repository from the
    #   branch of a pull request that Dependabot opened in the fork of the
    #   attacker, then comments @dependabot recreate on the pull request of
    #   Dependabot in the fork, so that Dependabot pushes to the branch.
    # attack-run-behavior: the push of Dependabot goes to the branch in the fork
    #   and starts no run of a.yml. A run of a.yml starts only on a push to the
    #   repository o/r. So the job merge of this reusable workflow never runs
    #   with github.actor dependabot[bot] for the pull request of the attacker.
    on:
      workflow_call:
    jobs:
      merge:
        if: github.actor == 'dependabot[bot]'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions:
          contents: write
          pull-requests: write
        steps:
          - run: gh pr merge --auto --rebase "$PR"
            env:
              PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.html_url }}
              GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    ```
    - finding on: .github/workflows/called.yml
    - .github/workflows/a.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: push
      jobs:
        a:
          uses: o/r/.github/workflows/b.yml@main
      ```
    - .github/workflows/b.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on:
        workflow_call:
      jobs:
        b:
          uses: ./.github/workflows/called.yml
      ```
- pull-request-target-blocked: a workflow whose on has pull_request_target and no other event (no workflow_call event either), in a repository whose Actions policies block the runs of the workflow on pull_request_target (repo.pull-request-target-allowed false): an event policy that an administrator sets without pull_request_target among the allowed events, or the default policy that GitHub adds to a public repository without an applicable event policy, from the time when GitHub enforces the default policy on the repository. GitHub's documents say that GitHub evaluates the policies before a run, and that a run that a policy does not allow fails with an error. The documents do not say whether a job of such a run starts before the run fails; the rule assumes that no job of such a run starts
  - finding kinds: bot-conditions.dependabot
  - fact kinds:
    - repo.pull-request-target-allowed (provider: repo-setting, answer that removes the finding: false)
  - example: pull-request-target-blocked.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, the job runs only when the actor is
    #   dependabot[bot], and then has gh pr merge --auto merge the pull request
    #   with a token that may write contents and pull requests.
    # reason: the Actions policies of the repository block the runs of the
    #   workflow on pull_request_target: the default policy that GitHub adds to a
    #   public repository without an applicable event policy, from the time when
    #   GitHub enforces the default policy on the repository, or an event policy
    #   whose list of allowed events does not have pull_request_target. GitHub's
    #   documents say that GitHub evaluates the policies before a run, and that a
    #   run that a policy does not allow fails with an error; the documents do not
    #   say whether a job of such a run starts before the run fails, and the rule
    #   assumes that no job starts.
    # cause: unless a file of facts or --fact says that the Actions policies block
    #   runs on pull_request_target (repo.pull-request-target-allowed false), the
    #   rule reports the finding. When no file of facts and no --fact answers
    #   repo.pull-request-target-allowed, the finding is conditional.
    # attack: the attacker enables Dependabot in the fork of the attacker, opens
    #   a pull request to this repository from the branch of a pull request that
    #   Dependabot opened in the fork, then comments @dependabot recreate on the
    #   pull request of Dependabot in the fork, so that Dependabot pushes to that
    #   branch.
    # attack-run-behavior: the pull request of the attacker triggers
    #   pull_request_target, and the run fails with an error, and no job of the
    #   run starts (the assumption of the reason), so gh pr merge never runs.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      merge:
        if: github.actor == 'dependabot[bot]'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions:
          contents: write
          pull-requests: write
        steps:
          - run: gh pr merge --auto --rebase "$PR"
            env:
              PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.html_url }}
              GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    ```
- actions-policy: a run that the Actions policies of the repository block, in four cases where the rule does not take the policies into account. First, an event policy that blocks an event of the attackers other than pull_request_target (such as issue_comment) in a workflow whose on has that event: the rules ask a fact only for pull_request_target. Second, an actor rule that does not allow the account of the attacker (for example, an actor rule that allows only the repository roles with write access): repo.pull-request-target-allowed is one value for all the runs of a workflow file on pull_request_target, and an actor rule blocks a run by the account that starts the run, so the fact cannot tell what an actor rule blocks. Third, a workflow whose on has pull_request_target and another event: the rule does not ask repo.pull-request-target-allowed for such a workflow, because a run on the other event can reach the job. When the if of the job is false on the other event, so that the job runs only on pull_request_target, and a policy blocks pull_request_target, the finding is a false positive. Fourth, a reusable workflow (on workflow_call) or an action that only workflows on pull_request_target call: the rule asks repo.pull-request-target-allowed only of a workflow whose on has pull_request_target, not of the reusable workflow or the action, so a finding in the reusable workflow or the action is still reported when the policies block the runs of every caller
  - finding kinds: bot-conditions.dependabot
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: actions-policy.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, the job runs only when the actor is
    #   dependabot[bot], and then has gh pr merge --auto merge the pull request
    #   with a token that may write contents and pull requests.
    # reason: an actor rule of the Actions policies of the repository allows
    #   only the repository roles with write access to trigger the workflow, and
    #   does not have dependabot[bot] among the allowed actors, so a run whose
    #   actor is dependabot[bot] fails. GitHub's documents say that GitHub
    #   evaluates the policies before a run, and that a run that a policy does not
    #   allow fails with an error; the documents do not say whether a job of such
    #   a run starts before the run fails, and the rule assumes that no job
    #   starts.
    # cause: the rule does not take the actor rules of the Actions policies into
    #   account: repo.pull-request-target-allowed is one value for all the runs of
    #   the workflow file on pull_request_target, and an actor rule blocks a run
    #   by the account that starts the run.
    # attack: the attacker enables Dependabot in the fork of the attacker, opens
    #   a pull request to this repository from the branch of a pull request that
    #   Dependabot opened in the fork, then comments @dependabot recreate on the
    #   pull request of Dependabot in the fork, so that Dependabot pushes to that
    #   branch.
    # attack-run-behavior: dependabot[bot] is not an allowed actor, so the run
    #   on pull_request_target that the push of Dependabot triggers fails with an
    #   error, and no job of the run starts (the assumption of the reason), so gh
    #   pr merge never runs.
    name: policy
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      merge:
        if: github.actor == 'dependabot[bot]'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions:
          contents: write
          pull-requests: write
        steps:
          - run: gh pr merge --auto --rebase "$PR"
            env:
              PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.html_url }}
              GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    ```
- actions-not-allowed: a workflow whose run GitHub does not start, or a job that GitHub fails in the step "Set up job", because of the setting of allowed actions of GitHub (the fact repo.allowed-actions, which the quality rule allowed-actions reads): GitHub does not start a run of a workflow that has a uses, or that calls a reusable workflow that has a uses, that the setting does not allow, and fails a job before any step of the job runs when a step of a composite action that the job runs has a uses that the setting does not allow, or when the setting requires a full commit SHA and a step names an action by a tag or a branch. The harm that the finding reports happens only when GitHub runs the workflow or the job, and the rule does not read repo.allowed-actions
  - finding kinds: bot-conditions.dependabot
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: actions-not-allowed.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the workflow of the true positive dependabot (dependabot.yml)
    #   of the rule, with a job added whose step uses
    #   example-org/not-allowed-action, which the setting of allowed actions of
    #   GitHub (repo.allowed-actions) blocks with
    #   !example-org/not-allowed-action@*. In the true positive, on
    #   pull_request_target, the job runs only when the actor is
    #   dependabot[bot], and then has gh pr merge --auto merge the pull request
    #   with a token that may write contents and pull requests.
    # reason: GitHub checks each uses of the workflow before the run starts, and
    #   does not start the run because of the uses of
    #   example-org/not-allowed-action: no job of the run runs, so what the
    #   reason of the true positive says does not happen (in runs that the
    #   authors of the rule made on GitHub, such runs ended as startup_failure).
    # cause: the rule does not read repo.allowed-actions.
    # attack: the attacker enables Dependabot in their fork, opens a pull
    #   request to this repository from the branch of a pull request Dependabot
    #   opened in the fork, then comments @dependabot recreate on Dependabot's
    #   pull request there, so that Dependabot pushes to that branch (Synacktiv
    #   did so against a copy of spring-projects/spring-security in 2024, and
    #   their file evil.txt was merged).
    # attack-run-behavior: GitHub does not start the run, so no step of the run
    #   runs, and the attack does nothing.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      merge:
        if: github.actor == 'dependabot[bot]'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions:
          contents: write
          pull-requests: write
        steps:
          - run: gh pr merge --auto --rebase "$PR"
            env:
              PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.html_url }}
              GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      not-allowed:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: example-org/not-allowed-action@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

### threat

- precondition callers-events: a reusable workflow or a composite action that is among the inputs runs on the events of the callers of the workflow or the action, whoever the callers are; when the inputs are the whole repository and hold every caller of the workflow or the action, the rule reads the workflow or the action on the events of the callers, with the values that the callers give under with
  - cites:
    - <https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows#workflow_call>
    - <https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7x29-qqmq-v6qc>
- precondition actor-compared: github.actor, github.triggering_actor, github.actor_id or github.event.sender is the user that triggered the run: the one who pushed, for synchronize
  - cites:
    - <https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/contexts#github-context>
    - <https://www.synacktiv.com/publications/github-actions-exploitation-dependabot>
- precondition dependabot-push: the owner of a fork may enable Dependabot there, and @dependabot recreate makes it push to the branch of its pull request; the deprecation of 2026-01-27 left recreate and rebase
  - cites:
    - <https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/supply-chain-security/dependabot-pull-request-comment-commands>
    - <https://www.synacktiv.com/publications/github-actions-exploitation-dependabot>
- actor: fork-pr-author
  - via: opens a pull request from the branch of Dependabot's pull request in their fork, then comments @dependabot recreate on Dependabot's pull request there; Dependabot's push runs pull_request_target on synchronize with the actor dependabot&#91;bot]
  - events: pull_request_target
  - run starters: pull_request_target: attacker
  - gains: read-secrets, write-with-token

### CVSS

#### bot-conditions.dependabot

- vector: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:L/SC:H/SI:H/SA:N/E:P
- CVSS-B: 9.9 (critical)
- CVSS-BT: 9.3 (critical)
- impact: H (from VC, VI, SC, SI)
- likelihood: high (from AV:N, AT:N, PR:N)
- severity: critical (impact H, likelihood high; the table: sisakulint --explain=terms)
- AV: N
  - reason: the attacker forks the repository and opens a pull request over the network
  - cites: none
- AC: L
  - reason: a comment @dependabot recreate on Dependabot's pull request in their fork makes the push
  - cites: none
- AT: N
  - reason: the attacker sets up all of it in their fork: Dependabot, a dependency it updates, and the pull request from its branch
  - cites: none
- PR: N
  - reason: on a public repository anyone opens a pull request from a fork
  - cites: none
- UI: N
  - reason: pull_request_target runs on the push with nobody doing anything
  - cites: none
- VC: H
  - reason: the job the if guards runs on the attacker's pull request with its secrets and token: what it reads, they get when it runs their code
  - cites: none
- VI: H
  - reason: such jobs approve and merge Dependabot's pull requests, so the attacker's is merged, or they write with the job's token
  - cites: none
- VA: L
  - reason: the job can cancel runs or delete what it may
  - cites: none
- SC: H
  - reason: the secrets of the job open what is past it
  - cites: none
- SI: H
  - reason: what is merged or released reaches those who use the repository
  - cites: none
- SA: N
  - reason: nothing past the repository is made unavailable by this as such
  - cites: none
- E: P
  - reason: Synacktiv passed the if of spring-projects/spring-security's merge-dependabot-pr.yml this way from a fork in 2024; spring-security and trpc then compared the author of the pull request
  - cites:
    - <https://www.synacktiv.com/publications/github-actions-exploitation-dependabot>

## cache-bloat

- problem: a step saves under a new key the content of a cache that restore-keys restored from another key, so the content of the older caches stays in each new cache
- expected: a cache is saved only by a run in which restore-keys restored no older cache
- targets: workflow
- quality rule: a finding of the quality rule alone gives no attacker a gain, and the findings of the quality rule set no bit of the exit code
- default run: always: in a run without --rule, the rule runs unless --skip-rule names the rule

### finding kinds

- cache-bloat.partial-restore
  - detected: the step may save under a new key the content of an older cache that restore-keys restored; the events on which the step may save: {saves_on}
  - arguments:
    - {saves_on}: The events on which the restore and the save both run and the save may save, each event named once.
  - consequence: the content of the older caches stays in each new cache, so the new cache grows and takes longer to restore and to save; when the caches of the repository pass the cache limit, GitHub deletes the caches used least recently
  - remedy: save the cache only in runs in which restore-keys restores no older cache (for example, a push run that builds without a restore), or remove restore-keys from the step
  - true positives:
    - partial-restore.remote-callee.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
      #   the repository example-org/cache-bloat-remote, which the fact
      #   workflow.definition answers with the workflow of the true positive
      #   partial-restore (partial-restore.remote-composite.yml) of the rule, with
      #   on: workflow_call in place of the on of
      #   partial-restore.remote-composite.yml. The job passes its secrets with
      #   secrets: inherit. In the true positive, on push, a step runs
      #   example-org/bloat-composite@v1, a composite action of another repository
      #   whose step uses actions/cache under a key unique to the run, with
      #   restore-keys.
      # reason: the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event that started the
      #   run of the calling job, so the reason of the true positive holds: no
      #   cache has the key of the run, so the step of the composite action
      #   restores the newest older cache by the prefix and saves its content
      #   under a new key at the end of the job; action.definition answers the
      #   file of the composite action.
      on: push
      jobs:
        c:
          uses: example-org/cache-bloat-remote/.github/workflows/w.yml@v1
          secrets: inherit
      ```
    - partial-restore.remote-composite.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on push, a step runs example-org/bloat-composite@v1, a
      #   composite action of another repository whose step uses actions/cache
      #   under a key unique to the run, with restore-keys.
      # reason: no cache has the key of the run, so the step of the composite
      #   action restores the newest older cache by the prefix and saves its
      #   content under a new key at the end of the job; action.definition
      #   answers the file of the composite action.
      on: push
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            - uses: example-org/bloat-composite@v1
      ```
    - partial-restore.restore-then-cache.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: the job restores ~/.npm by restore-keys with
      #   actions/cache/restore, and later writes actions/cache for ~/.npm with a
      #   key of the run and no restore-keys.
      # reason: actions/cache finds no cache of the key of the run, and at the
      #   end of the job saves ~/.npm, which holds the content of the older cache
      #   that the restore took, under the new key.
      on: push
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            - uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
              with:
                path: ~/.npm
                key: npm-${{ hashFiles('package-lock.json') }}
                restore-keys: npm-
            - uses: actions/cache@v4
              with:
                path: ~/.npm
                key: npm-${{ github.run_id }}
            - run: npm ci
      ```
    - partial-restore.split.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: actions/cache/restore restores by restore-keys, the build adds
      #   files to the path, and actions/cache/save saves the path under the key of
      #   the commit, on push and on pull_request.
      # reason: no cache has the key of the commit, so the restore takes an older
      #   cache by the prefix, and the save stores the content of the older cache,
      #   with the files of the build, under a new key. On pull_request the new
      #   cache goes to the scope of the merge ref, which also counts toward the
      #   cache limit of the repository.
      on: [push, pull_request]
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            - uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
              with:
                path: ~/.cache/build
                key: build-${{ github.sha }}
                restore-keys: build-
            - run: make
            - uses: actions/cache/save@v4
              with:
                path: ~/.cache/build
                key: build-${{ github.sha }}
      ```
    - partial-restore.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on push, actions/cache saves under a key unique to the run and
      #   restores the newest older cache by restore-keys, as the tips of
      #   actions/cache write the pattern ("Update a cache").
      # reason: no cache has the key of the run, so each run restores the newest
      #   older cache by the prefix and saves the content of the older cache, with
      #   what the run added, under a new key: the content of every older cache
      #   stays in the next cache.
      on: push
      jobs:
        primes:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            - name: update cache on every commit
              uses: actions/cache@v4
              with:
                path: prime-numbers
                key: primes-${{ runner.os }}-${{ github.run_id }}
                restore-keys: |
                  primes-${{ runner.os }}
            - run: ./generate-primes.sh
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - partial-restore.event.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: the restore runs on pull_request only and the save on push
      #   only, as upstream sisakulint advises.
      # reason: no run both restores by restore-keys and saves: a push builds
      #   from nothing and saves, and a pull request restores and saves nothing.
      on: [push, pull_request]
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            - uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
              if: github.event_name != 'push'
              with:
                path: ~/.cache/build
                key: build-${{ github.sha }}
                restore-keys: build-
            - run: make
            - uses: actions/cache/save@v4
              if: github.event_name == 'push'
              with:
                path: ~/.cache/build
                key: build-${{ github.sha }}
      ```
    - partial-restore.other-path.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: the job restores the npm cache directory by restore-keys, and
      #   saves the build output directory dist under a new key.
      # reason: the save stores dist, which no restore wrote: the content of the
      #   older npm cache does not go into the new cache.
      on: push
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            - uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
              with:
                path: ~/.npm
                key: npm-${{ hashFiles('package-lock.json') }}
                restore-keys: npm-
            - run: npm ci && npm run build
            - uses: actions/cache/save@v4
              with:
                path: dist
                key: dist-${{ github.sha }}
      ```
    - partial-restore.remote-composite.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on push, a step runs example-org/cache-composite@v1, a
      #   composite action of another repository whose step saves dist with
      #   actions/cache/save and restores nothing.
      # reason: a save that restored no older cache carries no older content.
      on: push
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            - uses: example-org/cache-composite@v1
      ```
    - partial-restore.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: the example "Always save cache" of the README of
      #   actions/cache/save: restore by an exact key, and save under the key that
      #   the restore computed, when the restore did not find the key.
      # reason: the restore takes only the exact key. When the restore finds no
      #   cache, the restore writes nothing to the path; when the restore finds the
      #   cache, the save is skipped, and GitHub would not save a second cache under
      #   the same key. The content of an older cache does not go into the new
      #   cache.
      on: push
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            - name: Restore cached Prime Numbers
              id: cache-prime-numbers-restore
              uses: actions/cache/restore@v5
              with:
                key: ${{ runner.os }}-prime-numbers
                path: |
                  path/to/dependencies
                  some/other/dependencies
            - name: Always Save Prime Numbers
              id: cache-prime-numbers-save
              if: always() && steps.cache-prime-numbers-restore.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
              uses: actions/cache/save@v5
              with:
                key: ${{ steps.cache-prime-numbers-restore.outputs.cache-primary-key }}
                path: |
                  path/to/dependencies
                  some/other/dependencies
      ```

### undetected forms

- expression-restore-keys: restore-keys written only as \${{ }}, whose value may be empty when the workflow runs; with an empty value, the step restores no cache of another key
  - finding kinds: cache-bloat.partial-restore
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: expression-restore-keys.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a workflow that other workflows call passes the restore-keys
    #   of actions/cache as an input, which a caller sets to npm-.
    # reason: with npm-, the step restores the newest npm- cache on a miss and
    #   saves the content of the older cache under the new key, as with
    #   restore-keys written as npm-.
    # cause: the rule does not know the value of ${{ inputs.restore-keys }}:
    #   the value is empty when a caller does not set the input, and then the
    #   step restores no cache of another key.
    on:
      workflow_call:
        inputs:
          restore-keys:
            type: string
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: actions/cache@v4
            with:
              path: ~/.npm
              key: npm-${{ hashFiles('package-lock.json') }}
              restore-keys: ${{ inputs.restore-keys }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
- key-prefix: a restore without restore-keys whose key is a prefix of the key that a later step saves; GitHub restores a cache whose key starts with the prefix
  - finding kinds: cache-bloat.partial-restore
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: key-prefix.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the key of the restore, deps-, is a prefix of the key that the
    #   save writes, deps- and the hash of go.sum; neither step has restore-keys.
    # reason: GitHub restores by the prefix of the key when no cache has the key
    #   itself, so the restore takes the newest deps- cache, and the save stores
    #   the content of the deps- cache, with what the build added, under a new
    #   key.
    # cause: the rule reads only restore-keys as a restore of another key, and
    #   does not compare the key of the restore with the key of the save.
    on: push
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
            with:
              path: ~/go/pkg/mod
              key: deps-
          - run: go build ./...
          - uses: actions/cache/save@v4
            with:
              path: ~/go/pkg/mod
              key: deps-${{ hashFiles('go.sum') }}
    ```
- other-action: a cache of another action, such as the cache input of actions/setup-node; or, in a composite action of another repository, an actions/cache/restore and a later save, or actions/cache when action.definition has no answer for the composite action (a run without --online and without the answer in --facts)
  - finding kinds: cache-bloat.partial-restore
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: other-action.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: actions/setup-node caches the npm cache by the cache input of
    #   actions/setup-node, which uses the cache of GitHub inside the action.
    # reason: whether actions/setup-node restores another key and saves a new
    #   key is in the code of the action, not in the workflow.
    # cause: the rule reads actions/cache, actions/cache/restore and
    #   actions/cache/save only, as written in the workflow.
    on: push
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
            with:
              node-version: 22
              cache: npm
          - run: npm ci
    ```
- path-spelling: a restore and a save that name one directory in two spellings, such as \~/.npm and /home/runner/.npm; the rule compares the lines of path as text
  - finding kinds: cache-bloat.partial-restore
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: path-spelling.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the restore names the npm cache directory as ~/.npm, and the
    #   save names the same directory as /home/runner/.npm.
    # reason: on the runner, ~ is /home/runner, so the save stores the content
    #   that the restore took from an older cache by restore-keys under a new
    #   key.
    # cause: the rule pairs a save with a restore only when a line of path is
    #   the same text in both steps.
    on: push
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
            with:
              path: ~/.npm
              key: npm-${{ hashFiles('package-lock.json') }}
              restore-keys: npm-
          - run: npm ci
          - uses: actions/cache/save@v4
            with:
              path: /home/runner/.npm
              key: npm-${{ hashFiles('package-lock.json') }}-${{ github.run_id }}
    ```
- remote-callee: a job or a step inside a reusable workflow of another repository (uses: owner/repo/.github/workflows/&lt;file>@&lt;ref>) whose content the fact workflow.definition does not give. For every rule: a run that does not ask the fact (a run without --online and without the answer in --facts). For a quality rule, also: a run where the linter asked the fact and got no answer (an answer of unknown: the GitHub API did not give the file), and a call deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact. The rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition. For a rule that is not a quality rule (a rule with a threat), the last two forms are the inconclusive kind remote-callee-unknown, not this form
  - finding kinds: cache-bloat.partial-restore
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-callee.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
    #   the repository example-org/cache-bloat-unanswered, whose content is the
    #   workflow of the true positive partial-restore
    #   (partial-restore.remote-composite.yml) of the rule, with on:
    #   workflow_call in place of the on of
    #   partial-restore.remote-composite.yml. The linter has no answer of the
    #   fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event
    #   that started the run of the calling job, and the linter does not read
    #   the reusable workflow.
    # cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from
    #   the answer of workflow.definition.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/cache-bloat-unanswered/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

### false positive forms

- pruned-path: a path whose content the build or the tool prunes on each run, so that the content of the older caches does not stay in the new cache
  - finding kinds: cache-bloat.partial-restore
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: pruned-path.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: actions/cache restores build/ by restore-keys, and the next
    #   step removes build/ and makes build/ again from nothing.
    # reason: the next step removes what the restore brought before the build,
    #   so the cache that actions/cache saves holds only what this run made: the
    #   content of the older cache does not stay in the new cache.
    # cause: whether a step prunes the path is in the script of the step, which
    #   the rule does not read.
    on: push
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: actions/cache@v4
            with:
              path: build
              key: build-${{ github.sha }}
              restore-keys: build-
          - run: rm -rf build && make
    ```
