- labeler-skipped-need: a job whose if calls no status function, that runs actions/labeler or waits for the label that actions/labeler adds (on the activity type labeled, in the job itself or in a job of a reusable workflow that the job calls), and that depends through the needs key on a job whose if calls a status function (for example, if: always()), where the job whose if calls a status function depends through the needs key, directly or through other jobs, on a job that GitHub skips, or that fails, in the run on the pull request of the attacker. GitHub applies a failure or a skip to every job after the skipped or failed job in the chain of the needs key, also after the job whose if calls a status function, so GitHub skips the job that runs actions/labeler or waits for the label, and the step of actions/labeler in a skipped job adds no label. The rule reads the ifs of the chain of the needs key only up to the job whose if calls a status function, and reads the job that runs actions/labeler or waits for the label as a job that runs.
  - finding kinds: cache-poisoning.writable-job, cache-poisoning.saved-checkout, cache-poisoning.attacker-key, cache-poisoning.attacker-path
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: .github/workflows/labeled.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: labeler.yml runs actions/labeler on pull_request_target with a
    #   personal access token in the job label, which needs the job report, whose
    #   if is always(), and report needs the job check, whose if is false for a
    #   pull request from a fork; the configuration .github/labeler.yml adds the
    #   label safe-to-test to a pull request that changes a file under site/;
    #   labeled.yml runs on pull_request_target on labeled when the label is
    #   safe-to-test, and the job has cache-mode write, checks out the head of the
    #   pull request and runs npm ci.
    # reason: GitHub skips the job check for the pull request of the attacker, and
    #   a skip applies to every job after the skipped job in the chain of the
    #   needs key, also after the job report, whose if calls always(), so GitHub
    #   skips the job label, and actions/labeler adds no label
    #   (https://github.com/github/docs/blob/404a5f4de6cd5311e3ce2d5c076571291e0107d6/data/reusables/actions/jobs/section-using-jobs-in-a-workflow-needs.md,
    #   and the observation in https://github.com/actions/runner/issues/2205).
    # cause: the rule reads the ifs of the chain of the needs key of the job label
    #   only up to the job report, whose if calls a status function, and reads the
    #   job label as one that runs.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"mkdir -p ~/.npm && echo PWNED > ~/.npm/PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork that
    #   changes a file under site/; GitHub skips the job check, runs the job
    #   report, and skips the job label, so actions/labeler adds no label, and
    #   labeled.yml does not start.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    jobs:
      build:
        if: github.event.label.name == 'safe-to-test'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        cache-mode: write
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
    - finding on: .github/workflows/labeled.yml
    - .github/labeler.yml (repo-file)
      ```yaml
      safe-to-test:
        - changed-files:
            - any-glob-to-any-file: 'site/**'
      ```
    - .github/workflows/labeler.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: pull_request_target
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        check:
          if: github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: echo checked
        report:
          needs: check
          if: always()
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: echo reported
        label:
          needs: report
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/labeler@v5
              with:
                repo-token: ${{ secrets.LABELER_PAT }}
      ```
- labeler-other-user: a step of actions/labeler whose if is true only when a step before the step of actions/labeler has failed (for example, if: failure()), after a step that has no timeout-minutes and that runs the code of the pull request of the attacker as a user that is neither root nor the user of the shell of the step (for example, sudo -u nobody, or su nobody -c), where a failure of the code does not end the step (for example, the left of || true, or the condition of an if statement of the shell script). The code of the attacker runs as a user that is not the user of the shell of the step, so the code of the attacker cannot stop the shell of the step by a signal, and the step does not fail. The rule reads the step that runs the code of the attacker as a step that the attacker can make fail, so the rule reads the step of actions/labeler as a step that runs after a failure.
  - finding kinds: cache-poisoning.writable-job, cache-poisoning.saved-checkout, cache-poisoning.attacker-key, cache-poisoning.attacker-path
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: .github/workflows/labeled.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: labeler.yml runs, on pull_request_target, actions/checkout of
    #   the head of the pull request into pr, then sudo -u nobody ./pr/build.sh
    #   || true, then actions/labeler with if: failure() and a personal access
    #   token; the configuration .github/labeler.yml adds the label safe-to-test
    #   to a pull request that changes a file under site/; labeled.yml runs on
    #   pull_request_target on labeled when the label is safe-to-test, and the
    #   job has cache-mode write, checks out the head of the pull request and
    #   runs npm ci.
    # reason: the step that runs ./pr/build.sh runs the code of the attacker as
    #   the user nobody, and a failure of the code does not end the step (||
    #   true); the code of the attacker runs as a user that is not the user of
    #   the shell of the step, so the code cannot stop the shell of the step,
    #   the step does not fail, and the step of actions/labeler, whose if is
    #   failure(), does not run (observed on 2026-11-16 on ubuntu-latest: kill
    #   from the user nobody to the shell of the step fails with Operation not
    #   permitted).
    # cause: the rule reads the step that runs ./pr/build.sh as a step that the
    #   attacker can make fail, so the rule reads the step of actions/labeler as
    #   a step that runs after a failure.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"mkdir -p ~/.npm && echo PWNED > ~/.npm/PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork that
    #   changes a file under site/ and whose pr/build.sh tries to stop the shell
    #   of the step; the kill fails, the step succeeds, actions/labeler does not
    #   run and adds no label, and labeled.yml does not start.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    jobs:
      build:
        if: github.event.label.name == 'safe-to-test'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        cache-mode: write
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
    - finding on: .github/workflows/labeled.yml
    - .github/labeler.yml (repo-file)
      ```yaml
      safe-to-test:
        - changed-files:
            - any-glob-to-any-file: 'site/**'
      ```
    - .github/workflows/labeler.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: pull_request_target
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        label:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
              with:
                ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
                allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
                persist-credentials: false
                path: pr
            - run: sudo -u nobody ./pr/build.sh || true
            - uses: actions/labeler@v5
              if: failure()
              with:
                repo-token: ${{ secrets.LABELER_PAT }}
      ```
- label-combination: a label that actions/labeler adds only together with another label whose presence makes the if of the job false, such as a label blocked that the if excludes with !contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.\*.name, 'blocked') and that actions/labeler adds on the same condition as the label that the job waits for; or a label that actions/labeler does not add, because the labels that actions/labeler would add together with the label are more than changed-files-labels-limit allows: the rule evaluates the if with the one label that the job waits for
  - finding kinds: cache-poisoning.writable-job, cache-poisoning.saved-checkout, cache-poisoning.attacker-key, cache-poisoning.attacker-path
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: .github/workflows/labeled.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: labeler.yml runs actions/labeler on pull_request_target with a
    #   personal access token; the configuration .github/labeler.yml adds the
    #   labels safe-to-test and blocked to a pull request that changes a file
    #   under site/; labeled.yml runs on pull_request_target on labeled when the
    #   label is safe-to-test and the pull request has no label blocked, and the
    #   job has cache-mode write, checks out the head of the pull request and runs
    #   npm ci.
    # reason: actions/labeler adds blocked whenever it adds safe-to-test, so the
    #   pull request of the attacker has the label blocked, and the job does not
    #   run for it.
    # cause: the rule evaluates the if with the label safe-to-test alone.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"mkdir -p ~/.npm && echo PWNED > ~/.npm/PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork that
    #   changes a file under site/; actions/labeler adds safe-to-test and blocked,
    #   and the if of labeled.yml is false.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    jobs:
      build:
        if: github.event.label.name == 'safe-to-test' && !contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'blocked')
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        cache-mode: write
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
    - finding on: .github/workflows/labeled.yml
    - .github/labeler.yml (repo-file)
      ```yaml
      safe-to-test:
        - changed-files:
            - any-glob-to-any-file: 'site/**'
      blocked:
        - changed-files:
            - any-glob-to-any-file: 'site/**'
      ```
    - .github/workflows/labeler.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: pull_request_target
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        label:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/labeler@v5
              with:
                repo-token: ${{ secrets.LABELER_PAT }}
      ```
- callee: a reusable workflow or a composite action when all of the following are true: the rule does not know all of the callers of the reusable workflow or the composite action; every workflow that runs the reusable workflow or the composite action (directly, or through another reusable workflow or composite action) is a workflow in the same repository; and the rule would report no finding of the finding kind if the rule read the reusable workflow or the composite action only on the events on which the workflows in the same repository run the reusable workflow or the composite action (for example, every workflow that runs the reusable workflow or the composite action runs only on push). When the rule does not know all of the callers, the rule can read the reusable workflow or the composite action on every event (the worst case). For example, the rule does not know all of the callers when no caller is among the inputs; when the inputs are not the whole repository; for a composite action, when an input is excluded or cannot be read; when a caller names the reusable workflow or the composite action by a name of the form owner/repo/path@ref instead of by a ./ path, in which owner/repo is the repository that the --repo flag names, or is any repository when no --repo flag is given; when a step names the composite action by a ./ path, and either no checkout step runs before that step or the last checkout step before that step is not a plain checkout step (a plain checkout step has no ref input, no repository input and no path input); when a step inside a composite action names another composite action by a ./ path; or when the rule does not know all of the callers of a caller
  - finding kinds: cache-poisoning.writable-job, cache-poisoning.saved-checkout, cache-poisoning.attacker-key, cache-poisoning.attacker-path
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - example: .github/workflows/called.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a.yml of the repository o/r runs on push alone and calls b.yml by
    #   the name o/r/.github/workflows/b.yml@main, not by the path
    #   ./.github/workflows/b.yml; b.yml calls this reusable workflow by the path
    #   ./.github/workflows/called.yml. No other workflow calls b.yml or this
    #   reusable workflow. The job of this reusable workflow, with cache-mode:
    #   write, saves build under a key that has the title of the pull request.
    # reason: when the run of the linter names the repository (--repo o/r), the
    #   only workflow that runs this reusable workflow is a.yml, through b.yml,
    #   and a.yml runs on push alone, and only a user who can push to the
    #   repository starts a run on push. The payload of push has no pull request,
    #   so github.event.pull_request.title is an empty string and the key is
    #   build-. A run without --repo reads the call by the name
    #   o/r/.github/workflows/b.yml@main as a call that may name a file of the
    #   repository, because the run does not know which repository the inputs
    #   are; the rule does not resolve the call to b.yml, so the rule reads
    #   b.yml, and this reusable workflow through b.yml, on every event and
    #   reports the same finding.
    # cause: the rule does not resolve the call by the name of the repository to
    #   b.yml, so the rule does not know all of the callers of b.yml, and reads
    #   b.yml, and this reusable workflow through b.yml, on every event.
    # attack-value: github.event.pull_request.title = "deps-Linux-5f4dcc3b5aa765d61d8327deb882cf99"
    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker cannot push to the repository, so the
    #   attacker starts no run of a.yml, and the job of this reusable workflow
    #   never saves to the cache under a key that has the title of a pull request
    #   of the attacker.
    on:
      workflow_call:
    jobs:
      c:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        cache-mode: write
        steps:
          - uses: actions/cache/save@v4
            with:
              path: build
              key: build-${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
    ```
    - finding on: .github/workflows/called.yml
    - .github/workflows/a.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: push
      jobs:
        a:
          uses: o/r/.github/workflows/b.yml@main
      ```
    - .github/workflows/b.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on:
        workflow_call:
      jobs:
        b:
          uses: ./.github/workflows/called.yml
      ```
- pull-request-target-blocked: a workflow whose on has pull_request_target and no other event (no workflow_call event either), in a repository whose Actions policies block the runs of the workflow on pull_request_target (repo.pull-request-target-allowed false): an event policy that an administrator sets without pull_request_target among the allowed events, or the default policy that GitHub adds to a public repository without an applicable event policy, from the time when GitHub enforces the default policy on the repository. GitHub's documents say that GitHub evaluates the policies before a run, and that a run that a policy does not allow fails with an error. The documents do not say whether a job of such a run starts before the run fails; the rule assumes that no job of such a run starts
  - finding kinds: cache-poisoning.writable-job, cache-poisoning.saved-checkout, cache-poisoning.attacker-key, cache-poisoning.attacker-path
  - fact kinds:
    - repo.pull-request-target-allowed (provider: repo-setting, answer that removes the finding: false)
  - example: pull-request-target-blocked.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a job with cache-mode: write checks out
    #   the base and saves node_modules to the cache.
    # reason: the Actions policies of the repository block the runs of the
    #   workflow on pull_request_target: the default policy that GitHub adds to a
    #   public repository without an applicable event policy, from the time when
    #   GitHub enforces the default policy on the repository, or an event policy
    #   whose list of allowed events does not have pull_request_target. GitHub's
    #   documents say that GitHub evaluates the policies before a run, and that a
    #   run that a policy does not allow fails with an error; the documents do not
    #   say whether a job of such a run starts before the run fails, and the rule
    #   assumes that no job starts.
    # cause: unless a file of facts or --fact says that the Actions policies block
    #   runs on pull_request_target (repo.pull-request-target-allowed false), the
    #   rule reports the finding. When no file of facts and no --fact answers
    #   repo.pull-request-target-allowed, the finding is conditional.
    # attack: a flaw of the job runs the code of the attacker, which saves an
    #   entry under the key of the release workflow.
    # attack-run-behavior: the pull request of the attacker triggers
    #   pull_request_target, and the run fails with an error, and no job of the
    #   run starts (the assumption of the reason), so the job never saves to the
    #   cache.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        cache-mode: write
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: actions/cache@v4
            with:
              path: node_modules
              key: deps-${{ hashFiles('package-lock.json') }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
- actions-policy: a run that the Actions policies of the repository block, in four cases where the rule does not take the policies into account. First, an event policy that blocks an event of the attackers other than pull_request_target (such as issue_comment) in a workflow whose on has that event: the rules ask a fact only for pull_request_target. Second, an actor rule that does not allow the account of the attacker (for example, an actor rule that allows only the repository roles with write access): repo.pull-request-target-allowed is one value for all the runs of a workflow file on pull_request_target, and an actor rule blocks a run by the account that starts the run, so the fact cannot tell what an actor rule blocks. Third, a workflow whose on has pull_request_target and another event: the rule does not ask repo.pull-request-target-allowed for such a workflow, because a run on the other event can reach the job. When the if of the job is false on the other event, so that the job runs only on pull_request_target, and a policy blocks pull_request_target, the finding is a false positive. Fourth, a reusable workflow (on workflow_call) or an action that only workflows on pull_request_target call: the rule asks repo.pull-request-target-allowed only of a workflow whose on has pull_request_target, not of the reusable workflow or the action, so a finding in the reusable workflow or the action is still reported when the policies block the runs of every caller
  - finding kinds: cache-poisoning.writable-job, cache-poisoning.saved-checkout, cache-poisoning.attacker-key, cache-poisoning.attacker-path
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: actions-policy.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a job with cache-mode: write checks out
    #   the base and saves node_modules to the cache.
    # reason: an actor rule of the Actions policies of the repository allows
    #   only the repository roles with write access to trigger the workflow, so a
    #   run that a pull request from an account without write access triggers
    #   fails. GitHub's documents say that GitHub evaluates the policies before a
    #   run, and that a run that a policy does not allow fails with an error; the
    #   documents do not say whether a job of such a run starts before the run
    #   fails, and the rule assumes that no job starts.
    # cause: the rule does not take the actor rules of the Actions policies into
    #   account: repo.pull-request-target-allowed is one value for all the runs of
    #   the workflow file on pull_request_target, and an actor rule blocks a run
    #   by the account that starts the run.
    # attack: a flaw of the job runs the code of the attacker, which saves an
    #   entry under the key of the release workflow.
    # attack-run-behavior: the account of the attacker is not an allowed actor,
    #   so the run on pull_request_target fails with an error, and no job of the
    #   run starts (the assumption of the reason), so the job never saves to the
    #   cache.
    name: policy
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        cache-mode: write
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: actions/cache@v4
            with:
              path: node_modules
              key: deps-${{ hashFiles('package-lock.json') }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
- app-checks-unasked: a run of status, check_suite or check_run in a repository where no app outside GitHub Actions makes a commit status or a check run for a commit that the attacker of the finding writes: the facts that the finding kind asks are false (repo.fork-pr-app-checks for a commit of a pull request from a fork, repo.merge-commit-app-checks for a commit that the merge of a pull request puts in a branch of the repository). In two cases, the rule does not ask these facts, and reports the finding whatever the values of the facts are. First, a workflow whose on has an event other than status, check_suite and check_run: the rule decides whether to ask the facts from the events of on alone, and does not read the if of the job, so the rule does not ask the facts even when the if of the job lets the job run only on status, check_suite or check_run. Second, a reusable workflow (on workflow_call) or an action (an action has no on) that only workflows on status, check_suite or check_run call: the rule asks the facts only of a workflow whose on has only events among these three, not of the reusable workflow or the action, so the rule reports a finding in the reusable workflow or the action whatever the values of the facts are
  - finding kinds: cache-poisoning.writable-job, cache-poisoning.saved-checkout, cache-poisoning.attacker-key, cache-poisoning.attacker-path
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file, repo-file)
  - example: app-checks-unasked.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on status and push, the job runs only on status (its if), and
    #   reads the commit of the status in the way the true positive of the kind
    #   does.
    # reason: no app outside GitHub Actions makes a commit status or a check run
    #   for a commit whose message an attacker writes in the repository: no app
    #   makes one for a commit of a pull request from a fork
    #   (repo.fork-pr-app-checks false), and no app makes one for a commit that
    #   the merge of a pull request puts in a branch
    #   (repo.merge-commit-app-checks false), so no run of status has such a
    #   commit, and the job does not run on push.
    # cause: the rule asks repo.fork-pr-app-checks and
    #   repo.merge-commit-app-checks only of a workflow whose on has no event
    #   other than status, check_suite and check_run, and the on of this
    #   workflow has push.
    # attack-value: github.event.commit.commit.message = "main"
    # attack-run-behavior: no app makes a status for the commit of the pull
    #   request from a fork, so no run of status starts with that commit, and a
    #   push by one who can write runs no job.
    on: [status, push]
    jobs:
      j:
        if: github.event_name == 'status'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        cache-mode: write
        steps:
          - uses: actions/cache/save@v4
            with:
              path: build
              key: build-${{ github.event.commit.commit.message }}
    ```
- actions-not-allowed: a workflow whose run GitHub does not start, or a job that GitHub fails in the step "Set up job", because of the setting of allowed actions of GitHub (the fact repo.allowed-actions, which the quality rule allowed-actions reads): GitHub does not start a run of a workflow that has a uses, or that calls a reusable workflow that has a uses, that the setting does not allow, and fails a job before any step of the job runs when a step of a composite action that the job runs has a uses that the setting does not allow, or when the setting requires a full commit SHA and a step names an action by a tag or a branch. The harm that the finding reports happens only when GitHub runs the workflow or the job, and the rule does not read repo.allowed-actions
  - finding kinds: cache-poisoning.writable-job, cache-poisoning.saved-checkout, cache-poisoning.attacker-key, cache-poisoning.attacker-path
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: actions-not-allowed.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the workflow of the true positive writable-job
    #   (writable-job.yml) of the rule, with a job added whose step uses
    #   example-org/not-allowed-action, which the setting of allowed actions of
    #   GitHub (repo.allowed-actions) blocks with
    #   !example-org/not-allowed-action@*. In the true positive, on
    #   pull_request_target, a job with cache-mode: write checks out the base
    #   and saves node_modules to the cache.
    # reason: GitHub checks each uses of the workflow before the run starts, and
    #   does not start the run because of the uses of
    #   example-org/not-allowed-action: no job of the run runs, so what the
    #   reason of the true positive says does not happen (in runs that the
    #   authors of the rule made on GitHub, such runs ended as startup_failure).
    # cause: the rule does not read repo.allowed-actions.
    # attack: a flaw of the job (a later change that checks out the pull
    #   request's code, or an injection) runs the attacker's code, which saves
    #   an entry under the key of the release workflow.
    # attack-run-behavior: GitHub does not start the run, so no step of the run
    #   runs, and the attack does nothing.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        cache-mode: write
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: actions/cache@v4
            with:
              path: node_modules
              key: deps-${{ hashFiles('package-lock.json') }}
          - run: npm ci
      not-allowed:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: example-org/not-allowed-action@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```
- absent-approval-label: a job that runs only when a label is added (pull_request_target with the activity type labeled), whose if compares the label with a name that no label of the repository has, in a run of the linter that adds the attacker triage-account: the rule reads every label that the if compares with as a label of the repository, and reads the attacker as able to add the label; when the repository has no such label, the attacker cannot add the label, because the triage role cannot create a label, and the job does not run on the pull request of the attacker. The linter does not read the labels of the repository
  - finding kinds: cache-poisoning.writable-job, cache-poisoning.saved-checkout, cache-poisoning.attacker-key, cache-poisoning.attacker-path
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - added attackers: triage-account
  - example: absent-approval-label.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target with the activity type labeled, a job
    #   that runs only when the label safe-to-test is added checks out the head
    #   of the pull request, runs npm ci, and has a token that writes and a
    #   cache that the job may save to.
    # reason: in a run of the linter that adds triage-account, the rule reads
    #   the label safe-to-test as a label that the attacker can add; when the
    #   repository has no label safe-to-test, the attacker cannot add the
    #   label, because the triage role cannot create a label, and the job does
    #   not run on the attacker's pull request.
    # cause: the rule does not read the labels of the repository: it reads
    #   every label that the if of the job compares with as a label that the
    #   repository has.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the head of the pull request = "{\"scripts\": {\"preinstall\": \"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: the repository has no label safe-to-test, so the
    #   attacker cannot add the label safe-to-test, no run of the job starts,
    #   and npm never runs the preinstall script.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    jobs:
      build:
        if: github.event.label.name == 'safe-to-test'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        cache-mode: write
        permissions:
          contents: write
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```

### threat

- precondition app-status-check: an app outside GitHub Actions, such as an outside CI, makes a commit status or a check run for a commit whose message an attacker writes (a commit of a pull request from a fork, or a commit that merges a pull request; the message of a commit that merges a pull request can have the title of the pull request), and the commit status or the check run starts a run of status, check_suite or check_run, which runs the workflow of the default branch, whatever branch the commit is on. The payload of a run of any of the three events has the SHA of the commit, and the payload of a run of status or check_suite also has the message, the author name and the committer name of the commit. A finding of a workflow whose on has only events among status, check_suite and check_run (one, two or all three) holds only when the fact of the commit is true: repo.fork-pr-app-checks for a commit of a pull request from a fork, and repo.merge-commit-app-checks for a commit that the merge of a pull request puts in a branch of the repository or that a merge queue of the repository makes. A finding kind asks the fact of each kind of commit that its attackers write; the finding of a finding kind that asks both facts holds when at least one of the two facts is true. The rule does not ask these facts of a workflow whose on has another event too, and reports the finding of such a workflow whatever the values of the facts are. The finding is conditional when no file of facts and no --fact answers the facts
  - observed: 2026-11-05, runner 2.338.2: a GitHub App made a commit status and a check run for a commit of a pull request from a fork: runs of status, check_suite and check_run started on the default branch, and the message of the commit, with \$( ) in it, was in commit.commit.message of status and in check_suite.head_commit.message of check_suite
  - observed: 2026-11-06, runner 2.338.2: the same again: the SHA of the commit of the pull request was in sha and commit.sha of status, check_suite.head_sha and check_suite.head_commit.id of check_suite, and check_run.head_sha and check_run.check_suite.head_sha of check_run; check_suite.after and check_suite.before were null; the author name and the committer name of the commit, with \$( ) in each, were in the payloads of status and check_suite
  - cites:
    - <https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows#status>
    - <https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows#check_suite>
    - <https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows#check_run>
- precondition callers-events: a reusable workflow or a composite action that is among the inputs runs on the events of the callers of the workflow or the action, whoever the callers are; when the inputs are the whole repository and hold every caller of the workflow or the action, the rule reads the workflow or the action on the events of the callers, with the values that the callers give under with
  - cites:
    - <https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows#workflow_call>
    - <https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7x29-qqmq-v6qc>
- precondition privileged-job: the job runs on an event that one without write access triggers, which runs on the default branch: pull_request_target, workflow_run, issue_comment, issues, discussion, discussion_comment, fork; status, check_suite and check_run where an app outside GitHub Actions makes a commit status or a check run for a commit whose message an attacker writes (the precondition app-status-check); not pull_request, whose caches are of the merge ref, with cache-mode write too; not pull_request_review and pull_request_review_comment, whose caches the rule reads as of the merge ref too (the undetected form review-event); not workflow_dispatch, which one with write access to the permission Actions dispatches and for which the one who dispatches the workflow chooses only a branch or a tag of the repository and the inputs: the run builds the repository's code, and a key, a path or a checkout that an input of workflow_dispatch decides is the inconclusive kind input-dispatch
  - observed: 2026-10-13, runner 2.337.0: a pull_request run saved its caches to refs/pull/&lt;n>/merge, with cache-mode: write too
  - cites:
    - <https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/dependency-caching>
- precondition no-approval: no one approves the run: either the job runs on at least one event other than pull_request_target with the activity type labeled, and a run on the other event starts with no label added, or no person adds the label that starts the run, as the label is a label that a workflow of the repository of the job adds to the pull request of an attacker by running actions/labeler with a token other than the GITHUB_TOKEN; and the job has no environment that has required reviewers (repo.environment-protected false: an environment is made with no protection rules)
  - observed: 2026-09-28, runner 2.337.0: a push after the label ran no labeled run, and ran pull_request_target on synchronize
- precondition cache-writes: the job's cache-mode, or else the workflow's, is write or write-only: on those events GitHub lets a job save to the cache of the default branch's scope only then; a reusable workflow's, when the job that calls it writes none
  - observed: 2026-10-13, runner 2.337.0: on pull_request_target, issue_comment and workflow_run, a job with cache-mode write or write-only saved a cache to the default branch's scope, and one without it was denied
  - cites:
    - <https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/dependency-caching>
    - <https://github.com/github/docs/blob/5815d11586b0796688963a98c889680e60d72dc4/content/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/dependency-caching.md>
- precondition flaw-in-job: a flaw runs the attacker's code in the job: an injection, a checkout of their code; the code saves to the cache with no action of the cache needed; the rule does not look for it, the other rules report those they see
  - cites:
    - <https://github.com/AdnaneKhan/Cacheract/blob/10f00b0cfba6a416c86a16145698720281436358/README.md>
- precondition restored-later: a later run of the repository restores the entry and runs what it has: any workflow of the default branch restores its caches, and the attacker can save under a key that run looks up next
  - cites:
    - <https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/dependency-caching>
    - <https://tanstack.com/blog/npm-supply-chain-compromise-postmortem>
- precondition pr-tree: the checkout brings the pull request's code: its head or merge commit, refs/pull/&lt;n>/head or merge, or the fork as the repository; a branch's name with the base repository brings the base's branch of that name, if any
  - observed: 2026-09-28, runner 2.337.0: a checkout of the fork's head SHA, refs/pull/&lt;n>/head and refs/pull/&lt;n>/merge from the base repository brought the fork's commit and the merge commit; one of head.ref with the base repository failed, as the base had no such branch
  - cites:
    - <https://securitylab.github.com/resources/github-actions-preventing-pwn-requests/>
- precondition no-guard: on pull_request_target and workflow_run, the release of actions/checkout does not refuse a fork's code: v1, a release before the guard (v2.8.0, v3.7.0, v4.4.0, v5.1.0, v6.1.0, v7.0.0), a commit pinned before it, or allow-unsafe-pr-checkout set; issue_comment is not guarded
  - observed: 2026-09-28, runner 2.337.0: v7.0.1 and the major tag v4 refused the fork's head SHA and refs/pull/&lt;n>/head on pull_request_target and workflow_run, and allowed them with allow-unsafe-pr-checkout; v4.2.2 pinned by its SHA fetched them; on issue_comment v7.0.1 fetched refs/pull/&lt;n>/head
  - cites:
    - <https://github.blog/changelog/2026-06-18-safer-pull_request_target-defaults-for-github-actions-checkout>
- precondition saves-tree: actions/cache, at the end of the job, or actions/cache/save after the checkout, saves a path that is the tree, in it or above it: a path in the workspace, no clean checkout of the same place done in between
  - cites:
    - <https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/dependency-caching>
- precondition attacker-cache-input: the key or the path of actions/cache or actions/cache/save has a value the attacker writes on the event: the title, the body or the branch of the pull request or the issue, the comment
  - cites:
    - <https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/dependency-caching>
- actor: fork-pr-author
  - via: opens or updates a pull request from a fork, which runs pull_request_target, and workflow_run after its pull_request; or pushes a commit to the pull request, and an app outside GitHub Actions makes a commit status or a check run for the commit, and the commit status or the check run starts a run of status, check_suite or check_run whose actor is the app
  - events: pull_request_target, workflow_run, status, check_suite, check_run
  - run starters: pull_request_target: attacker, workflow_run: attacker, status: attacker, check_suite: attacker, check_run: attacker
  - gains: write-cache
- actor: issue-author
  - via: opens an issue or a discussion
  - events: issues, discussion
  - run starters: issues: attacker, discussion: attacker
  - gains: write-cache
- actor: commenter
  - via: comments on an issue, a pull request or a discussion, or reviews a pull request from a branch of the repository or comments on the diff of the pull request
  - events: issue_comment, discussion_comment, pull_request_review, pull_request_review_comment
  - run starters: issue_comment: attacker, discussion_comment: attacker, pull_request_review: attacker, pull_request_review_comment: attacker
  - gains: write-cache
- actor: anyone-who-forks
  - via: forks the repository
  - events: fork
  - run starters: fork: attacker
  - gains: write-cache
- actor: merged-commit-author
  - via: writes the message of a commit that is merged, or put in a merge queue, and an app outside GitHub Actions makes a commit status or a check run for the commit, and the commit status or the check run starts a run of status, check_suite or check_run
  - events: status, check_suite, check_run
  - run starters: status: other, check_suite: other, check_run: other
  - gains: write-cache
- incident tanstack-2026: 2026-05-11: a pull request ran its code in a pull_request_target job, whose actions/cache saved the pnpm store the code changed to the default branch's scope under the key of the release workflow; the release workflow restored it and published 84 versions of npm packages
  - advisory: <https://tanstack.com/blog/npm-supply-chain-compromise-postmortem>
  - compromised: tanstack/router

#### cache-poisoning.writable-job

- vector: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:L/VA:L/SC:H/SI:H/SA:N/E:P
- CVSS-B: 7.0 (high)
- CVSS-BT: 4.9 (medium)
- impact: H (from SC, SI)
- likelihood: medium (from AV:N, AT:P, PR:N)
- severity: high (impact H, likelihood medium; the table: sisakulint --explain=terms)
- AV: N
  - reason: the attacker opens an issue, a comment or a pull request over the network
  - cites: none
- AC: L
  - reason: once a flaw runs their code in the job, it saves to the cache as the job may, with no action of the cache needed (Cacheract)
  - cites:
    - <https://github.com/AdnaneKhan/Cacheract/blob/10f00b0cfba6a416c86a16145698720281436358/README.md>
- AT: P
  - reason: a flaw has to run the attacker's code in the job, and a later run has to restore the entry they save
  - cites: none
- PR: N
  - reason: on a public repository anyone opens an issue or a pull request from a fork
  - cites: none
- UI: N
  - reason: the event runs the job with nobody doing anything
  - cites: none
- VC: N
  - reason: the cache gives the run nothing to read that the job does not
  - cites: none
- VI: L
  - reason: the entries of the cache change; the repository does not as such
  - cites: none
- VA: L
  - reason: entries the attacker saves can push others out of the cache
  - cites: none
- SC: H
  - reason: a later run that restores the entry runs it with its own secrets: in the TanStack incident a release run minted a token to publish
  - cites:
    - <https://tanstack.com/blog/npm-supply-chain-compromise-postmortem>
- SI: H
  - reason: what that run builds and publishes reaches those who use the repository: 84 versions of npm packages in the TanStack incident
  - cites:
    - <https://tanstack.com/blog/npm-supply-chain-compromise-postmortem>
- SA: N
  - reason: nothing past the repository is made unavailable by this as such
  - cites: none
- E: P
  - reason: Cacheract saves a cache from any code run in a job that may; the TanStack incident ran in a job that saved before GitHub made the attacker's events read the cache only, not through cache-mode
  - cites:
    - <https://github.com/AdnaneKhan/Cacheract/blob/10f00b0cfba6a416c86a16145698720281436358/README.md>
    - <https://tanstack.com/blog/npm-supply-chain-compromise-postmortem>

## code-injection

- problem: a value an attacker controls is written by \${{ }} into a run script or the script of actions/github-script, where it runs as code; or the script of a run of bash passes such a value, through a variable of env, to a command or a place that reads the value as code
- expected: no value an attacker controls is written by \${{ }} into such a script where it runs as code, and no script passes such a value, through a variable of env, to a command or a place that reads the value as code
- severity: critical (the worst of its kinds)
- targets: workflow, action-metadata
- facets:
  - weakness: script-injection
  - attack-means: string
- default run: always: in a run without --rule, the rule runs unless --skip-rule names the rule

### finding kinds

- code-injection.controlled
  - detected: {expr_ref} is written into {sink_kind} by \${{ }}, and an attacker controls it on {controlled_on}
  - arguments:
    - {expr_ref}: The reference in the expression, such as github.event.issue.title.
    - {sink_kind}: The kind of script in which a value is written as code: the run script of a step, or the script of actions/github-script.
    - {controlled_on}: The events on which an attacker controls the value of the expression, each event named once.
  - consequence: the value becomes code
  - remedy: pass it through env and read the variable
  - severity: critical (found from the CVSS metrics below by the table)
  - fix kinds: env-var, env-var-review
  - fact kinds: repo.pull-request-target-allowed (provider: repo-setting), repo.fork-pr-app-checks (provider: repo-setting), repo.merge-commit-app-checks (provider: repo-setting)
  - attackers: fork-pr-author, issue-author, commenter, merged-commit-author, anyone-who-forks
  - preconditions: runner-writes, attacker-writes, attacker-event, callers-events, app-status-check
  - incidents: ultralytics-2024
  - true positives:
    - called/action.yaml (action-metadata, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: the directory of a composite action has action.yml as a
      #   directory and action.yaml as a file; a workflow on issues calls the
      #   action, whose run step echoes the title of the issue, written in by ${{
      #   }}.
      # reason: the runner reads action.yml only when it is a file, and reads
      #   action.yaml when action.yml is a directory, so action.yaml runs. Anyone
      #   who opens an issue writes its title, and ${{ }} puts the title into the
      #   script before the shell parses the script, so a double quote in the
      #   title ends the echo's string and what follows runs as commands.
      # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
      # attack-run-behavior: the script becomes echo ""; echo PWNED; echo "", and
      #   the shell runs the second echo as a command, which prints PWNED.
      name: echo title
      description: echo the title of the issue
      runs:
        using: composite
        steps:
          - run: echo "${{ github.event.issue.title }}"
            shell: bash
      ```
      - finding on: called/action.yaml
      - .github/workflows/ci.yml (workflow)
        ```yaml
        on: issues
        jobs:
          j:
            runs-on: ubuntu-latest
            steps:
              - uses: ./called
        ```
      - called/action.yml/keep (repo-file)
        ```yaml
        action.yml is a directory here, not a file
        ```
    - .github/workflows/called.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: the called workflow writes inputs.t into a run by ${{ }}; the
      #   caller ci.yml runs on issues and gives the issue's title as t.
      # reason: anyone who opens an issue writes its title, and ${{ }} puts the
      #   title into the script before the shell parses it, so a double quote in
      #   it ends the echo's string and what follows runs as commands.
      # attack-value: inputs.t = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
      # attack-run-behavior: ci.yml gives the title as t, and the script of the
      #   called workflow's step becomes echo ""; echo PWNED; echo "", and the
      #   shell runs the second echo as a command, which prints PWNED.
      on:
        workflow_call:
          inputs:
            t: {type: string}
      jobs:
        j:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: echo "${{ inputs.t }}"
      ```
      - finding on: .github/workflows/called.yml
      - .github/workflows/ci.yml (workflow)
        ```yaml
        on: issues
        jobs:
          c:
            uses: ./.github/workflows/called.yml
            with:
              t: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
        ```
    - controlled.ghsa-6q4m-7476-932w.action.yml (action-metadata, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a composite action with no caller among the files that the linter
      #   reads, whose step writes the name of a branch into run by ${{ }}. The step
      #   is the step get-github-ref-name of action.yml of
      #   rlespinasse/github-slug-action (commit
      #   a362e5fb42057a3a23a62218b050838f1bacca5d, the parent of the fix
      #   102b1a064a9b145e56556e22b18b19c624538d94, lines 60-68); the steps before
      #   and after it are left out.
      #   helpers/version/action.yml of home-assistant/actions (commit
      #   3516188c0268acb4d0b0a7a984f9668c348deca0, GHSL-2023-179) writes
      #   github.head_ref into [[ ! -z "…" ]] of its step publish the same way
      #   (line 104).
      # reason: with no caller among the files that the linter reads, the rule reads
      #   the action on every event an attacker triggers, pull_request_target among
      #   the events. On pull_request_target, the author of a pull request names its
      #   head branch, which github.head_ref gives, and the runner puts the name into
      #   the script before bash reads the script, so a $( ) in the name runs as a
      #   command.
      # attack-value: github.head_ref = "a$(echo${IFS}PWNED)"
      # attack-run-behavior: the author of a pull request from a fork names its head
      #   branch a$(echo${IFS}PWNED) (a name of a branch has no space, and ${IFS}
      #   stands for one). The step runs refname="a$(echo${IFS}PWNED)", and bash runs
      #   the command substitution, which prints PWNED.
      # advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6q4m-7476-932w
      # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2023-179_Home_Assistant/
      name: GitHub Slug Action
      description: a step that writes the name of a branch into run
      runs:
        using: composite
        steps:
          - id: get-github-ref-name
            run: |
              refname="${{ github.head_ref || github.ref_name }}"
              if [ -f "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ]; then
                echo "github-ref-name=${refname}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              else
                echo "::set-output name=github-ref-name::${refname}"
              fi
            shell: bash
      ```
    - controlled.ghsa-7x29-qqmq-v6qc.action.yml (action-metadata, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a composite action puts github.event.pull_request.head.ref and
      #   github.head_ref into the script of its step. This is the form of the
      #   composite action ultralytics/actions at commit af42cbd, which wrote the
      #   two values into the run: key of its step.
      # reason: the runner puts the name of the head branch into the script before
      #   bash reads the script, so the author of a pull request writes code that
      #   the step runs in the workflow that uses the action.
      # attack-value: github.event.pull_request.head.ref = "x\";echo${IFS}PWNED;#"
      # attack-run-behavior: the first line of the script becomes echo
      #   "github.event.pull_request.head.ref: x";echo${IFS}PWNED;#", and bash
      #   prints PWNED.
      # advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7x29-qqmq-v6qc
      name: actions
      description: the form of ultralytics/actions af42cbd
      runs:
        using: composite
        steps:
          - name: Print
            run: |
              echo "github.event.pull_request.head.ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}"
              echo "github.head_ref: ${{ github.head_ref }}"
            shell: bash
      ```
    - controlled.ghsa-8v8w-v8xg-79rf.action.yml (action-metadata, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a composite action with no caller among the files that the linter
      #   reads, whose step writes the name of the head branch into run by ${{ }}.
      #   The step is the step branch of action.yml of tj-actions/branch-names
      #   v7.0.6 (commit ab304d8562e2f137165e1d930e6d22d431189074, lines 39-44 and
      #   58); the lines for the base ref and the ref, the lines that strip refs/heads/
      #   and the branch for ::set-output are left out.
      # reason: with no caller among the files that the linter reads, the rule reads
      #   the action on every event an attacker triggers, pull_request_target among
      #   the events. On pull_request_target, the author of a pull request names its
      #   head branch, which github.event.pull_request.head.ref and github.head_ref
      #   give, and the runner puts the name into the script before bash reads the
      #   script, so a $( ) in the name runs as a command.
      # attack-value: github.head_ref = "a$(echo${IFS}PWNED)"
      # attack-run-behavior: the author of a pull request from a fork names its head
      #   branch a$(echo${IFS}PWNED) (a name of a branch has no space, and ${IFS}
      #   stands for one). The step runs printf "%q" "a$(echo${IFS}PWNED)", and bash
      #   runs the command substitution in the double quotes before printf starts,
      #   which prints PWNED.
      # advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8v8w-v8xg-79rf
      name: Branch Names
      description: a step that writes the name of the head branch into run
      runs:
        using: composite
        steps:
          - id: branch
            run: |
              if [[ "${{ github.ref }}" != "refs/tags/"* ]]; then
                HEAD_REF=$(printf "%q" "${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref || github.head_ref }}")
                echo "head_ref_branch=$(eval printf "%s" "$HEAD_REF")" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              fi
            shell: bash
      ```
    - called/action.yml (action-metadata, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a composite action whose steps write an input into run by ${{ }},
      #   in the ways of four advisories, and a caller,
      #   .github/workflows/validate.yml, which gives the body of a pull request as
      #   each input on pull_request_target. The step ydb is
      #   .github/actions/validate_pr_description/action.yaml of ydb-platform/ydb
      #   (commit dd07662a0e0b98b6bbd07da00386bb889c683c27, lines 6-9): the input in
      #   double quotes of echo. The step prek is the step Resolve download URL of
      #   action.yaml of j178/prek-action (v1.0.5, commit
      #   93b4659bafa2a5a18b7aaa0130b417f0ae29b1ac, lines 26-29): the input in double
      #   quotes of [ ]; lines 31-37 of the script and the steps after the step are
      #   left out. The step sonar is the step Run SonarScanner of action.yml of
      #   SonarSource/sonarqube-scan-action (v5.3.0, commit
      #   8c71dc039c2dd71d3821e89a2b58ecc7fee6ced9, lines 53-55): the input as the
      #   words of an array, with no quotes; the lines that run the scanner (lines
      ```

      ```yaml
      #   openapi.yml of jellyfin/jellyfin (commit
      #   92a0d26f31743ca0015fcc3e0a4fe094792ac63c, GHSL-2023-107) writes
      #   github.head_ref into git merge-base (line 51).

      #   the head repository of the pull request into a run on pull_request_target
      #   the same way.
      # reason: the author of a pull request, from a fork too, writes its title, and
      #   the runner puts the title into the script before bash reads the script;
      #   the if of the step reads the head branch, which the author also names.
      # attack-value: github.event.pull_request.title = "x\"; echo PWNED>/proc/$$/fd/1; echo \""
      # attack-run-behavior: the author of a pull request from a fork whose head
      #   branch starts with mergify/bp/ titles it with the value; the script
      #   becomes ORI_PR=$(echo "x"; echo PWNED>/proc/$$/fd/1; echo "" | …), and
      #   bash runs the second echo as a command, which prints PWNED to the log of
      #   the step, with the token of the job.
      # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-058_GHSL-2024-059_starrocks/
      # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-057_infinispan/
      # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-048_infinispan/
      # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-049_EVE/
      # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-145_Discord_js/
      # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-053_Hedy/
      # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-051_Misskey/
      # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-041_GHSL-2024-042_KubeBlocks/
      # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2023-100_Apache_Ignite/
      # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2023-107_Jellyfin/
      # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2020-240-scikit-learn-workflow/
      # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2020-242-telegramdesktop-tdesktop-workflow/
      # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2020-244-nonebot-nonebot2-workflow/
      # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2021-007-dmlc-gluon-nlp-workflows/
      # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2021-015-a2o-snoopy-workflows/
      # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2021-017-teal-language-tl-workflows/
      # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2021-016-Tautulli-workflows/
      # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2023-027_Engine_for_Cocos_Creator/
      # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2023-022_Cloudstack/
      # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2023-099_Design_patterns_implemented_in_Java/
      # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2023-101_Zcash/
      # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2023-104_CDK_for_Terraform/
      # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2023-110_Wing_Language/
      on:
        pull_request_target:
      permissions: write-all
      jobs:
        sync-checker:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          name: SYNC CHECKER
          steps:
            - name: backport assign
              id: backport_assign
              if: startsWith(github.head_ref, 'mergify/bp/') && github.event.action == 'opened'
              env:
                GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
                PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.number }}
                REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
              run: |
                ORI_PR=$(echo "${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}" | grep -oP '\(backport #\K\d+' | tail -n 1)
                author=$(gh pr view ${ORI_PR} -R ${REPO} --json author -q '.author.login')
                if [[ ! "${author}" =~ "mergify" ]]; then
                  gh pr edit ${PR_NUMBER} -R ${REPO} --add-assignee ${author} || true
                  echo "ORI_PR=${ORI_PR}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
                fi
      ```

      ```yaml
      # situation: on workflow_run of runs on master, release/* and next/*, a step

      #   into a JavaScript string of its script by ${{ }}. This is the step Generate
      #   Slack Payload of release-and-tests-fail-bot.yml of Kong/kong (commit
      #   99cb0608050cbd14611e7795960aade9fc6360cc, lines 1-17, 47-59 and 66); the

      #   constants and the step that posts the payload are left out.
      #   notify-tsc-members-mention.yml of asyncapi/.github (commit
      #   703ea72bb92c214b226ecb1484df21a23f835c8d, GHSL-2024-052) writes the titles
      #   of issues, pull requests and discussions into JavaScript strings of
      #   actions/github-script the same way (lines 72, 117, 162, 207, 252 and 297).
      # reason: on workflow_run, the author of a pull request from a fork names the
      #   head branch of the triggering run, which
      #   github.event.workflow_run.head_branch gives (a branch named release/… of
      #   the fork passes the filter of branches), and the runner puts the name into
      #   the script before node.js reads the script, so a " in the name ends the
      #   string and the rest runs as JavaScript.
      # attack-value: github.event.workflow_run.head_branch = "release/x\";console.log('PWNED');\""
      # attack-run-behavior: the script becomes const branch_name = "release/x";
      #   console.log('PWNED');""; and node.js runs console.log, which prints PWNED,
      #   with secrets.PAT and the Slack webhook of the job within reach.
      # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-126_Kong/
      # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-052_AsyncAPI/
      on:
        workflow_run:
          workflows: ["Package & Release", "Build & Test"]
          types:
            - completed
          branches:
            - master
            - release/*
            - next/*
      jobs:
        notify_failure:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - name: Generate Slack Payload
              id: generate-payload
              uses: actions/github-script@v7
              with:
                script: |
                  const branch_name = "${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}";
                  return { text: `branch: "${branch_name}"` };
      ```

      ```yaml
      # situation: on workflow_run, after the artifact of the triggering run is
      #   unzipped, a step reads pr/pr_base of the artifact into a variable of the
      #   script and writes PR_BASE=<value> to $GITHUB_ENV, and a later step writes

      #   ${{ }}. This is pr-sonar.yml of adobe/react-spectrum-charts (commit
      #   886e2d55d381ff4233a83b4a46f602bac73f2e0f, lines 1-9 and 42-68); the
      #   checkout of the code of the pull request, the download with
      #   actions/github-script, the lines for PR_NUMBER and PR_BRANCH, the echo
      #   lines and the steps after line 68 are left out.
      # reason: on workflow_run, the author of a pull request from a fork names the
      #   head branch of the triggering run, which github.event.workflow_run.head_branch
      #   gives, and the runner puts the name into the script before bash reads the
      #   script (GHSL-2024-267). The rule reports the head branch; it does not
      #   follow pr_base through the variable of the script into $GITHUB_ENV and
      #   env.PR_BASE (GHSL-2024-266 and the rest of GHSL-2024-267; the
      #   envvar-injection undetected form script-var).
      # attack-value: github.event.workflow_run.head_branch = "x;echo${IFS}PWNED;#"
      # attack-run-behavior: the author of a pull request from a fork names its head
      #   branch x;echo${IFS}PWNED;# (a name of a branch has no space, and ${IFS}
      #   stands for one). The step Checkout base branch runs git checkout x, then
      #   echo PWNED, which prints PWNED, with the token of the job.
      # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-266_GHSL-2024-267_Adobe_React_Spectrum_Charts/
      on:
        workflow_run:
          workflows: [PR Build]
          types: [completed]
      jobs:
        sonar:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          timeout-minutes: 30
          steps:
            - name: Unzip artifacts 📁
              run: unzip rsc-pr-build-artifacts.zip
            - name: Setup workflow variables 📝
              run: |
                pr_base="$(<pr/pr_base)"
                echo "PR_BASE=${pr_base}" >> $GITHUB_ENV
            - name: Checkout base branch 🌳
              run: |
                git remote add upstream ${{ github.event.repository.clone_url }}
                git fetch upstream
                git checkout -B ${{ env.PR_BASE }} upstream/${{ env.PR_BASE }}
                git checkout ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}
                git clean -ffdx && git reset --hard HEAD
      ```

      ```yaml
      # situation: a composite action that downloads and installs lychee and runs

      #   8ad54d3568ac3176a9fb57a0233cf04410b55cde, the parent of the fix
      #   7cd0af4c74a61395d455af97419279d86aafaede, as it was (lychee-action
      #   before 2.0.2). The advisory
      #   (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-65rg-554r-9j5x, CVE-2024-48908):
      #   "The GitHub Action variable `inputs.lycheeVersion` can be used to
      #   execute arbitrary code in the context of the action." The advisory's
      #   proof of concept gives the value in with; here the issue's title gives

      # attack-value: inputs.lycheeVersion = "$(printenv >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY && echo \"v0.16.1\")' ]]; echo PWNED; [[ '"
      # attack-run-behavior: the value stands in five places of the script of
      #   Download and extract lychee. The first test becomes if [[ '$(printenv >>
      #   $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY && echo "v0.16.1")' ]]; echo PWNED; [[ '' =~
      #   ^v0\.0|^v0\.1[0-5]\. ]]; then: the single quote ends the quoted string,
      #   ]] ends the test, and bash runs echo PWNED as a command of the if's
      #   condition, which prints PWNED; the last test is false, so the else
      #   branch runs, and its tests for nightly and latest print PWNED the same
      #   way. In the last else, the value is inside the double quotes of
      #   DOWNLOAD_URL, where bash runs the advisory's command substitution,
      #   printenv >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY, which writes the step's environment to
      #   the job summary, and puts v0.16.1 in its place; the step then goes on to
      #   curl and tar.
      # advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-65rg-554r-9j5x
      name: "Lychee Broken Link Checker"
      description: "Quickly check links in Markdown, HTML, and text files"

      inputs:
        args:
          description: "Lychee arguments (https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee#commandline-parameters)"
          default: "--verbose --no-progress './**/*.md' './**/*.html' './**/*.rst'"
          required: false
        debug:
          description: "Enable debug output in action (set -x). Helpful for troubleshooting."
          default: false
          required: false
        fail:
          description: "Fail entire pipeline on error (i.e. when lychee exit code is not 0)"
          default: true
          required: false
        failIfEmpty:
          description: "Fail entire pipeline if no links were found"
          default: true
          required: false
        format:
          description: "Summary output format (e.g. json)"
          default: "markdown"
          required: false
        jobSummary:
          description: "Write GitHub job summary at the end of the job (written on Markdown output only)"
          default: true
          required: false
        lycheeVersion:
          description: "Use custom version of lychee link checker"
          default: v0.16.1
          required: false
        output:
          description: "Summary output file path"
          default: "lychee/out.md"
          required: false
        token:
          description: "Your GitHub Access Token, defaults to: {{ github.token }}"
          default: ${{ github.token }}
          required: false

      outputs:
        exit_code:
          description: "The exit code returned from Lychee"
          value: ${{ steps.run-lychee.outputs.exit_code }}

      runs:
        using: "composite"
        steps:
          - name: Set up environment
            run: |
              echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
              mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin"
            shell: bash

          - name: Clean up existing lychee files
            run: |
              # Remove any existing lychee binaries or archives to prevent conflicts
              rm -f "$HOME/.local/bin/lychee"
              rm -rf lychee
              rm -f "${{ steps.lychee-filename.outputs.filename }}"
            shell: bash

          - name: Download and extract lychee
            id: lychee-setup
            run: |
              # Determine filename and download URL based on version
              if [[ '${{ inputs.lycheeVersion }}' =~ ^v0\.0|^v0\.1[0-5]\. ]]; then
                FILENAME="lychee-${{ inputs.lycheeVersion }}-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz"
                DOWNLOAD_URL="https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee/releases/download/${{ inputs.lycheeVersion }}/${FILENAME}"
              else
                FILENAME="lychee-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz"
                if [[ '${{ inputs.lycheeVersion }}' == 'nightly' ]]; then
                  DOWNLOAD_URL="https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee/releases/download/nightly/${FILENAME}"
                elif [[ '${{ inputs.lycheeVersion }}' == 'latest' ]]; then
                  DOWNLOAD_URL="https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee/releases/latest/download/${FILENAME}"
                else
                  DOWNLOAD_URL="https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee/releases/download/lychee-${{ inputs.lycheeVersion }}/${FILENAME}"
                fi
              fi

              echo "Downloading from: ${DOWNLOAD_URL}"
              curl -sfLO "${DOWNLOAD_URL}"

              echo "Extracting ${FILENAME}"
              tar -xvzf "${FILENAME}"

              # Output filename for use in later steps
              echo "filename=${FILENAME}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            shell: bash

          - name: Install lychee
            run: |
              install -t "$HOME/.local/bin" -D lychee
            shell: bash

          - name: Clean up installation files
            run: |
              # Remove the downloaded archive and any unnecessary files after installation
              rm -f "${{ steps.lychee-setup.outputs.filename }}"
              shopt -s extglob
              rm -f lychee!(*-bin|*-lib|*.toml)
            shell: bash

          - name: Run Lychee
            id: run-lychee
            run: |
              # This step runs lychee and captures its exit code.
              # We use 'set +e' to prevent the script from exiting immediately if lychee fails.
              # This allows us to capture the exit code and pass it both to GitHub Actions (via GITHUB_OUTPUT)
              # and to the shell (via the final 'exit $EXIT_CODE').
              # This ensures that:
              # 1. The step fails if lychee fails
              # 2. The exit code is available as an output for subsequent steps
              # 3. The exit code is properly propagated to the workflow
              set +e
              ${{ github.action_path }}/entrypoint.sh
              EXIT_CODE=$?
              echo "exit_code=$EXIT_CODE" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
              exit $EXIT_CODE
            env:
              # https://github.com/actions/runner/issues/665
              INPUT_TOKEN: ${{ inputs.TOKEN }}
              INPUT_ARGS: ${{ inputs.ARGS }}
              INPUT_DEBUG: ${{ inputs.DEBUG }}
              INPUT_FAIL: ${{ inputs.FAIL }}
              INPUT_FAILIFEMPTY: ${{ inputs.FAILIFEMPTY }}
              INPUT_FORMAT: ${{ inputs.FORMAT }}
              INPUT_JOBSUMMARY: ${{ inputs.JOBSUMMARY }}
              INPUT_OUTPUT: ${{ inputs.OUTPUT }}
            shell: bash
      branding:
        icon: "external-link"
        color: "purple"
      ```
      - finding on: called/action.yml
      - .github/workflows/links.yml (workflow)
        ```yaml
        # The caller: on issues, it gives the issue's title as lycheeVersion, which
        # the action writes into run (the advisory's input, from an attacker).
        on: issues
        jobs:
          links:
            runs-on: ubuntu-latest
            steps:
              - uses: actions/checkout@v4
              - uses: ./called
                with:
                  lycheeVersion: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
        ```
    - controlled.no-caller.action.yml (action-metadata, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a composite action with no caller among the files that the
      #   linter reads; a run step echoes the title of an issue, written in by ${{
      #   }}.
      # reason: with no caller among the files that the linter reads, the rule
      #   reads the action on every event an attacker triggers, issues among the
      #   events. Anyone who opens an issue writes its title, and ${{ }} puts the
      #   title into the script before the shell parses the script, so a double
      #   quote in the title ends the echo's string and what follows runs as
      #   commands.
      # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
      # attack-run-behavior: the script becomes echo ""; echo PWNED; echo "", and
      #   the shell runs the second echo as a command, which prints PWNED.
      name: echo title
      description: echo the title of the issue
      runs:
        using: composite
        steps:
          - run: echo "${{ github.event.issue.title }}"
            shell: bash
      ```

      ```yaml
      #   what follows runs as commands.
      ```
