      ```yaml
                BODY: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
              run: echo "body=$(printf '%s' "${BODY}" | tr -d '\n')" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      ```
- envvar-injection.wiki
  - detected: {expr_ref} is written to \$GITHUB_ENV, and an attacker who controls it on gollum can start a name of their own
  - arguments:
    - {expr_ref}: The reference as written.
  - consequence: a line break in the value, or a name before its =, sets other environment variables of the steps after it
  - remedy: keep the value after the = and take its line breaks out, or write it as name&lt;&lt;DELIM with a random delimiter
  - severity: critical (found from the CVSS metrics below by the table)
  - fix kinds: env-var-review
  - fact kinds: repo.wiki-open (provider: repo-setting)
  - attackers: wiki-editor
  - preconditions: runner-reads-lines, wiki-title-lines, attacker-event, callers-events, wiki-open, bash-env
  - true positives:
    - wiki.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on gollum, a step writes page= and the wiki page's title to
      #   $GITHUB_ENV.
      # reason: anyone may edit the wiki when it is open to all (repo.wiki-open
      #   true), and the runner reads $GITHUB_ENV one line at a time as NAME=value,
      #   so a line of the title such as LD_PRELOAD=... becomes a variable of its
      #   own, which changes what the programs of the later steps load.
      # attack-value: github.event.pages[0].title = "x\nPWNED=1"
      # attack-run-behavior: PAGE holds x, a line break and PWNED=1, so echo
      #   appends the two lines page=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_ENV; the runner
      #   reads each line as NAME=value and sets page to x and PWNED to 1 for the
      #   steps after it. A line LD_PRELOAD=<path> in place of PWNED=1 is set the
      #   same way.
      on: gollum
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                PAGE: ${{ github.event.pages[0].title }}
              run: echo "page=$PAGE" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - wiki.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on gollum, a step takes the newlines out of the wiki page's
      #   title (tr -d '\n') and then writes it to $GITHUB_ENV as page=.
      # reason: in the written line, a newline of the wiki page's title is what
      #   would start another variable, such as LD_PRELOAD; with every newline
      #   taken out, all of it stays the value of the one line page=.
      # attack-value: github.event.pages[0].title = "x\nPWNED=1"
      # attack-run-behavior: printf '%s' "${PAGE}" | tr -d '\n' prints xPWNED=1,
      #   so echo appends the one line page=xPWNED=1 to $GITHUB_ENV; the runner
      #   sets page to xPWNED=1, and no variable PWNED.
      on: gollum
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                PAGE: ${{ github.event.pages[0].title }}
              run: echo "page=$(printf '%s' "${PAGE}" | tr -d '\n')" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      ```

### fix kinds

- env-var-review: move the expressions into the env of the step and read them as "\${NAME}" where they were unquoted (bash and sh), as \$env:NAME (pwsh) or as process.env.NAME (github-script); take the line breaks out of what is written to \$GITHUB_ENV or \$GITHUB_OUTPUT, or make the delimiter of name&lt;&lt;DELIM random
  - safety: review
  - possible side effects:
    - unquoted-one-word: An unquoted place becomes one word: a value with blanks is no longer read as several words, and outside &#91;&#91; ]] is no longer globbed.
    - pattern-literal: On the right of ==, =, != or =\~ inside &#91;&#91; ]], the value is compared as a string, not matched as a pattern or a regular expression.
    - pwsh-unchecked: The rule does not read the quoting of pwsh, so how \$env:NAME is read at that place is not checked.
    - github-script-unchecked: The rule does not read the JavaScript of github-script, so how process.env.NAME is read at that place is not checked.
    - line-breaks-removed: The line breaks of a value written to \$GITHUB_ENV or \$GITHUB_OUTPUT are taken out, which changes a value that had them.
    - random-delimiter: The random delimiter is made with od and /dev/urandom; in a container without them the step fails.
    - value-not-read-as-script: The value of the \${{ }} expression is no longer parsed by the program that reads the script (the shell, or the JavaScript runtime of actions/github-script) as part of the script text: characters of the value that the program interpreted before the fix (such as \$, \`, \\, double quotes and line breaks) are taken as plain characters, and a workflow that relied on the program interpreting those characters runs differently.

### undetected forms

- pull-request: a job that runs only on pull_request, in one of two cases. In the first case, only the pull requests of the repository run the workflow: the author of a pull request can change the workflow itself, so the run of the job gives the author what the run has (read-only from a fork, or what a private repository sends to the runs of pull requests from forks: secrets, a token that writes) without the flaw of the rule, and the flaw of the rule adds nothing to what the author gets. In the second case, a ruleset of the organization or the enterprise runs the workflow on the pull requests of its other repositories (Require workflows to pass before merging, of GitHub Enterprise): the author of such a pull request cannot change the workflow, and whether the run has more than the pull_request workflow of the author would get (the token, secrets) is known from GitHub's documentation only, as no such run was observed; making a required check pass is outside the threat model of the rule. The workflow does not say which case holds, and the rule does not read which case holds
  - finding kinds: envvar-injection.controlled, envvar-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: pull-request.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request, a run writes the pull request's body to
    #   $GITHUB_ENV.
    # reason: when only the pull requests of the repository run the workflow, the
    #   author of the pull request can change the workflow itself and gets what the
    #   run has without the flaw, so the flaw adds nothing to what the author gets;
    #   when a ruleset of the organization or the enterprise runs the workflow on
    #   the pull requests of its other repositories, the author cannot change the
    #   workflow, and what the run of the ruleset has beyond the author's own
    #   pull_request workflow is not known. The workflow does not say which case
    #   holds.
    # cause: pull_request is none of the attacker's events the rule reads. The
    #   rule does not read whether a ruleset runs the workflow.
    # attack-value: github.event.pull_request.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
    # attack-run-behavior: the script becomes echo "t=x<line break>PWNED=1" >>
    #   "$GITHUB_ENV", which appends t=x and PWNED=1; the runner sets t to x and
    #   PWNED to 1. When a ruleset of the organization runs the workflow on a pull
    #   request of another repository, the same steps run in the run of the ruleset;
    #   what the run of the ruleset has was not observed, so whether the steps do
    #   harm in the run of the ruleset is not known.
    on: pull_request
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "t=${{ github.event.pull_request.body }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
    ```
- dispatch: a value of the event of workflow_dispatch other than its inputs, in a job that runs only on workflow_dispatch: the event has the ref, which is a branch or a tag that the repository already has, and values that GitHub fills, such as the login of the account that dispatches the workflow; the event has no text of an issue, a comment or a pull request. Whoever dispatches the workflow chooses the ref and the inputs of the dispatch, and nothing else of the event. A token that cannot change the files of the repository can dispatch the workflow, such as a fine-grained token that has the permission Actions with write access and no permission Contents. The rule reports an input of the dispatch with the inconclusive kind input-dispatch
  - finding kinds: envvar-injection.controlled, envvar-injection.wiki
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: dispatch.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on workflow_dispatch, a run writes github.event.issue.body to
    #   $GITHUB_ENV. If the workflow also ran on issues, the rule would report
    #   the same step.
    # reason: no added gain: on workflow_dispatch the event has no issue object,
    #   so the expression of the body gives an empty string; whoever dispatches
    #   the workflow chooses the ref and the inputs of the dispatch, and the step
    #   reads no input of the dispatch.
    # cause: the table of the attacker's events that the rule reads does not
    #   have workflow_dispatch; the rule reports an input of a dispatch with the
    #   inconclusive kind input-dispatch.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
    # attack-run-behavior: with the value put in, the script becomes echo
    #   "t=x<line break>PWNED=1" >> "$GITHUB_ENV", which appends t=x and
    #   PWNED=1; the runner sets t to x and PWNED to 1. On workflow_dispatch the
    #   event has no issue object, though: the expression gives an empty string,
    #   and the script appends the line t= only.
    on: workflow_dispatch
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "t=${{ github.event.issue.body }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
    ```
- repository-dispatch: a value of the client_payload of repository_dispatch (github.event.client_payload): only a credential with write access to the permission Contents of the repository can send repository_dispatch, and the credential premise assumes that no attacker holds such a credential; the sender chooses the whole client_payload
  - finding kinds: envvar-injection.controlled, envvar-injection.wiki
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: repository-dispatch.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on repository_dispatch, a run writes the value body of the
    #   client_payload to $GITHUB_ENV.
    # reason: the form adds nothing to what the attacker gets (the disposition
    #   no-added-gain): only a credential with write access to the permission
    #   Contents of the repository can send repository_dispatch, and the
    #   credential premise assumes that no attacker holds such a credential; the
    #   sender chooses the whole client_payload.
    # cause: the table of the attacker's events that the rule reads leaves out
    #   repository_dispatch on purpose: the credential premise leaves the sender
    #   of repository_dispatch out of the threat model.
    # attack-value: github.event.client_payload.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
    # attack-run-behavior: when a repository_dispatch with the value in its
    #   client_payload runs the workflow, the script appends the lines t=x and
    #   PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_ENV, and the runner sets t to x and PWNED to 1.
    on: repository_dispatch
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "t=${{ github.event.client_payload.body }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
    ```
- app-written: a value that an app outside GitHub Actions writes into a field of a commit status or a check run (the fields context, description and target_url of status; the fields name, output, details_url and external_id of check_run): the app may copy a value of a pull request from a fork into the field, such as the name of a job that a configuration file of the pull request gives to an outside CI; the rule reads the field as a field whose value the app chooses
  - finding kinds: envvar-injection.controlled, envvar-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: app-written.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on check_run, which an app outside GitHub Actions starts when
    #   the app makes a check run for a commit, the job writes the name of the
    #   check run (github.event.check_run.name) where the rule reads it.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the app writes the name of the check run, and an
    #   app may copy a value of a pull request from a fork into the name, such
    #   as the name of a job that a configuration file of the pull request gives
    #   to an outside CI.
    # cause: the table of what an attacker controls reads the values that the
    #   app writes into a commit status or a check run as the values that the
    #   app chooses.
    # attack-value: github.event.check_run.name = "a\nBASH_ENV=/tmp/x.sh"
    # attack-run-behavior: an outside CI copies the name of a job from the
    #   configuration file of the pull request from a fork into the name of the
    #   check run; the run of check_run starts on the default branch, and the
    #   value does there what the attack value of the message of the commit does
    #   on status.
    on: check_run
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "t=${{ github.event.check_run.name }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
    ```
- deployment-status: a value of the payload of deployment_status, such as the SHA of the deployment (deployment.sha), when an app outside GitHub Actions makes a deployment and a status of the deployment for a commit of a pull request from a fork: no run of deployment_status started when the authors of the linter tried this, and why the run did not start was not found; the rule does not read deployment_status as an event that an attacker starts
  - finding kinds: envvar-injection.controlled, envvar-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: deployment-status.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on deployment_status, which an app outside GitHub Actions
    #   starts when the app makes a status of a deployment, the job writes the
    #   description of the deployment (github.event.deployment.description)
    #   where the rule reads it.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): no run of deployment_status started when a GitHub
    #   App made a deployment and a status of the deployment for a commit of a
    #   pull request from a fork (seen on GitHub), and why the run did not start
    #   was not found.
    # cause: the table of the attacker's events that the rule reads does not
    #   have deployment_status.
    # attack-value: github.event.deployment.description = "a\nBASH_ENV=/tmp/x.sh"
    # attack-run-behavior: an outside app makes a deployment for the commit of
    #   the pull request from a fork with a description that the pull request
    #   gives, and a status of the deployment; if a run of deployment_status
    #   starts on the default branch, the value does there what the attack value
    #   of the message of the commit does on status.
    on: deployment_status
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "t=${{ github.event.deployment.description }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
    ```
- dispatch-relay: a workflow on an event of an attacker that puts a value the attacker writes into the client_payload of a repository_dispatch that the workflow sends (gh api with client_payload to the endpoint dispatches, peter-evans/repository-dispatch), and a workflow on repository_dispatch that uses the value: the flaw is in the workflow that sends the repository_dispatch, and the rule does not read what a workflow sends to another workflow
  - finding kinds: envvar-injection.controlled, envvar-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - example: .github/workflows/receiver.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: sender.yml runs on issues opened, and with the GITHUB_TOKEN
    #   sends a repository_dispatch of the type relay whose client_payload has the
    #   body of the issue as the value body; receiver.yml runs on that
    #   repository_dispatch, and a run writes the value body of the client_payload
    #   to $GITHUB_ENV.
    # reason: the author of the issue writes the value, and sender.yml relays
    #   the value to receiver.yml in a repository_dispatch that a run of the
    #   repository sends with a token of the repository; GitHub creates a workflow
    #   run for a repository_dispatch sent with the GITHUB_TOKEN, as an exception
    #   to the rule that an event that the GITHUB_TOKEN triggers creates no
    #   workflow run.
    # cause: the rule reads the events of each workflow alone, and does not read
    #   what a workflow sends to another workflow as the client_payload of a
    #   repository_dispatch.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens an issue whose body is the value;
    #   sender.yml sends the value, and in the run of receiver.yml the script
    #   appends the lines t=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_ENV, and the runner sets t to
    #   x and PWNED to 1.
    on:
      repository_dispatch:
        types: [relay]
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "t=${{ github.event.client_payload.body }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
    ```
    - .github/workflows/sender.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on:
        issues:
          types: [opened]
      permissions:
        contents: write
      jobs:
        relay:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
                VALUE: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
              run: gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/dispatches" -f event_type=relay -f "client_payload[body]=$VALUE"
      ```
- dispatch-input-call: an input of workflow_dispatch that a caller of the same repository passes, as an input of the call (under the key with: of the calling job or step), to a reusable workflow or a composite action, which uses the input as a value: the one who dispatches the caller chooses the value, and the rule reads the events of a called workflow or action from the table of the callers, and does not follow the value of an input of workflow_dispatch that the caller gives
  - finding kinds: envvar-injection.controlled, envvar-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - example: .github/workflows/called.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: caller.yml runs on workflow_dispatch with the input x, and
    #   calls called.yml with the input x of the dispatch as the input x of
    #   called.yml; called.yml writes the input x to $GITHUB_ENV.
    # reason: the one who dispatches caller.yml chooses the value:
    #   input-dispatch reports such a value where a workflow on workflow_dispatch
    #   refers to its input directly, but through the call the value is the input
    #   x of called.yml.
    # cause: the rule reads the events of a called workflow from the table of
    #   the callers, and does not follow the value of an input of
    #   workflow_dispatch that a caller gives in with.
    # attack-value: inputs.x = "x\nPWNED=1"
    # attack-run-behavior: when the one who dispatches caller.yml gives the
    #   value as x, the script appends the lines t=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_ENV,
    #   and the runner sets t to x and PWNED to 1.
    on:
      workflow_call:
        inputs:
          x: {type: string}
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "t=${{ inputs.x }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
    ```
    - .github/workflows/caller.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on:
        workflow_dispatch:
          inputs:
            x: {type: string}
      jobs:
        call:
          uses: ./.github/workflows/called.yml
          with:
            x: ${{ inputs.x }}
          secrets: inherit
      ```
- not-attacker: secrets, vars, runner, the outcome of a step, the result of a job. A run of the linter that adds the attacker variables-writer reports a reference of vars where the rule reads the value as written by the attacker, and a run of the linter that adds the attacker secrets-writer reports such a reference of secrets except secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN (--add-attacker); no run reports runner, the outcome of a step or the result of a job
  - finding kinds: envvar-injection.controlled, envvar-injection.wiki
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - added attackers: variables-writer, secrets-writer
  - example: not-attacker.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, a run writes secrets, variables and the runner to
    #   $GITHUB_ENV.
    # reason: no added gain: no attacker writes them.
    # cause: the rule reads as what an attacker may write only references to
    #   github (through its table of contexts), env, the outputs of steps and of
    #   jobs needed, inputs and matrix; secrets, vars and runner are none of
    #   these, so it reads them as values no attacker writes.
    # attack-value: secrets.TOKEN = "x\nPWNED=1"
    # attack-run-behavior: were the secret this value, the script would append
    #   t=x and PWNED=1 <vars.NAME> <runner.os> to $GITHUB_ENV, and the runner
    #   would set PWNED to 1 <vars.NAME> <runner.os>.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "t=${{ secrets.TOKEN }} ${{ vars.NAME }} ${{ runner.os }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
    ```
- merged-pusher: a value that the author of a pull request writes in the profile of the account of the author (the profile name, the public email of the profile), in github.event.pull_request.merged_by of a merged pull request, or in github.event.pusher of the push that GitHub makes when GitHub merges a pull request by a rebase, by auto-merge or from a merge queue: the rule reads merged_by and the pusher as the account that merged or pushed, and the account that merged or pushed holds a credential that can merge or push; whether GitHub sets merged_by of a merged pull request, or the pusher of the push that GitHub makes when GitHub merges a pull request by a rebase, by auto-merge or from a merge queue, to the account of the author of the merged pull request was not checked
  - finding kinds: envvar-injection.controlled, envvar-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: merged-pusher.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on a pull request that is closed, a step writes the name of the
    #   account that merged the pull request to $GITHUB_ENV.
    # reason: whether GitHub sets merged_by of a merged pull request to the
    #   account of the author of the pull request was not checked: no payload with
    #   merged_by was seen on GitHub. Were merged_by the author, the author would
    #   write the name of merged_by, which is the profile name of the account of
    #   the author.
    # cause: the table of what an attacker controls reads merged_by as the
    #   account that merged the pull request, and the account that merged the pull
    #   request holds a credential that can merge.
    # attack-value: github.event.pull_request.merged_by.name = "x\nPWNED=1"
    # attack-run-behavior: were merged_by the author of the pull request and the
    #   profile name of the account of the author this value, echo would append
    #   the two lines merger=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_ENV, and the runner would
    #   set PWNED to 1 for the steps after the step.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [closed]
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              MERGER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.merged_by.name }}
            run: echo "merger=$MERGER" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
    ```
- compared: a context compared, negated, or given to contains, startsWith, endsWith or hashFiles: what is written out is a bool or a hash
  - finding kinds: envvar-injection.controlled, envvar-injection.wiki
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: compared.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, a run writes to $GITHUB_ENV the issue's body given
    #   to contains and compared with ==.
    # reason: no added gain: what is written out is a bool.
    # cause: the rule reads the value of a comparison or of contains as a bool,
    #   not the attacker's text.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
    # attack-run-behavior: contains and == make false of the body, so the script
    #   becomes echo "t=false false" >> "$GITHUB_ENV", and the runner sets t to
    #   false false, and no variable PWNED, with any body.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "t=${{ contains(github.event.issue.body, 'x') }} ${{ github.event.issue.body == 'x' }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
    ```
- new-activity-type: an activity type GitHub added after the schemas the tables are made from, written in types: a value of types the tables do not have is dropped, as GitHub drops one it has no such activity type for
  - finding kinds: envvar-injection.controlled, envvar-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: pin-update)
  - example: new-activity-type.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues of an activity type added_later, a run writes the
    #   issue's title to $GITHUB_ENV.
    # reason: a todo (a pin update): an activity type GitHub added after the
    #   pinned schemas is missed until the pins are updated.
    # cause: the analysis drops a value of types it does not know, as GitHub
    #   does for a value it has no such activity type for, so the job has no
    #   attacker's event.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "x\nPWNED=1"
    # attack-run-behavior: on an issue of the type added_later, the script
    #   becomes echo "TITLE=x<line break>PWNED=1" >> "$GITHUB_ENV", which
    #   appends TITLE=x and PWNED=1; the runner sets TITLE to x and PWNED to 1.
    on:
      issues:
        types: [added_later]
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "TITLE=${{ github.event.issue.title }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
    ```
- outside-caller: a reusable workflow or composite action that callers in the repository decide, called from another repository on an event, or with a value, an attacker controls: the caller's run has the caller's token and secrets, not the repository's
  - finding kinds: envvar-injection.controlled, envvar-injection.wiki
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: .github/workflows/called.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the workflow is called; a run writes github.event.issue.body to
    #   $GITHUB_ENV. Its one caller in the repository, ci.yml, runs on push.
    # reason: no added gain for this repository: ci.yml calls the workflow on
    #   push alone, and github.event of a push has no issue, so the value that the
    #   run reads is not a value that an attacker wrote. Another repository may
    #   call the workflow on an event whose payload has what an attacker wrote,
    #   but that run has the token and the secrets of the other repository.
    # cause: the rule reads a called workflow on the events of its callers in
    #   the repository, and ci.yml runs on push alone.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
    # attack-run-behavior: called by ci.yml on push, the event has no issue, so
    #   BODY is empty and echo appends the one line body=. Called by a workflow
    #   of another repository on issues with this body, echo appends body=x and
    #   PWNED=1, and the runner sets PWNED to 1 in that run.
    on:
      workflow_call:
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              BODY: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
            run: echo "body=$BODY" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
    ```
    - .github/workflows/ci.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: push
      jobs:
        call:
          uses: ./.github/workflows/called.yml
      ```
- no-line-break: a context that cannot hold a line break, written after the = of a line or in the body of name&lt;&lt;DELIM: a SHA, a number, a date, the name of an account, a repository or a branch, the description of a fork (github.event.forkee.description), a URL (before the =, any value an attacker controls is reported)
  - finding kinds: envvar-injection.controlled, envvar-injection.wiki
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: no-line-break.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, workflow_run, merge_group, fork, and
    #   issues and discussion transferred, runs write branches' names, a number
    #   and a SHA after the = of lines of $GITHUB_ENV. issues and discussion run only
    #   when transferred: changes.new_repository is in the payload of that
    #   action alone.
    # reason: no added gain: a branch's name cannot hold a line break: "They
    #   cannot have ASCII control characters (i.e. bytes whose values are lower
    #   than \040, or \177 DEL)" (git-check-ref-format, git v2.51.0). The second
    #   step is the form of GHSL-2025-105 (vets-api,
    #   https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2025-105_vets-api/),
    #   which the advisory reports as code injection: code-injection reports it.
    # cause: the rule's table of contexts reads the branches' names as
    #   structured (an attacker shapes them within a form without line breaks)
    #   and the number and the SHA as fixed. A fixed value is not taken as an
    #   attacker's, and a structured one not as written with line breaks; after
    #   the =, the rule reports only a value written with line breaks.
    # attack-value: github.event.workflow_run.head_branch = "x\nPWNED=1"
    # attack-run-behavior: were a branch so named, the second step's script
    #   would become echo "pr_branch=x<line break>PWNED=1" >> $GITHUB_ENV, which
    #   appends pr_branch=x and PWNED=1, and the runner would set PWNED to 1.
    #   git and GitHub refuse a branch whose name has a line break, so
    #   head_branch never holds this value.
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2025-105_vets-api/
    on:
      pull_request_target:
      workflow_run:
      merge_group:
      fork:
      issues:
        types: [transferred]
      discussion:
        types: [transferred]
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "h=${{ github.head_ref }} n=${{ github.event.pull_request.number }} s=${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          - run: echo "pr_branch=${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}" >> $GITHUB_ENV
          - run: |
              echo "a=${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
              echo "b=${{ github.event.pull_request.head.label }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
              echo "c=${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
              echo "d=${{ github.event.pull_request.base.label }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
              echo "e=${{ github.event.workflow_run.pull_requests[0].head.ref }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
              echo "f=${{ github.event.workflow_run.pull_requests[0].base.ref }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
              echo "g=${{ github.event.workflow_run.referenced_workflows[0].ref }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
              echo "h=${{ github.event.pull_request.head.repo.default_branch }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
              echo "i=${{ github.event.pull_request.base.repo.default_branch }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
              echo "j=${{ github.event.forkee.default_branch }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
              echo "k=${{ github.event.changes.new_repository.default_branch }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
              echo "m=${{ github.event.merge_group.head_ref }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
              echo "n=${{ github.event.merge_group.base_ref }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
    ```
- line-free: a value written through \$( ) whose pipeline starts with echo or printf '%s' of it and ends with tr -d with \\n in the set, or tr turning \\n into another byte
  - finding kinds: envvar-injection.controlled, envvar-injection.wiki
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: line-free.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, a run writes the issue's body to $GITHUB_ENV through
    #   $( ) whose pipeline ends with tr -d '\n'.
    # reason: no added gain: the line breaks are taken out, so the value is one
    #   line.
    # cause: the rule reads such a pipeline as taking the line breaks out.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
    # attack-run-behavior: echo "$B" | tr -d '\n' prints xPWNED=1, so echo
    #   appends the one line b=xPWNED=1 to $GITHUB_ENV; the runner sets b to
    #   xPWNED=1, and no variable PWNED, with any body.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              B: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
            run: echo "b=$(echo "$B" | tr -d '\n')" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
    ```
- random-delimiter: the body of name&lt;&lt;DELIM whose delimiter is \$GHA_DELIM, set before it to ghadelimiter\_ and 16 random bytes in hex as the fix writes it
  - finding kinds: envvar-injection.controlled, envvar-injection.wiki
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: random-delimiter.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, a run writes the issue's body to $GITHUB_ENV in
    #   b<<DELIM, whose delimiter is ghadelimiter_ and 16 random bytes in hex.
    # reason: no added gain: the attacker cannot write the delimiter.
    # cause: the rule reads the delimiter of its own fix's form as random.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nghadelimiter_00000000000000000000000000000000\nPWNED=1"
    # attack-run-behavior: the body guesses the delimiter as ghadelimiter_ and
    #   32 zeros; GHA_DELIM is ghadelimiter_ and 32 hex digits from
    #   /dev/urandom, so the guess is not the delimiter (but by a chance of 1 in
    #   2^128), and the runner reads the body's three lines as the value of b,
    #   up to the line GHA_DELIM, and sets no variable PWNED.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              B: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
            run: |
              GHA_DELIM="ghadelimiter_$(od -An -N16 -tx1 /dev/urandom | tr -d ' \n')"; { echo "b<<${GHA_DELIM}"; echo "$B"; echo "${GHA_DELIM}"; } >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
    ```
- script-var: a shell variable no env of the workflow sets: one the script sets (from a file, an artifact, an API), a positional parameter of a function the script calls with the value, or the runner
  - finding kinds: envvar-injection.controlled, envvar-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: script-var.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on workflow_run, a run writes to $GITHUB_ENV a value from a
    #   file of an artifact through a variable the script sets, the form of
    #   Feign's comment-pr.yml (GHSL-2024-173,
    #   https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-173_Feign/); another
    #   writes a commit message through a positional parameter of a function and
    #   an indirection the script sets.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): following the variables of the script
    #   would find it.
    # cause: the value goes through a variable the script sets, which the rule
    #   does not follow.
    # attack-value: the file pr_number.txt of the artifact pr_number = "111\nLD_PRELOAD=/home/runner/work/feign/feign/inject.so\nPWNED=1"
    # attack-run-behavior: the value is that of GHSL-2024-173's PoC, with the
    #   line PWNED=1 added. PR_NUMBER=$(cat pr_number.txt) holds its three
    #   lines, and echo appends PR_NUMBER=111,
    #   LD_PRELOAD=/home/runner/work/feign/feign/inject.so and PWNED=1 to
    #   $GITHUB_ENV; the runner sets the three, and a program a later step
    #   starts, such as node, loads inject.so from the artifact.
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-173_Feign/
    on:
      workflow_run:
        workflows: ["receive-pr"]
        types: [completed]
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
            with:
              name: pr_number
              run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
          - run: |
              PR_NUMBER=$(cat pr_number.txt)
              echo "PR_NUMBER=$PR_NUMBER" >> $GITHUB_ENV
          # a positional parameter of a function the script calls with the value
          - env:
              T: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_commit.message }}
            run: |
              f() { echo "a=$1" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"; }
              f "$T"
              # the indirection names T through X, which the script sets
              X=T
              echo "a=${!X}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
    ```
- nested-shell: what another shell or program the script starts writes to the environment file, from its code (eval, bash -c, sh -c) or from the environment it reads itself (python -c and the like)
  - finding kinds: envvar-injection.controlled, envvar-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: nested-shell.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, a run writes the issue's title to $GITHUB_ENV
    #   through eval, bash -c and python -c.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): reading what another shell or program
    #   writes to the environment file would find it.
    # cause: the tree does not read the code of eval or bash -c, and python
    #   reads the value from its environment itself.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "x\nPWNED=1"
    # attack-run-behavior: eval runs echo "a=$T", bash -c runs it with T from
    #   its environment, and python prints a= and T, each appending a=x and
    #   PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_ENV; the runner sets a to x and PWNED to 1 (three
    #   times).
    on: issues
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              T: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
            run: |
              eval 'echo "a=$T" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"'
              bash -c 'echo "a=$T" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"'
              python3 -c 'import os; print("a=" + os.environ["T"])' >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
    ```
- lastpipe-not-literal: an assignment or an exec in the last command of a pipeline after a shopt -s lastpipe whose option name the script does not write as a literal word (shopt -s "\$o"): bash runs the last command of the pipeline in the shell that runs the pipeline, so the assignment or the exec stays after the pipeline, and the rule reads the last command as a command in a subshell
  - finding kinds: envvar-injection.controlled, envvar-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: lastpipe-not-literal.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues opened, a step turns lastpipe on with shopt -s and
    #   the option name in a variable, sets out to $GITHUB_ENV in the last command
    #   of a pipeline, and writes V=$V to "$out".
    # reason: a todo (the same file): with lastpipe, bash runs the last command
    #   of the pipeline in the shell itself, so out stays $GITHUB_ENV after the
    #   pipeline and the value goes to $GITHUB_ENV.
    # cause: the rule follows lastpipe only after shopt -s lastpipe written as
    #   literal words, and reads the last command as a command in a subshell.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
    # attack-run-behavior: the value goes to $GITHUB_ENV.
    on:
      issues:
        types: [opened]
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              V: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
            run: |
              o=lastpipe
              shopt -s "$o"
              true | out=$GITHUB_ENV
              echo "V=$V" >> "$out"
    ```
- name-not-literal: an assignment whose variable name the script does not write as a literal word (n=key; declare "\$n=\$X"; or read -r "\$n"): bash assigns the word after = (with declare) or the line that read reads (with read) to the variable whose name is the value of n, and the rule does not read the assignment
  - finding kinds: envvar-injection.controlled, envvar-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: name-not-literal.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues opened, a step sets n to the name out, assigns
    #   $GITHUB_ENV to the variable that n names with declare, and writes
    #   V=$V to "$out".
    # reason: a todo (the same file): bash assigns $GITHUB_ENV to out, so
    #   the value goes to $GITHUB_ENV.
    # cause: the variable name of the assignment is not a literal word, so the
    #   rule does not read the assignment.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
    # attack-run-behavior: the value goes to $GITHUB_ENV.
    on:
      issues:
        types: [opened]
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              V: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
            run: |
              n=out
              declare "$n=$GITHUB_ENV"
              echo "V=$V" >> "$out"
    ```
- recursive-unset-local: a variable that a shell function unsets inside a recursive call of a function, where a function between the two calls made the variable local (f() { if &#91; -z "\$inner" ]; then inner=1; h; else g; fi; }; h() { s=x; local s=y; f; }; g() { unset s; }): bash takes away the local of the nearest calling function that made the variable local, and the variable then holds the value from before the nearest calling function made the variable local; the rule reads the recursive call where the first call of the function runs, without the calls in between, and does not read the value that the unset reveals
  - finding kinds: envvar-injection.controlled, envvar-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: recursive-unset-local.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues opened, a step defines f, which calls h on the first
    #   call of f and calls g on the second call of f; h sets out to $GITHUB_ENV,
    #   makes out local with /dev/null, and calls f. g unsets out and writes V=
    #   and "$V" to the file in "$out".
    # reason: a todo (the same file): in the second call of f, the unset in g
    #   takes away the local that h made, and out holds the value that h set
    #   before h made out local: $GITHUB_ENV, which gets the issue's body.
    # cause: the rule reads the second call of f, which f makes through h, where
    #   the first call of f runs, without the call of h, so the rule does not read
    #   the value that the unset reveals.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
    # attack-run-behavior: the runner sets PWNED for the steps after the step.
    on:
      issues:
        types: [opened]
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              V: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
            run: |
              f() { if [ -z "$inner" ]; then inner=1; h; else g; fi; }
              g() { unset out; echo "V=$V" >> "$out"; }
              h() { out="$GITHUB_ENV"; local out=/dev/null; f; }
              f
    ```
- unset-caller-local: a variable that a shell function unsets after a calling function made the variable local, when an assignment to the variable or a second unset of the variable follows the unset (s=x; reset() { unset s; }; point() { local s=y; reset; s=z; }; point): bash takes away the local of the calling function, so that the assignment after the unset sets the variable outside the calling function, and a second unset takes away the local of the next calling function or unsets the variable outside the functions; the rule keeps the local of the calling function after the unset, gives the variable back the value from before the calling function made the variable local when the calling function returns, and reads the second unset as the first unset
  - finding kinds: envvar-injection.controlled, envvar-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: unset-caller-local.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues opened, a step sets out to /dev/null and defines reset,
    #   which unsets out; point makes out local with /dev/null, calls reset, and
    #   sets out to $GITHUB_ENV. The step calls point and then writes V= and "$V"
    #   to the file in "$out".
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the unset in reset takes away the local that
    #   point made, so the assignment in point after reset sets the out of the
    #   step: $GITHUB_ENV, which gets the issue's body.
    # cause: the rule keeps the local of point after the unset in reset, and gives
    #   out back /dev/null when point returns, so the rule does not read the value
    #   that point set after reset.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
    # attack-run-behavior: the runner sets PWNED for the steps after the step.
    on:
      issues:
        types: [opened]
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              V: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
            run: |
              out=/dev/null
              reset() { unset out; }
              point() { local out=/dev/null; reset; out="$GITHUB_ENV"; }
              point
              echo "V=$V" >> "$out"
    ```
- wrapped-tee: tee run through another command or by its path (sudo tee, command tee, /usr/bin/tee): the rule reads tee by its name alone
  - finding kinds: envvar-injection.controlled, envvar-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: wrapped-tee.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, a run writes the issue's title to $GITHUB_ENV by
    #   sudo tee, command tee and /usr/bin/tee.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): reading tee through another command or by
    #   its path would find it.
    # cause: the rule reads tee by its name alone.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "x\nPWNED=1"
    # attack-run-behavior: each echo prints a=x and PWNED=1, and sudo tee,
    #   command tee and /usr/bin/tee each append them to $GITHUB_ENV; the runner
    #   sets a to x and PWNED to 1.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              T: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
            run: |
              echo "a=$T" | sudo tee -a "$GITHUB_ENV"
              echo "a=$T" | command tee -a "$GITHUB_ENV"
              echo "a=$T" | /usr/bin/tee -a "$GITHUB_ENV"
    ```
- if-compared: a value that an if compares with strings that the workflow writes in the if (strings compared by == with the value and joined by ||, or the strings of contains(fromJSON('&#91;...]'), value)), where each string has only ASCII letters, digits, spaces, -, \_, . and /, does not start with -, and has no - right after a space. The if of the job limits the value in every step of the job, and the if of a step with a run: script limits the value in that step only. In those steps the value equals one of the strings when the case of the letters is ignored, so the rule does not report the value. The attacker still chooses the case of each letter of the value. GitHub's server, which evaluates the if of a job, also takes the Kelvin sign as equal to the letter k and the long s as equal to the letter s; the runner, which evaluates the if of a step, takes the Kelvin sign as equal to the letter k. Where the case of a letter changes what the value names, such as a command, a variable, a file on a file system that tells names apart by their case (the default file system of a Linux runner), a host or a tool, the choice of the case can cause harm
  - finding kinds: envvar-injection.controlled, envvar-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: if-compared.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issue_comment, a job runs only when the comment's body is
    #   bash_env, and a step writes ${{ github.event.comment.body }} as the name
    #   of the variable, the part of a line of $GITHUB_ENV before the =.
    # reason: the job's if lets the body be only the string bash_env, ignoring
    #   the case of its letters, so the body has no line break; the attacker
    #   still chooses the case, and BASH_ENV is the variable whose file bash
    #   reads before each later script.
    # cause: the rule does not treat a value that the if of the job compares
    #   with such a string as written by the attacker.
    # attack-value: github.event.comment.body = "BASH_ENV"
    # attack-run-behavior: the if passes, and the step writes the line
    #   BASH_ENV=./setup.sh to $GITHUB_ENV.
    on:
      issue_comment:
        types: [created]
    jobs:
      j:
        if: github.event.comment.body == 'bash_env'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "${{ github.event.comment.body }}=./setup.sh" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
    ```
- other-shell: a run of pwsh, cmd or python, and a run whose shell the rule cannot determine to be bash or sh: a shell: value whose command is not bash or sh, such as pwsh -File {0}; a shell: value of bash or sh with an option that the rule does not read, such as bash -c 'make' {0}, bash -v {0} or bash -O extglob {0}; a shell: value that names bash or sh by a path, such as /usr/bin/bash -e {0}, on a runner where the rule does not know that the path exists (any runner other than one whose runs-on is a single label that starts with ubuntu-, or with macos- for /bin/bash and /bin/sh) or in a step of a composite action; a shell: that is an expression; or a step without shell: whose job and workflow have no defaults.run.shell and whose job has a runs-on that is not a single label that starts with ubuntu-, macos- or windows-, such as self-hosted or an expression: the rule reads the runs of bash and sh only
  - finding kinds: envvar-injection.controlled, envvar-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: other-shell.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, a run of pwsh writes the issue's body to
    #   $GITHUB_ENV.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): reading pwsh would find it.
    # cause: the rule reads runs of bash and sh only.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
    # attack-run-behavior: pwsh's echo writes b=x, a line break and PWNED=1 to
    #   $GITHUB_ENV, appending the lines b=x and PWNED=1; the runner sets b to x
    #   and PWNED to 1.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - shell: pwsh
            env:
              B: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
            run: echo "b=$env:B" >> $env:GITHUB_ENV
    ```
  - example: other-shell.pwsh-expression.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, a run of pwsh writes the issue's body to
    #   $GITHUB_ENV with a ${{ }} in the script.
    # reason: reading pwsh would find the write to $GITHUB_ENV. code-injection
    #   reports the ${{ }}, and the fix of the step reads $env:ISSUE_BODY in
    #   place of the ${{ }}. The fix of the step does not take the line breaks
    #   out of the issue's body, because no rule reports the write to
    #   $GITHUB_ENV in a run of pwsh, so the run after the fix still writes the
    #   line breaks of the issue's body to $GITHUB_ENV.
    # cause: the rule reads runs of bash and sh only.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
    # attack-run-behavior: pwsh's echo writes b=x, a line break and PWNED=1 to
    #   $GITHUB_ENV, appending the lines b=x and PWNED=1; the runner sets b to x
    #   and PWNED to 1.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - shell: pwsh
            run: echo "b=${{ github.event.issue.body }}" >> $env:GITHUB_ENV
    ```
- github-script: core.exportVariable and core.setOutput of actions/github-script: @actions/core writes a random delimiter, and refuses a value that has it
  - finding kinds: envvar-injection.controlled, envvar-injection.wiki
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: github-script.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, actions/github-script calls core.exportVariable with
    #   the issue's body.
    # reason: no added gain: @actions/core writes a random delimiter, and
    #   refuses a value that has it.
    # cause: the rule does not read JavaScript.
    # attack-value: the issue's body, which the script reads as context.payload.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
    # attack-run-behavior: core.exportVariable appends B<<ghadelimiter_<a random
    #   UUID>, x, PWNED=1 and the delimiter to $GITHUB_ENV, and the runner sets
    #   B to x, a line break and PWNED=1, and no variable PWNED; a body with the
    #   delimiter's line in it makes exportVariable throw instead.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/github-script@v7
            with:
              script: core.exportVariable('B', context.payload.issue.body)
    ```
- other-file: a value written to the file \$GITHUB_STATE, which the post step of a JavaScript action reads
  - finding kinds: envvar-injection.controlled, envvar-injection.wiki
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: other-file.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, a run writes the issue's body to $GITHUB_STATE.
    # reason: no added gain: $GITHUB_STATE is a file that the
    #   post step of a JavaScript action reads.
    # cause: the rule reads writes to $GITHUB_ENV only.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
    # attack-run-behavior: echo appends b=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_STATE, and
    #   the runner keeps them as the state b and PWNED, which the post steps of
    #   the job's actions get as STATE_b and STATE_PWNED; nothing is written to
    #   $GITHUB_ENV, and no variable PWNED is set.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              B: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
            run: echo "b=$B" >> "$GITHUB_STATE"
    ```
- github-path: a value written to \$GITHUB_PATH
  - finding kinds: envvar-injection.controlled, envvar-injection.wiki
  - disposition: other-rule (rule: envpath-injection)
  - example: github-path.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, a run writes the issue's body to $GITHUB_PATH.
    # reason: another rule's: envpath-injection reports a value written to
    #   $GITHUB_PATH.
    # cause: the rule reads writes to $GITHUB_ENV only.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
    # attack-run-behavior: echo appends the lines x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_PATH,
    #   and the runner puts both before the PATH of the steps after it; nothing
    #   is written to $GITHUB_ENV, and no variable PWNED is set.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              B: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
            run: echo "$B" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
    ```
- case-arm: a write to the environment file, or an exec (the builtin of the shell) that opens the environment file, inside an arm of a case statement of the shell: the rule finds the case statement and does not read the commands in the arms of the case statement
  - finding kinds: envvar-injection.controlled, envvar-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: case-arm.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues opened, a step writes BODY= and the issue's body to
    #   $GITHUB_ENV inside an arm of a case that skips an empty value.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the arm runs, and each later line of the
    #   body such as NAME=value sets an environment variable of the steps after
    #   it.
    # cause: the shell parser does not read the commands of a case.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
    # attack-run-behavior: the value is not empty, so the case takes its
    #   second arm, and echo writes the lines BODY=x and PWNED=1 to
    #   $GITHUB_ENV; the runner sets BODY and PWNED for the steps after it.
    on:
      issues:
        types: [opened]
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              V: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
            run: |
              case "$V" in
                "") ;;
                *) echo "BODY=$V" >> "$GITHUB_ENV" ;;
              esac
    ```
- file-content: the content of a file that a command of the script writes into \$GITHUB_ENV by printing the file, not through a shell variable (cat values.txt >> \$GITHUB_ENV, tee -a \$GITHUB_ENV < values.txt, or the content passed through sed or tr between the file and \$GITHUB_ENV), such as a file of an artifact that was uploaded by a run that an attacker started: the rule reads the text of the script, and does not follow where the file comes from (the step that downloads the file)
  - finding kinds: envvar-injection.controlled, envvar-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: file-content.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on workflow_run, the script of a step copies into $GITHUB_ENV, with
    #   cat, the content of a file of an artifact that was uploaded by the run
    #   that triggered the workflow, by printing the file, not through a shell
    #   variable.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): reading, in the workflow, the command that
    #   copies the file and the step that downloads the file would find it.
    #   artifact-poisoning reports the download of the artifact, and this rule
    #   reports nothing.
    # cause: the rule reads the text of the script, and does not follow where
    #   the file comes from (the step that downloads the file).
    # attack-value: the file values.txt of the artifact values = "A=1\nLD_PRELOAD=/home/runner/work/r/r/inject.so\nPWNED=1"
    # attack-run-behavior: download-artifact puts values.txt in the workspace, and cat appends
    #   the three lines of values.txt to $GITHUB_ENV; the runner sets A,
    #   LD_PRELOAD and PWNED for the steps after the step of cat; the artifact
    #   also holds inject.so, which download-artifact puts in the workspace too,
    #   and a program that a later step starts loads that inject.so.
    on:
      workflow_run:
        workflows: ["receive-pr"]
        types: [completed]
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
            with:
              name: values
              run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
          - run: cat values.txt >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
    ```
  - example: file-content.ghsl-2024-252.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on workflow_run, a step downloads runtime-versions.md, a file of
    #   the artifact of the triggering run, and the script of the next step writes
    #   it to $GITHUB_ENV between the lines RUNTIME_VERSIONS<<EOF and EOF, with
    #   cat. This is write-prerelease-comment.yml of cloudflare/workers-sdk (commit
    #   ce7db9d9cb4f5bcd5a326b86dde051cb54b999fb, lines 1-14 and 39-54); the step
    #   with actions/github-script, the second download and the steps after line
    #   54 are left out. docs-preview-deploy.yml of docker-mailserver/docker-mailserver
    #   (commit c29fe3ff0bc888016720536228878b3f19131056, GHSL-2024-255) has the
    #   form without the heredoc: it extracts the artifact and runs cat pr.env >>
    #   "${GITHUB_ENV}". doc-publish-pr.yml of zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr (commit
    #   9c0f92db475f0e27673ac366276026eddf1a150c, GHSL-2024-253) runs echo
    #   "PR_NUM=$(<pr_num/pr_num)" >> $GITHUB_ENV (line 31), and docs-preview.yml of
    #   litestar-org/litestar (commit ffaf5616b19f6f0f4128209c8b49dbcb41568aa2,
    #   GHSL-2024-177) runs echo "PR_NUMBER=$(cat docs-preview/.pr_number)" >>
    #   $GITHUB_ENV.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): reading, in the workflow, the command that
    #   copies the file and the step that downloads the file would find it.
    #   artifact-poisoning reports the download of the artifact, and this rule
    #   reports nothing.
    # cause: the rule reads the text of the script, and does not follow where
    #   the file comes from (the step that downloads the file).
    # attack-value: the file runtime-versions.md of the artifact runtime-versions.md = "x\nEOF\nLD_PRELOAD=/home/runner/work/r/r/inject.so\nPWNED=1"
    # attack-run-behavior: the author of a pull request from a fork makes the
    #   triggering run upload runtime-versions.md with the value; the line EOF in
    #   the file ends the value of RUNTIME_VERSIONS, and the runner sets
    #   LD_PRELOAD and PWNED for the steps after the step of cat.
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-252_Cloudflare_workers-sdk/
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-255_docker-mailserver/
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-253_Zephyr/
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-177_Litestar/
    on:
      workflow_run:
        workflows: ["Create Pull Request Prerelease"]
        types:
          - completed
    jobs:
      comment:
        if: ${{ github.repository_owner == 'cloudflare' }}
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        name: Write comment to the PR
        steps:
          - name: "Download runtime versions"
            uses: dawidd6/action-download-artifact@v2
            with:
              run_id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
              name: runtime-versions.md
          - name: "Put runtime versions on the environment"
            id: runtime_versions
            run: |
              {
                echo 'RUNTIME_VERSIONS<<EOF'
                cat runtime-versions.md
                echo EOF
              } >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
    ```
- fork-review: a job on pull_request_review or pull_request_review_comment that runs only for a pull request from a fork, such as a job whose if: condition is github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name != github.repository: the run of a review that the attacker writes on the pull request of another person from a fork has the secrets of the repository or a token that writes only where a private repository gives secrets or a token that writes to the runs of pull requests from forks (repo.fork-pr-secrets, repo.fork-pr-write-tokens). The rule does not read the facts repo.fork-pr-secrets and repo.fork-pr-write-tokens for the runs of a review, and does not count the run of a review of a pull request from a fork as a run of the attacker. When the attacker opened the pull request from a fork, a review of that pull request gives the attacker nothing more than the pull request itself gives: the run takes the workflow of the merge commit of the pull request (GitHub's documentation gives refs/pull/&lt;n>/merge as the ref of the run of a review), and the attacker can change that workflow in the pull request
  - finding kinds: envvar-injection.controlled, envvar-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: fork-review.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on comments on the diff, a step writes the comment's body to
    #   $GITHUB_ENV, in a job that runs only for a pull request from a fork.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the job runs only for a pull request from a
    #   fork. Where a private repository gives secrets or a token that writes
    #   to the runs of pull requests from forks, the run of a review that the
    #   attacker writes on the pull request of another person from a fork has
    #   those secrets or that token, and the job runs for the attacker.
    # cause: the rule does not read the settings of a private repository for
    #   the runs of pull requests from forks, and does not count the run of a
    #   review of a pull request from a fork as a run of the attacker.
    # attack-value: github.event.comment.body = "x\nNODE_OPTIONS=--require=/tmp/PWNED.js"
    # attack-run-behavior: the comment of the attacker on the diff of the pull
    #   request of another person from a fork starts the job a; the line after
    #   the line break sets NODE_OPTIONS for the later steps of the job.
    on: pull_request_review_comment
    jobs:
      a:
        if: github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name != github.repository
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              B: ${{ github.event.comment.body }}
            run: echo "body=$B" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
    ```
- call-after-exec: a write by a function that the script defines before an exec that points the standard output to \$GITHUB_ENV, and that the script calls after the exec (f() { echo "V=\$V"; }; exec >>"\$GITHUB_ENV"; f): bash writes what the body of the function prints to \$GITHUB_ENV; the rule reads the commands that run after the exec by the place of each command in the text of the script, and does not read the body of the function, which comes before the exec in the text, as a command that runs after the exec
  - finding kinds: envvar-injection.controlled, envvar-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: call-after-exec.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues opened, a step defines a function f that writes V=
    #   and the issue's body to its standard output, points the standard output
    #   of the script to $GITHUB_ENV with exec, and calls f.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): f runs after the exec, so the body goes
    #   to $GITHUB_ENV.
    # cause: the rule reads the commands that run after the exec by their place
    #   in the text of the script, and the body of f comes before the exec.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
    # attack-run-behavior: the value goes to $GITHUB_ENV.
    on:
      issues:
        types: [opened]
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              V: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
            run: |
              f() { echo "V=$V"; }
              exec >>"$GITHUB_ENV"
              f
    ```
- substitution-pipe-end: a print inside a \$( ) with a redirect that duplicates file descriptor 0 or file descriptor 2, where the script closed that file descriptor before the \$( ) and bash places an end of the pipe of the \$( ) on that file descriptor (exec 2>&-; echo "\$( echo "V=\$V" >>"\$GITHUB_ENV" 3>&2 )"): bash opens the pipe of the \$( ) on the lowest closed file descriptors and does not close an end of the pipe that is file descriptor 0, 1 or 2 inside the \$( ), so the redirect that duplicates the file descriptor does not fail and bash runs the print; the rule reads file descriptor 0 or file descriptor 2 inside the \$( ) as closed, and reads the print as a command that bash does not run because the redirect that duplicates the file descriptor fails
  - finding kinds: envvar-injection.controlled, envvar-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: substitution-pipe-end.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues opened, a step closes the standard error, and inside
    #   a $( ) appends V= and the issue's body to $GITHUB_ENV with a redirect
    #   that duplicates descriptor 2 to descriptor 3.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): bash opens the pipe of the $( ) on the
    #   lowest closed descriptors, so descriptor 2 inside the $( ) is the end of
    #   the pipe that reads; the duplicate does not fail, and the body goes to
    #   $GITHUB_ENV.
    # cause: the rule reads descriptor 2 inside the $( ) as closed, and reads
    #   the echo as a command that bash does not run.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
    # attack-run-behavior: the value goes to $GITHUB_ENV.
    on:
      issues:
        types: [opened]
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              V: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
            run: |
              exec 2>&-
              echo "$( echo "V=$V" >>"$GITHUB_ENV" 3>&2 )"
    ```
- github-output: a value written to \$GITHUB_OUTPUT
  - finding kinds: envvar-injection.controlled, envvar-injection.wiki
  - disposition: other-rule (rule: output-clobbering)
  - example: github-output.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, a run writes the issue's body to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
    # reason: another rule's: output-clobbering reports a value written to
    #   $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
    # cause: the rule reads writes to $GITHUB_ENV only.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
    # attack-run-behavior: echo appends b=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and
    #   the runner sets the outputs b to x and PWNED to 1 of the step; nothing
    #   is written to $GITHUB_ENV, and no variable PWNED is set.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              B: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
            run: echo "b=$B" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    ```
- insider-association: an if that lets in MEMBER or COLLABORATOR by the author_association of the issue, the pull request or the discussion the run is of, which the following pass: a member or a collaborator whose repository role is Read only, who gets, in the run, a token that writes and the secrets, more than what the Read role gives; the account of such a member or collaborator, taken over; and an outsider who becomes a MEMBER with the Read role, in an organization that lets anyone become a member (a bot that invites whoever asks). A member or a collaborator whose role is Triage or above holds a credential that can add a label or write to the repository, which the credential premise assumes no attacker holds. Who is a member, and with what role, is not in the workflow
  - finding kinds: envvar-injection.controlled, envvar-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - added attackers: read-member, triage-account, writer-issues-token, required-reviewer
  - example: insider-association.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues opened, a job whose if lets in an issue whose
    #   author_association is MEMBER writes the issue's body to $GITHUB_ENV.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): a member of the organization, who may have read
    #   access only, passes this if (in an organization that lets anyone become a
    #   member, such as by a bot that invites whoever asks, an outsider becomes such
    #   a member), and gets the job's token and secrets past what the Read role
    #   gives; who is a member, and with what role, is not in the workflow.
    # cause: the rule evaluates the if with the attacker's author_association
    #   (NONE, FIRST_TIMER, FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR or CONTRIBUTOR), for which it
    #   is false, so no attacker's event runs the job.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
    # attack-run-behavior: on an issue a member opens, the job runs and echo
    #   appends body=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_ENV; the runner sets body to x and
    #   PWNED to 1. On an issue whose author_association is NONE, FIRST_TIMER,
    #   FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR or CONTRIBUTOR, the if skips the job.
    on:
      issues:
        types: [opened]
    jobs:
      a:
        if: github.event.issue.author_association == 'MEMBER'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              BODY: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
            run: echo "body=$BODY" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
    ```
- split-env-name: a variable named by the part of a key of env before the first =, such as A for the key A=B, which the runner sets to the rest of the key, =, and the value (in a step in a job's container, to the rest of the key alone): the rule reads a variable of env by a key equal to the name of the variable
  - finding kinds: envvar-injection.controlled, envvar-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: split-env-name.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues opened, a step has the env key T=X with the issue's
    #   title, and writes $T to $GITHUB_ENV.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the runner sets the variable T to X= and
    #   the title, and a title with a line break writes a line of its own to
    #   $GITHUB_ENV.
    # cause: the rule reads a variable of env by a key equal to its name, and
    #   no key is T.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "x\nPWNED=1"
    # attack-run-behavior: T is X=x, a line break and the rest of the title, and
    #   echo writes the lines TITLE=X=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_ENV; the runner sets
    #   PWNED for the steps after it.
    on:
      issues:
        types: [opened]
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              T=X: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
            run: echo "TITLE=$T" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          - run: make
    ```
- wiki-summary: the summary of a wiki page (github.event.pages&#91;\*].summary) in a job that runs on gollum: the rule reads the summary as a value that nobody writes. The gollum payloads that the authors of the linter saw had a null summary each time: for pages made and edited on the web interface of GitHub and pushed by git, an edit message on the web interface and a commit message of git did not go into the summary. The authors saw only pages that the owner of a public repository made and edited, and did not try an edit by an account with no role in the repository
  - finding kinds: envvar-injection.controlled, envvar-injection.wiki
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: wiki-summary.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on gollum, a step writes the summary of the wiki page to
    #   $GITHUB_ENV.
    # reason: a limitation (run time): GitHub decides the summary of a wiki page
    #   when the event happens. The gollum payloads that the authors of the
    #   linter saw had a null summary each time, for pages made and edited on
    #   the web interface and pushed by git; an edit by an account with no role
    #   in the repository was not tried.
    # cause: the rule reads the summary of a wiki page as a value that nobody
    #   writes.
    # attack-value: github.event.pages[0].summary = "x\nPWNED=1"
    # attack-run-behavior: if GitHub ever put a summary that the editor of the
    #   wiki writes in the payload, a line break in the summary would set
    #   another environment variable of the steps after the step.
    on: gollum
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              SUMMARY: ${{ github.event.pages[0].summary }}
            run: echo "summary=$SUMMARY" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
    ```
- remote-callee: a job or a step inside a reusable workflow of another repository (uses: owner/repo/.github/workflows/&lt;file>@&lt;ref>) whose content the fact workflow.definition does not give. For every rule: a run that does not ask the fact (a run without --online and without the answer in --facts). For a quality rule, also: a run where the linter asked the fact and got no answer (an answer of unknown: the GitHub API did not give the file), and a call deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact. The rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition. For a rule that is not a quality rule (a rule with a threat), the last two forms are the inconclusive kind remote-callee-unknown, not this form
  - finding kinds: envvar-injection.controlled, envvar-injection.wiki
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-callee.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
    #   the repository example-org/envvar-injection-unanswered, whose content is
    #   the workflow of the true positive controlled
    #   (controlled.custom-shell.yml) of the rule, with on: workflow_call in
    #   place of the on of controlled.custom-shell.yml. The linter has no answer
    #   of the fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event
    #   that started the run of the calling job, and the linter does not read
    #   the reusable workflow.
    # cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from
    #   the answer of workflow.definition.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
    # attack-run-behavior: BODY holds x, a line break and PWNED=1, so echo
    #   appends the two lines body=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_ENV; the runner
    #   reads each line as NAME=value and sets body to x and PWNED to 1 for the
    #   later steps.
    on:
      issues:
        types: [opened]
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/envvar-injection-unanswered/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

### inconclusive

- step-output-run: the output of a step that runs a script (steps.&lt;id>.outputs), which the script writes to \$GITHUB_OUTPUT
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: step-output-run.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the step s runs a script that writes the output o to
    #   $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the next step writes steps.s.outputs.o to
    #   $GITHUB_ENV by ${{ }}.
    # reason: the output is what the script writes at run time, so whether an
    #   attacker controls it is not known.
    # cause: the rule does not yet follow what a script writes to
    #   $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
    # attack-value: steps.s.outputs.o = "x\nPWNED=1"
    # attack-run-behavior: here s writes o=x, so o is x and the step appends the
    #   one line v=x. Were o this value (a script of s that writes an attacker's
    #   text as o), the script would become echo "v=x<line break>PWNED=1" >>
    #   "$GITHUB_ENV", which appends v=x and PWNED=1, and the runner would set
    #   PWNED to 1.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: s
            run: echo "o=x" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          - run: echo "v=${{ steps.s.outputs.o }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
    ```
- step-output-local-action: the output of a step that uses a local action (./, in the workspace of the job, which is the repository that the job checks out; \$/, the repository of the action)
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - example: step-output-local-action.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the step s uses the local action ./.github/actions/a, and the
    #   next step writes steps.s.outputs.o to $GITHUB_ENV by ${{ }}.
    # reason: the output is what the local action sets; that action is in the
    #   workspace of the job (the repository the job checks out), not in this
    #   workflow, so whether an attacker controls the output is not known.
    # cause: the rule does not read the outputs a local action sets: it gives
    #   this kind to steps.<id>.outputs of any step that uses a local action,
    #   whether its action.yml is among the files read or not.
    # attack-value: steps.s.outputs.o = "x\nPWNED=1"
    # attack-run-behavior: when ./.github/actions/a sets o to an attacker's text
    #   such as this value, the script becomes echo "v=x<line break>PWNED=1" >>
    #   "$GITHUB_ENV", which appends v=x and PWNED=1; the runner sets v to x and
    #   PWNED to 1.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: s
            uses: ./.github/actions/a
          - run: echo "v=${{ steps.s.outputs.o }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
    ```
- step-output-remote-action: the output of a step that uses an action of another repository
