    - {vulnerable_version_range}: The range of versions the advisory says the vulnerability affects, as GitHub writes the range.
  - consequence: an attacker may use the vulnerability the advisory describes; GitHub's rating of the advisory is its own, and the severity of this finding is found by another table
  - remedy: upgrade to a version the advisory says is fixed, or stop using the action
  - severity: medium (found from the CVSS metrics below by the table)
  - fix kinds: upgrade-version
  - attackers: advisory-attacker
  - preconditions: affects-version, tag-runs
  - true positives:
    - advisory-low.ghsa-xcf7-88g6-7xr8.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on pull_request_target, a job checks out the head of the pull
      #   request with actions/checkout v4.2.2, writes a secret into the .env file
      #   beside the Compose file, and runs tmatens/compose-lint pinned to the
      #   commits of v0.24.0 with sarif-file at the root of the workspace, of
      #   v0.31.0 with sarif-file in a subdirectory, and of v0.32.0. The
      #   advisories name no workflow; the steps follow the configurations that
      #   the advisories describe: a workflow that writes secrets into the .env
      #   file beside the Compose file and runs on pull requests from authors who
      #   should not see the secrets (GHSA-jf3h-8jvx-vcrg and GHSA-rm8w-w798-g545),
      #   a pull request that commits a symlink that compose-lint reads
      #   (GHSA-whr6-fgpq-fpv9, GHSA-88f4-frh5-gmcr and GHSA-6wcv-rj3c-mhv3), and an
      #   input sarif-file that names a file in a subdirectory
      #   (GHSA-xcf7-88g6-7xr8). On pull_request, the author of a pull request from
      #   a fork can change the workflow, and the job gets no secret, so the
      #   example runs on pull_request_target. The rule also reports
      #   GHSA-6f4g-xm8v-pgv6, which GitHub rates medium, on the step of v0.24.0;
      #   the example of GHSA-6f4g-xm8v-pgv6 is
      #   advisory-medium.ghsa-6f4g-xm8v-pgv6. The fix of the rule upgrades each
      #   of the three steps to the commit of v0.33.0. For the step of v0.32.0,
      #   0.33.0 is the first patched version of GHSA-rm8w-w798-g545. For the
      #   steps of v0.24.0 and of v0.31.0, the greatest first patched version of
      #   the advisories of the steps is 0.32.0, which is in the range of
      #   GHSA-rm8w-w798-g545, so the fix moves on to 0.33.0, which is in the
      #   range of no advisory of the package.
      # reason: the six advisories, which GitHub rates low, are in the code of the
      #   action, which the workflow does not show. GHSA-jf3h-8jvx-vcrg says
      #   compose-lint from 0.22.0 to 0.31.0 quotes the value that a variable of
      #   the .env file gives to image: in the text of a finding, and
      #   GHSA-rm8w-w798-g545 says compose-lint 0.32.0 does so in a run that stops
      #   at 20,000 findings. GHSA-6wcv-rj3c-mhv3 says compose-lint from 0.22.0 to
      #   0.30.0 reads a .env file that is a symlink to a file outside the project,
      #   such as /proc/self/environ. GHSA-whr6-fgpq-fpv9 (up to 0.24.0) and
      #   GHSA-88f4-frh5-gmcr (up to 0.31.0) say a parse error of compose-lint
      #   quotes a line of a file outside the project that a symlink of the Compose
      #   file or of .compose-lint.yml names. GHSA-xcf7-88g6-7xr8 says the Action
      #   v0.30.0 and v0.31.0 prints the resolved path of the directory of
      #   sarif-file, which a symlink of the pull request names, with the
      #   processing of workflow commands on.
      # attack: two pull requests from a fork. The first pull request changes the
      #   image of a service of the Compose file to "${DB_PASSWORD}" and commits
      #   .compose-lint.yml as a symlink to a file of credentials on the runner,
      #   against the step of v0.24.0. The second pull request commits the
      #   directory out, which the input sarif-file of the step of v0.31.0 names,
      #   as a symlink to a directory whose name holds a line break and a workflow
      #   command; the directory that the symlink names holds a regular file named
      #   reports, so the directory out/reports cannot be created. The second pull
      #   request is against the step of v0.31.0.
      # attack-run-behavior: in the run of the first pull request, compose-lint
      #   v0.24.0 quotes the value of DB_PASSWORD and a part of a line of the file
      #   of credentials in the SARIF that the action uploads to Code Scanning. In
      #   the run of the second pull request, the action v0.31.0 fails to create
      #   the directory of sarif-file, prints the name of the directory before the
      #   step ends, and the runner reads the second line of the name as a
      #   workflow command.
      # advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xcf7-88g6-7xr8
      # advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rm8w-w798-g545
      # advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-whr6-fgpq-fpv9
      # advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-88f4-frh5-gmcr
      # advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jf3h-8jvx-vcrg
      # advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6wcv-rj3c-mhv3
      on: pull_request_target
      jobs:
        lint:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          permissions:
            contents: read
            security-events: write
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2
              with:
                ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
            - run: printf 'DB_PASSWORD=%s\n' "$DB_PASSWORD" > .env
              env:
                DB_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.DB_PASSWORD }}
            - uses: tmatens/compose-lint@d6e1817352200adbd0a72893fd7ea7880874759b # v0.24.0
              with:
                sarif-file: results.sarif
            - uses: tmatens/compose-lint@a6a7a76736de1c72abfa96c41ff8af556ffdc55f # v0.31.0
              with:
                sarif-file: out/reports/results.sarif
            - uses: tmatens/compose-lint@2d42617e4c6416f797bbfc6a057950131fa02df3 # v0.32.0
      ```
    - advisory-low.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml

            - run: npm ci && npm test
            - run: kubectl apply -f deploy.yaml

                KUBECONFIG_DATA: ${{ secrets.KUBECONFIG }}
      ```

      ```yaml
            - run: npm ci && npm test
      ```

- known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-unknown
  - detected: {uses} runs {version} of {package}, which {ghsa_id} (not rated by GitHub) says is vulnerable ({vulnerable_version_range})
  - arguments:
    - {uses}: The uses, as written.
    - {version}: A version of a package in the form that the GitHub Advisory Database compares: an optional v, numbers of at most 9 digits joined by dots, and a prerelease after a hyphen, such as v4.1.2, 4 or 2.0.0-beta.1. A version tag of an action has the same form.
    - {package}: The name of a package of the actions ecosystem of the GitHub Advisory Database: owner/repo of an action or a reusable workflow, and the path to the action or the workflow in the repository when the action or the workflow is not at the root. GitHub compares owner and repo without case; sisakulint writes owner and repo in lower case, and the path as written.
    - {ghsa_id}: The ID of an advisory of the GitHub Advisory Database, GHSA-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx.
    - {vulnerable_version_range}: The range of versions the advisory says the vulnerability affects, as GitHub writes the range.
  - consequence: an attacker may use the vulnerability the advisory describes; GitHub's rating of the advisory is its own, and the severity of this finding is found by another table
  - remedy: upgrade to a version the advisory says is fixed, or stop using the action
  - severity: critical (found from the CVSS metrics below by the table)
  - fix kinds: upgrade-version
  - attackers: advisory-attacker
  - preconditions: affects-version, tag-runs
  - true positives:
    - advisory-unknown.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a step uses example-org/example-action pinned to the commit of
      #   v1.0.0.
      # reason: an advisory GitHub has not rated says the versions before 1.0.1
      #   are vulnerable. No advisory of the actions ecosystem was unrated on
      #   2026-10-15, so the repository, its commits, the advisory and its ID are
      #   made up for this example.
      # attack: someone uses the vulnerability the advisory describes.
      # attack-run-behavior: v1.0.0 runs the vulnerable code in the job.
      on: push
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: example-org/example-action@1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 # v1.0.0
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - advisory-unknown.never-runs.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on push, the job whose id is disabled has if: false, and the job
      #   whose id is on-failure needs the job build and has if: needs.build.result
      #   == 'failure'; each of the two jobs uses example-org/example-action pinned
      #   to the commit of v1.0.0, which an advisory says is vulnerable; GitHub has
      #   not rated the advisory (the repository, the commits of the repository and
      #   the advisory are made up for this example, as in the true positive
      #   advisory-unknown).
      # reason: GitHub skips the job disabled because the if of the job disabled is
      #   false. The if of the job on-failure calls no status function, so GitHub
      #   evaluates the if of the job on-failure only when the job build succeeded;
      #   needs.build.result is then success, and the if is false. When the job
      #   build fails or is skipped, GitHub skips the job on-failure without
      #   evaluating the if. So neither job runs
      #   (https://github.com/github/docs/blob/404a5f4de6cd5311e3ce2d5c076571291e0107d6/data/reusables/actions/jobs/section-using-conditions-to-control-job-execution.md).
      # attack: someone uses the vulnerability that the advisory describes.
      # attack-run-behavior: GitHub skips the job disabled and the job on-failure,
      #   so the vulnerable code of v1.0.0 does not run.
      on: push
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: echo built
        disabled:
          if: false
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: example-org/example-action@1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 # v1.0.0
        on-failure:
          needs: build
          if: needs.build.result == 'failure'
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: example-org/example-action@1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 # v1.0.0
      ```
    - advisory-unknown.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: the step uses example-org/example-action pinned to the commit
      #   of v1.0.1 (made up, as the true positive).
      # reason: the advisory says 1.0.1 fixes it; GitHub gives no advisory for
      #   1.0.1.
      # attack: someone uses the vulnerability the advisory describes.
      # attack-run-behavior: v1.0.1 runs the fixed code.
      on: push
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: example-org/example-action@2222222222222222222222222222222222222222 # v1.0.1
      ```

### fix kinds

- upgrade-version: pin a uses pinned to a full SHA to the commit of the first version that fixes every advisory found and is in the range of no advisory of the package, and name the version of the commit in the comment at the end of the line of the uses
  - safety: review
  - fact kinds: git.ref-commit
  - possible side effects:
    - version-changed: The action or the reusable workflow runs another version, whose inputs, outputs and behavior may differ.

### undetected forms

- url-package: an advisory whose package is named by a URL (https://github.com/owner/repo/path) rather than owner/repo: GitHub does not give it for affects=owner/repo, and the rule does not ask by URL
  - finding kinds: known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-critical, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-high, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-medium, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-low, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-unknown
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: url-package.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a step uses the composite action filter-test-configs of
    #   pytorch/pytorch, pinned to a commit (the SHA is made up).
    # reason: GHSA-hw6r-g8gj-2987, which GitHub rates medium, names its package
    #   https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/.github/actions/filter-test-configs;
    #   GitHub gives it neither for affects=pytorch/pytorch nor for the path.
    # cause: the rule asks for owner/repo and owner/repo/path, not for a URL.
    # attack: someone uses the vulnerability the advisory describes.
    # attack-run-behavior: the action runs as the uses names it, and the rule
    #   says nothing.
    on: push
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: pytorch/pytorch/.github/actions/filter-test-configs@3333333333333333333333333333333333333333
    ```
- remote-composite: a vulnerable action that a composite action of another repository uses, when action.definition has no answer for the composite action (a run without --online and without the answer in --facts): the rule reads the steps of a composite action of another repository only from the answer
  - finding kinds: known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-critical, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-high, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-medium, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-low, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-unknown
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-composite.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a step uses example-org/composite-action (made up), a composite
    #   action whose action.yml, in its own repository, uses
    #   actions/download-artifact pinned to the commit of v4.1.2.
    # reason: the action this workflow names has no advisory; the one it uses
    #   inside has GHSA-cxww-7g56-2vh6 (path traversal in the files of an
    #   artifact).
    # cause: the rule reads the uses of the inputs, not of the action.yml of
    #   another repository.
    # attack: someone who makes the artifact the composite action downloads
    #   puts in it a file whose name climbs out of the path.
    # attack-run-behavior: v4.1.2, run inside the composite action, writes that
    #   file where its name points, and the rule says nothing.
    on: push
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: example-org/composite-action@4444444444444444444444444444444444444444
    ```
- outside-other-path: a uses whose path goes with .. above the root of its repository into the directory where the runner puts another uses' action, and names an action at another path there: the rule reads the other uses, not the action at that path
  - finding kinds: known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-critical, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-high, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-medium, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-low, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-unknown
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: outside-other-path.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the first step uses actions/cache/restore at the tag v3; the
    #   second step names actions/cache/restore by a full SHA, but its path goes
    #   with .. above the root of the repository, into the directory where the
    #   runner puts actions/cache at v3, and names the path save there.
    # reason: the second step runs actions/cache/save at v3, which the first
    #   step downloads; an advisory of actions/cache/save at that version is an
    #   advisory of the code that runs.
    # cause: for the second step, the rule reads the action of the first step
    #   (restore), not the action at the path of the second step (save).
    # attack: whoever can exploit the advisory of actions/cache/save, as the
    #   advisory says, does so through the second step.
    # attack-run-behavior: the runner downloads actions/cache at v3 for the
    #   first step, and the second step runs the save action of that download.
    on: push
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/cache/restore@v3
            with:
              path: build
              key: build
          - uses: actions/cache/restore/../../v3/save@0123456789012345678901234567890123456789
            with:
              path: build
              key: build
    ```
- docker: a uses of a Docker image (docker://): the actions ecosystem of the GitHub Advisory Database names packages by repository, not by image
  - finding kinds: known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-critical, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-high, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-medium, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-low, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-unknown
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: docker.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a step runs a Docker image.
    # reason: the actions ecosystem of the GitHub Advisory Database names
    #   packages by repository; an image is not one, and its vulnerabilities are
    #   not advisories of an action.
    # cause: the rule reads only the uses that name another repository
    #   (owner/repo), as the packages of the actions ecosystem are named.
    # attack: none of this rule's threat.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step runs the image the tag names.
    on: push
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: docker://alpine:3.18
    ```
- installed-version: an action whose code installs a tool at the version that an input of the step gives, not at the version that the version tag of the action gives, where the version of the tool is in the range of an advisory and the version tag of the action is not (tmatens/compose-lint from v0.18.0 installs the version of the compose-lint package that the input whose name is version gives): the rule compares the ranges of the advisories with the version tag of the action, and does not read the code of the action, though the code of the action decides the version of the tool that the step installs
  - finding kinds: known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-critical, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-high, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-medium, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-low, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-unknown
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: installed-version.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a job checks out the head of the pull
    #   request with actions/checkout v4.2.2, writes a secret into the .env file
    #   beside the Compose file, and runs tmatens/compose-lint pinned to the
    #   commit of v0.33.0 with the input whose name is version set to 0.31.0.
    #   The action tmatens/compose-lint from v0.18.0 installs the version of the
    #   compose-lint package that the input whose name is version gives (lines
    #   118 to 127 of action.yml at the commit of v0.33.0), so the step installs
    #   compose-lint 0.31.0.
    # reason: compose-lint 0.31.0 is in the range of GHSA-jf3h-8jvx-vcrg (from
    #   0.22.0 to 0.31.0), which says compose-lint quotes the value that a
    #   variable of the .env file gives to image: in the text of a finding;
    #   v0.33.0, the version tag of the action, is in the range of no advisory.
    # cause: the rule compares the ranges of the advisories with the version tag
    #   of the action, and does not read the code of the action, though the code
    #   of the action decides the version of compose-lint that the step
    #   installs.
    # attack: the author of a pull request from a fork changes the image of a
    #   service of the Compose file to "${DB_PASSWORD}".
    # attack-run-behavior: compose-lint 0.31.0 quotes the value of DB_PASSWORD
    #   in the SARIF that the action uploads to Code Scanning, and the rule
    #   reports nothing on the step.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      lint:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions:
          contents: read
          security-events: write
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: printf 'DB_PASSWORD=%s\n' "$DB_PASSWORD" > .env
            env:
              DB_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.DB_PASSWORD }}
          - uses: tmatens/compose-lint@691e08bd1881ada886e3f556d0793079e8114451 # v0.33.0
            with:
              version: 0.31.0
              sarif-file: results.sarif
    ```
- remote-callee: a job or a step inside a reusable workflow of another repository (uses: owner/repo/.github/workflows/&lt;file>@&lt;ref>) whose content the fact workflow.definition does not give. For every rule: a run that does not ask the fact (a run without --online and without the answer in --facts). For a quality rule, also: a run where the linter asked the fact and got no answer (an answer of unknown: the GitHub API did not give the file), and a call deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact. The rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition. For a rule that is not a quality rule (a rule with a threat), the last two forms are the inconclusive kind remote-callee-unknown, not this form
  - finding kinds: known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-critical, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-high, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-medium, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-low, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-unknown
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-callee.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
    #   the repository example-org/known-vulnerable-actions-unanswered, whose
    #   content is the workflow of the true positive advisory-critical
    #   (advisory-critical.yml) of the rule, with on: workflow_call in place of
    #   the on of advisory-critical.yml. The linter has no answer of the fact
    #   workflow.definition for the reusable workflow.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event
    #   that started the run of the calling job, and the linter does not read
    #   the reusable workflow.
    # cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from
    #   the answer of workflow.definition.
    # attack-value: the name of the pull request's branch = "a$(echo${IFS}PWNED)"
    # attack-run-behavior: the action's script runs the command in the branch
    #   name, with the token and the secrets of the job of the base repository.
    on: pull_request_target
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/known-vulnerable-actions-unanswered/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

### inconclusive

- advisories-unknown: the advisories of the package are not known: no file of facts answers, and --online was not given or failed
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: advisories-unknown.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a step uses example-org/unanswered-action pinned to a commit
    #   (made up), and nothing answers what advisories it has (no file of facts,
    #   no --online).
    # reason: the rule cannot tell whether an advisory names the version it
    #   runs.
    # attack: someone uses a vulnerability of the action, if the version is
    #   one an advisory names.
    # attack-run-behavior: a vulnerable version runs the vulnerable code; a
    #   fixed one does not.
    on: push
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: example-org/unanswered-action@5555555555555555555555555555555555555555 # v1.0.0
    ```
- remote-unknown: a uses of another repository that a step reaches through composite actions, whose action.definition was asked and has no answer (the archive is larger than the limit, the run has used up the requests it may send to the GitHub API, the token cannot read the repository, or the action is deeper than the 4 levels of actions the linter reads): whether a step of the action uses a vulnerable action is not known
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-unknown.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a step runs example-org/unreachable-composite@v1, a composite action of another
    #   repository; the archive is larger than the limit.
    # reason: whether a step of the action uses an action with an advisory is
    #   in a file the run could not read, or one the runner may run otherwise.
    # attack: someone who makes the artifact a step of the composite action
    #   downloads puts in it a file whose name climbs out of the path.
    # attack-run-behavior: when the step is there, v4.1.2 writes the files of
    #   a crafted artifact where their names point.
    on: push
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: example-org/unreachable-composite@v1
    ```
- archive-substituted: a composite action of another repository whose action.yml (or action.yaml) in the archive the runner downloads is unlike its blob (export-subst): placeholders such as %d and %(describe) take the names of refs created after the commit, so the actions its steps use may differ from those read
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: archive-substituted.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a step runs example-org/substituted-composite@v1, a composite action of another
    #   repository; the archive the runner downloads has the file of the action unlike its blob (export-subst).
    # reason: whether a step of the action uses an action with an advisory is
    #   in a file the run could not read, or one the runner may run otherwise.
    # attack: someone who makes the artifact a step of the composite action
    #   downloads puts in it a file whose name climbs out of the path.
    # attack-run-behavior: when the step is there, v4.1.2 writes the files of
    #   a crafted artifact where their names point.
    on: push
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: example-org/substituted-composite@v1
    ```
- version-unknown: the package has advisories, but the version the uses runs is not known: no version tag points to its commit (the head of a branch, a commit between releases), only a major tag does (v2) while a range has a bound within that major (< 2.7.5), or the commit or its tags are not known
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: version-unknown.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a step uses tj-actions/changed-files@main, whose head no
    #   version tag points to.
    # reason: the package has advisories, but the commit main runs has no
    #   version, so the rule cannot ask which of them affect it.
    # attack: someone uses a vulnerability of the code main has, if it has one
    #   an advisory names.
    # attack-run-behavior: the runner runs the head of main, whatever it is
    #   when the job starts.
    on: push
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: tj-actions/changed-files@main
    ```
- remote-callee-unknown: a job that calls a reusable workflow of another repository, when the linter asked the fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow and got no answer (the token that the linter uses cannot read the file, the file is larger than the limit, or the linter has used up the requests it may send to the GitHub API), or when the call is deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact: the rule does not read the jobs and the steps of the reusable workflow
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-callee-unknown.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
    #   the repository example-org/known-vulnerable-actions-unknown, whose
    #   content is the workflow of the true positive advisory-critical
    #   (advisory-critical.yml) of the rule, with on: workflow_call in place of
    #   the on of advisory-critical.yml. The linter asked the fact
    #   workflow.definition for the reusable workflow and got no answer.
    # reason: what the jobs of the reusable workflow do is in the file that the
    #   linter could not read; whoever changes the uses, such as the author of a
    #   pull request, can name a reusable workflow that the token that the
    #   linter uses cannot read.
    # attack-value: the name of the pull request's branch = "a$(echo${IFS}PWNED)"
    # attack-run-behavior: the action's script runs the command in the branch
    #   name, with the token and the secrets of the job of the base repository.
    on: pull_request_target
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/known-vulnerable-actions-unknown/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

### false positive forms

- compromise-window: an advisory of tags that were moved to malicious commits for a time and then moved back: its range has the versions whose tags were moved, though the commits they name now are not malicious (the advisory of tj-actions/changed-files says the tags are safe to use again)
  - finding kinds: known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-critical, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-high, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-medium, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-low, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-unknown
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: compromise-window.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a step uses tj-actions/changed-files pinned to the commit of
    #   v44.5.1.
    # reason: GHSA-mrrh-fwg8-r2c3 is of the tags of tj-actions/changed-files
    #   moved to a malicious commit in March 2025; its range, <= 45.0.7, is of
    #   the versions whose tags were moved. The advisory says: "If you are using
    #   tagged versions (e.g., v35, v44.5.1), no action is required as these
    #   tags have been updated and are now safe to use." The commit of v44.5.1
    #   is not the malicious one.
    # cause: the rule reads only the range of an advisory, not what it says of
    #   the commits.
    # attack: the attacker of 2025 moves the tags again; this workflow names a
    #   commit, which no tag moves.
    # attack-run-behavior: the runner runs the commit 03334d09, which was not
    #   the malicious one.
    on: push
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: tj-actions/changed-files@03334d095e2739fa9ac4034ec16f66d5d01e9eba # v44.5.1
    ```
- other-path: an advisory of owner/repo, of the action at the root of the repository, read of an action at a path of the same repository whose code the vulnerability is not in
  - finding kinds: known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-critical, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-high, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-medium, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-low, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-unknown
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: other-path.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a step uploads a SARIF file another tool made, with
    #   github/codeql-action/upload-sarif pinned to the commit of v3.28.2.
    # reason: GHSA-vqf5-2xx6-9wfm, of the package github/codeql-action, exposes
    #   the environment only when "The workflow run fails before the CodeQL
    #   database is finalized within the github/codeql-action/analyze step"
    #   (its text). upload-sarif makes no database.
    # cause: the rule reads an advisory of owner/repo as one of every action of
    #   the repository.
    # attack: someone who can read the artifacts of the repository downloads
    #   the debug artifact of a failed analysis.
    # attack-run-behavior: this job uploads a SARIF file and makes no debug
    #   artifact of a database.
    on: push
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@d68b2d4edb4189fd2a5366ac14e72027bd4b37dd # v3.28.2
            with:
              sarif_file: results.sarif
    ```
- repository-workflow: an advisory whose vulnerability is in a workflow of the repository of the action, not in action.yml or the code that action.yml runs: a step that uses the action runs action.yml and the code that action.yml runs, not the workflows of the repository of the action, so the step does not run the vulnerable workflow; the answer of the GitHub Advisory Database does not say where the vulnerability is (the field vulnerable_functions is empty), so the rule cannot tell such an advisory from an advisory whose vulnerability is in action.yml or the code that action.yml runs
  - finding kinds: known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-critical, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-high, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-medium, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-low, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-unknown
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: repository-workflow.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step uses Tiryoh/actions-mkdocs pinned to the
    #   commit of v0.24.0, whose package GHSA-6p2j-742g-835f names with the
    #   range <= 0.24.0. The vulnerability of the advisory is in a workflow of
    #   the repository Tiryoh/actions-mkdocs (.github/workflows/release-candidate.yaml
    #   writes the title of an issue into run), not in the action: "This issue
    #   is limited to the repository's internal workflow configuration and does
    #   not directly affect downstream users of the published `actions-mkdocs`
    #   GitHub Action."
    # reason: the step runs action.yml of Tiryoh/actions-mkdocs, which the
    #   vulnerability is not in; the workflows of the repository of the action
    #   run only in that repository, not in the workflow that uses the action.
    # cause: the rule reads every advisory of the package of the uses as an
    #   advisory of the action; the answer of the GitHub Advisory Database does
    #   not say where the vulnerability is (the field vulnerable_functions of
    #   the package is empty).
    # attack: none: the vulnerable workflow is not in the repository of this
    #   workflow.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step builds the documentation with mkdocs; no
    #   step reads the title of an issue.
    # advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6p2j-742g-835f
    on: push
    jobs:
      docs:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: Tiryoh/actions-mkdocs@14d3fd544b7a2bcffcdd86b05d558f20c244c9fc # v0.24.0
    ```
- installed-version: an action whose code installs a tool at the version that an input of the step gives, or at the newest version in the registry of the tool when the job runs, not at the version that the version tag of the action gives, where the version tag of the action is in the range of an advisory and the version of the tool is not (tmatens/compose-lint from v0.18.0 with the input whose name is version set to latest, and tmatens/compose-lint up to v0.17.0 without the input whose name is version, install the newest version of the compose-lint package): the rule compares the ranges of the advisories with the version tag of the action, and does not read the code of the action, though the code of the action decides the version of the tool that the step installs
  - finding kinds: known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-critical, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-high, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-medium, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-low, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-unknown
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: installed-version.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a job checks out the head of the pull
    #   request with actions/checkout v4.2.2, writes a secret into the .env file
    #   beside the Compose file, and runs tmatens/compose-lint pinned to the
    #   commit of v0.24.0 with the input whose name is version set to latest.
    #   The action tmatens/compose-lint from v0.18.0 installs the newest version
    #   of the compose-lint package in PyPI when the input whose name is version
    #   is latest (lines 88 to 97 of action.yml at the commit of v0.24.0); on
    #   2026-11-13, the newest version of compose-lint in PyPI is 1.4.0.
    # reason: the rule reports five advisories on the step, because v0.24.0, the
    #   version tag of the action, is in the ranges of the five advisories; the
    #   step installs the newest version of compose-lint, which is in the range
    #   of no advisory when the newest version is 0.33.0 or later.
    # cause: the rule compares the ranges of the advisories with the version tag
    #   of the action, and does not read the code of the action, though the code
    #   of the action decides the version of compose-lint that the step
    #   installs.
    # attack: the author of a pull request from a fork changes the image of a
    #   service of the Compose file to "${DB_PASSWORD}", and commits
    #   .compose-lint.yml as a symlink to a file on the runner.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step runs a version of compose-lint that the
    #   advisories say is fixed: compose-lint quotes the reference ${DB_PASSWORD}
    #   in place of the value, and refuses .compose-lint.yml that resolves
    #   outside the working directory.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      lint:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions:
          contents: read
          security-events: write
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: printf 'DB_PASSWORD=%s\n' "$DB_PASSWORD" > .env
            env:
              DB_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.DB_PASSWORD }}
          - uses: tmatens/compose-lint@d6e1817352200adbd0a72893fd7ea7880874759b # v0.24.0
            with:
              version: latest
              sarif-file: results.sarif
    ```
- advisory-condition: an advisory whose vulnerability needs an input, an event or a setting the step does not have: the rule does not read what the advisory says it needs
  - finding kinds: known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-critical, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-high, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-medium, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-low, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-unknown
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: advisory-condition.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job analyzes Python alone with github/codeql-action/init
    #   and analyze pinned to the commit of v3.28.2.
    # reason: GHSA-vqf5-2xx6-9wfm exposes the environment only for a
    #   "Code scanning workflow configured to scan the Java/Kotlin languages"
    #   (its text): the CodeQL Kotlin extractor logs the environment. This job
    #   scans Python, so the extractor does not run.
    # cause: the rule does not read what an advisory says its vulnerability
    #   needs.
    # attack: someone who can read the artifacts of the repository downloads
    #   the debug artifact of a failed analysis.
    # attack-run-behavior: no Kotlin extractor runs, so no file of the
    #   environment is written for a debug artifact to hold.
    on: push
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: github/codeql-action/init@d68b2d4edb4189fd2a5366ac14e72027bd4b37dd # v3.28.2
            with:
              languages: python
          - uses: github/codeql-action/analyze@d68b2d4edb4189fd2a5366ac14e72027bd4b37dd # v3.28.2
    ```
- actions-not-allowed: a workflow whose run GitHub does not start, or a job that GitHub fails in the step "Set up job", because of the setting of allowed actions of GitHub (the fact repo.allowed-actions, which the quality rule allowed-actions reads): GitHub does not start a run of a workflow that has a uses, or that calls a reusable workflow that has a uses, that the setting does not allow, and fails a job before any step of the job runs when a step of a composite action that the job runs has a uses that the setting does not allow, or when the setting requires a full commit SHA and a step names an action by a tag or a branch. The harm that the finding reports happens only when GitHub runs the workflow or the job, and the rule does not read repo.allowed-actions
  - finding kinds: known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-critical, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-high, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-medium, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-low, known-vulnerable-actions.advisory-unknown
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: actions-not-allowed.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the workflow of the true positive advisory-critical
    #   (advisory-critical.yml) of the rule, with a job added whose step uses
    #   example-org/not-allowed-action, which the setting of allowed actions of
    #   GitHub (repo.allowed-actions) blocks with
    #   !example-org/not-allowed-action@*. In the true positive, on
    #   pull_request_target, a step reads the branch names with
    #   tj-actions/branch-names pinned to the commit of v7.0.6.
    # reason: GitHub checks each uses of the workflow before the run starts, and
    #   does not start the run because of the uses of
    #   example-org/not-allowed-action: no job of the run runs, so what the
    #   reason of the true positive says does not happen (in runs that the
    #   authors of the rule made on GitHub, such runs ended as startup_failure).
    # cause: the rule does not read repo.allowed-actions.
    # attack-value: the name of the pull request's branch = "a$(echo${IFS}PWNED)"
    # attack-run-behavior: GitHub does not start the run, so no step of the run
    #   runs, and the attack does nothing.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: tj-actions/branch-names@ab304d8562e2f137165e1d930e6d22d431189074 # v7.0.6
      not-allowed:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: example-org/not-allowed-action@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

### threat

- precondition affects-version: GitHub answers affects=package@version with the advisories whose range has that version; it reads a version of a major number alone as major.0.0, so the rule asks the most precise version tag of the commit
  - observed: 2026-10-15: affects=actions/download-artifact@v4, @4 and @4.1.2 gave GHSA-cxww-7g56-2vh6 (>= 4.0.0, < 4.1.3), @4.1.3 none; affects=tj-actions/changed-files@main gave none; the package was compared without case, and a version with or without v alike
  - cites:
    - <https://github.com/github/rest-api-description/blob/507b88ecbdccb4789ce77228fa2f2fde4bdeaf1f/descriptions/api.github.com/api.github.com.json>
- precondition tag-runs: the runner runs the tag when a branch and a tag have the same name, for the uses of a step and of a job, so the version is read of the tag's commit
  - observed: 2026-10-15, runner 2.337.0: a step's action and a reusable workflow, both named by a branch and a tag of one name, ran the commit of the tag
- actor: advisory-attacker
  - via: uses the vulnerability an advisory describes, in the way the advisory describes
  - gains: run-code, read-secrets, write-with-token, write-cache
- incident tj-actions-2025: 2025-03-14, CVE-2025-30066: the tags v1 to v45.0.7 were moved to a commit that prints secrets to the log
  - advisory: <https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mrrh-fwg8-r2c3>
  - compromised: tj-actions/changed-files
- incident reviewdog-2025: 2025-03-11, CVE-2025-30154: the tag v1 was moved to code that prints secrets to the log; the reviewdog actions that use it @v1 were hit whatever their own pin
  - advisory: <https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qmg3-hpqr-gqvc>
  - compromised: reviewdog/action-setup
  - downstream: reviewdog/action-shellcheck, reviewdog/action-composite-template, reviewdog/action-staticcheck, reviewdog/action-ast-grep, reviewdog/action-typos
- incident trivy-2026: 2026-03-19, CVE-2026-33634: with stolen credentials, a commit swapped the actions/checkout of a workflow for an impostor commit (70379aad) that fetched malicious code, and was tagged v0.69.4 to run the release; 76 of the 77 version tags of aquasecurity/trivy-action and all 7 of aquasecurity/setup-trivy were force-pushed to credential-stealing commits
  - advisory: <https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-69fq-xp46-6x23>
  - compromised: aquasecurity/trivy, aquasecurity/trivy-action, aquasecurity/setup-trivy

## missing-timeout-minutes

- problem: a job on a runner writes no timeout-minutes, so a job that stops making progress runs for 360 minutes before GitHub cancels the job
- expected: every job on a runner writes timeout-minutes
- targets: workflow
- quality rule: a finding of the quality rule alone gives no attacker a gain, and the findings of the quality rule set no bit of the exit code
- default run: named: the rule runs only when --rule names the rule

### finding kinds

- missing-timeout-minutes.job
  - detected: the job {job} has no timeout-minutes
  - arguments:
    - {job}: The job's ID.
  - consequence: a job that stops making progress runs until GitHub cancels the job after 360 minutes, and the job uses the runner for the whole 360 minutes
  - remedy: write timeout-minutes on the job, a little above the time that the job usually takes
  - true positives:
    - job.remote-callee.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
      #   the repository example-org/missing-timeout-minutes-remote, which the
      #   fact workflow.definition answers with the workflow of the true positive
      #   job (job.yml) of the rule, with on: workflow_call in place of the on of
      #   job.yml. The job passes its secrets with secrets: inherit. In the true
      #   positive, a job builds on push and writes no timeout-minutes.
      # reason: the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event that started the
      #   run of the calling job, so the reason of the true positive holds: GitHub
      #   cancels a job after 360 minutes when timeout-minutes is not written, so
      #   a build that stops making progress holds the runner for 360 minutes.
      on: push
      jobs:
        c:
          uses: example-org/missing-timeout-minutes-remote/.github/workflows/w.yml@v1
          secrets: inherit
      ```
    - job.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a job builds on push and writes no timeout-minutes.
      # reason: GitHub cancels a job after 360 minutes when timeout-minutes is not
      #   written, so a build that stops making progress holds the runner for 360
      #   minutes.
      on: push
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: make
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - job.called.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: the only job calls a reusable workflow of the repository.
      # reason: a job that calls a reusable workflow cannot write timeout-minutes
      #   (the workflow-job of the schema has no such key); the jobs of the called
      #   workflow write timeout-minutes, and the rule reads those jobs in the file
      #   of the called workflow.
      on: push
      jobs:
        build:
          uses: ./.github/workflows/build.yml
      ```
    - job.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a job builds on push and writes timeout-minutes: 30.
      # reason: GitHub cancels the job after the 30 minutes written, so a build
      #   that hangs does not hold the runner for 360 minutes.
      on: push
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          timeout-minutes: 30
          steps:
            - run: make
      ```

### undetected forms

- remote-callee: a job or a step inside a reusable workflow of another repository (uses: owner/repo/.github/workflows/&lt;file>@&lt;ref>) whose content the fact workflow.definition does not give. For every rule: a run that does not ask the fact (a run without --online and without the answer in --facts). For a quality rule, also: a run where the linter asked the fact and got no answer (an answer of unknown: the GitHub API did not give the file), and a call deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact. The rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition. For a rule that is not a quality rule (a rule with a threat), the last two forms are the inconclusive kind remote-callee-unknown, not this form
  - finding kinds: missing-timeout-minutes.job
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-callee.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
    #   the repository example-org/missing-timeout-minutes-unanswered, whose
    #   content is the workflow of the true positive job (job.yml) of the rule,
    #   with on: workflow_call in place of the on of job.yml. The linter has no
    #   answer of the fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event
    #   that started the run of the calling job, and the linter does not read
    #   the reusable workflow.
    # cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from
    #   the answer of workflow.definition.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/missing-timeout-minutes-unanswered/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

## output-clobbering

- problem: a value an attacker writes with line breaks is written to \$GITHUB_OUTPUT, where each line break starts another output of the step
- expected: no value an attacker writes with line breaks is written to \$GITHUB_OUTPUT with its line breaks, or with a delimiter an attacker can write
- severity: critical (the worst of its kinds)
- targets: workflow, action-metadata
- facets:
  - weakness: environment-file-injection
  - attack-means: string
- default run: always: in a run without --rule, the rule runs unless --skip-rule names the rule

### finding kinds

- output-clobbering.controlled
  - detected: {expr_ref} is written to \$GITHUB_OUTPUT, and an attacker who controls it on {controlled_on} can start a name of their own
  - arguments:
    - {expr_ref}: The reference as written: a context in \${{ }}, or a variable of env.
    - {controlled_on}: The events on which an attacker controls the value of the expression where the value can start a name (with line breaks after the =, with any value before the =), each event named once.
  - consequence: a line break in the value, or a name before its =, sets other outputs of the step
  - remedy: keep the value after the = and take its line breaks out, or write it as name&lt;&lt;DELIM with a random delimiter
  - severity: critical (found from the CVSS metrics below by the table)
  - fix kinds: env-var-review
  - fact kinds: repo.pull-request-target-allowed (provider: repo-setting), repo.fork-pr-app-checks (provider: repo-setting), repo.merge-commit-app-checks (provider: repo-setting)
  - attackers: fork-pr-author, issue-author, commenter, merged-commit-author, anyone-who-forks
  - preconditions: runner-reads-lines, attacker-writes-lines, attacker-event, callers-events, app-status-check
  - true positives:
    - controlled.default-assignment.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issues opened, a step sets out to $GITHUB_OUTPUT with the operator
      #   := of a parameter expansion, and writes v=$V to "$out".
      # reason: bash assigns $GITHUB_OUTPUT to out, which is
      #   unset, so the value goes to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
      # attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
      # attack-run-behavior: the value goes to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
      on:
        issues:
          types: [opened]
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                V: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
              run: |
                : "${out:=$GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
                echo "v=$V" >> "$out"
      ```
    - controlled.descriptor-per-path.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issues opened, a step opens descriptor 3 on $GITHUB_OUTPUT when
      #   QUIET is empty and on /dev/null otherwise, and writes v=$V to
      #   descriptor 3.
      # reason: QUIET is not set in the step, so bash runs the branch that
      #   opens descriptor 3 on $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the value goes to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
      # attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
      # attack-run-behavior: the value goes to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
      on:
        issues:
          types: [opened]
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                V: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
              run: |
                if [ -z "$QUIET" ]; then exec 3>>"$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else exec 3>/dev/null; fi
                echo "v=$V" >&3
      ```
    - controlled.exec-in-braces.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issues opened, a step opens descriptor 3 on $GITHUB_OUTPUT
      #   with exec inside braces, and writes body= and the issue's body to it.
      # reason: braces run in the shell itself, so the descriptor stays open
      #   after them, and the runner reads $GITHUB_OUTPUT one line at a time:
      #   each later line of the body such as x=y is read as an output of its
      #   own beside body.
      # attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
      # attack-run-behavior: BODY holds the two lines x and PWNED=1; exec inside
      #   the braces opens descriptor 3 on $GITHUB_OUTPUT for the rest of the
      #   script, so echo writes the lines body=x and PWNED=1 there, and the
      #   runner sets the outputs body (x) and PWNED (1).
      on:
        issues:
          types: [opened]
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                BODY: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
              run: |
                { exec 3>> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; }
                echo "body=$BODY" >&3
      ```
    - controlled.jump-path.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issues opened, a step sets out to /dev/null; in a for loop,
      #   the step sets out to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, leaves the loop with break when
      #   STOP is empty, and sets out to /dev/null after the break; after the
      #   loop, the step writes v= and the issue's body to "$out".
      # reason: STOP is not set in the step, so the
      #   loop ends at the break with out holding $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the body
      #   goes to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
      # attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
      # attack-run-behavior: the value goes to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
      on:
        issues:
          types: [opened]
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                V: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
              run: |
                out=/dev/null
                for i in 1 2; do out=$GITHUB_OUTPUT; [ -z "$STOP" ] && break; out=/dev/null; done
                echo "v=$V" >> "$out"
      ```
    - controlled.no-caller.action.yml (action-metadata, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a composite action with no caller among the files that the
      #   linter reads; a step writes body= and the body of an issue to
      #   $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
      # reason: with no caller among the files that the linter reads, the rule
      #   reads the action on every event an attacker triggers, issues among the
      #   events. Anyone who opens an issue writes its body, and the runner reads
      #   $GITHUB_OUTPUT one line at a time as name=value with nothing that escapes
      #   the line breaks of the body, so each later line of the body such as x=y is
      #   read as an output of its own beside body.
      # attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
      # attack-run-behavior: BODY holds the two lines x and PWNED=1, so echo
      #   writes the lines body=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the runner
      #   reads each line as name=value and sets the outputs body (x) and PWNED (1).
      #   A line approved=true in the body sets the output approved in the same way,
      #   and wins over an approved the step wrote before the line.
      name: save body
      description: give the body of the issue as an output
      runs:
        using: composite
        steps:
          - env:
              BODY: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
            run: echo "body=$BODY" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            shell: bash
      ```
    - controlled.remote-callee.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
      #   the repository example-org/output-clobbering-remote, which the fact
      #   workflow.definition answers with the workflow of the true positive
      #   controlled (controlled.default-assignment.yml) of the rule, with on:
      #   workflow_call in place of the on of controlled.default-assignment.yml.
      #   The job passes its secrets with secrets: inherit. In the true positive,
      #   on issues opened, a step sets out to $GITHUB_OUTPUT with the operator :=
      #   of a parameter expansion, and writes v=$V to "$out".
      # reason: the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event that started the
      #   run of the calling job, so the reason of the true positive holds: bash
      #   assigns $GITHUB_OUTPUT to out, which is unset, so the value goes to
      #   $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
      # attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
      # attack-run-behavior: the value goes to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
      on:
        issues:
          types: [opened]
      jobs:
        c:
          uses: example-org/output-clobbering-remote/.github/workflows/w.yml@v1
          secrets: inherit
      ```
    - controlled.skipped-assignment.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issues opened, a step sets out to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, defines a
      #   function f that sets out to /dev/null only when Q is set, calls f, and
      #   writes v= and the issue's body to "$out".
      # reason: Q is not set in the step, so f is not
      #   defined, the call fails, out holds $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the body goes to
      #   $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
      # attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
      # attack-run-behavior: the value goes to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
      on:
        issues:
          types: [opened]
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                V: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
              run: |
                out=$GITHUB_OUTPUT
                if [ -n "$Q" ]; then f() { out=/dev/null; }; fi
                f
                echo "v=$V" >> "$out"
      ```
    - controlled.status-commit.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on status, which an app outside GitHub Actions starts when the
      #   app writes a status for a commit, the job writes the message of the
      #   commit of the status (github.event.commit.commit.message) after t= into
      #   $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
      # reason: an outside CI that writes a status for a commit of a pull request
      #   from a fork starts a run of status on the default branch, with the
      #   message of that commit, which the author of the pull request writes, in
      #   the payload (seen on GitHub).
      # attack-value: github.event.commit.commit.message = "a\nPWNED=1"
      # attack-run-behavior: an outside CI writes a status for the commit of the
      #   pull request from a fork whose message is the value; the run of status
      #   starts on the default branch, echo writes the lines t=a and PWNED=1 to
      #   $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the runner sets the outputs t and PWNED of the step.
      on: status
      jobs:
        j:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: echo "t=${{ github.event.commit.commit.message }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      ```
    - controlled.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml

      # attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
      # attack-run-behavior: BODY holds the two lines x and PWNED=1, so echo writes
      #   the lines body=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the runner reads each
      #   line as name=value and sets the outputs body (x) and PWNED (1). A line
      ```

  - true negatives:
    - controlled.background-exec.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issues opened, a step runs exec 3>> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" in the
      #   background, waits for it, and writes the issue's body to
      #   descriptor 3, and goes on when the write fails (|| true).
      # reason: the background exec opens descriptor 3 in a subshell that ends
      #   with it, so the write to descriptor 3 fails and nothing reaches
      #   $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
      # attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
      # attack-run-behavior: descriptor 3 is not open when echo runs, so bash
      #   reports a bad file descriptor, || true keeps the step going, and the
      #   runner gets no output from the value.
      on:
        issues:
          types: [opened]
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                V: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
              run: |
                exec 3>> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" &
                wait
                echo "v=$V" >&3 || true
      ```
    - controlled.closed-on-each-path.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issues opened, the step s opens a descriptor on
      #   $GITHUB_OUTPUT with exec {fd} when QUIET is empty and on /dev/null
      #   otherwise, closes the descriptor whose number fd holds with exec
      #   {fd}>&-, writes v= and the issue's body to the descriptor whose number
      #   fd holds, and goes on when the write fails (|| true); the next step
      #   reads the output v.
      # reason: exec {fd}>&- closes the descriptor that exec {fd} in the branch of
      #   if opened, so the write fails on both paths, and the body does not go to
      #   $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
      # attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
      # attack-run-behavior: the write fails with a bad file descriptor, || true
      #   keeps the step going, and the runner sets no output of the step s.
      on:
        issues:
          types: [opened]
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - id: s
              env:
                V: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
              run: |
                if [ -z "$QUIET" ]; then exec {fd}>>"$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else exec {fd}>/dev/null; fi
                exec {fd}>&-
                echo "v=$V" >&$fd || true
            - env:
                W: ${{ steps.s.outputs.v }}
              run: echo "$W"
      ```
    - controlled.fork.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on fork, a step writes the description of the fork to
      #   $GITHUB_OUTPUT after the = of a line.
      # reason: GitHub refuses a line break in the description of a repository,
      #   so the value stays the value of its one line, and starts no line of a
      #   name of the attacker's.
      # attack-value: github.event.forkee.description = "x PWNED=1"
      # attack-run-behavior: the description holds no line break, so echo writes
      #   the one line d=x PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the runner sets the
      #   output d to x PWNED=1 and no PWNED.
      on: fork
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: |
                echo "d=${{ github.event.forkee.description }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      ```
    - controlled.if-guard.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on an opened issue, a step writes the issue's title to
      #   $GITHUB_OUTPUT; the step's if lets it run only when the issue's
      #   author_association is OWNER.
      # reason: the if skips the step for an issue an outsider opens, whose
      #   author_association is not OWNER, so only a title the owner wrote is
      #   written to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
      # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "x\nPWNED=1"
      # attack-run-behavior: for an issue whose author_association is not OWNER, the
      #   if is false and the step is skipped: nothing is written to $GITHUB_OUTPUT,
      #   and no PWNED is set.
      on:
        issues:
          types: [opened]
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - if: github.event.issue.author_association == 'OWNER'
              env:
                V: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
              run: echo "v=$V" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      ```
    - controlled.reassigned-file-variable.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issues opened, a step sets out to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, sets it
      #   again to /dev/null, and writes v= and the issue's body to "$out".
      # reason: the second assignment points out at /dev/null, so the body goes
      #   nowhere and no output is set.
      # attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
      # attack-run-behavior: out is /dev/null when echo runs, so the lines v=x and
      #   PWNED=1 go to /dev/null, and the runner sets no output from them.

        issues:
          types: [opened]
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                V: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
              run: |
                out=$GITHUB_OUTPUT
                out=/dev/null
                echo "v=$V" >> "$out"
      ```
    - controlled.space-cut-expansion.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml

      #   the title of the issue> to an environment file, with a parameter
      #   expansion that removes everything from the first white-space character
      #   of the title to the end; the next step reads the output host.
      # reason: the parameter expansion ${TITLE%%[[:space:]]*} removes everything
      #   from the first white-space character of the title (the class
      #   [[:space:]], which includes the line break) to the end, so the line that
      #   the step writes has no line break; the runner splits the environment
      #   file at line breaks, so the title sets only the output host.
      # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "x\nPWNED=1"
      # attack-run-behavior: the step writes the one line host=x to
      #   $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the runner sets the output host to x, and does not
      #   set an output PWNED.

          types: [opened]
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - id: s
              env:

              run: echo "host=${TITLE%%[[:space:]]*}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

                HOST: ${{ steps.s.outputs.host }}
              run: ping -c 1 "$HOST"
      ```

    - controlled.subshell-assignment.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issues opened, a step sets out to $GITHUB_OUTPUT inside

      # reason: bash runs ( ... ) in a subshell, so after the subshell out is
      #   empty, and the body does not go to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
      # attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
      ```

    - controlled.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on an opened issue, a step takes the newlines out of the
      #   issue's body (tr -d '\n') and then writes it to $GITHUB_OUTPUT as body=.
      # reason: in the written line, a newline of the issue's body is what would
      #   set another output of the step; with every newline taken out, all of it
      #   stays the value of the one line body=.
      # attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
      # attack-run-behavior: tr -d '\n' takes the line break out, so echo writes the
      #   one line body=xPWNED=1 to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the runner sets the output
      ```
