## secret-exposure

- problem: a \${{ }} reads the secrets without naming a secret, and GitHub then sends the job every secret of the repository, including the secrets that no expression of the job names, and also every secret of the environment of the job when the job references an environment (the key environment of the job)
- expected: the job names each secret it needs, secrets.NAME
- severity: high
- targets: workflow
- facets:
  - weakness: excessive-privilege
  - attack-means: none
- default run: always: in a run without --rule, the rule runs unless --skip-rule names the rule

### finding kinds

- secret-exposure.all-secrets
  - detected: {reference} reads the secrets without naming one
  - arguments:
    - {reference}: The reference as written.
  - consequence: GitHub sends the job every secret of the repository, including the secrets that no expression of the job names, and also every secret of the environment of the job when the job references an environment. The memory of the runner holds every secret that GitHub sends the job, and code that runs in a step of the job can read every secret in the memory of the runner. The harm comes from two kinds of code: an action that turns malicious, and code that an attacker writes and that a flaw of the job runs. The harm is each secret that one of the two kinds of code can read now and could not read if each job of each workflow that can read the secret named only the secrets that the job needs. In the workflows that name only the needed secrets, GitHub sends each job only the secrets that the job names, and code that runs in a job can still read every secret that the job names. An action counts in every job, of any workflow, that runs the action; the code of an attacker counts only in the jobs whose flaw runs the code of the attacker
  - remedy: name each secret the job needs, secrets.NAME, and pick one by an if for each value of the matrix rather than by a secrets&#91;...] whose name is computed
  - severity: high (found from the CVSS metrics below by the table)
  - fact kinds: repo.pull-request-target-allowed (provider: repo-setting)
  - attackers: maintainer-of-called, fork-pr-author, issue-author, commenter, anyone-who-forks
  - preconditions: nameless-reads-all, code-in-job
  - true positives:
    - all-secrets.container-env.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on push, the container of the job `build` has
      #   toJSON(secrets) in its env, under the variable ALL, and a step of the
      #   job uses the action some/build-action. The action needs no secret, and
      #   the repository has secrets, such as a deploy token.
      # reason: toJSON(secrets) reads the secrets without naming one, so GitHub
      #   sends the job every secret of the repository, and the runner starts the
      #   container with the variable ALL set to all the secrets as one JSON; the
      #   steps of the job, the action among them, run in that container.
      # attack: the maintainer of some/build-action, or one who took over the
      #   account of the maintainer, moves the tag v1 to code that reads the
      #   variable ALL and sends the value of ALL to a server of the attacker
      #   over the network.
      # attack-run-behavior: GitHub sends the job every secret of the
      #   repository, the runner starts the container with ALL set to all the
      #   secrets as one JSON, and the code of the action reads ALL in the
      #   container.
      on: push
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          container:
            image: node:20
            env:
              ALL: ${{ toJSON(secrets) }}
          steps:
            - uses: some/build-action@v1
      ```
    - all-secrets.remote-callee.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
      #   the repository example-org/secret-exposure-remote, which the fact
      #   workflow.definition answers with the workflow of the true positive
      #   all-secrets (all-secrets.container-env.yml) of the rule, with on:
      #   workflow_call in place of the on of all-secrets.container-env.yml. The
      #   job passes its secrets with secrets: inherit. In the true positive, on
      #   push, the container of the job `build` has toJSON(secrets) in its env,
      #   under the variable ALL, and a step of the job uses the action
      #   some/build-action. The action needs no secret, and the repository has
      #   secrets, such as a deploy token.
      # reason: the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event that started the
      #   run of the calling job, so the reason of the true positive holds:
      #   toJSON(secrets) reads the secrets without naming one, so GitHub sends
      #   the job every secret of the repository, and the runner starts the
      #   container with the variable ALL set to all the secrets as one JSON; the
      #   steps of the job, the action among them, run in that container.
      # attack: the maintainer of some/build-action, or one who took over the
      #   account of the maintainer, moves the tag v1 to code that reads the
      #   variable ALL and sends the value of ALL to a server of the attacker over
      #   the network.
      # attack-run-behavior: GitHub sends the job every secret of the repository,
      #   the runner starts the container with ALL set to all the secrets as one
      #   JSON, and the code of the action reads ALL in the container.
      on: push
      jobs:
        c:
          uses: example-org/secret-exposure-remote/.github/workflows/w.yml@v1
          secrets: inherit
      ```
    - all-secrets.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on pull_request_target, a job passes toJSON(secrets) to the env
      #   of a step that runs a third-party action; the action needs NPM_TOKEN
      #   only. The repository has other secrets too, such as a deploy key, that
      #   no job running the action needs.
      # reason: toJSON(secrets) reads the secrets without naming one, so GitHub
      #   sends the job every secret of the repository, not only NPM_TOKEN.
      # attack: the maintainer of some/deploy-action, or one who took over the
      #   account of the maintainer, moves the tag v1 to code that reads the env
      #   of the step and the memory of the runner and sends the secrets out.
      # attack-run-behavior: the runner gets every secret of the repository at
      #   the start of the job and puts them all, as one JSON, in the env ALL of
      #   the step; the action's code reads ALL and has every secret.
      on: pull_request_target
      jobs:
        deploy:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: some/deploy-action@v1
              env:
                ALL: ${{ toJSON(secrets) }}
                NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - .github/workflows/called.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: this reusable workflow, called.yml, puts toJSON(secrets) in the
      #   env of a step. mid.yml, a workflow that only a caller runs, calls
      #   called.yml with secrets: inherit, and the job deploy of ci.yml calls
      #   mid.yml on push and passes mid.yml only the secret DEPLOY_KEY, by name.
      #   All three files are given to the linter.
      # reason: the secrets context of mid.yml has only DEPLOY_KEY, which ci.yml
      #   passed by name; secrets: inherit in mid.yml passes called.yml only
      #   DEPLOY_KEY, so toJSON(secrets) in called.yml makes GitHub pass the
      #   runner of the job of called.yml only DEPLOY_KEY, the one secret that
      #   the job would get by naming DEPLOY_KEY.
      # attack: an action of the job of called.yml turns malicious and reads the
      #   secrets in the runner of the job.
      # attack-run-behavior: a push starts ci.yml, which runs mid.yml and then
      #   called.yml; the runner of the job of called.yml has DEPLOY_KEY and no
      #   other secret of the repository, so the action finds DEPLOY_KEY only.
      on:
        workflow_call:
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        deploy:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: ./deploy.sh
              env:
                ALL: ${{ toJSON(secrets) }}
      ```
      - .github/workflows/ci.yml (workflow)
        ```yaml
        on: push
        permissions: {}
        jobs:
          deploy:
            uses: ./.github/workflows/mid.yml
            secrets:
              DEPLOY_KEY: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_KEY }}
        ```
      - .github/workflows/mid.yml (workflow)
        ```yaml
        on:
          workflow_call:
            secrets:
              DEPLOY_KEY:
                required: true
        permissions: {}
        jobs:
          deploy:
            uses: ./.github/workflows/called.yml
            secrets: inherit
        ```
    - all-secrets.never-runs.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on push, the job whose id is disabled has if: false, and the job
      #   whose id is on-failure needs the job build and has if: needs.build.result
      #   == 'failure'; each of the two jobs puts toJSON(secrets) in the env of a
      #   step that uses some/deploy-action.
      # reason: GitHub skips the job disabled because the if of the job disabled is
      #   false. The if of the job on-failure calls no status function, so GitHub
      #   evaluates the if of the job on-failure only when the job build succeeded;
      #   needs.build.result is then success, and the if is false. When the job
      #   build fails or is skipped, GitHub skips the job on-failure without
      #   evaluating the if. So neither job runs
      #   (https://github.com/github/docs/blob/404a5f4de6cd5311e3ce2d5c076571291e0107d6/data/reusables/actions/jobs/section-using-conditions-to-control-job-execution.md).
      # attack: the maintainer of some/deploy-action, or whoever takes over an
      #   account of the maintainer, changes the action so that the action reads the
      #   env of the step.
      # attack-run-behavior: GitHub skips the job disabled and the job on-failure,
      #   so GitHub sends no secret to a runner for the job disabled or for the job
      #   on-failure.
      on: push
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: echo built
        disabled:
          if: false
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: some/deploy-action@v1
              env:
                ALL: ${{ toJSON(secrets) }}
        on-failure:
          needs: build
          if: needs.build.result == 'failure'
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: some/deploy-action@v1
              env:
                ALL: ${{ toJSON(secrets) }}
      ```
    - all-secrets.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on pull_request_target, a job passes the step of a
      #   third-party action the two secrets it needs, by name.
      # reason: secrets.NPM_TOKEN and secrets['GH_TOKEN'] name their secrets (a
      #   string literal in the brackets names one too), so GitHub sends the job
      #   only those two.
      # attack: the maintainer of some/deploy-action, or one who took over their
      #   account, moves the tag v1 to code that reads the step's env and the
      #   runner's memory and sends them out.
      # attack-run-behavior: the runner gets NPM_TOKEN and GH_TOKEN only; the
      #   action's code finds no other secret of the repository in the env or in
      #   the runner's memory.
      on: pull_request_target
      jobs:
        deploy:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: some/deploy-action@v1
              env:
                NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
                GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets['GH_TOKEN'] }}
      ```

### undetected forms

- remote-caller: a workflow that only a caller runs, whose callers in the repository all pass their secrets by name, directly or through workflows that only callers run and that call the workflow with secrets: inherit, and that a caller in another repository calls with secrets: inherit, directly or through such a workflow: that caller's every secret reaches the job, and the rule sees only the callers in the repository
  - finding kinds: secret-exposure.all-secrets
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: remote-caller)
  - example: .github/workflows/called.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a reusable workflow, run only when called, passes
    #   toJSON(secrets) to an action. ci.yml of the repository calls it passing
    #   DEPLOY_TOKEN by name; a workflow of another repository of the
    #   organization calls it with secrets: inherit.
    # reason: a limitation (decided by remote-caller): the caller in the other
    #   repository passes every secret it has, and the job's toJSON(secrets)
    #   reads them all, so GitHub sends that run's job every one.
    # cause: the rule reads the callers in the repository only, which all pass
    #   by name, and so reports nothing.
    # attack: the maintainer of some/deploy-action, or one who took over their
    #   account, moves the tag v1 to code that reads the step's env.
    # attack-run-behavior: in the run the other repository starts, the
    #   runner of the job gets every secret of that repository, and the
    #   action's code reads them in ALL.
    on:
      workflow_call:
        secrets:
          DEPLOY_TOKEN:
            required: false
    jobs:
      deploy:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: some/deploy-action@v1
            env:
              ALL: ${{ toJSON(secrets) }}
    ```
    - .github/workflows/ci.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: push
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        deploy:
          uses: ./.github/workflows/called.yml
          secrets:
            DEPLOY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
      ```
- remote-callee: a job or a step inside a reusable workflow of another repository (uses: owner/repo/.github/workflows/&lt;file>@&lt;ref>) whose content the fact workflow.definition does not give. For every rule: a run that does not ask the fact (a run without --online and without the answer in --facts). For a quality rule, also: a run where the linter asked the fact and got no answer (an answer of unknown: the GitHub API did not give the file), and a call deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact. The rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition. For a rule that is not a quality rule (a rule with a threat), the last two forms are the inconclusive kind remote-callee-unknown, not this form
  - finding kinds: secret-exposure.all-secrets
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-callee.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
    #   the repository example-org/secret-exposure-unanswered, whose content is
    #   the workflow of the true positive all-secrets
    #   (all-secrets.container-env.yml) of the rule, with on: workflow_call in
    #   place of the on of all-secrets.container-env.yml. The linter has no
    #   answer of the fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event
    #   that started the run of the calling job, and the linter does not read
    #   the reusable workflow.
    # cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from
    #   the answer of workflow.definition.
    # attack: the maintainer of some/build-action, or one who took over the
    #   account of the maintainer, moves the tag v1 to code that reads the
    #   variable ALL and sends the value of ALL to a server of the attacker over
    #   the network.
    # attack-run-behavior: GitHub sends the job every secret of the repository,
    #   the runner starts the container with ALL set to all the secrets as one
    #   JSON, and the code of the action reads ALL in the container.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/secret-exposure-unanswered/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

### inconclusive

- remote-callee-unknown: a job that calls a reusable workflow of another repository, when the linter asked the fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow and got no answer (the token that the linter uses cannot read the file, the file is larger than the limit, or the linter has used up the requests it may send to the GitHub API), or when the call is deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact: the rule does not read the jobs and the steps of the reusable workflow
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-callee-unknown.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
    #   the repository example-org/secret-exposure-unknown, whose content is the
    #   workflow of the true positive all-secrets
    #   (all-secrets.container-env.yml) of the rule, with on: workflow_call in
    #   place of the on of all-secrets.container-env.yml. The linter asked the
    #   fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow and got no answer.
    # reason: what the jobs of the reusable workflow do is in the file that the
    #   linter could not read; whoever changes the uses, such as the author of a
    #   pull request, can name a reusable workflow that the token that the
    #   linter uses cannot read.
    # attack: the maintainer of some/build-action, or one who took over the
    #   account of the maintainer, moves the tag v1 to code that reads the
    #   variable ALL and sends the value of ALL to a server of the attacker over
    #   the network.
    # attack-run-behavior: GitHub sends the job every secret of the repository,
    #   the runner starts the container with ALL set to all the secrets as one
    #   JSON, and the code of the action reads ALL in the container.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/secret-exposure-unknown/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

### false positive forms

- no-other-secret: a job in which each piece of code that runs in the job could still read each secret that GitHub sends the job, if each job of each workflow that can read the secret named only the secrets that the job needs. A piece of code is an action, which can read the secrets of every job, of any workflow, that runs the action, or code that an attacker writes, which can read the secrets of each job whose flaw runs the code of the attacker. In a job that names only the needed secrets, any piece of code that runs in the job can read every secret that the job names. The secrets are the secrets of the repository, of the organization of the repository and of the environment of the job. The observations of this rule did not check whether GitHub sends a job the secrets of the organization, so the form counts the secrets of the organization as if GitHub sends the job the secrets of the organization: counting more secrets keeps more jobs out of the form, and keeps out every job where a secret of the organization could cause the harm. Example: the jobs of a matrix that run the same steps and each pick one secret by the value of the matrix, in a repository whose only secrets are the secrets that the jobs pick. If each job of the matrix named only the secret that the job picks, the action in each job could still read the secret that the job picks, so the action could still read each of the secrets, in the job that picks the secret
  - finding kinds: secret-exposure.all-secrets
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: no-other-secret.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, the job `deploy` has a matrix with two values, DEV
    #   and PROD, and GitHub runs one job for each value. Each of the two jobs
    #   has one step, which runs the action some/deploy-action and picks a
    #   deploy token by the value of the matrix with secrets[format(...)]. The
    #   repository and the organization of the repository have no secrets but
    #   DEPLOY_TOKEN_DEV and DEPLOY_TOKEN_PROD, and the job `deploy` has no
    #   environment.
    # reason: GitHub sends each of the two jobs every secret, so the job for
    #   DEV gets DEPLOY_TOKEN_PROD too. If each job named only the token that
    #   the job picks, the job for PROD would still get DEPLOY_TOKEN_PROD and
    #   would run the same action, and the action can read every secret that
    #   the job gets, so the code of the action could still read both tokens.
    # cause: the rule does not know which secrets the repository and its
    #   organization have (a fact it does not ask), nor which secrets a step
    #   needs.
    # attack: the maintainer of some/deploy-action, or one who took over the
    #   account of the maintainer, moves the tag v1 to code that reads the
    #   memory of the runner.
    # attack-run-behavior: the runner of each job of the matrix gets
    #   DEPLOY_TOKEN_DEV and DEPLOY_TOKEN_PROD, the only secrets. The code of
    #   the action finds both tokens. If each job named the token that the job
    #   needs, the same code would still get each token, in the job that needs
    #   the token.
    on: push
    jobs:
      deploy:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        strategy:
          matrix:
            env: [DEV, PROD]
        steps:
          - uses: some/deploy-action@v1
            with:
              token: ${{ secrets[format('DEPLOY_TOKEN_{0}', matrix.env)] }}
    ```
- named-callers: a workflow that only a caller runs, whose callers are in other repositories and each passes its secrets by name: the job gets only those, which the rule does not see
  - finding kinds: secret-exposure.all-secrets
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: remote-caller)
  - example: named-callers.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a reusable workflow, run only when called, passes
    #   toJSON(secrets) to an action; it is called from other repositories,
    #   each of which passes it DEPLOY_TOKEN by name.
    # reason: the job of a called workflow gets the secrets its caller passes,
    #   so toJSON(secrets) has only DEPLOY_TOKEN.
    # cause: the callers are not among the files given to the linter, so the
    #   rule reads the worst case: a caller that passes every secret with
    #   secrets: inherit.
    # attack: the maintainer of some/deploy-action, or one who took over their
    #   account, moves the tag v1 to code that reads the step's env.
    # attack-run-behavior: each caller passes DEPLOY_TOKEN, and the runner of
    #   the called job gets it alone; the action's code finds DEPLOY_TOKEN in
    #   ALL, which the job reads anyway.
    on:
      workflow_call:
        secrets:
          DEPLOY_TOKEN:
            required: true
    jobs:
      deploy:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: some/deploy-action@v1
            env:
              ALL: ${{ toJSON(secrets) }}
    ```
- pull-request-target-blocked: a workflow whose on has pull_request_target and no other event (no workflow_call event either), in a repository whose Actions policies block the runs of the workflow on pull_request_target (repo.pull-request-target-allowed false): an event policy that an administrator sets without pull_request_target among the allowed events, or the default policy that GitHub adds to a public repository without an applicable event policy, from the time when GitHub enforces the default policy on the repository. GitHub's documents say that GitHub evaluates the policies before a run, and that a run that a policy does not allow fails with an error. The documents do not say whether a job of such a run starts before the run fails; the rule assumes that no job of such a run starts
  - finding kinds: secret-exposure.all-secrets
  - fact kinds:
    - repo.pull-request-target-allowed (provider: repo-setting, answer that removes the finding: false)
  - example: pull-request-target-blocked.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a job passes toJSON(secrets) to the env
    #   of a step that runs a third-party action; the action needs NPM_TOKEN only.
    # reason: the Actions policies of the repository block the runs of the
    #   workflow on pull_request_target: the default policy that GitHub adds to a
    #   public repository without an applicable event policy, from the time when
    #   GitHub enforces the default policy on the repository, or an event policy
    #   whose list of allowed events does not have pull_request_target. GitHub's
    #   documents say that GitHub evaluates the policies before a run, and that a
    #   run that a policy does not allow fails with an error; the documents do not
    #   say whether a job of such a run starts before the run fails, and the rule
    #   assumes that no job starts.
    # cause: unless a file of facts or --fact says that the Actions policies block
    #   runs on pull_request_target (repo.pull-request-target-allowed false), the
    #   rule reports the finding. When no file of facts and no --fact answers
    #   repo.pull-request-target-allowed, the finding is conditional.
    # attack: the maintainer of some/deploy-action, or one who took over the
    #   account of the maintainer, moves the tag v1 to code that sends out the env
    #   of the step.
    # attack-run-behavior: no pull request starts a job of the workflow: each
    #   run on pull_request_target fails with an error, and no job of the run
    #   starts (the assumption of the reason), so the runner gets no secret and
    #   the action never runs.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      deploy:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: some/deploy-action@v1
            env:
              ALL: ${{ toJSON(secrets) }}
              NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
    ```
- actions-policy: a run that the Actions policies of the repository block, in four cases where the rule does not take the policies into account. First, an event policy that blocks an event of the attackers other than pull_request_target (such as issue_comment) in a workflow whose on has that event: the rules ask a fact only for pull_request_target. Second, an actor rule that does not allow the account of the attacker (for example, an actor rule that allows only the repository roles with write access): repo.pull-request-target-allowed is one value for all the runs of a workflow file on pull_request_target, and an actor rule blocks a run by the account that starts the run, so the fact cannot tell what an actor rule blocks. Third, a workflow whose on has pull_request_target and another event: the rule does not ask repo.pull-request-target-allowed for such a workflow, because a run on the other event can reach the job. When the if of the job is false on the other event, so that the job runs only on pull_request_target, and a policy blocks pull_request_target, the finding is a false positive. Fourth, a reusable workflow (on workflow_call) or an action that only workflows on pull_request_target call: the rule asks repo.pull-request-target-allowed only of a workflow whose on has pull_request_target, not of the reusable workflow or the action, so a finding in the reusable workflow or the action is still reported when the policies block the runs of every caller
  - finding kinds: secret-exposure.all-secrets
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: actions-policy.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target and issues, a job that runs only on
    #   pull_request_target (its if) passes toJSON(secrets) to the env of a step
    #   that runs a third-party action; the action needs NPM_TOKEN only.
    # reason: the Actions policies of the repository block the runs of the
    #   workflow on pull_request_target (the default policy of GitHub for a public
    #   repository, from the time when GitHub enforces the default policy on the
    #   repository, or an event policy), and the if of the job is false on issues,
    #   so no run starts the job. GitHub's documents say that GitHub evaluates the
    #   policies before a run, and that a run that a policy does not allow fails
    #   with an error; the documents do not say whether a job of such a run starts
    #   before the run fails, and the rule assumes that no job starts.
    # cause: the on of the workflow has issues besides pull_request_target, so
    #   the rule does not ask repo.pull-request-target-allowed for the workflow.
    # attack: the maintainer of some/deploy-action, or one who took over the
    #   account of the maintainer, moves the tag v1 to code that sends out the env
    #   of the step.
    # attack-run-behavior: the run on pull_request_target fails with an error,
    #   and no job of the run starts (the assumption of the reason); on issues,
    #   the if of the job is false and the job is skipped; so the runner gets no
    #   secret and the action never runs.
    on: [pull_request_target, issues]
    jobs:
      deploy:
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request_target'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: some/deploy-action@v1
            env:
              ALL: ${{ toJSON(secrets) }}
              NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
    ```
- actions-not-allowed: a workflow whose run GitHub does not start, or a job that GitHub fails in the step "Set up job", because of the setting of allowed actions of GitHub (the fact repo.allowed-actions, which the quality rule allowed-actions reads): GitHub does not start a run of a workflow that has a uses, or that calls a reusable workflow that has a uses, that the setting does not allow, and fails a job before any step of the job runs when a step of a composite action that the job runs has a uses that the setting does not allow, or when the setting requires a full commit SHA and a step names an action by a tag or a branch. The harm that the finding reports happens only when GitHub runs the workflow or the job, and the rule does not read repo.allowed-actions
  - finding kinds: secret-exposure.all-secrets
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: actions-not-allowed.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the workflow of the true positive all-secrets (all-secrets.yml)
    #   of the rule, with a job added whose step uses
    #   example-org/not-allowed-action, which the setting of allowed actions of
    #   GitHub (repo.allowed-actions) blocks with
    #   !example-org/not-allowed-action@*. In the true positive, on
    #   pull_request_target, a job passes toJSON(secrets) to the env of a step
    #   that runs a third-party action; the action needs NPM_TOKEN only. The
    #   repository has other secrets too, such as a deploy key, that no job
    #   running the action needs.
    # reason: GitHub checks each uses of the workflow before the run starts, and
    #   does not start the run because of the uses of
    #   example-org/not-allowed-action: no job of the run runs, so what the
    #   reason of the true positive says does not happen (in runs that the
    #   authors of the rule made on GitHub, such runs ended as startup_failure).
    # cause: the rule does not read repo.allowed-actions.
    # attack: the maintainer of some/deploy-action, or one who took over the
    #   account of the maintainer, moves the tag v1 to code that reads the env
    #   of the step and the memory of the runner and sends the secrets out.
    # attack-run-behavior: GitHub does not start the run, so no step of the run
    #   runs, and the attack does nothing.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      deploy:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: some/deploy-action@v1
            env:
              ALL: ${{ toJSON(secrets) }}
              NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
      not-allowed:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: example-org/not-allowed-action@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

### threat

- precondition nameless-reads-all: GitHub sends a job's runner only the secrets the job names, and every secret of the repository when a \${{ }} of the job reads the secrets without naming one, in a step's env, run, with, name, working-directory, timeout-minutes or continue-on-error, the job's env or outputs, the env or the credentials of the job's container or of a service, or the workflow's env, even in a step whose if is false; a reusable workflow's job gets those its caller passes, all with secrets: inherit, and, when the caller writes toJSON(secrets) as the value of a key under secrets:, every secret of the caller as the value of that one key; when the caller is itself a job of a reusable workflow, secrets: inherit passes only what the caller of that reusable workflow passed, so the rule follows the callers up and does not report a finding on a read when every path of calls up from the read has at least one call that passes named secrets or no secret, in place of secrets: inherit; in a job that references an environment, GitHub sends the secrets of the environment in the same way as the secrets of the repository (observed with the env of a step), and GitHub sends no secret of an environment to a job that references no environment; the observations of this rule did not check whether GitHub sends a job the secrets of the organization, and did not check which secrets GitHub sends a job whose environment has protection rules (such as required reviewers) after a required reviewer approves the job; the rule reports a finding on a job whose environment has protection rules too, as on a job whose environment has no protection rules
  - observed: 2026-11-06, runner 2.337.0: the reusable workflows were called by ./ and by owner/repo/path@sha from the same repository, from another repository of the same organization, and two calls deep. A job of a called workflow got in its runner only the secrets that the job read by name, with secrets: inherit and with secrets passed one by one. The job got every secret that the caller passed when the job read toJSON(secrets), and a secret passed one by one that the job did not read was not in the runner of the job
  - observed: 2026-10-14, runner 2.337.0: a job that named PROBE_A masked it and printed PROBE_B as it is, and its job message had no PROBE_B; a job with toJSON(secrets), secrets&#91;format(...)] or secrets.\*, also in a step whose if is false, masked both and its message had every secret; a called job's toJSON(secrets) masked only what its caller passed, every secret with secrets: inherit; toJSON(secrets) in a step's run, with or name, the job's env or outputs, or the workflow's env masked both; a called job given toJSON(secrets) under secrets: had every secret's name in it
  - observed: 2026-10-23, runner 2.337.0: toJSON(secrets) in the env of the job's container, the env of a service, the username or the password of the container's credentials, the username of a service's credentials, or a step's working-directory, timeout-minutes or continue-on-error masked both PROBE_A and PROBE_B; with secrets.PROBE_A in the username of the credentials of the job's container and no other secret in the job, a step that echoed the values of PROBE_A and PROBE_B as literals printed the value of PROBE_A as \*\*\* and the value of PROBE_B unmasked
  - observed: 2026-10-23, runner 2.338.0: in jobs that reference the environment e: a job that named PROBE_A masked PROBE_A and not PROBE_ENV, the secret of e; a job that named PROBE_ENV masked PROBE_ENV and not PROBE_A; a job with toJSON(secrets) masked PROBE_A, PROBE_B and PROBE_ENV. A job with toJSON(secrets) that references no environment masked PROBE_A and PROBE_B and printed PROBE_ENV unmasked. Each job of a matrix whose step read secrets&#91;format('PROBE\_{0}', matrix.p)] masked PROBE_A and PROBE_B, for the value A of p and for the value B
  - cites:
    - <https://github.com/github/docs/blob/ba6f6f9b9b31c4f0a991fbcb1005080526424804/content/actions/concepts/security/secrets.md>
    - <https://github.com/github/docs/blob/ba6f6f9b9b31c4f0a991fbcb1005080526424804/content/actions/reference/security/secure-use.md>
    - <https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/reusing-workflow-configurations>
    - <https://github.com/github/docs/blob/935221fd662811fa04955b1759bf67b96b7ae028/content/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/contexts.md>
    - <https://github.com/github/docs/blob/01c4e7416d12324b53d3a4f35ea7ae01d9bbc4e6/content/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/deployments-and-environments.md>
- precondition code-in-job: code that runs in the job reads what its runner holds: an action of the job that turns malicious, as tj-actions/changed-files did, which read the runner's memory, or an attacker's code that a flaw of the job runs; the step whose env has toJSON(secrets) has them in its env
  - cites:
    - <https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mrrh-fwg8-r2c3>
    - <https://securitylab.github.com/resources/github-actions-preventing-pwn-requests/>
- actor: maintainer-of-called
  - via: pushes to an action the job uses, or takes over an account that maintains it, and has it read the runner's memory or the step's env
  - gains: read-secrets
- actor: fork-pr-author
  - via: opens or updates a pull request from a fork, which runs pull_request_target, and workflow_run after its pull_request
  - events: pull_request_target, workflow_run
  - run starters: pull_request_target: attacker, workflow_run: attacker
  - gains: read-secrets, write-with-token
- actor: issue-author
  - via: opens an issue or a discussion
  - events: issues, discussion
  - run starters: issues: attacker, discussion: attacker
  - gains: read-secrets, write-with-token
- actor: commenter
  - via: comments on an issue, a pull request or a discussion, or reviews a pull request from a branch of the repository or comments on the diff of the pull request
  - events: issue_comment, discussion_comment, pull_request_review, pull_request_review_comment
  - run starters: issue_comment: attacker, discussion_comment: attacker, pull_request_review: attacker, pull_request_review_comment: attacker
  - gains: read-secrets, write-with-token
- actor: anyone-who-forks
  - via: forks the repository
  - events: fork
  - run starters: fork: attacker
  - gains: read-secrets, write-with-token

### CVSS

#### secret-exposure.all-secrets

- vector: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:N/VA:N/SC:H/SI:H/SA:L/E:U
- CVSS-B: 9.1 (critical)
- CVSS-BT: 6.7 (medium)
- impact: H (from VC, SC, SI)
- likelihood: medium (from AV:N, AT:P, PR:N)
- severity: high (impact H, likelihood medium; the table: sisakulint --explain=terms)
- AV: N
  - reason: the attacker pushes to an action the job uses, or reaches a flaw of the job, over the network
  - cites: none
- AC: L
  - reason: once their code runs in the job, every secret is in it
  - cites: none
- AT: P
  - reason: the attacker's code has to run in the job: an action of it turns malicious, or a flaw runs it there
  - cites: none
- PR: N
  - reason: on a public repository anyone opens an issue or a pull request from a fork
  - cites: none
- UI: N
  - reason: the job runs on its events with nobody doing anything
  - cites: none
- VC: H
  - reason: the attacker reads the secrets that the code of the attacker could not read if each job named only the secrets that the job needs, up to every secret of the repository
  - cites: none
- VI: N
  - reason: the secrets do not write to the repository as such
  - cites: none
- VA: N
  - reason: the secrets do not act on the repository as such
  - cites: none
- SC: H
  - reason: the secrets open what is past the job: clouds, registries, other repositories
  - cites: none
- SI: H
  - reason: they write what the secrets may: deployments, packages
  - cites: none
- SA: L
  - reason: they can delete what the secrets may
  - cites: none
- E: U
  - reason: no report was found of secrets taken from a job because it read toJSON(secrets) or secrets&#91;...] (searched 2026-10-14)
  - cites: none

## secret-in-log

- problem: a value the shell made from a secret is printed to the log of the run; the runner registers the secret, each line of the secret and encoded forms of the secret such as the base64 of the secret, and masks only those strings
- expected: either no value made from a secret is printed, or each line of a value made from a secret is registered with ::add-mask:: before the value is printed
- severity: critical (the worst of its kinds)
- targets: workflow, action-metadata
- facets:
  - weakness: credential-leak
  - attack-means: none
- default run: always: in a run without --rule, the rule runs unless --skip-rule names the rule

### finding kinds

- secret-in-log.private
  - detected: {transform} makes a value from the secret {secret}, and the value is printed in {place}
  - arguments:
    - {transform}: How the shell made the value from the secret: the operator of a parameter expansion (substring, prefix-removal, suffix-removal, replacement, case-change, expansion), or the command (jq, base64 and the like).
    - {secret}: The name of the secret, in upper case; GITHUB_TOKEN for the job's token.
    - {place}: The place where the run prints the value: the output of the step, the job summary, the trace that set -x or the -x option in the shell: value of the step turns on, the env in the header of each later step (\$GITHUB_ENV), or the header of the step. Those who can read the log of the run can read each of the places; the job summary is on the page of the run, apart from the log.
  - consequence: the runner registers the secret, each line of the secret and encoded forms of the secret such as the base64 of the secret, and masks only those strings, not a value the shell makes from the secret: whoever has read access to the repository reads the value in the log; the log of the run is kept for 90 days by default
  - remedy: do not print the value; if the value must be printed, register each line of the value with ::add-mask:: before the value is printed; delete the logs of the runs that printed the value, and rotate the secret
  - severity: high (found from the CVSS metrics below by the table)
  - fact kinds: repo.public (provider: repo-setting)
  - attackers: log-reader
  - preconditions: derived-unmasked, printed-places, mask-after, readable-log
  - true positives:
    - private.remote-callee.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
      #   the repository example-org/secret-in-log-remote, which the fact
      #   workflow.definition answers with the workflow of the true positive
      #   private (private.yml) of the rule, with on: workflow_call in place of
      #   the on of private.yml. The job passes its secrets with secrets: inherit.
      #   In the true positive, on push, in a private repository (repo.public
      #   answered false), a step prints the first characters of the secret
      #   DEPLOY_TOKEN to check which token is set.
      # reason: the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event that started the
      #   run of the calling job, so the reason of the true positive holds: the
      #   runner masks DEPLOY_TOKEN where the whole token is in the log, not a
      #   substring of the token, so the first eight characters of the token are
      #   in the log as they are.
      # attack: one with read access to the repository opens the run's log and
      #   reads the first characters of the token.
      # attack-run-behavior: the step prints "token starts with" and eight
      #   characters of the token; the log keeps them for 90 days by default.
      on: push
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        c:
          uses: example-org/secret-in-log-remote/.github/workflows/w.yml@v1
          secrets: inherit
      ```
    - private.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on push, in a private repository (repo.public answered false),
      #   a step prints the first characters of the secret DEPLOY_TOKEN to check
      #   which token is set.
      # reason: the runner masks DEPLOY_TOKEN where the whole token is in the log,
      #   not a substring of the token, so the first eight characters of the token
      #   are in the log as they are.
      # attack: one with read access to the repository opens the run's log and
      #   reads the first characters of the token.
      # attack-run-behavior: the step prints "token starts with" and eight
      #   characters of the token; the log keeps them for 90 days by default.
      on: push
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        check:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                DEPLOY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
              run: echo "token starts with ${DEPLOY_TOKEN:0:8}"
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - private+public.append-earlier-value.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on push, in a public repository (repo.public true), a step sets
      #   fd to 1, appends 1 to fd, and prints the private key out of the secret
      #   GCP_SA_KEY to the descriptor whose number fd holds.
      # reason: fd holds 11 at the print, and bash writes the print to descriptor
      #   11, which the step does not open, so the log has no part of the secret.
      # attack: anyone signed in to GitHub opens the run's log and reads the
      #   private key.
      # attack-run-behavior: the print fails with a bad file descriptor, and the
      #   log has no part of the secret.
      on: push
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        deploy:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                GCP_SA_KEY: ${{ secrets.GCP_SA_KEY }}
              run: |
                fd=1
                fd+=1
                echo "key: $(echo "$GCP_SA_KEY" | jq -r '.private_key')" >&$fd || true
      ```
    - private+public.call-descriptor.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on push, in a public repository (repo.public true), a step opens
      #   file descriptor 3 to /dev/null, defines a function f that prints the
      #   secret DEPLOY_TOKEN without the first character of the secret to the file
      #   descriptor whose number fd holds, and calls f twice: once with fd=1 and
      #   the standard output of the call sent to /dev/null, and once with fd=3.
      # reason: at each call the print goes to /dev/null, so the step prints no
      #   part of the secret.
      # attack: anyone who can read the run opens the log of the run and reads
      #   the secret.
      # attack-run-behavior: the step prints nothing.
      on: push
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        deploy:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                DEPLOY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
              run: |
                exec 3>/dev/null
                f() { echo "token: ${DEPLOY_TOKEN:1}" >&"$fd"; }
                fd=1; f >/dev/null
                fd=3; f
      ```
    - private+public.closed-on-each-path.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on push, in a public repository (repo.public true), a step opens
      #   a descriptor on the standard error with exec {fd} when QUIET is empty and
      #   on /dev/null otherwise, closes the descriptor whose number fd holds with
      #   exec {fd}>&-, and prints the private key out of the secret GCP_SA_KEY to
      #   the descriptor whose number fd holds.
      # reason: exec {fd}>&- closes the descriptor that exec {fd} in the branch of
      #   if opened, so the print fails on both paths, and the log has no part of
      #   the secret.
      # attack: anyone signed in to GitHub opens the run's log and reads the
      #   private key.
      # attack-run-behavior: the print fails with a bad file descriptor, and the
      #   log has no part of the secret.
      on: push
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        deploy:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                GCP_SA_KEY: ${{ secrets.GCP_SA_KEY }}
              run: |
                if [ -z "$QUIET" ]; then exec {fd}>&2; else exec {fd}>/dev/null; fi
                exec {fd}>&-
                echo "key: $(echo "$GCP_SA_KEY" | jq -r '.private_key')" >&$fd || true
      ```
    - private+public.exec-in-substitution.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on push, in a public repository (repo.public true), a step sets x
      #   to the output of a $( ) in which exec points the standard output to
      #   /dev/null and then an echo prints the secret GCP_SA_KEY without the first
      #   character of the secret, and prints x.
      # reason: the exec sends the print in the $( ) to /dev/null, so x is empty,
      #   and the log has no part of the secret.
      # attack: anyone signed in to GitHub opens the run's log and reads the
      #   secret.
      # attack-run-behavior: the step prints "key:" and nothing of the secret.
      on: push
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        deploy:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                GCP_SA_KEY: ${{ secrets.GCP_SA_KEY }}
              run: |
                x=$(exec >/dev/null; echo "${GCP_SA_KEY:1}")
                echo "key: $x"
      ```
    - private+public.failing-redirect.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on push, in a public repository (repo.public true), a step sets X
      #   to safe, then assigns the secret DEPLOY_TOKEN without the first character
      #   of the secret to X in a compound command whose redirect copies file
      #   descriptor 9, which is not open, goes on when the compound command fails
      #   (|| true), and prints X.
      # reason: the copy of file descriptor 9 fails, so bash does not run the
      #   compound command, X keeps safe, and the step prints no part of the
      #   secret.
      # attack: anyone who can read the run opens the log of the run and reads
      #   the secret.
      # attack-run-behavior: the step prints "token: safe".
      on: push
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        deploy:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                DEPLOY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
              run: |
                X=safe
                { X="${DEPLOY_TOKEN:1}"; } 3>&9 || true
                echo "token: $X"
      ```
    - private+public.return-in-substitution.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on push, in a public repository (repo.public true), a step
      #   defines a function f that sets x to the output of a $( ) that runs return
      #   and then prints the secret GCP_SA_KEY without its first character, and
      #   prints x; the step calls f.
      # reason: return ends the commands of the $( ), so the print in the $( )
      #   does not run, x is empty, and the log has no part of the secret.
      # attack: anyone signed in to GitHub opens the run's log and reads the
      #   secret.
      # attack-run-behavior: the step prints "key:" and nothing of the secret.
      on: push
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        deploy:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                GCP_SA_KEY: ${{ secrets.GCP_SA_KEY }}
              run: |
                f() { x=$(return; echo "${GCP_SA_KEY:1}"); echo "key: $x"; }
                f
      ```
    - private+public.subshell-assignment.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on push, in a public repository, a step sets t to the secret
      #   TOKEN without its first character inside ( ... ), and after the ( ... )
      #   prints t.
      # reason: bash runs ( ... ) in a subshell, so after the subshell t is empty,
      #   and echo prints nothing of the secret.
      # attack: anyone opens the run's log.
      # attack-run-behavior: the log has the line t= alone.
      on: push
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                S: ${{ secrets.TOKEN }}
              run: |
                ( t=${S:1} )
                echo "t=$t"
      ```
    - private+public.subshell-function.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on push, in a public repository, a step defines the function f,
      #   which prints t, inside ( ... ), then sets t to the secret TOKEN without
      #   its first character, and calls f.
      # reason: bash runs ( ... ) in a subshell, so after the subshell f is not
      #   defined, and the call of f prints nothing of the secret.
      # attack: anyone opens the run's log.
      # attack-run-behavior: the call of f fails with f: command not found, and the
      #   log has the line t= alone from the call inside ( ... ).
      on: push
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                S: ${{ secrets.TOKEN }}
              run: |
                ( f() { echo "t=$t"; }; f )
                t=${S:1}
                f
      ```
    - private+public.subshell-pipeline.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on push, in a public repository, a step sets t to the secret
      #   TOKEN without its first character in the first command of a pipeline,
      #   and after the pipeline prints t.
      # reason: bash runs each command of a pipeline of more than one command in
      #   a subshell, so after the pipeline t is empty, and echo prints nothing of
      #   the secret.
      # attack: anyone opens the run's log.
      # attack-run-behavior: the log has the line t= alone.
      on: push
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                S: ${{ secrets.TOKEN }}
              run: |
                { t=${S:1}; } | cat
                echo "t=$t"
      ```
    - private.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on push, in a private repository (repo.public answered false),
      #   a step takes the password out of the JSON secret DB, registers the
      #   password with ::add-mask:: and prints the password after.
      # reason: the runner masks a value from the line after its ::add-mask::
      #   on, so the password is printed as ***.
      # attack: one with read access to the repository opens the run's log to
      #   read the password.
      # attack-run-behavior: the line of ::add-mask:: is not printed, and the step
      #   prints "password: ***".
      on: push
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        migrate:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                DB: ${{ secrets.DB }}
              run: |
                PASSWORD=$(jq -r .password <<< "$DB")
                echo "::add-mask::$PASSWORD"
                echo "password: $PASSWORD"
      ```
- secret-in-log.public
  - detected: {transform} makes a value from the secret {secret}, and the value is printed in {place}
  - arguments:
    - {transform}: How the shell made the value from the secret: the operator of a parameter expansion (substring, prefix-removal, suffix-removal, replacement, case-change, expansion), or the command (jq, base64 and the like).
    - {secret}: The name of the secret, in upper case; GITHUB_TOKEN for the job's token.
    - {place}: The place where the run prints the value: the output of the step, the job summary, the trace that set -x or the -x option in the shell: value of the step turns on, the env in the header of each later step (\$GITHUB_ENV), or the header of the step. Those who can read the log of the run can read each of the places; the job summary is on the page of the run, apart from the log.
  - consequence: the runner registers the secret, each line of the secret and encoded forms of the secret such as the base64 of the secret, and masks only those strings, not a value the shell makes from the secret: anyone signed in to GitHub reads the value in the log; the log of the run is kept for 90 days by default
  - remedy: do not print the value; if the value must be printed, register each line of the value with ::add-mask:: before the value is printed; delete the logs of the runs that printed the value, and rotate the secret
  - severity: critical (found from the CVSS metrics below by the table)
  - fact kinds: repo.public (provider: repo-setting)
  - attackers: log-reader
  - preconditions: derived-unmasked, printed-places, mask-after, readable-log
  - true positives:
    - public.append-value.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on push, in a public repository (repo.public true), a step sets
      #   KEY to the private key out of the secret GCP_SA_KEY, appends a suffix to
      #   KEY with KEY+=, and prints KEY.
      # reason: KEY+= keeps the value of KEY before it and adds the suffix after
      #   it, so the print writes the private key to the log, and the runner does
      #   not mask the private key.
      # attack: anyone signed in to GitHub opens the run's log and reads the
      #   private key.
      # attack-run-behavior: the step prints the private key and the suffix.
      on: push
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        deploy:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                GCP_SA_KEY: ${{ secrets.GCP_SA_KEY }}
              run: |
                KEY="$(echo "$GCP_SA_KEY" | jq -r '.private_key')"
                KEY+=" (end)"
                echo "key: $KEY"
      ```
    - public.custom-shell-xtrace.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on push, in a public repository (repo.public true), a step whose
      #   shell: is bash -x {0} assigns a substring of the secret TOKEN.
      # reason: bash -x starts the script with the trace on, as set -x does, so
      #   the trace prints the assignment with the substring, which the runner
      #   does not mask.
      # attack: anyone signed in to GitHub opens the run's log and reads the
      #   substring in the trace.
      # attack-run-behavior: the trace prints "+ PREFIX=" and the substring; the
      #   log keeps the substring for 90 days by default.
      on: push
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        check:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - shell: bash -x {0}
              env:
                TOKEN: ${{ secrets.TOKEN }}
              run: PREFIX=${TOKEN:0:12}
      ```
    - public.default-assignment.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on push, in a public repository (repo.public true), a step sets a
      #   variable to the private key out of the secret GCP_SA_KEY with the operator
      #   := of a parameter expansion, and prints the variable.
      # reason: bash assigns the private key to the
      #   variable, which is unset, and the runner does not mask the private key.
      # attack: anyone signed in to GitHub opens the run's log and reads the
      #   private key.
      # attack-run-behavior: the step prints "key:" and the private key.
      on: push
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        deploy:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                GCP_SA_KEY: ${{ secrets.GCP_SA_KEY }}
              run: |
                : "${PRIVATE_KEY:=$(echo "$GCP_SA_KEY" | jq -r '.private_key')}"
                echo "key: $PRIVATE_KEY"
      ```
    - public.descriptor-not-literal.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml

      #   PRIVATE_KEY to the private key out of the secret GCP_SA_KEY, sets fd to
      #   the output of echo 2, and prints PRIVATE_KEY with >&$fd.
      # reason: bash duplicates the descriptor 2, the standard error, so the
      #   private key goes to the log, and the runner does not mask the private
      #   key.
      # attack: anyone signed in to GitHub opens the run's log and reads the
      #   private key.
      # attack-run-behavior: the step prints "key:" and the private key on the
      #   standard error.

      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        deploy:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest

            - env:
                GCP_SA_KEY: ${{ secrets.GCP_SA_KEY }}
              run: |
                PRIVATE_KEY="$(echo "$GCP_SA_KEY" | jq -r '.private_key')"
                fd=$(echo 2)
                echo "key: $PRIVATE_KEY" >&$fd
      ```

      ```yaml
            - env:
      ```

      ```yaml
      # attack: anyone signed in to GitHub opens the run's log and reads the private
      ```

      ```yaml
      # situation: on push, in a public repository (repo.public true), a step points
      ```

      ```yaml
      #   error with exec after && when VERBOSE is empty, and prints the private key
      ```
