      ```yaml
              run: |
                echo "key: $API_KEY"
                STATUS=$(curl -fsS -H "x-api-key: $API_KEY" https://api.example.com/status)
                echo "status: $STATUS"
      ```

### undetected forms

- lastpipe-not-literal: an assignment or an exec in the last command of a pipeline after a shopt -s lastpipe whose option name the script does not write as a literal word (shopt -s "\$o"): bash runs the last command of the pipeline in the shell that runs the pipeline, so the assignment or the exec stays after the pipeline, and the rule reads the last command as a command in a subshell
  - finding kinds: secret-in-log.private, secret-in-log.public
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: lastpipe-not-literal.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, in a public repository (repo.public true), a step turns
    #   lastpipe on with shopt -s and the option name in a variable, takes the
    #   private key out of the secret GCP_SA_KEY with jq into a variable in the
    #   last command of a pipeline, and prints the variable.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): with lastpipe, bash runs the last command
    #   of the pipeline in the shell that runs the pipeline, so the variable
    #   holds the private key when echo runs, and the runner does not mask it.
    # cause: the rule follows lastpipe only after shopt -s lastpipe written as
    #   literal words, and reads the last command as a command in a subshell.
    # attack: anyone signed in to GitHub opens the run's log and reads the
    #   private key.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step prints "key:" and the private key.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      deploy:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              GCP_SA_KEY: ${{ secrets.GCP_SA_KEY }}
            run: |
              o=lastpipe
              shopt -s "$o"
              true | PRIVATE_KEY=$(echo "$GCP_SA_KEY" | jq -r '.private_key')
              echo "key: $PRIVATE_KEY"
    ```
- name-not-literal: an assignment whose variable name the script does not write as a literal word (n=key; declare "\$n=\$X"; or read -r "\$n"): bash assigns the word after = (with declare) or the line that read reads (with read) to the variable whose name is the value of n, and the rule does not read the assignment
  - finding kinds: secret-in-log.private, secret-in-log.public
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: name-not-literal.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, in a public repository (repo.public true), a step sets n
    #   to the name PRIVATE_KEY, assigns the private key out of the secret
    #   GCP_SA_KEY to the variable that n names with declare, and prints
    #   PRIVATE_KEY.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): bash assigns the private key to
    #   PRIVATE_KEY, and the runner does not mask the private key.
    # cause: the variable name of the assignment is not a literal word, so the
    #   rule does not read the assignment.
    # attack: anyone signed in to GitHub opens the run's log and reads the
    #   private key.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step prints "key:" and the private key.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      deploy:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              GCP_SA_KEY: ${{ secrets.GCP_SA_KEY }}
            run: |
              n=PRIVATE_KEY
              declare "$n=$(echo "$GCP_SA_KEY" | jq -r '.private_key')"
              echo "key: $PRIVATE_KEY"
    ```
- recursive-unset-local: a variable that a shell function unsets inside a recursive call of a function, where a function between the two calls made the variable local (f() { if &#91; -z "\$inner" ]; then inner=1; h; else g; fi; }; h() { s=x; local s=y; f; }; g() { unset s; }): bash takes away the local of the nearest calling function that made the variable local, and the variable then holds the value from before the nearest calling function made the variable local; the rule reads the recursive call where the first call of the function runs, without the calls in between, and does not read the value that the unset reveals
  - finding kinds: secret-in-log.private, secret-in-log.public
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: recursive-unset-local.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, in a public repository (repo.public true), a step
    #   defines f, which calls h on the first call of f and calls g on the second
    #   call of f; h sets s to the secret DEPLOY_TOKEN without the first character
    #   of the secret, makes s local with safe, and calls f. g unsets s and prints
    #   "token: " and $s.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): in the second call of f, the unset in g
    #   takes away the local that h made, and s holds the value that h set before
    #   h made s local: the token without the first character, which the runner
    #   does not mask.
    # cause: the rule reads the second call of f, which f makes through h, where
    #   the first call of f runs, without the call of h, so the rule does not read
    #   the value that the unset reveals.
    # attack: anyone who can read the run opens the log of the run and reads
    #   the token without the first character.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step prints "token: " and the token without the
    #   first character.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      deploy:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              DEPLOY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
            run: |
              f() { if [ -z "$inner" ]; then inner=1; h; else g; fi; }
              g() { unset s; echo "token: $s"; }
              h() { s="${DEPLOY_TOKEN:1}"; local s=safe; f; }
              f
    ```
- unset-caller-local: a variable that a shell function unsets after a calling function made the variable local, when an assignment to the variable or a second unset of the variable follows the unset (s=x; reset() { unset s; }; point() { local s=y; reset; s=z; }; point): bash takes away the local of the calling function, so that the assignment after the unset sets the variable outside the calling function, and a second unset takes away the local of the next calling function or unsets the variable outside the functions; the rule keeps the local of the calling function after the unset, gives the variable back the value from before the calling function made the variable local when the calling function returns, and reads the second unset as the first unset
  - finding kinds: secret-in-log.private, secret-in-log.public
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: unset-caller-local.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, in a public repository (repo.public true), a step sets s
    #   to x and defines reset, which unsets s; point makes s local with safe,
    #   calls reset, and sets s to the secret DEPLOY_TOKEN without the first
    #   character of the secret. The step calls point and then prints "token: "
    #   and $s.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the unset in reset takes away the local that
    #   point made, so the assignment in point after reset sets the s of the step:
    #   the token without the first character, which the runner does not mask.
    # cause: the rule keeps the local of point after the unset in reset, and gives
    #   s back x when point returns, so the rule does not read the value that
    #   point set after reset.
    # attack: anyone who can read the run opens the log of the run and reads
    #   the token without the first character.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step prints "token: " and the token without the
    #   first character.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      deploy:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              DEPLOY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
            run: |
              s=x
              reset() { unset s; }
              point() { local s=safe; reset; s="${DEPLOY_TOKEN:1}"; }
              point
              echo "token: $s"
    ```
- split-env-name: a variable named by the part of a key of env before the first =, such as A for the key A=B, which the runner sets to the rest of the key, =, and the value (in a step in a job's container, to the rest of the key alone): the rule reads a variable of env by a key equal to the name of the variable
  - finding kinds: secret-in-log.private, secret-in-log.public
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: split-env-name.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step has the env key T=X with the secret DEPLOY_TOKEN,
    #   and prints the first 8 characters of $T.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the runner sets the variable T to X= and
    #   the secret, and the 6 characters of the secret in what the step prints
    #   are a part of the secret, which the runner does not mask.
    # cause: the rule reads a variable of env by a key equal to its name, and
    #   no key is T.
    # attack: one who may read the run's log reads the first characters of the
    #   secret.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step prints X= and the first 6 characters of
    #   DEPLOY_TOKEN.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              T=X: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
            run: echo "${T:0:8}"
    ```
- secret-input: a secret that a step of an action reads by inputs.&lt;name>, either because a caller among the files that the linter reads gives the secret under with:, or because the default of inputs.&lt;name> is \${{ github.token }}: the rule does not follow the value under with: into inputs.&lt;name> and does not read the default of inputs.&lt;name>; when no caller of the action is among the files that the linter reads, whether inputs.&lt;name> holds a secret is not known
  - finding kinds: secret-in-log.private, secret-in-log.public
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - example: called/action.yml (action-metadata, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the composite action gets the JSON key of a service account as
    #   inputs.key, takes the private key out with jq and prints the private key;
    #   ci.yml calls the action on push and gives the secret GCP_SA_KEY as key
    #   under with:.
    # reason: a todo (a file of the repository): the runner masks the whole JSON
    #   where the whole JSON is in the log, not the private key that jq extracts
    #   from the JSON, so the private key is in the log as the private key is.
    # cause: the rule does not follow the value under with: of the caller into
    #   inputs.key of the action, so the rule does not know that inputs.key holds
    #   a secret.
    # attack: anyone who may read the log of the run opens the log and reads the
    #   private key.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step prints "key:" and the private key; the log
    #   keeps the private key for 90 days by default.
    name: deploy
    description: deploy with the key
    inputs:
      key:
        description: the JSON key of the service account
    runs:
      using: composite
      steps:
        - env:
            GCP_SA_KEY: ${{ inputs.key }}
          run: |
            PRIVATE_KEY=$(echo "$GCP_SA_KEY" | jq -r '.private_key')
            echo "key: $PRIVATE_KEY"
          shell: bash
    ```
    - .github/workflows/ci.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: push
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        deploy:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2
            - uses: ./called
              with:
                key: ${{ secrets.GCP_SA_KEY }}
      ```
- extracted: a value fromJSON takes out of a secret in a \${{ }}, and a value the shell makes from that value: the header of the step prints the value first
  - finding kinds: secret-in-log.private, secret-in-log.public
  - disposition: other-rule (rule: unmasked-secret-exposure)
  - example: extracted.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step takes the password out of the JSON secret DB
    #   with fromJSON in its env, and prints the password.
    # reason: other-rule: the header of the step prints the env with the
    #   password before the script runs, which unmasked-secret-exposure reports.
    # cause: secret-in-log reads a value the shell makes, not one a ${{ }}
    #   takes out.
    # attack: one who may read the run's log opens the log and reads the
    #   password in the header of the step.
    # attack-run-behavior: the header prints PASSWORD with the password, and the
    #   step prints the password again.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      migrate:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              PASSWORD: ${{ fromJSON(secrets.DB).password }}
            run: |
              echo "password: $PASSWORD"
    ```
- other-command: a value printed by a command that the table of commands built into this linter does not declare to write a value made from its input, such as awk, a python -c or a command line of a service: the rule does not know whether the command writes what it reads
  - finding kinds: secret-in-log.private, secret-in-log.public
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: other-command.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step takes the second field of the secret CREDS with
    #   awk and prints the field.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): awk writes the field of the secret, which
    #   the runner does not mask.
    # cause: the commands table does not declare awk to write a value made from
    #   its input, so the rule does not know what awk prints.
    # attack: one who may read the run's log opens the log and reads the field.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step prints the field of CREDS as it is.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      check:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              CREDS: ${{ secrets.CREDS }}
            run: |
              echo "$CREDS" | awk -F: '{print $2}'
    ```
- debug-if: a value that the shell makes from a secret and writes to an output of a step, which the if of a later step reads: a rerun with debug logging prints, in the log of the run, the values that the if evaluates; a credential with read access to the repository can open the log, and a credential whose only write access is to the permission Actions can start the rerun; on 2026-10-23 a rerun with debug logging printed the values that the if of a step evaluated, in the lines ##&#91;debug]Evaluating and ##&#91;debug]Expanded. In the workflow file, the rule reads the commands of a run script that print to the log, and not the if of a step
  - finding kinds: secret-in-log.private, secret-in-log.public
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: debug-if.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, the step c writes the value user, which jq takes out
    #   of the secret CONFIG, to its output user, and the if of the next step
    #   compares steps.c.outputs.user with an empty string.
    # reason: a rerun with debug logging prints the values that the if
    #   evaluates, and the runner does not mask the value that jq takes out of a
    #   secret; a credential whose only write access is to the permission
    #   Actions can start the rerun, and the credential premise keeps the holder
    #   of such a credential as a possible attacker.
    # cause: in the workflow file, the rule reads the commands of a run script
    #   that print to the log, and not the if that reads an output of a step.
    # attack: the attacker reruns the run with debug logging, with a credential
    #   whose only write access is to the permission Actions, and reads the log
    #   of the rerun.
    # attack-run-behavior: on 2026-10-23, a rerun with debug logging printed the
    #   values that the if of a step evaluated in the lines ##[debug]Evaluating
    #   and ##[debug]Expanded; here the line ##[debug]Expanded would have the
    #   value user of the secret CONFIG.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      deploy:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: c
            env:
              CONFIG: ${{ secrets.CONFIG }}
            run: echo "user=$(jq -r .user <<< "$CONFIG")" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          - if: ${{ steps.c.outputs.user != '' }}
            run: ./deploy.sh
    ```
- file: a value made from a secret written to a file and printed from the file
  - finding kinds: secret-in-log.private, secret-in-log.public
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: file.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step writes the base64 of the secret SIGNING_KEY to
    #   a file and prints the file.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the base64 with its line break is not a
    #   form the runner registers, and cat prints the base64.
    # cause: the rule does not follow a value through a file.
    # attack: one who may read the run's log opens the log and decodes the
    #   base64.
    # attack-run-behavior: cat prints the base64 of the key as it is.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      sign:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.SIGNING_KEY }}
            run: |
              echo "$SIGNING_KEY" | base64 > key.b64
              cat key.b64
    ```
- called-outputs: a value made from a secret in an output of a called workflow or a called action, printed by the caller
  - finding kinds: secret-in-log.private, secret-in-log.public
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - example: .github/workflows/called.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the workflow is called by caller.yml on push; the workflow
    #   outputs a substring of the secret TOKEN, and a job of caller.yml after
    #   the call prints the output.
    # reason: a todo (a file of the repository): the header of the step prints the
    #   substring, which the runner does not mask.
    # cause: the rule does not read the outputs of a called workflow.
    # attack: one who may read the run's log opens the log and reads the
    #   substring.
    # attack-run-behavior: the header of the step of show prints the substring
    #   of TOKEN as it is.
    on:
      workflow_call:
        outputs:
          prefix:
            value: ${{ jobs.cut.outputs.prefix }}
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      cut:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        outputs:
          prefix: ${{ steps.p.outputs.prefix }}
        steps:
          - id: p
            env:
              TOKEN: ${{ secrets.TOKEN }}
            run: echo "prefix=${TOKEN:0:12}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    ```
    - .github/workflows/caller.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: push
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        make:
          uses: ./.github/workflows/called.yml
          secrets: inherit
        show:
          needs: make
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: echo "${{ needs.make.outputs.prefix }}"
      ```
- multi-line-mask: a value of more than one line that the script registers with ::add-mask:: and one variable (not a secret of the secrets context): ::add-mask:: registers the first line of the value alone, and the echo of ::add-mask:: prints the lines after the first, which stay unmasked; the rule takes the value as masked, as the rule does not know how many lines the value has
  - finding kinds: secret-in-log.private, secret-in-log.public
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: multi-line-mask.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step takes the private key of more than one line out
    #   of the JSON secret GCP_SA_KEY with jq, registers the private key with
    #   ::add-mask:: and prints the private key.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the runner reads the line of ::add-mask::
    #   and registers its first line only; the echo of ::add-mask:: prints the
    #   lines after the first, and the last echo prints those lines again.
    # cause: the rule takes a value registered with ::add-mask:: as masked, as
    #   the rule does not know how many lines the value has.
    # attack: one who may read the run's log opens the log and reads the lines
    #   of the private key after the first.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step prints the lines of the private key after
    #   the first, twice.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      deploy:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              GCP_SA_KEY: ${{ secrets.GCP_SA_KEY }}
            run: |
              PRIVATE_KEY=$(jq -r .private_key <<< "$GCP_SA_KEY")
              echo "::add-mask::$PRIVATE_KEY"
              echo "$PRIVATE_KEY"
    ```
- whole-context: a value made from toJSON(secrets): the value may be a registered secret, a part of one, or the JSON around the secrets, which the rule does not tell apart
  - finding kinds: secret-in-log.private, secret-in-log.public
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: whole-context.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step puts toJSON(secrets) in its env and prints the
    #   names of the secrets with jq.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the names are not masked, and a value jq
    #   takes out may be a secret, a part of one, or the JSON around them.
    # cause: the rule does not tell apart what jq takes out of the whole secrets
    #   context.
    # attack: one who may read the run's log opens the log and reads what jq
    #   printed.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step prints the names of the secrets of the job.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      list:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              ALL: ${{ toJSON(secrets) }}
            run: echo "$ALL" | jq -r 'keys[]'
    ```
- other-shell: a run of a shell that is not bash or sh, of bash or sh with an option that the rule does not read, such as bash -v {0}, or of bash or sh named by a path, such as /bin/bash -x {0}, on a runner where the rule does not know that the path exists or in a step of a composite action
  - finding kinds: secret-in-log.private, secret-in-log.public
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: other-shell.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a run of pwsh prints the first twelve characters of
    #   the secret TOKEN.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): Substring prints a part of the token,
    #   which the runner does not mask.
    # cause: the rule reads runs of bash and sh only.
    # attack: one who may read the run's log opens the log and reads the
    #   twelve characters.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step prints "token: " and twelve characters of
    #   the token.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      check:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - shell: pwsh
            env:
              TOKEN: ${{ secrets.TOKEN }}
            run: |
              Write-Output "token: $($env:TOKEN.Substring(0, 12))"
    ```
- shell-form: a form of the shell the rule does not read as a change of the value: printf with a precision (%.4s), an expansion of an array (\${A&#91;@]:0:4}), what a descriptor that exec points at the log prints (exec 3>&1 and >&3), and a function called twice with an assignment between the calls
  - finding kinds: secret-in-log.private, secret-in-log.public
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: shell-form.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step prints the first four characters of the
    #   secret DEPLOY_TOKEN with printf and a precision.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): printf %.4s prints four characters of the
    #   token, which the runner does not mask.
    # cause: the rule reads printf of %s as the value as it is, which the runner
    #   masks, not a precision that cuts the value.
    # attack: one who may read the run's log opens the log and reads the four
    #   characters.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step prints "token: " and four characters of the
    #   token.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      check:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              DEPLOY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
            run: |
              printf 'token: %.4s\n' "$DEPLOY_TOKEN"
    ```
- process-substitution: what a step prints after exec sends the output to a process substitution (exec > >(tee -a build.log)), or what a redirect to a process substitution prints: tee in the process substitution writes the output to the log
  - finding kinds: secret-in-log.private, secret-in-log.public
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: process-substitution.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step sends what it prints through a process
    #   substitution to tee, and then prints four characters of the secret
    #   DEPLOY_TOKEN.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): tee writes what the step prints both to
    #   build.log and to the log, and the runner does not mask the four
    #   characters.
    # cause: the rule does not take a process substitution (>(tee ...)), to
    #   which exec or a redirect sends the output, as the log.
    # attack: one who may read the run's log opens the log and reads the four
    #   characters.
    # attack-run-behavior: tee prints "token: " and four characters of the token
    #   to the log.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              DEPLOY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
            run: |
              exec > >(tee -a build.log) 2>&1
              echo "token: ${DEPLOY_TOKEN:0:4}"
    ```
- writer-function-output: a value made from a secret that the body of a shell function prints, where a call of the function with no arguments is a command of a pipeline whose last command is not a simple command and writes to \$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY (f | { cat; } >>"\$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"), or where the body of a function that a call with arguments runs calls the function (g() { f; }; g a >>"\$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"): the rule reads such a pipeline and such a call by every simple command, without the bodies of the called functions, and reads only the bodies of the function the call with arguments names
  - finding kinds: secret-in-log.private, secret-in-log.public
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: writer-function-output.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, in a public repository (repo.public true), a step
    #   defines a function f that prints "key:" and the secret GCP_SA_KEY without
    #   the first character of the secret, and appends the output of f to
    #   $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY through a pipe to cat in a group.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the group passes the output of f to the
    #   job summary, and the runner does not mask a value made from the secret.
    # cause: the rule reads a pipeline whose last command is a group by every
    #   simple command, without the body of f.
    # attack: anyone who can read the run opens the job summary of the run and
    #   reads the secret.
    # attack-run-behavior: the job summary of the run gets "key:" and the secret
    #   without the first character.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      deploy:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              GCP_SA_KEY: ${{ secrets.GCP_SA_KEY }}
            run: |
              f() { echo "key: ${GCP_SA_KEY:1}"; }
              f | { cat; } >>"$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    ```
- case-arm: a value made from a secret that an assignment in an arm of a case statement of the shell makes, or that a command in an arm of a case statement prints (case "\$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" in push) X="\${KEY:1}";; esac; echo "\$X"): the rule finds the case statement and does not read the commands in the arms of the case statement
  - finding kinds: secret-in-log.private, secret-in-log.public
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: case-arm.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step assigns the secret DEPLOY_TOKEN without the
    #   first character of the secret to X in an arm of a case statement that
    #   matches the name of the event, and prints X.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): on push the arm runs, and the step prints
    #   the token without the first character, which the runner does not mask.
    # cause: the rule finds the case statement and does not read the commands
    #   in the arms of the case statement.
    # attack: one who may read the run's log opens the log and reads the token
    #   without the first character.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step prints "token: " and the token without the
    #   first character.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      check:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              DEPLOY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
            run: |
              case "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" in push) X="${DEPLOY_TOKEN:1}";; *) X=none;; esac
              echo "token: $X"
    ```
- action-output: an action whose code prints a value made from a secret, where the code of the action is the own code of the action, a program that the action starts, or the post step of the action, which the runner runs at the end of the job, and where the code of the action reads the secret from an input of the action, from the environment of the step or from a file. Examples of a secret from an input of the action: GHSA-26wh-cc3r-w6pj, GHSA-4mgv-m5cm-f9h7, and the GITHUB_TOKEN that shivammathur/setup-php gives to Composer, a program that setup-php starts, where Composer prints the GITHUB_TOKEN (GHSA-5wxr-w449-57cm). Examples of a secret from a file: the post step of setup-steamcmd prints config/config.vdf, where running steamcmd +login in a step after the main step of setup-steamcmd saved the token of the Steam account (GHSA-c5qx-p38x-qf5w), and a parse error of tmatens/compose-lint up to 0.31.0 quotes the first characters of the value of a secret in a file of credentials outside the checkout, which a symlink of a pull request names in place of .compose-lint.yml (GHSA-88f4-frh5-gmcr)
  - finding kinds: secret-in-log.private, secret-in-log.public
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: action-output.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step passes the GITHUB_TOKEN to
    #   canonical/get-workflow-version-action v1.0.0, whose exception output may
    #   print a part of the token (GHSA-26wh-cc3r-w6pj: "the token may be
    #   truncated—causing part of the GITHUB_TOKEN to be displayed in plaintext in
    #   the GitHub Actions logs"). The job php is the form of GHSA-5wxr-w449-57cm:
    #   shivammathur/setup-php before 2.37.1 with a pinned Composer version (tools:
    #   composer:2.9.7) gives the GITHUB_TOKEN to Composer, which prints the token
    #   when it rejects the format of the token. The job steam is the form of
    #   GHSA-c5qx-p38x-qf5w and GHSA-mj96-mh85-r574: a step after the main step of
    #   setup-steamcmd logs in with steamcmd, which saves the token of the Steam
    #   account in config/config.vdf, and the post step of setup-steamcmd, which
    #   runs at the end of the job after the later steps
    #   (RageAgainstThePixel/setup-steamcmd v1.2.7, commit
    #   ec536b530bd3bd059377d0d0c376c52c6b870de1, src/logging.ts lines 29 and 34),
    #   prints the .vdf files; the action takes no secret as an input (its
    #   action.yml has no inputs). The job vault is the form of
    #   GHSA-4mgv-m5cm-f9h7: hashicorp/vault-action before 2.2.0 reads a secret
    #   from Vault and, for a secret of several lines, "did not correctly handle
    #   the marking of multi-line variables", so the runner does not mask the
    #   lines of the secret that the action prints in its output. The advisories
    #   name no workflow; the jobs are the configurations that the advisories
    #   describe.
    # reason: a limitation (the run decides): the code of the action prints the
    #   part of the token, which the runner does not mask.
    # cause: the rule reads the run scripts of the workflow, not the code of an
    #   action.
    # attack: one who may read the run's log opens the log and uses the part of
    #   the token while the job runs.
    # attack-run-behavior: when the step fails, the action prints an exception
    #   with a part of the token. In the job php, Composer prints the token in
    #   its error; in the job steam, the post step of setup-steamcmd, at the end
    #   of the job, prints
    #   config.vdf with the saved token of the Steam account, which does not
    #   expire when the job ends.
    # advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-26wh-cc3r-w6pj
    # advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4mgv-m5cm-f9h7
    # advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5wxr-w449-57cm
    # advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c5qx-p38x-qf5w
    # advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mj96-mh85-r574
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      version:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: canonical/get-workflow-version-action@a5d53b08d254a157ea441c9819ea5002ffc12edc # v1.0.0
            with:
              repository-name: canonical/data-platform-workflows
              file-name: build_charm.yaml
              github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      php:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: shivammathur/setup-php@accd6127cb78bee3e8082180cb391013d204ef9f # 2.37.0
            with:
              php-version: '8.3'
              tools: composer:2.9.7
      steam:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: RageAgainstThePixel/setup-steamcmd@ec536b530bd3bd059377d0d0c376c52c6b870de1 # v1.2.7
          - run: steamcmd +login "$STEAM_USERNAME" "$STEAM_PASSWORD" +quit
            env:
              STEAM_USERNAME: ${{ secrets.STEAM_USERNAME }}
              STEAM_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.STEAM_PASSWORD }}
      vault:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: hashicorp/vault-action@5e5c06a3c8e96b7c4757fe7a10e03469cdbd07bb # v2.1.2
            with:
              url: https://vault.example.com
              token: ${{ secrets.VAULT_TOKEN }}
              secrets: secret/data/ci certificate | CERTIFICATE
    ```
  - example: action-output.ghsa-88f4-frh5-gmcr.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a job writes a file of AWS credentials
    #   with a secret into the home directory of the runner, outside the
    #   checkout, checks out the head of the pull request with actions/checkout
    #   v4.2.2, and runs tmatens/compose-lint pinned to the commit of v0.24.0.
    #   The advisory names no workflow; the step follows the configuration that
    #   GHSA-88f4-frh5-gmcr describes: a pull request commits .compose-lint.yml
    #   as a symlink to a file on the runner. GHSA-88f4-frh5-gmcr describes a
    #   file of credentials in the INI form, of which the parse error quoted the
    #   head of the second line (aws_access_key_id = and the first characters of
    #   the value).
    # reason: a limitation (the run decides): a parse error of compose-lint up
    #   to 0.31.0 quotes about 30 characters around the place where the YAML
    #   parser fails in .compose-lint.yml, so the log has the first characters
    #   of the value of the secret and not the whole value; the runner masks a
    #   registered value only where the whole value is in a line of the log.
    # cause: the rule reads the run scripts of the workflow, not the code of an
    #   action.
    # attack: the author of a pull request from a fork commits .compose-lint.yml
    #   as a symlink to /home/runner/.aws/credentials.
    # attack-run-behavior: compose-lint fails to parse the file of credentials
    #   and quotes the first characters of the value of AWS_KEY_ID in the log of
    #   the step, which the author of the pull request reads on a public
    #   repository.
    # advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-88f4-frh5-gmcr
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      lint:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: |
              mkdir -p "$HOME/.aws"
              printf '[default]\naws_access_key_id = %s\naws_secret_access_key = %s\n' "$AWS_KEY_ID" "$AWS_SECRET" > "$HOME/.aws/credentials"
            env:
              AWS_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.AWS_KEY_ID }}
              AWS_SECRET: ${{ secrets.AWS_SECRET }}
          - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - uses: tmatens/compose-lint@d6e1817352200adbd0a72893fd7ea7880874759b # v0.24.0
    ```
- remote-callee: a job or a step inside a reusable workflow of another repository (uses: owner/repo/.github/workflows/&lt;file>@&lt;ref>) whose content the fact workflow.definition does not give. For every rule: a run that does not ask the fact (a run without --online and without the answer in --facts). For a quality rule, also: a run where the linter asked the fact and got no answer (an answer of unknown: the GitHub API did not give the file), and a call deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact. The rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition. For a rule that is not a quality rule (a rule with a threat), the last two forms are the inconclusive kind remote-callee-unknown, not this form
  - finding kinds: secret-in-log.private, secret-in-log.public
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-callee.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
    #   the repository example-org/secret-in-log-unanswered, whose content is
    #   the workflow of the true positive private (private.yml) of the rule,
    #   with on: workflow_call in place of the on of private.yml. The linter has
    #   no answer of the fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event
    #   that started the run of the calling job, and the linter does not read
    #   the reusable workflow.
    # cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from
    #   the answer of workflow.definition.
    # attack: one with read access to the repository opens the run's log and
    #   reads the first characters of the token.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step prints "token starts with" and eight
    #   characters of the token; the log keeps them for 90 days by default.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/secret-in-log-unanswered/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

### inconclusive

- call-body-unknown: a call of a function after the rule has read the bodies of the functions at 4,096 calls in the script, such as a call after a chain of functions in which each function calls the next function twice (f1() { f0; f0; }; ... f13() { f12; f12; }; f13; w): the rule does not read the bodies of the functions at the calls past the 4,096 calls, so the rule does not decide the assignments, the writes, the prints and the requests in the bodies of the functions at the calls past the 4,096 calls
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: call-body-unknown.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, in a public repository (repo.public true), a step
    #   defines a function w that sets PRIVATE_KEY to the private key out of the
    #   secret GCP_SA_KEY, runs a chain of functions f0 to f13 in which each
    #   function calls the function before it twice (16,383 calls), calls w, and
    #   prints PRIVATE_KEY.
    # reason: the call of w comes after the 4,096 calls of functions that the
    #   rule follows when it reads what the commands of the step print, so the
    #   rule does not read the body of w for the prints and reports an
    #   Inconclusive at the call of w; the rule still reads the value that w
    #   assigns, and also reports the print of the private key.
    # attack: anyone signed in to GitHub opens the run's log and reads the
    #   private key.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step prints "key:" and the private key.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      deploy:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              GCP_SA_KEY: ${{ secrets.GCP_SA_KEY }}
            run: |
              w() { PRIVATE_KEY="$(echo "$GCP_SA_KEY" | jq -r '.private_key')"; }
              f0() { :; }
              f1() { f0; f0; }
              f2() { f1; f1; }
              f3() { f2; f2; }
              f4() { f3; f3; }
              f5() { f4; f4; }
              f6() { f5; f5; }
              f7() { f6; f6; }
              f8() { f7; f7; }
              f9() { f8; f8; }
              f10() { f9; f9; }
              f11() { f10; f10; }
              f12() { f11; f11; }
              f13() { f12; f12; }
              f13
              w
              echo "key: $PRIVATE_KEY"
    ```
- remote-callee-unknown: a job that calls a reusable workflow of another repository, when the linter asked the fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow and got no answer (the token that the linter uses cannot read the file, the file is larger than the limit, or the linter has used up the requests it may send to the GitHub API), or when the call is deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact: the rule does not read the jobs and the steps of the reusable workflow
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-callee-unknown.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
    #   the repository example-org/secret-in-log-unknown, whose content is the
    #   workflow of the true positive private (private.yml) of the rule, with
    #   on: workflow_call in place of the on of private.yml. The linter asked
    #   the fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow and got no
    #   answer.
    # reason: what the jobs of the reusable workflow do is in the file that the
    #   linter could not read; whoever changes the uses, such as the author of a
    #   pull request, can name a reusable workflow that the token that the
    #   linter uses cannot read.
    # attack: one with read access to the repository opens the run's log and
    #   reads the first characters of the token.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step prints "token starts with" and eight
    #   characters of the token; the log keeps them for 90 days by default.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/secret-in-log-unknown/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

### false positive forms

- branch-not-run: an assignment in a branch of if, after && or ||, in the body of a loop, or in the body of a function called there, that bash does not run (if false; then s=\$KEY; fi): the rule does not read the value of a condition, so the rule reads the assignment as one that may run, and reads the variable as one that may hold the value of the assignment
  - finding kinds: secret-in-log.public, secret-in-log.private
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: branch-not-run.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, in a public repository (repo.public true), a step sets a
    #   variable to the private key out of the secret GCP_SA_KEY in an if whose
    #   condition is false, and prints the variable.
    # reason: bash does not run the branch, so the variable is empty when echo
    #   runs, and the log has no part of the secret.
    # cause: the rule does not read the value of the condition of an if, and
    #   reads the assignment in the branch as one that may run.
    # attack: anyone signed in to GitHub opens the run's log and reads the
    #   private key.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step prints "key:" alone.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      deploy:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              GCP_SA_KEY: ${{ secrets.GCP_SA_KEY }}
            run: |
              if false; then PRIVATE_KEY=$(echo "$GCP_SA_KEY" | jq -r '.private_key'); fi
              echo "key: $PRIVATE_KEY"
    ```
- writer-body: a value made from a secret that the body of a shell function prints after an exec in the body points the standard output elsewhere, after a return in the body, or with a redirect of the print that points the standard output elsewhere, where a call of the function with arguments writes to \$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY (f() { exec >/dev/null; echo "\${KEY:1}"; }; f a >>"\$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"): the job summary gets nothing from the print; the rule reads what such a call writes from every command of the body of the function, and does not read where the commands of the body point the standard output or which commands of the body run
  - finding kinds: secret-in-log.public, secret-in-log.private
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: writer-body.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, in a public repository (repo.public true), a step
    #   defines a function f that points the standard output to /dev/null with
    #   exec and then prints the secret GCP_SA_KEY without the first character of
    #   the secret, and calls f with an argument, appending the standard output of
    #   the call to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY.
    # reason: the exec sends the print to /dev/null, so the job summary gets no
    #   part of the secret.
    # cause: the rule reads what a call of a function with arguments writes
    #   from every command of the body of the function, and does not read where
    #   the exec in the body points the standard output.
    # attack: anyone who can read the run opens the job summary of the run and
    #   reads the secret.
    # attack-run-behavior: the job summary of the run is empty.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      deploy:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              GCP_SA_KEY: ${{ secrets.GCP_SA_KEY }}
            run: |
              f() { exec >/dev/null; echo "${GCP_SA_KEY:1}"; }
              f report >>"$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    ```
- pipeline-descriptor: a value made from a secret that a command of a \$( ) prints after an exec in the \$( ) points the standard output at a file descriptor that an exec before a pipeline opened, where the \$( ) is in a word of a command of the pipeline and the last command of the pipeline writes to \$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY (exec 3>/dev/null; echo "\$(exec >&amp;3; echo "\${KEY:1}")" | cat >>"\$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"): the print goes where the file descriptor points, not to the value of the \$( ), so the job summary gets nothing from the print; the rule reads such a pipeline without the file descriptors that the commands before the pipeline opened
  - finding kinds: secret-in-log.public, secret-in-log.private
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: pipeline-descriptor.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, in a public repository (repo.public true), a step opens
    #   file descriptor 3 on /dev/null with exec, and appends to
    #   $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY, through cat, a line of "key:" and a $( ) in which
    #   exec points the standard output at file descriptor 3 and then an echo
    #   prints the secret GCP_SA_KEY without the first character of the secret.
    # reason: the exec in the $( ) sends the print to file descriptor 3, which
    #   points at /dev/null, so the $( ) is empty and the job summary gets no
    #   part of the secret.
    # cause: the rule reads a pipeline whose last command writes to the job
    #   summary without the file descriptors that the exec before the pipeline
    #   opened, and reads the print as a part of the value of the $( ).
    # attack: anyone who can read the run opens the job summary of the run and
    #   reads the secret.
    # attack-run-behavior: the job summary of the run gets "key:" alone.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      deploy:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              GCP_SA_KEY: ${{ secrets.GCP_SA_KEY }}
            run: |
              exec 3>/dev/null
              echo "key: $(exec >&3; echo "${GCP_SA_KEY:1}")" | cat >>"$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    ```
- pipeline-compound: a value made from a secret that a command of a pipeline prints elsewhere than the pipe, by a redirect of the command or after an exec in a \$( ) of the command, where the last command of the pipeline is not a simple command and writes to \$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY (echo "\$(exec >/dev/null; echo "\${KEY:1}")" | { cat; } >>"\$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"): the job summary gets nothing from the print; the rule reads such a pipeline by every simple command, and does not read where the commands point the standard output
  - finding kinds: secret-in-log.public, secret-in-log.private
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: pipeline-compound.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, in a public repository (repo.public true), a step
    #   appends to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY, through a pipe to cat in a group, a line
    #   of "key:" and a $( ) in which exec points the standard output to /dev/null
    #   and then an echo prints the secret GCP_SA_KEY without the first character
    #   of the secret.
    # reason: the exec sends the print to /dev/null, so the $( ) is empty and
    #   the job summary gets no part of the secret.
    # cause: the rule reads a pipeline whose last command is a group by every
    #   simple command, and does not read where the exec in the $( ) points the
    #   standard output.
    # attack: anyone who can read the run opens the job summary of the run and
    #   reads the secret.
    # attack-run-behavior: the job summary of the run gets "key:" alone.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      deploy:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              GCP_SA_KEY: ${{ secrets.GCP_SA_KEY }}
            run: |
              echo "key: $(exec >/dev/null; echo "${GCP_SA_KEY:1}")" | { cat; } >>"$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    ```
- failing-pipe-redirect: a value made from a secret that a pipeline writes to \$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY, where a redirect of the last command of the pipeline copies a file descriptor that is not open (echo "\${KEY:1}" | cat >&3 >>"\$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"): bash does not run the last command, so the job summary gets nothing; the rule reads the last command of such a pipeline as writing to the job summary, and does not read whether a redirect of the last command fails
  - finding kinds: secret-in-log.public, secret-in-log.private
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: failing-pipe-redirect.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, in a public repository (repo.public true), a step pipes
    #   "key:" and the secret GCP_SA_KEY without the first character of the secret
    #   to cat, whose redirects copy file descriptor 3, which is not open, and
    #   append to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY, and goes on when cat fails (|| true).
    # reason: the copy of file descriptor 3 fails, so bash does not run cat, and
    #   the job summary gets no part of the secret.
    # cause: the rule reads the last command of the pipeline as writing to the
    #   job summary, and does not read whether a redirect of the last command
    #   fails.
    # attack: anyone who can read the run opens the job summary of the run and
    #   reads the secret.
    # attack-run-behavior: the job summary of the run is empty.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      deploy:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              GCP_SA_KEY: ${{ secrets.GCP_SA_KEY }}
            run: |
              echo "key: ${GCP_SA_KEY:1}" | cat >&3 >>"$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY" || true
    ```
- background-write: a value made from a secret that a command, which the script runs in the background (&) with no wait for the command, writes to \$GITHUB_ENV after the shell of the script ends (for example: (sleep 5; echo "P=\${KEY:1}" >> "\$GITHUB_ENV") &): a write that the command makes after the shell of the script ends does not reach the steps after the step, so the header of a later step does not print the value; the rule reads the write as a write that reaches \$GITHUB_ENV, because whether the command writes before the shell of the script ends depends on how long the commands take when the step runs
  - finding kinds: secret-in-log.public, secret-in-log.private
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: background-write.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, in a public repository (repo.public true), a step runs
    #   in the background (&), with no wait, a subshell that sleeps 5 seconds and
    #   then writes P= and the secret DEPLOY_TOKEN without the first character of
    #   the secret to $GITHUB_ENV; the shell of the script ends before the write;
    #   a later step runs.
    # reason: a write that the background command makes after the shell of the
    #   script ends does not reach the steps after the step (seen on the runner
    #   on 2026-11-17), so the header of the later step prints no P.
    # cause: the rule reads the write in the background as a write that reaches
    #   $GITHUB_ENV, and does not read when the background command writes.
    # attack: anyone who can read the run opens the log of the run and reads
    #   the secret.
    # attack-run-behavior: the header of the later step has no P in its env.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      deploy:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              DEPLOY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
            run: |
              (sleep 5; echo "P=${DEPLOY_TOKEN:1}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV") &
          - run: echo done
    ```
- masked-encoding: a value the shell made that is a form the runner registers: the base64 of the value without a line break and not folded (base64 -w0, echo -n), the base64 of a value whose length is a multiple of 3, with the line break base64 writes (the head of the output is the base64 of the value, which the runner masks; the last characters left in the log encode the line break alone), or jq -c . of a secret whose JSON is already in the form jq -c writes
  - finding kinds: secret-in-log.public, secret-in-log.private
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: masked-encoding.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step prints the base64 of the secret API_KEY, made
    #   without a line break and not folded.
    # reason: the runner registers the base64 of each secret it gets, so the
    #   base64 is printed as ***.
    # cause: the rule takes a value base64 makes as a value the runner does not
    #   mask, as the rule does not tell the forms the runner registers.
    # attack: one who may read the run's log opens the log to read the base64.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step prints "***".
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      check:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              API_KEY: ${{ secrets.API_KEY }}
            run: echo "$(printf '%s' "$API_KEY" | base64 -w0)"
    ```
- secret-lines: whole lines of a secret of the secrets context with more than one line, taken by head, tail, grep or sed -n: for a secret of the secrets context, the runner registers each line of the secret
  - finding kinds: secret-in-log.public, secret-in-log.private
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: secret-lines.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step prints the first line of the secret
    #   PRIVATE_KEY, a key of more than one line.
    # reason: the runner registers each line of each secret it gets, so the
    #   first line is printed as ***.
    # cause: the rule takes what head prints as a value made from the secret,
    #   as the rule does not know that the secret has more than one line.
    # attack: one who may read the run's log opens the log to read the line.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step prints "***".
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      check:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.PRIVATE_KEY }}
            run: echo "$PRIVATE_KEY" | head -n 1
    ```
- other-mask: a value registered by a ::add-mask:: of an expression or of another variable holding the same value, by core.setSecret of actions/github-script, or by an action
  - finding kinds: secret-in-log.public, secret-in-log.private
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: other-mask.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step registers the password taken out of the secret
    #   DB with ::add-mask:: of a substitution, and prints the password from
    #   another variable after.
    # reason: the runner masks the password from the line after its ::add-mask::
    #   on, so the password is printed as ***.
    # cause: the rule reads a registration of one variable, not of a
    #   substitution that writes the same value.
    # attack: one who may read the run's log opens the log to read the password.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step prints "password: ***".
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      migrate:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              DB: ${{ secrets.DB }}
            run: |
              echo "::add-mask::$(jq -r .password <<< "$DB")"
              PASSWORD=$(jq -r .password <<< "$DB")
              echo "password: $PASSWORD"
    ```
- unchanged-value: a command or an expansion that gives a value of one line as the value was: tr -d '\\n', head -n1, sort or uniq of one line, \${X%\$'\\n'}, a sed that does not match; the runner masks the value of the secret
  - finding kinds: secret-in-log.public, secret-in-log.private
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: unchanged-value.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step removes the line breaks of the secret
    #   DEPLOY_TOKEN with tr and prints the result; the secret is one line.
    # reason: for a secret of one line, tr -d '\n' gives the value of the
    #   secret as the value was, which the runner masks, so the log has ***.
    # cause: the rule reads tr as a command that changes the input, and does
    #   not know that a value of one line comes out of tr -d '\n' as the value
    #   was.
    # attack: one who may read the run's log opens the log to read the token.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step prints "token: ***".
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              DEPLOY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
            run: |
              echo "token: $(echo "$DEPLOY_TOKEN" | tr -d '\n')"
    ```
- filter-result: a command that changes the input, whose program gives a value that holds nothing of the input: jq 'type == "array"', jq length and the like; the output does not give the value of the secret
  - finding kinds: secret-in-log.public, secret-in-log.private
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: filter-result.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step checks with jq that the secret DOMAINS is a
    #   JSON array, and jq prints the answer.
    # reason: the filter type == "array" gives true or false, which holds
    #   nothing of the secret; the log has true.
    # cause: the rule reads jq as a command that writes a value made from the
    #   input, and does not read what the filter of jq gives.
    # attack: one who may read the run's log opens the log to read the secret.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step prints "true".
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      deploy:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              DOMAINS: ${{ secrets.DOMAINS }}
            run: |
              jq -e 'type == "array"' <<< "$DOMAINS"
    ```
- function-calls: the body of a function that prints an argument or a variable, where the call that carries the value made from a secret sends the output to a file, or where a ::add-mask:: that comes before the call, but after the body in the text, registers the value: the rule reads the body with the arguments of every call, and compares a ::add-mask:: with the body by the place in the text
  - finding kinds: secret-in-log.public, secret-in-log.private
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: function-calls.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a function prints its argument; a step calls the
    #   function with four characters of the secret DEPLOY_TOKEN and sends the
    #   output of that call to a file, and calls the function again with a
    #   literal.
    # reason: the call that carries the four characters writes to out.txt, not
    #   to the log; the log has the literal alone.
    # cause: the rule reads the body of the function with the arguments of
    #   every call, and takes the body as printing because one call prints. The
    #   rule also compares a ::add-mask:: with the body by the place in the
    #   text, not by the order of the calls.
    # attack: one who may read the run's log opens the log to read the four
    #   characters.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step prints "safe" alone.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              DEPLOY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
            run: |
              h() { echo "$1"; }
              h "${DEPLOY_TOKEN:0:4}" > out.txt
              h safe
    ```
- private-repository: a private or internal repository, where the value is secret-in-log.private: whoever may read the repository reads the value
  - finding kinds: secret-in-log.public
  - fact kinds:
    - repo.public (provider: repo-setting, answer that removes the finding: false)
  - example: private-repository.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step prints a substring of the secret DEPLOY_TOKEN,
    #   in a private repository.
    # reason: the repository is private or internal, so the value is
    #   secret-in-log.private, not .public: only those with read access, every
    #   member of the enterprise for an internal one, read the log.
    # cause: unless a file of facts or --fact says that the repository is not
    #   public (repo.public false), the rule reports the finding. When no source
    #   answers repo.public, the finding is conditional.
    # attack: anyone without access to the repository tries to read the run's
    #   log to take the substring of the token.
    # attack-run-behavior: GitHub does not show the log of a private or
    #   internal repository to those without read access; those with it read
    #   eight characters of the token.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      check:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              DEPLOY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
            run: echo "token starts with ${DEPLOY_TOKEN:0:8}"
    ```
- actions-not-allowed: a workflow whose run GitHub does not start, or a job that GitHub fails in the step "Set up job", because of the setting of allowed actions of GitHub (the fact repo.allowed-actions, which the quality rule allowed-actions reads): GitHub does not start a run of a workflow that has a uses, or that calls a reusable workflow that has a uses, that the setting does not allow, and fails a job before any step of the job runs when a step of a composite action that the job runs has a uses that the setting does not allow, or when the setting requires a full commit SHA and a step names an action by a tag or a branch. The harm that the finding reports happens only when GitHub runs the workflow or the job, and the rule does not read repo.allowed-actions
  - finding kinds: secret-in-log.private, secret-in-log.public
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: actions-not-allowed.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the workflow of the true positive private (private.yml) of the
    #   rule, with a job added whose step uses example-org/not-allowed-action,
    #   which the setting of allowed actions of GitHub (repo.allowed-actions)
    #   blocks with !example-org/not-allowed-action@*. In the true positive, on
    #   push, in a private repository (repo.public answered false), a step
    #   prints the first characters of the secret DEPLOY_TOKEN to check which
    #   token is set.
    # reason: GitHub checks each uses of the workflow before the run starts, and
    #   does not start the run because of the uses of
    #   example-org/not-allowed-action: no job of the run runs, so what the
    #   reason of the true positive says does not happen (in runs that the
    #   authors of the rule made on GitHub, such runs ended as startup_failure).
    # cause: the rule does not read repo.allowed-actions.
    # attack: one with read access to the repository opens the run's log and
    #   reads the first characters of the token.
    # attack-run-behavior: GitHub does not start the run, so no step of the run
    #   runs, and the attack does nothing.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      check:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              DEPLOY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
            run: echo "token starts with ${DEPLOY_TOKEN:0:8}"
      not-allowed:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: example-org/not-allowed-action@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

### threat

- precondition derived-unmasked: the runner masks what is registered (the value of each secret the job gets, each line of the value, the forms the encoders of the runner make of the value, and what ::add-mask:: registers) where the registered value is in a line of the log as it is; a value the shell makes from a secret (a substring, a value with a part replaced or the case changed, what jq takes out, a base64 of the value with a line break or folded at 76 characters, a hex dump, the value reversed or folded) is printed as it is; a digest does not give the value, so the rule does not report a digest
  - observed: 2026-10-20, runner 2.337.0: the value of a secret, the value through an assignment or \$(echo ...), and the value with more around the value were masked; \${S:0:10}, \${S#probe-}, \${S//-/\_}, \${S^^}, jq -r .pass, jq ., rev, xxd -p, fold -w 9, the base64 of a 13-character and a 14-character value with a line break, and the base64 of a 67-character value folded at 76 characters were printed as they are
  - cites:
    - <https://github.com/actions/runner/blob/397b032cbf865e9c3ddfab89d533ec19325e1273/src/Sdk/DTLogging/Logging/SecretMasker.cs>
    - <https://github.com/actions/runner/blob/397b032cbf865e9c3ddfab89d533ec19325e1273/src/Sdk/DTLogging/Logging/ValueEncoders.cs>
    - <https://github.com/actions/runner/blob/397b032cbf865e9c3ddfab89d533ec19325e1273/src/Runner.Worker/Worker.cs>
    - <https://github.com/github/docs/blob/ba6f6f9b9b31c4f0a991fbcb1005080526424804/content/actions/reference/security/secure-use.md>
- precondition printed-places: the log has what the script writes to the standard output and error it inherits, the trace on the standard error that set -x or the -x option in the shell: value of the step turns on, and the job summary; the header of each step after a step that writes \$GITHUB_ENV prints the variables written in the env of the header, and the header of a step prints the run of the step with each \${{ }} evaluated, the env of the step and the with of the step, outputs of steps and jobs included
  - observed: 2026-10-20, runner 2.337.0: set -x printed an assignment of a value made from a secret; a value made from a secret written to \$GITHUB_ENV was in the env of the header of the next step, and one written to \$GITHUB_OUTPUT was in the header of a later step that read the output in the run and the env of the step, and of a step of another job that read the job's output
  - cites:
    - <https://github.com/actions/runner/blob/397b032cbf865e9c3ddfab89d533ec19325e1273/src/Runner.Worker/Handlers/ScriptHandler.cs>
    - <https://github.com/actions/runner/blob/397b032cbf865e9c3ddfab89d533ec19325e1273/src/Runner.Worker/FileCommandManager.cs>
    - <https://github.com/actions/runner/blob/397b032cbf865e9c3ddfab89d533ec19325e1273/src/Runner.Worker/ActionRunner.cs>
    - <https://github.com/github/docs/blob/666463860bec200da6c8db9cb9334e7335d9b753/content/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-commands.md>
- precondition mask-after: ::add-mask:: masks the value from the line after the ::add-mask:: on, in every later step of the job; a value made from the registered value is another value, and a value of more than one line has the lines after the first printed by the echo of ::add-mask:: itself
  - observed: 2026-10-20, runner 2.337.0: a value printed before the ::add-mask:: of the value was printed as it is and masked after the ::add-mask::; a value registered in a step was masked in the env of a later step's header; the second line of a value of two lines was printed by the ::add-mask:: of the value and after the ::add-mask::
  - cites:
    - <https://github.com/actions/runner/blob/397b032cbf865e9c3ddfab89d533ec19325e1273/src/Runner.Worker/ActionCommandManager.cs>
    - <https://github.com/github/docs/blob/666463860bec200da6c8db9cb9334e7335d9b753/content/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-commands.md>
- precondition readable-log: anyone signed in to GitHub reads the logs of a public repository (repo.public true), those with read access the logs of a private or internal one, where every member of the enterprise has read access to an internal one, for 90 days by default
  - cites:
    - <https://github.com/github/docs/blob/ba6f6f9b9b31c4f0a991fbcb1005080526424804/content/actions/how-tos/monitor-workflows/use-workflow-run-logs.md>
    - <https://github.com/github/docs/blob/ba6f6f9b9b31c4f0a991fbcb1005080526424804/data/reusables/actions/about-artifact-log-retention.md>
    - <https://github.com/github/docs/blob/8b39dc44a066dda794bfacdd25653ff86324ef21/content/repositories/creating-and-managing-repositories/about-repositories.md>
- actor: log-reader
  - via: reads the log of a run, or downloads the log
  - gains: read-secrets

## secrets-in-artifacts

- problem: a step leaves a credential in a file of the workspace, and actions/upload-artifact after it puts the file in an artifact, which anyone who can read the repository downloads
- expected: the file left out of the artifact's path, or the upload before the step that writes it
- severity: critical (the worst of its kinds)
- targets: workflow, action-metadata
- facets:
  - weakness: credential-leak
  - attack-means: none
- default run: always: in a run without --rule, the rule runs unless --skip-rule names the rule

### finding kinds

- secrets-in-artifacts.lasting
  - detected: {uses} leaves a credential that does not expire in the workspace, and {upload} puts it in an artifact
  - arguments:
    - {uses}: The uses, as written, of one step that runs before the upload and leaves a credential that the upload takes: the first of those steps that leaves a credential on no condition, else the first of those steps.
    - {upload}: The uses of the upload, as written.
  - consequence: anyone who can read the repository's artifacts takes the credential and uses what it opens
  - remedy: leave the file out of the path (a line !gha-creds-\*.json), upload before the step that writes it, or have the step not write it (create_credentials_file: false)
  - severity: critical (found from the CVSS metrics below by the table)
  - attackers: artifact-reader
  - preconditions: leaves-credential-file, artifact-taken
  - true positives:
    - lasting.no-caller.action.yml (action-metadata, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a composite action with no caller among the files that the
      #   linter reads; google-github-actions/auth writes the service account key of
      #   inputs.credentials_json to gha-creds-*.json in the workspace, and
      #   actions/upload-artifact uploads the workspace.
      # reason: path: . puts gha-creds-*.json in the artifact, and a service
      #   account key works until someone deletes the key in Google Cloud, not only
      #   while the job runs.
      # attack: a reader of the artifacts of the repository (anyone, in a public
      #   repository) downloads the artifact through the API, and takes the service
      #   account key from gha-creds-*.json.
      # attack-run-behavior: google-github-actions/auth writes the service account
      #   key the caller gives as credentials_json to gha-creds-<hex>.json at the
      #   top of the workspace, and the upload of path . puts the file in the
      #   artifact; the key keeps working after the run until someone deletes the
      #   key in Google Cloud.
      name: build
      description: authenticate and upload the workspace
      inputs:
        credentials_json:
          description: the key of the service account
      runs:
        using: composite
        steps:
          - uses: google-github-actions/auth@v2
            with:
              credentials_json: ${{ inputs.credentials_json }}
          - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
            with:
              path: .
      ```
    - lasting.remote-callee.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
      #   the repository example-org/secrets-in-artifacts-remote, which the fact
      #   workflow.definition answers with the workflow of the true positive
      #   lasting (lasting.yml) of the rule, with on: workflow_call in place of
      #   the on of lasting.yml. The job passes its secrets with secrets: inherit.
      #   In the true positive, google-github-actions/auth writes the service
      #   account key of secrets.GCP_KEY to gha-creds-*.json in the workspace, and
      #   actions/upload-artifact uploads the workspace.
      # reason: the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event that started the
      #   run of the calling job, so the reason of the true positive holds: path:
      #   . puts gha-creds-*.json in the artifact, and a service account key works
      #   until someone deletes it in Google Cloud, not only while the job runs.
      # attack: a reader of the repository's artifacts (anyone, in a public
      #   repository) downloads the artifact through the API, and takes the
      #   service account key from gha-creds-*.json.
      # attack-run-behavior: google-github-actions/auth writes the service account
      #   key of secrets.GCP_KEY to gha-creds-<hex>.json at the top of the
      #   workspace, and the upload of path . puts it in the artifact; the key
      #   keeps working after the run until someone deletes it in Google Cloud.
      on: push
      jobs:
        c:
          uses: example-org/secrets-in-artifacts-remote/.github/workflows/w.yml@v1
          secrets: inherit
      ```
    - lasting.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: google-github-actions/auth writes the service account key of
      #   secrets.GCP_KEY to gha-creds-*.json in the workspace, and
      #   actions/upload-artifact uploads the workspace.
      # reason: path: . puts gha-creds-*.json in the artifact, and a service
      #   account key works until someone deletes it in Google Cloud, not only
      #   while the job runs.
      # attack: a reader of the repository's artifacts (anyone, in a public
      #   repository) downloads the artifact through the API, and takes the
      #   service account key from gha-creds-*.json.
      # attack-run-behavior: google-github-actions/auth writes the service account
      #   key of secrets.GCP_KEY to gha-creds-<hex>.json at the top of the
      #   workspace, and the upload of path . puts it in the artifact; the key
      #   keeps working after the run until someone deletes it in Google Cloud.
      on: push
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: google-github-actions/auth@v2
              with:
      ```

  - true negatives:
    - lasting.never-runs.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on push, the job whose id is disabled has if: false, and the job
      #   whose id is on-failure needs the job build and has if: needs.build.result
      #   == 'failure'; each of the two jobs runs google-github-actions/auth v2 with
      #   the secret GCP_KEY, which writes a key file of the service account in the
      #   workspace, and uploads the workspace as an artifact.
      # reason: GitHub skips the job disabled because the if of the job disabled is
      #   false. The if of the job on-failure calls no status function, so GitHub
      #   evaluates the if of the job on-failure only when the job build succeeded;
      #   needs.build.result is then success, and the if is false. When the job
      #   build fails or is skipped, GitHub skips the job on-failure without
      #   evaluating the if. So neither job runs
      #   (https://github.com/github/docs/blob/404a5f4de6cd5311e3ce2d5c076571291e0107d6/data/reusables/actions/jobs/section-using-conditions-to-control-job-execution.md).
      # attack: anyone who can read the repository downloads the artifacts of the
      #   run and reads the key file.
      # attack-run-behavior: GitHub skips the job disabled and the job on-failure,
      #   so no step writes the key file and no step uploads an artifact.
      on: push
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: echo built
        disabled:
          if: false
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: google-github-actions/auth@v2
              with:
                credentials_json: ${{ secrets.GCP_KEY }}
            - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
              with:
                path: .
        on-failure:
          needs: build
          if: needs.build.result == 'failure'
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: google-github-actions/auth@v2
              with:
                credentials_json: ${{ secrets.GCP_KEY }}
            - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
              with:
                path: .
      ```
    - lasting.yml (workflow, true-negative)

      ```yaml
            - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
      ```
