## set-output-injection

- problem: a step that has an id prints a value an attacker controls to the log of the step, and the runner reads a set-output command in the printed value as a command that sets an output of the step; the runner sets the outputs of a step only when the step has an id
- expected: no value an attacker controls is printed to the log of a step that has an id, or such a value is printed only between ::stop-commands::TOKEN and ::TOKEN:: with a random TOKEN
- severity: critical
- targets: workflow, action-metadata
- facets:
  - weakness: workflow-command-injection
  - attack-means: string
- default run: always: in a run without --rule, the rule runs unless --skip-rule names the rule

### finding kinds

- set-output-injection.controlled
  - detected: the value of {expr_ref} is printed to the log of a step, the step has an id, and an attacker who controls the value on {controlled_on} can write a set-output command in the value
  - arguments:
    - {expr_ref}: The reference as written: a context in \${{ }}, such as github.event.issue.title, or a variable of env, such as \$TITLE.
    - {controlled_on}: The events on which an attacker writes a workflow command in the value, each event named once.
  - consequence: with or without ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS, the runner reads a line that the step prints, when the line holds ##&#91;set-output name=NAME;]value or starts with ::set-output, as a command that sets the output NAME of the step; the runner sets the outputs of a step only when the step has an id; the steps after the step, and the outputs of the job and of an action that name the output, get the value of the attacker as the output of the step, and a step that writes \${{ steps.&lt;id>.outputs.NAME }} into its run script runs code of the attacker
  - remedy: do not print the value to the log; if the value must be printed, print the value only between ::stop-commands::TOKEN and ::TOKEN::, where TOKEN is a value the step chooses at random for each run (the rule does not read stop-commands and keeps reporting the step: a known false positive, stopped-commands)
  - severity: critical (found from the CVSS metrics below by the table)
  - fact kinds: repo.pull-request-target-allowed (provider: repo-setting), repo.fork-pr-app-checks (provider: repo-setting), repo.merge-commit-app-checks (provider: repo-setting)
  - attackers: fork-pr-author, issue-author, commenter, merged-commit-author, anyone-who-forks
  - preconditions: log-set-output, attacker-event, callers-events, app-status-check
  - true positives:
    - controlled.custom-shell-xtrace.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issues, the step p, which has an id and whose shell: is
      #   bash -x {0}, passes the title of the issue to git log, and the release
      #   step writes the output tag of the step p into its script.
      # reason: bash -x starts the script with the trace on, as set -x does, so
      #   the trace prints the command with the title on the standard error,
      #   where the runner reads ##[set-output name=NAME;] anywhere in a line as a
      #   command that sets the output NAME of a step with an id; the title is
      #   the attacker's.
      # attack: the attacker opens an issue titled x ##[set-output
      #   name=tag;]$(id).
      # attack-run-behavior: the trace prints the git log command with the title,
      #   the runner sets the output tag of the step to $(id), and the release
      #   step writes the output into its script and runs id, with the token and
      #   the secrets of the job.
      on: issues
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        j:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - id: p
              shell: bash -x {0}
              env:
                TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
              run: git log --grep "$TITLE" > log.txt
            - run: ./release.sh "${{ steps.p.outputs.tag }}"
      ```
    - controlled.failed-duplicate.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issues, the step p passes the title of the issue in the
      #   environment variable TITLE, runs exec >&4, where descriptor 4 is not
      #   open, goes on when the exec fails (|| true), and prints TITLE; the
      #   release step writes the output tag of the step p into its script.
      # reason: the exec fails, bash does not copy the
      #   descriptor 4 to the standard output, and the standard output still goes
      #   to the log; the step prints the title to the log.
      # attack: the attacker opens an issue titled x ##[set-output
      #   name=tag;]$(id).
      # attack-run-behavior: the step prints the title, the runner sets the
      #   output tag to $(id), and the release step runs id.
      on: issues
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        j:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - id: p
              env:
                TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
              run: |
                exec >&4 || true
                echo "issue: $TITLE"
            - run: ./release.sh "${{ steps.p.outputs.tag }}"
      ```
    - controlled.jump-path.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issues, the step p passes the title of the issue in the
      #   environment variable TITLE, defines a function f that returns when STOP
      #   is empty and sets TITLE to a fixed word after the return, calls f, and
      #   prints TITLE; the release step writes the output tag of the step p into
      #   its script.
      # reason: STOP is not set in the step, so f
      #   returns before the assignment, TITLE holds the title when echo runs,
      #   and the step prints the title.
      # attack: the attacker opens an issue titled x ##[set-output
      #   name=tag;]$(id).
      # attack-run-behavior: the step prints the title, the runner sets the
      #   output tag to $(id), and the release step runs id.
      on: issues
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        j:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - id: p
              env:
                TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
              run: |
                f() { [ -z "$STOP" ] && return; TITLE=safe; }
                f
                echo "issue: $TITLE"
            - run: ./release.sh "${{ steps.p.outputs.tag }}"
      ```
    - controlled.no-caller.action.yml (action-metadata, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a composite action with no caller among the files that the
      #   linter reads; the step p, which has an id, prints the title of an issue,
      #   and the next step, which runs ./release.sh, writes the output tag of the
      #   step p into the script of the next step.
      # reason: with no caller among the files that the linter reads, the rule
      #   reads the action on every event an attacker triggers, issues among the
      #   events. The runner reads ##[set-output name=NAME;] anywhere in a printed
      #   line as a command that sets the output NAME of a step with an id, even
      #   when ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS is not set, and the title is the
      #   attacker's.
      # attack: the attacker opens an issue titled x ##[set-output
      #   name=tag;]$(id).
      # attack-run-behavior: the step p prints the value, the runner sets the
      #   output tag of the step p to $(id), and the next step writes the output
      #   into the script of the next step and runs id, with the token and the
      #   secrets of the job.
      name: release
      description: release the tag
      runs:
        using: composite
        steps:
          - id: p
            env:
              TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
            run: |
              echo "issue: $TITLE"
            shell: bash
          - run: ./release.sh "${{ steps.p.outputs.tag }}"
            shell: bash
      ```
    - controlled.remote-callee.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
      #   the repository example-org/set-output-injection-remote, which the fact
      #   workflow.definition answers with the workflow of the true positive
      #   controlled (controlled.custom-shell-xtrace.yml) of the rule, with on:
      #   workflow_call in place of the on of controlled.custom-shell-xtrace.yml.
      #   The job passes its secrets with secrets: inherit. In the true positive,
      #   on issues, the step p, which has an id and whose shell: is bash -x {0},
      #   passes the title of the issue to git log, and the release step writes
      #   the output tag of the step p into its script.
      # reason: the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event that started the
      #   run of the calling job, so the reason of the true positive holds: bash
      #   -x starts the script with the trace on, as set -x does, so the trace
      #   prints the command with the title on the standard error, where the
      #   runner reads ##[set-output name=NAME;] anywhere in a line as a command
      #   that sets the output NAME of a step with an id; the title is the
      #   attacker's.
      # attack: the attacker opens an issue titled x ##[set-output
      #   name=tag;]$(id).
      # attack-run-behavior: the trace prints the git log command with the title,
      #   the runner sets the output tag of the step to $(id), and the release
      #   step writes the output into its script and runs id, with the token and
      #   the secrets of the job.
      on: issues
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        c:
          uses: example-org/set-output-injection-remote/.github/workflows/w.yml@v1
          secrets: inherit
      ```
    - controlled.skipped-assignment.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issues, the step p passes the title of the issue in the
      #   environment variable TITLE, defines a function f that sets TITLE to a
      #   fixed word only when Q is set, calls f, and prints TITLE; the release
      #   step writes the output tag of the step p into its script.
      # reason: Q is not set in the step, so f is not
      #   defined, the call fails, TITLE holds the title when echo runs, and the
      #   step prints the title.
      # attack: the attacker opens an issue titled x ##[set-output
      #   name=tag;]$(id).
      # attack-run-behavior: the step prints the title, the runner sets the output
      #   tag to $(id), and the release step runs id.
      on: issues
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        j:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - id: p
              env:
                TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
              run: |
                if [ -n "$Q" ]; then f() { TITLE=safe; }; fi
                f
                echo "issue: $TITLE"
            - run: ./release.sh "${{ steps.p.outputs.tag }}"
      ```
    - controlled.status-commit.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on status, which an app outside GitHub Actions starts when the
      #   app writes a status for a commit, the job writes the message of the
      #   commit of the status (github.event.commit.commit.message) into a run,
      #   before a step that reads an output.
      # reason: an outside CI that writes a status for a commit of a pull request
      #   from a fork starts a run of status on the default branch, with the
      #   message of that commit, which the author of the pull request writes, in
      #   the payload (seen on GitHub).
      # attack-value: github.event.commit.commit.message = "::set-output name=tag::v9"
      # attack-run-behavior: an outside CI writes a status for the commit of the
      #   pull request from a fork whose message is the value; the run of status
      #   starts on the default branch, and the message, printed by the run, sets
      #   the output tag of the step to v9, which the next step reads.
      on: status
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        j:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - id: p
              run: echo "${{ github.event.commit.commit.message }}"
            - run: ./release.sh "${{ steps.p.outputs.tag }}"
      ```
    - controlled.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issues, the step p, which has an id, prints the title of
      #   the issue, and the release step writes the output tag of the step p
      #   into its script.
      # reason: the runner reads ##[set-output name=NAME;] anywhere in a
      #   printed line as a command that sets the output NAME of a step with
      #   an id, with no ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS, and the title is the
      #   attacker's.
      # attack: the attacker opens an issue titled x ##[set-output
      #   name=tag;]$(id).
      # attack-run-behavior: the step prints the value, the runner sets the
      #   output tag of the step to $(id), and the release step writes the
      #   output into its script and runs id, with the token and the secrets
      #   of the job.
      on: issues
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        j:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - id: p
              env:
                TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
              run: |
                echo "issue: $TITLE"
            - run: ./release.sh "${{ steps.p.outputs.tag }}"
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - controlled.pusher.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on push, the step p prints the name and the email of the
      #   pusher, and the release step writes the output tag of the step p into
      #   its script.
      # reason: the pusher is the account that pushed, or, for a push that the
      #   merge of a pull request makes, the account that merged the pull request. A
      #   push and a merge need a credential that can push or merge, such as an
      #   account with the role write or above, and the credential premise assumes
      #   that no attacker holds such a credential when the attack starts, so no
      #   attacker writes the name or the email of the pusher.
      # attack: the author of a pull request writes x ##[set-output
      #   name=tag;]$(id) in the name or the email of the account of the author, and
      #   an account that can merge merges the pull request.
      # attack-run-behavior: for a merge commit and for a squash, the pusher of
      #   the push that the merge makes is the account that merged the pull request,
      #   so the step prints the name and the email of the account that merged the
      #   pull request, and the runner sets no output from the account of the
      #   author.
      on: push
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        j:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - id: p
              run: echo "pushed by ${{ github.event.pusher.name }} <${{ github.event.pusher.email }}>"
            - run: ./release.sh "${{ steps.p.outputs.tag }}"
      ```
    - controlled.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issues, a step with no id prints the title of the issue.
      # reason: the runner keeps the outputs of a step only when the step has
      #   an id, so a set-output command in the title sets nothing that a
      #   later step reads.
      # attack: the attacker opens an issue titled x ##[set-output
      #   name=tag;]$(id).
      # attack-run-behavior: the runner warns that set-output is deprecated,
      #   and no step reads an output of the step.
      on: issues
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        j:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
              run: |
                echo "issue: $TITLE"
            - run: echo next
      ```

### undetected forms

- fork-review: a job on pull_request_review or pull_request_review_comment that runs only for a pull request from a fork, such as a job whose if: condition is github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name != github.repository: the run of a review that the attacker writes on the pull request of another person from a fork has the secrets of the repository or a token that writes only where a private repository gives secrets or a token that writes to the runs of pull requests from forks (repo.fork-pr-secrets, repo.fork-pr-write-tokens). The rule does not read the facts repo.fork-pr-secrets and repo.fork-pr-write-tokens for the runs of a review, and does not count the run of a review of a pull request from a fork as a run of the attacker. When the attacker opened the pull request from a fork, a review of that pull request gives the attacker nothing more than the pull request itself gives: the run takes the workflow of the merge commit of the pull request (GitHub's documentation gives refs/pull/&lt;n>/merge as the ref of the run of a review), and the attacker can change that workflow in the pull request
  - finding kinds: set-output-injection.controlled
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: fork-review.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on comments on the diff, the step p prints the comment's body
    #   and a later step passes the output tag of the step p to ./release.sh,
    #   in a job that runs only for a pull request from a fork.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the job runs only for a pull request from a
    #   fork. Where a private repository gives secrets or a token that writes
    #   to the runs of pull requests from forks, the run of a review that the
    #   attacker writes on the pull request of another person from a fork has
    #   those secrets or that token, and the job runs for the attacker.
    # cause: the rule does not read the settings of a private repository for
    #   the runs of pull requests from forks, and does not count the run of a
    #   review of a pull request from a fork as a run of the attacker.
    # attack-value: github.event.comment.body = "::set-output name=tag::v9.9.9-PWNED"
    # attack-run-behavior: the comment of the attacker on the diff of the pull
    #   request of another person from a fork starts the job a; the runner
    #   reads the printed line as the command set-output, and ./release.sh
    #   gets v9.9.9-PWNED as the tag.
    on: pull_request_review_comment
    jobs:
      a:
        if: github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name != github.repository
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: p
            env:
              B: ${{ github.event.comment.body }}
            run: echo "c=$B"
          - run: ./release.sh "${{ steps.p.outputs.tag }}"
    ```
- if-compared: a value that an if compares with strings that the workflow writes in the if (strings compared by == with the value and joined by ||, or the strings of contains(fromJSON('&#91;...]'), value)), where each string has only ASCII letters, digits, spaces, -, \_, . and /, does not start with -, and has no - right after a space. The if of the job limits the value in every step of the job, and the if of a step with a run: script limits the value in that step only. In those steps the value equals one of the strings when the case of the letters is ignored, so the rule does not report the value. The attacker still chooses the case of each letter of the value. GitHub's server, which evaluates the if of a job, also takes the Kelvin sign as equal to the letter k and the long s as equal to the letter s; the runner, which evaluates the if of a step, takes the Kelvin sign as equal to the letter k. Where the case of a letter changes what the value names, such as a command, a variable, a file on a file system that tells names apart by their case (the default file system of a Linux runner), a host or a tool, the choice of the case can cause harm
  - finding kinds: set-output-injection.controlled
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: if-compared.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issue_comment, a job runs only when the comment's body is
    #   tag, and a step that has an id prints a set-output command whose name
    #   is ${{ github.event.comment.body }}; the step has an id, so the runner
    #   sets the outputs of the step from the workflow commands that the step
    #   prints.
    # reason: the job's if lets the body be only the string tag, ignoring the
    #   case of its letters, so the body is no workflow command; the attacker
    #   still chooses the case of the name of the output, and the author of
    #   this example has not checked whether the case of the name of an output
    #   changes which output a later step reads.
    # cause: the rule does not treat a value that the if of the job compares
    #   with such a string as written by the attacker.
    # attack-value: github.event.comment.body = "TAG"
    # attack-run-behavior: the if passes, and the step prints
    #   ::set-output name=TAG::v1.
    on:
      issue_comment:
        types: [created]
    jobs:
      j:
        if: github.event.comment.body == 'tag'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: p
            run: echo "::set-output name=${{ github.event.comment.body }}::v1"
    ```
- pull-request: a job that runs only on pull_request, in one of two cases. In the first case, only the pull requests of the repository run the workflow: the author of a pull request can change the workflow itself, so the run of the job gives the author what the run has (read-only from a fork, or what a private repository sends to the runs of pull requests from forks: secrets, a token that writes) without the flaw of the rule, and the flaw of the rule adds nothing to what the author gets. In the second case, a ruleset of the organization or the enterprise runs the workflow on the pull requests of its other repositories (Require workflows to pass before merging, of GitHub Enterprise): the author of such a pull request cannot change the workflow, and whether the run has more than the pull_request workflow of the author would get (the token, secrets) is known from GitHub's documentation only, as no such run was observed; making a required check pass is outside the threat model of the rule. The workflow does not say which case holds, and the rule does not read which case holds
  - finding kinds: set-output-injection.controlled
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: pull-request.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request, the step p prints the title of the pull
    #   request, and the release step writes the output tag of the step p
    #   into its script.
    # reason: when only the pull requests of the repository run the workflow, the
    #   author of the pull request can change the workflow itself and gets what the
    #   run has without the flaw, so the flaw adds nothing to what the author gets;
    #   when a ruleset of the organization or the enterprise runs the workflow on
    #   the pull requests of its other repositories, the author cannot change the
    #   workflow, and what the run of the ruleset has beyond the author's own
    #   pull_request workflow is not known. The workflow does not say which case
    #   holds.
    # cause: the rule does not count pull_request as an event of an attacker. The
    #   rule does not read whether a ruleset runs the workflow.
    # attack: the author of a pull request from a fork titles the pull
    #   request x ##[set-output name=tag;]$(id).
    # attack-run-behavior: the runner sets the output tag, and the release step
    #   runs id with what the run of the pull request has. When a ruleset of the
    #   organization runs the workflow on a pull request of another repository, the
    #   same steps run in the run of the ruleset; what the run of the ruleset has
    #   was not observed, so whether the steps do harm in the run of the ruleset is
    #   not known.
    on: pull_request
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: p
            run: echo "${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}"
          - run: ./release.sh "${{ steps.p.outputs.tag }}"
    ```
- dispatch: a value of the event of workflow_dispatch other than its inputs, in a job that runs only on workflow_dispatch: the event has the ref, which is a branch or a tag that the repository already has, and values that GitHub fills, such as the login of the account that dispatches the workflow; the event has no text of an issue, a comment or a pull request. Whoever dispatches the workflow chooses the ref and the inputs of the dispatch, and nothing else of the event. A token that cannot change the files of the repository can dispatch the workflow, such as a fine-grained token that has the permission Actions with write access and no permission Contents. The rule reports an input of the dispatch with the inconclusive kind input-dispatch
  - finding kinds: set-output-injection.controlled
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: dispatch.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on workflow_dispatch, the step p prints the title of the issue,
    #   and the release step writes the output tag of the step p into its
    #   script. If the workflow also ran on issues, the rule would report the
    #   same steps.
    # reason: no added gain: on workflow_dispatch the event has no issue object,
    #   so the expression of the title gives an empty string; whoever dispatches
    #   the workflow chooses the ref and the inputs of the dispatch, and the steps
    #   read no input.
    # cause: the table of the attacker's events that the rule reads does not
    #   have workflow_dispatch; the rule reports an input of a dispatch with the
    #   inconclusive kind input-dispatch.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "x ##[set-output name=tag;]$(id)"
    # attack-run-behavior: with the value put in, the step prints the value, the
    #   runner sets the output tag of the step to $(id), and the release step
    #   writes the output into its script and runs id. On workflow_dispatch the
    #   event has no issue object, though: the expression gives an empty string,
    #   and the step prints an empty line.
    on: workflow_dispatch
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: p
            run: echo "${{ github.event.issue.title }}"
          - run: ./release.sh "${{ steps.p.outputs.tag }}"
    ```
- repository-dispatch: a value of the client_payload of repository_dispatch (github.event.client_payload): only a credential with write access to the permission Contents of the repository can send repository_dispatch, and the credential premise assumes that no attacker holds such a credential; the sender chooses the whole client_payload
  - finding kinds: set-output-injection.controlled
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: repository-dispatch.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on repository_dispatch, the step p prints the value title of
    #   the client_payload, and the release step writes the output tag of the step
    #   p into its script.
    # reason: the form adds nothing to what the attacker gets (the disposition
    #   no-added-gain): only a credential with write access to the permission
    #   Contents of the repository can send repository_dispatch, and the
    #   credential premise assumes that no attacker holds such a credential; the
    #   sender chooses the whole client_payload.
    # cause: the table of the attacker's events that the rule reads leaves out
    #   repository_dispatch on purpose: the credential premise leaves the sender
    #   of repository_dispatch out of the threat model.
    # attack-value: github.event.client_payload.title = "x ##[set-output name=tag;]$(id)"
    # attack-run-behavior: when a repository_dispatch with the value in its
    #   client_payload runs the workflow, the step p prints the value, the runner
    #   sets the output tag of the step p to $(id), and the release step writes
    #   the output into its script and runs id.
    on: repository_dispatch
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: p
            run: echo "${{ github.event.client_payload.title }}"
          - run: ./release.sh "${{ steps.p.outputs.tag }}"
    ```
- app-written: a value that an app outside GitHub Actions writes into a field of a commit status or a check run (the fields context, description and target_url of status; the fields name, output, details_url and external_id of check_run): the app may copy a value of a pull request from a fork into the field, such as the name of a job that a configuration file of the pull request gives to an outside CI; the rule reads the field as a field whose value the app chooses
  - finding kinds: set-output-injection.controlled
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: app-written.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on check_run, which an app outside GitHub Actions starts when
    #   the app makes a check run for a commit, the job writes the name of the
    #   check run (github.event.check_run.name) where the rule reads it.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the app writes the name of the check run, and an
    #   app may copy a value of a pull request from a fork into the name, such
    #   as the name of a job that a configuration file of the pull request gives
    #   to an outside CI.
    # cause: the table of what an attacker controls reads the values that the
    #   app writes into a commit status or a check run as the values that the
    #   app chooses.
    # attack-value: github.event.check_run.name = "::set-output name=tag::v9"
    # attack-run-behavior: an outside CI copies the name of a job from the
    #   configuration file of the pull request from a fork into the name of the
    #   check run; the run of check_run starts on the default branch, and the
    #   value does there what the attack value of the message of the commit does
    #   on status.
    on: check_run
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: p
            run: echo "${{ github.event.check_run.name }}"
          - run: ./release.sh "${{ steps.p.outputs.tag }}"
    ```
- deployment-status: a value of the payload of deployment_status, such as the SHA of the deployment (deployment.sha), when an app outside GitHub Actions makes a deployment and a status of the deployment for a commit of a pull request from a fork: no run of deployment_status started when the authors of the linter tried this, and why the run did not start was not found; the rule does not read deployment_status as an event that an attacker starts
  - finding kinds: set-output-injection.controlled
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: deployment-status.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on deployment_status, which an app outside GitHub Actions
    #   starts when the app makes a status of a deployment, the job writes the
    #   description of the deployment (github.event.deployment.description)
    #   where the rule reads it.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): no run of deployment_status started when a GitHub
    #   App made a deployment and a status of the deployment for a commit of a
    #   pull request from a fork (seen on GitHub), and why the run did not start
    #   was not found.
    # cause: the table of the attacker's events that the rule reads does not
    #   have deployment_status.
    # attack-value: github.event.deployment.description = "::set-output name=tag::v9"
    # attack-run-behavior: an outside app makes a deployment for the commit of
    #   the pull request from a fork with a description that the pull request
    #   gives, and a status of the deployment; if a run of deployment_status
    #   starts on the default branch, the value does there what the attack value
    #   of the message of the commit does on status.
    on: deployment_status
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: p
            run: echo "${{ github.event.deployment.description }}"
          - run: ./release.sh "${{ steps.p.outputs.tag }}"
    ```
- dispatch-relay: a workflow on an event of an attacker that puts a value the attacker writes into the client_payload of a repository_dispatch that the workflow sends (gh api with client_payload to the endpoint dispatches, peter-evans/repository-dispatch), and a workflow on repository_dispatch that uses the value: the flaw is in the workflow that sends the repository_dispatch, and the rule does not read what a workflow sends to another workflow
  - finding kinds: set-output-injection.controlled
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - example: .github/workflows/receiver.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: sender.yml runs on issues opened, and with the GITHUB_TOKEN
    #   sends a repository_dispatch of the type relay whose client_payload has the
    #   title of the issue as the value title; receiver.yml runs on that
    #   repository_dispatch, and the step p prints the value title of the
    #   client_payload, and the release step writes the output tag of the step p
    #   into its script.
    # reason: the author of the issue writes the value, and sender.yml relays
    #   the value to receiver.yml in a repository_dispatch that a run of the
    #   repository sends with a token of the repository; GitHub creates a workflow
    #   run for a repository_dispatch sent with the GITHUB_TOKEN, as an exception
    #   to the rule that an event that the GITHUB_TOKEN triggers creates no
    #   workflow run.
    # cause: the rule reads the events of each workflow alone, and does not read
    #   what a workflow sends to another workflow as the client_payload of a
    #   repository_dispatch.
    # attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "x ##[set-output name=tag;]$(id)"
    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens an issue whose title is the value;
    #   sender.yml sends the value, and in the run of receiver.yml the step p
    #   prints the value, the runner sets the output tag of the step p to $(id),
    #   and the release step writes the output into its script and runs id.
    on:
      repository_dispatch:
        types: [relay]
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: p
            run: echo "${{ github.event.client_payload.title }}"
          - run: ./release.sh "${{ steps.p.outputs.tag }}"
    ```
    - .github/workflows/sender.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on:
        issues:
          types: [opened]
      permissions:
        contents: write
      jobs:
        relay:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - env:
                GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
                VALUE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
              run: gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/dispatches" -f event_type=relay -f "client_payload[title]=$VALUE"
      ```
- dispatch-input-call: an input of workflow_dispatch that a caller of the same repository passes, as an input of the call (under the key with: of the calling job or step), to a reusable workflow or a composite action, which uses the input as a value: the one who dispatches the caller chooses the value, and the rule reads the events of a called workflow or action from the table of the callers, and does not follow the value of an input of workflow_dispatch that the caller gives
  - finding kinds: set-output-injection.controlled
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - example: .github/workflows/called.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: caller.yml runs on workflow_dispatch with the input x, and
    #   calls called.yml with the input x of the dispatch as the input x of
    #   called.yml; called.yml prints the input x in the step p, and the release
    #   step writes the output tag of the step p into its script.
    # reason: the one who dispatches caller.yml chooses the value:
    #   input-dispatch reports such a value where a workflow on workflow_dispatch
    #   refers to its input directly, but through the call the value is the input
    #   x of called.yml.
    # cause: the rule reads the events of a called workflow from the table of
    #   the callers, and does not follow the value of an input of
    #   workflow_dispatch that a caller gives in with.
    # attack-value: inputs.x = "x ##[set-output name=tag;]$(id)"
    # attack-run-behavior: when the one who dispatches caller.yml gives the
    #   value as x, the step p prints the value, the runner sets the output tag of
    #   the step p to $(id), and the release step writes the output into its
    #   script and runs id.
    on:
      workflow_call:
        inputs:
          x: {type: string}
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: p
            run: echo "${{ inputs.x }}"
          - run: ./release.sh "${{ steps.p.outputs.tag }}"
    ```
    - .github/workflows/caller.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on:
        workflow_dispatch:
          inputs:
            x: {type: string}
      jobs:
        call:
          uses: ./.github/workflows/called.yml
          with:
            x: ${{ inputs.x }}
          secrets: inherit
      ```
- not-attacker: secrets, vars, runner, the outcome of a step, the result of a job. A run of the linter that adds the attacker variables-writer reports a reference of vars where the rule reads the value as written by the attacker, and a run of the linter that adds the attacker secrets-writer reports such a reference of secrets except secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN (--add-attacker); no run reports runner, the outcome of a step or the result of a job
  - finding kinds: set-output-injection.controlled
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - added attackers: variables-writer, secrets-writer
  - example: not-attacker.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, the step p prints the variable RELEASE_TAG and the
    #   secret RELEASE_NOTE, which reach the step through env. The step p also
    #   prints runner.os. The release step writes the output tag of the step p
    #   into its script.
    # reason: no added gain in a run that adds no attacker: no attacker writes
    #   vars, secrets or runner.os, and one who may change the repository's
    #   settings sets the variable and the secret. A run of the linter that adds
    #   variables-writer (--add-attacker) reports the variable, a run that adds
    #   secrets-writer reports the secret, and no run reports runner.os.
    # cause: the rule does not count vars, secrets and runner as values of an
    #   attacker.
    # attack: one who may change the repository's settings sets RELEASE_TAG to
    #   x ##[set-output name=tag;]$(id); in a run that adds no attacker, no
    #   attacker can set the variable.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step prints the values; no attacker sets the
    #   output tag.
    on: issues
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: p
            env:
              TAG: ${{ vars.RELEASE_TAG }}
              NOTE: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_NOTE }}
            run: |
              echo "tag: $TAG"
              echo "note: $NOTE"
              echo "${{ runner.os }}"
          - run: ./release.sh "${{ steps.p.outputs.tag }}"
    ```
- merged-pusher: a value that the author of a pull request writes in the profile of the account of the author (the profile name, the public email of the profile), in github.event.pull_request.merged_by of a merged pull request, or in github.event.pusher of the push that GitHub makes when GitHub merges a pull request by a rebase, by auto-merge or from a merge queue: the rule reads merged_by and the pusher as the account that merged or pushed, and the account that merged or pushed holds a credential that can merge or push; whether GitHub sets merged_by of a merged pull request, or the pusher of the push that GitHub makes when GitHub merges a pull request by a rebase, by auto-merge or from a merge queue, to the account of the author of the merged pull request was not checked
  - finding kinds: set-output-injection.controlled
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: merged-pusher.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on a pull request that is closed, the step p prints the name of
    #   the account that merged the pull request, and the release step writes the
    #   output tag of the step p into its script.
    # reason: whether GitHub sets merged_by of a merged pull request to the
    #   account of the author of the pull request was not checked: no payload with
    #   merged_by was seen on GitHub. Were merged_by the author, the author would
    #   write the name of merged_by, which is the profile name of the account of
    #   the author.
    # cause: the table of what an attacker controls reads merged_by as the
    #   account that merged the pull request, and the account that merged the pull
    #   request holds a credential that can merge.
    # attack: the author of a pull request writes x ##[set-output
    #   name=tag;]$(id) in the profile name of the account of the author, and the
    #   pull request is merged.
    # attack-run-behavior: were merged_by the author of the pull request, the
    #   runner would set the output tag of the step p, and the release step would
    #   run id.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [closed]
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: p
            env:
              MERGER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.merged_by.name }}
            run: echo "merged by $MERGER"
          - run: ./release.sh "${{ steps.p.outputs.tag }}"
    ```
- compared: a context compared, negated, or given to contains, startsWith, endsWith or hashFiles: what is written out is a bool or a hash
  - finding kinds: set-output-injection.controlled
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: compared.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, the step p prints whether the title of the issue
    #   is x, and the release step writes the output tag of the step p into
    #   its script.
    # reason: no added gain: the printed value is true or false.
    # cause: the rule does not count a comparison as a value of an attacker.
    # attack: the attacker titles the issue as wished; the step prints true
    #   or false.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step prints false, and no output is set.
    on: issues
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: p
            run: echo "${{ github.event.issue.title == 'x' }}"
          - run: ./release.sh "${{ steps.p.outputs.tag }}"
    ```
- new-activity-type: an activity type GitHub added after the schemas the tables are made from, written in types: a value of types the tables do not have is dropped, as GitHub drops one it has no such activity type for
  - finding kinds: set-output-injection.controlled
  - disposition: todo (needs: pin-update)
  - example: new-activity-type.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on an activity type of issues that the tables do not have,
    #   the step p prints the title of the issue, and the release step
    #   writes the output tag of the step p into its script.
    # reason: a todo (a pin update): GitHub may add the activity type after
    #   the schemas the tables are made from.
    # cause: the rule drops an activity type that the tables do not have, as
    #   GitHub drops one with no such activity type.
    # attack: the attacker writes the title x ##[set-output name=tag;]$(id),
    #   if GitHub sends the activity type.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step prints the value, the runner sets the
    #   output tag of the step to $(id), and the release step writes the
    #   output into its script and runs id.
    on: 
      issues:
        types: [no-such-type]
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: p
            env:
              TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
            run: echo "$TITLE"
          - run: ./release.sh "${{ steps.p.outputs.tag }}"
    ```
- outside-caller: a reusable workflow or composite action that callers in the repository decide, called from another repository on an event, or with a value, an attacker controls: the caller's run has the caller's token and secrets, not the repository's
  - finding kinds: set-output-injection.controlled
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: .github/workflows/called.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the workflow is called; the step p prints
    #   github.event.issue.body, and the release step writes the output tag of
    #   the step p into its script. The one caller of the workflow in the
    #   repository, ci.yml, runs on push.
    # reason: no added gain for this repository: ci.yml calls the workflow on
    #   push alone, and github.event of a push has no issue, so the value that the
    #   run reads is not a value that an attacker wrote. Another repository may
    #   call the workflow on an event whose payload has what an attacker wrote,
    #   but that run has the token and the secrets of the other repository.
    # cause: the rule reads a called workflow on the events of its callers in
    #   the repository, and ci.yml runs on push alone.
    # attack: an attacker opens an issue in another repository whose workflow
    #   calls this one, with the body x ##[set-output name=tag;]$(id).
    # attack-run-behavior: called by ci.yml on push, the event has no issue, so
    #   the step prints an empty line. Called on issues by another repository,
    #   the runner sets the output tag in that run, and the release step runs
    #   id there.
    on:
      workflow_call:
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: p
            env:
              BODY: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
            run: echo "$BODY"
          - run: ./release.sh "${{ steps.p.outputs.tag }}"
    ```
    - .github/workflows/ci.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: push
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        call:
          uses: ./.github/workflows/called.yml
      ```
- split-env-name: a variable named by the part of a key of env before the first =, such as A for the key A=B, which the runner sets to the rest of the key, =, and the value (in a step in a job's container, to the rest of the key alone): the rule reads a variable of env by a key equal to the name of the variable
  - finding kinds: set-output-injection.controlled
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: split-env-name.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues opened, the env of the step p has the name T=X
    #   with the title of the issue, the step p prints $T, and the release
    #   step writes the output tag of the step p into its script.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the runner makes the variable T, whose
    #   value is X= and the title, so the printed value holds the title.
    # cause: the rule reads the name T=X as written, and no variable of that
    #   name is printed.
    # attack: the attacker writes x ##[set-output name=tag;]$(id) in the
    #   value.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step prints the value, the runner sets the
    #   output tag of the step to $(id), and the release step writes the
    #   output into its script and runs id.
    on:
      issues:
        types: [opened]
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: p
            env:
              T=X: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
            run: echo "$T"
          - run: ./release.sh "${{ steps.p.outputs.tag }}"
    ```
- other-shell: a run of pwsh, cmd or python, and a run whose shell the rule cannot determine to be bash or sh: a shell: value whose command is not bash or sh, such as pwsh -File {0}; a shell: value of bash or sh with an option that the rule does not read, such as bash -c 'make' {0}, bash -v {0} or bash -O extglob {0}; a shell: value that names bash or sh by a path, such as /usr/bin/bash -e {0}, on a runner where the rule does not know that the path exists (any runner other than one whose runs-on is a single label that starts with ubuntu-, or with macos- for /bin/bash and /bin/sh) or in a step of a composite action; a shell: that is an expression; or a step without shell: whose job and workflow have no defaults.run.shell and whose job has a runs-on that is not a single label that starts with ubuntu-, macos- or windows-, such as self-hosted or an expression: the rule reads the runs of bash and sh only
  - finding kinds: set-output-injection.controlled
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: other-shell.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, the step p prints the title of the issue with
    #   pwsh, and the release step writes the output tag of the step p into
    #   its script.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the runner reads the output of pwsh as
    #   it reads the output of bash.
    # cause: the rule reads bash and sh.
    # attack: the attacker writes x ##[set-output name=tag;]$(id) in the
    #   value.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step prints the value, the runner sets the
    #   output tag of the step to $(id), and the release step writes the
    #   output into its script and runs id.
    on: issues
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: p
            shell: pwsh
            env:
              TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
            run: Write-Output $env:TITLE
          - run: ./release.sh "${{ steps.p.outputs.tag }}"
    ```
- script-var: a shell variable the script sets (from a file, an API, the value of env through an assignment) or a positional parameter of a function, printed to the log
  - finding kinds: set-output-injection.controlled
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: script-var.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, the step p sets a variable of the script to the
    #   title of the issue and prints the variable, and the release step
    #   writes the output tag of the step p into its script.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the variable holds the title, which
    #   the attacker writes.
    # cause: the rule reads the variables of env, not those the script sets.
    # attack: the attacker writes x ##[set-output name=tag;]$(id) in the
    #   value.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step prints the value, the runner sets the
    #   output tag of the step to $(id), and the release step writes the
    #   output into its script and runs id.
    on: issues
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: p
            env:
              TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
            run: |
              T="$TITLE"
              echo "$T"
          - run: ./release.sh "${{ steps.p.outputs.tag }}"
    ```
- other-output: a value an attacker controls that a command of the run script other than echo, printf, cat and tee prints: cat of a file of a pull request, git log, jq of \$GITHUB_EVENT_PATH; also what a descriptor that exec points at the log (exec 3>&1) prints, and what goes to the log through a process substitution (exec > >(tee -a build.log))
  - finding kinds: set-output-injection.controlled
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: other-output.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, the step p prints a file of the
    #   repository with cat, and the release step writes the output tag of
    #   the step p into its script.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): a command other than echo, printf, cat
    #   of a here-string and tee prints what the rule does not read, which
    #   may be an attacker's.
    # cause: the rule reads what echo, printf, cat and tee print of env and
    #   ${{ }}.
    # attack: an attacker whose text reaches the file writes x ##[set-output
    #   name=tag;]$(id) in the file.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step prints the value; were the value an
    #   attacker's x ##[set-output name=tag;]$(id), the runner would set the
    #   output tag of the step, and the release step would run id.
    on: pull_request_target
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - id: p
            run: cat NOTES.md
          - run: ./release.sh "${{ steps.p.outputs.tag }}"
    ```
- decoded-escape: the title of a wiki page printed by a command that decodes escapes in the value (printf with the value in its format, echo -e, printf %b): the attacker writes \\055 in the title, the command prints a - in its place, and the printed line can hold ##&#91;set-output name=NAME;]value; the rule reads the title as holding no -
  - finding kinds: set-output-injection.controlled
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: decoded-escape.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on gollum, the step p prints the title of a wiki page with
    #   printf, which reads the title as its format, and the release step writes
    #   the output tag of the step p into its script.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): printf turns \055 in the title into -, so
    #   the printed line holds ##[set-output name=tag;], which the title as
    #   written cannot hold.
    # cause: the rule reads the title of a wiki page as holding no -, and does
    #   not read which commands decode escapes.
    # attack: an attacker who may edit the wiki titles a page x
    #   ##[set\055output name=tag;]$(id).
    # attack-run-behavior: printf prints x ##[set-output name=tag;]$(id), the
    #   runner sets the output tag of the step p, and the release step runs id.
    on: gollum
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: p
            env:
              T: ${{ github.event.pages[0].title }}
            run: printf "$T\n"
          - run: ./release.sh "${{ steps.p.outputs.tag }}"
    ```
- action-output: a value an attacker controls that an action prints to the log of the step that uses the action, where the step has an id: the rule reads only the run scripts of bash and sh, not the code of an action, such as the script of actions/github-script, a local action or an action of another repository
  - finding kinds: set-output-injection.controlled
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file, repo-file, fact)
  - example: action-output.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues, the step p uses actions/github-script to log the
    #   title of the issue, and the release step writes the output tag of
    #   the step p into its script.
    # reason: a todo: the runner reads the log of the script of the action
    #   as it reads the log of a run, and the title is the attacker's.
    # cause: the rule reads the run scripts of bash and sh, not the code of
    #   an action.
    # attack: the attacker writes x ##[set-output name=tag;]$(id) in the
    #   value.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step prints the value, the runner sets the
    #   output tag of the step to $(id), and the release step writes the
    #   output into its script and runs id.
    on: issues
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: p
            uses: actions/github-script@v7
            env:
              TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
            with:
              script: console.log(process.env.TITLE)
          - run: ./release.sh "${{ steps.p.outputs.tag }}"
    ```
- insider-association: an if that lets in MEMBER or COLLABORATOR by the author_association of the issue, the pull request or the discussion the run is of, which the following pass: a member or a collaborator whose repository role is Read only, who gets, in the run, a token that writes and the secrets, more than what the Read role gives; the account of such a member or collaborator, taken over; and an outsider who becomes a MEMBER with the Read role, in an organization that lets anyone become a member (a bot that invites whoever asks). A member or a collaborator whose role is Triage or above holds a credential that can add a label or write to the repository, which the credential premise assumes no attacker holds. Who is a member, and with what role, is not in the workflow
  - finding kinds: set-output-injection.controlled
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - added attackers: read-member, triage-account, writer-issues-token, required-reviewer
  - example: insider-association.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issues opened, a job whose if lets in an issue whose
    #   author_association is MEMBER prints the body of the issue in the
    #   step p, and the release step writes the output tag of the step p
    #   into its script.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): a member of the organization, who may have read
    #   access only, passes this if (in an organization that lets anyone become a
    #   member, such as by a bot that invites whoever asks, an outsider becomes such
    #   a member), and gets the token and the secrets of the job past what the Read
    #   role gives; who is a member, and with what role, is not in the workflow.
    # cause: the rule evaluates the if with the attacker's
    #   author_association (NONE, FIRST_TIMER, FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR or
    #   CONTRIBUTOR), for which the if is false, so no attacker's event runs
    #   the job.
    # attack: a member whose role is read opens an issue whose body is x
    #   ##[set-output name=tag;]$(id).
    # attack-run-behavior: on an issue a member opens, the job runs, the
    #   runner sets the output tag, and the release step runs id. On an
    #   issue whose author_association is NONE, FIRST_TIMER,
    #   FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR or CONTRIBUTOR, the if skips the job.
    on:
      issues:
        types: [opened]
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      a:
        if: github.event.issue.author_association == 'MEMBER'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: p
            env:
              BODY: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
            run: echo "$BODY"
          - run: ./release.sh "${{ steps.p.outputs.tag }}"
    ```
- remote-callee: a job or a step inside a reusable workflow of another repository (uses: owner/repo/.github/workflows/&lt;file>@&lt;ref>) whose content the fact workflow.definition does not give. For every rule: a run that does not ask the fact (a run without --online and without the answer in --facts). For a quality rule, also: a run where the linter asked the fact and got no answer (an answer of unknown: the GitHub API did not give the file), and a call deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact. The rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition. For a rule that is not a quality rule (a rule with a threat), the last two forms are the inconclusive kind remote-callee-unknown, not this form
  - finding kinds: set-output-injection.controlled
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-callee.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
    #   the repository example-org/set-output-injection-unanswered, whose
    #   content is the workflow of the true positive controlled
    #   (controlled.custom-shell-xtrace.yml) of the rule, with on: workflow_call
    #   in place of the on of controlled.custom-shell-xtrace.yml. The linter has
    #   no answer of the fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event
    #   that started the run of the calling job, and the linter does not read
    #   the reusable workflow.
    # cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from
    #   the answer of workflow.definition.
    # attack: the attacker opens an issue titled x ##[set-output
    #   name=tag;]$(id).
    # attack-run-behavior: the trace prints the git log command with the title,
    #   the runner sets the output tag of the step to $(id), and the release
    #   step writes the output into its script and runs id, with the token and
    #   the secrets of the job.
    on: issues
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/set-output-injection-unanswered/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

### inconclusive

- structured-value: a value where whether an attacker can write ##&#91; and ] in the value was not checked, such as a structured value (a URL, or github.event.forkee.description, which is the description of a fork; the account that makes the fork writes the description, and the description holds no line break). Two kinds of structured value are not of this kind: the email of a git commit, which was checked to hold ##&#91; and ] and is reported, and the names of refs and repositories, which hold no &#91; and are not reported. The name of a wiki page (page_name) is of this kind. For a page made on the web interface of GitHub, the page name holds no blank, because GitHub turns each blank of the title into a - after trimming the blanks at the head and the end of the title; a set-output command needs a blank between the word set-output and the property name=, so the page name holds no set-output command. For a page pushed by git, the page name keeps each blank and - of the file name of the page and can hold a set-output command, and a push by git from an account with the role read or triage was not tried (GitHub refused a push by git from an account with no role in the repository). The rule cannot tell from the value which way the page was made. Any other value that an attacker controls on gollum alone is of this kind too, such as github.event.pages&#91;0]&#91;x] where x is an expression, or toJSON(github.event). The title of a wiki page is not of this kind: the title holds no -, so the title as written holds no command whose name has a -, and the rule reports nothing on the title (a command that decodes escapes can make a - of the title: decoded-escape)
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: structured-value.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on fork, the step p prints the description of the fork that
    #   the fork event is about, and the release step writes the output tag of
    #   the step p into its script.
    # reason: the account that makes the fork writes the description of the
    #   fork, and whether GitHub takes ##[ and ] in the description of a fork
    #   was not checked; GitHub refused a line break in the description of a
    #   fork.
    # cause: the table of what an attacker controls reads the description of
    #   a fork as structured, and the characters that GitHub takes in the
    #   description of a fork were not checked on GitHub.
    # attack: an attacker forks the repository and writes x ##[set-output
    #   name=tag;]$(id) as the description of the fork.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step prints the description of the fork; were
    #   the description the attacker's x ##[set-output name=tag;]$(id), the
    #   runner would set the output tag of the step p, and the release step
    #   would run id.
    on: fork
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: p
            env:
              DESCRIPTION: ${{ github.event.forkee.description }}
            run: echo "forked as $DESCRIPTION"
          - run: ./release.sh "${{ steps.p.outputs.tag }}"
    ```
- step-output-run: the output of a step that runs a script (steps.&lt;id>.outputs), which the script writes to \$GITHUB_OUTPUT
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: step-output-run.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the step s runs a script that writes the output o, the step
    #   p prints steps.s.outputs.o, and the release step writes the output
    #   tag of the step p into its script.
    # reason: the output o is what the script writes at run time, so whether
    #   an attacker controls the printed value is not known.
    # cause: the rule does not yet follow what a script writes to
    #   $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
    # attack: an attacker who controls the value writes x ##[set-output
    #   name=tag;]$(id) in the value.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step prints the value; were the value an
    #   attacker's x ##[set-output name=tag;]$(id), the runner would set the
    #   output tag of the step, and the release step would run id.
    on: issues
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: s
            run: echo "o=x" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          - id: p
            run: echo "${{ steps.s.outputs.o }}"
          - run: ./release.sh "${{ steps.p.outputs.tag }}"
    ```
- step-output-local-action: the output of a step that uses a local action (./, in the workspace of the job, which is the repository that the job checks out; \$/, the repository of the action)
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - example: step-output-local-action.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the step s uses a local action, the step p prints the
    #   output o of the step s, and the release step writes the output tag
    #   of the step p into its script.
    # reason: whether an attacker controls the output of the step s is not
    #   known.
    # cause: the rule does not read the action of the workspace.
    # attack: an attacker who controls the value writes x ##[set-output
    #   name=tag;]$(id) in the value.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step prints the value; were the value an
    #   attacker's x ##[set-output name=tag;]$(id), the runner would set the
    #   output tag of the step, and the release step would run id.
    on: issues
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: s
            uses: ./.github/actions/a
          - id: p
            run: echo "${{ steps.s.outputs.o }}"
          - run: ./release.sh "${{ steps.p.outputs.tag }}"
    ```
- step-output-remote-action: the output of a step that uses an action of another repository
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)

- step-output-docker: the output of a step that runs a Docker image (docker://), which the image writes at run time
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: step-output-docker.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the step s uses a Docker image, the step p prints the
    #   output o of the step s, and the release step writes the output tag
    #   of the step p into its script.
    # reason: whether an attacker controls the output of the step s is not
    #   known.
    # cause: what the image writes is decided at run time.
    # attack: an attacker who controls the value writes x ##[set-output
    #   name=tag;]$(id) in the value.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step prints the value; were the value an
    #   attacker's x ##[set-output name=tag;]$(id), the runner would set the
    #   output tag of the step, and the release step would run id.
    on: issues
    permissions: {}

        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    ```

- job-output: the output of another job of the workflow (needs.&lt;id>.outputs)
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: job-output.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the job a writes the output o from a script, the step p of
    #   the job b prints needs.a.outputs.o, and the release step writes the
    #   output tag of the step p into its script.
    # reason: the output o is what the script of the job a writes at run
    #   time.
    # cause: the rule does not yet follow the outputs of another job.
    # attack: an attacker who controls the value writes x ##[set-output
    #   name=tag;]$(id) in the value.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step prints the value; were the value an
    #   attacker's x ##[set-output name=tag;]$(id), the runner would set the
    #   output tag of the step, and the release step would run id.
    on: issues
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        outputs:
          o: ${{ steps.s.outputs.o }}
        steps:
          - id: s
            run: echo "o=x" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      b:
        needs: a
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: p
            run: echo "${{ needs.a.outputs.o }}"
          - run: ./release.sh "${{ steps.p.outputs.tag }}"
    ```

- job-output-remote-call: the output of a job that calls a reusable workflow of another repository
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)

- input-dispatch: an input of workflow_dispatch (inputs, github.event.inputs): whoever dispatches the workflow chooses the value of the input. A credential whose only write access is to the permission Actions can dispatch the workflow, and the credential premise keeps the holder of such a credential as a possible attacker; the linter does not know whether such a credential exists or who holds it. The rule reports the value in a job with an environment that has required reviewers too, where a required reviewer of the environment can stop the run
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: dispatcher)
  - example: input-dispatch.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on workflow_dispatch, the step p prints the input x, and
    #   the release step writes the output tag of the step p into its
    #   script.
    # reason: whoever dispatches the workflow chooses the input.
    # cause: the rule leaves the inputs of a dispatch to who dispatches.
    # attack: an attacker who controls the value writes x ##[set-output
    #   name=tag;]$(id) in the value.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step prints the value; were the value an
    #   attacker's x ##[set-output name=tag;]$(id), the runner would set the
    #   output tag of the step, and the release step would run id.
    on:
      workflow_dispatch:
        inputs:
          x: {}
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: p
            run: echo "${{ inputs.x }}"
          - run: ./release.sh "${{ steps.p.outputs.tag }}"
    ```
- input-call: an input of a reusable workflow or a composite action (inputs), which the caller gives
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file, fact)
  - example: input-call.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a reusable workflow prints its input x in the step p, and
    #   the release step writes the output tag of the step p into its
    #   script; no caller is in the repository.
    # reason: the caller gives the input x.
    # cause: the rule does not know what a caller of another repository
    #   gives.
    # attack: an attacker who controls the value writes x ##[set-output
    #   name=tag;]$(id) in the value.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step prints the value; were the value an
    #   attacker's x ##[set-output name=tag;]$(id), the runner would set the
    #   output tag of the step, and the release step would run id.
    on:
      workflow_call:
        inputs:
          x:
            type: string
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: p
            run: echo "${{ inputs.x }}"
          - run: ./release.sh "${{ steps.p.outputs.tag }}"
    ```
- matrix: a value of a matrix that is not written out in the workflow
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: matrix.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the step p prints a value of the matrix that comes from
    #   vars, and the release step writes the output tag of the step p into
    #   its script.
    # reason: the value of the matrix is not written out in the workflow.
    # cause: the rule does not read vars.
    # attack: an attacker who controls the value writes x ##[set-output
    #   name=tag;]$(id) in the value.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step prints the value; were the value an
    #   attacker's x ##[set-output name=tag;]$(id), the runner would set the
    #   output tag of the step, and the release step would run id.
    on: issues
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        strategy:
          matrix:
            include:

        steps:
    ```

- env-unset: an env the workflow does not set, which a step before may set at run time (\$GITHUB_ENV)
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file, fact)
  - example: env-unset.yml (workflow, inconclusive)

    ```yaml
    # cause: the rule does not read what the steps write to $GITHUB_ENV at

    #   name=tag;]$(id) in the value.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step prints the value; were the value an
    #   attacker's x ##[set-output name=tag;]$(id), the runner would set the
    #   output tag of the step, and the release step would run id.
    on: issues

    ```
- env-dynamic: a variable of the env of the workflow, a job or a step, where the whole env of the workflow, the job or the step is one \${{ }}
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: env-dynamic.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the env of the job is one ${{ }}, the step p prints env.X,
    #   and the release step writes the output tag of the step p into its
    #   script.
    # reason: the variables of the env of the job are decided at run time.
    # cause: the rule does not evaluate the env of the job.
    # attack: an attacker who controls the value writes x ##[set-output
    #   name=tag;]$(id) in the value.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step prints the value; were the value an
    #   attacker's x ##[set-output name=tag;]$(id), the runner would set the
    #   output tag of the step, and the release step would run id.
    on: issues
    permissions: {}

      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        env: ${{ fromJSON(vars.E) }}

          - id: p

          - run: ./release.sh "${{ steps.p.outputs.tag }}"
    ```
- env-whole: the whole env (toJSON(env)), or an env whose name is not known, which has what steps set at run time
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file, fact)
  - example: env-whole.yml (workflow, inconclusive)

    ```yaml
    # situation: the step p prints toJSON(env), and the release step writes
    #   the output tag of the step p into its script.
    # reason: the whole env has what the steps set at run time.
    # cause: the rule does not read the env that the steps set at run time.
    # attack: an attacker who controls the value writes x ##[set-output
    #   name=tag;]$(id) in the value.
    # attack-run-behavior: the step prints the value; were the value an
    #   attacker's x ##[set-output name=tag;]$(id), the runner would set the
    #   output tag of the step, and the release step would run id.
    on: issues
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
    ```
