  - true negatives:
    - private+public.masked-env-output.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on push, in a public repository or in a private one, the env
      #   of the job `read` has the whole secret TOKEN, and an output of the job
      #   `read` has env.TOKEN and the password of the JSON secret DB; the later
      #   job `print` prints the output.
      # reason: env.TOKEN is the value of the secret TOKEN, which the runner
      #   masks, and the runner drops an output whose value contains a value that
      #   the runner masks, so the job `print` gets an empty value.
      # attack: one who may read the log of the run opens the log of the job
      #   `print` to read the password.
      # attack-run-behavior: the job `read` warns that it skips the output
      #   credential since the output may contain a secret; the header of the
      #   step of the job `print` shows the run: script of the step with an empty
      #   value.
      on: push
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        read:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          env:
            TOKEN: ${{ secrets.TOKEN }}
          outputs:
            credential: ${{ env.TOKEN }}-${{ fromJSON(secrets.DB).pass }}
          steps:
            - run: echo read
        print:
          needs: read
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: echo "${{ needs.read.outputs.credential }}"
      ```
    - private+public.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on push, in a public repository or in a private one, a step
      #   reads the client id and the client secret from two secrets, one for
      #   each value.
      # reason: each value is a whole secret, which the runner masks wherever the
      #   log has it, the header of the step included.
      # attack: one who may read the run's log opens it to read the client
      #   secret.
      # attack-run-behavior: the header of the step prints CLIENT_ID and
      #   CLIENT_SECRET as ***.
      on: push
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        deploy:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - name: log in to azure
              env:
                CLIENT_ID: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
                CLIENT_SECRET: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET }}
              run: az login --service-principal -u "$CLIENT_ID" -p "$CLIENT_SECRET" --tenant contoso.onmicrosoft.com
      ```
    - public.never-runs.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on push, the job whose id is disabled has if: false, and the job
      #   whose id is on-failure needs the job build and has if: needs.build.result
      #   == 'failure'; each of the two jobs puts values that fromJSON takes out of
      #   the secret AZURE_CREDENTIALS in the env of a step.
      # reason: GitHub skips the job disabled because the if of the job disabled is
      #   false. The if of the job on-failure calls no status function, so GitHub
      #   evaluates the if of the job on-failure only when the job build succeeded;
      #   needs.build.result is then success, and the if is false. When the job
      #   build fails or is skipped, GitHub skips the job on-failure without
      #   evaluating the if. So neither job runs
      #   (https://github.com/github/docs/blob/404a5f4de6cd5311e3ce2d5c076571291e0107d6/data/reusables/actions/jobs/section-using-conditions-to-control-job-execution.md).
      # attack: anyone signed in to GitHub opens the log of the run and reads the
      #   header of the step.
      # attack-run-behavior: GitHub skips the job disabled and the job on-failure,
      #   so the runner prints no header of the step, and the values are not in the
      #   log.
      on: push
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: echo built
        disabled:
          if: false
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - name: log in to azure
              env:
                CLIENT_ID: ${{ fromJSON(secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS).clientId }}
                CLIENT_SECRET: ${{ fromJSON(secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS).clientSecret }}
              run: az login --service-principal -u "$CLIENT_ID" -p "$CLIENT_SECRET" --tenant contoso.onmicrosoft.com
        on-failure:
          needs: build
          if: needs.build.result == 'failure'
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - name: log in to azure
              env:
                CLIENT_ID: ${{ fromJSON(secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS).clientId }}
                CLIENT_SECRET: ${{ fromJSON(secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS).clientSecret }}
              run: az login --service-principal -u "$CLIENT_ID" -p "$CLIENT_SECRET" --tenant contoso.onmicrosoft.com
      ```

### undetected forms

- debug-if: a value taken out of a secret by fromJSON in an if, through an env that holds the secret, as an if cannot refer to the secrets context (env: CONFIG: \${{ secrets.CONFIG }} and if: fromJSON(env.CONFIG).user != ''): a rerun with debug logging prints, in the log of the run, the values that the if evaluates; a credential with read access to the repository can open the log, and a credential whose only write access is to the permission Actions can start the rerun; on 2026-10-23 a rerun with debug logging printed the value that fromJSON took out of a JSON literal in an if, in the lines ##&#91;debug]Evaluating and ##&#91;debug]Expanded. In the workflow file, the rule reads only the places whose values the header of a step prints in the log (the env, the run, the with and the name of the step), and not the if
  - finding kinds: unmasked-secret-exposure.private, unmasked-secret-exposure.public
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: debug-if.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, the env CONFIG of the job holds the secret CONFIG, and
    #   the if of a step compares the value user, which fromJSON takes out of
    #   env.CONFIG, with an empty string (an if cannot refer to the secrets
    #   context itself).
    # reason: a rerun with debug logging prints the values that the if
    #   evaluates, and the runner does not mask a value that fromJSON takes out of
    #   a secret; a credential whose only write access is to the permission
    #   Actions can start the rerun, and the credential premise keeps the holder
    #   of such a credential as a possible attacker. The authors of the linter did
    #   not check whether the rerun prints a value taken out of a secret, as the
    #   observation used a JSON literal.
    # cause: in the workflow file, the rule reads only the places whose values
    #   the header of a step prints in the log (the env, the run, the with and the
    #   name of the step), and not the if.
    # attack: the attacker reruns the run with debug logging, with a credential
    #   whose only write access is to the permission Actions, and reads the log
    #   of the rerun.
    # attack-run-behavior: on 2026-10-23, a rerun with debug logging of a step
    #   whose if took the value user out of a JSON literal by fromJSON printed
    #   the line ##[debug]Expanded: (true && ('<the value>' != '')) in the log of
    #   the step; with the secret CONFIG, the line would have the value user of
    #   the secret.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      deploy:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        env:
          CONFIG: ${{ secrets.CONFIG }}
        steps:
          - if: fromJSON(env.CONFIG).user != ''
            run: ./deploy.sh
    ```
- output-with-secret: an output of a job whose value the rule reads as having a value that the runner masks in every run, while the value has no value that the runner masks in some runs: a whole secret that is empty in some runs (a secret that is not set), an operand before && that is false in some runs (github.event_name == 'push' && env), or env&#91;INDEX] whose INDEX names a variable that the env does not have in some runs. The rule assumes that the runner drops the output, and so the rule does not follow the output to the jobs that read the output; in a run where the value has no value that the runner masks, the value taken out of a secret reaches the later job
  - finding kinds: unmasked-secret-exposure.private, unmasked-secret-exposure.public
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: output-with-secret.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, an output of the job `read` has the secret
    #   OPTIONAL_TOKEN and the password of the JSON secret DB; the repository
    #   does not set OPTIONAL_TOKEN in some forks or environments; the later job
    #   `print` prints the output.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): when OPTIONAL_TOKEN is not set, the
    #   secret is empty, the output has only the password, which the runner
    #   does not mask, so the runner keeps the output and the job `print`
    #   prints the password.
    # cause: the rule assumes that the output has a whole secret, which the
    #   runner would drop, and so does not follow the output.
    # attack: one who may read the log of the run opens the log of the job
    #   `print` in a run where OPTIONAL_TOKEN is not set.
    # attack-run-behavior: in a run where OPTIONAL_TOKEN is not set, the header
    #   of the step of the job `print` shows the run: script of the step with
    #   the password in it, unmasked.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      read:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        outputs:
          credential: ${{ secrets.OPTIONAL_TOKEN }}${{ fromJSON(secrets.DB).password }}
        steps:
          - run: echo read
      print:
        needs: read
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "${{ needs.read.outputs.credential }}"
    ```
  - example: output-with-secret.and-false.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push and on pull_request, the env of the job `read` has the
    #   whole secret TOKEN, and an output of the job `read` is the JSON of
    #   github.event_name == 'push' && env and the password of the JSON secret
    #   DB; the later job `print` prints the output.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): on pull_request, the operand before && is
    #   false, the output is false and the password, which the runner does not
    #   mask, so the runner keeps the output and the job `print` prints the
    #   password.
    # cause: the rule reads the value of && as the last operand, the env with
    #   the whole secret TOKEN, and assumes that the runner drops the output.
    # attack: one who may read the log of the run opens the log of the job
    #   `print` in a run on pull_request.
    # attack-run-behavior: on pull_request, the header of the step of the job
    #   `print` shows the run: script of the step with the password in it,
    #   unmasked.
    on: [push, pull_request]
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      read:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        env:
          TOKEN: ${{ secrets.TOKEN }}
        outputs:
          credential: ${{ toJSON(github.event_name == 'push' && env) }}-${{ fromJSON(secrets.DB).password }}
        steps:
          - run: echo read
      print:
        needs: read
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "${{ needs.read.outputs.credential }}"
    ```
  - example: output-with-secret.env-missing.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push and on pull_request, the env of the job `read` has the
    #   whole secret TOKEN under push, and an output of the job `read` is
    #   env[github.event_name] and the password of the JSON secret DB; the
    #   later job `print` prints the output.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): on pull_request, the env has no variable
    #   pull_request, env[github.event_name] is null, and the output has only
    #   the password, which the runner does not mask, so the runner keeps the
    #   output and the job `print` prints the password.
    # cause: the rule reads env[github.event_name] as one of the variables of
    #   the env, each with a whole secret, and assumes that the runner drops the
    #   output.
    # attack: one who may read the log of the run opens the log of the job
    #   `print` in a run on pull_request.
    # attack-run-behavior: on pull_request, the header of the step of the job
    #   `print` shows the run: script of the step with the password in it,
    #   unmasked.
    on: [push, pull_request]
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      read:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        env:
          push: ${{ secrets.TOKEN }}
        outputs:
          credential: ${{ env[github.event_name] }}-${{ fromJSON(secrets.DB).password }}
        steps:
          - run: echo read
      print:
        needs: read
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "${{ needs.read.outputs.credential }}"
    ```
- called-output: a value taken out of a secret in an output of a reusable workflow (on.workflow_call.outputs), which a job of the caller reads with needs and prints: the rule does not follow the outputs of a called workflow to the caller
  - finding kinds: unmasked-secret-exposure.private, unmasked-secret-exposure.public
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - example: .github/workflows/called.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a reusable workflow whose output password has the password of
    #   the JSON secret DB; ci.yml calls this workflow on push in its job
    #   `config`, and the job `print` of ci.yml prints the output.
    # reason: a todo (a file of the repository): the runner does not mask the
    #   password, keeps the output, and the job `print` of ci.yml prints the
    #   password in the header of its step.
    # cause: the rule does not follow the outputs of a called workflow to the
    #   jobs of the caller that read the outputs with needs.
    # attack: one who may read the log of the run opens the log of the job
    #   `print` of ci.yml.
    # attack-run-behavior: the header of the step of the job `print` shows the
    #   run: script of the step with the password in it, unmasked.
    on:
      workflow_call:
        outputs:
          password:
            value: ${{ jobs.read.outputs.password }}
    jobs:
      read:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        outputs:
          password: ${{ fromJSON(secrets.DB).password }}
        steps:
          - run: echo read
    ```
    - .github/workflows/ci.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: push
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        config:
          uses: ./.github/workflows/called.yml
          secrets: inherit
        print:
          needs: config
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: echo "${{ needs.config.outputs.password }}"
      ```
- needs-other-place: a value taken out of a secret in an output of a job, read with needs in a key where GitHub does not allow the secrets context in an expression but where the runner prints the value, such as the image, options, ports or volumes of a container or a service, or defaults.run.shell; or such a value passed to a reusable workflow in the with of a job that calls the reusable workflow, where a step of the called workflow may print the value: the rule inspects only the keys where GitHub allows the secrets context
  - finding kinds: unmasked-secret-exposure.private, unmasked-secret-exposure.public
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: needs-other-place.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, an output of the job `read` has the password of the
    #   JSON secret DB, and the later job `print` writes the output into the
    #   options of its container.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the runner prints the docker create
    #   command with the options at the start of the job `print`, and does not
    #   mask the password.
    # cause: the rule inspects only the keys where GitHub allows the secrets
    #   context in an expression, and options is not one of those keys.
    # attack: one who may read the log of the run opens the log of the job
    #   `print`.
    # attack-run-behavior: the log section Initialize containers of the job
    #   `print`, which the runner prints at the start of the job, has docker
    #   create with --label v= and the password, unmasked.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      read:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        outputs:
          password: ${{ fromJSON(secrets.DB).password }}
        steps:
          - run: echo read
      print:
        needs: read
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        container:
          image: ubuntu:24.04
          options: --label v=${{ needs.read.outputs.password }}
        steps:
          - run: echo print
    ```
- escaped-twice: toJSON(secrets), toJSON(secrets.X), or toJSON(env.X) where the variable X of the env holds a whole secret, in the env of the job's container or of a service: the runner prints the docker create command with each value of the JSON escaped a second time, the mask does not match a value escaped twice, and so the runner prints a secret that has a double quote in its value unmasked. Whether unmasked-secret-exposure reports a toJSON in the env of a container or of a service is not decided, because the harm depends on whether a secret has a double quote in its value, which the workflow does not show. secret-exposure reports toJSON(secrets) for a different harm, every secret reaching the job; no rule reports toJSON(secrets.X) or toJSON(env.X) in the env of a container
  - finding kinds: unmasked-secret-exposure.private, unmasked-secret-exposure.public
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: escaped-twice.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a service of the job `test` has toJSON(secrets) in
    #   its env, under the variable ALL, and the repository has a secret whose
    #   value is a JSON.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the runner prints the docker create
    #   command of the service with the JSON of the secrets escaped a second
    #   time, the mask does not match a value escaped twice, and so the runner
    #   prints the secret that has a double quote in its value unmasked.
    # cause: the rule inspects values taken out of a secret by fromJSON, not a
    #   whole secret that the runner escapes twice.
    # attack: one who may read the log of the run opens the log of the job
    #   `test`.
    # attack-run-behavior: the log section Initialize containers, which the
    #   runner prints at the start of the job, has docker create
    #   with -e "ALL=" and the JSON, where each secret without a double quote is
    #   *** and the JSON secret is in the escaped form, unmasked.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      test:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        services:
          db:
            image: postgres:16
            env:
              ALL: ${{ toJSON(secrets) }}
        steps:
          - run: make test
    ```
  - example: escaped-twice.env.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, the env of the job has the secret PG under the name PG,
    #   and the env of a service has toJSON(env.PG).
    # reason: a todo (the same file): whether the rule reports this form is not
    #   decided, as the harm depends on whether the secret PG has a double quote
    #   in its value.
    # cause: the runner prints the docker create command of the service with
    #   the JSON of env.PG escaped a second time, which the mask does not match.
    # attack: one who may read the log of the run opens the log to read the
    #   secret PG.
    # attack-run-behavior: if the secret PG has a double quote in its value,
    #   the docker create command of the service prints the value unmasked.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      test:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        env:
          PG: ${{ secrets.PG }}
        services:
          db:
            image: postgres:16
            env:
              PG_JSON: ${{ toJSON(env.PG) }}
        steps:
          - run: make test
    ```
- github-env: a variable that a step writes to \$GITHUB_ENV and that a later step or an output of the job reads with env.NAME: the runner puts the variables that the steps write to \$GITHUB_ENV over the variables of the same name in the env of the job and of the workflow, and the rule reads env.NAME only from the env written in the workflow file. So the rule does not report fromJSON(env.NAME).key when a step writes a JSON secret to \$GITHUB_ENV under NAME, and the rule reads an output of the job that has env.NAME as an output that the runner drops when the env of the job has a whole secret under NAME, even when a step writes another value to \$GITHUB_ENV under NAME
  - finding kinds: unmasked-secret-exposure.private, unmasked-secret-exposure.public
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: github-env.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step writes the JSON secret DB to $GITHUB_ENV under
    #   the name DB, and a later step takes the password out of env.DB with
    #   fromJSON into the env of the later step.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the rule reads env.DB only from the env
    #   written in the workflow file, where no env has DB.
    # cause: the rule does not read the writes of the steps to $GITHUB_ENV.
    # attack: one who may read the log of the run opens the log to read the
    #   password.
    # attack-run-behavior: the header of the later step prints PASSWORD with
    #   the value that fromJSON took out, which the runner does not mask.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      migrate:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              DB_JSON: ${{ secrets.DB }}
            run: |
              {
                echo 'DB<<END_OF_DB'
                echo "$DB_JSON"
                echo 'END_OF_DB'
              } >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          - env:
              PASSWORD: ${{ fromJSON(env.DB).password }}
            run: ./migrate.sh
    ```
- env-object-property: a property of a value that is the whole env in some runs and another value in other runs, such as fromJSON((github.head_ref || env).DB).pass or case(github.ref == 'refs/heads/main', env, vars).DB: the rule reads the value as a value without the variables of the env, so the rule does not report a value taken out of a secret that a variable of the env holds
  - finding kinds: unmasked-secret-exposure.private, unmasked-secret-exposure.public
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: env-object-property.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, the env of the job has the JSON secret DB under DB,
    #   and the run of a step takes the password out of
    #   (github.head_ref || env).DB with fromJSON.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): on push, github.head_ref is empty, so the
    #   value of || is the env, and the run has the password, which the runner
    #   does not mask.
    # cause: the rule reads a value that is the env in some runs as a value
    #   without the variables of the env.
    # attack: one who may read the log of the run opens the log to read the
    #   password.
    # attack-run-behavior: the header of the step prints the run with the
    #   password in it, unmasked.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      migrate:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        env:
          DB: ${{ secrets.DB }}
        steps:
          - run: ./migrate.sh "${{ fromJSON((github.head_ref || env).DB).password }}"
    ```
- unknown-os-case: env.NAME whose NAME differs only in upper and lower case from the name of a variable of the env (env.db and DB), in a job whose OS the runs-on does not decide, such as a \${{ }} of a matrix or the labels of a self-hosted runner without windows: the runner matches the names of the env context in any case on Windows and only in the same case on Linux and macOS, and the rule matches the names in any case only in a job whose runs-on decides Windows
  - finding kinds: unmasked-secret-exposure.private, unmasked-secret-exposure.public
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: unknown-os-case.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a job runs on Linux and on Windows by a matrix, its
    #   env has the JSON secret DB under the name DB, and a step takes the
    #   password out of env.db with fromJSON into the env of the step.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the runs-on of the job is a ${{ }} of the
    #   matrix, so the rule does not know that the job runs on Windows, and
    #   matches env.db with DB only in the same case.
    # cause: the runner matches the names of the env context in any case on
    #   Windows, so env.db is the secret DB in the run on Windows.
    # attack: one who may read the log of the run opens the log of the run on
    #   Windows to read the password.
    # attack-run-behavior: on Windows, the header of the step prints PASSWORD
    #   with the value that fromJSON took out, which the runner does not mask.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      migrate:
        strategy:
          matrix:
            os: [ubuntu-latest, windows-latest]
        runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
        env:
          DB: ${{ secrets.DB }}
        steps:
          - env:
              PASSWORD: ${{ fromJSON(env.db).password }}
            run: ./migrate.sh
    ```
- shell-derived: a value taken out of a secret in the shell, such as by jq, and printed
  - finding kinds: unmasked-secret-exposure.private, unmasked-secret-exposure.public
  - disposition: other-rule (rule: secret-in-log)
  - example: shell-derived.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step gets the JSON secret DB whole in its env, and
    #   echoes its password taken out by jq.
    # reason: another rule's: secret-in-log reports what the shell makes of a
    #   secret and prints to the log.
    # cause: the rule reads the ${{ }} of the workflow, not the script.
    # attack: one who may read the run's log opens it to read the password.
    # attack-run-behavior: the runner masks DB whole, and the password jq writes
    #   is not DB, so the log has it as it is.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      migrate:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              DB: ${{ secrets.DB }}
            run: echo "password is $(jq -r .password <<<"$DB")"
    ```
- json-scalar: a secret whose value is a JSON number, or a JSON string of 8 characters or fewer with its quotes, read whole by fromJSON: the runner masks a value without its quotes only when it is longer than 8 characters, and the rule takes the value as an object it does not print
  - finding kinds: unmasked-secret-exposure.private, unmasked-secret-exposure.public
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: json-scalar.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, the secret API_KEY holds a JSON string, "k-123" with
    #   its quotes, and a step reads it whole by fromJSON.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): fromJSON gives k-123 without the quotes,
    #   and the runner masks a value without its quotes only when the value is
    #   longer than 8 characters ("k-123" is 7).
    # cause: the rule takes a secret read whole by fromJSON as an object or an
    #   array, which a string makes Object or Array.
    # attack: one who may read the run's log opens it to read the key.
    # attack-run-behavior: the header of the step prints KEY with k-123, which
    #   the runner does not mask.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      call:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              KEY: ${{ fromJSON(secrets.API_KEY) }}
            run: ./call.sh
    ```
- whole-map: a whole env, with, container env or container credentials written as one \${{ }} of a secret read by fromJSON, such as env: \${{ fromJSON(secrets.J) }}: the authors of the rule have not checked whether GitHub accepts that form, and whether the runner then prints each value of the secret. In the same way, env.NAME where the whole env of the step or of the job is written as one \${{ }}: the rule skips the env written as one \${{ }} and reads env.NAME from the env of the levels above the env written as one \${{ }} (the env of the job and of the workflow for a step, the env of the workflow for a job), so the rule misses a secret that the env written as one \${{ }} has under NAME
  - finding kinds: unmasked-secret-exposure.private, unmasked-secret-exposure.public
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: whole-map.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step's whole env is the JSON secret DB read by
    #   fromJSON.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): whether GitHub takes such an env, and the
    #   runner prints each of its values in the step's header, was not checked.
    # cause: the rule takes a secret read whole by fromJSON as an object, which
    #   it does not print.
    # attack: one who may read the run's log opens it to read the password.
    # attack-run-behavior: if the runner sets the env from the object, its
    #   header prints each key with its value, the password among them.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      migrate:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env: ${{ fromJSON(secrets.DB) }}
            run: ./migrate.sh
    ```
  - example: whole-map.env-level.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, the whole env of a step is the JSON secret ENV read by
    #   fromJSON, and the run of the step takes the password out of env.DB, a
    #   JSON value of ENV, with fromJSON.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the rule skips an env written as one
    #   ${{ }} and reads env.DB from the env of the job and of the workflow,
    #   where no env has DB.
    # cause: the rule does not read the names of an env written as one ${{ }}.
    # attack: one who may read the log of the run opens the log to read the
    #   password.
    # attack-run-behavior: if GitHub takes such an env, the header of the step
    #   prints the run with the value that fromJSON took out, which the runner
    #   does not mask.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      migrate:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env: ${{ fromJSON(secrets.ENV) }}
            run: ./migrate.sh "${{ fromJSON(env.DB).password }}"
    ```
  - example: whole-map.job-env.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, the whole env of a job is the JSON secret ENV read by
    #   fromJSON, and a step takes the password out of env.DB, a JSON value of
    #   ENV, with fromJSON into the env of the step.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the rule skips an env written as one
    #   ${{ }} and reads env.DB from the env of the workflow, where no env has
    #   DB.
    # cause: the rule does not read the names of an env written as one ${{ }}.
    # attack: one who may read the log of the run opens the log to read the
    #   password.
    # attack-run-behavior: if GitHub takes such an env, the header of the step
    #   prints PASSWORD with the value that fromJSON took out, which the runner
    #   does not mask.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      migrate:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        env: ${{ fromJSON(secrets.ENV) }}
        steps:
          - env:
              PASSWORD: ${{ fromJSON(env.DB).password }}
            run: ./migrate.sh
    ```
- remote-callee: a job or a step inside a reusable workflow of another repository (uses: owner/repo/.github/workflows/&lt;file>@&lt;ref>) whose content the fact workflow.definition does not give. For every rule: a run that does not ask the fact (a run without --online and without the answer in --facts). For a quality rule, also: a run where the linter asked the fact and got no answer (an answer of unknown: the GitHub API did not give the file), and a call deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact. The rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition. For a rule that is not a quality rule (a rule with a threat), the last two forms are the inconclusive kind remote-callee-unknown, not this form
  - finding kinds: unmasked-secret-exposure.private, unmasked-secret-exposure.public
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-callee.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
    #   the repository example-org/unmasked-secret-exposure-unanswered, whose
    #   content is the workflow of the true positive private (private.yml) of
    #   the rule, with on: workflow_call in place of the on of private.yml. The
    #   linter has no answer of the fact workflow.definition for the reusable
    #   workflow.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event
    #   that started the run of the calling job, and the linter does not read
    #   the reusable workflow.
    # cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from
    #   the answer of workflow.definition.
    # attack: someone with read access to the repository, who may not read its
    #   secrets, opens the run's log and reads the client secret.
    # attack-run-behavior: the header of the step prints CLIENT_ID and
    #   CLIENT_SECRET with their values; the log keeps them for 90 days by
    #   default.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/unmasked-secret-exposure-unanswered/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

### inconclusive

- remote-callee-unknown: a job that calls a reusable workflow of another repository, when the linter asked the fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow and got no answer (the token that the linter uses cannot read the file, the file is larger than the limit, or the linter has used up the requests it may send to the GitHub API), or when the call is deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact: the rule does not read the jobs and the steps of the reusable workflow
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-callee-unknown.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
    #   the repository example-org/unmasked-secret-exposure-unknown, whose
    #   content is the workflow of the true positive private (private.yml) of
    #   the rule, with on: workflow_call in place of the on of private.yml. The
    #   linter asked the fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow and
    #   got no answer.
    # reason: what the jobs of the reusable workflow do is in the file that the
    #   linter could not read; whoever changes the uses, such as the author of a
    #   pull request, can name a reusable workflow that the token that the
    #   linter uses cannot read.
    # attack: someone with read access to the repository, who may not read its
    #   secrets, opens the run's log and reads the client secret.
    # attack-run-behavior: the header of the step prints CLIENT_ID and
    #   CLIENT_SECRET with their values; the log keeps them for 90 days by
    #   default.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/unmasked-secret-exposure-unknown/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

### false positive forms

- registered-earlier: a value an earlier step of the job registered with ::add-mask::, in the env, with, run or name of a later step: the runner masks the value there. The runner does not mask, and so this rule reports with no false positive, a value in the env of the job or of the workflow, because the header of the step that registers the value prints that env before the registration, and a value in the env or in the username of the credentials of a container, because the runner prints those at the start of the job, before any step runs
  - finding kinds: unmasked-secret-exposure.public, unmasked-secret-exposure.private
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: registered-earlier.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step gets the JSON secret DB whole, takes its
    #   password out with jq and registers it with ::add-mask::; a later step
    #   puts fromJSON(secrets.DB).password in its env.
    # reason: the runner masks what a step registers in every later step, so
    #   the later step's header prints PASSWORD as ***.
    # cause: the rule does not read the script of the earlier step, where the
    #   value is registered.
    # attack: one who may read the run's log opens it to read the password.
    # attack-run-behavior: the first step's header prints DB as ***, and the
    #   second step's header prints PASSWORD as ***.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      migrate:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - env:
              DB: ${{ secrets.DB }}
            run: echo "::add-mask::$(jq -r .password <<<"$DB")"
          - env:
              PASSWORD: ${{ fromJSON(secrets.DB).password }}
            run: ./migrate.sh
    ```
- registered-output: a value that a step of a job registered with ::add-mask::, in an output of the job, which a later job reads with needs: the runner drops an output whose value contains a value that the runner masks, and the later job gets an empty value
  - finding kinds: unmasked-secret-exposure.public, unmasked-secret-exposure.private
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: registered-output.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step of the job `read` registers the password of
    #   the JSON secret DB with ::add-mask::, and an output of the job `read`
    #   has the same password; the later job `print` prints the output.
    # reason: the runner drops an output whose value contains a value that the
    #   runner masks, and the step registered the password, so the job `print`
    #   gets an empty value.
    # cause: the rule does not inspect the script of the step that registers
    #   the value.
    # attack: one who may read the log of the run opens the log of the job
    #   `print` to read the password.
    # attack-run-behavior: the job `read` warns that it skips the output
    #   password since the output may contain a secret; the header of the step
    #   of the job `print` shows the run: script of the step with an empty
    #   value.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      read:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        outputs:
          password: ${{ fromJSON(secrets.DB).password }}
        steps:
          - env:
              DB: ${{ secrets.DB }}
            run: echo "::add-mask::$(jq -r .password <<<"$DB")"
      print:
        needs: read
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "${{ needs.read.outputs.password }}"
    ```
- env-object-key: a value that fromJSON reads back out of the JSON of the whole env, such as fromJSON(toJSON(env)).TOKEN, where the variable TOKEN of the env holds the whole secret TOKEN or toJSON(secrets): the value is the whole secret TOKEN or the JSON of the secrets context, whose values the runner masks; the rule reads the JSON of the whole env as a JSON secret, and reads each value that fromJSON reads out of the JSON of the whole env as a value taken out of a secret
  - finding kinds: unmasked-secret-exposure.public, unmasked-secret-exposure.private
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: env-object-key.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, the env of the job has the whole secret TOKEN under
    #   TOKEN, and a step reads TOKEN back out of the JSON of the whole env with
    #   fromJSON(toJSON(env)).TOKEN in its env.
    # reason: fromJSON(toJSON(env)).TOKEN is the whole secret TOKEN, which the
    #   runner masks, so the header of the step prints TOKEN as ***.
    # cause: the rule reads the JSON of the whole env as a JSON secret, and a
    #   value that fromJSON reads out of the JSON of the whole env as a value
    #   taken out of a secret.
    # attack: one who may read the log of the run opens the log to read the
    #   secret TOKEN.
    # attack-run-behavior: the header of the step prints TOKEN as ***.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      deploy:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        env:
          TOKEN: ${{ secrets.TOKEN }}
        steps:
          - env:
              TOKEN_AGAIN: ${{ fromJSON(toJSON(env)).TOKEN }}
            run: ./deploy.sh
    ```
- masked-alternative: an output of a job whose value has A || B where A is a whole secret, such as \${{ secrets.TOKEN || '' }}-\${{ fromJSON(secrets.DB).pass }}: a secret that is set is not empty, so A || B is the secret in every run, and the runner drops the output; the rule reads A || B as either A or B, and so reads the output as an output that the runner may keep. When the secret is not set, the output has no value that the runner masks, and the finding is right
  - finding kinds: unmasked-secret-exposure.public, unmasked-secret-exposure.private
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: masked-alternative.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, an output of the job `read` is secrets.TOKEN || ''
    #   and the password of the JSON secret DB, where the repository sets the
    #   secret TOKEN; the later job `print` prints the output.
    # reason: the secret TOKEN is set and not empty, so secrets.TOKEN || '' is
    #   the secret TOKEN in every run, which the runner masks; the runner drops
    #   the output, and the job `print` gets an empty value.
    # cause: the rule reads secrets.TOKEN || '' as either the secret TOKEN or
    #   the empty string, and so reads the output as an output that the runner
    #   may keep.
    # attack: one who may read the log of the run opens the log of the job
    #   `print` to read the password.
    # attack-run-behavior: the job `read` warns that it skips the output
    #   credential since the output may contain a secret; the header of the
    #   step of the job `print` shows the run: script of the step with an
    #   empty value.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      read:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        outputs:
          credential: ${{ secrets.TOKEN || '' }}-${{ fromJSON(secrets.DB).password }}
        steps:
          - run: echo read
      print:
        needs: read
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "${{ needs.read.outputs.credential }}"
    ```
- env-property: an output of a job whose value has a property NAME of a value that is the whole env, such as (github.event_name != '' && env).TOKEN, where the variable TOKEN of the env holds a whole secret: the value is the whole secret, and the runner drops the output; the rule reads a property of a value that is not written as env.NAME as any one variable of the env, and so reads the output as an output that the runner may keep
  - finding kinds: unmasked-secret-exposure.public, unmasked-secret-exposure.private
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: env-property.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, the env of the job `read` has the whole secret TOKEN
    #   under TOKEN, and an output of the job `read` is
    #   (github.event_name != '' && env).TOKEN and the password of the JSON
    #   secret DB; the later job `print` prints the output.
    # reason: github.event_name is not empty, so the property TOKEN is the
    #   secret TOKEN in every run, which the runner masks; the runner drops the
    #   output, and the job `print` gets an empty value.
    # cause: the rule reads a property of a value that is not written as
    #   env.TOKEN as any one variable of the env, and so reads the output as an
    #   output that the runner may keep.
    # attack: one who may read the log of the run opens the log of the job
    #   `print` to read the password.
    # attack-run-behavior: the job `read` warns that it skips the output
    #   credential since the output may contain a secret; the header of the
    #   step of the job `print` shows the run: script of the step with an
    #   empty value.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      read:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        env:
          TOKEN: ${{ secrets.TOKEN }}
        outputs:
          credential: ${{ (github.event_name != '' && env).TOKEN }}-${{ fromJSON(secrets.DB).password }}
        steps:
          - run: echo read
      print:
        needs: read
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "${{ needs.read.outputs.credential }}"
    ```
- env-index: env&#91;INDEX] whose INDEX the workflow file does not write as a name, such as env&#91;matrix.key]: the rule reads env&#91;INDEX] as any one variable of the env. So the rule reports a value taken out of a secret by fromJSON(env&#91;INDEX]).key when a variable of the env holds a secret and INDEX names a variable without a secret in every run, and the rule reports an output of the job that has env&#91;INDEX] and a value taken out of a secret when INDEX names a variable with a whole secret in every run, an output that the runner drops
  - finding kinds: unmasked-secret-exposure.public, unmasked-secret-exposure.private
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: env-index.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, the env of the job has the JSON secret DB under DB and
    #   a JSON literal under N, and a step takes pass out of env[matrix.key]
    #   with fromJSON, where matrix.key is N in every run.
    # reason: env[matrix.key] is the JSON literal N in every run, which holds no
    #   secret, so the header of the step prints a value without a secret.
    # cause: the rule reads env[matrix.key] as any variable of the env, the
    #   secret DB among them.
    # attack: one who may read the log of the run opens the log to read the
    #   value of pass.
    # attack-run-behavior: the header of the step prints PASS with the value x
    #   of the JSON literal.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      migrate:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        strategy:
          matrix:
            key: [N]
        env:
          DB: ${{ secrets.DB }}
          N: '{"pass": "x"}'
        steps:
          - env:
              PASS: ${{ fromJSON(env[matrix.key]).pass }}
            run: ./migrate.sh
    ```
  - example: env-index.output.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, the env of the job `read` has the whole secret TOKEN
    #   under TOKEN and a literal under N, an output of the job `read` is
    #   env[matrix.key] and the password of the JSON secret DB, where
    #   matrix.key is TOKEN in every run; the later job `print` prints the
    #   output.
    # reason: env[matrix.key] is the whole secret TOKEN in every run, which the
    #   runner masks, so the runner drops the output and the job `print` gets
    #   an empty value.
    # cause: the rule reads env[matrix.key] as any one variable of the env, so
    #   the rule reads the output as an output that the runner may keep.
    # attack: one who may read the log of the run opens the log of the job
    #   `print` to read the password.
    # attack-run-behavior: the job `read` warns that it skips the output
    #   credential since the output may contain a secret; the header of the
    #   step of the job `print` shows the run: script of the step with an empty
    #   value.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      read:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        strategy:
          matrix:
            key: [TOKEN]
        env:
          TOKEN: ${{ secrets.TOKEN }}
          N: plain
        outputs:
          credential: ${{ env[matrix.key] }}-${{ fromJSON(secrets.DB).password }}
        steps:
          - run: echo read
      print:
        needs: read
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "${{ needs.read.outputs.credential }}"
    ```
- unknown-os-case: env.NAME in a job whose OS the runs-on does not decide, where the env of a nearer level has a variable whose name differs from NAME only in upper and lower case and the env of a farther level holds a secret under NAME (db: plain in the env of the job and DB: \${{ secrets.DB }} in the env of the workflow): on Windows, the variable of the nearer level replaces the variable of the farther level, so env.NAME has no secret; in a job whose OS the runs-on does not decide, the rule matches the names only in the same case and reads the secret of the farther level. In a job whose OS the runs-on does not decide, the rule also reports an output of the job that has env.NAME and a value taken out of a secret, as an output that the runner may keep, when one of the variables whose names differ only in upper and lower case holds a whole secret: the runner drops the output on the OS where env.NAME is the whole secret
  - finding kinds: unmasked-secret-exposure.public, unmasked-secret-exposure.private
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: unknown-os-case.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, the env of the workflow has the JSON secret DB under
    #   DB, a job runs on Windows by a matrix, the env of the job has a JSON
    #   literal under db, and a step takes the password out of env.DB with
    #   fromJSON into the env of the step.
    # reason: on Windows, the runner matches the names of the env context in
    #   any case, so db of the env of the job replaces DB of the env of the
    #   workflow, and env.DB is the JSON literal, which holds no secret.
    # cause: the runs-on of the job is a ${{ }} of the matrix, so the rule does
    #   not know that the job runs on Windows, and matches the names only in the
    #   same case.
    # attack: one who may read the log of the run opens the log to read the
    #   password.
    # attack-run-behavior: the header of the step prints PASSWORD with the
    #   value placeholder of the JSON literal.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    env:
      DB: ${{ secrets.DB }}
    jobs:
      migrate:
        strategy:
          matrix:
            os: [windows-latest]
        runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
        env:
          db: '{"password": "placeholder"}'
        steps:
          - env:
              PASSWORD: ${{ fromJSON(env.DB).password }}
            run: ./migrate.ps1
    ```
  - example: unknown-os-case.output.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a job `read` runs on Windows by a matrix, the env of
    #   the job `read` has the whole secret TOKEN under the name token, and an
    #   output of the job `read` is env.TOKEN and the password of the JSON
    #   secret DB; the later job `print` prints the output.
    # reason: on Windows, the runner matches the names of the env context in
    #   any case, so env.TOKEN is the whole secret TOKEN, which the runner
    #   masks; the runner drops the output, and the job `print` gets an empty
    #   value.
    # cause: the runs-on of the job `read` is a ${{ }} of the matrix, so the
    #   rule does not know that the job runs on Windows, and does not read
    #   env.TOKEN as the variable token.
    # attack: one who may read the log of the run opens the log of the job
    #   `print` to read the password.
    # attack-run-behavior: the job `read` warns that it skips the output
    #   credential since the output may contain a secret; the header of the
    #   step of the job `print` shows the run: script of the step with an empty
    #   value.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      read:
        strategy:
          matrix:
            os: [windows-latest]
        runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
        env:
          token: ${{ secrets.TOKEN }}
        outputs:
          credential: ${{ env.TOKEN }}-${{ fromJSON(secrets.DB).password }}
        steps:
          - run: echo read
      print:
        needs: read
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "${{ needs.read.outputs.credential }}"
    ```
- whole-map: env.NAME where the whole env of the step or of the job is written as one \${{ }} that may have a variable under NAME, and the env of a level above holds a secret under NAME: the variable of the env written as one \${{ }} replaces the variable of the level above, so env.NAME may have no secret; the rule skips the env written as one \${{ }} and reads the secret of the level above. In the same way, the rule reports an output of the job that has env.NAME and a value taken out of a secret, as an output that the runner may keep, when the env of a level above holds a whole secret under NAME; the runner drops the output when the env written as one \${{ }} has no variable under NAME. The authors of the rule have not checked whether GitHub accepts an env written as one \${{ }}
  - finding kinds: unmasked-secret-exposure.public, unmasked-secret-exposure.private
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: whole-map.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, the env of the job has the JSON secret DB under DB,
    #   the whole env of a step is the configuration variable STEP_ENV read by
    #   fromJSON, which has a JSON literal under DB, and the run of the step
    #   takes the password out of env.DB with fromJSON.
    # reason: if GitHub takes such an env, DB of the env of the step replaces
    #   DB of the env of the job, so env.DB is the JSON literal, which holds no
    #   secret.
    # cause: the rule skips an env written as one ${{ }} and reads env.DB from
    #   the env of the job.
    # attack: one who may read the log of the run opens the log to read the
    #   password.
    # attack-run-behavior: if GitHub takes such an env, the header of the step
    #   prints the run with the value of the JSON literal.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      migrate:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        env:
          DB: ${{ secrets.DB }}
        steps:
          - env: ${{ fromJSON(vars.STEP_ENV) }}
            run: ./migrate.sh "${{ fromJSON(env.DB).password }}"
    ```
  - example: whole-map.output.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, the env of the workflow has the whole secret TOKEN
    #   under TOKEN, the whole env of the job `read` is the configuration
    #   variable JOB_ENV read by fromJSON, which has no TOKEN, and an output of
    #   the job `read` is env.TOKEN and the password of the JSON secret DB; the
    #   later job `print` prints the output.
    # reason: if GitHub takes such an env, env.TOKEN is the whole secret TOKEN
    #   of the env of the workflow, which the runner masks; the runner drops the
    #   output, and the job `print` gets an empty value.
    # cause: the rule reads env.TOKEN as a variable that the env written as one
    #   ${{ }} may replace, so the rule reads the output as an output that the
    #   runner may keep.
    # attack: one who may read the log of the run opens the log of the job
    #   `print` to read the password.
    # attack-run-behavior: if GitHub takes such an env, the job `read` warns
    #   that it skips the output credential since the output may contain a
    #   secret; the header of the step of the job `print` shows the run: script
    #   of the step with an empty value.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    env:
      TOKEN: ${{ secrets.TOKEN }}
    jobs:
      read:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        env: ${{ fromJSON(vars.JOB_ENV) }}
        outputs:
          credential: ${{ env.TOKEN }}-${{ fromJSON(secrets.DB).password }}
        steps:
          - run: echo read
      print:
        needs: read
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "${{ needs.read.outputs.credential }}"
    ```
- github-env: fromJSON(env.NAME).key, where the env of the job or of the workflow has a JSON secret under NAME and a step before writes a value without a secret to \$GITHUB_ENV under NAME: the runner puts the value of \$GITHUB_ENV over the env of the job and of the workflow, so env.NAME has no secret; the rule reads env.NAME only from the env written in the workflow file
  - finding kinds: unmasked-secret-exposure.public, unmasked-secret-exposure.private
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: github-env.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, the env of the job has the JSON secret DB under the
    #   name DB, a step writes a JSON literal to $GITHUB_ENV under the name DB,
    #   and a later step takes the password out of env.DB with fromJSON into
    #   the env of the later step.
    # reason: the runner puts the value of $GITHUB_ENV over the env of the job,
    #   so env.DB in the later step is the JSON literal, which holds no secret.
    # cause: the rule reads env.DB only from the env written in the workflow
    #   file, where env.DB is the secret DB.
    # attack: one who may read the log of the run opens the log to read the
    #   password.
    # attack-run-behavior: the header of the later step prints PASSWORD with
    #   the value placeholder of the JSON literal.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      migrate:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        env:
          DB: ${{ secrets.DB }}
        steps:
          - run: echo 'DB={"password":"placeholder"}' >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          - env:
              PASSWORD: ${{ fromJSON(env.DB).password }}
            run: ./migrate.sh
    ```
- private-repository: a private or internal repository, where the value is unmasked-secret-exposure.private: whoever may read the repository reads it
  - finding kinds: unmasked-secret-exposure.public
  - fact kinds:
    - repo.public (provider: repo-setting, answer that removes the finding: false)
  - example: private-repository.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step takes the client secret out of the JSON
    #   secret AZURE_CREDENTIALS into its env, in a private repository.
    # reason: the repository is private or internal, so the value is
    #   unmasked-secret-exposure.private, not .public: only those with read
    #   access, every member of the enterprise for an internal one, read the
    #   log.
    # cause: unless a file of facts or --fact says that the repository is not
    #   public (repo.public false), the rule reports the finding. When no source
    #   answers repo.public, the finding is conditional.
    # attack: anyone without access to the repository tries to read the run's
    #   log to take the client secret.
    # attack-run-behavior: GitHub does not show the log of a private or
    #   internal repository to those without read access; those with it read
    #   the value in the step's header.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      deploy:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - name: log in to azure
            env:
              CLIENT_ID: ${{ fromJSON(secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS).clientId }}
              CLIENT_SECRET: ${{ fromJSON(secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS).clientSecret }}
            run: az login --service-principal -u "$CLIENT_ID" -p "$CLIENT_SECRET" --tenant contoso.onmicrosoft.com
    ```
- actions-not-allowed: a workflow whose run GitHub does not start, or a job that GitHub fails in the step "Set up job", because of the setting of allowed actions of GitHub (the fact repo.allowed-actions, which the quality rule allowed-actions reads): GitHub does not start a run of a workflow that has a uses, or that calls a reusable workflow that has a uses, that the setting does not allow, and fails a job before any step of the job runs when a step of a composite action that the job runs has a uses that the setting does not allow, or when the setting requires a full commit SHA and a step names an action by a tag or a branch. The harm that the finding reports happens only when GitHub runs the workflow or the job, and the rule does not read repo.allowed-actions
  - finding kinds: unmasked-secret-exposure.private, unmasked-secret-exposure.public
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: actions-not-allowed.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the workflow of the true positive private (private.yml) of the
    #   rule, with a job added whose step uses example-org/not-allowed-action,
    #   which the setting of allowed actions of GitHub (repo.allowed-actions)
    #   blocks with !example-org/not-allowed-action@*. In the true positive, on
    #   push, in a private repository (repo.public false), a step takes clientId
    #   and clientSecret out of the JSON secret AZURE_CREDENTIALS into its env.
    # reason: GitHub checks each uses of the workflow before the run starts, and
    #   does not start the run because of the uses of
    #   example-org/not-allowed-action: no job of the run runs, so what the
    #   reason of the true positive says does not happen (in runs that the
    #   authors of the rule made on GitHub, such runs ended as startup_failure).
    # cause: the rule does not read repo.allowed-actions.
    # attack: someone with read access to the repository, who may not read its
    #   secrets, opens the run's log and reads the client secret.
    # attack-run-behavior: GitHub does not start the run, so no step of the run
    #   runs, and the attack does nothing.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      deploy:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - name: log in to azure
            env:
              CLIENT_ID: ${{ fromJSON(secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS).clientId }}
              CLIENT_SECRET: ${{ fromJSON(secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS).clientSecret }}
            run: az login --service-principal -u "$CLIENT_ID" -p "$CLIENT_SECRET" --tenant contoso.onmicrosoft.com
      not-allowed:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: example-org/not-allowed-action@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

### threat

- precondition part-unmasked: the runner masks the values of the secrets its job gets, each of their lines, and the forms its encoders make of them (Base64, a JSON escape, a value without its quotes), not a part of one: a value fromJSON takes out of a secret, or a JSON fromJSON and toJSON write anew, is printed as it is
  - observed: 2026-10-14, runner 2.337.0: a secret holding a JSON was masked whole; its user and pass taken out by fromJSON were printed as they are in the env of the workflow, the job and the step, a run, a with, a step's name, and in the values of case() and ||
  - cites:
    - <https://github.com/actions/runner/blob/397b032cbf865e9c3ddfab89d533ec19325e1273/src/Runner.Worker/Worker.cs>
    - <https://github.com/actions/runner/blob/397b032cbf865e9c3ddfab89d533ec19325e1273/src/Runner.Common/HostContext.cs>
    - <https://github.com/github/docs/blob/ba6f6f9b9b31c4f0a991fbcb1005080526424804/content/actions/reference/security/secure-use.md>
- precondition header-printed: the runner prints in the header of a step, before it runs, the env of the step with those of the job and the workflow, the with of an action, and the run with its \${{ }} evaluated; a ::add-mask:: in that run comes after it
  - observed: 2026-10-14, runner 2.337.0: the header of each step printed its env with the job's and the workflow's, its run with the \${{ }} evaluated, and the with of a local action, before the step's output
  - cites:
    - <https://github.com/actions/runner/blob/397b032cbf865e9c3ddfab89d533ec19325e1273/src/Runner.Worker/Handlers/Handler.cs>
    - <https://github.com/actions/runner/blob/397b032cbf865e9c3ddfab89d533ec19325e1273/src/Runner.Worker/Handlers/ScriptHandler.cs>
- precondition command-printed: at the start of the job, the runner prints the docker create command of the job's container and of each service with the values of the env of the container, and, when the credentials of a container have both a username and a password, the docker login command with the username; without both, the runner does not log in and prints no docker login command. The runner passes the password to docker login on its standard input and does not print the password
  - observed: 2026-10-23, runner 2.337.0: a value taken out of a secret by fromJSON was printed unmasked in the docker create command of the job's container and of a service, where the value was in the env of the container, and in the docker login command, where the value was the username of the credentials of the job's container
  - cites:
    - <https://github.com/actions/runner/blob/397b032cbf865e9c3ddfab89d533ec19325e1273/src/Runner.Worker/Container/DockerCommandManager.cs>
- precondition output-kept: the runner prints only the name of each output of a job. The runner keeps an output whose value contains no value that the runner masks (a whole secret, or a value that a step of the job registered with ::add-mask::), and the runner drops an output whose value contains such a value. When a step of a later job reads the kept output with needs in its env, with or run, the runner prints the value in the header of that step, as the runner prints any other value there
  - observed: 2026-10-23, runner 2.337.0: an output of a job with the value of the key pass of a JSON secret, taken out by fromJSON, printed only the name of the output in that job; a later job that read the output with needs printed the value of pass unmasked in the env and the run of the headers of its steps; an output with a value that a step of its job registered with ::add-mask:: was dropped, and the later job got an empty value
  - cites:
    - <https://github.com/actions/runner/blob/397b032cbf865e9c3ddfab89d533ec19325e1273/src/Runner.Worker/JobExtension.cs>
- precondition readable-log: anyone signed in to GitHub reads the logs of a public repository (repo.public true), those with read access the logs of a private or internal one, where every member of the enterprise has read access to an internal one, for 90 days by default
  - cites:
    - <https://github.com/github/docs/blob/ba6f6f9b9b31c4f0a991fbcb1005080526424804/content/actions/how-tos/monitor-workflows/use-workflow-run-logs.md>
    - <https://github.com/github/docs/blob/ba6f6f9b9b31c4f0a991fbcb1005080526424804/data/reusables/actions/about-artifact-log-retention.md>
    - <https://github.com/github/docs/blob/8b39dc44a066dda794bfacdd25653ff86324ef21/content/repositories/creating-and-managing-repositories/about-repositories.md>
- actor: log-reader
  - via: reads the log of a run, or downloads it
  - gains: read-secrets
