## unsound-contains

- problem: an if compares a reference with a string by contains, startsWith or endsWith, which is true for a part of a value: with the string first, a value the attacker chooses, such as the attacker's login, passes when the value is only a part of a name in the string; with the reference first, a value of the attacker's that has the string as a part passes
- expected: the if compares whole values: when the string is the first argument, contains(fromJSON('&#91;"alice", "bob"]'), the reference); when the reference is the first argument, the reference == 'the string'
- severity: critical (the worst of its kinds)
- targets: workflow, action-metadata
- facets:
  - weakness: gate-bypass
  - attack-means: string
- default run: always: in a run without --rule, the rule runs unless --skip-rule names the rule

### finding kinds

- unsound-contains.substring
  - detected: {func} of '{literal}' and {path} in an if on {attacker_on} lets a part of the string through
  - arguments:
    - {func}: The function, as written.
    - {literal}: The string.
    - {path}: The reference, as written.
    - {attacker_on}: The privileged events the if may run on, each event named once.
  - consequence: an attacker passes the if with a value that is only a part of one in the string, such as a login that is part of a name
  - remedy: compare whole values: contains(fromJSON('&#91;...]'), the reference)
  - severity: high (found from the CVSS metrics below by the table)
  - fix kinds: contains-array
  - fact kinds: repo.pull-request-target-allowed (provider: repo-setting)
  - attackers: fork-pr-author, issue-author, commenter, anyone-who-forks
  - preconditions: substring, chosen-login, callers-events
  - true positives:
    - .github/workflows/labeled.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: labeler.yml runs actions/labeler on pull_request_target with a
      #   personal access token; the configuration .github/labeler.yml adds the
      #   label test to a pull request that changes a file under site/; labeled.yml
      #   runs on pull_request_target on labeled when contains('safe-to-test',
      #   github.event.label.name) is true, and the job checks out the head of the
      #   pull request and runs npm ci.
      # reason: the attacker chooses the files that the pull request changes, which
      #   actions/labeler reads, and a label that a personal access token adds
      #   starts the labeled run, so no person approves the run before the label
      #   starts the run.
      # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
      # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork that
      #   changes a file under site/ and the files of the attack; actions/labeler
      #   adds the label test, which starts labeled.yml, and
      #   contains('safe-to-test', 'test') is true, the checkout fetches the head of
      #   the pull request, and npm ci runs the preinstall script of the pull
      #   request, which prints PWNED, with the secrets of the repository.
      on:
        pull_request_target:
          types: [labeled]
      jobs:
        build:
          if: contains('safe-to-test', github.event.label.name)
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
              with:
                ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
            - run: npm ci
      ```
      - finding on: .github/workflows/labeled.yml
      - .github/labeler.yml (repo-file)
        ```yaml
        test:
          - changed-files:
              - any-glob-to-any-file: 'site/**'
        ```
      - .github/workflows/labeler.yml (workflow)
        ```yaml
        on: pull_request_target
        permissions: {}
        jobs:
          label:
            runs-on: ubuntu-latest
            steps:
              - uses: actions/labeler@v5
                with:
                  repo-token: ${{ secrets.LABELER_PAT }}
        ```
    - .github/workflows/labeled.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: labeler.yml runs, on pull_request_target,
      #   actions/checkout@v4 of the head of the pull request, which the guard of
      #   actions/checkout stops, and then actions/labeler with if: always() and a
      #   personal access token; the configuration .github/labeler.yml adds the
      #   label test to a pull request that changes a file under site/; labeled.yml
      #   runs on pull_request_target on labeled when contains('safe-to-test',
      #   github.event.label.name) is true, and the job checks out the head of the
      #   pull request and runs npm ci.

      #   always(), on the pull request of the attacker, and a label that the
      #   token adds starts the labeled run, so no person approves the run before
      #   the label starts the run.
      # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
      # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork that

      #   adds the label test, which starts labeled.yml, and
      #   contains('safe-to-test', 'test') is true, the checkout fetches the head of

      #   request, which prints PWNED, with the secrets of the repository.

        pull_request_target:
          types: [labeled]
      jobs:
        build:
          if: contains('safe-to-test', github.event.label.name)
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:

                ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
            - run: npm ci

      #   run of the calling job, so the reason of the true positive holds: any
      #   login that is a part of 'alice bob', such as ali, passes the if, and

      # situation: labeler.yml runs actions/labeler on pull_request_target with a
      #   personal access token in the job label, which needs the job build and
      #   has the if contains(needs.*.result, 'failure'); the configuration

      #   does not start.

            - run: npm ci

        permissions: {}

      #   comments on the issue, and tries to pin the comment.

      #   as the actor.

- unsound-contains.superstring
  - detected: {func}({path}, '{literal}') in an if on {attacker_on} is true for values other than '{literal}'
  - arguments:
    - {func}: The function, as written.
    - {path}: The reference, as written.
    - {literal}: The string.
    - {attacker_on}: The privileged events the if may run on, each event named once.
  - consequence: an attacker passes the if with a value that the attacker chooses and that has the string at the place that the function checks: for the string alice, the login alice-x passes contains and startsWith, and the login x-alice passes contains and endsWith
  - remedy: compare the whole value: the reference == 'the string'
  - severity: critical (found from the CVSS metrics below by the table)
  - fix kinds: equality
  - fact kinds: repo.pull-request-target-allowed (provider: repo-setting)
  - attackers: fork-pr-author, issue-author, commenter, anyone-who-forks
  - preconditions: substring, chosen-login, callers-events
  - true positives:
    - superstring.no-caller.action.yml (action-metadata, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a composite action with no caller among the files that the
      #   linter reads; a step runs ./deploy.sh with the token of the job only if
      #   contains(the login of the actor, 'alice') holds.
      # reason: with no caller among the files that the linter reads, the rule
      #   reads the action on every event an attacker triggers, issue_comment among
      #   the events. contains with the login as the first argument is true for any
      #   login that has alice as a part, such as alice-x, and anyone can register
      #   such a login and comment on an issue.
      # attack-value: github.actor = "alice-x"
      # attack-run-behavior: a comment by the account alice-x on any issue runs
      #   the job of a caller on issue_comment; contains('alice-x', 'alice') is
      #   true, so ./deploy.sh runs with TOKEN set to the token of the job.
      name: deploy
      description: deploy for alice
      runs:
        using: composite
        steps:
          - if: contains(github.actor, 'alice')
            run: ./deploy.sh
            shell: bash
            env:
              TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      ```
    - superstring.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issue_comment, the job runs ./deploy.sh with
      #   secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN only if contains(the commenter's login, 'alice')
      #   holds. snapshot.yml of nuxt/create-nuxt-app (commit
      #   1aa53fd846e0d0390f0407653b624b1e46ef1d6e, GHSL-2020-276) runs its job on
      #   pull_request_target only if contains(github.actor, 'renovate') holds
      #   (line 8); the page says the check "is bypassable with a user name like
      #   renovate2, notrenovate".
      # reason: contains with the login as its first argument is true for any
      #   login that has alice as a part, such as alice-x, and anyone can
      #   register such a login and comment on an issue.
      # attack-value: github.event.comment.user.login = "alice-x"
      # attack-run-behavior: a comment by the account alice-x on any issue starts
      #   the job deploy on issue_comment; contains('alice-x', 'alice') is true,
      #   so ./deploy.sh runs with TOKEN set to DEPLOY_TOKEN's value.
      # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2020-276-nuxt-create-nuxt-app-workflow/
      on: issue_comment

        deploy:
          if: contains(github.event.comment.user.login, 'alice')

  - true negatives:
    - superstring.association.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issue_comment, the job runs ./deploy.sh with the secret
      #   DEPLOY_TOKEN only if contains(the commenter's author_association,
      #   'MEMBER') holds.
      # reason: the author_association of a comment by someone outside the
      #   repository is NONE, FIRST_TIMER, FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR or CONTRIBUTOR,
      #   and no such value has MEMBER as a part; so an outsider cannot pass the
      #   if, although contains is true for a part of the value.

    - called/action.yml (action-metadata, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: the composite action of the true positive superstring.no-caller
      #   of this rule; the only caller, ci.yml, runs on push and calls the action

      # reason: the files that the linter reads are the whole repository and hold
      #   every caller of the action, so the rule reads the action on the events of
      #   the callers, here push alone, and a push comes from one who can write to
      #   the repository, not from the attacker.

      # attack-run-behavior: the attacker cannot push to the repository, so the
      #   attacker starts no run of ci.yml, and the steps of the action never run on
      #   an event of the attacker.

        using: composite
        steps:

            shell: bash
            env:

        ```yaml

            runs-on: ubuntu-latest

              - uses: ./called
        ```
    - superstring.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issue_comment, the job runs ./deploy.sh with the secret
      #   DEPLOY_TOKEN only if the commenter's login is alice, compared by ==.
      # reason: == compares the login with alice as a whole, unlike
      #   contains(the login, 'alice'), which is true for any login with alice as
      #   a part, such as alice-x; so only alice passes.

### fix kinds

- contains-array: compare whole values: contains(fromJSON('&#91;...]'), the reference), the words of the string split by white space and commas
  - safety: review
  - possible side effects:
    - substring-not-matched: A part of the string no longer matches, and how the string is split into values is a guess of what the author meant.
- equality: compare the whole value: contains(the reference, 'the string') becomes the reference == 'the string', when the string has the form of the value of the reference (a login, owner/name)
  - safety: review
  - possible side effects:
    - superstring-not-matched: The fix assumes that the author meant the whole value: a value that has the string as a part and is not the string no longer matches.

### undetected forms

- npm-abbreviation: a command that runs npm followed by an abbreviation of the name of an npm command that runs code of the checked out tree (for example, npm tes for npm test), in a run step or in a permission of an agent. npm runs a word as an npm command when the word is the beginning of exactly one command name or alias name of the npm release that the job uses. The rule does not read abbreviations of npm command names.
  - finding kinds: unsound-contains.substring, unsound-contains.superstring
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: .github/workflows/labeled.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: labeler.yml runs, on pull_request_target, actions/checkout of
    #   the head of the pull request into the workspace, then npm tes, then
    #   actions/labeler with if: failure() and a personal access token; the
    #   configuration .github/labeler.yml adds the label test to a pull request
    #   that changes a file under site/; labeled.yml runs on pull_request_target
    #   on labeled when contains('safe-to-test', github.event.label.name) is
    #   true, which the label test makes true.
    # reason: a limitation (run time): npm reads tes as the npm command test,
    #   because tes is the beginning of no other command name or alias name of
    #   the npm release that the job uses, and npm test runs the script test of
    #   the package.json of the pull request, which can fail the step, so that
    #   actions/labeler adds the label test; which names the npm release has is
    #   known when the job runs.
    # cause: the rule does not read abbreviations of npm command names, so the
    #   rule reads npm tes as a step that runs no code of the pull request and
    #   that the attacker cannot make fail, and reads the label as one that a
    #   person adds.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"test\":\"exit 1\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork that
    #   changes a file under site/; npm tes runs the script test, which fails
    #   the step, actions/labeler adds the label test, and labeled.yml starts
    #   for the pull request with no person approving it.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    jobs:
      build:
        if: contains('safe-to-test', github.event.label.name)
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
    - .github/labeler.yml (repo-file)
      ```yaml
      test:
        - changed-files:
            - any-glob-to-any-file: 'site/**'
      ```
    - .github/workflows/labeler.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: pull_request_target
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        label:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
              with:
                ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
                allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
                persist-credentials: false
            - run: npm tes
            - uses: actions/labeler@v5
              if: failure()
              with:
                repo-token: ${{ secrets.LABELER_PAT }}
      ```
- npm-option-value-command: a command that runs npm with an option placed before the npm command, when the value of the option is the name of an npm command and the npm command runs code of the checked out tree (for example, npm --cache view ci, in which view is the name of a directory), in a run step or in a permission of an agent. The rule reads the first word after npm, other than the value of the option --prefix or -C, that is the name or the alias name of an npm command as the npm command, and so reads the value view as the npm command.
  - finding kinds: unsound-contains.substring, unsound-contains.superstring
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: .github/workflows/labeled.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: labeler.yml runs, on pull_request_target, actions/checkout of
    #   the head of the pull request into the workspace, then npm --cache view
    #   ci, then actions/labeler with if: failure() and a personal access token;
    #   the configuration .github/labeler.yml adds the label test to a pull
    #   request that changes a file under site/; labeled.yml runs on
    #   pull_request_target on labeled when contains('safe-to-test',
    #   github.event.label.name) is true, which the label test makes true.
    # reason: a limitation (run time): npm reads view as the value of the
    #   option --cache, which takes a value, and runs npm ci, which runs the
    #   script preinstall of the package.json of the pull request, which can
    #   fail the step, so that actions/labeler adds the label test; which
    #   options take a value is in the definitions of the npm release that the
    #   job uses, which is known when the job runs.
    # cause: the rule reads the first word after npm that is the name of an
    #   npm command as the npm command, so the rule reads npm --cache view ci as
    #   npm view, a step that runs no code of the pull request and that the
    #   attacker cannot make fail, and reads the label as one that a person
    #   adds.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"exit 1\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork that
    #   changes a file under site/; npm --cache view ci runs the script
    #   preinstall, which fails the step, actions/labeler adds the label test,
    #   and labeled.yml starts for the pull request with no person approving it.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    jobs:
      build:
        if: contains('safe-to-test', github.event.label.name)
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
    - .github/labeler.yml (repo-file)
      ```yaml
      test:
        - changed-files:
            - any-glob-to-any-file: 'site/**'
      ```
    - .github/workflows/labeler.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: pull_request_target
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        label:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
              with:
                ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
                allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
                persist-credentials: false
            - run: npm --cache view ci
            - uses: actions/labeler@v5
              if: failure()
              with:
                repo-token: ${{ secrets.LABELER_PAT }}
      ```
- caller-by-repository-name: a comparison in a reusable workflow that a workflow of the same repository calls by the name owner/repo/.github/workflows/&lt;file>@&lt;ref> of the repository (the repository that --repo names) instead of the path ./.github/workflows/&lt;file>: the rule does not resolve the call by the name to the file, so the rule reads the if on every event; the rule reports a comparison only when the compared value is the attacker's value in every run that the if lets in, and on push the login is empty, so the rule reports nothing
  - finding kinds: unsound-contains.substring, unsound-contains.superstring
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)

The attacker run table has no rows of a run whose actor is an app. The rule also does not read a value of the payload of deployment_status, because the rule does not read deployment_status as an event that an attacker starts

    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker, with an account whose login is ali,

The rule does not read the facts repo.fork-pr-secrets and repo.fork-pr-write-tokens for the runs of a review, and does not count the run of a review of a pull request from a fork as a run of the attacker. When the attacker opened the pull request from a fork, a review of that pull request gives the attacker nothing more than the pull request itself gives: the run takes the workflow of the merge commit of the pull request (GitHub's documentation gives refs/pull/&lt;n>/merge as the ref of the run of a review), and the attacker can change that workflow in the pull request

    # reason: a todo (a fact): the job runs only for a pull request from a

    #   to the runs of pull requests from forks, the run of a review that the

    # cause: the rule does not read the settings of a private repository for

    # situation: labeler.yml runs actions/labeler on pull_request_target with a

- outside-caller: a reusable workflow or composite action that callers in the repository decide, called from another repository on an event, or with a value, an attacker controls: the caller's run has the caller's token and secrets, not the repository's
  - finding kinds: unsound-contains.substring, unsound-contains.superstring
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: .github/workflows/called.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the workflow is called; a job with a secret runs when the
    #   commenter's login is a part of a string of names. Its one caller in the

    #   push alone, and github.event of a push has no comment, so the value that
    #   the run reads is not a value that an attacker wrote. Another repository

    #   wrote, but that run has the token and the secrets of the other repository.
    # cause: the rule reads a called workflow on the events of its callers in
    #   the repository, and ci.yml runs on push alone.
    # attack-value: github.event.comment.user.login = "ali"
    # attack-run-behavior: ci.yml calls this workflow on push, whose event has
    #   no comment, so the attacker's comment does not start it; a caller of
    #   another repository on issue_comment would let ali's comment pass the if
    #   and run ./deploy.sh with that caller's DEPLOY_TOKEN.
    on:
      workflow_call:
    jobs:
      deploy:
        if: contains('alice bob', github.event.comment.user.login)
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: ./deploy.sh
            env:
              TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
    ```
    - .github/workflows/ci.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: push
      jobs:
        call:
          uses: ./.github/workflows/called.yml
      ```
- some-events-path: a comparison of a value whose path one privileged event of the job has and another privileged event of the job does not have, such as github.event.comment.user.login, which issue_comment has and issues does not, in a job on issues and issue_comment: the rule reports no finding, even on the event that has the path

  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)

    #   the job.

- caller-value: a value compared in an action through inputs.&lt;name>, which a caller gives under with:, such as with: who: \${{ github.event.comment.user.login }}: the rule does not follow the value under with: into inputs.&lt;name>

  - finding kinds: unsound-contains.substring, unsound-contains.superstring
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: not-attacker-event.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push, a step runs when github.actor is a part of a string of
    #   names.
    # reason: only those who can write to the repository push, and the
    #   credential premise assumes that no attacker has a credential that pushes,
    #   so no attacker is the actor of the run.

    # attack-value: github.actor = "longuser"

    #   so no run of push has github.actor longuser, and the step runs only for
    #   the accounts that push.

    jobs:

- pull-request: a job that runs only on pull_request, in one of two cases. In the first case, only the pull requests of the repository run the workflow: the author of a pull request can change the workflow itself, so the run of the job gives the author what the run has (read-only from a fork, or what a private repository sends to the runs of pull requests from forks: secrets, a token that writes) without the flaw of the rule, and the flaw of the rule adds nothing to what the author gets. In the second case, a ruleset of the organization or the enterprise runs the workflow on the pull requests of its other repositories (Require workflows to pass before merging, of GitHub Enterprise): the author of such a pull request cannot change the workflow, and whether the run has more than the pull_request workflow of the author would get (the token, secrets) is known from GitHub's documentation only, as no such run was observed; making a required check pass is outside the threat model of the rule. The workflow does not say which case holds, and the rule does not read which case holds
  - finding kinds: unsound-contains.substring, unsound-contains.superstring
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: pull-request.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request, a step runs when github.actor is a part of a
    #   string of names, as in woodruffw/gha-hazmat's unsound-contains.yml
    #   (vulnerable-3, c34857d4ab14af4fdd4c492ba72b9eeb4844da77).
    # reason: when only the pull requests of the repository run the workflow, the
    #   author of the pull request can change the workflow itself and gets what the
    #   run has without the flaw, so the flaw adds nothing to what the author gets;
    #   when a ruleset of the organization or the enterprise runs the workflow on
    #   the pull requests of its other repositories, the author cannot change the
    #   workflow, and what the run of the ruleset has beyond the author's own
    #   pull_request workflow is not known. The workflow does not say which case
    #   holds.
    # cause: pull_request is none of the privileged events the rule reads the if
    #   on. The rule does not read whether a ruleset runs the workflow.
    # attack-value: github.actor = "longuser"
    # attack-run-behavior: a pull request from the fork of the account longuser
    #   runs pull_request with github.actor longuser, a part of longusername, so
    #   the step runs echo hello.
    on: pull_request
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - if: contains('longusername anotherlongusername', github.actor)
            run: echo hello
    ```
- dispatch-actor: a comparison of the actor in a workflow that runs on workflow_dispatch: the actor of a run of workflow_dispatch is the holder of the credential that dispatches the workflow, so whether the name of the actor is a part of a name in the string depends on the account whose credential dispatches the workflow; the inputs, whose whole value the one who dispatches the workflow chooses, and the ref, a branch or a tag of the repository, add nothing to a comparison of a part, as the undetected forms chosen-name and writer-value of this rule say
  - finding kinds: unsound-contains.substring, unsound-contains.superstring
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: dispatcher)
  - example: dispatch-actor.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on workflow_dispatch, a step that reads the secret DEPLOY_TOKEN
    #   runs when github.actor is a part of a string of names.
    # reason: the actor of a run of workflow_dispatch is the holder of the
    #   credential that dispatches the workflow; a credential whose only write
    #   access is to the permission Actions can dispatch the workflow, and the
    #   credential premise keeps the holder of such a credential as a possible
    #   attacker, so whether the name of the actor is a part of a name in the
    #   string is decided by who holds such a credential.
    # cause: the rule reads the if on the privileged events, and workflow_dispatch
    #   is not one.
    # attack: the attacker dispatches the workflow with a credential of the
    #   account longuser whose only write access is to the permission Actions.
    # attack-run-behavior: the run of workflow_dispatch has github.actor
    #   longuser, a part of longusername, so the step runs ./deploy.sh with the
    #   secret DEPLOY_TOKEN in its env.
    on: workflow_dispatch
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - if: contains('longusername anotherlongusername', github.actor)
            env:
              DEPLOY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
            run: ./deploy.sh
    ```
- writer-value: a value only those who can write decide (github.ref on push)
  - finding kinds: unsound-contains.substring, unsound-contains.superstring
  - disposition: no-added-gain

          - run: ./deploy.sh
            env:
              TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
    ```
- script-label: a label that a workflow of the same repository adds from what an attacker wrote, with a token other than the GITHUB_TOKEN, by a script (gh pr edit --add-label, the labels endpoint of the REST API through gh api, addLabels of actions/github-script) or by an action other than actions/labeler: the label is on the pull request or the issue of the attacker, and the rule does not read the scripts and the actions that add labels
  - finding kinds: unsound-contains.substring, unsound-contains.superstring
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - example: .github/workflows/labeled.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: labeler.yml runs on pull_request_target and adds the label test
    #   with gh and a personal access token to a pull request whose title has
    #   [site]; labeled.yml runs on pull_request_target on labeled when
    #   contains('safe-to-test', github.event.label.name) is true, and the job
    #   checks out the head of the pull request and runs npm ci.
    # reason: the attacker writes the title of the pull request, and a label that
    #   a personal access token adds starts the labeled run, so no person approves
    #   the run before the label starts the run.
    # cause: the rule reads the steps of actions/labeler, and does not read the
    #   scripts that add labels.
    # attack-value: the title of the pull request = "[site] fix"
    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork whose
    #   title has [site]; gh adds the label test, which starts labeled.yml, and
    #   contains('safe-to-test', 'test') is true, the checkout fetches the head of
    #   the pull request, and npm ci runs the preinstall script of the pull
    #   request, which prints PWNED, with the secrets of the repository.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    jobs:
      build:
        if: contains('safe-to-test', github.event.label.name)
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
    - .github/workflows/labeler.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml

      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        label:
          if: contains(github.event.pull_request.title, '[site]')
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: gh pr edit "$PR" --repo "$REPO" --add-label test

                REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
      ```
- outside-bot-label: a label that a bot outside the repository adds, such as a bot that adds a label for a command in a comment: the settings of the bot are outside the repository, and the rule does not read whether the bot adds the label for a comment of any user
  - finding kinds: unsound-contains.substring, unsound-contains.superstring
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)

          - run: npm ci

- labeler-pull-request: actions/labeler in a workflow on pull_request with a token other than the GITHUB_TOKEN: a run on the event pull_request for a pull request from a fork gets the secret of the token only when a private repository sends secrets to the runs of pull requests from forks (repo.fork-pr-secrets), and the rule does not read the workflows on pull_request that add labels

  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)

    # attack-run-behavior: when the repository sends secrets to the runs of pull

- labeler-other-event: actions/labeler in a workflow on an event that is not an event of a pull request (workflow_run, schedule), with the number of a pull request in pr-number: the step that finds the number of the pull request and gives the number to pr-number decides which pull request actions/labeler labels, and the rule does not read the step that finds the number

- remote-callee: a job or a step inside a reusable workflow of another repository (uses: owner/repo/.github/workflows/&lt;file>@&lt;ref>) whose content the fact workflow.definition does not give. For every rule: a run that does not ask the fact (a run without --online and without the answer in --facts). For a quality rule, also: a run where the linter asked the fact and got no answer (an answer of unknown: the GitHub API did not give the file), and a call deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact. The rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition. For a rule that is not a quality rule (a rule with a threat), the last two forms are the inconclusive kind remote-callee-unknown, not this form
  - finding kinds: unsound-contains.substring, unsound-contains.superstring
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-callee.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
    #   the repository example-org/unsound-contains-unanswered, whose content is
    #   the workflow of the true positive substring (substring.review.yml) of
    #   the rule, with on: workflow_call in place of the on of
    #   substring.review.yml. The linter has no answer of the fact
    #   workflow.definition for the reusable workflow.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event
    #   that started the run of the calling job, and the linter does not read
    #   the reusable workflow.
    # cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from
    #   the answer of workflow.definition.
    # attack-value: github.event.comment.user.login = "ali"
    # attack-run-behavior: a comment by the account ali on the diff of a pull
    #   request whose branch is in the repository starts the job deploy;
    #   contains('alice bob', 'ali') is true, so ./deploy.sh runs with TOKEN set
    #   to DEPLOY_TOKEN's value.
    on: pull_request_review_comment
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/unsound-contains-unanswered/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

### inconclusive

- remote-callee-unknown: a job that calls a reusable workflow of another repository, when the linter asked the fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow and got no answer (the token that the linter uses cannot read the file, the file is larger than the limit, or the linter has used up the requests it may send to the GitHub API), or when the call is deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact: the rule does not read the jobs and the steps of the reusable workflow
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-callee-unknown.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
    #   the repository example-org/unsound-contains-unknown, whose content is
    #   the workflow of the true positive substring (substring.review.yml) of
    #   the rule, with on: workflow_call in place of the on of
    #   substring.review.yml. The linter asked the fact workflow.definition for
    #   the reusable workflow and got no answer.
    # reason: what the jobs of the reusable workflow do is in the file that the
    #   linter could not read; whoever changes the uses, such as the author of a
    #   pull request, can name a reusable workflow that the token that the
    #   linter uses cannot read.
    # attack-value: github.event.comment.user.login = "ali"
    # attack-run-behavior: a comment by the account ali on the diff of a pull
    #   request whose branch is in the repository starts the job deploy;
    #   contains('alice bob', 'ali') is true, so ./deploy.sh runs with TOKEN set
    #   to DEPLOY_TOKEN's value.
    on: pull_request_review_comment
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/unsound-contains-unknown/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

### false positive forms

- unmatchable-pattern: a label of the configuration of actions/labeler whose globs or regular expressions match no path or no branch name, such as the glob pages/\*\* together with the negated glob !pages/\*\*: the rule reads each glob and each regular expression as one that a pull request can match
  - finding kinds: unsound-contains.substring, unsound-contains.superstring
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: .github/workflows/labeled.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: labeler.yml runs actions/labeler on pull_request_target with a
    #   personal access token; the configuration .github/labeler.yml adds the
    #   label test to a pull request that changes a file that is under site/ and
    #   not under site/, which no file is; labeled.yml runs on pull_request_target
    #   on labeled when contains('safe-to-test', github.event.label.name) is true,
    #   and the job checks out the head of the pull request and runs npm ci.
    # reason: no file matches both globs, so actions/labeler never adds the label,
    #   and only a person adds it.
    # cause: the rule reads each glob as one that a pull request can match.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork that
    #   changes a file under site/; actions/labeler adds no label, and labeled.yml
    #   does not run until a person adds the label test.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    jobs:
      build:
        if: contains('safe-to-test', github.event.label.name)
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
    - finding on: .github/workflows/labeled.yml
    - .github/labeler.yml (repo-file)
      ```yaml
      test:
        - changed-files:
            - all-globs-to-any-file: ['site/**', '!site/**']
      ```
    - .github/workflows/labeler.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: pull_request_target
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        label:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/labeler@v5
              with:
                repo-token: ${{ secrets.LABELER_PAT }}
      ```
- labeled-actor-if: an if that compares the actor or the sender of the labeled run with a name or a type, such as github.event.sender.login == 'release-bot' or github.event.sender.type != 'Bot': the actor of a labeled run whose label actions/labeler adds is the account or the app of the token of actions/labeler, the linter does not know the name or the type of the actor, and the rule reads the if as one that the labeled run passes
  - finding kinds: unsound-contains.substring, unsound-contains.superstring
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: .github/workflows/labeled.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: labeler.yml runs actions/labeler on pull_request_target with a
    #   personal access token; the configuration .github/labeler.yml adds the
    #   label test to a pull request that changes a file under site/; labeled.yml
    #   runs on pull_request_target on labeled when contains('safe-to-test',
    #   github.event.label.name) is true and the sender of the run is the account
    #   release-bot, and the job checks out the head of the pull request and runs
    #   npm ci.
    # reason: the personal access token of actions/labeler belongs to an account
    #   other than release-bot, so the sender of the labeled run is not
    #   release-bot, and the job does not run for the label of actions/labeler.
    # cause: the rule does not know the name of the account of the token, and
    #   reads the if as one that the labeled run passes.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork that
    #   changes a file under site/; actions/labeler adds the label test, which
    #   starts labeled.yml, and the if is false, as the sender of the run is the
    #   account of the token and not release-bot.

      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    jobs:
      build:
        if: contains('safe-to-test', github.event.label.name) && github.event.sender.login == 'release-bot'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
    - finding on: .github/workflows/labeled.yml
    - .github/labeler.yml (repo-file)
      ```yaml
      test:
        - changed-files:
            - any-glob-to-any-file: 'site/**'
      ```
    - .github/workflows/labeler.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: pull_request_target
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        label:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/labeler@v5
              with:
                repo-token: ${{ secrets.LABELER_PAT }}

- labeler-skipped-need: a job whose if calls no status function, that runs actions/labeler or waits for the label that actions/labeler adds (on the activity type labeled, in the job itself or in a job of a reusable workflow that the job calls), and that depends through the needs key on a job whose if calls a status function (for example, if: always()), where the job whose if calls a status function depends through the needs key, directly or through other jobs, on a job that GitHub skips, or that fails, in the run on the pull request of the attacker. GitHub applies a failure or a skip to every job after the skipped or failed job in the chain of the needs key, also after the job whose if calls a status function, so GitHub skips the job that runs actions/labeler or waits for the label, and the step of actions/labeler in a skipped job adds no label. The rule reads the ifs of the chain of the needs key only up to the job whose if calls a status function, and reads the job that runs actions/labeler or waits for the label as a job that runs.
  - finding kinds: unsound-contains.substring, unsound-contains.superstring
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: .github/workflows/labeled.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: labeler.yml runs actions/labeler on pull_request_target with a
    #   personal access token in the job label, which needs the job report, whose
    #   if is always(), and report needs the job check, whose if is false for a
    #   pull request from a fork; the configuration .github/labeler.yml adds the
    #   label test to a pull request that changes a file under site/; labeled.yml
    #   runs on pull_request_target on labeled when contains('safe-to-test',
    #   github.event.label.name) is true, and the job checks out the head of the
    #   pull request and runs npm ci.
    # reason: GitHub skips the job check for the pull request of the attacker, and
    #   a skip applies to every job after the skipped job in the chain of the
    #   needs key, also after the job report, whose if calls always(), so GitHub
    #   skips the job label, and actions/labeler adds no label
    #   (https://github.com/github/docs/blob/404a5f4de6cd5311e3ce2d5c076571291e0107d6/data/reusables/actions/jobs/section-using-jobs-in-a-workflow-needs.md,
    #   and the observation in https://github.com/actions/runner/issues/2205).
    # cause: the rule reads the ifs of the chain of the needs key of the job label
    #   only up to the job report, whose if calls a status function, and reads the
    #   job label as one that runs.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork that
    #   changes a file under site/; GitHub skips the job check, runs the job
    #   report, and skips the job label, so actions/labeler adds no label, and
    #   labeled.yml does not start.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    jobs:
      build:
        if: contains('safe-to-test', github.event.label.name)
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
    - finding on: .github/workflows/labeled.yml
    - .github/labeler.yml (repo-file)
      ```yaml
      test:
        - changed-files:
            - any-glob-to-any-file: 'site/**'
      ```
    - .github/workflows/labeler.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: pull_request_target
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        check:
          if: github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: echo checked
        report:
          needs: check
          if: always()
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: echo reported
        label:
          needs: report
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/labeler@v5
              with:
                repo-token: ${{ secrets.LABELER_PAT }}
      ```
- labeler-other-user: a step of actions/labeler whose if is true only when a step before the step of actions/labeler has failed (for example, if: failure()), after a step that has no timeout-minutes and that runs the code of the pull request of the attacker as a user that is neither root nor the user of the shell of the step (for example, sudo -u nobody, or su nobody -c), where a failure of the code does not end the step (for example, the left of || true, or the condition of an if statement of the shell script). The code of the attacker runs as a user that is not the user of the shell of the step, so the code of the attacker cannot stop the shell of the step by a signal, and the step does not fail. The rule reads the step that runs the code of the attacker as a step that the attacker can make fail, so the rule reads the step of actions/labeler as a step that runs after a failure.
  - finding kinds: unsound-contains.substring, unsound-contains.superstring
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: .github/workflows/labeled.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: labeler.yml runs, on pull_request_target, actions/checkout of
    #   the head of the pull request into pr, then sudo -u nobody ./pr/build.sh
    #   || true, then actions/labeler with if: failure() and a personal access
    #   token; the configuration .github/labeler.yml adds the label test to a
    #   pull request that changes a file under site/; labeled.yml runs on
    #   pull_request_target on labeled when contains('safe-to-test',
    #   github.event.label.name) is true, and the job checks out the head of the
    #   pull request and runs npm ci.
    # reason: the step that runs ./pr/build.sh runs the code of the attacker as
    #   the user nobody, and a failure of the code does not end the step (||
    #   true); the code of the attacker runs as a user that is not the user of
    #   the shell of the step, so the code cannot stop the shell of the step,
    #   the step does not fail, and the step of actions/labeler, whose if is
    #   failure(), does not run (observed on 2026-11-16 on ubuntu-latest: kill
    #   from the user nobody to the shell of the step fails with Operation not
    #   permitted).
    # cause: the rule reads the step that runs ./pr/build.sh as a step that the
    #   attacker can make fail, so the rule reads the step of actions/labeler as
    #   a step that runs after a failure.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork that
    #   changes a file under site/ and whose pr/build.sh tries to stop the shell
    #   of the step; the kill fails, the step succeeds, actions/labeler does not
    #   run and adds no label, and labeled.yml does not start.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    jobs:
      build:
        if: contains('safe-to-test', github.event.label.name)
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
    - finding on: .github/workflows/labeled.yml
    - .github/labeler.yml (repo-file)
      ```yaml
      test:
        - changed-files:
            - any-glob-to-any-file: 'site/**'
      ```
    - .github/workflows/labeler.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: pull_request_target
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        label:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
              with:
                ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
                allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
                persist-credentials: false
                path: pr
            - run: sudo -u nobody ./pr/build.sh || true
            - uses: actions/labeler@v5
              if: failure()
              with:
                repo-token: ${{ secrets.LABELER_PAT }}
      ```
- label-combination: a label that actions/labeler adds only together with another label whose presence makes the if of the job false, such as a label blocked that the if excludes with !contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.\*.name, 'blocked') and that actions/labeler adds on the same condition as the label that the job waits for; or a label that actions/labeler does not add, because the labels that actions/labeler would add together with the label are more than changed-files-labels-limit allows: the rule evaluates the if with the one label that the job waits for
  - finding kinds: unsound-contains.substring, unsound-contains.superstring
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: .github/workflows/labeled.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: labeler.yml runs actions/labeler on pull_request_target with a
    #   personal access token; the configuration .github/labeler.yml adds the
    #   labels test and blocked to a pull request that changes a file under site/;
    #   labeled.yml runs on pull_request_target on labeled when
    #   contains('safe-to-test', github.event.label.name) is true and the pull
    #   request has no label blocked, and the job checks out the head of the pull
    #   request and runs npm ci.
    # reason: actions/labeler adds blocked whenever it adds test, so the pull
    #   request of the attacker has the label blocked, and the job does not run
    #   for it.
    # cause: the rule evaluates the if with the label test alone.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork that
    #   changes a file under site/; actions/labeler adds test and blocked, and the
    #   if of labeled.yml is false.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    jobs:
      build:
        if: contains('safe-to-test', github.event.label.name) && !contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'blocked')
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
    - finding on: .github/workflows/labeled.yml
    - .github/labeler.yml (repo-file)
      ```yaml
      test:
        - changed-files:
            - any-glob-to-any-file: 'site/**'
      blocked:
        - changed-files:
            - any-glob-to-any-file: 'site/**'
      ```
    - .github/workflows/labeler.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: pull_request_target
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        label:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/labeler@v5
              with:
                repo-token: ${{ secrets.LABELER_PAT }}
      ```
- fork-flag-review: a job on pull_request_review or pull_request_review_comment whose if: condition lets the job run only when the head repository of the pull request is a fork, such as a job whose if: condition is github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork: on a pull request from a branch of the repository, the head repository is the repository itself, so in a repository that is not a fork the job runs only for a review of a pull request from a fork. The run of a review of a pull request from a fork has the secrets of the repository or a token that writes only where a private repository gives secrets or a token that writes to the runs of pull requests from forks (the undetected form fork-review). The rule does not read whether the repository that runs the workflow (not the head repository of the pull request) is a fork, and reports the job as if the job ran for a review of a pull request from a branch of the repository
  - finding kinds: unsound-contains.substring
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: fork-flag-review.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on comments on the diff, the job runs ./deploy.sh with
    #   secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN only if contains('alice bob', the login of the
    #   commenter) holds and the pull request is from a fork.
    # reason: the job runs only when the head repository of the pull request
    #   is a fork. On a pull request from a branch of the repository, the head
    #   repository is the repository itself, so in a repository that is not a
    #   fork the job runs only for a review of a pull request from a fork. In
    #   a public repository, the run of such a review has no secrets and a
    #   token that only reads; in a private repository, the run has neither
    #   secrets nor a token that writes unless the repository gives secrets or
    #   a token that writes to the runs of pull requests from forks (the
    #   undetected form fork-review).
    # cause: the rule does not read whether the repository that runs the
    #   workflow (not the head repository of the pull request) is a fork, and
    #   reads the job as if the job ran for a review of a pull request from a
    #   branch of the repository.
    # attack-value: github.event.comment.user.login = "ali"
    # attack-run-behavior: in a public repository that is not a fork, a review
    #   of a pull request from a branch of the repository does not start the
    #   job, as the head repository of such a pull request is the repository
    #   itself; a review of a pull request from a fork starts the job with no
    #   secrets and a token that only reads, so the value reaches no secret
    #   and no token that writes.
    on: pull_request_review_comment
    jobs:
      deploy:
        if: github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork && (contains('alice bob', github.event.comment.user.login))
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: ./deploy.sh
            env:
              TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
    ```
- callee: a reusable workflow or a composite action when all of the following are true: the rule does not know all of the callers of the reusable workflow or the composite action; every workflow that runs the reusable workflow or the composite action (directly, or through another reusable workflow or composite action) is a workflow in the same repository; and the rule would report no finding of the finding kind if the rule read the reusable workflow or the composite action only on the events on which the workflows in the same repository run the reusable workflow or the composite action (for example, every workflow that runs the reusable workflow or the composite action runs only on push). When the rule does not know all of the callers, the rule can read the reusable workflow or the composite action on every event (the worst case). For example, the rule does not know all of the callers when no caller is among the inputs; when the inputs are not the whole repository; for a composite action, when an input is excluded or cannot be read; when a caller names the reusable workflow or the composite action by a name of the form owner/repo/path@ref instead of by a ./ path, in which owner/repo is the repository that the --repo flag names, or is any repository when no --repo flag is given; when a step names the composite action by a ./ path, and either no checkout step runs before that step or the last checkout step before that step is not a plain checkout step (a plain checkout step has no ref input, no repository input and no path input); when a step inside a composite action names another composite action by a ./ path; or when the rule does not know all of the callers of a caller
  - finding kinds: unsound-contains.substring, unsound-contains.superstring
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - example: called/action.yml (action-metadata, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: ci.yml of the repository runs on push alone; the job of ci.yml
    #   checks out the branch main with ref: main and then calls this composite
    #   action by ./called. No other workflow calls this composite action. A step
    #   of this composite action runs ./deploy.sh with the token of the job only
    #   if the if of the step, contains(github.actor, 'alice'), is true.
    # reason: a run of push starts only when a user who can push to the
    #   repository pushes, so the actor of every run of this composite action is
    #   a user who can write to the repository, and an attacker with a login such as alice-x
    #   starts no run of this composite action.
    # cause: the last checkout step before the step that calls this composite
    #   action by a ./ path has the ref input, so the rule does not know which
    #   action.yml the workspace holds, does not know all of the callers of this
    #   composite action, and reads this composite action on every event,
    #   issue_comment among the events.
    # attack-value: github.actor = "alice-x"
    # attack-run-behavior: a comment by the account alice-x on an issue starts no
    #   run of ci.yml. A run of ci.yml starts only on a push to the repository.
    #   So the step of this composite action never runs with github.actor
    #   alice-x.
    name: deploy
    description: deploy for alice
    runs:
      using: composite
      steps:
        - if: contains(github.actor, 'alice')
          run: ./deploy.sh
          shell: bash
          env:
            TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    ```
    - finding on: called/action.yml
    - .github/workflows/ci.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: push
      jobs:
        deploy:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
              with:
                ref: main
            - uses: ./called
      ```
- pull-request-target-blocked: a workflow whose on has pull_request_target and no other event (no workflow_call event either), in a repository whose Actions policies block the runs of the workflow on pull_request_target (repo.pull-request-target-allowed false): an event policy that an administrator sets without pull_request_target among the allowed events, or the default policy that GitHub adds to a public repository without an applicable event policy, from the time when GitHub enforces the default policy on the repository. GitHub's documents say that GitHub evaluates the policies before a run, and that a run that a policy does not allow fails with an error. The documents do not say whether a job of such a run starts before the run fails; the rule assumes that no job of such a run starts
  - finding kinds: unsound-contains.substring, unsound-contains.superstring
  - fact kinds:
    - repo.pull-request-target-allowed (provider: repo-setting, answer that removes the finding: false)
  - example: pull-request-target-blocked.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, the job runs ./deploy.sh with
    #   secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN only if contains('alice bob', the login of the author
    #   of the pull request) holds.
    # reason: the Actions policies of the repository block the runs of the
    #   workflow on pull_request_target: the default policy that GitHub adds to a
    #   public repository without an applicable event policy, from the time when
    #   GitHub enforces the default policy on the repository, or an event policy
    #   whose list of allowed events does not have pull_request_target. GitHub's
    #   documents say that GitHub evaluates the policies before a run, and that a
    #   run that a policy does not allow fails with an error; the documents do not
    #   say whether a job of such a run starts before the run fails, and the rule
    #   assumes that no job starts.
    # cause: unless a file of facts or --fact says that the Actions policies block
    #   runs on pull_request_target (repo.pull-request-target-allowed false), the
    #   rule reports the finding. When no file of facts and no --fact answers
    #   repo.pull-request-target-allowed, the finding is conditional.
    # attack-value: github.event.pull_request.user.login = "ali"
    # attack-run-behavior: the pull request of the attacker triggers
    #   pull_request_target, and the run fails with an error, and no job of the
    #   run starts (the assumption of the reason), so ./deploy.sh never runs.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      deploy:
        if: contains('alice bob', github.event.pull_request.user.login)
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: ./deploy.sh
            env:
              TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
    ```
- actions-policy: a run that the Actions policies of the repository block, in four cases where the rule does not take the policies into account. First, an event policy that blocks an event of the attackers other than pull_request_target (such as issue_comment) in a workflow whose on has that event: the rules ask a fact only for pull_request_target. Second, an actor rule that does not allow the account of the attacker (for example, an actor rule that allows only the repository roles with write access): repo.pull-request-target-allowed is one value for all the runs of a workflow file on pull_request_target, and an actor rule blocks a run by the account that starts the run, so the fact cannot tell what an actor rule blocks. Third, a workflow whose on has pull_request_target and another event: the rule does not ask repo.pull-request-target-allowed for such a workflow, because a run on the other event can reach the job. When the if of the job is false on the other event, so that the job runs only on pull_request_target, and a policy blocks pull_request_target, the finding is a false positive. Fourth, a reusable workflow (on workflow_call) or an action that only workflows on pull_request_target call: the rule asks repo.pull-request-target-allowed only of a workflow whose on has pull_request_target, not of the reusable workflow or the action, so a finding in the reusable workflow or the action is still reported when the policies block the runs of every caller
  - finding kinds: unsound-contains.substring, unsound-contains.superstring
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: actions-policy.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, the job runs ./deploy.sh with
    #   secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN only if contains('alice bob', the login of the author
    #   of the pull request) holds.
    # reason: an actor rule of the Actions policies of the repository allows
    #   only the repository roles with write access to trigger the workflow, so a
    #   run that a pull request from an account without write access triggers
    #   fails. GitHub's documents say that GitHub evaluates the policies before a
    #   run, and that a run that a policy does not allow fails with an error; the
    #   documents do not say whether a job of such a run starts before the run
    #   fails, and the rule assumes that no job starts.
    # cause: the rule does not take the actor rules of the Actions policies into
    #   account: repo.pull-request-target-allowed is one value for all the runs of
    #   the workflow file on pull_request_target, and an actor rule blocks a run
    #   by the account that starts the run.
    # attack-value: github.event.pull_request.user.login = "ali"
    # attack-run-behavior: the account of the attacker is not an allowed actor,
    #   so the run on pull_request_target fails with an error, and no job of the
    #   run starts (the assumption of the reason), so ./deploy.sh never runs.
    name: policy
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      deploy:
        if: contains('alice bob', github.event.pull_request.user.login)
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: ./deploy.sh
            env:
              TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
    ```
- actions-not-allowed: a workflow whose run GitHub does not start, or a job that GitHub fails in the step "Set up job", because of the setting of allowed actions of GitHub (the fact repo.allowed-actions, which the quality rule allowed-actions reads): GitHub does not start a run of a workflow that has a uses, or that calls a reusable workflow that has a uses, that the setting does not allow, and fails a job before any step of the job runs when a step of a composite action that the job runs has a uses that the setting does not allow, or when the setting requires a full commit SHA and a step names an action by a tag or a branch. The harm that the finding reports happens only when GitHub runs the workflow or the job, and the rule does not read repo.allowed-actions
  - finding kinds: unsound-contains.substring, unsound-contains.superstring
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: actions-not-allowed.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the workflow of the true positive substring (substring.yml) of
    #   the rule, with a job added whose step uses
    #   example-org/not-allowed-action, which the setting of allowed actions of
    #   GitHub (repo.allowed-actions) blocks with
    #   !example-org/not-allowed-action@*. In the true positive, on
    #   issue_comment, the job runs ./deploy.sh with secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN only
    #   if contains('alice bob', the commenter's login) holds.
    #   draft-new-release.yml of
    #   thomaseizinger/github-action-gitflow-release-workflow (commit
    #   4eec5c972a744f1da50b9fc9485f39d12f95d400, GHSL-2020-186) runs its job on
    #   issues only if contains('thomaseizinger,yourusername',
    #   github.event.issue.user.login) holds (line 14).
    # reason: GitHub checks each uses of the workflow before the run starts, and
    #   does not start the run because of the uses of
    #   example-org/not-allowed-action: no job of the run runs, so what the
    #   reason of the true positive says does not happen (in runs that the
    #   authors of the rule made on GitHub, such runs ended as startup_failure).
    # cause: the rule does not read repo.allowed-actions.
    # attack-value: github.event.comment.user.login = "ali"
    # attack-run-behavior: GitHub does not start the run, so no step of the run
    #   runs, and the attack does nothing.
    on: issue_comment
    jobs:
      deploy:
        if: contains('alice bob', github.event.comment.user.login)
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: ./deploy.sh
            env:
              TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
      not-allowed:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: example-org/not-allowed-action@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

### threat

- precondition callers-events: a reusable workflow or a composite action that is among the inputs runs on the events of the callers of the workflow or the action, whoever the callers are; when the inputs are the whole repository and hold every caller of the workflow or the action, the rule reads the workflow or the action on the events of the callers, with the values that the callers give under with
  - cites:
    - <https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows#workflow_call>
    - <https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7x29-qqmq-v6qc>
- precondition substring: contains(search, item) is true when the item is a part of the first argument, startsWith(search, item) and endsWith(search, item) when the item is the start or the end of the first argument, all ignoring case: when the string is the first argument, a reference whose value is a part of the string passes; when the reference is the first argument, a reference whose value has the string as a part passes
  - cites:
    - <https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/expressions#contains>
- precondition chosen-login: the attacker chooses the login they register, letters, digits and dashes, 39 at most, as long as no one has it. Besides the login, on pull_request_target on labeled, where a workflow of the same repository runs actions/labeler on the pull request of the attacker with a token other than the GITHUB_TOKEN, the attacker chooses which label of the configuration of actions/labeler the pull request gets, by the files that the pull request changes and by the name of the head branch
  - cites:
    - <https://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor/blob/3c8c3f6aec1dbe9db2cf4bcb2b9216eb5b9c4b95/docs/audits.md#unsound-contains>
- actor: fork-pr-author
  - via: opens or updates a pull request from a fork, which runs pull_request_target, and workflow_run after its pull_request
  - events: pull_request_target, workflow_run
  - run starters: pull_request_target: attacker, workflow_run: attacker
  - gains: read-secrets, write-with-token
- actor: issue-author
  - via: opens an issue or a discussion
  - events: issues, discussion
  - run starters: issues: attacker, discussion: attacker
  - gains: read-secrets, write-with-token
- actor: commenter
  - via: comments on an issue, a pull request or a discussion, or reviews a pull request from a branch of the repository or comments on the diff of the pull request
  - events: issue_comment, discussion_comment, pull_request_review, pull_request_review_comment
  - run starters: issue_comment: attacker, discussion_comment: attacker, pull_request_review: attacker, pull_request_review_comment: attacker
  - gains: read-secrets, write-with-token
- actor: anyone-who-forks
  - via: forks the repository
  - events: fork
  - run starters: fork: attacker
  - gains: read-secrets, write-with-token

### CVSS

#### unsound-contains.substring

- vector: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:L/SC:H/SI:H/SA:N/E:U
- CVSS-B: 9.5 (critical)
- CVSS-BT: 8.2 (high)
- impact: H (from VC, VI, SC, SI)
- likelihood: medium (from AV:N, AT:P, PR:N)
- severity: high (impact H, likelihood medium; the table: sisakulint --explain=terms)
- AV: N
  - reason: the attacker opens an issue, a comment, a review or a pull request over the network
  - cites: none
- AC: L
  - reason: the value is one the attacker chooses
  - cites: none
- AT: P
  - reason: a login that is a part of the string has to be free to register, which the attacker does not decide
  - cites: none
- PR: N
  - reason: on a public repository anyone opens an issue or a pull request from a fork, or reviews a pull request
  - cites: none
- UI: N
  - reason: the event runs the job with nobody doing anything
  - cites: none
- VC: H
  - reason: the job the if guards runs for the attacker with its secrets and token
  - cites: none
- VI: H
  - reason: what such a job does for those it lets in, it does for the attacker
