## untrusted-checkout

- problem: a privileged job that no one approves checks out the code of a pull request, which a step after it may run with the job's secrets and token
- expected: a privileged job checks out only the base's code, or reads the pull request's code as data only
- severity: critical (the worst of its kinds)
- targets: workflow, action-metadata
- facets:
  - weakness: untrusted-code-execution
  - attack-means: code
- default run: always: in a run without --rule, the rule runs unless --skip-rule names the rule

### finding kinds

- untrusted-checkout.executed
  - detected: {uses} checks out {checkout_ref} on {pr_code_on}, and {runs} runs it
  - arguments:
    - {uses}: The uses of the checkout, as written.
    - {checkout_ref}: The reference that names the pull request's code, as written: a context, such as github.event.pull_request.head.sha, or refs/pull/&lt;n>/merge.
    - {pr_code_on}: The privileged events on which the finding holds, each event named once.
    - {runs}: The steps after the checkout that run the checked out code: for each step, the name of the step, or steps&#91;&lt;n>] when the step has no name, with n counted from 0 among all the steps of the job or of the action.
  - consequence: the pull request's author runs their code with the job's secrets and its token
  - remedy: check out the base's code, or run the pull request's code in a pull_request workflow and pass only data to a privileged one
  - severity: critical (found from the CVSS metrics below by the table)
  - fix kinds: base-checkout
  - fact kinds: repo.environment-protected (provider: repo-setting), git.commit-contains (provider: github), repo.pull-request-target-allowed (provider: repo-setting), repo.fork-pr-app-checks (provider: repo-setting)
  - attackers: fork-pr-author, commenter
  - preconditions: privileged-event, pr-tree, no-guard, no-approval, runs-tree, callers-events, app-status-check
  - incidents: spotbugs-2024
  - true positives:
    - .github/workflows/labeled.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: labeler.yml runs actions/labeler on pull_request_target with a
      #   personal access token; the configuration .github/labeler.yml adds the
      #   label safe-to-test to a pull request that changes a file under site/;
      #   labeled.yml runs on pull_request_target on labeled when the label is
      #   safe-to-test, and the job checks out the head of the pull request and runs
      #   npm ci.
      # reason: the attacker chooses the files that the pull request changes, which
      #   actions/labeler reads, and a label that a personal access token adds
      #   starts the labeled run, so no person approves the run before the label
      #   starts the run.
      # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
      # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork that
      #   changes a file under site/ and the files of the attack; actions/labeler
      #   adds the label safe-to-test, which starts labeled.yml, and the checkout
      #   fetches the head of the pull request, and npm ci runs the preinstall
      #   script of the pull request, which prints PWNED, with the secrets of the
      #   repository.
      on:
        pull_request_target:
          types: [labeled]
      jobs:
        build:
          if: github.event.label.name == 'safe-to-test'
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
              with:
                ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
            - run: npm ci
      ```
      - finding on: .github/workflows/labeled.yml
      - .github/labeler.yml (repo-file)
        ```yaml
        safe-to-test:
          - changed-files:
              - any-glob-to-any-file: 'site/**'
        ```
      - .github/workflows/labeler.yml (workflow)
        ```yaml
        on: pull_request_target
        permissions: {}
        jobs:
          label:
            runs-on: ubuntu-latest
            steps:
              - uses: actions/labeler@v5
                with:
                  repo-token: ${{ secrets.LABELER_PAT }}
        ```
    - executed.composer-test.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: pull_request_target checks out the head of a pull request from
      #   a fork, with the guard of actions/checkout taken away, and composer test runs
      #   its code.
      # reason: pull_request_target runs the job with the base repository's token
      #   and secrets, while head.sha is the commit the fork's author pushed, and
      #   composer runs the script test of that commit's
      #   composer.json as a command of composer, and the script pre-command-run
      #   before any command.
      # attack-value: the file composer.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"test\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
      # attack-run-behavior: the checkout fetches head.sha, the fork's commit,
      #   and composer test runs the script test of its composer.json, which prints
      #   PWNED, with the base repository's GITHUB_TOKEN, which the checkout
      #   left in .git/config, and its secrets.
      on: pull_request_target
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
              with:
                ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
                allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
            - run: composer test
      ```
    - .github/workflows/labeled.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: the workflows of fooagen/zellij
      #   (https://github.com/fooagen/zellij/tree/039c8d5962dd341bb58dd7dcd09eb2cf7389ac7a/.github).
      #   For the example, build-artefacts.yaml is named labeled.yml and the
      #   directory docs is named pages, and the checkout has
      #   allow-unsafe-pr-checkout true, so that the checkout behaves as the
      #   checkout of the original did before actions/checkout refused the code of a
      #   fork on pull_request_target. In the workflows, labeler.yaml runs
      #   actions/labeler on pull_request_target with a personal access token; the
      #   configuration .github/labeler.yaml adds the label documentation to a pull
      #   request that changes a Markdown file under pages/; labeled.yml checks out
      #   the merge commit of the pull request and runs npm ci in pages. On
      #   2026-04-25 a pull request from a fork that changed a .mdx file and
      #   pages/package.json got the label, and the labeled run succeeded.
      # reason: the attacker chooses the files of the pull request, which
      #   actions/labeler reads, and a label that a personal access token adds
      #   starts the labeled run, so no person approves the run, and npm ci runs
      #   the pages/package.json of the pull request.
      # attack-value: the file pages/package.json in the pull request's merge commit = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
      # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork that
      #   changes a .mdx file under pages/ and pages/package.json; actions/labeler
      #   adds the label documentation, which starts labeled.yml; the checkout
      #   fetches the merge commit, and npm ci runs the preinstall script of the
      #   pull request, which prints PWNED, with the token of the run.
      name: Build Docs Artefacts

      on:
        pull_request_target:
          types: [labeled]

      permissions:
        contents: read
        pull-requests: write

      jobs:
        build-and-greet:
          if: github.event.label.name == 'documentation'
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest

          steps:
            - name: Checkout PR code
              uses: actions/checkout@v4
              with:
                ref: refs/pull/${{ github.event.number }}/merge
                allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true

            - name: Setup Node.js
              uses: actions/setup-node@v4
              with:
                node-version: 20
                cache: npm
                cache-dependency-path: 'pages/package-lock.json'

            - name: Install dependencies
              working-directory: pages
              run: npm ci

            - name: Build Docusaurus artifacts
              working-directory: pages
              run: npm run build

            - name: Post Welcome Comment
              uses: actions/github-script@v7
              with:
                script: |
                  const gifUrl = "https://media.giphy.com/media/KJ1f5iTl4Oo7u/giphy.gif";

                  github.rest.issues.createComment({
                    issue_number: context.issue.number,
                    owner: context.repo.owner,
                    repo: context.repo.repo,
                    body: `👋 **Thanks for contributing to our documentation!**\n\nThe artifacts have been successfully built for this pull request.\n\n![Thank You GIF](${gifUrl})`
                  })
      ```
      - finding on: .github/workflows/labeled.yml
      - .github/labeler.yaml (repo-file)
        ```yaml
        documentation:
          - changed-files:
              - any-glob-to-any-file:
                  - 'pages/**/*.md'
                  - 'pages/**/*.mdx'
              - all-globs-to-all-files:
                  - 'pages/**/*.md'
                  - 'pages/**/*.mdx'
        ```
      - .github/workflows/labeler.yaml (workflow)
        ```yaml
        name: "Auto Labeler"

        on:
          pull_request_target:
            types: [opened]

        permissions:
          contents: read
          pull-requests: write

        jobs:
          triage:
            runs-on: ubuntu-latest
            steps:
              - name: Apply Documentation Label
                uses: actions/labeler@v5
                with:
                  configuration-path: .github/labeler.yaml
                  sync-labels: true
                  repo-token: ${{ secrets.PAT }}
        ```

      ```yaml
      # situation: on pull_request_target, a job checks out the head commit of the
      #   pull request with actions/checkout v4.2.2, a release older than the first
      #   release of actions/checkout that refuses to check out the code of a pull
      #   request without the input allow-unsafe-pr-checkout, and runs npx
      #   markdownlint-cli. This is ci.yml of eigent-ai/eigent (commit
      #   2a406536e78b3cf50d9add8c3ef81a5b6d75db48, lines 4, 78 and 81).

      # attack: the author of the pull request writes node_modules/.bin/markdownlint

      # attack-run-behavior: npx runs the file of the author.
      # advisory: https://github.com/eigent-ai/eigent/security/advisories/GHSA-gvh4-93cq-5xxp

          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2
              with:
                ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
            - run: npx markdownlint-cli '**/*.md'
      ```

      ```yaml
      # situation: the workflow runs on pull_request_target; the if of the job
      #   whose id is a is false; the job whose id is b needs the job a and has no
      #   if; the job whose id is test needs the job b and has the if failure();
      #   the job whose id is report has no needs and has the if failure(); the
      #   job test and the job report check out the head of the pull request and
      #   run npm ci.
      # reason: GitHub skips the job a, whose if is false, and skips the job b,
      #   which needs the job a. In the if of a job, failure() is true only when a
      #   job that the job needs, directly or through other jobs, fails. No job
      #   fails in this workflow, so failure() is false in the if of the job test
      #   and in the if of the job report, and GitHub skips the job test and the
      #   job report
      #   (https://github.com/github/docs/blob/404a5f4de6cd5311e3ce2d5c076571291e0107d6/content/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/expressions.md).
      # attack-value: the file package.json in the head of the pull request = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
      # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork; GitHub
      #   skips every job of the workflow, so no job checks out the head of the
      #   pull request.
      on: pull_request_target
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        a:
          if: false
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: echo a
        b:
          needs: a
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: echo b
        test:
          needs: b
          if: failure()
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
              with:
                ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
            - run: npm ci
        report:
          if: failure()
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
              with:
                ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
            - run: npm ci
      ```

      ```yaml
      # situation: the workflows of fooagen/zellij
      #   (https://github.com/fooagen/zellij/tree/039c8d5962dd341bb58dd7dcd09eb2cf7389ac7a/.github).
      #   For the example, build-artefacts.yaml is named labeled.yml and the
      #   directory docs is named pages. In the workflows, labeler.yaml runs
      #   actions/labeler on pull_request_target with a personal access token; the
      #   configuration .github/labeler.yaml adds the label documentation to a pull
      #   request that changes a Markdown file under pages/ (under one
      #   changed-files, the configuration has two conditions, and actions/labeler
      #   adds the label when either condition holds); labeled.yml runs on
      #   pull_request_target on labeled when the label is documentation, checks out
      #   the merge commit of the pull request with actions/checkout@v4, and runs
      #   npm ci and npm run build in pages. On 2026-04-25 a pull request from a
      #   fork that changed a .mdx file and pages/package.json got the label, and
      #   the labeled run succeeded, before actions/checkout refused the code of a
      #   fork on pull_request_target.
      # reason: actions/checkout@v4 refuses refs/pull/<n>/merge of a pull request
      #   from a fork on pull_request_target, so the checkout fails and no code of
      #   the pull request runs.
      # attack-value: the file pages/package.json in the pull request's merge commit = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
      # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork that
      #   changes a .mdx file under pages/ and pages/package.json; actions/labeler
      #   adds the label documentation, which starts labeled.yml, and the checkout
      #   fails, so npm ci does not run.
      name: Build Docs Artefacts

      on:
        pull_request_target:
          types: [labeled]

      permissions:
        contents: read
        pull-requests: write

      jobs:
        build-and-greet:
          if: github.event.label.name == 'documentation'
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest

          steps:
            - name: Checkout PR code
              uses: actions/checkout@v4
              with:
                ref: refs/pull/${{ github.event.number }}/merge

            - name: Setup Node.js
              uses: actions/setup-node@v4
              with:
                node-version: 20
                cache: npm
                cache-dependency-path: 'pages/package-lock.json'

            - name: Install dependencies
              working-directory: pages
              run: npm ci

            - name: Build Docusaurus artifacts
              working-directory: pages
              run: npm run build

            - name: Post Welcome Comment
              uses: actions/github-script@v7
              with:
                script: |
                  const gifUrl = "https://media.giphy.com/media/KJ1f5iTl4Oo7u/giphy.gif";

                  github.rest.issues.createComment({
                    issue_number: context.issue.number,
                    owner: context.repo.owner,
                    repo: context.repo.repo,
                    body: `👋 **Thanks for contributing to our documentation!**\n\nThe artifacts have been successfully built for this pull request.\n\n![Thank You GIF](${gifUrl})`
                  })
      ```

        ```yaml
              - any-glob-to-any-file:
                  - 'pages/**/*.md'
                  - 'pages/**/*.mdx'
              - all-globs-to-all-files:
                  - 'pages/**/*.md'
                  - 'pages/**/*.mdx'
        ```

        ```yaml
            steps:
              - name: Apply Documentation Label
                uses: actions/labeler@v5
                with:
                  configuration-path: .github/labeler.yaml
                  sync-labels: true
                  repo-token: ${{ secrets.PAT }}
        ```

      ```yaml
      jobs:
        build:
          if: github.event.label.name == 'safe-to-test'
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
              with:
                ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
            - run: npm ci
      ```

        ```yaml
        permissions: {}
        jobs:

            runs-on: ubuntu-latest

            if: contains(needs.*.result, 'failure')
        ```

      ```yaml
      # situation: labeler.yml runs actions/labeler on pull_request_target with a
      #   personal access token; the configuration .github/labeler.yml adds the
      #   label safe-to-test to a pull request that changes a file under site/;
      #   labeled.yml runs on pull_request_target on labeled, and the job build,
      #   which needs the job pre and runs when the label is safe-to-test and
      #   needs.pre.result is failure, checks out the head of the pull request and
      #   runs npm ci.
      # reason: the if of the job build calls no status function, so GitHub
      #   evaluates the if only when the job pre succeeded, where needs.pre.result
      #   is success, and the if is false; when the job pre fails or is skipped,
      #   GitHub skips the job build; so the job build does not run
      #   (https://github.com/github/docs/blob/404a5f4de6cd5311e3ce2d5c076571291e0107d6/content/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/expressions.md,
      #   status check functions).
      # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
      # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork that
      #   changes a file under site/; actions/labeler adds the label safe-to-test,
      #   which starts labeled.yml; GitHub runs the job pre, and the if of the job
      #   build is false, so the job build does not run.
      on:
        pull_request_target:
          types: [labeled]
      jobs:
        pre:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: echo pre
        build:
          needs: pre
          if: github.event.label.name == 'safe-to-test' && needs.pre.result == 'failure'
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
              with:
                ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
            - run: npm ci
      ```

        ```yaml
        safe-to-test:
          - changed-files:
              - any-glob-to-any-file: 'site/**'
        ```
      - .github/workflows/labeler.yml (workflow)

        ```yaml
        on: pull_request_target
        ```

      ```yaml
      #   build is false; the job test needs the job build, has no if, checks out
      #   the head of the pull request, and runs npm ci.
      # reason: GitHub skips the job build, whose if is false, and skips the job
      #   test, which needs the job build and has no if that calls a status
      #   function; so the job test does not run
      #   (https://github.com/github/docs/blob/404a5f4de6cd5311e3ce2d5c076571291e0107d6/data/reusables/actions/jobs/section-using-jobs-in-a-workflow-needs.md).
      # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
      # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork; GitHub
      #   skips the job build and the job test, so the job test does not run.
      on: pull_request_target
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        build:
          if: false
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: echo built
        test:
          needs: build
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2

                ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
            - run: npm ci
      ```

    - executed.pinned-comment.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on issue_comment pinned, the checkout fetches
      #   refs/pull/<the issue's number>/head, and npm ci runs in it.
      # reason: GitHub pins comments of issues only, not of pull requests, so the
      #   issue's number names no pull request and the ref fetches no code of
      #   one.
      # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
      # attack-run-behavior: the issue of a pinned comment is no pull request, so
      #   refs/pull/<number>/head does not exist, the checkout fails, and npm ci
      #   does not run.
      on: {issue_comment: {types: [pinned]}}
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
              with:
                ref: refs/pull/${{ github.event.issue.number }}/head
            - run: npm ci
      ```
    - called/action.yml (action-metadata, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: the composite action of the true positive executed.no-caller of
      #   this rule; the only caller, ci.yml, runs on pull_request and calls the
      #   action after actions/checkout.
      # reason: the files that the linter reads are the whole repository and hold
      #   every caller of the action, so the rule reads the action on the events of
      #   the callers, in this example, pull_request alone. A run of pull_request for a pull
      #   request from a fork has a read-only GITHUB_TOKEN and no secrets of the
      #   repository.
      # attack-value: the file package.json in the head of the pull request = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
      # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork, which
      #   starts a run of ci.yml on pull_request; npm ci runs the preinstall of the
      #   package.json and prints PWNED, with the read-only GITHUB_TOKEN of the run
      #   of pull_request and no secret. The author of the pull request can get the
      #   same read-only GITHUB_TOKEN without the action, by changing ci.yml in the
      #   pull request.
      name: test
      description: test the pull request
      runs:
        using: composite
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
              allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
          - run: npm ci
            shell: bash
      ```

      ```yaml
      #   every caller of the action, so the rule reads the action on the events of
      #   the callers, here push alone, and a push comes from one who can write to
      #   the repository, not from the attacker.
      # attack-value: the file package.json in the head of the pull request = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
      # attack-run-behavior: the attacker cannot push to the repository, so the
      #   attacker starts no run of ci.yml, and the steps of the action never run on
      #   an event of the attacker.
      name: test
      description: test the pull request
      runs:
        using: composite
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
              allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
          - run: npm ci
            shell: bash
      ```

      ```yaml
      # situation: on pull_request_target, the checkout of the head of the pull
      #   request has the path ${{ runner.temp }}/pr, and npm ci and
      #   $RUNNER_TEMP/pr/build.sh run after it, on a hosted runner.

      #   when the path is not under it; the runner puts runner.temp at
      #   <work>/_temp, next to the workspace <work>/<repository>/<repository>, so
      #   the checkout fails before it fetches anything, and no step runs the code
      #   of the pull request.
      # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
      # attack-run-behavior: the checkout fails with "Repository path ... is not
      #   under ...", the job stops, and neither npm ci nor build.sh runs.
      on: pull_request_target
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
              with:
                ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}

            - run: npm ci
            - run: bash $RUNNER_TEMP/pr/build.sh
      ```

    - executed.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on pull_request_target, the checkout, with no ref, fetches the
      #   workspace, and npm ci runs in it.
      # reason: without a ref of the pull request, the checkout on
      #   pull_request_target fetches the base branch's commit, so npm ci runs the
      #   base's code, not the pull request's.
      # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
      # attack-run-behavior: with no ref, the checkout fetches the commit of the
      #   base branch, so npm ci reads the base's package.json, and the pull
      #   request's preinstall does not run.
      on: pull_request_target
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4

                allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
      ```

- untrusted-checkout.checkout
  - detected: {uses} checks out {checkout_ref} on {pr_code_on}
  - arguments:
    - {uses}: The uses of the checkout, as written.
    - {checkout_ref}: The reference that names the pull request's code, as written.
    - {pr_code_on}: The privileged events on which the finding holds, each event named once.
  - consequence: a step that runs any of it (a build, a test, a script) runs the pull request's author's code with the job's secrets and its token
  - remedy: check out the base's code, or say in a file of facts that the checkout is only read as data
  - severity: critical (found from the CVSS metrics below by the table)
  - fix kinds: base-checkout
  - fact kinds: repo.environment-protected (provider: repo-setting), checkout.executed (provider: user-supplied), git.commit-contains (provider: github), repo.pull-request-target-allowed (provider: repo-setting), repo.fork-pr-app-checks (provider: repo-setting)
  - attackers: fork-pr-author, commenter
  - preconditions: privileged-event, pr-tree, no-guard, no-approval, runs-tree, callers-events, app-status-check
  - incidents: spotbugs-2024
  - true positives:
    - checkout.ghsa-g86g-chm8-7r2p.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on pull_request_target, actions/checkout checks out the merge
      #   commit of the pull request into the root of the workspace, and
      #   check-spelling v0.0.18 (before v0.0.19) reads the files of the checkout.
      #   The job is .github/workflows/spelling.yml of check-spelling/check-spelling
      #   v0.0.18 (commit 08f08a6ff6b9ebae06cb8fe463374a8a5a37e03c, lines 1-21 and
      #   27-30), with uses: ./ (the action of its own repository) written as the
      #   action of the repository check-spelling/check-spelling at the same commit;
      #   the events push and issue_comment, the if of the checkout and the second
      #   checkout are left out.
      # reason: pull_request_target runs the job with the base repository's token,
      #   while the merge commit holds the files the author of the pull request,
      #   from a fork too, pushed, so the files that check-spelling reads are the
      #   author's. GHSA-g86g-chm8-7r2p says that "an attacker can send a crafted
      #   Pull Request that causes a GITHUB_TOKEN to be exposed" through a symlink.
      #   The finding does not say what runs after the checkout: the finding holds
      #   when a step after the checkout runs the files of the checkout (the fact
      #   checkout.executed true), and is conditional when no file of facts and no
      #   --fact answers the fact.
      # attack: the author of a pull request from a fork commits a symbolic link to a
      #   file of the runner that holds the token, and opens the pull request.
      # attack-run-behavior: check-spelling reads the file that the link names as a
      #   file of the pull request and puts its words, the token among them, in its
      #   report, which anyone who reads the log or the comment reads; with the token
      #   the attacker pushes to the base repository.
      # advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g86g-chm8-7r2p
      on: pull_request_target
      jobs:
        build:
          name: Spell checker
          runs-on: ubuntu-20.04
          steps:
            - name: checkout-merge
              uses: actions/checkout@v2.0.0
              with:
                ref: refs/pull/${{github.event.pull_request.number}}/merge
            - name: check-spelling
              uses: check-spelling/check-spelling@08f08a6ff6b9ebae06cb8fe463374a8a5a37e03c # v0.0.18
              with:
                experimental_apply_changes_via_bot: 1
      ```
    - checkout.ghsa-pqwm-q9pv-ph8r.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on pull_request_target, actions/checkout checks out the head of
      #   the pull request into the root of the workspace, and three steps use actions
      #   that read files of the checkout: shivammathur/setup-php 2.37.0, which reads
      #   the version of PHP from .php-version, composer.lock or composer.json;
      #   psf/black 26.1.0 with use_pyproject true, which reads the version of black
      #   from pyproject.toml; and google-github-actions/run-gemini-cli v0.1.21, whose
      #   gemini-cli reads .gemini/.env of the workspace. The advisories describe the
      #   form and name no workflow: GHSA-pqwm-q9pv-ph8r says "a privileged workflow
      #   such as pull_request_target that checks out untrusted pull request code
      #   before invoking setup-php", GHSA-v53h-f6m7-xcgm "A malicious pull request
      #   could edit pyproject.toml", and GHSA-wpqr-6v78-jr5g "CI workflows that
      #   review user-submitted pull requests". The checkout is pinned to v4.2.2, a
      #   release that does not stop the checkout of the code of a fork on
      #   pull_request_target; the tag v4 now names a release (v4.4.0) that fails with
      #   an error there.
      # reason: pull_request_target runs the job with the base repository's token
      #   and secrets, while head.sha is the commit the author of the pull request,
      #   from a fork too, pushed, so the files that the three actions read are the
      #   author's. The finding does not say what runs after the checkout: the
      #   finding holds when a step after the checkout runs the files of the
      #   checkout (the fact checkout.executed true), and is conditional when no
      #   file of facts and no --fact answers the fact; here each of the three
      #   actions runs the files of the checkout.
      # attack: the author of a pull request from a fork commits .php-version, a
      #   pyproject.toml whose version of black is a direct URL to a repository of
      #   theirs, and .gemini/.env, and opens the pull request.
      # attack-run-behavior: setup-php 2.37.0 writes the version from .php-version
      #   into the script it generates and runs, black installs the package of the URL
      #   and runs it, and gemini-cli loads the environment of .gemini/.env before its
      #   sandbox starts; each runs the author's code with the base repository's
      #   token, which the checkout left in .git/config, and the secrets of the job.
      # advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pqwm-q9pv-ph8r
      # advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-v53h-f6m7-xcgm
      # advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wpqr-6v78-jr5g
      # advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jj69-4grx-fqj5
      on: pull_request_target
      permissions:
        contents: write
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2
              with:
                ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
            - uses: shivammathur/setup-php@accd6127cb78bee3e8082180cb391013d204ef9f # 2.37.0
            - uses: psf/black@6305bf1ae645ab7541be4f5028a86239316178eb # 26.1.0
              with:
                use_pyproject: true
            - uses: google-github-actions/run-gemini-cli@9dbec29a20fab3f35017a40ad0eb798a257d4d51 # v0.1.21
              with:
                prompt: Review the pull request.
                gemini_api_key: ${{ secrets.GEMINI_API_KEY }}
      ```
    - checkout.ghsl-2025-094.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on pull_request_target, with contents: write, a job checks out
      #   the head branch of the pull request from the head repository with
      #   actions/checkout v4.2.2, a release older than the first release of
      #   actions/checkout that refuses to check out the code of a pull request
      #   without the input allow-unsafe-pr-checkout, and runs uv pip install with
      #   -e on the directory of the checkout. This is pr_autoupdate.yaml of
      #   ag2ai/faststream (commit 12fdfa25651a672ba4abcae981df255d782cbd93, lines
      #   4, 25-26 and 46).
      # reason: uv pip install -e builds the project of the checkout, which runs the
      #   build backend that pyproject.toml of the author of the pull request names;
      #   uv is not in the table of tools of the rule, so the rule reports the kind
      #   checkout, which holds when a later step runs the files.
      # attack: the author of the pull request writes a build backend in
      #   pyproject.toml of the head branch.
      # attack-run-behavior: uv pip install runs the build backend of the author.
      # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2025-094_ag2ai_faststream/
      on:
        pull_request_target:
          types: [opened, synchronize, ready_for_review]
      permissions:
        contents: write
      jobs:
        autoupdate:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2
              with:
                repository: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name }}
                ref: ${{ github.head_ref }}
                persist-credentials: false
            - run: uv pip install --system --group dev -e .
      ```
    - checkout.ghsl-2026-208.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on workflow_run, a job checks out the head commit of the run that
      #   triggered the workflow, from the head repository of the run (the fork of a
      #   pull request), and runs SonarScanner with the secret SONAR_TOKEN and
      #   -Dproject.settings=sonar.properties. These are the steps of sonarcloud.yml
      #   of kptdev/kpt (commit 6345d96d661eae1f6cdcb97b1f70080ce35f61a4, lines
      #   90-147).
      # reason: SonarScanner reads sonar.properties of the commit that the job
      #   checked out, and the author of the fork writes sonar.host.url in that
      #   file, so the scanner sends SONAR_TOKEN to a host of the author.
      #   request-forgery does not report it (the undetected form workspace-config).
      # attack: the author of the pull request of a fork writes
      #   sonar.host.url=https://attacker.example in sonar.properties of the head
      #   commit.
      # attack-run-behavior: the scanner reads sonar.properties of the checkout and
      #   sends SONAR_TOKEN to https://attacker.example.
      # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2026-208_kptdev_kpt_repository/
      on:
        workflow_run:
          workflows: [Go]
          types: [completed]
      jobs:
        sonarqube:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          permissions:
            actions: read
            contents: read
            pull-requests: read
          steps:
            - name: Checkout PR head
              uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v7.0.0
              with:
                repository: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name }}
                ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
                fetch-depth: 0
                persist-credentials: false
                allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
            - name: SonarQube Scan on PR
              uses: SonarSource/sonarqube-scan-action@713881670b6b3676cda39549040e2d88c70d582e # v8.2.0
              env:
                SONAR_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SONAR_TOKEN }}
              with:
                args: >
                  -Dsonar.projectKey=kptdev_kpt
                  -Dsonar.organization=kptdev
                  -Dproject.settings=sonar.properties
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - checkout.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on pull_request_target, the checkout, with no ref, fetches into
      #   pr/, and a step only runs echo.
      # reason: without a ref of the pull request, the checkout on
      #   pull_request_target fetches the base branch's commit, so the tree in pr/
      #   holds none of the pull request's code.
      # attack-value: the file build.sh in the pull request's head = "#!/bin/sh\necho PWNED\n"
      # attack-run-behavior: with no ref, the checkout fetches the commit of the
      #   base branch into pr, so the pull request's build.sh is not there, and
      #   the job only runs echo checked out.
      on: pull_request_target
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
              with:
                allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
                path: pr
            - run: echo checked out
      ```

### fix kinds

- base-checkout: check out the base's code: take out the inputs that name the pull request's (ref, and repository when it is the fork)
  - safety: review
  - possible side effects:
    - pr-code-not-built: The job no longer builds or tests the code of the pull request.

### undetected forms

- outside-caller: a reusable workflow or composite action that callers in the repository decide, called from another repository on an event, or with a value, an attacker controls: the caller's run has the caller's token and secrets, not the repository's
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout.executed, untrusted-checkout.checkout
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: .github/workflows/called.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the workflow is called; it checks out the pull request's head
    #   SHA with allow-unsafe-pr-checkout and runs sudo pr/build.sh. Its one
    #   caller in the repository, ci.yml, runs on push.
    # reason: no added gain for this repository: ci.yml calls the workflow on
    #   push alone, and github.event of a push has no pull request, so the value
    #   that the run reads is not a value that an attacker wrote. Another
    #   repository may call the workflow on an event whose payload has what an
    #   attacker wrote, but that run has the token and the secrets of the other
    #   repository.
    # cause: the rule reads a called workflow on the events of its callers in
    #   the repository, and ci.yml runs on push alone.
    # attack-value: the file build.sh in the pull request's head = "#!/bin/sh\necho PWNED\n"
    # attack-run-behavior: ci.yml calls it on push, whose event has no
    #   pull_request, so the ref is empty and the checkout fetches the pushed
    #   commit into pr, and sudo pr/build.sh runs that commit's build.sh; the
    #   pull request's build.sh is not fetched. A workflow of another repository
    #   that calls it on pull_request_target would fetch the pull request's
    #   head, with that repository's token.
    on:
      workflow_call:
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
              allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
              path: pr
          - run: sudo pr/build.sh
    ```
    - .github/workflows/ci.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: push
      jobs:
        call:
          uses: ./.github/workflows/called.yml
      ```
- git-in-run: the code of a pull request fetched by git or gh in a run (git fetch origin pull/&lt;n>/head, gh pr checkout), not by actions/checkout
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout.executed, untrusted-checkout.checkout
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: git-in-run.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a run fetches the pull request's head
    #   with git, checks it out, and runs npm ci.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): reading git in a run would find it.
    # cause: the rule reads checkouts by actions/checkout only.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: git fetch takes pull/<n>/head of the base repository,
    #   which GitHub keeps at the fork's head, git checkout pr switches the
    #   workspace to it, and npm ci runs its preinstall, which prints PWNED,
    #   with the GITHUB_TOKEN actions/checkout left in .git/config and the job's
    #   secrets.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - run: |
              git fetch origin "pull/${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}/head:pr"
              git checkout pr
              npm ci
    ```
  - example: git-in-run.ghsl-2025-080.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issue_comment, when the comment is on a pull request and
    #   starts with @nf-core-bot changelog, and on pull_request_target opened, a
    #   run step sets PR_NUMBER to the number of the pull request and checks out
    #   the pull request with gh pr checkout $PR_NUMBER; a later step runs a
    #   python script of the checked-out tree, with a secret token. This is
    #   changelog.yml of nf-core/tools (commit
    #   75e643ad2c62cdc8ecd39aa56c0c314efd4b13e4, lines 1-37 and 50-55). The step
    #   that sets up Python, the step that installs packages, the variables of
    #   the python step other than the token, and the steps after the python
    #   step are left out. update-textual-snapshots.yml of the same commit
    #   (GHSL-2025-078, lines 1-13, 28-32 and 45-49) runs only on issue_comment,
    #   checks out the pull request with gh pr checkout and the number of the
    #   issue written by ${{ }}, and then runs pytest on the checked-out tree.
    #   galata-update.yml of jupyterlab/jupyterlab (commit
    #   362818faf8472179a3d0a87a58c3279efe003912, GHSL-2024-144, whose issue is
    #   GHSL-2024-138) runs gh pr checkout ${{ github.event.issue.number }} on
    #   issue_comment and then bash ./scripts/ci_install.sh of the pull request.
    #   scala3doc.yaml of lampepfl/dotty (commit
    #   3f4b10156da96e6ccea58e4955587c94a95294ac, GHSL-2020-272) runs git fetch
    #   and git checkout of refs/pull/$PR_NUMBER/merge on pull_request_target
    #   (lines 25-26), and pr.yml of gpuweb/cts (commit
    #   d516cfa8fe73f31b7c788e6b182360b843d52587, GHSL-2020-317) runs git fetch
    #   and git checkout of github.event.pull_request.head.sha (lines 17-18);
    #   later steps run sbt and npm over the checkout.
    # reason: the rule does not read gh or git in a run; reading gh pr checkout,
    #   or git fetch and git checkout of the pull request, in the run step would
    #   find the checkout of the pull request.
    # cause: the rule reads checkouts by actions/checkout only.
    # attack-value: the file .github/workflows/changelog.py in the pull request's head = "print(\"PWNED\")\n"
    # attack-run-behavior: when the author of a pull request from a fork opens
    #   the pull request, or comments @nf-core-bot changelog on the pull request,
    #   gh pr checkout switches the workspace to the head of the pull request,
    #   and python runs the changelog.py of the author, which prints PWNED, with
    #   the secret NF_CORE_BOT_AUTH_TOKEN in the environment.
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2025-080_nf-core_tools/
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2025-078_nf-core_tools/
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-144_JupyterLab/
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2020-272-lampepfl-dotty-workflow/
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2020-317-gpuweb-cts-workflow/
    on:
      issue_comment:
        types: [created]
      pull_request_target:
        types: [opened]
        branches:
          - dev
    jobs:
      update_changelog:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        if: |
          github.repository_owner == 'nf-core' && (
            github.event_name == 'pull_request_target' ||
            github.event.issue.pull_request && startsWith(github.event.comment.body, '@nf-core-bot changelog')
          )
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4
            with:
              token: ${{ secrets.NF_CORE_BOT_AUTH_TOKEN }}
          - name: Checkout Pull Request
            env:
              GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NF_CORE_BOT_AUTH_TOKEN }}
            run: |
              if [[ "${{ github.event_name }}" == "issue_comment" ]]; then
                PR_NUMBER="${{ github.event.issue.number }}"
              elif [[ "${{ github.event_name }}" == "pull_request_target" ]]; then
                PR_NUMBER="${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}"
              fi
              gh pr checkout $PR_NUMBER
          - name: Update CHANGELOG.md from the PR title
            env:
              GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NF_CORE_BOT_AUTH_TOKEN }}
            run: |
              python ${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/.github/workflows/changelog.py
    ```
- artifact: the code of a pull request brought by the artifact of a run it drives: artifact-poisoning reports it
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout.executed, untrusted-checkout.checkout
  - disposition: other-rule (rule: artifact-poisoning)
  - example: artifact.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on workflow_run, the artifact of the run workflow_run follows
    #   is downloaded into the workspace, and ./build.sh runs.
    # reason: another rule's: the pull request's code comes in an artifact,
    #   which artifact-poisoning reports.
    # cause: the rule reads checkouts by actions/checkout, not downloads.
    # attack-value: the file build.sh in the artifact of the pull request's ci run = "#!/bin/sh\necho PWNED\n"
    # attack-run-behavior: the fork's pull request changes ci so its run uploads
    #   build.sh; when that run completes, the download takes its artifact by
    #   workflow_run.id with the token into the workspace, and ./build.sh runs
    #   it, with this run's token and the base repository's secrets.
    on:
      workflow_run:
        workflows: [ci]
        types: [completed]
    permissions: {actions: read}
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
            with:
              run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
              github-token: ${{ github.token }}
          - run: ./build.sh
    ```
- cache: the code of a pull request brought by a cache that another run or job wrote
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout.executed, untrusted-checkout.checkout
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: cache.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, actions/cache/restore restores
    #   node_modules, and npm test runs.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the pull request's code comes in a cache
    #   another run wrote, not by a checkout.
    # cause: the rule does not read caches.
    # attack: code of the pull request, run in another run that shares the base
    #   branch's cache scope, saves node_modules under the key deps-<hash> with
    #   a module that prints PWNED when it is loaded.
    # attack-run-behavior: the restore puts that node_modules in the workspace,
    #   and npm test runs the test script, which loads the planted module, with
    #   the base repository's token and secrets.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
            with:
              path: node_modules
              key: deps-${{ hashFiles('package-lock.json') }}
          - run: npm test
    ```
- remote-action: a checkout in an action of another repository: the rule does not read the action
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout.executed, untrusted-checkout.checkout
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-action.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a step uses an action of another
    #   repository whose checkout takes the pull request's code, as in the
    #   Ultralytics incident (ultralytics/actions
    #   eb1201bd933b9f6096c64525ccaee3684c91bf14, action.yml:94: repository: ${{
    #   github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name || github.repository }}).
    #   The job review uses anthropics/claude-code-action pinned to the commit
    #   of v1.0.73, which checks out the head branch of the pull request and
    #   starts every MCP server of the .mcp.json of the checkout
    #   (GHSA-8q5r-mmjf-575q: "checking out PR head branches
    #   (attacker-controlled), reading `.mcp.json` from the working directory
    #   via default setting sources, and unconditionally enabling all project
    #   MCP servers via `enableAllProjectMcpServers`"); the advisory names no
    #   workflow, and the job is the automatic trigger it describes.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the checkout is in an action of another
    #   repository.
    # cause: the rule does not read the action.yml of another repository.
    # attack-value: the file prettier.config.js in the pull request's head = "console.log(\"PWNED\"); module.exports = {};\n"
    # attack-run-behavior: the action checks out the branch github.head_ref of
    #   github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name, the fork, with its token
    #   input, and its later steps run tools over that tree when their inputs
    #   turn them on: with prettier: true, npx prettier loads the pull request's
    #   prettier.config.js, which prints PWNED. This example passes no inputs,
    #   and the action's defaults turn those steps off. In the job review,
    #   claude-code-action v1.0.73 checks out the head branch of the pull
    #   request and starts the server of its .mcp.json, a command that the
    #   author of the pull request writes, with the secrets of the job, before
    #   the agent chooses any tool.
    # advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8q5r-mmjf-575q
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      format:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: ultralytics/actions@main
      review:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: anthropics/claude-code-action@1b422b3517b51140e4484faab676c5e68b914866 # v1.0.73
            with:
              anthropic_api_key: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
              prompt: Review the pull request.
    ```
  - example: remote-action.ghsl-2026-203.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issue_comment, when the comment is on a pull request and
    #   contains please update snapshots, a step uses the composite action
    #   update-snapshots-checkout of jupyterlab/maintainer-tools; a later step
    #   uses the local action ./.github/actions/build-dist. The action stops
    #   unless the author_association of the comment is OWNER, COLLABORATOR or
    #   MEMBER, stops when the head repository of the pull request was pushed
    #   at a later whole second than the comment, and then checks out
    #   the pull request with gh pr checkout in a run step. This is
    #   playwright-update.yml of jupyter/notebook (commit
    #   1cabcced0af1f7d6e43f06cec6883576399d6ac1, lines 1-35), with the action
    #   at commit b48fcdb87e70c45789abd80d4042b06641e47b46 (action.yml, lines
    #   15-36 and 54-91). The matrix of the job, the step Base Setup and the
    #   steps after the step Build are left out.
    # reason: the rule does not read the action.yml of another repository, and
    #   inside the action, the checkout of the pull request is gh pr checkout in
    #   a run step, which the rule does not read either (the undetected form
    #   git-in-run); reading both would find the checkout of the pull request.
    # cause: the rule does not read the action.yml of another repository.
    # attack-value: the file .github/actions/build-dist/action.yml in the pull request's head = "runs:\n  using: composite\n  steps:\n    - run: echo PWNED\n      shell: bash\n"
    # attack-run-behavior: after an OWNER, a COLLABORATOR or a MEMBER comments
    #   please update snapshots, the author of the pull request pushes a commit
    #   in the same second as the comment; the times compare equal, so the
    #   action does not stop, and the action checks out the pushed commit. The
    #   step Build then runs the author's
    #   ./.github/actions/build-dist/action.yml, which prints PWNED, with the
    #   GITHUB_TOKEN of contents: write.
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2026-203_jupyter_notebook_repository/
    on:
      issue_comment:
        types: [created, edited]
    jobs:
      update-snapshots:
        if: github.event.issue.pull_request && contains(github.event.comment.body, 'please update snapshots')
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions:
          contents: write
          pull-requests: write
        steps:
          - uses: jupyterlab/maintainer-tools/.github/actions/update-snapshots-checkout@b48fcdb87e70c45789abd80d4042b06641e47b46 # v1
            with:
              github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          - name: Build
            uses: ./.github/actions/build-dist
    ```
- literal-ref: a ref written out, such as a branch's name of the repository
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout.executed, untrusted-checkout.checkout
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: literal-ref.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, actions/checkout checks out gh-pages, a
    #   branch of the repository written out, and make runs.
    # reason: no added gain: the ref is the repository's, not the pull
    #   request's.
    # cause: the rule reads a ref written out as the base's code.
    # attack-value: the file Makefile in the pull request's head = "all:\n	echo PWNED\n"
    # attack-run-behavior: the checkout fetches gh-pages of the base repository,
    #   not the pull request's head, so make runs the base's Makefile, and the
    #   pull request's does not run.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: gh-pages
          - run: make
    ```
- branch-name-ref: the name of the pull request's branch as the ref with the base repository: from a fork, the base has no such branch, or its own; from the repository, the author can write to it
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout.executed, untrusted-checkout.checkout
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: branch-name-ref.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, actions/checkout checks out the pull
    #   request's branch name with the base repository, and npm ci runs.
    #   snapshot.yml of nuxt/create-nuxt-app (commit
    #   1aa53fd846e0d0390f0407653b624b1e46ef1d6e, GHSL-2020-276) and sync.yml of
    #   nuxt/modules (commit 2ae2a0c2fcb1869153b658522340d0b5b24b3376) check out
    #   github.head_ref the same way and run yarn; the page says the workflows
    #   check out "a branch from the base repository named as the branch from
    #   the PR".
    # reason: no added gain: from a fork the base has no such branch (the
    #   checkout fails); from the repository the author can write to it.
    # cause: the rule reads a branch's name as the pull request's code only with
    #   the fork as the repository.
    # attack-value: the file package.json on the pull request's branch = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: the checkout fetches the branch github.head_ref names
    #   from the base repository: for a fork's branch the base has no such
    #   branch and the step fails, or has one of the same name, whose
    #   package.json is the base's; for a branch of the repository, npm ci runs
    #   the preinstall its author pushed.
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2020-276-nuxt-create-nuxt-app-workflow/
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.head_ref }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
- pull-request: a job that runs only on pull_request, in one of two cases. In the first case, only the pull requests of the repository run the workflow: the author of a pull request can change the workflow itself, so the run of the job gives the author what the run has (read-only from a fork, or what a private repository sends to the runs of pull requests from forks: secrets, a token that writes) without the flaw of the rule, and the flaw of the rule adds nothing to what the author gets. In the second case, a ruleset of the organization or the enterprise runs the workflow on the pull requests of its other repositories (Require workflows to pass before merging, of GitHub Enterprise): the author of such a pull request cannot change the workflow, and whether the run has more than the pull_request workflow of the author would get (the token, secrets) is known from GitHub's documentation only, as no such run was observed; making a required check pass is outside the threat model of the rule. The workflow does not say which case holds, and the rule does not read which case holds
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout.executed, untrusted-checkout.checkout
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: pull-request.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request, the pull request's head SHA is checked out,
    #   and npm ci runs.
    # reason: when only the pull requests of the repository run the workflow, the
    #   author of the pull request can change the workflow itself and gets what the
    #   run has without the flaw, so the flaw adds nothing to what the author gets;
    #   when a ruleset of the organization or the enterprise runs the workflow on
    #   the pull requests of its other repositories, the author cannot change the
    #   workflow, and what the run of the ruleset has beyond the author's own
    #   pull_request workflow is not known. The workflow does not say which case
    #   holds.
    # cause: the rule reads checkouts on pull_request_target, workflow_run and
    #   issue_comment only. The rule does not read whether a ruleset runs the
    #   workflow.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: the fork's pull request runs this workflow on
    #   pull_request; the checkout fetches head.sha and npm ci runs the preinstall,
    #   which prints PWNED, with a read-only GITHUB_TOKEN and none of the base
    #   repository's secrets. When a ruleset of the organization runs the workflow
    #   on a pull request of another repository, the same steps run in the run of
    #   the ruleset; what the run of the ruleset has was not observed, so whether
    #   the steps do harm in the run of the ruleset is not known.
    on: pull_request
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
- new-activity-type: an activity type GitHub added after the schemas the tables are made from, written in types: a value of types the tables do not have is dropped, as GitHub drops one it has no such activity type for
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout.executed, untrusted-checkout.checkout
  - disposition: todo (needs: pin-update)
  - example: new-activity-type.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target of an activity type added_later, the
    #   pull request's head SHA is checked out, and npm ci runs.
    # reason: a todo (a pin update): an activity type GitHub added after the
    #   pinned schemas is missed until the pins are updated.
    # cause: the analysis drops a value of types it does not know, as GitHub
    #   does for a value it has no such activity type for, so the job has no
    #   attacker's event.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: when GitHub sends pull_request_target with the
    #   activity type added_later, the job checks out head.sha and npm ci runs
    #   the preinstall, which prints PWNED, with the base repository's
    #   GITHUB_TOKEN in .git/config and its secrets.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [added_later]
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
- not-privileged: a job only on events that no attacker triggers (push, schedule), or on the events of a review (pull_request_review, pull_request_review_comment), where the code of the attacker reaches the checkout only in the run of a review of the pull request of the attacker, which runs the workflow of the merge commit of the pull request (refs/pull/&lt;n>/merge), and the attacker can change that workflow in the pull request (a job on pull_request is the undetected form pull-request); on workflow_dispatch, a checkout with no input of workflow_dispatch in its ref and repository, and no value made from one, brings a branch or a tag of the repository, which only those who can write to the repository change (the one who dispatches the workflow chooses the branch or the tag); repository_dispatch, whose sender has write access to the permission Contents, which the credential premise assumes no attacker has
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout.executed, untrusted-checkout.checkout
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: not-privileged.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push and pull_request_review, the pull request's head SHA is
    #   checked out, and npm ci runs.
    # reason: only those who can write to the repository push, and the code of
    #   the attacker reaches the checkout only in the run of a review of the pull
    #   request of the attacker, which runs the workflow of the merge commit of
    #   the pull request, a workflow that the attacker can change in the pull
    #   request.
    # cause: the rule reads checkouts on pull_request_target, workflow_run and
    #   issue_comment only.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: on pull_request_review of the fork's pull request,
    #   the checkout fetches head.sha and npm ci runs the preinstall, in the run
    #   of the workflow of the merge commit, which the attacker could change in
    #   the pull request to run the same code without the checkout; on push
    #   the event has no pull_request, so the ref is empty and the checkout
    #   fetches the pushed commit.
    on: [push, pull_request_review]
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
- guarded-checkout: a checkout on pull_request_target or workflow_run by a release of actions/checkout that refuses a fork's code (a major tag from v2, or a release from the guard), without allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: the step fails before anything runs
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout.executed, untrusted-checkout.checkout
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: guarded-checkout.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, actions/checkout@v4 checks out the pull
    #   request's head SHA, and npm ci runs.
    # reason: no added gain: actions/checkout@v4 (the major tag moved to v4.4.0
    #   on 2026-07-20) refuses the fork's head on pull_request_target; the step
    #   fails before npm runs.
    # cause: the rule takes a major tag of actions/checkout from v2 as refusing
    #   a fork's code.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: actions/checkout@v4 sees that the head repository is
    #   a fork and the event is pull_request_target, and without
    #   allow-unsafe-pr-checkout fails the step; npm ci does not run.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
  - example: guarded-checkout.ghsl-2025-009.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, actions/checkout@v4 checks out the head
    #   branch of the pull request from the head repository, and pip installs the
    #   checked-out tree. This is benchmarks.yml of projectmesa/mesa (commit
    #   cfb19251ab720497a4ba5093160958c2621adbf4, lines 3-21 and 50-60). The steps
    #   before the checkout, which run the benchmarks of the main branch, and the
    #   steps after pip install are left out. GHSL-2025-006 has the same form: the
    #   job visualize of validate-lut-files.yml of
    #   bramstroker/homeassistant-powercalc (commit
    #   e5195a551b8b15944cecd8d0a587a5ce4d852f16, lines 3-7 and 25-37) checks out
    #   github.event.pull_request.head.sha with actions/checkout@v4 and uses the
    #   composite action ./.github/workflows/poetry-composite-action of the
    #   checkout.
    # reason: a major tag of actions/checkout moves to the latest release of the
    #   major version, and the tag v4 now names a release (v4.4.0 or later; the tags
    #   v2 and v3 name v2.8.0 and v3.7.0, which also refuse) that refuses the code
    #   of a fork on pull_request_target, so the checkout fails before pip runs.
    #   When GitHub Security Lab reported the workflow (2025-01-13), the tag v4
    #   named a release without the refusal, and the workflow of that time ran the
    #   code of the fork.
    # cause: the rule reads each major tag of actions/checkout from v2 to v4 as
    #   the release that the tag names now, which refuses the code of a fork; the
    #   rule does not read the release that the tag named in the past.
    # attack-value: the file setup.py in the pull request's head = "print(\"PWNED\")\n"
    # attack-run-behavior: actions/checkout@v4 sees that the head repository is a
    #   fork and the event is pull_request_target; the checkout without the input
    #   allow-unsafe-pr-checkout fails, and pip install does not run.
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2025-009_Mesa/
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2025-006_homeassistant-powercalc/
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [opened, ready_for_review, labeled]
        branches:
          - main
    permissions:
      issues: write
      pull-requests: write
    jobs:
      run-benchmarks:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - name: Checkout PR branch
            uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}
              repository: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name }}
              persist-credentials: false
          - name: Install Mesa of the PR branch
            run: pip install --no-deps .
    ```
- guard-gap: a checkout the guard of actions/checkout lets through at run time that the rule takes as refused: a fork deleted since the pull request, whose repository is not in the event (refs/pull/&lt;n>/head written with capitals, which its pattern does not match, is reported)
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout.executed, untrusted-checkout.checkout
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: guard-gap.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, actions/checkout@v4 checks out the pull
    #   request's head SHA, and npm ci runs.
    # reason: a limitation (run time): the guard checks a fork by the id of the
    #   head repository in the event (actions/checkout v7.0.1
    #   src/unsafe-pr-checkout-helper.ts:53); a fork deleted since the pull
    #   request has none, and the checkout is let through at run time.
    # cause: the rule takes @v4 as refusing, and reports nothing.
    # attack: the author opens the pull request from a fork whose package.json
    #   has a preinstall that prints PWNED, and deletes the fork before the run.
    # attack-run-behavior: the event then has no id of the head repository, so
    #   the guard of actions/checkout lets the checkout through; it fetches
    #   head.sha, which refs/pull/<n>/head keeps, and npm ci runs the preinstall
    #   with the base repository's GITHUB_TOKEN in .git/config and its secrets.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
- script-label: a label that a workflow of the same repository adds from what an attacker wrote, with a token other than the GITHUB_TOKEN, by a script (gh pr edit --add-label, the labels endpoint of the REST API through gh api, addLabels of actions/github-script) or by an action other than actions/labeler: the label is on the pull request or the issue of the attacker, and the rule does not read the scripts and the actions that add labels
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout.executed, untrusted-checkout.checkout
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - added attackers: triage-account, writer-pull-requests-token, app-installation-token
  - example: .github/workflows/labeled.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: labeler.yml runs on pull_request_target and adds the label
    #   safe-to-test with gh and a personal access token to a pull request whose
    #   title has [site]; labeled.yml runs on pull_request_target on labeled when
    #   the label is safe-to-test, and the job checks out the head of the pull
    #   request and runs npm ci.
    # reason: the attacker writes the title of the pull request, and a label that
    #   a personal access token adds starts the labeled run, so no person approves
    #   the run before the label starts the run.
    # cause: the rule reads the steps of actions/labeler, and does not read the
    #   scripts that add labels.
    # attack-value: the title of the pull request = "[site] fix"
    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork whose
    #   title has [site]; gh adds the label safe-to-test, which starts
    #   labeled.yml, and the checkout fetches the head of the pull request, and
    #   npm ci runs the preinstall script of the pull request, which prints PWNED,
    #   with the secrets of the repository.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    jobs:
      build:
        if: github.event.label.name == 'safe-to-test'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
    - .github/workflows/labeler.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml

      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        label:
          if: contains(github.event.pull_request.title, '[site]')
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: gh pr edit "$PR" --repo "$REPO" --add-label safe-to-test
              env:
                GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.LABELER_PAT }}
                PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
                REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
      ```
- outside-bot-label: a label that a bot outside the repository adds, such as a bot that adds a label for a command in a comment: the settings of the bot are outside the repository, and the rule does not read whether the bot adds the label for a comment of any user
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout.executed, untrusted-checkout.checkout

  - added attackers: triage-account, writer-pull-requests-token, app-installation-token

    ```yaml
    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork and

            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
- labeler-pull-request: actions/labeler in a workflow on pull_request with a token other than the GITHUB_TOKEN: a run on the event pull_request for a pull request from a fork gets the secret of the token only when a private repository sends secrets to the runs of pull requests from forks (repo.fork-pr-secrets), and the rule does not read the workflows on pull_request that add labels

- deployment-status: a value of the payload of deployment_status, such as the SHA of the deployment (deployment.sha), when an app outside GitHub Actions makes a deployment and a status of the deployment for a commit of a pull request from a fork: no run of deployment_status started when the authors of the linter tried this, and why the run did not start was not found; the rule does not read deployment_status as an event that an attacker starts
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout.executed, untrusted-checkout.checkout
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: deployment-status.yml (workflow, undetected)

    ```yaml
    # situation: on deployment_status, which an app outside GitHub Actions starts
    #   when the app makes a status of a deployment, the job checks out the
    #   commit of the deployment (github.event.deployment.sha) and runs npm ci.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): no run of deployment_status started when a GitHub
    #   App made a deployment and a status of the deployment for a commit of a
    #   pull request from a fork (seen on GitHub), and why the run did not start
    #   was not found.
    # cause: the table of the attacker's events that the rule reads does not
    #   have deployment_status.
    # attack-value: the file package.json at the head of the pull request from a fork = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: an outside app makes a deployment for the commit of
    ```
