- merged-pusher: a value that the author of a pull request writes in the profile of the account of the author (the profile name, the public email of the profile), in github.event.pull_request.merged_by of a merged pull request, or in github.event.pusher of the push that GitHub makes when GitHub merges a pull request by a rebase, by auto-merge or from a merge queue: the rule reads merged_by and the pusher as the account that merged or pushed, and the account that merged or pushed holds a credential that can merge or push; whether GitHub sets merged_by of a merged pull request, or the pusher of the push that GitHub makes when GitHub merges a pull request by a rebase, by auto-merge or from a merge queue, to the account of the author of the merged pull request was not checked
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout.executed, untrusted-checkout.checkout
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: merged-pusher.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on a pull request that is closed, actions/checkout checks out
    #   the ref that the name of the account that merged the pull request names,
    #   and make runs.
    # reason: whether GitHub sets merged_by of a merged pull request to the
    #   account of the author of the pull request was not checked: no payload with
    #   merged_by was seen on GitHub. Were merged_by the author, the author would
    #   write the name of merged_by, which is the profile name of the account of
    #   the author.
    # cause: the table of what an attacker controls reads merged_by as the
    #   account that merged the pull request, and the account that merged the pull
    #   request holds a credential that can merge.
    # attack: the author of a pull request sets the profile name of the account
    #   of the author to refs/pull/<number>/head, the ref of the head of the pull
    #   request, and the pull request is merged.
    # attack-run-behavior: were merged_by the author of the pull request, the
    #   checkout would fetch the head of the pull request, and make would run the
    #   Makefile of the pull request with the token of the run.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [closed]
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.merged_by.name }}
          - run: make
    ```
- npm-abbreviation: a command that runs npm followed by an abbreviation of the name of an npm command that runs code of the checked out tree (for example, npm tes for npm test), in a run step or in a permission of an agent. npm runs a word as an npm command when the word is the beginning of exactly one command name or alias name of the npm release that the job uses. The rule does not read abbreviations of npm command names.
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout.executed
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: npm-abbreviation.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a job checks out the head of the pull
    #   request and runs npm tes.
    # reason: a limitation (run time): npm reads tes as the npm command test,
    #   because tes is the beginning of no other command name or alias name of
    #   the npm release that the job uses, and npm test runs the script test of
    #   the package.json of the pull request; which names the npm release has is known when
    #   the job runs.
    # cause: the rule does not read abbreviations of npm command names, so the
    #   rule reads npm tes as a step that runs no code of the tree and reports
    #   untrusted-checkout.checkout, not untrusted-checkout.executed.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"test\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: npm tes runs the script test of the pull request,
    #   which prints PWNED, in the job that has the base repository's token and
    #   secrets.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
              allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
          - run: npm tes
    ```
- npm-option-value-command: a command that runs npm with an option placed before the npm command, when the value of the option is the name of an npm command and the npm command runs code of the checked out tree (for example, npm --cache view ci, in which view is the name of a directory), in a run step or in a permission of an agent. The rule reads the first word after npm, other than the value of the option --prefix or -C, that is the name or the alias name of an npm command as the npm command, and so reads the value view as the npm command.
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout.executed
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: npm-option-value-command.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a job checks out the head of the pull
    #   request and runs npm --cache view ci.
    # reason: a limitation (run time): npm reads view as the value of the
    #   option --cache, which takes a value, and runs npm ci, which runs the
    #   script preinstall of the package.json of the pull request; which options take
    #   a value is in the definitions of the npm release that the job uses,
    #   which is known when the job runs.
    # cause: the rule reads the first word after npm that is the name of an
    #   npm command as the npm command, so the rule reads npm --cache view ci as
    #   npm view, a step that runs no code of the tree, and reports untrusted-checkout.checkout, not
    #   untrusted-checkout.executed.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: npm --cache view ci runs the script preinstall,
    #   which prints PWNED, in the job that has the base repository's token and
    #   secrets.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
              allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
          - run: npm --cache view ci
    ```
- approved: a job a person approves (a job that runs only on pull_request_target with the activity type labeled, when no workflow of the same repository adds the label with actions/labeler to the pull request of an attacker, or a job with an environment that has required reviewers): this rule does not report the checkout of such a job, and untrusted-checkout-toctou reports the checkout
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout.executed, untrusted-checkout.checkout
  - disposition: other-rule (rule: untrusted-checkout-toctou)
  - added attackers: triage-account, writer-pull-requests-token, app-installation-token
  - example: approved.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target labeled, refs/pull/<n>/head is checked
    #   out, and npm ci runs.
    # reason: another rule's: a label approves the run;
    #   untrusted-checkout-toctou reads it.
    # cause: the rule leaves out a job a label approves.
    # attack: after a maintainer reads the pull request and adds a label, its
    #   author pushes a commit whose package.json has a preinstall that prints
    #   PWNED, before the job's checkout fetches.
    # attack-run-behavior: the labeled run checks out refs/pull/<n>/head, which
    #   then names the pushed commit, and npm ci runs its preinstall, with the
    #   base repository's GITHUB_TOKEN in .git/config and its secrets.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: refs/pull/${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}/head
          - run: npm ci
    ```
- insider-association: an if that lets in MEMBER or COLLABORATOR by the author_association of the issue, the pull request or the discussion the run is of, which the following pass: a member or a collaborator whose repository role is Read only, who gets, in the run, a token that writes and the secrets, more than what the Read role gives; the account of such a member or collaborator, taken over; and an outsider who becomes a MEMBER with the Read role, in an organization that lets anyone become a member (a bot that invites whoever asks). A member or a collaborator whose role is Triage or above holds a credential that can add a label or write to the repository, which the credential premise assumes no attacker holds. Who is a member, and with what role, is not in the workflow
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout.executed, untrusted-checkout.checkout
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - added attackers: read-member, triage-account, required-reviewer
  - example: insider-association.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a job whose if lets in MEMBER or
    #   COLLABORATOR checks out the pull request's head SHA with
    #   allow-unsafe-pr-checkout, and npm ci runs.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): a member of the organization, who may have read
    #   access only, passes this if (in an organization that lets anyone become a
    #   member, such as by a bot that invites whoever asks, an outsider becomes such
    #   a member), and gets the job's token and secrets past what the Read role
    #   gives; who is a member, and with what role, is not in the workflow.
    # cause: the rule evaluates the if with the attacker's author_association
    #   (NONE, FIRST_TIMER, FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR or CONTRIBUTOR), for which it
    #   is false, so no attacker's event runs the job.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: for a pull request whose author is a MEMBER or
    #   COLLABORATOR, the if is true, the checkout fetches head.sha, and npm ci
    #   runs the preinstall with the base repository's GITHUB_TOKEN in
    #   .git/config and its secrets; for an author with NONE, FIRST_TIMER,
    #   FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR or CONTRIBUTOR the job is skipped.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      a:
        if: contains(fromJSON('["MEMBER", "COLLABORATOR"]'), github.event.pull_request.author_association)
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
              allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
          - run: npm ci
    ```
- dispatch-input-call: an input of workflow_dispatch that a caller of the same repository passes, as an input of the call (under the key with: of the calling job or step), to a reusable workflow or a composite action, which uses the input as a value: the one who dispatches the caller chooses the value, and the rule reads the events of a called workflow or action from the table of the callers, and does not follow the value of an input of workflow_dispatch that the caller gives
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout.executed, untrusted-checkout.checkout
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - example: .github/workflows/called.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: caller.yml runs on workflow_dispatch with the input x, and
    #   calls called.yml with the input x of the dispatch as the input x of
    #   called.yml; called.yml checks out the ref that the input x names, and runs
    #   npm ci.
    # reason: the one who dispatches caller.yml chooses the value:
    #   input-dispatch reports such a value where a workflow on workflow_dispatch
    #   refers to its input directly, but through the call the value is the input
    #   x of called.yml.
    # cause: the rule reads the events of a called workflow from the table of
    #   the callers, and does not follow the value of an input of
    #   workflow_dispatch that a caller gives in with.
    # attack-value: inputs.x = "refs/pull/1/head"
    # attack-run-behavior: when the one who dispatches caller.yml gives the
    #   value as x, when the pull request 1 is from a fork whose package.json has
    #   the preinstall script echo PWNED, the checkout fetches the head of the
    #   fork's pull request, and npm ci runs the preinstall script, which prints
    #   PWNED, with the secrets of the repository.
    on:
      workflow_call:
        inputs:
          x: {type: string}
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ inputs.x }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
    - .github/workflows/caller.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on:
        workflow_dispatch:
          inputs:
            x: {type: string}
      jobs:
        call:
          uses: ./.github/workflows/called.yml
          with:
            x: ${{ inputs.x }}
          secrets: inherit
      ```
- dispatch-derived: a value that an env or the output of a step makes from an input of workflow_dispatch, in a job that runs only on workflow_dispatch (env: REF: refs/pull/\${{ inputs.pr }}/head; the output of gh pr view with the input pr), used as the ref of a checkout, the run that a download takes (the input run-id of actions/download-artifact), the key or the path of the cache, or a prompt: the one who dispatches the workflow chooses the value too, and the rule reports only an input of workflow_dispatch that the value refers to directly (input-dispatch)
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout.executed, untrusted-checkout.checkout
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: dispatch-derived.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on workflow_dispatch with the input pr, the env REF of the job
    #   is refs/pull/<the input pr>/head, the checkout takes the ref env.REF, and
    #   npm ci runs.
    # reason: the one who dispatches the workflow chooses the input, and the env
    #   or the output of a step makes the value from the input, so the one who
    #   dispatches the workflow chooses the value too.
    # cause: the rule reports an input of workflow_dispatch that a value refers
    #   to directly (input-dispatch), and does not follow a value that an env or
    #   the output of a step makes from the input in a job that runs only on
    #   workflow_dispatch.
    # attack-value: inputs.pr = "1"
    # attack-run-behavior: when the one who dispatches the workflow gives the
    #   value, when the pull request 1 is from a fork whose package.json has the
    #   preinstall script echo PWNED, the checkout fetches the head of the fork's
    #   pull request, and npm ci runs the preinstall script, which prints PWNED,
    #   with the secrets of the repository.
    on:
      workflow_dispatch:
        inputs:
          pr: {type: string}
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        env:
          REF: refs/pull/${{ inputs.pr }}/head
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ env.REF }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
- converted-issue: refs/pull/&lt;the issue's number> on issue_comment pinned or unpinned, which the rule reads as naming no pull request, as GitHub pins no comment of one: an issue made a pull request after its comment was pinned (the issue of POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls) may have the attacker's head there; who may make one, and whether the pin and the unpin events then come, is not seen
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout.executed, untrusted-checkout.checkout
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: converted-issue.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issue_comment unpinned, the checkout fetches
    #   refs/pull/<the issue's number>/head, and npm ci runs in it with a
    #   secret.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): if the author of an issue may make it a pull
    #   request from their fork after a comment on it was pinned, the unpin
    #   comes on a pull request whose head is theirs.
    # cause: the rule reads the issue's number on pinned and unpinned as naming
    #   no pull request, as GitHub pins no comment of one.
    # attack: an outsider opens an issue a maintainer pins a comment on, makes
    #   the issue a pull request from their fork, and waits for the unpin.
    # attack-run-behavior: refs/pull/<number>/head is the fork's head, and npm
    #   ci runs its package.json with TOKEN in the environment.
    on: {issue_comment: {types: [unpinned]}}
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: refs/pull/${{ github.event.issue.number }}/head
          - run: npm ci
            env:
              TOKEN: ${{ secrets.TOKEN }}
    ```
- remote-callee: a job or a step inside a reusable workflow of another repository (uses: owner/repo/.github/workflows/&lt;file>@&lt;ref>) whose content the fact workflow.definition does not give. For every rule: a run that does not ask the fact (a run without --online and without the answer in --facts). For a quality rule, also: a run where the linter asked the fact and got no answer (an answer of unknown: the GitHub API did not give the file), and a call deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact. The rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition. For a rule that is not a quality rule (a rule with a threat), the last two forms are the inconclusive kind remote-callee-unknown, not this form
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout.executed, untrusted-checkout.checkout
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-callee.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
    #   the repository example-org/untrusted-checkout-unanswered, whose content
    #   is the workflow of the true positive executed
    #   (executed.composer-test.yml) of the rule, with on: workflow_call in
    #   place of the on of executed.composer-test.yml. The linter has no answer
    #   of the fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event
    #   that started the run of the calling job, and the linter does not read
    #   the reusable workflow.
    # cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from
    #   the answer of workflow.definition.
    # attack-value: the file composer.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"test\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: the checkout fetches head.sha, the fork's commit, and
    #   composer test runs the script test of its composer.json, which prints
    #   PWNED, with the base repository's GITHUB_TOKEN, which the checkout left
    #   in .git/config, and its secrets.
    on: pull_request_target
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/untrusted-checkout-unanswered/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```
- combined-credentials: a job that runs only when a label is added to a pull request (pull_request_target with the activity type labeled), whose if needs both a label and the author_association MEMBER or COLLABORATOR of the author of the pull request, in a run of the linter that adds read-member and writer-pull-requests-token or app-installation-token, and does not add triage-account: one attacker who holds both credentials opens the pull request from the account with the read role and adds the label with the token, and the job runs for the pull request of the attacker in the same way that the job runs for a pull request after a person who can add labels adds the label to approve the pull request. The linter runs the rules once for each added attacker alone and reads each added attacker as a separate attacker, so no run lets one attacker past both the if of author_association and the approval by the label. A run that adds triage-account reports the job, as an account with the triage role both has the author_association MEMBER or COLLABORATOR and adds a label
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout.executed, untrusted-checkout.checkout
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - added attackers: triage-account
  - example: combined-credentials.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target with the activity type labeled, a job
    #   whose if needs the label safe-to-test and the author_association MEMBER
    #   of the author of the pull request checks out the head of the pull
    #   request with allow-unsafe-pr-checkout, and runs make test.
    # reason: a todo (more analysis by the linter): one attacker who holds
    #   both an account with the read role and a token of a writer with the
    #   Pull requests permission (the added attackers read-member and
    #   writer-pull-requests-token) opens the pull request from the account,
    #   whose author_association is MEMBER, and adds the label with the token,
    #   and the job runs the code of the pull request.
    # cause: the linter runs the rules once for each added attacker alone, and
    #   reads each added attacker as a separate attacker: the run that adds
    #   read-member does not let the attacker add a label, and the run that
    #   adds writer-pull-requests-token reads the author of the pull request
    #   as an outsider. A run that adds triage-account reports the job, as an
    #   account with the triage role both has the author_association MEMBER
    #   and adds a label.
    # attack-value: the file Makefile in the head of the pull request = "test:\n\techo PWNED\n"
    # attack-run-behavior: the member account opens a pull request from a fork,
    #   the token adds the label safe-to-test, the if is true, the checkout
    #   fetches head.sha, and make runs the target test of the pull request
    #   with the token and the secrets of the base repository.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    jobs:
      test:
        if: contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'safe-to-test') && github.event.pull_request.author_association == 'MEMBER'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
              allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
          - run: make test
    ```

### inconclusive

- checkout-with-dynamic: a checkout whose with is a whole \${{ }}: its ref and repository are not known
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: checkout-with-dynamic.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, the with of the checkout is a whole ${{
    #   }}, and npm ci runs after it.
    # reason: with is a whole ${{ }}, so the ref and the repository of the
    #   checkout are not known.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: when vars.CHECKOUT gives a ref of the pull request's
    #   code (refs/pull/<n>/head, say) and allow-unsafe-pr-checkout, the
    #   checkout fetches the pull request's head, and npm ci runs its
    #   preinstall, which prints PWNED, with the base repository's GITHUB_TOKEN
    #   in .git/config and its secrets.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with: ${{ fromJSON(vars.CHECKOUT) }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
- checkout-ref-unknown: a checkout whose ref or repository has what a step or a job computes, an input other than one of workflow_dispatch (or an input of workflow_dispatch in a workflow that also has workflow_call, when a workflow on an event of a pull request calls the workflow), an env, a matrix or a variable: whether it names a pull request's code is not analyzed
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: checkout-ref-unknown.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, the checkout takes its ref from the
    #   output of a step, as in the first step of the tj-actions incident
    #   (spotbugs/sonar-findbugs e240bc1aca68337b2b40e100fb24552d27eeb8cc,
    #   .github/workflows/sonarqube.yml:37-45: haya14busa/action-cond gives
    #   refs/pull/<n>/merge, and the checkout reads steps.condval.outputs.value;
    #   ./mvnw runs after it).
    # reason: the ref is what a step computes, so whether it names the code of a
    #   pull request is not analyzed.
    # attack-value: the file mvnw in the pull request's merge commit = "#!/bin/sh\necho PWNED\n"
    # attack-run-behavior: on pull_request_target, haya14busa/action-cond gives
    #   refs/pull/<n>/merge as steps.condval.outputs.value; when the ref is
    #   that, the checkout fetches the merge commit with the pull request's
    #   mvnw, and ./mvnw verify runs it, which prints PWNED, with the job's
    #   GITHUB_TOKEN in .git/config and its secrets.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        branches: [master]
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: haya14busa/action-cond@v1
            id: condval
            with:
              cond: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request_target' }}
              if_true: refs/pull/${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}/merge
              if_false: ''
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ steps.condval.outputs.value }}
          - run: ./mvnw verify
    ```
  - example: checkout-ref-unknown.ghsl-2024-150.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on workflow_run, the job changes runs the composite action
    #   gradio-app/gradio/.github/actions/changes, which writes the merge commit
    #   of the pull request of the run to its output merge_sha, and the job
    #   test-hygiene checks out needs.changes.outputs.merge_sha and runs a
    #   script of the checkout. This is test-hygiene.yml of gradio-app/gradio
    #   (commit edcd5748f6c0faf2028a8e6a330aad5eccf103d5, line 41); what the
    #   advisory calls a reusable workflow is a composite action.
    # reason: the ref of the checkout is an output of a job, which the rule does
    #   not follow to the composite action that writes the output.
    # attack: the author of a pull request writes scripts/generate_notebooks.py
    #   in the pull request.
    # attack-run-behavior: the job test-hygiene checks out the merge commit of
    #   the pull request and runs python scripts/generate_notebooks.py of the
    #   author.
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-150_GHSL-2024-157_Gradio/
    on:
      workflow_run:
        workflows: [trigger]
        types: [requested]
    jobs:
      changes:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        outputs:
          merge_sha: ${{ steps.changes.outputs.merge_sha }}
        steps:
          - uses: gradio-app/gradio/.github/actions/changes@main
            id: changes
      test-hygiene:
        needs: changes
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ needs.changes.outputs.merge_sha }}
          - run: pip install nbformat && python scripts/generate_notebooks.py
    ```
  - example: checkout-ref-unknown.ghsl-2024-168.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, actions/checkout v4.1.6 checks out the ref
    #   ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request_target' &&
    #   format('refs/pull/{0}/merge', github.event.number) || '' }}, the merge
    #   commit of the pull request on that event, and later steps run the local
    #   action ./.github/workflows/actions/get-core-dependencies and npm run build
    #   of the checkout. This is pack-and-comment.yml of ionic-team/stencil (commit
    #   8a7d89a4d9b506673e7a73fea9f0ba04964727a2, lines 1-28); the comments and the
    #   steps after line 28 are left out. tech-debt-burndown.yml of the same commit
    #   checks out the same ref in three jobs.
    # reason: the rule does not evaluate the expression of the ref with the event
    #   of the run, so it does not know that the ref is refs/pull/<number>/merge
    #   on pull_request_target, the code that the author of the pull request
    #   writes.
    # cause: the rule reads a ref with an expression other than a value of the
    #   context as not known.
    # attack: the author of a pull request from a fork changes the action.yml of
    #   ./.github/workflows/actions/get-core-dependencies or package.json and opens
    #   the pull request.
    # attack-run-behavior: the checkout takes the merge commit with the author's
    #   files (v4.1.6 does not refuse the code of a fork), and the step Get Core
    #   Dependencies runs the author's action with the token of the job of the base
    #   repository.
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-168_Stencil/
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        branches:
          - '**'
    jobs:
      pack:
        name: Pack and Comment
        runs-on: 'ubuntu-22.04'
        steps:
          - name: Checkout Code
            uses: actions/checkout@a5ac7e51b41094c92402da3b24376905380afc29 # v4.1.6
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request_target' && format('refs/pull/{0}/merge', github.event.number) || '' }}
              persist-credentials: false
          - name: Get Core Dependencies
            uses: ./.github/workflows/actions/get-core-dependencies
          - name: Core Build
            run: npm run build -- --ci
            shell: bash
    ```
  - example: checkout-ref-unknown.ghsl-2024-208.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issue_comment, a step uses actions/github-script to get the
    #   pull request of the comment from the API and returns pr.data, a step
    #   writes fromJSON of that output's head.sha to its output sha, and
    #   actions/checkout checks out that sha; a later step runs
    #   ./scripts/build_docker.py of the checkout, and a step after it gives the
    #   AWS secrets to aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials. This is the job
    #   ephemeral-docker-build of ephemeral-env.yml of apache/superset (commit
    #   c5594f29792c7f83fde9320097b8a0e6323417e5, lines 1-5 and 85-135). The jobs
    #   before it, whose gate the advisory bypasses with a comment that is not
    #   /testenv, the concurrency, the steps for QEMU and Buildx and the
    #   arguments of build_docker.py are left out. push-chart-ci.yaml of
    #   cilium/cilium (commit 736337ca18ae7f23541567a4452cdd362d035817,
    #   GHSL-2024-226_GHSL-2024-227) has the same form on workflow_run: a run step
    #   writes github.event.workflow_run.head_sha to its output ref when the head
    #   repository is a fork, and actions/checkout checks out that output (line
    #   86).
    #   autorelease-preview.yml of excalidraw/excalidraw (commit
    #   148b895f462e02e2b18649caf57abc0416fd6d4a, GHSL-2024-158) has the form of
    #   Superset on a comment @excalibot trigger release: actions/github-script
    #   returns the head sha of the pull request, and actions/checkout checks out
    #   that output (line 31).
    #   zwave-js-bot.yml of zwave-js/zwavejs2mqtt (commit
    #   e758e76c3a7015d9a8cbb901e344dfba00a25d82, GHSL-2021-047) has the form of
    #   Superset on a comment @zwave-js-bot fix lint: actions/github-script
    #   returns the pull request, actions/checkout checks out fromJSON of that
    #   output's head.ref (line 66), and a later step runs npm install.
    # reason: steps.get-sha.outputs.sha is the head commit of the pull request,
    #   which the author of the pull request writes; the rule does not follow the
    #   output of a step back to what the script of actions/github-script
    #   returns.
    # cause: the rule does not read what actions/github-script returns.
    # attack: the author of a pull request from a fork changes
    #   scripts/build_docker.py in the head commit and comments on the pull
    #   request.
    # attack-run-behavior: actions/checkout checks out the head commit (the
    #   refusal of actions/checkout covers pull_request_target and workflow_run,
    #   not issue_comment), and the step Build ephemeral env image runs the
    #   author's script; the AWS secrets come to the job in a later step.
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-208_Apache_Superset/
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-226_GHSL-2024-227_Cilium/
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-158_Excalidraw/
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2021-047-zwave-js-zwavejs2mqtt-workflows/
    on:
      issue_comment:
        types: [created]
    jobs:
      ephemeral-docker-build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
        steps:
          - name: Get Info from comment
            uses: actions/github-script@v7
            id: get-pr-info
            with:
              script: |
                const request = {
                    owner: context.repo.owner,
                    repo: context.repo.repo,
                    pull_number: ${{ github.event.issue.number }},
                }
                const pr = await github.rest.pulls.get(request);
                return pr.data;
          - name: Debug
            id: get-sha
            run: |
              echo "sha=${{ fromJSON(steps.get-pr-info.outputs.result).head.sha }}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ steps.get-sha.outputs.sha }}
              persist-credentials: false
          - name: Build ephemeral env image
            run: ./scripts/build_docker.py "ci" "pull_request"
          - uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
            with:
              aws-access-key-id: ${{ secrets.AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID }}
              aws-secret-access-key: ${{ secrets.AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }}
    ```

    ```yaml
    #   5166fc7a513634316408e9b29f68fd584e1524c0, GHSL-2024-171) has the same form
    #   with alessbell/pull-request-comment-branch v2.1.0 on a comment /sipify,
    #   and runs ./scripts/sipify_all.sh of the checkout. bloat.yml of
    #   linebender/druid (commit 1c0d227bba9c56221b255071d95396915bee1172,
    #   GHSL-2021-048, and the same file of linebender/norad and
    #   linebender/runebender) has the same form with cmyr/bloat-cmp/get-revs on a
    #   comment /bloat: actions/checkout checks out the output head of the action
    #   (line 58), and actions-rs/cargo builds the checkout.
    # reason: the outputs head_owner, head_repo and head_ref of the action name
    #   the head of the pull request, which the author of the pull request
    #   writes; the rule does not know what an output of an action of another
    #   repository holds.
    # cause: the rule does not yet ask for the action.yml of another repository
    #   as a fact.
    # attack: the author of a pull request from a fork writes
    #   .github/actions/setup/action.yml in the head commit and comments
    #   /update-vrt on the pull request; the if of the job reads only the body
    #   of the comment.

    #   branch, actions/checkout checks out the head branch (the refusal of
    #   actions/checkout covers pull_request_target and workflow_run, not

    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-171_QGIS/
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2021-048-linebender-druid-workflows/

      issue_comment:
        types: [created]
    permissions:
      pull-requests: write
      contents: write
    jobs:
      update-vrt:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        if: |
          github.event.issue.pull_request &&
          contains(github.event.comment.body, '/update-vrt')
        steps:
          - name: Get PR branch
            uses: gotson/pull-request-comment-branch@head-repo-owner-dist
            id: comment-branch
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              repository: ${{ steps.comment-branch.outputs.head_owner }}/${{ steps.comment-branch.outputs.head_repo }}
              ref: ${{ steps.comment-branch.outputs.head_ref }}
          - name: Set up environment
            uses: ./.github/actions/setup
    ```

    ```yaml
    # situation: on issue_comment, when the comment is /benchmarks, a run step
    #   writes the name of the head branch of the pull request (gh pr view --json
    #   headRefName) to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, actions/checkout@v4 checks out that name
    #   with the input repository not set, and a later step uses the local action
    #   ./.github/actions/setup-nx. This is performance.yml of ag-grid/ag-grid
    #   (commit 7d969b0a0374d1e0ce690ae1159ceb7b6091f325, the commit of the
    #   advisory's links; performance.yml at that commit is the same blob as at
    #   6b5582325b9eb843e2d566aff8b530eaee5996ad; lines 3-5, 43-52, 72-95 and
    #   115-119). The triggers workflow_dispatch and schedule, the env of the
    #   workflow except PR_ID, the step Notify start and the test of its output in
    #   the script (lines 56-70 and 80), the two echo lines of the script (lines
    #   78-79), the branches of the script for the other events (lines 83-89), and
    #   the steps between the step Checkout and the step Setup and after the step
    #   Setup are left out; the if of the job keeps only its part for issue_comment,
    #   and PR_ID keeps only github.event.issue.number.
    # reason: the rule does not read what the run step writes to the output, so
    #   the ref is not known. The advisory says that the code of the pull request
    #   runs; the source of actions/checkout does not fetch the code of a pull
    #   request from a fork in this form. With the input repository not set,
    #   actions/checkout fetches from the repository of the run (src/input-helper.ts
    #   of v4.4.0, 11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262, lines 22-24), and for a
    #   ref that is not a SHA and does not start with refs/, actions/checkout
    #   fetches only +refs/heads/<ref>* and +refs/tags/<ref>* (src/ref-helper.ts,
    #   lines 106-111). The base repository has no branch of a fork: the base
    #   repository has refs/pull/<number>/head and refs/pull/<number>/merge only
    #   (GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/matching-refs on 2026-11-07). A run of the
    #   same form on 2026-11-07 (actions/checkout@v4 resolved to 11d5960a) showed
    #   two results: for a pull request from a fork whose branch name the base
    #   repository does not have, the fetch failed (git exited with code 1) and the
    #   later step found no file of the fork; for a pull request from a fork whose
    #   branch has the name of a branch of the base repository, the checkout took
    #   the branch of the base repository, not the commit of the fork. Two kinds of
    #   names would reach the code of the fork, as actions/checkout takes a ref that
    #   starts with refs/ as a full name of a ref and a ref of 40 hexadecimal digits
    #   as a commit, but GitHub refused a push of a branch named refs/pull/32/head
    #   ("Invalid branch or tag name") and of a branch named by the 40 hexadecimal
    #   digits of a commit ("branch or tag names consisting of 40 or 64 hex
    #   characters are not allowed"), on 2026-11-07. gh pr view --json headRefName
    #   gives the name of the branch without its owner (cli/cli v2.76.1,
    #   api/queries_pr.go line 37). So the checkout brings the code of a branch of
    #   the base repository, to which only an account with write access to the
    #   repository can push; if the rule read what the run step writes, the form
    #   would be the one of the declaration branch-name-ref (a checkout of a name of
    #   a branch, which brings no code of a fork). The timeline of the advisory says
    #   how ag-grid fixed the workflow, by approval of the runs of pull requests
    #   from forks: "2025-08-05: Issue fixed by requiring approval for external
    #   forked PR"; in the form of this example, a pull request from a fork brings
    #   no code, and a pull request from a branch of the base repository brings the
    #   code of the branch.
    # attack: the author of a pull request from a fork writes
    #   .github/actions/setup-nx/action.yml in the head branch and comments
    #   /benchmarks on the pull request.
    # attack-run-behavior: gh pr view gives the name of the head branch, which is
    #   in the fork; actions/checkout fetches +refs/heads/<name>* and
    #   +refs/tags/<name>* from the base repository, which has no ref of the name,
    #   and the fetch fails (git exits with code 1), so the step Setup does not run
    #   the action.yml of the author.
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2025-082_ag-grid_ag-grid/
    on:
      issue_comment:
        types: [created]
    env:
      PR_ID: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
    permissions:
      contents: read
    jobs:
      benchmark:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions:
          pull-requests: write
          issues: write
        if: github.event_name == 'issue_comment' && github.event.comment.body == '/benchmarks'
        steps:
          - name: Assign correct Branch name
            id: get-branch
            env:
              REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
              GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
            run: |
              echo "branch=$(gh pr view $PR_ID --repo $REPO --json headRefName --jq '.headRefName')" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          - name: Checkout
            uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              fetch-depth: 1
              ref: ${{ steps.get-branch.outputs.branch }}
          - name: Setup
            id: setup
            uses: ./.github/actions/setup-nx
            with:
              cache_mode: rw
    ```

      ```yaml
      on: pull_request_target
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        label:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/labeler@v5
              with:
                repo-token: ${{ secrets.LABELER_PAT }}
                configuration-path: ${{ vars.LABELER_CONFIG }}
      ```
  - example: .github/workflows/labeled.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: labeler.yml runs actions/labeler on pull_request_target with a
    #   personal access token, with the if failure(), after a step that writes
    #   the title of the pull request into its script; labeled.yml runs on
    #   pull_request_target on labeled when the label is safe-to-test, and the
    #   job checks out the head of the pull request and runs npm ci.
    # reason: actions/labeler runs only after a step before actions/labeler
    #   fails, and the linter does not know whether the attacker can make the
    #   step before actions/labeler fail.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: when the attacker can make the step before
    #   actions/labeler fail, the attacker opens a pull request from a fork
    #   that changes a file under site/ and the files of the attack, and makes
    #   the step before actions/labeler fail; actions/labeler adds the label
    #   safe-to-test, which starts labeled.yml, and the checkout fetches the
    #   head of the pull request, and npm ci runs the preinstall script of the
    #   pull request, which prints PWNED, with the secrets of the repository.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    jobs:
      build:
        if: github.event.label.name == 'safe-to-test'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
    - .github/labeler.yml (repo-file)
      ```yaml
      safe-to-test:
        - changed-files:
            - any-glob-to-any-file: 'site/**'
      ```
    - .github/workflows/labeler.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: pull_request_target
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        label:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: echo "${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}"
            - uses: actions/labeler@v5
              if: failure()
              with:
                repo-token: ${{ secrets.LABELER_PAT }}
      ```
- input-dispatch: a checkout whose ref or repository has a \${{ }} that refers to an input of workflow_dispatch (inputs, github.event.inputs), alone or with other values: whoever dispatches the workflow chooses the value of the input. A credential whose only write access is to the permission Actions can dispatch the workflow, and the credential premise keeps the holder of such a credential as a possible attacker; the linter does not know whether such a credential exists or who holds it. The rule reports the value in a job with an environment that has required reviewers too, where a required reviewer of the environment can stop the run
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: dispatcher)
  - example: input-dispatch.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on workflow_dispatch, the checkout takes its ref from the input
    #   ref, and npm ci runs.
    # reason: whoever dispatches the workflow chooses the value of the input,
    #   and the workflow does not tell who that is, so whether an attacker
    #   chooses the code that the checkout brings is not known; nothing the rule
    #   could read is expected to tell it.
    # attack-value: inputs.ref = "refs/pull/1/head"
    # attack-run-behavior: when the one who dispatches the workflow gives
    #   refs/pull/1/head as the input ref, and the pull request 1 is from a fork
    #   whose package.json has the preinstall script echo PWNED, the checkout
    #   fetches the head of the fork's pull request (actions/checkout refuses
    #   the code of a fork on pull_request_target and workflow_run only), and
    #   npm ci runs the preinstall script, which prints PWNED, with the secrets
    #   of the repository and the GITHUB_TOKEN in .git/config.
    on:
      workflow_dispatch:
        inputs:
          ref: {type: string}
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ inputs.ref }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
- remote-callee-unknown: a job that calls a reusable workflow of another repository, when the linter asked the fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow and got no answer (the token that the linter uses cannot read the file, the file is larger than the limit, or the linter has used up the requests it may send to the GitHub API), or when the call is deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact: the rule does not read the jobs and the steps of the reusable workflow
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-callee-unknown.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
    #   the repository example-org/untrusted-checkout-unknown, whose content is
    #   the workflow of the true positive executed (executed.composer-test.yml)
    #   of the rule, with on: workflow_call in place of the on of
    #   executed.composer-test.yml. The linter asked the fact
    #   workflow.definition for the reusable workflow and got no answer.
    # reason: what the jobs of the reusable workflow do is in the file that the
    #   linter could not read; whoever changes the uses, such as the author of a
    #   pull request, can name a reusable workflow that the token that the
    #   linter uses cannot read.
    # attack-value: the file composer.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"test\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: the checkout fetches head.sha, the fork's commit, and
    #   composer test runs the script test of its composer.json, which prints
    #   PWNED, with the base repository's GITHUB_TOKEN, which the checkout left
    #   in .git/config, and its secrets.
    on: pull_request_target
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/untrusted-checkout-unknown/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

### false positive forms

- environment-expression: an environment whose name is a \${{ }} and has required reviewers: which environment it is is known when the job runs, so it is read as approving nothing
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout.executed, untrusted-checkout.checkout
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: environment-expression.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the job on pull_request_target checks out the pull request's
    #   head and runs npm ci, in an environment that a ${{ }} picks.
    # reason: both environments have required reviewers, who approve the job
    #   before it runs.
    # cause: which environment the job takes is known when it runs, so it is
    #   read as approving nothing.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: the job waits until a required reviewer of production
    #   or staging, whichever the expression gives, approves it; a reviewer who
    #   reads the pull request's package.json does not approve, and the checkout
    #   and npm ci do not run. An approval followed by a push is
    #   untrusted-checkout-toctou's.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        environment: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref == 'main' && 'production' || 'staging' }}
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
              allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
          - run: npm ci
    ```
- not-executed: a job that uses nothing of the tree it checks out as code or as the settings of a tool, and has no tool that follows a symlink of the tree to a file outside the checkout and puts the content of the file outside the checkout in the log or in an upload that the attacker can read (a job that reads a file of the tree as data is this form, except in the two cases below): no step runs a script, a build, a test or an action of the tree, no tool reads a file of the tree as settings that decide where a request goes or what command runs, and no tool follows a symlink of the tree to a file outside the checkout and puts the content of the file outside the checkout in the log or in an upload that the attacker can read, such as an artifact. A job whose tool reads settings that decide where a request goes or what command runs from the tree is not this form: SonarSource's scanner reads sonar.host.url from a project file of the tree and can send a secret to the host that the pull request names. A job whose tool follows a symlink of the tree to a file outside the checkout and puts the content of the file outside the checkout in the log or in an upload that the attacker can read is not this form either: a parse error of tmatens/compose-lint quotes a line of a file of credentials outside the checkout that a symlink of a pull request names (GHSA-whr6-fgpq-fpv9, GHSA-88f4-frh5-gmcr)
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout.checkout
  - fact kinds:
    - checkout.executed (provider: user-supplied, answer that removes the finding: false)
  - example: not-executed.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the job on pull_request_target checks out the pull request's
    #   head and only counts the lines of a file of it.
    # reason: the job runs nothing of the tree it checks out, and no tool reads a
    #   file of the tree as settings.
    # cause: unless a file of facts or --fact says that no step runs the tree of
    #   the checkout (checkout.executed false), the rule reports the finding, also
    #   when no step is seen to run the tree. When no file of facts and no --fact
    #   answers checkout.executed, the finding is conditional.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: the checkout fetches head.sha into pr, with the pull
    #   request's package.json, and the job only runs wc -l pr/README.md, which
    #   counts lines; nothing reads package.json, and the preinstall does not
    #   run.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
              allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
              path: pr
          - run: wc -l pr/README.md
    ```
- remote-not-executed: a job of a reusable workflow of another repository that uses nothing of the tree it checks out in the ways that the form not-executed names: the fact checkout.executed names a step of the input and cannot name a step of a reusable workflow of another repository, so no answer of the fact removes the finding
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout.checkout
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-not-executed.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the job on pull_request_target calls the reusable workflow
    #   w.yml of the repository example-org/remote-checkout-workflow, whose job
    #   checks out the pull request's head and only counts the lines of a file
    #   of it.
    # reason: the job of the reusable workflow runs nothing of the tree it
    #   checks out, and no tool reads a file of the tree as settings.
    # cause: when no step is seen to run the tree, the rule takes it as run; the
    #   fact checkout.executed names a step of the input, and has no form for a
    #   step of a reusable workflow of another repository, so a file of facts
    #   cannot remove the finding.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: the checkout fetches head.sha into pr, with the pull
    #   request's package.json, and the job of the reusable workflow only runs
    #   wc -l pr/README.md, which counts lines; nothing reads package.json, and
    #   the preinstall does not run.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/remote-checkout-workflow/.github/workflows/w.yml@v1
    ```
- environment-protected: a job whose environment has required reviewers, who approve it before it runs
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout.executed, untrusted-checkout.checkout
  - fact kinds:
    - repo.environment-protected (provider: repo-setting, answer that removes the finding: true)
  - example: environment-protected.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the job on pull_request_target checks out the pull request's
    #   head and runs npm ci, in the environment production.
    # reason: the environment production has required reviewers, who approve the
    #   job before it runs (then it is untrusted-checkout-toctou's).
    # cause: unless a file of facts or --fact says that the environment has
    #   required reviewers (repo.environment-protected true), the rule reports the
    #   finding. When no source answers repo.environment-protected, the finding is
    #   conditional.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: the job waits until a required reviewer of production
    #   approves it; a reviewer who reads the pull request's package.json does
    #   not approve, and the checkout and npm ci do not run. An approval
    #   followed by a push is untrusted-checkout-toctou's.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        environment: production
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
              allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
          - run: npm ci
    ```
- label-name-if: a job whose if compares github.event.label.name with == to a string that is not empty, in a workflow on pull_request_target whose types have labeled and an activity type whose payload has no label, such as types: &#91;labeled, opened] (the payload of opened, synchronize and reopened has no label): on that activity type, github.event.label.name is an empty string, and the if is false, so the job runs only after a label is added; the rule does not read github.event.label.name as an empty string on that activity type, and reports the job as a job that runs on that activity type without an approval
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout.executed, untrusted-checkout.checkout
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: label-name-if.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target with types labeled and opened, the job
    #   runs only if github.event.label.name is safe to test; the job checks out
    #   the pull request's head and runs npm ci.
    # reason: the payload of opened has no label, so github.event.label.name is
    #   an empty string and the if is false on opened; the job runs only on
    #   labeled, after a maintainer adds the label safe to test (then a push
    #   after the label is untrusted-checkout-toctou's).
    # cause: the rule does not read github.event.label.name as an empty string
    #   on the other activity type, and reads the job as a job that runs on
    #   opened without an approval.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: the run on opened skips the job; npm ci runs only
    #   after a maintainer adds the label safe to test to the pull request.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled, opened]
    jobs:
      build:
        if: github.event.label.name == 'safe to test'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
              allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
          - run: npm ci
    ```
- npm-unknown-command: a command that runs npm with a word that is not an option and is not the name, an alias name, or the beginning of exactly one name of an npm command, before the name of an npm command that runs code of the checked out tree (for example, npm web ci), in a run step or in a permission of an agent. npm stops with an error at the first word that is not an option when the word is not the name of an npm command, and runs no code of the tree. The rule reads the first word after npm, other than the value of the option --prefix or -C, that is the name or the alias name of an npm command as the npm command.
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout.executed
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: npm-unknown-command.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a job checks out the head of the pull
    #   request and runs npm web ci.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): npm stops with an error at web, the
    #   first word that is not an option, because web is not the name, an alias
    #   name or the beginning of exactly one name of an npm command, and npm
    #   runs no code of the pull request.
    # cause: the rule reads the first word after npm that is the name of an
    #   npm command, ci, as the npm command, so the rule reports untrusted-checkout.executed.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: npm web ci stops with the error Unknown command and
    #   does not run the script preinstall, so PWNED is not printed.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
              allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
          - run: npm web ci
    ```
- npm-option-value-operand: a command that runs npm version, npm uninstall, npm explore or npm edit with no operand, but with an option whose value the rule reads as an operand (for example, npm version --preid beta), in a run step or in a permission of an agent. In that case, npm runs no code of the checked out tree. The rule reads every word after the npm command that is not an option, other than the value of the option --prefix or -C, as an operand.
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout.executed
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: npm-option-value-operand.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a job checks out the head of the pull
    #   request and runs npm version --preid beta.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): npm version with no operand prints the
    #   version of the package.json and runs no script of the pull request; beta is the
    #   value of the option --preid.
    # cause: the rule reads beta as an operand of npm version, so the rule
    #   reports untrusted-checkout.executed.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request = "{\"scripts\":{\"preversion\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: npm version --preid beta prints the version and does
    #   not run the script preversion, so PWNED is not printed.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
              allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
          - run: npm version --preid beta
    ```
- cd-out-of-tree: a run step with a command that changes the directory of the shell or of a tool (cd, pushd, popd, env -C, sudo -D, and in pwsh a word that is Set-Location or one of its aliases), in which a tool runs in a directory out of the checked out tree (for example, cd \${{ runner.temp }} && npm ci, after a checkout of the tree into the directory pr). The rule does not read the directory that the command changes to, and reads every tool of the step as a tool that may run in any directory.
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout.executed
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: cd-out-of-tree.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a job checks out the head of the pull
    #   request and runs cd ${{ runner.temp }} && npm ci.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the step changes its directory to runner.temp,
    #   out of the pull request, which the job puts into the directory pr, and npm ci reads
    #   the package.json of runner.temp, so npm runs no code of the pull request.
    # cause: the rule does not read the directory that a cd command changes
    #   to, and reads npm ci of a step with a cd command as a tool that may run
    #   in any directory, so the rule reports untrusted-checkout.executed.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: npm ci in runner.temp finds no package.json of the
    #   attacker and does not run the script preinstall, so PWNED is not
    #   printed.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
              allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
              path: pr
          - run: cd ${{ runner.temp }} && npm ci
    ```
- ignored-pnpmfile: a command that runs a pnpm command that runs no code of the checked out tree, with the pnpm setting ignore-pnpmfile set to true (for example, pnpm --config.ignore-pnpmfile=true store prune), in a run step or in a permission of an agent. pnpm loads no .pnpmfile.cjs of the tree when the pnpm setting ignore-pnpmfile is true. The rule reads every run of pnpm as a run that runs code of the tree.
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout.executed
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: ignored-pnpmfile.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a job checks out the head of the pull
    #   request and runs pnpm --config.ignore-pnpmfile=true store prune.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): pnpm loads no .pnpmfile.cjs of the tree
    #   when the pnpm setting ignore-pnpmfile is true, and the pnpm command
    #   store prune runs no script of the package.json, so pnpm runs no code of
    #   the pull request; the job still checks out the code of the pull request
    #   with the base repository's token, which the finding
    #   untrusted-checkout.checkout says.
    # cause: the rule reads every run of pnpm as a run that runs code of the
    #   tree, so the rule reports untrusted-checkout.executed.
    # attack-value: the file .pnpmfile.cjs in the pull request's head = "console.log('PWNED')"
    # attack-run-behavior: pnpm --config.ignore-pnpmfile=true store prune does
    #   not load the .pnpmfile.cjs of the pull request and removes packages from
    #   the store of pnpm, so PWNED is not printed.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
              allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
          - run: pnpm --config.ignore-pnpmfile=true store prune
    ```
- absolute-path-out-of-tree: a command that runs a tool in a directory, or runs a file, that a path out of the checked out tree names, when the path is an absolute path that names the directory of a tool or a file given to an interpreter, or a path that leaves the workspace by .. (for example, pnpm --dir /opt/tool install, bash /opt/x.sh, or npm --prefix ../other ci after a checkout of the tree into the directory pr), in a run step or in a permission of an agent. The rule reads an absolute path, and a path that leaves the workspace by .., as a path that may name a directory of the tree, because the workspace that holds the tree also has an absolute path, and a path that leaves the workspace by .. may come back into the workspace.
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout.executed
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: absolute-path-out-of-tree.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a job checks out the head of the pull
    #   request and runs pnpm --dir /opt/tool install.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): pnpm runs in /opt/tool, out of the pull request, and loads the
    #   .pnpmfile.cjs and the package.json of /opt/tool, so pnpm runs no code
    #   of the pull request.
    # cause: the rule reads the absolute path /opt/tool as a path that may name
    #   a directory of the tree, so the rule reports untrusted-checkout.executed.
    # attack-value: the file .pnpmfile.cjs in the pull request = "console.log('PWNED')"
    # attack-run-behavior: pnpm --dir /opt/tool install does not load the .pnpmfile.cjs
    #   of the attacker, so PWNED is not printed.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
              allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
          - run: pnpm --dir /opt/tool install
    ```
  - example: absolute-path-out-of-tree.dotdot.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a job checks out the head of the pull
    #   request into the directory pr and runs ./../other/x.sh.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): ./../other/x.sh names the file x.sh of a
    #   directory other beside the workspace, out of pr, so the step runs no
    #   code of the pull request.
    # cause: the rule reads a path that leaves the workspace by .. as a path
    #   that may come back into the workspace, so the rule reports
    #   untrusted-checkout.executed.
    # attack-value: the file other/x.sh in the pull request = "#!/bin/sh\necho PWNED\n"
    # attack-run-behavior: ./../other/x.sh runs a file out of the workspace,
    #   not pr/other/x.sh of the attacker, so PWNED is not printed.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
              allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
              path: pr
          - run: ./../other/x.sh
    ```
- pytest-path-out-of-tree: a command that runs pytest, in a directory of the checked out tree or in a directory that holds the tree, with only paths out of the tree as its arguments (for example, pytest /opt/tests run in the root of the tree, or pytest tests run in the root of the workspace when the tree is in the directory pr), in a run step or in a permission of an agent. In that case, pytest collects no test and loads no conftest.py of the tree. The rule reads the directory that pytest runs in, and every directory under it, as directories whose tests pytest collects.
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout.executed
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: pytest-path-out-of-tree.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a job checks out the head of the pull
    #   request and runs pytest /opt/tests.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): pytest collects the tests of /opt/tests only, and loads no
    ```
