## untrusted-checkout-toctou

- problem: a privileged job that a person approves checks out the code of a pull request by what its author can move, so a push after the approval runs code no one approved
- expected: a job that a person approves checks out the commit the approval saw (github.event.pull_request.head.sha)
- severity: medium
- targets: workflow, action-metadata
- facets:
  - weakness: untrusted-code-execution
  - attack-means: code, operation
- default run: always: in a run without --rule, the rule runs unless --skip-rule names the rule

### finding kinds

- untrusted-checkout-toctou.mutable-ref
  - detected: {uses} checks out {checkout_ref} on {pr_code_on} after {approval}, and {checkout_ref} can move
  - arguments:
    - {uses}: The uses of the checkout, as written.
    - {checkout_ref}: The reference that names what can move, as written: a branch's name with the fork as the repository, refs/pull/&lt;n>/head, or the fork itself.
    - {pr_code_on}: The privileged events on which the finding holds, each event named once.
    - {approval}: What makes a person approve a run before the run checks out the code of a pull request.
  - consequence: the author pushes after the approval, and the job runs code no one approved with its secrets and its token
  - remedy: check out the commit the approval saw: github.event.pull_request.head.sha
  - severity: medium (found from the CVSS metrics below by the table)
  - fix kinds: pin-head-sha, pin-head-sha-review
  - fact kinds: repo.environment-protected (provider: repo-setting), git.commit-contains (provider: github), repo.pull-request-target-allowed (provider: repo-setting)
  - attackers: fork-pr-author
  - preconditions: privileged-event, pr-tree, no-guard, approved, movable-checkout, callers-events
  - true positives:
    - mutable-ref.no-caller.action.yml (action-metadata, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a composite action with no caller among the files that the
      #   linter reads; when the event is pull_request_target labeled with the label
      #   safe, a step checks out refs/pull/<n>/head and the next step runs npm ci.
      # reason: with no caller among the files that the linter reads, the rule
      #   reads the action on every event an attacker triggers, pull_request_target
      #   labeled among the events. The label is the approval, but
      #   refs/pull/<n>/head names the head of the pull request when the checkout
      #   fetches the head, not the commit that was labelled, so a push between the
      #   label and the fetch is what npm ci runs.
      # attack: after a maintainer reads the pull request and adds the label safe,
      #   the author of the pull request pushes to the branch of the fork a commit
      #   whose package.json has a preinstall that prints PWNED, before the checkout
      #   fetches.
      # attack-run-behavior: the labeled run checks out refs/pull/<n>/head, which
      #   GitHub has moved to the pushed commit, and npm ci runs the preinstall,
      #   with the GITHUB_TOKEN of the base repository in .git/config and the
      #   secrets that the job of a workflow that calls the action gives the steps.
      name: test
      description: test the labelled pull request
      runs:
        using: composite
        steps:
          - if: github.event_name == 'pull_request_target' && github.event.action == 'labeled' && github.event.label.name == 'safe'
            uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: refs/pull/${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}/head
              allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
          - if: github.event_name == 'pull_request_target' && github.event.action == 'labeled' && github.event.label.name == 'safe'
            run: npm ci
            shell: bash
      ```
    - mutable-ref.remote-callee.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
      #   the repository example-org/untrusted-checkout-toctou-remote, which the
      #   fact workflow.definition answers with the workflow of the true positive
      #   mutable-ref (mutable-ref.yml) of the rule, with on: workflow_call in
      #   place of the on of mutable-ref.yml. The job passes its secrets with
      #   secrets: inherit. In the true positive, on pull_request_target labeled,
      #   the job checks out refs/pull/<n>/head and runs npm ci.
      # reason: the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event that started the
      #   run of the calling job, so the reason of the true positive holds: the
      #   label is the approval, but refs/pull/<n>/head names the pull request's
      #   head when the checkout fetches it, not the commit that was labelled, so
      #   a push between the label and the fetch is what npm ci runs.
      # attack: after a maintainer reads the pull request and adds a label, its
      #   author pushes to the fork's branch a commit whose package.json has a
      #   preinstall that prints PWNED, before the job's checkout fetches.
      # attack-run-behavior: the labeled run checks out refs/pull/<n>/head, which
      #   GitHub has moved to the pushed commit, and npm ci runs its preinstall,
      #   with the base repository's GITHUB_TOKEN in .git/config and its secrets.
      on:
        pull_request_target:
          types: [labeled]
      jobs:
        c:
          uses: example-org/untrusted-checkout-toctou-remote/.github/workflows/w.yml@v1
          secrets: inherit
      ```
    - mutable-ref.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on pull_request_target labeled, the job checks out
      #   refs/pull/<n>/head and runs npm ci.
      # reason: the label is the approval, but refs/pull/<n>/head names the pull
      #   request's head when the checkout fetches it, not the commit that was
      #   labelled, so a push between the label and the fetch is what npm ci runs.
      # attack: after a maintainer reads the pull request and adds a label, its
      #   author pushes to the fork's branch a commit whose package.json has a
      #   preinstall that prints PWNED, before the job's checkout fetches.
      # attack-run-behavior: the labeled run checks out refs/pull/<n>/head, which
      #   GitHub has moved to the pushed commit, and npm ci runs its preinstall,
      #   with the base repository's GITHUB_TOKEN in .git/config and its secrets.
      on:
        pull_request_target:
          types: [labeled]
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
              with:
                ref: refs/pull/${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}/head
                allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
            - run: npm ci
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - mutable-ref.app-commit.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on check_suite, the job waits for the approval of the
      #   environment release, then checks out the commit of the check suite
      #   (github.event.check_suite.head_sha) and runs npm ci.
      # reason: the payload of check_suite names the commit by its SHA, which a
      #   push after the approval cannot move, so the checkout brings the commit
      #   that the reviewer of the environment saw.
      # attack: after a reviewer of the environment approves the run, the author
      #   of the pull request from a fork pushes to the branch of the pull request
      #   a commit whose package.json has a preinstall that prints PWNED.
      # attack-run-behavior: the checkout fetches the SHA of the payload, the
      #   commit before the push, so the pushed preinstall does not run.
      on:
        check_suite:
          types: [completed]
      jobs:
        j:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          environment: release
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
              with:
                ref: ${{ github.event.check_suite.head_sha }}
            - run: npm ci
      ```
    - mutable-ref.approval-if.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on pull_request_target labeled, the job checks out
      #   refs/pull/<n>/head and runs npm ci, only if the pull request's head
      #   repository is this repository.
      # reason: the if skips a pull request from a fork, whose head repository is
      #   the fork, so the head branch is in this repository, and only those who
      #   may push to it can move refs/pull/<n>/head after the label.
      # attack: after a maintainer reads the pull request and adds a label, its
      #   author pushes to the fork's branch a commit whose package.json has a
      #   preinstall that prints PWNED, before the job's checkout fetches.
      # attack-run-behavior: for the fork's pull request, head.repo.full_name is
      #   the fork, not github.repository, so the if is false and the job is
      #   skipped: nothing is checked out, and the pushed preinstall does not run.
      on:
        pull_request_target:
          types: [labeled]
      jobs:
        a:
          if: github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
              with:
                ref: refs/pull/${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}/head
                allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
            - run: npm ci
      ```
    - called/action.yml (action-metadata, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: the composite action of the true positive mutable-ref.no-caller
      #   of this rule; the only caller, ci.yml, runs on push and calls the action
      #   after actions/checkout.
      # reason: the files that the linter reads are the whole repository and hold
      #   every caller of the action, so the rule reads the action on the events of
      #   the callers, here push alone, and a push comes from one who can write to
      #   the repository, not from the attacker. The if of the step of the action is
      #   false on push as well; the rule reports nothing because of the event of
      #   the caller, not because of the steps.
      # attack: after a maintainer reads the pull request and adds the label safe,
      #   the author of the pull request pushes to the branch of the fork a commit
      #   whose package.json has a preinstall that prints PWNED, before the checkout
      #   fetches.
      # attack-run-behavior: the attacker cannot push to the repository, so the
      #   attacker starts no run of ci.yml, and the steps of the action never run on
      #   an event of the attacker.
      name: test
      description: test the labelled pull request
      runs:
        using: composite
        steps:
          - if: github.event_name == 'pull_request_target' && github.event.action == 'labeled' && github.event.label.name == 'safe'
            uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: refs/pull/${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}/head
              allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
          - if: github.event_name == 'pull_request_target' && github.event.action == 'labeled' && github.event.label.name == 'safe'
            run: npm ci
            shell: bash
      ```
      - .github/workflows/ci.yml (workflow)
        ```yaml
        on: push
        jobs:
          j:
            runs-on: ubuntu-latest
            steps:
              - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2
              - uses: ./called
        ```
    - mutable-ref.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: on pull_request_target labeled, the checkout fetches
      #   github.event.pull_request.head.sha, and npm ci runs it.
      # reason: in place of refs/pull/<n>/head, which a push after the label
      #   moves, the job checks out the head SHA the labeled event recorded; a
      #   later push does not change that SHA, so npm ci runs the commit that was
      #   there when the label was added.
      # attack: after a maintainer reads the pull request and adds a label, its
      #   author pushes to the fork's branch a commit whose package.json has a
      #   preinstall that prints PWNED, before the job's checkout fetches.
      # attack-run-behavior: the checkout fetches the head.sha the labeled event
      #   recorded, the commit that was labelled, not the pushed one, so npm ci
      #   runs the package.json the maintainer read; the push starts a synchronize
      #   event, which this workflow does not take.
      on:
        pull_request_target:
          types: [labeled]
      jobs:
        a:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v4
              with:
                ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
                allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
            - run: npm ci
      ```

### fix kinds

- pin-head-sha: check out the commit the approval saw: github.event.pull_request.head.sha in place of a branch or refs/pull/&lt;n>/head
  - safety: safe
  - fact kinds: repo.environment-protected
- pin-head-sha-review: check out the head the approval saw in place of refs/pull/&lt;n>/merge
  - safety: review
  - fact kinds: repo.environment-protected
  - possible side effects:
    - merge-commit-replaced: The job checks out the head commit, not the merge commit with the base, so the code it gets differs.

### undetected forms

- outside-caller: a reusable workflow or composite action that callers in the repository decide, called from another repository on an event, or with a value, an attacker controls: the caller's run has the caller's token and secrets, not the repository's
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout-toctou.mutable-ref
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: .github/workflows/called.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the workflow is called; it checks out refs/pull/<n>/head with
    #   allow-unsafe-pr-checkout and runs npm ci. Its one caller in the
    #   repository, ci.yml, runs on push.
    # reason: no added gain for this repository: ci.yml calls the workflow on
    #   push alone, and github.event of a push has no pull request, so the value
    #   that the run reads is not a value that an attacker wrote. Another
    #   repository may call the workflow on an event whose payload has what an
    #   attacker wrote, but that run has the token and the secrets of the other
    #   repository.
    # cause: the rule reads a called workflow on the events of its callers in
    #   the repository, and ci.yml runs on push alone.
    # attack: after a maintainer reads the pull request and adds a label, its
    #   author pushes to the fork's branch a commit whose package.json has a
    #   preinstall that prints PWNED, before the job's checkout fetches.
    # attack-run-behavior: ci.yml calls it on push, whose event has no
    #   pull_request, so the ref is refs/pull//head, which names nothing, and
    #   the checkout fails before npm ci. A workflow of another repository that
    #   calls it on a labeled pull_request_target would fetch the pushed commit,
    #   with that repository's token.
    on:
      workflow_call:
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: refs/pull/${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}/head
              allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
          - run: npm ci
    ```
    - .github/workflows/ci.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: push
      jobs:
        call:
          uses: ./.github/workflows/called.yml
      ```
- git-in-run: the code of a pull request fetched by git or gh in a run (git fetch origin pull/&lt;n>/head, gh pr checkout), not by actions/checkout
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout-toctou.mutable-ref
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: git-in-run.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a run fetches the pull request's head
    #   with git, checks it out, and runs npm ci.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): reading git in a run would find it.
    # cause: the rule reads checkouts by actions/checkout only.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: git fetch takes pull/<n>/head of the base repository,
    #   which GitHub keeps at the fork's head, git checkout pr switches the
    #   workspace to it, and npm ci runs its preinstall, which prints PWNED,
    #   with the GITHUB_TOKEN actions/checkout left in .git/config and the job's
    #   secrets.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - run: |
              git fetch origin "pull/${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}/head:pr"
              git checkout pr
              npm ci
    ```
- artifact: the code of a pull request brought by the artifact of a run it drives: artifact-poisoning reports it
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout-toctou.mutable-ref
  - disposition: other-rule (rule: artifact-poisoning)
  - example: artifact.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on workflow_run, the artifact of the run workflow_run follows
    #   is downloaded into the workspace, and ./build.sh runs.
    # reason: another rule's: the pull request's code comes in an artifact,
    #   which artifact-poisoning reports.
    # cause: the rule reads checkouts by actions/checkout, not downloads.
    # attack-value: the file build.sh in the artifact of the pull request's ci run = "#!/bin/sh\necho PWNED\n"
    # attack-run-behavior: the fork's pull request changes ci so its run uploads
    #   build.sh; when that run completes, the download takes its artifact by
    #   workflow_run.id with the token into the workspace, and ./build.sh runs
    #   it, with this run's token and the base repository's secrets.
    on:
      workflow_run:
        workflows: [ci]
        types: [completed]
    permissions: {actions: read}
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
            with:
              run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
              github-token: ${{ github.token }}
          - run: ./build.sh
    ```
- cache: the code of a pull request brought by a cache that another run or job wrote
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout-toctou.mutable-ref
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: cache.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, actions/cache/restore restores
    #   node_modules, and npm test runs.
    # reason: a todo (the same file): the pull request's code comes in a cache
    #   another run wrote, not by a checkout.
    # cause: the rule does not read caches.
    # attack: code of the pull request, run in another run that shares the base
    #   branch's cache scope, saves node_modules under the key deps-<hash> with
    #   a module that prints PWNED when it is loaded.
    # attack-run-behavior: the restore puts that node_modules in the workspace,
    #   and npm test runs the test script, which loads the planted module, with
    #   the base repository's token and secrets.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
            with:
              path: node_modules
              key: deps-${{ hashFiles('package-lock.json') }}
          - run: npm test
    ```
- remote-action: a checkout in an action of another repository: the rule does not read the action
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout-toctou.mutable-ref
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-action.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, a step uses an action of another
    #   repository whose checkout takes the pull request's code, as in the
    #   Ultralytics incident (ultralytics/actions
    #   eb1201bd933b9f6096c64525ccaee3684c91bf14, action.yml:94: repository: ${{
    #   github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name || github.repository }}).
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the checkout is in an action of another
    #   repository.
    # cause: the rule does not read the action.yml of another repository.
    # attack-value: the file prettier.config.js in the pull request's head = "console.log(\"PWNED\"); module.exports = {};\n"
    # attack-run-behavior: the action checks out the branch github.head_ref of
    #   github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name, the fork, with its token
    #   input, and its later steps run tools over that tree when their inputs
    #   turn them on: with prettier: true, npx prettier loads the pull request's
    #   prettier.config.js, which prints PWNED. This example passes no inputs,
    #   and the action's defaults turn those steps off.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      format:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: ultralytics/actions@main
    ```
- literal-ref: a ref written out, such as a branch's name of the repository
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout-toctou.mutable-ref
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: literal-ref.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, actions/checkout checks out gh-pages, a
    #   branch of the repository written out, and make runs.
    # reason: no added gain: the ref is the repository's, not the pull
    #   request's.
    # cause: the rule reads a ref written out as the base's code.
    # attack-value: the file Makefile in the pull request's head = "all:\n	echo PWNED\n"
    # attack-run-behavior: the checkout fetches gh-pages of the base repository,
    #   not the pull request's head, so make runs the base's Makefile, and the
    #   pull request's does not run.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: gh-pages
          - run: make
    ```
- branch-name-ref: the name of the pull request's branch as the ref with the base repository: from a fork, the base has no such branch, or its own; from the repository, the author can write to it
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout-toctou.mutable-ref
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: branch-name-ref.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, actions/checkout checks out the pull
    #   request's branch name with the base repository, and npm ci runs.
    # reason: no added gain: from a fork the base has no such branch (the
    #   checkout fails); from the repository the author can write to it.
    # cause: the rule reads a branch's name as the pull request's code only with
    #   the fork as the repository.
    # attack-value: the file package.json on the pull request's branch = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: the checkout fetches the branch github.head_ref names
    #   from the base repository: for a fork's branch the base has no such
    #   branch and the step fails, or has one of the same name, whose
    #   package.json is the base's; for a branch of the repository, npm ci runs
    #   the preinstall its author pushed.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.head_ref }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
- pull-request: a job that runs only on pull_request, in one of two cases. In the first case, only the pull requests of the repository run the workflow: the author of a pull request can change the workflow itself, so the run of the job gives the author what the run has (read-only from a fork, or what a private repository sends to the runs of pull requests from forks: secrets, a token that writes) without the flaw of the rule, and the flaw of the rule adds nothing to what the author gets. In the second case, a ruleset of the organization or the enterprise runs the workflow on the pull requests of its other repositories (Require workflows to pass before merging, of GitHub Enterprise): the author of such a pull request cannot change the workflow, and whether the run has more than the pull_request workflow of the author would get (the token, secrets) is known from GitHub's documentation only, as no such run was observed; making a required check pass is outside the threat model of the rule. The workflow does not say which case holds, and the rule does not read which case holds
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout-toctou.mutable-ref
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: pull-request.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request, the pull request's head SHA is checked out,
    #   and npm ci runs.
    # reason: when only the pull requests of the repository run the workflow, the
    #   author of the pull request can change the workflow itself and gets what the
    #   run has without the flaw, so the flaw adds nothing to what the author gets;
    #   when a ruleset of the organization or the enterprise runs the workflow on
    #   the pull requests of its other repositories, the author cannot change the
    #   workflow, and what the run of the ruleset has beyond the author's own
    #   pull_request workflow is not known. The workflow does not say which case
    #   holds.
    # cause: the rule reads checkouts on pull_request_target, workflow_run and
    #   issue_comment only. The rule does not read whether a ruleset runs the
    #   workflow.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: the fork's pull request runs this workflow on
    #   pull_request; the checkout fetches head.sha and npm ci runs the preinstall,
    #   which prints PWNED, with a read-only GITHUB_TOKEN and none of the base
    #   repository's secrets. When a ruleset of the organization runs the workflow
    #   on a pull request of another repository, the same steps run in the run of
    #   the ruleset; what the run of the ruleset has was not observed, so whether
    #   the steps do harm in the run of the ruleset is not known.
    on: pull_request
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
- new-activity-type: an activity type GitHub added after the schemas the tables are made from, written in types: a value of types the tables do not have is dropped, as GitHub drops one it has no such activity type for
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout-toctou.mutable-ref
  - disposition: todo (needs: pin-update)
  - example: new-activity-type.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target of an activity type added_later, a job
    #   of the environment approve checks out refs/pull/<n>/head, and npm ci runs.
    # reason: a todo (a pin update): an activity type GitHub added after the
    #   pinned schemas is missed until the pins are updated.
    # cause: the analysis drops a value of types it does not know, as GitHub
    #   does for a value it has no such activity type for, so the job has no
    #   attacker's event.
    # attack: after a reviewer of the environment approve approves the job, the
    #   author of the pull request from a fork pushes to the branch of the pull
    #   request a commit whose package.json has a preinstall that prints PWNED.
    # attack-run-behavior: when GitHub sends pull_request_target with the
    #   activity type added_later, the job waits for the environment's reviewers;
    #   after the approval, the checkout fetches refs/pull/<n>/head, which names
    #   the pushed commit, and npm ci runs its preinstall.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [added_later]
    jobs:
      j:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        environment: approve
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: refs/pull/${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}/head
          - run: npm ci
    ```
- not-privileged: a job only on events that no attacker triggers (push, schedule), or on the events of a review (pull_request_review, pull_request_review_comment), where the code of the attacker reaches the checkout only in the run of a review of the pull request of the attacker, which runs the workflow of the merge commit of the pull request (refs/pull/&lt;n>/merge), and the attacker can change that workflow in the pull request (a job on pull_request is the undetected form pull-request); on workflow_dispatch, a checkout with no input of workflow_dispatch in its ref and repository, and no value made from one, brings a branch or a tag of the repository, which only those who can write to the repository change (the one who dispatches the workflow chooses the branch or the tag); repository_dispatch, whose sender has write access to the permission Contents, which the credential premise assumes no attacker has
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout-toctou.mutable-ref
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: not-privileged.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on push and pull_request_review, the pull request's head SHA is
    #   checked out, and npm ci runs.
    # reason: only those who can write to the repository push, and the code of
    #   the attacker reaches the checkout only in the run of a review of the pull
    #   request of the attacker, which runs the workflow of the merge commit of
    #   the pull request, a workflow that the attacker can change in the pull
    #   request.
    # cause: the rule reads checkouts on pull_request_target, workflow_run and
    #   issue_comment only.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: on pull_request_review of the fork's pull request,
    #   the checkout fetches head.sha and npm ci runs the preinstall, in the run
    #   of the workflow of the merge commit, which the attacker could change in
    #   the pull request to run the same code without the checkout; on push
    #   the event has no pull_request, so the ref is empty and the checkout
    #   fetches the pushed commit.
    on: [push, pull_request_review]
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
- guarded-checkout: a checkout on pull_request_target or workflow_run by a release of actions/checkout that refuses a fork's code (a major tag from v2, or a release from the guard), without allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: the step fails before anything runs
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout-toctou.mutable-ref
  - disposition: no-added-gain
  - example: guarded-checkout.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, actions/checkout@v4 checks out the pull
    #   request's head SHA, and npm ci runs.
    # reason: no added gain: actions/checkout@v4 (the major tag moved to v4.4.0
    #   on 2026-07-20) refuses the fork's head on pull_request_target; the step
    #   fails before npm runs.
    # cause: the rule takes a major tag of actions/checkout from v2 as refusing
    #   a fork's code.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: actions/checkout@v4 sees that the head repository is
    #   a fork and the event is pull_request_target, and without
    #   allow-unsafe-pr-checkout fails the step; npm ci does not run.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
- guard-gap: a checkout the guard of actions/checkout lets through at run time that the rule takes as refused: a fork deleted since the pull request, whose repository is not in the event (refs/pull/&lt;n>/head written with capitals, which its pattern does not match, is reported)
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout-toctou.mutable-ref
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: guard-gap.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, actions/checkout@v4 checks out the pull
    #   request's head SHA, and npm ci runs.
    # reason: a limitation (run time): the guard checks a fork by the id of the
    #   head repository in the event (actions/checkout v7.0.1
    #   src/unsafe-pr-checkout-helper.ts:53); a fork deleted since the pull
    #   request has none, and the checkout is let through at run time.
    # cause: the rule takes @v4 as refusing, and reports nothing.
    # attack: the author opens the pull request from a fork whose package.json
    #   has a preinstall that prints PWNED, and deletes the fork before the run.
    # attack-run-behavior: the event then has no id of the head repository, so
    #   the guard of actions/checkout lets the checkout through; it fetches
    #   head.sha, which refs/pull/<n>/head keeps, and npm ci runs the preinstall
    #   with the base repository's GITHUB_TOKEN in .git/config and its secrets.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
- sha-ref: a checkout of the commit the event names (github.event.pull_request.head.sha): when the author pushes a commit after a review and before the label, the person who adds the label may not see the commit, and the labeled run checks out the pushed commit (GHSL-2025-077); whether such a push comes between the review and the label is decided when the workflow runs
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout-toctou.mutable-ref
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: sha-ref.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target labeled, a job with the label preview
    #   checks out the pull request's head SHA and runs pip install -r
    #   requirements.txt: the shape of GHSL-2025-077 (beeware/beeware.github.io
    #   ci.yml).
    # reason: limitation: the commit is that of the time of the label, so a
    #   commit pushed after the review and before the label runs with the job's
    #   token and secrets (GHSL-2025-077); whether such a push comes is decided
    #   when the workflow runs.
    # cause: the rule reports a ref the author can move after the approval (a
    #   branch, refs/pull/<n>/...), and a SHA does not move.
    # attack: after a maintainer reviews the pull request and before the label
    #   preview is added, its author pushes a commit whose requirements.txt
    #   names a package of theirs whose setup code prints PWNED.
    # attack-run-behavior: the labeled run checks out head.sha, the commit at
    #   the time of the label, which is the pushed one, and pip install -r
    #   requirements.txt installs that package and runs its setup code, with the
    #   base repository's GITHUB_TOKEN in .git/config and its secrets.
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2025-077_beeware_beeware_github_io/
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    jobs:
      preview:
        if: contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'preview')
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: pip install -r requirements.txt
    ```
- dispatch-checkout: a checkout whose ref or repository refers to an input of workflow_dispatch: no label approves a run of workflow_dispatch, as a label approves only a run of pull_request_target with the activity type labeled; the one who dispatches the workflow chooses the value of the input, and untrusted-checkout reports the input as input-dispatch
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout-toctou.mutable-ref
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: dispatcher)
  - example: dispatch-checkout.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target with labeled alone and on
    #   workflow_dispatch, the checkout takes its ref from the input ref of
    #   workflow_dispatch, and npm ci runs.
    # reason: the one who dispatches the workflow chooses the value of the
    #   input, and no label approves a run of workflow_dispatch, as a label
    #   approves only a run of pull_request_target with the activity type labeled;
    #   untrusted-checkout reports the input as input-dispatch.
    # cause: the rule reads the references that the author of a pull request
    #   can move after a label or a reviewer of an environment approves the
    #   run; an input of workflow_dispatch is not such a reference.
    # attack-value: inputs.ref = "refs/pull/1/head"
    # attack-run-behavior: in a run of pull_request_target on labeled, the
    #   workflow, which has both triggers, has no input of workflow_dispatch, so
    #   inputs.ref is empty and the checkout fetches the commit of the event in
    #   the base repository. When the one who dispatches the workflow gives
    #   refs/pull/1/head as the input ref, and the pull request 1 is from a fork
    #   whose package.json has the preinstall script echo PWNED, no label stands
    #   before the job: the checkout fetches the head of the fork's pull request,
    #   and npm ci runs the preinstall script, which prints PWNED, with the
    #   secrets of the repository.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
      workflow_dispatch:
        inputs:
          ref: {type: string}
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ inputs.ref }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
- approval-none: a job that no one approves: untrusted-checkout reports it
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout-toctou.mutable-ref
  - disposition: other-rule (rule: untrusted-checkout)
  - example: approval-none.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target, refs/pull/<n>/head is checked out, and
    #   npm ci runs; no one approves the run.
    # reason: another rule's: untrusted-checkout reports it.
    # cause: the rule reads a job a person approves (a label, an environment)
    #   only.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: no label or reviewer stands before the job: the
    #   checkout fetches refs/pull/<n>/head, the fork's head, and npm ci runs
    #   its preinstall, which prints PWNED, with the base repository's
    #   GITHUB_TOKEN in .git/config and its secrets.
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: refs/pull/${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}/head
          - run: npm ci
    ```
- comment-approval: a job on issue_comment whose if reads the comment or its author as an approval: untrusted-checkout reports it
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout-toctou.mutable-ref
  - disposition: other-rule (rule: untrusted-checkout)
  - example: comment-approval.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on issue_comment, a job runs on a maintainer's comment, checks
    #   out refs/pull/<n>/head and runs a script of it, as in GHSL-2026-166
    #   (mongodb/node-mongodb-native 7f8edf30e376738fd554ac232d238e7022bc86a8,
    #   .github/workflows/release_notes.yml:10,21,44,56).
    # reason: another rule's: untrusted-checkout reports it as a checkout no one
    #   approves.
    # cause: the rule reads a label or an environment as an approval, not a
    #   comment.
    # attack: after a maintainer comments run release_notes on the pull request,
    #   its author pushes a commit whose .github/scripts/pr_list.mjs prints
    #   PWNED, before the job's checkout fetches.
    # attack-run-behavior: the comment's run passes the if, checks out
    #   refs/pull/<n>/head, which then names the pushed commit, and node runs
    #   its pr_list.mjs, with the job's GITHUB_TOKEN in .git/config and its
    #   secrets.
    # advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2026-166_MongoDB_Node_js_Driver/
    on:
      issue_comment:
        types: [created]
    jobs:
      notes:
        if: ${{ github.event.issue.pull_request && github.event.comment.body == 'run release_notes' }}
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: refs/pull/${{ github.event.issue.number }}/head
          - run: node .github/scripts/pr_list.mjs
    ```
- insider-association: an if that lets in MEMBER or COLLABORATOR by the author_association of the issue, the pull request or the discussion the run is of, which the following pass: a member or a collaborator whose repository role is Read only, who gets, in the run, a token that writes and the secrets, more than what the Read role gives; the account of such a member or collaborator, taken over; and an outsider who becomes a MEMBER with the Read role, in an organization that lets anyone become a member (a bot that invites whoever asks). A member or a collaborator whose role is Triage or above holds a credential that can add a label or write to the repository, which the credential premise assumes no attacker holds. Who is a member, and with what role, is not in the workflow
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout-toctou.mutable-ref
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: insider-association.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target labeled, a job whose if lets in MEMBER
    #   or COLLABORATOR checks out refs/pull/<n>/head with
    #   allow-unsafe-pr-checkout, and npm ci runs.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): a member of the organization, who may have read
    #   access only, passes this if (in an organization that lets anyone become a
    #   member, such as by a bot that invites whoever asks, an outsider becomes such
    #   a member), and gets the job's token and secrets past what the Read role
    #   gives; who is a member, and with what role, is not in the workflow.
    # cause: the rule evaluates the if with the attacker's author_association
    #   (NONE, FIRST_TIMER, FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR or CONTRIBUTOR), for which it
    #   is false, so no attacker's event runs the job.
    # attack: after a maintainer labels a pull request whose author is a MEMBER
    #   or a COLLABORATOR whose role is read, the author pushes a commit whose
    #   package.json has a preinstall that prints PWNED.
    # attack-run-behavior: the if is true for the author's association, the
    #   checkout fetches refs/pull/<n>/head, which then names the pushed commit,
    #   and npm ci runs its preinstall, with the base repository's GITHUB_TOKEN
    #   in .git/config and its secrets; for an author with NONE, FIRST_TIMER,
    #   FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR or CONTRIBUTOR the job is skipped.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    jobs:
      a:
        if: contains(fromJSON('["MEMBER", "COLLABORATOR"]'), github.event.pull_request.author_association)
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: refs/pull/${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}/head
              allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
          - run: npm ci
    ```
- automatic-label-checkout: a job on pull_request_target on labeled with no environment, whose run starts by a label that a workflow of the repository of the job adds to the pull request of an attacker by running actions/labeler with a token other than the GITHUB_TOKEN, where the attacker chooses the files of the pull request freely: no person approves the run; this rule does not report the checkout of such a job, and untrusted-checkout reports the checkout
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout-toctou.mutable-ref
  - disposition: other-rule (rule: untrusted-checkout)
  - example: .github/workflows/labeled.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: labeler.yml runs actions/labeler on pull_request_target with a
    #   personal access token, and the configuration .github/labeler.yml adds the
    #   label safe-to-test to a pull request that changes a file under site/;
    #   labeled.yml runs on pull_request_target on labeled, and the job checks out
    #   the head of the pull request and runs npm ci.
    # reason: the attacker chooses the files that the pull request changes, which
    #   actions/labeler reads, and a label that a personal access token adds
    #   starts the labeled run, so no person approves the run.
    # cause: the rule reads a checkout after an approval by a person, and a label
    #   that actions/labeler adds to the pull request of the attacker is no such
    #   approval: untrusted-checkout reports the checkout.
    # attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
    # attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork that
    #   changes a file under site/ and the files of the attack; actions/labeler
    #   adds the label safe-to-test, which starts labeled.yml, and the checkout
    #   fetches the head of the pull request, and npm ci runs the preinstall
    #   script of the pull request, which prints PWNED, with the secrets of the
    #   repository.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    jobs:
      build:
        if: github.event.label.name == 'safe-to-test'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
    - .github/labeler.yml (repo-file)
      ```yaml
      safe-to-test:
        - changed-files:
            - any-glob-to-any-file: 'site/**'
      ```
    - .github/workflows/labeler.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: pull_request_target
      permissions: {}
      jobs:
        label:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/labeler@v5
              with:
                repo-token: ${{ secrets.LABELER_PAT }}
      ```
- remote-callee: a job or a step inside a reusable workflow of another repository (uses: owner/repo/.github/workflows/&lt;file>@&lt;ref>) whose content the fact workflow.definition does not give. For every rule: a run that does not ask the fact (a run without --online and without the answer in --facts). For a quality rule, also: a run where the linter asked the fact and got no answer (an answer of unknown: the GitHub API did not give the file), and a call deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact. The rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition. For a rule that is not a quality rule (a rule with a threat), the last two forms are the inconclusive kind remote-callee-unknown, not this form
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout-toctou.mutable-ref
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-callee.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
    #   the repository example-org/untrusted-checkout-toctou-unanswered, whose
    #   content is the workflow of the true positive mutable-ref
    #   (mutable-ref.yml) of the rule, with on: workflow_call in place of the on
    #   of mutable-ref.yml. The linter has no answer of the fact
    #   workflow.definition for the reusable workflow.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event
    #   that started the run of the calling job, and the linter does not read
    #   the reusable workflow.
    # cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from
    #   the answer of workflow.definition.
    # attack: after a maintainer reads the pull request and adds a label, its
    #   author pushes to the fork's branch a commit whose package.json has a
    #   preinstall that prints PWNED, before the job's checkout fetches.
    # attack-run-behavior: the labeled run checks out refs/pull/<n>/head, which
    #   GitHub has moved to the pushed commit, and npm ci runs its preinstall,
    #   with the base repository's GITHUB_TOKEN in .git/config and its secrets.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/untrusted-checkout-toctou-unanswered/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

### inconclusive

- checkout-with-dynamic: a checkout whose with is a whole \${{ }}: its ref and repository are not known
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: checkout-with-dynamic.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: in a job a label approves (pull_request_target, labeled), the
    #   with of the checkout is a whole ${{ }}, and npm ci runs after it.
    # reason: with is a whole ${{ }}, so the ref and the repository of the
    #   checkout are not known.
    # attack: after a maintainer reads the pull request and adds a label, its
    #   author pushes to the fork's branch a commit whose package.json has a
    #   preinstall that prints PWNED, before the job's checkout fetches.
    # attack-run-behavior: when vars.CHECKOUT gives a ref the author moves after
    #   the label (refs/pull/<n>/head, say) and allow-unsafe-pr-checkout, the
    #   checkout fetches the pushed commit, and npm ci runs its preinstall, with
    #   the base repository's GITHUB_TOKEN in .git/config and its secrets.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with: ${{ fromJSON(vars.CHECKOUT) }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
- checkout-ref-unknown: a checkout whose ref or repository has what a step or a job computes, an input other than one of workflow_dispatch (or an input of workflow_dispatch in a workflow that also has workflow_call, when a workflow on an event of a pull request calls the workflow), an env, a matrix or a variable: whether it names a pull request's code is not analyzed
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: checkout-ref-unknown.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: in a job a label approves (pull_request_target, labeled), the
    #   checkout takes its ref from the output of a step, and npm ci runs after
    #   it.
    # reason: the ref is what a step computes, so whether it names the code of a
    #   pull request is not analyzed.
    # attack: after a maintainer reads the pull request and adds a label, its
    #   author pushes to the fork's branch a commit whose package.json has a
    #   preinstall that prints PWNED, before the job's checkout fetches.
    # attack-run-behavior: when steps.pr.outputs.ref names a ref the author
    #   moves after the label (the head branch of a pull request from the
    #   repository, or refs/pull/<n>/head), the checkout fetches it when the job
    #   runs, which then names the pushed commit, and npm ci runs its
    #   preinstall, with the base repository's GITHUB_TOKEN in .git/config and
    #   its secrets.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - id: pr
            run: echo "ref=$(gh pr view --json headRefName -q .headRefName)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
            with:
              ref: ${{ steps.pr.outputs.ref }}
          - run: npm ci
    ```
- remote-callee-unknown: a job that calls a reusable workflow of another repository, when the linter asked the fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow and got no answer (the token that the linter uses cannot read the file, the file is larger than the limit, or the linter has used up the requests it may send to the GitHub API), or when the call is deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact: the rule does not read the jobs and the steps of the reusable workflow
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-callee-unknown.yml (workflow, inconclusive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
    #   the repository example-org/untrusted-checkout-toctou-unknown, whose
    #   content is the workflow of the true positive mutable-ref
    #   (mutable-ref.yml) of the rule, with on: workflow_call in place of the on
    #   of mutable-ref.yml. The linter asked the fact workflow.definition for
    #   the reusable workflow and got no answer.
    # reason: what the jobs of the reusable workflow do is in the file that the
    #   linter could not read; whoever changes the uses, such as the author of a
    #   pull request, can name a reusable workflow that the token that the
    #   linter uses cannot read.
    # attack: after a maintainer reads the pull request and adds a label, its
    #   author pushes to the fork's branch a commit whose package.json has a
    #   preinstall that prints PWNED, before the job's checkout fetches.
    # attack-run-behavior: the labeled run checks out refs/pull/<n>/head, which
    #   GitHub has moved to the pushed commit, and npm ci runs its preinstall,
    #   with the base repository's GITHUB_TOKEN in .git/config and its secrets.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/untrusted-checkout-toctou-unknown/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

### false positive forms

- callee: a reusable workflow or a composite action when all of the following are true: the rule does not know all of the callers of the reusable workflow or the composite action; every workflow that runs the reusable workflow or the composite action (directly, or through another reusable workflow or composite action) is a workflow in the same repository; and the rule would report no finding of the finding kind if the rule read the reusable workflow or the composite action only on the events on which the workflows in the same repository run the reusable workflow or the composite action (for example, every workflow that runs the reusable workflow or the composite action runs only on push). When the rule does not know all of the callers, the rule can read the reusable workflow or the composite action on every event (the worst case). For example, the rule does not know all of the callers when no caller is among the inputs; when the inputs are not the whole repository; for a composite action, when an input is excluded or cannot be read; when a caller names the reusable workflow or the composite action by a name of the form owner/repo/path@ref instead of by a ./ path, in which owner/repo is the repository that the --repo flag names, or is any repository when no --repo flag is given; when a step names the composite action by a ./ path, and either no checkout step runs before that step or the last checkout step before that step is not a plain checkout step (a plain checkout step has no ref input, no repository input and no path input); when a step inside a composite action names another composite action by a ./ path; or when the rule does not know all of the callers of a caller
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout-toctou.mutable-ref
  - disposition: todo (needs: repo-file)
  - example: .github/workflows/called.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: ci.yml of the repository o/r runs on push alone and calls this
    #   reusable workflow by the name o/r/.github/workflows/called.yml@main, not
    #   by the path ./.github/workflows/called.yml. No other workflow calls this
    #   reusable workflow. The job of this reusable workflow waits for the
    #   approval of the environment approve, whose required reviewers approve the
    #   job, and then checks out refs/pull/<n>/head and runs npm ci.
    # reason: when the run of the linter names the repository (--repo o/r), the
    #   only workflow that runs this reusable workflow is ci.yml, and ci.yml runs
    #   on push alone. The payload of push has no pull request, so no reviewer
    #   approves a run for a pull request of an attacker, and the attacker has no
    #   pull request whose head the attacker moves after the approval. A run
    #   without --repo reads the call by the name
    #   o/r/.github/workflows/called.yml@main as a call that may name a file of
    #   the repository, because the run does not know which repository the inputs
    #   are; the rule does not resolve the call to this file, so the rule reads
    #   this file on every event and reports the same finding.
    # cause: the rule does not resolve the call by the name of the repository to
    #   this file, so the rule does not know all of the callers of this reusable
    #   workflow, and reads this reusable workflow on every event,
    #   pull_request_target among the events.
    # attack: after a reviewer approves the job for the pull request of the
    #   attacker, the attacker pushes a new commit to the branch of the pull
    #   request.
    # attack-run-behavior: only a push to the repository o/r runs ci.yml, so the
    #   job of this reusable workflow never runs for a pull request of the
    #   attacker, and the push of the attacker to the branch of the pull request
    #   changes nothing that the job checks out.
    on:
      workflow_call:
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        environment: approve
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: refs/pull/${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}/head
              allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
          - run: npm ci
    ```
    - finding on: .github/workflows/called.yml
    - .github/workflows/ci.yml (workflow)
      ```yaml
      on: push
      jobs:
        call:
          uses: o/r/.github/workflows/called.yml@main
      ```
- pull-request-target-blocked: a workflow whose on has pull_request_target and no other event (no workflow_call event either), in a repository whose Actions policies block the runs of the workflow on pull_request_target (repo.pull-request-target-allowed false): an event policy that an administrator sets without pull_request_target among the allowed events, or the default policy that GitHub adds to a public repository without an applicable event policy, from the time when GitHub enforces the default policy on the repository. GitHub's documents say that GitHub evaluates the policies before a run, and that a run that a policy does not allow fails with an error. The documents do not say whether a job of such a run starts before the run fails; the rule assumes that no job of such a run starts
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout-toctou.mutable-ref
  - fact kinds:
    - repo.pull-request-target-allowed (provider: repo-setting, answer that removes the finding: false)
  - example: pull-request-target-blocked.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target labeled, the job checks out
    #   refs/pull/<n>/head and runs npm ci.
    # reason: the Actions policies of the repository block the runs of the
    #   workflow on pull_request_target: the default policy that GitHub adds to a
    #   public repository without an applicable event policy, from the time when
    #   GitHub enforces the default policy on the repository, or an event policy
    #   whose list of allowed events does not have pull_request_target. GitHub's
    #   documents say that GitHub evaluates the policies before a run, and that a
    #   run that a policy does not allow fails with an error; the documents do not
    #   say whether a job of such a run starts before the run fails, and the rule
    #   assumes that no job starts.
    # cause: unless a file of facts or --fact says that the Actions policies block
    #   runs on pull_request_target (repo.pull-request-target-allowed false), the
    #   rule reports the finding. When no file of facts and no --fact answers
    #   repo.pull-request-target-allowed, the finding is conditional.
    # attack: after a maintainer adds a label, the author of the pull request
    #   pushes to the branch of the fork a commit whose package.json has a
    #   preinstall that prints PWNED.
    # attack-run-behavior: the pull request of the attacker triggers
    #   pull_request_target, and the run fails with an error, and no job of the
    #   run starts (the assumption of the reason), so npm ci never runs.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: refs/pull/${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}/head
              allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
          - run: npm ci
    ```
- actions-policy: a run that the Actions policies of the repository block, in four cases where the rule does not take the policies into account. First, an event policy that blocks an event of the attackers other than pull_request_target (such as issue_comment) in a workflow whose on has that event: the rules ask a fact only for pull_request_target. Second, an actor rule that does not allow the account of the attacker (for example, an actor rule that allows only the repository roles with write access): repo.pull-request-target-allowed is one value for all the runs of a workflow file on pull_request_target, and an actor rule blocks a run by the account that starts the run, so the fact cannot tell what an actor rule blocks. Third, a workflow whose on has pull_request_target and another event: the rule does not ask repo.pull-request-target-allowed for such a workflow, because a run on the other event can reach the job. When the if of the job is false on the other event, so that the job runs only on pull_request_target, and a policy blocks pull_request_target, the finding is a false positive. Fourth, a reusable workflow (on workflow_call) or an action that only workflows on pull_request_target call: the rule asks repo.pull-request-target-allowed only of a workflow whose on has pull_request_target, not of the reusable workflow or the action, so a finding in the reusable workflow or the action is still reported when the policies block the runs of every caller
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout-toctou.mutable-ref
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: actions-policy.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: on pull_request_target labeled, the job checks out
    #   refs/pull/<n>/head and runs npm ci.
    # reason: an actor rule of the Actions policies of the repository allows
    #   only the repository roles with write access to trigger the workflow, so a
    #   run that a pull request from an account without write access triggers
    #   fails. GitHub's documents say that GitHub evaluates the policies before a
    #   run, and that a run that a policy does not allow fails with an error; the
    #   documents do not say whether a job of such a run starts before the run
    #   fails, and the rule assumes that no job starts.
    # cause: the rule does not take the actor rules of the Actions policies into
    #   account: repo.pull-request-target-allowed is one value for all the runs of
    #   the workflow file on pull_request_target, and an actor rule blocks a run
    #   by the account that starts the run.
    # attack: after a maintainer adds a label, the author of the pull request
    #   pushes to the branch of the fork a commit whose package.json has a
    #   preinstall that prints PWNED.
    # attack-run-behavior: the account of the attacker is not an allowed actor,
    #   so the run on pull_request_target fails with an error, and no job of the
    #   run starts (the assumption of the reason), so npm ci never runs.
    name: policy
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: refs/pull/${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}/head
              allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
          - run: npm ci
    ```
- actions-not-allowed: a workflow whose run GitHub does not start, or a job that GitHub fails in the step "Set up job", because of the setting of allowed actions of GitHub (the fact repo.allowed-actions, which the quality rule allowed-actions reads): GitHub does not start a run of a workflow that has a uses, or that calls a reusable workflow that has a uses, that the setting does not allow, and fails a job before any step of the job runs when a step of a composite action that the job runs has a uses that the setting does not allow, or when the setting requires a full commit SHA and a step names an action by a tag or a branch. The harm that the finding reports happens only when GitHub runs the workflow or the job, and the rule does not read repo.allowed-actions
  - finding kinds: untrusted-checkout-toctou.mutable-ref
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: actions-not-allowed.yml (workflow, false-positive)
    ```yaml
    # situation: the workflow of the true positive mutable-ref (mutable-ref.yml)
    #   of the rule, with a job added whose step uses
    #   example-org/not-allowed-action, which the setting of allowed actions of
    #   GitHub (repo.allowed-actions) blocks with
    #   !example-org/not-allowed-action@*. In the true positive, on
    #   pull_request_target labeled, the job checks out refs/pull/<n>/head and
    #   runs npm ci.
    # reason: GitHub checks each uses of the workflow before the run starts, and
    #   does not start the run because of the uses of
    #   example-org/not-allowed-action: no job of the run runs, so what the
    #   reason of the true positive says does not happen (in runs that the
    #   authors of the rule made on GitHub, such runs ended as startup_failure).
    # cause: the rule does not read repo.allowed-actions.
    # attack: after a maintainer reads the pull request and adds a label, its
    #   author pushes to the fork's branch a commit whose package.json has a
    #   preinstall that prints PWNED, before the job's checkout fetches.
    # attack-run-behavior: GitHub does not start the run, so no step of the run
    #   runs, and the attack does nothing.
    on:
      pull_request_target:
        types: [labeled]
    jobs:
      a:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: refs/pull/${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}/head
              allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
          - run: npm ci
      not-allowed:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: example-org/not-allowed-action@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```

### threat

- precondition callers-events: a reusable workflow or a composite action that is among the inputs runs on the events of the callers of the workflow or the action, whoever the callers are; when the inputs are the whole repository and hold every caller of the workflow or the action, the rule reads the workflow or the action on the events of the callers, with the values that the callers give under with
  - cites:
    - <https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows#workflow_call>
    - <https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7x29-qqmq-v6qc>
- precondition privileged-event: the job runs on pull_request_target, workflow_run or issue_comment, which a pull request from a fork or a comment triggers, with the repository's secrets and a token that may write; not pull_request, pull_request_review or pull_request_review_comment: from a fork they run the pull request's own workflow, which its author can change, read-only unless a private repository sends them secrets or a token that writes; from a branch of the repository, the code checked out is of one who can write
  - observed: 2026-09-28, runner 2.337.0: a pull request from a fork ran pull_request_target, workflow_run after its pull_request, and issue_comment on a comment, each with the repository's secret and a token that created a ref
  - cites:
    - <https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/securely-using-pull_request_target>
- precondition pr-tree: the checkout brings the pull request's code: its head or merge commit, refs/pull/&lt;n>/head or merge, or the fork as the repository; a branch's name with the base repository brings the base's branch of that name, if any
  - observed: 2026-09-28, runner 2.337.0: a checkout of the fork's head SHA, refs/pull/&lt;n>/head and refs/pull/&lt;n>/merge from the base repository brought the fork's commit and the merge commit; one of head.ref with the base repository failed, as the base had no such branch
  - cites:
    - <https://securitylab.github.com/resources/github-actions-preventing-pwn-requests/>
- precondition no-guard: on pull_request_target and workflow_run, the release of actions/checkout does not refuse a fork's code: v1, a release before the guard (v2.8.0, v3.7.0, v4.4.0, v5.1.0, v6.1.0, v7.0.0), a commit pinned before it, or allow-unsafe-pr-checkout set; issue_comment is not guarded
  - observed: 2026-09-28, runner 2.337.0: v7.0.1 and the major tag v4 refused the fork's head SHA and refs/pull/&lt;n>/head on pull_request_target and workflow_run, and allowed them with allow-unsafe-pr-checkout; v4.2.2 pinned by its SHA fetched them; on issue_comment v7.0.1 fetched refs/pull/&lt;n>/head
  - cites:
    - <https://github.blog/changelog/2026-06-18-safer-pull_request_target-defaults-for-github-actions-checkout>
- precondition approved: a person approves the run: a job that runs only on pull_request_target with the activity type labeled, whose label needs a credential with write access to the permission Issues or Pull requests, which the credential premise assumes no attacker holds, and no workflow of the same repository runs actions/labeler that adds the label to the pull request of an attacker with a token other than the GITHUB_TOKEN; or a job whose environment has required reviewers (repo.environment-protected)
  - cites:
    - <https://securitylab.github.com/resources/github-actions-preventing-pwn-requests/>
- precondition movable-checkout: the checkout fetches what the author moves: refs/pull/&lt;n>/head or merge, or a branch of the fork; github.event.pull_request.head.sha is the head when the label was added
  - observed: 2026-09-28, runner 2.337.0: a commit pushed after the label, while the labeled run waited, was fetched by refs/pull/&lt;n>/head; github.event.pull_request.head.sha fetched the head of the time of the label; the push ran no labeled run
- actor: fork-pr-author
  - via: pushes to the pull request's branch after a maintainer approves it
  - events: pull_request_target, workflow_run
  - run starters: pull_request_target: other, workflow_run: attacker
  - gains: run-code, read-secrets, write-with-token, write-cache

### CVSS

#### untrusted-checkout-toctou.mutable-ref

- vector: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:A/VC:H/VI:H/VA:L/SC:H/SI:H/SA:N/E:P
- CVSS-B: 8.7 (high)
- CVSS-BT: 7.3 (high)
- impact: H (from VC, VI, SC, SI)
- likelihood: low (from AV:N, AT:P, PR:N; lowered by UI:A)
- severity: medium (impact H, likelihood low; the table: sisakulint --explain=terms)
- AV: N
  - reason: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork, or comments on one, over the network
  - cites: none
- AC: L
  - reason: a change of a script, a build file or a package manifest of the pull request is all it takes
  - cites: none
- AT: P
  - reason: the push must come after the approval and before a checkout fetches the ref: in the run itself (the time from the label to the step, seconds to minutes), or before a re-run of the run, which a credential with write access to the permission Actions may start within 30 days, such as the credential of an attacker whose only write access is to the permission Actions, and which runs with the payload of the approval, so that a label taken off since still lets the job run (observed on 2026-09-28)
  - cites:
    - <https://securitylab.github.com/resources/github-actions-preventing-pwn-requests/>
    - <https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/manage-workflow-runs/re-run-workflows-and-jobs>
- PR: N
  - reason: nothing of the repository is needed
  - cites: none
- UI: A
  - reason: a maintainer adds the label, or approves the environment, after looking at the pull request
  - cites: none
- VC: H
  - reason: the code reads the job's secrets and GITHUB_TOKEN
  - cites: none
- VI: H
  - reason: with the job's token the code can push, and write releases and packages
  - cites: none
- VA: L
  - reason: the code can fail or stop the job
  - cites: none
- SC: H
  - reason: the secrets open what is past the job: clouds, registries, other repositories
  - cites: none
- SI: H
  - reason: what the job publishes reaches those who use it; in the tj-actions incident a stolen token of this kind led to moved tags
  - cites:
    - <https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/github-actions-supply-chain-attack/>
- SA: N
  - reason: nothing past the job is made unavailable by this as such
  - cites: none
- E: P
  - reason: GitHub Security Lab reported the race in label-gated workflows, and a checkout of refs/pull/&lt;n>/head after a maintainer's comment (GHSL-2026-166); no attack in the wild was found
  - cites:
    - <https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2026-166_MongoDB_Node_js_Driver/>
