- <https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2026-166_MongoDB_Node_js_Driver/>

## uses-path

- problem: a step's uses writes its owner, repository or path with parts that GitHub drops or resolves (empty parts such as // or a / before @, a part that is . or .., or, in a uses of another repository, a backslash, which GitHub reads as /), or with .. that goes above the root of the repository or of the workspace, so that the uses as written does not name the action that runs
- expected: every uses names the action that runs as GitHub reads the uses: no empty part, no part that is . or .. (the ./ at the start of a local action stays), and / between the parts
- targets: workflow, action-metadata
- quality rule: a finding of the quality rule alone gives no attacker a gain, and the findings of the quality rule set no bit of the exit code
- default run: always: in a run without --rule, the rule runs unless --skip-rule names the rule

### finding kinds

- uses-path.outside-repository
  - detected: the path of the uses {uses} goes with .. above the root of the repository that the uses names
  - arguments:
    - {uses}: The uses, as written.
  - consequence: the runner puts each action that the job downloads in \_actions/&lt;owner>/&lt;repo>/&lt;ref> on the runner, and runs the action of the directory that the path names, outside the repository that the uses names. When another uses of the job, or of a composite action that the job uses, downloads an action into that directory, the step runs that action; when no uses does, the job fails before the steps of the job run. The ref after @ does not decide the code that runs. For a uses of another repository whose path stays in \_actions, commit-sha reports, on this step, the ref of the action that runs when that ref is not a full commit SHA
  - remedy: write a uses of the action that is meant to run, as owner/repo/path@ref of that action (/path only when the action is in a directory of the repository), without ..
  - true positives:
    - outside-repository.remote-callee.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
      #   the repository example-org/uses-path-remote, which the fact
      #   workflow.definition answers with the workflow of the true positive
      #   outside-repository (outside-repository.yml) of the rule, with on:
      #   workflow_call in place of the on of outside-repository.yml. The job
      #   passes its secrets with secrets: inherit. In the true positive, the
      #   first step uses a composite action of example-org/ci-tools pinned to a
      #   full SHA, whose action.yml uses actions/github-script@v7; the second
      #   step names example-org/ci-tools by a full SHA, but its path goes with ..
      #   above the root of the repository, to actions/github-script/v7.
      # reason: the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event that started the
      #   run of the calling job, so the reason of the true positive holds: the
      #   runner puts each action of the job, a composite action's own uses among
      #   them, in _actions/<owner>/<repo>/<ref>, and reads the path of the second
      #   step from the directory of example-org/ci-tools there; the second step
      #   runs actions/github-script at the tag v7, not an action of
      #   example-org/ci-tools.
      on: push
      jobs:
        c:
          uses: example-org/uses-path-remote/.github/workflows/w.yml@v1
          secrets: inherit
      ```
    - outside-repository.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: the first step uses a composite action of example-org/ci-tools
      #   pinned to a full SHA, whose action.yml uses actions/github-script@v7;
      #   the second step names example-org/ci-tools by a full SHA, but its path
      #   goes with .. above the root of the repository, to
      #   actions/github-script/v7.
      # reason: the runner puts each action of the job, a composite action's own
      #   uses among them, in _actions/<owner>/<repo>/<ref>, and reads the path of
      #   the second step from the directory of example-org/ci-tools there; the
      #   second step runs actions/github-script at the tag v7, not an action of
      #   example-org/ci-tools.
      on: push
      jobs:
        lint:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: example-org/ci-tools/setup@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683
            - uses: example-org/ci-tools/../../../actions/github-script/v7@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683
              with:
                script: console.log("done")
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - outside-repository.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a step uses example-org/ci-tools/lint by a full SHA.
      # reason: the path stays in the repository, so the full SHA decides the
      #   code that runs.
      on: push
      jobs:
        lint:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: example-org/ci-tools/lint@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683
      ```
- uses-path.outside-workspace
  - detected: the path of the uses {uses} goes with .. above the root of the workspace
  - arguments:
    - {uses}: The uses, as written.
  - consequence: the runner resolves the path from the workspace of the job; a ./ uses of an action.yml is resolved from the workspace of the job that runs the action, too. The .. takes the path to a directory of the runner above the workspace, so the step runs an action of the checked-out repository only when the path comes back into the workspace through the name of the directory of the workspace; otherwise the step runs what earlier steps and the runner put in another directory of the runner
  - remedy: write ./ and the path of the action from the root of the workspace, without ..
  - true positives:
    - outside-workspace.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: after a checkout, a step uses ./../app/.github/actions/setup,
      #   a path that goes with .. above the root of the workspace.
      # reason: the runner resolves the path from the workspace, which is
      #   /home/runner/work/<repository>/<repository> on a GitHub-hosted runner;
      #   the step runs the action of the checked-out repository only when the
      #   repository is named app, and otherwise the action of another directory
      #   of the runner.
      on: push
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683
            - uses: ./../app/.github/actions/setup
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - outside-workspace.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: after a checkout, a step uses ./.github/actions/setup.
      # reason: the path names a directory of the checked-out repository.
      on: push
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683
            - uses: ./.github/actions/setup
      ```
- uses-path.unnormalized-path
  - detected: the uses {uses} has parts that GitHub drops or resolves, and GitHub reads the uses as {normalized}
  - arguments:
    - {uses}: The uses, as written.
    - {normalized}: The uses as GitHub reads the uses: empty parts dropped, . and .. resolved, a backslash read as /.
  - consequence: GitHub runs the action of the uses as GitHub reads the uses, not as the uses is written; a person or a tool that reads the uses as written may take the uses for a different action
  - remedy: write the uses as GitHub reads the uses: no empty part, no part that is . or .. (the ./ at the start of a local action stays), and / between the parts
  - true positives:
    - unnormalized-path.yml (workflow, true-positive)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a step uses actions/cache/restore/../save, pinned to a full
      #   SHA, after a build.
      # reason: the runner resolves .. as text, so the step runs
      #   actions/cache/save; a person or a tool that reads the path as written
      #   may take the step for actions/cache/restore.
      on: push
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: make
            - uses: actions/cache/restore/../save@0057852bfaa89a56745cba8c7296529d2fc39830
              with:
                path: build
                key: build-${{ github.sha }}
      ```
  - true negatives:
    - unnormalized-path.yml (workflow, true-negative)
      ```yaml
      # situation: a step uses actions/cache/save, pinned to a full SHA, after a
      #   build.
      # reason: the uses is written as GitHub reads the uses.
      on: push
      jobs:
        build:
          runs-on: ubuntu-latest
          steps:
            - run: make
            - uses: actions/cache/save@0057852bfaa89a56745cba8c7296529d2fc39830
              with:
                path: build
                key: build-${{ github.sha }}
      ```

### undetected forms

- folded-uses: a uses written as \${{ }} around a string literal (not a folded scalar of YAML), such as \${{ 'actions/checkout/./@v4' }}, which GitHub reads as the string: the rule reads only a uses written as the string itself
  - finding kinds: uses-path.outside-repository, uses-path.outside-workspace, uses-path.unnormalized-path
  - disposition: todo (needs: same-file)
  - example: folded-uses.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a step uses ${{ 'actions/cache/restore/../save@0057852bfaa89a56745cba8c7296529d2fc39830' }}, which
    #   GitHub evaluates to the string and runs as actions/cache/save.
    # reason: the uses as written does not name the action that runs.
    # cause: the rule reads the uses as written, and a folded uses is written as
    #   a ${{ }} expression.
    on: push
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: make
          - uses: ${{ 'actions/cache/restore/../save@0057852bfaa89a56745cba8c7296529d2fc39830' }}
            with:
              path: build
              key: build-${{ github.sha }}
    ```
- windows-runner: a job on a Windows runner, where how the runner reads a backslash in a ./ or \$/ path, and a path that differs from a directory only in upper and lower case, was not observed: the rule reads the uses as a Linux runner reads the uses, and does not look at letter case
  - finding kinds: uses-path.outside-repository, uses-path.outside-workspace, uses-path.unnormalized-path
  - disposition: limitation (decided by: run-time)
  - example: windows-runner.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job on a Windows runner uses ./.github\actions\setup after a
    #   checkout.
    # reason: a Windows runner may read the backslash as a separator of the
    #   path, so the step may run ./.github/actions/setup.
    # cause: the rule reads the uses as a Linux runner reads the uses, where a
    #   backslash of a ./ path is a character of the name of a directory.
    on: push
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: windows-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683
          - uses: ./.github\actions\setup
    ```
- remote-callee: a job or a step inside a reusable workflow of another repository (uses: owner/repo/.github/workflows/&lt;file>@&lt;ref>) whose content the fact workflow.definition does not give. For every rule: a run that does not ask the fact (a run without --online and without the answer in --facts). For a quality rule, also: a run where the linter asked the fact and got no answer (an answer of unknown: the GitHub API did not give the file), and a call deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact. The rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition. For a rule that is not a quality rule (a rule with a threat), the last two forms are the inconclusive kind remote-callee-unknown, not this form
  - finding kinds: uses-path.outside-repository, uses-path.outside-workspace, uses-path.unnormalized-path
  - disposition: todo (needs: fact)
  - example: remote-callee.yml (workflow, undetected)
    ```yaml
    # situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
    #   the repository example-org/uses-path-unanswered, whose content is the
    #   workflow of the true positive outside-repository
    #   (outside-repository.yml) of the rule, with on: workflow_call in place of
    #   the on of outside-repository.yml. The linter has no answer of the fact
    #   workflow.definition for the reusable workflow.
    # reason: a todo (a fact): the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event
    #   that started the run of the calling job, and the linter does not read
    #   the reusable workflow.
    # cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from
    #   the answer of workflow.definition.
    on: push
    permissions: {}
    jobs:
      c:
        uses: example-org/uses-path-unanswered/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
    ```
